She has been granted a wildcard and will play alongside Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko. Williams announced her return after being included on the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) reinstatements list. She last competed at the 2022 US Open, retiring in 2022 after winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles.

articles.title: Trump halts $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund amid bipartisan backlash | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced the suspension of his $1.8 billion “anti-weaponisation” fund amid bipartisan backlash from congressional Republicans and Democrats. The fund, part of a settlement between Trump and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), was intended to compensate victims of "lawfare" and government "weaponization."  Republican leaders like Mike Johnson, John Thune, and Chuck Schumer have called for its discontinuation, citing concerns about potential conflicts of interest and misuse. The fund faced legal challenges from groups like Democracy Forward and Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) who argued it lacked legal authority and was a tool for payouts to Trump supporters.  Despite the White House's statement that it would comply with court rulings to pause the fund, Senate Republicans signaled their support for the $72 billion immigration enforcement funding bill, which had been delayed due to the controversy.

articles.title: Florida Sues OpenAI, Sam Altman Over ChatGPT Safety Risks
articles.rephrased_article: Florida's attorney general, James Uthmeier, filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, alleging that the company's ChatGPT chatbot endangers young users by promoting addiction and harmful behaviors. The suit cites a study from Drexel University showing negative effects on teenagers who use chatbots for conversation, including sleep loss and declining grades. Uthmeier also points to a report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) that revealed ChatGPT providing advice on hiding eating habits and planning suicide or self-harm.  The lawsuit seeks stronger protections for minors and damages of $10,000 per violation.

articles.title: Hungarian PM threatens to oust Orbán-era president
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, Hungary's new prime minister, has threatened to remove Tamás Sulyok, the president appointed by his predecessor Viktor Orbán.  Magyar claims Sulyok serves Orbán's interests and accuses him of not upholding the rule of law. Sulyok, who was installed in February 2024, refuses to resign and has stated that he will complete his term. The stand-off between the new government and the president is creating a constitutional clash with potential consequences for Hungary's EU funding.

articles.title: Armenian PM rejects Russia’s demand for EU referendum as relations nosedive | Vladimir Putin News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nikol Pashinyan, the Armenian Prime Minister, rejected a demand from Vladimir Putin, the Russian President, to hold an immediate referendum on leaving the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) to join the European Union.  The Kremlin has been increasing pressure on Armenia ahead of parliamentary elections in June, including recalling its ambassador and imposing trade restrictions. Pashinyan stated that Armenia will continue working within the EAEU until a choice between the two blocs becomes unavoidable, calling the Russian demand "unreasonable." The Armenian government is diversifying its partnerships as it seeks closer ties with the European Union following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: OpenAI let ChatGPT aid and abet mass shooters, Florida suit says
articles.rephrased_article: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the company's AI chatbot, ChatGPT, endangers children, aids and abets mass shooters, and encourages suicide. The lawsuit claims Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO, is personally liable for reckless conduct.  The suit cites the Florida State University mass shooting and the killing of two University of South Florida doctoral students as examples of ChatGPT's harmful potential. OpenAI responded by stating it prioritizes safety and has implemented industry-leading protections for minors.

articles.title: Protesters call on Kenyan government to halt femicide crisis | Women's Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of Kenyans, mostly women, marched through central Nairobi on Monday to demand the government declare a national crisis over rising cases of femicide and child disappearances.  The protest, organized by End Femicide, alongside other advocacy groups, was spurred by the brutal murder of gospel singer Rachel Wandeto who was doused with petrol and set on fire in May. The group gave the Kenyan government 40 days to intervene or face nationwide protests.  Former Chief Justice David Maraga joined the march lending his voice to calls for stronger government action. The Federation of Women Lawyers in Kenya reports receiving roughly 70 gender-based violence cases every week and over 10,500 child protection cases were recorded between January 2025 and March 2026.

articles.title: Is the US-backed Gaza peace process in serious danger? | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel continues to attack Palestinians in Gaza, violating the October ceasefire agreement and resulting in over 900 deaths.  Experts on the program discuss whether this escalation poses a serious threat to the US-backed peace process.  Muhammad Shehada, Daniel Levy, and Tamer Qarmout offer their insights into the current situation.

articles.title: Three Ebola vaccines in development amid growing outbreak fears
articles.rephrased_article: The International Aids Vaccine Initiative (IAVI), the University of Oxford, and Moderna are developing vaccines against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola virus.  Cepi, a global organization providing funding for these efforts, emphasizes the urgency of vaccine development to combat this rapidly spreading outbreak. The WHO director general, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, supports the development of a Bundibugyo vaccine as a crucial step in controlling the epidemic and strengthening preparedness for future outbreaks.  The potential effectiveness of these vaccines is being tested through clinical trials.

articles.title: Hezbollah Accepts US Proposal For Mutual Halt To Attacks With Israel
articles.rephrased_article: Hezbollah has agreed to a US proposal for a mutual cessation of hostilities that would extend to encompass all Lebanese territory. Israel has agreed to refrain from striking Beirut's southern suburbs in exchange for Hezbollah halting its attacks against Israel, according to the Lebanese embassy in Washington.  The arrangement is contingent on a full ceasefire across Lebanon and the withdrawal of Israeli troops.

articles.title: Who was Dave Fiji? Indian-origin pilot killed in helicopter crash in Georgia hours after marrying long-time partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dave Fiji, an Indian-origin pilot with Delta Air Lines, was killed in a helicopter crash near Dawsonville, Georgia, shortly after his wedding ceremony. The couple boarded the Robinson R66 helicopter for a post-wedding send-off and the aircraft crashed during takeoff, killing both the pilot and Fiji.  Jesni, Fiji's long-time partner, survived the crash with injuries and is recovering in hospital. The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the accident.

articles.title: Lactose Intolerance Patches Enter the Market, But Do They Really Work?
articles.rephrased_article: A new company has launched wearable transdermal lactose relief patches, claiming to help people enjoy dairy products without experiencing symptoms.  Dr Aravinda S N, Lead Consultant – Internal Medicine at Aster RV Hospital, Bangalore, cautions that while some users report feeling better, there is limited scientific evidence supporting the effectiveness of these patches and they may not be suitable for everyone. Dr Aravinda suggests consulting a healthcare professional before using them and emphasizes that they are not a substitute for proven treatments like lactase enzyme supplements or dietary changes.

articles.title: Trump needs this war to end but Iran is not backing down
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Iran are engaged in a tense standoff, with neither side willing to return to war despite the ceasefire.  The US maintains its military presence near Iran while Iran continues to assert its resolve and demands concessions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The situation is further complicated by disagreements within the US government regarding potential concessions to Iran. Qatar, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are all working towards a diplomatic solution, but progress remains elusive.  The ongoing tension has significant global economic implications.

articles.title: The silken voice of Hindi cinema falls silent - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suman Kalyanpur, a renowned singer, passed away in Mumbai on May 31, 2026, after a brief illness.  Born in Dhaka in 1937, she began her career singing Noor Jehan songs and later gained recognition for her collaborations with legendary musicians like Mohd Rafi and Talat Mahmood. Her soft-spoken nature and understated expressions made her voice unique, earning her comparisons to Lata Mangeshkar, but ultimately establishing a distinct style that resonated across generations.  Kalyanpur's legacy is marked by her contributions to Hindi film music, particularly in the golden age of the industry, where she sang in around 100 films and became known for her intimate vocal delivery and emotional depth.

articles.title: Iran warns Israeli attacks in Lebanon threaten ceasefire with US
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has warned that Israeli attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon could threaten the ceasefire agreement with the US.  Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, stated that any violation of the ceasefire would affect all fronts. Donald Trump confirmed ongoing talks with both Israel and Hezbollah, while Netanyahu insisted on Israeli strikes against Hezbollah targets in response to attacks. The Lebanese president's office reported Hezbollah's acceptance of a US proposal for a mutual cessation of attacks, but tensions remain high between the US and Iran.  The ceasefire agreement, which came into force on April 8th, has failed to end the fighting.

articles.title: Kaynes shares plunge 43% from October peak. Is a tactical rebound on the cards or more pain ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Anand James, Chief Market Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, suggests a potential short-term downward trend in the Nifty, with support levels around 26,085–26,065.  The IT sector is expected to continue its upward momentum, potentially reaching 39,500, while PSU banks may experience a pullback early next week. COFORGE and ABCAPITAL are recommended as potential buy opportunities with targets of 2,080-2180 and 368-377 respectively.

articles.title: FPIs pull out Rs 27,000 cr in May; 2026 outflows hit Rs 2.2 lakh cr-mark - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have withdrawn a record Rs 2.2 lakh crore from the Indian equity market in 2026, exceeding the total outflows of Rs 1.66 lakh crore in 2025.  Himanshu Srivastava, Principal - Manager Research at Morningstar Investment Research India, attributed this trend to global growth uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and volatility in crude oil prices, which have dampened risk appetite towards emerging markets. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, highlighted the impact of sustained FPI selling on the rupee's depreciation, potentially reaching 96 to the US dollar.  He also noted that capital flows into AI-focused companies are diverting funds away from India.

articles.title: There is a leadership vacuum in Infosys, time to get Nandan Nilekani back: Mohandas Pai - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mohandas Pai, former Infosys Board Member, believes the recent high-profile exits are a result of leadership vacuum and poor chemistry within the company. He suggests that the board needs to address this issue by appointing a new CEO with experience in enterprise management and fostering a strong connection between Nandan Nilekani, the executive chairman, and the next generation of leaders.  Pai also believes that some bloodletting is necessary for the company's future success and that external expertise may be needed.

articles.title: Our commitment for press freedom, and autonomy of public broadcast is absolute: Prakash Javadekar - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Minister of state (independent charge) for information and broadcasting, environment and climate change, Prakash Javadekar, has outlined the government's approach to communication and media. The new I&B ministry will establish a social media hub to manage all ministers' social media outreach, including Facebook, Twitter, and other platforms.  The ministry aims to enhance transparency, effectiveness, and accessibility within the government's communications strategy.  Javadekar also emphasized the importance of public broadcaster autonomy while addressing concerns about potential media control. He highlighted the need for synergy between ministries and a focus on learning from the new government's approach to communication.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Centralized control of ministers' social media raises concerns about censorship and propaganda.

articles.title: Raamdeo Agarwal: We may see rapid growth over the next few years: Raamdeo Agrawal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Raamdeo Agrawal, Joint Managing Director of Motilal Oswal Financial Services, believes the Indian economy is poised for a multi-year bull run due to a new government with clear mandates and potential for strong economic growth. He acknowledges that while there are challenges, such as inflation and supply chain issues, the market has yet to fully price in the positive changes brought about by the new government.  Agrawal suggests investors should focus on companies with solid fundamentals and avoid low-quality stocks, emphasizing patience and long-term investment strategies for potential gains.

articles.title: Confidence level of industry improving: KV Kamath, ICICI Bank - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: KV Kamath, Chairman of ICICI Bank, believes the Indian economy will see growth in the first term of the current government. He anticipates a fiscal discipline approach in the upcoming budget and sees corporate investment picking up within three to six months. Kamath also expects a positive impact from reforms addressing stalled projects and monetary policy adjustments driven by fiscal discipline.  He predicts that interest rates could begin to decline within the next 12 months, potentially starting with a quarter percentage point reduction in the first half of the year.

articles.title: Narendra Modi has his eyes set on boosting business: Joao Cravinho, EU Ambassador - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ambassador Joao Cravinho, head of the European Union delegation in India, met with Narendra Modi during his time as Gujarat Chief Minister.  He believes that the new Prime Minister has a clear vision for India and governance, and that EU member states have the potential to drive economic growth in India. The EU is already the largest trading partner and source of foreign direct investment for India. Cravinho expressed confidence that the FTA negotiations will benefit India and hopes for progress before the next India-EU Summit at Brussels.

articles.title: Every decision of government needn’t be a big reform: Anand Mahindra - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Anand Mahindra, chairman and MD of Mahindra & Mahindra, expressed optimism about the new Indian government's 10-point agenda, particularly its focus on empowering bureaucrats. He believes this will address bureaucratic paralysis and create a more inclusive economy.  Narendra Modi's leadership has been lauded by business leaders for his clear vision and commitment to economic growth. Mahindra & Mahindra remains committed to investing in India despite economic downturns, citing the company's long-term perspective on the market. The company is also confident in its ability to capitalize on opportunities in defense and infrastructure development.  The US administration is urged to rebuild a strong relationship with India as it seeks to enhance its global role.

articles.title: Worried Amitabh Bachchan fans pray to Lord Shiva for his recovery - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Amitabh Bachchan fans in Kolkata performed a yagna today to pray for his speedy recovery.  The event, held at Ekdaliya Evergreen Park, was attended by hundreds of fans who have been worried about the actor's health since he underwent abdominal surgery on February 11th. Banerjee, from the Amitabh Bachchan Fans Association of Kolkata, stated that they have been monitoring media reports and praying for his well-being.  Fans believe his "workaholic nature" contributed to his medical condition, and are planning a celebratory event upon his return home.

articles.title: Documents reveal contents of the first telegraph message between India & England - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Newly discovered documents reveal the first telegraph messages sent from Porthcurno, England to Mumbai on June 23, 1870, marking a technological breakthrough in communication between Britain and its former colonies.  The Managing Director in London and the Manager in Bombay exchanged messages via undersea cables laid by the British Indian Submarine Telegraph Company. The first message was "How are you all?", which received a reply of "All well". This marked the beginning of a revolution that connected the world through telegraphy, with Porthcurno serving as a hub for international cable communications from 1870 to 1970 and later becoming a training college for the communications industry.  The museum, now housing rare equipment and details of the history of telegraph, has received millions in funding to develop an international education program that includes community groups in India.

articles.title: India Meteorological Department to use dynamic models for forecasts - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: M Rajeevan, of the National Atmospheric Research Laboratory, highlighted the need for improved monsoon prediction models in light of the 2009 drought.  He noted that state-of-the-art coupled ocean atmospheric models have shown improvement in predicting interannual variability of Indian summer monsoon rainfall. Michel Jarraud, secretary general of the World Meteorological Organisation, emphasized the importance of global data, supercomputers, and translating scientific progress into practical applications for better weather forecasting.

articles.title: Kenya Protest: 'This will expose our people to Ebola': Big protest in Kenya against quarantine centre for affected US citizens - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of youths protested in Nanyuki, Kenya, against plans to establish an Ebola quarantine center at Laikipia Air Base. The demonstration followed a court order suspending the facility's establishment and halting the arrival of foreign patients pending a case filed by local legal groups. Kenya’s Health Minister Aden Duale stated the center was intended for everyone, not exclusively US nationals, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged $13.5 million in support.  Local leaders, including Laikipia Governor Joshua Irungu, voiced opposition to the facility due to potential exposure risks to local residents.

articles.title: Delhi HC recognises ‘right to be forgotten’, lays down framework for de-indexing judicial records - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court ruled that the "right to be forgotten" exists under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, granting individuals the right to have personal information removed from public digital accessibility. The court established a framework for de-indexing judicial records and masking personal identifiers from publicly accessible court records, ruling that such information should not indefinitely link individuals to past legal proceedings, especially when they are acquitted or proceedings have ended.  The court emphasized the importance of open justice while acknowledging exceptions in cases involving convictions for serious offenses.

articles.title: Harvard scientists create synthetic cells from scratch and witness Darwinian evolution in real time | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from Harvard University have created self-reproducing cells using only non-living chemicals, a breakthrough that could revolutionize our understanding of abiogenesis.  The research team irradiated a homogeneous solution of substances with green light, resulting in vesicle-like structures similar to primitive cells that underwent development, reorganization, and reproduction autonomously. This finding suggests that life may not require complex biological components to evolve, potentially paving the way for artificial life forms and expanding our search for extraterrestrial life.  The study's implications extend beyond Earth, offering a potential pathway for understanding how simple chemical systems could transition into living organisms.

articles.title: LK Advani's 'gift' makes its way to State Department exhibition hall - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The US Secretary of State Colin Powell's gift from the then Indian Home Minister, Lal Krishna Advani, a cloisonne elephant figurine made by Indian artist Neeru Goel, has been selected for display at the State Department exhibition hall.  The elephant, representing India's cultural iconography of elephants as symbols of wealth, wisdom, and strength, is one of fewer than 50 gifts received by Powell over the years. The State Department described the figurine, which depicts a man riding in an elephant howdah, as reflecting the historical significance of elephants in Indian life for transportation, warfare, land protection, and forest traversal.

articles.title: Jill Biden says she was shocked after Kamala Harris lost to Trump, 'You were?' asks interviewer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jill Biden stated in a new interview that she was certain Kamala Harris would win the 2024 election and beat Donald Trump, but was shocked when it did not happen. In her memoir, "Views from the East Wing," released tomorrow, Biden describes witnessing President Joe Biden's struggles during the presidential debate and expressing concerns about his health. She also recounts leaving notes for her husband, including encouraging messages and critiques of foreign policy decisions.

articles.title: CMRL appeal against ED probe: HC directs status quo till June 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court has ordered the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to maintain the status quo in the pay-off case involving Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd. (CMRL) and Exalogic Solutions. The court will rule on Friday, June 5th, after CMRL appealed a single bench order dismissing its plea to quash the ED's investigation into alleged misappropriation of public funds.  The ED has agreed to refrain from taking any further action until then.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of power and suppression of justice are at play.

articles.title: Delhi World Book fair: A fair like no other - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The 20th edition of the World Book Fair (WBF) in Delhi is a mammoth affair, attracting over 800,000 visitors and featuring over 1,300 exhibitors. While no reliable business statistics are available, organizers estimate the fair's turnover to be over Rs 30 crore, exceeding the revenue of leading bookstores in India. The fair, which moved from its traditional January end date to early February, aims to boost India's rights business and provide a direct interface between publishers and readers. Despite concerns about timing impacting library budgets and school exams, the WBF remains relevant as it offers a unique opportunity for discovery and browsing.

articles.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke interview: "We will continue to use every constitutional means available to make our voices heard" - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), announced plans to return to India on June 6th and stage a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.  Dipke stated that CJP will continue using satire and other means to advocate for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, after the party's petition demanding his resignation received over eight lakh signatures.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Marie Antoinette: “When everyone else is losing their heads, it is important to…” — what this quote reveals about calmness, leadership, emotional control, decision-making, and why staying composed can become your greatest strength | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The quote attributed to Marie Antoinette, "When everyone else is losing their heads, it is important to keep yours," highlights the importance of remaining calm during times of stress and uncertainty.  While emotions are natural responses to challenging situations, history shows that individuals who maintain composure often find solutions while those overwhelmed by emotion make poor decisions. This quote emphasizes the value of clear thinking over impulsive reactions, particularly in moments when others become anxious or panicked.

articles.title: After the Oscars, what's next for silent stars of The Artist? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The team behind the Oscar-winning film "The Artist" - including director Michel Hazanavicius, producer Thomas Langmann, and actor Jean Dujardin - are likely to be facing a whirlwind of opportunities after their big win. Having celebrated at various parties, they will now need to decide how to best leverage their newfound success.  As with many Oscar winners, the team can secure significant paydays through back-end earnings from the film's box office performance and by capitalizing on their current status.

articles.title: 'I truly supported it': Jill Biden admits she wanted Joe Biden to pardon Hunter, feared Trump would target their family - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jill Biden stated that she supported her husband Joe Biden's decision to pardon their son, Hunter Biden, due to the perceived unfairness of the legal process following Donald Trump's election. She believes the Justice Department changed after Trump's victory and that they would have targeted Hunter.  She acknowledged wanting him to pardon Hunter at the time and agreed with her husband's decision.

articles.title: Air Marshal Tarun Chaudhry assumes charge as Chief of Central Air Command - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Air Marshal Tarun Chaudhry assumed command of the Indian Air Force’s Central Air Command on June 1, 2026. A decorated officer with extensive experience in various roles within the IAF, including serving as Defence Attaché at the Embassy of India in Sweden, he brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise to his new position. He succeeds Air Marshal Balakrishnan Manikantan, who retired after 40 years of service.

articles.title: First Indian-American woman to take a company public in US says returning to India was not an option at her time - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vinita Gupta, the first Indian woman to take her company public in the US, believes India has become a more attractive destination for tech professionals.  She suggests that while opportunities are emerging in India, Silicon Valley's focus on individual talent and global inclusivity makes it an ideal place for those seeking career advancement. Gupta emphasizes that the US remains a welcoming environment despite recent challenges faced by Indian-Americans due to political climate and economic concerns.

articles.title: HC orders inquiry into amassing of ₹800 crore of Chettinad family money by educationist Meena Muthiah’s employee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court has ordered a police inquiry into the death of K.T.R. Raja Karuppan Chetty, an employee of educationist and philanthropist Meena Muthiah who passed away in May 2026. The court's order was prompted by a complaint alleging that Mr. Chetty misappropriated ₹800 crore belonging to the Chettinad family through his close relationship with Ms. Muthiah.  The inquiry, which must conclude swiftly due to the deceased's role as secretary of Kumara Rajah Muthiah School of Traditional Arts & Crafts, is expected to investigate allegations of criminal conspiracy, forgery, and financial mismanagement.

articles.title: Managing data - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Debasish Maitra, a professor at IRMA, Anand, argues that India needs a centralized database system to improve data consistency across ministries and departments. articles.title: First Indian-American woman to take a company public in US says returning to India was not an option at her time - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vinita Gupta, the first woman of Indian origin to take her company public in the US, believes that India has become prosperous enough for skilled engineers to find good jobs there.  She suggests that while new opportunities exist in India, Silicon Valley's focus on individual talent and global inclusivity makes it a valuable destination for tech professionals. Gupta, who came to the US in 1974 after completing her education in India, believes that the US remains an egalitarian environment where individuals can thrive regardless of their origin or background.

articles.title: Colourful welcome marks new academic year in schools across Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anoop Jacob, Minister for Food and Civil Supplies, inaugurated the district-level ‘Praveshanolsavam’ at Government Higher Secondary School in Ernakulam. Jacob emphasized the importance of basic infrastructure for schools to encourage enrollment.  He also highlighted the government's commitment to modernizing primary schools through CSR schemes. Mathew Kuzhalnadan, MLA, presided over the event. K.G. Radhakrishnan, Ernakulam district panchayat president, delivered the keynote address.

articles.title: Therapy donkeys are helping psychiatric patients heal at a hospital on outskirts of Paris - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ville-Evrard hospital in Neuilly-sur-Marne, France, is utilizing animal-assisted therapy with donkeys to help patients manage mental health conditions.  Patients engage in activities like grooming and caring for the animals, which they say helps reduce isolation and improve emotional regulation. The program, launched in 2016 and formally recognized as a healthcare service in 2022, has expanded beyond donkeys to include other animals such as guinea pigs, chickens, goats, turtles, and rabbits.

articles.title: Close call as roof of building on school campus in Kerala capital collapses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A roof collapse at the Samagra Shiksha Kerala (SSK) district project office on the campus of Central High School in Thiruvananthapuram caused damage but no injuries on Pravesanotsavam day.  N. Samsudheen, Minister for General Education, stated that permission for work on the roof should have been obtained due to the office's function, and a report is being sought from the Deputy Director of Education (DDE). Chempazhanthy Udayan, chairperson of the Corporation Education standing committee, said the school was 100 meters away and a fitness certificate could have been obtained.

articles.title: Serena Williams is returning to pro tennis at age 44 after nearly 4 years away from the sport
articles.rephrased_article: Serena Williams, a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion, is returning to professional tennis after nearly four years away. She accepted a wild card invitation to play doubles at the upcoming Queen’s Club tournament in London. Martina Navratilova, the previous oldest former No. 1 to launch a comeback, expressed excitement over Williams' return and its potential to inspire younger players.  Naomi Osaka also expressed anticipation for Williams' return to the court. The WTA Tour welcomed Williams back and highlighted her legacy as one of the greatest athletes of all time.

articles.title: Indian box office marks 15% jump to hit Rs 4,219 crore as early 2026 outshines a dull 2025 | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian box office experienced a 15% increase from January to April, reaching Rs 4,219 crore.  Dharandhar: The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh, emerged as the top performer during this period, grossing Rs 1,275 crore.  Malayalam cinema saw its share of the box office grow significantly in April, doubling from January-March to 8%.  While April's collections were lower than previous months, films like Bhooth Bangla and Vaazha 2 contributed significantly to the total gross.   The top 10 grossing films of 2026 include Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Border 2, Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu,  Bhooth Bangla, The RajaSaab, Vaazha 2, and others.

articles.title: 388 cells on 2 floors, this cemetery beats the space crunch in Vallakkunnu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The St. Alphonsa’s Church in Vallakkunnu, Kerala, has opened a unique two-storey cemetery that stands out from traditional burial grounds. The 388 burial cells within the covered facility allow mourners to participate in ceremonies regardless of weather conditions. Designed by architect Manosh Thomas, the structure efficiently utilizes space while addressing environmental concerns.  The project cost ₹1.75 crore and has attracted attention from both parishioners and outsiders.

articles.title: Bid to ‘sell’ train seat: Surat court reduces railway porter’s jail term from 1 month to 2 days | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: An additional sessions court in Surat reduced the jail sentence of Raghu Dayma, a railway porter convicted for illegally selling a train seat, from one month to two days. The court also increased the fine amount from Rs 500 to Rs 1,500.  The court's decision came after an appeal filed by Dayma, who was initially sentenced by the Judicial Magistrate First Class (Railways) court in Surat. Kamal Saiyed, a senior correspondent for The Indian Express, reported on the case and provided context about the court proceedings.

articles.title: Managing data - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Debasish Maitra, a professor at IRMA, Anand, argues that a centralized database system is crucial for improving the consistency of employment data in India. He believes this would enhance access and efficiency for policymakers and diverse groups of people.

articles.rephrased_article: Kerala is facing a controversy over its "Vande Mataram" song usage, while India's National Eligibility Entrance Test-Undergraduate (NEET-UG) reforms have been announced. articles.title: Hooch deaths: 4 Pune Rural cops suspended for being in contact with key accused | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Following the tragic deaths linked to methanol-laced illicit liquor, the Pune Rural police suspended four constables who were allegedly in contact with key accused Radheshyam Prajapati.  The investigation into the incident is being handled by the Maharashtra CID and has resulted in the arrest of several suspects, including Karnelsingh Virka, his son Gurmangatsingh, Yogesh Ramchandra Vhankade (alias Sikandar Rathod), Radheshyam Prajapati, and Kalpesh Agrawal.  The state excise department has also registered three cases related to this incident. The investigation is ongoing, with authorities examining potential links between the deaths and other reported incidents of methanol-laced liquor consumption.

articles.title: Watch: Iran suspends talks as Israel widens Lebanon offensive | Above the Fold | 01.06.2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: West Bengal's cabinet expansion is a major news story, alongside ongoing Israel-Lebanon tensions and the hostage crisis in Manipur.  Key changes to UPI and LPG distribution are also being discussed. Additionally, the start of SIR enumeration in four states and actor-turned-politician Vijay's first public address have garnered attention.

articles.title: Trinamool MLAs facing threats, not being allowed to attend party meetings: Mamata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, chairperson of the Trinamool Congress, accused the police and local BJP officials of threatening her party's MLAs, preventing them from attending meetings. She claimed these threats included calls to break the party and false cases under the Arms Act.  Banerjee also alleged that many party leaders were pressured into silence due to fear. The meeting called by Sobhandeb Chatterjee, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, was cancelled after only 20 of the 80 MLAs attended.  Agnimitra Paul, BJP Minister, stated that the Trinamool's lack of ideological base led to its decline.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of threats and intimidation against elected officials raise serious concerns about democratic processes.

articles.title: Kangana Ranaut recalls her mother’s harsh words after Gangster: ‘Our society won’t accept’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Kangana Ranaut recalled her parents' initial disapproval of her acting career, stemming from their conservative upbringing and negative perceptions of the film industry.  During a recent interview, she explained that her family viewed films negatively, leading to resistance when she first entered the field. Ranaut emphasized that while awards and recognition have helped bridge the gap between her family and her chosen profession, her decisions were ultimately driven by personal values and a desire to earn respect for herself and her convictions.

articles.title: ‘She has kept the best room for herself’: Inside Harsh Beniwal’s lavish family home in Delhi | Art-and-culture News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Farah Khan, Harsh Beniwal, and his family welcomed Farah Khan into their Delhi home for a video tour. The home features warm neutral tones, curved seating, layered lighting, and natural light, creating a comfortable and inviting atmosphere.  The space reflects Harsh's personality and career journey, with a gaming room that he rarely uses due to his focus on family time. Athul Raj, a counselling psychologist, emphasizes the impact of home environments on emotional health, suggesting personalized spaces like cozy corners and quiet lounges can reduce mental fatigue and provide emotional relief.

articles.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy accuses his Maharashtra counterpart of showing callous apathy towards Tummidihatti barrage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy accused Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis of being apathetic to his requests for talks regarding the construction of the proposed Tummidihatti barrage in Telangana's Adilabad district.  Revanth Reddy demanded that Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy take the initiative to facilitate these talks, warning that farmers would erupt in anger if the project is not completed. He also asserted that the state government was committed to purchasing all procured paddy and maize by June 15th or face consequences, including dumping the grains in front of BJP leaders' houses.

articles.title: NSE pre-IPO window to close soon with filing weeks away. Can buying unlisted shares now make you good money? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NSE, India's largest stock exchange, continues to attract interest due to its upcoming IPO. Analysts caution that investors should not solely rely on the approaching DRHP filing as a guarantee for quick profits, as valuation and entry price remain key considerations. While NSE enjoys strong profitability and market dominance, its current unlisted share price already reflects significant optimism around the listing. Experts emphasize focusing on valuation, offer pricing, market conditions, and the final IPO structure rather than rushing to buy shares based solely on the DRHP filing's proximity.

articles.title: Twelve years of dedication, a legacy of achievement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi received accolades from Norway and Sweden, joining a list of 32 international honors he has been awarded during his 12-year term.  His leadership has been praised for its focus on national development, with achievements including economic reforms, infrastructure projects, and initiatives aimed at empowering women and farmers. The Shiv Sena, a political party within the National Democratic Alliance, continues to support Modi, recognizing his dedication to the nation's progress. Despite facing criticism from the opposition, Modi remains committed to serving the people and has implemented policies that have improved the lives of millions.  His unwavering commitment to India's development and strong leadership style have earned him widespread admiration both domestically and internationally.

articles.title: Norse Atlantic Airways Offers Dirt-Cheap Tickets. There’s a Catch | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Norse Atlantic Airways, a low-cost airline, has faced criticism for its customer service practices. The company relies heavily on AI agents to handle inquiries, but complaints have emerged about the lack of human intervention and potential scams associated with this approach.  Customers report being unable to reach live representatives, encountering fraudulent websites and phone numbers, and facing financial losses after interacting with these systems. While Norse Atlantic Airways claims its AI agent Freya has been successful in managing customer inquiries, many customers have reported difficulties obtaining refunds or resolving issues through the company's automated system.  The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is aware of the complaints and suggests that consumers may consider filing claims with their state attorney general's office for further investigation.

articles.title: Ex-House Help Kalita Majhi Takes Oath As Bengal Minister Of State
articles.rephrased_article: Kalita Majhi, a BJP MLA from Ausgram, was sworn in as Minister of State on Monday.  She joined Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's cabinet, expanding the West Bengal Council of Ministers to 41.  Majhi previously worked as domestic help and had to give up formal education due to financial hardship. She began her political career as a booth-level worker and was elected in the 2021 Assembly elections.

articles.title: Release of 14 abducted Kukis ‘cancelled’ after protests in Manipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The United Naga Council (UNC) cancelled the planned release of 14 Kuki civilians in Manipur on Monday, June 1, 2026, after protests by a section of Nagas. The UNC, which represents Nagas in Manipur, stated that the release was called off due to "prevailing sentiments of the Naga public" following protestors' demands for the simultaneous release of six abducted Nagas.  The hostage crisis began after the killing of three church leaders on May 13th and resulted in a previous exchange of hostages between Kuki and Naga groups.

articles.title: After Water Crisis, Delhi Plans 1,500 Rainwater Harvesting Projects Before Monsoon
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has launched a pre-monsoon rainwater harvesting drive to improve groundwater recharge. The initiative, which will see the construction of 500 new structures and restoration of 1,000 non-functional systems across government buildings by June 30th, aims to capture rainwater that would otherwise flow into drains. Delhi Water Minister Parvesh Verma emphasized the importance of continuous water conservation efforts, highlighting that every drop of rain is a valuable resource. The project is expected to recharge around 733 million liters of water annually and address concerns over declining groundwater levels in the city.

articles.title: Universal Audio Volt 876 USB Audio Interface Review: Pro-Level Polish | WIRED
articles.sentiment_target: Universal Audio Volt 876 USB Audio Interface
articles.rephrased_article: In 2006, the author struggled with audio interface latency and ultimately opted for a delay pedal.  Line 6 and Universal Audio were not yet established in the market. The author's experience highlights the evolution of audio interfaces since then, emphasizing their improved quality, lower prices, and plug-and-play functionality. Modern interfaces have made music production accessible to a wider audience, including those using mobile devices.

articles.title: Accused Dies In Encounter After Assam Attack Leaves 1 Dead, Girl Critical
articles.rephrased_article: Roz Ali, the main accused in the Assam murder case, died during a police operation following his arrest.  The incident occurred after 19-year-old Madhurjya Barman and a 17-year-old girl were attacked while returning home. Madhurjya Barman was associated with the Paschim Nalbari Regional Students' Union, while the injured teenage girl remains under treatment.  The Assam Police are continuing their investigation into the case.

articles.title: Supreme Court gets 5 new judges; strength to go up to 37 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre cleared the appointment of five judges to the Supreme Court, increasing its strength to 37. The appointments, following a recommendation by the Collegium, were approved by President and include Justice Sheel Nagu, Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court; Justice Shree Chandrashekhar, Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court; Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva, Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court; Justice Arun Palli, Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh; and senior advocate V. Mohana. The appointments follow an amendment to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Ordinance, 2026 which increased the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 judges.

articles.title: Why Congress Needs Overhaul In Punjab: Challenges Ahead Of 2027
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) secured a decisive victory in the Punjab local body elections, winning 958 seats and demonstrating strong dominance. The Congress party saw its seat count plummet from 1,399 to just 397, highlighting internal factionalism issues within the party. The BJP gained urban ground, increasing its seats from 49 to 172.  The Akali Dal also experienced a decline in its electoral performance.  The Congress High Command is preparing for significant changes within the Punjab unit, including potential replacements for the state president and leadership positions.

articles.title: ‘She has kept the best room for herself’: Inside Harsh Beniwal’s lavish family home in Delhi | Art-and-culture News - The Indian Express

articles.title: Delhi Records Coolest June Start In 3 Years With Below Normal Temperatures
articles.rephrased_article: The national capital experienced the coolest June 1st in three years, with Safdarjung observatory recording a maximum temperature of 36.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees below seasonal norm.  No rainfall was recorded across five monitoring stations over the past 24 hours. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts temperatures to gradually rise from tomorrow as the current rain activity weakens.

articles.title: Ukraine’s forcibly transferred children must not be a bargaining chip | Child Rights | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia has been accused of forcibly transferring over 20,000 Ukrainian children to its territory since the invasion began in 2014. International investigations have found these transfers were unlawful under international humanitarian law, and despite warrants issued by the International Criminal Court and findings from the European Court of Human Rights, Russia has not returned them. The situation has driven families to desperate measures, including risky missions by NGOs like Save Ukraine.  The Ukrainian government, along with international partners, are working to establish a comprehensive tracing mechanism, intensify legal efforts against Russian officials, and fully implement sanctions on Russia.

articles.title: ‘Old enough to pull trigger’: Delhi teen dies 4 days after being shot, family demands minor accused be tried as adult | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A 17-year-old boy, who was shot in the head outside a Delhi eatery on May 27th while with a friend, died from his injuries on Monday. The victim's family demanded that one of the accused, a 16-year-old juvenile, be tried as an adult.  The Delhi Police Crime Branch is investigating the case and is expected to add murder charges to the existing FIR. Two other suspects, aged 18 and 24, were arrested for the murder. An automatic pistol was recovered from the juvenile's possession.

articles.title: Doctors in Kochi perform heart transplant on 48-year-old Malappuram native - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Aster Medcity in Malappuram successfully performed the first heart transplant at the hospital, giving a 48-year-old man from Malappuram a new lease on life. The procedure involved transplanting a heart harvested from a 23-year-old man who was declared brain-dead following a road accident.  The donor's parents consented to the donation of four organs, with the liver going to Baby Memorial Hospital, Kozhikode, and the kidneys allocated to Aster MIMS, Kozhikode, and Government Medical College Hospital, Kozhikode. The recipient had suffered a massive anterior wall myocardial infarction and required multiple blood pressure support medications and an intra-aortic balloon pump for cardiac stabilization.

articles.title: How the world failed Ryan and Yaman | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Israeli strike killed two Palestinian children, Ryan and Yaman An, in Gaza City on January 2024. The mother of the children, who lost both her sons in the attack, describes their deaths as a part of a larger pattern of violence against Palestinian children. She notes that despite international laws and organizations dedicated to protecting children, these tragedies continue to occur.  The mother mourns the loss of her children and expresses frustration at the world's lack of action to prevent such atrocities.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights the ongoing, systemic harm to Palestinian children, a grave injustice.

articles.title: Hungary’s Magyar to amend the constitution to remove President Tamas Sulyok | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hungary’s Prime Minister Peter Magyar has promised to amend the constitution to remove President Tamas Sulyok, who he accuses of being a puppet of former Prime Minister Viktor Orban. Sulyok has refused to resign despite Magyar's deadline and claims that the president is obstructing the new government's plans by refusing to act on issues like dehumanizing statements made by Orban and legislation banning an LGBTQ pride event.  The process will take about a month, according to Magyar, who said he would inform lawmakers of his legislative proposals today.

articles.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea over non-compliance with disability panels’ recommendations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court issued notice on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition alleging widespread non-compliance with disability commission recommendations, reducing disability rights to "illusory promises." The petition, filed by lawyer and disability rights activist Shashank Pandey, argued that authorities rarely comply with the recommendations of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (CCPD), despite having the power to do so under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (RPwD) 2016.  The court asked the Union Government to respond and directed a response by July 21, 2026.

articles.title: us iran war strait of hormuz blockade how ships are bypassing iran attacks with us help as us iran negotiations continue
articles.rephrased_article: US forces have facilitated the passage of at least 70 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz over the past three weeks, helping them avoid detection by turning off transponders. This assistance comes as negotiations between US and Iran remain stalled amid ongoing conflict concerns. While the US Central Command continues to communicate with commercial ships seeking safe transit, Iran has suspended talks with US officials, citing attacks on Lebanon and a desire to block the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: ‘Spoiled insulin’: Sudan war disrupts drug supplies, fuelling smuggling | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing conflict in Sudan has crippled the country's healthcare infrastructure, leading to shortages of essential medicines and a surge in smuggling networks.  Sudan is facing its largest humanitarian crisis, with millions lacking basic healthcare services. The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that 40 percent of health facilities nationwide are nonoperational, while hospitals and pharmacies have been looted and destroyed by armed groups.  The conflict has also disrupted pharmaceutical production, forcing patients to rely on smuggled medicines often contaminated or expired, posing a serious threat to public health.

articles.title: ‘Make in Haryana’ Industrial Policy eyes future-ready industries with AI-driven ecosystem | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini launched the 'Make in Haryana' Industrial Policy, aiming to attract Rs 5 lakh crore in investments and position the state as a powerhouse for future-ready manufacturing. The policy focuses on data centers, GCCs, AI-driven investment facilitation, and emerging technologies. Rao Narbir Singh, the Industries and Commerce Minister, emphasized the need for speed and trust in attracting global investors.  Anant Raj Limited signed an MoU with the Haryana government to invest ₹20,000 crore in data center infrastructure, while other companies like Reliance MET City and India Cellular and Electronics Association (ICEA) also pledged investments.

articles.title: India, Myanmar Vow Deeper Ties On Security, Trade And Connectivity
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Myanmar President U Min Aung Hlaing met in New Delhi, where they pledged deeper cooperation in security, trade, and infrastructure.  Modi positioned Myanmar as a key partner in India's foreign policy initiatives, including Neighbourhood First, Act East, and MAHASAGAR. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also emphasizing the importance of preventing misuse of sovereign territory for activities threatening national security. The visit included discussions on connectivity projects like the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport project and the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, as well as trade facilitation and people-to-people initiatives.  Modi announced an expansion of scholarships for Myanmar students, while Min Aung Hlaing offered prayers at Buddhist sites in Bodh Gaya.

articles.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea over non-compliance with disability panels’ recommendations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court issued notice on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition alleging widespread non-compliance with disability commission recommendations, reducing disability rights to "illusory promises." The plea, filed by lawyer and disability rights activist Shashank Pandey, highlighted that despite the power granted to disability commissions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (RPwD), 2016, authorities rarely comply with their recommendations.  The court directed the Union Government to respond on July 21, 2026. The petition also requested directions for effective enforcement mechanisms and an independent audit of disability commission offices.

articles.title: Bengal Cabinet Expansion: Meet 35 New Faces In Suvendu Adhikari's Government
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari expanded his West Bengal government on Monday, inducting 35 ministers. The expansion includes 13 Cabinet Ministers, three Ministers of State (Independent Charge), and 19 Ministers of State, reflecting the BJP's commitment to regional, social, and community representation.  The new cabinet members represent a mix of experienced legislators, former parliamentarians, professionals, and first-time ministers. This move is seen as an effort to strengthen governance while accommodating diverse perspectives across the state.

articles.title: Egypt’s new monorail offers a modern ride, but Cairo is still not convinced | Inequality News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cairo’s new East Nile monorail opened to the public in May, offering a modern and efficient transit experience. The 56.6km line connects central Cairo with the New Administrative Capital, aiming to alleviate traffic congestion. While passengers praise its cleanliness, comfort, and speed, concerns remain about affordability.  The fare structure is tiered, with prices ranging from 20 pounds for up to five stations to 80 pounds for the full route. The project's cost of $2.8 billion was funded by partnerships between Alstom, Arab Contractors, Orascom, and Siemens.  However, many commuters find the fares unaffordable given their limited incomes. Experts suggest that the monorail is a necessary infrastructure investment for new city development but acknowledges the need to ensure accessibility for all socioeconomic groups.

articles.title: I came to know about my brother’s death only through Google search: Himachal Pradesh accident victim’s sister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jayanthashree G., sister of accident victim Karthigeyan P.G., discovered her brother's death through his YouTube search history and news reports on Google after their taxi plunged into a 500-meter deep gorge in Himachal Pradesh. The incident occurred on May 29 while the families were traveling to Dalhousie for a National Taekwondo Competition.  Karthigeyan, who ran a food catering business, was accompanied by his wife Manimala, and their son Nandan.  The accident claimed the lives of seven people, including Karthigeyan's family and other passengers.

articles.title: Chinese Firm Develops Technology That Uses AI To Predict Future Protestors
articles.rephrased_article: Geedge Networks, a Chinese company, is developing AI technology that analyzes location data and internet usage to predict potential government dissenters in China.  Leaked documents reveal the software generates profiles of citizens and uses AI to identify individuals who may criticize the government. Vanderbilt researchers warn that this technology, if unchecked, could lead to widespread surveillance and control over citizens. This development raises concerns about the ethical implications of using AI for mass surveillance and censorship.

articles.title: Indian PM Modi meets Myanmar military gov’t leader in New Delhi | Narendra Modi News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Myanmar’s military leader Min Aung Hlaing in New Delhi, despite criticism from opposition groups.  India stated its policy is not intended to comment on the internal political arrangements in Myanmar and believes engagement is the best way forward. During their meeting, the leaders discussed trade, defense, security cooperation, border management, and regional issues. India and Myanmar also agreed to deepen collaboration across sectors, including trade, energy, and critical minerals, as well as accelerate major connectivity projects.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Meeting with a military junta accused of human rights abuses is concerning.

articles.title: Ukraine Russia Drone War, Pentagon, Trump: $54 Billion Drone Swarm: Pentagon's Plan To Flood Skies With Flying Bombs
articles.rephrased_article: The US military is seeking low-cost combat drones from startups, aiming to rapidly expand its drone capabilities.  A competition called "Drone Dominance" has been launched with a $1.1 billion budget to identify promising manufacturers. The Pentagon is prioritizing innovation and speed over traditional defense contractors, as seen in the selection of companies like Neros, founded by former drone racer Soren Monroe-Anderson, and Skycutter.  The competition aims to develop expendable drones designed for high-speed maneuvers and precision strikes.

articles.title: ‘Make in Haryana’ Industrial Policy eyes future-ready industries with AI-driven ecosystem | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini launched the ‘Make in Haryana’ Industrial Policy, aiming to attract Rs 5 lakh crore in investments and position the state as a hub for future-ready industries. The policy focuses on data centers, global capability centers (GCCs), mega industrial parks, and next-generation technology, with incentives including capital subsidies, R&D support, tax benefits, and sustainability subsidies.  The government also unveiled a revamped “Single Window 2.0” system and a new logo for the state's upcoming Global Investors Summit.  Major companies like National Australia Bank (NAB) and Reliance MET City have pledged investments in the state.

articles.title: China: Fans break glass door trying to see TV star
articles.rephrased_article: Fans at a shopping center in Nanning, China, broke glass doors to get a glimpse of actor Zhang Linghe, who was scheduled to attend an eyewear event. The event was canceled and moved online after the incident, with organizers apologizing for any inconvenience caused.  The actor's studio stated they would reimburse travel and accommodation costs for fans who traveled from afar. Molsion also promised to upgrade safety measures for future events.

articles.title: As Israel pushes past the Litani, Lebanese question the purpose of UNIFIL | Israel attacks Lebanon | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has advanced deeper into Lebanese territory than at any point since its withdrawal in 2000, prompting questions about the effectiveness of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL).  The UN body's mandate ends on December 31, 2026, and its inability to prevent the invasion has led to criticism from both sides. The situation is further complicated by ongoing Israeli attacks and Hezbollah's retaliatory actions. Despite calls for a continued peacekeeping presence, financial cuts have reduced UNIFIL's force size, leaving many concerned about the future of peace in southern Lebanon.

articles.title: I came to know about my brother’s death only through Google search: Himachal Pradesh accident victim’s sister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jayanthashree G., sister of Karthigeyan P.G., discovered the tragic accident that claimed her brother's life through his YouTube search history and news reports on Google. The accident occurred on the Bairgarh-Sach-Pass-Killar Road in Chamba District of Himachal Pradesh when a taxi plunged into a 500-meter deep gorge, killing seven people including Karthigeyan and his family.  The families were traveling from Bengaluru to Dalhousie for their children's participation in a National Taekwondo Competition. Ms. Jayanthashree stated that contacting authorities in Himachal Pradesh was difficult due to lack of information and officials unaware of the accident.

articles.title: Nigeria police warn against reprisal attacks against South Africans
articles.rephrased_article: Nigerian police have issued a warning against reprisal attacks on South African nationals or businesses following recent anti-migrant protests in South Africa. The police urged Nigerians to remain calm and refrain from violence, stating that such actions would only create further crises.  The Nigerian government is addressing the situation at the highest levels, while South African authorities have condemned "criminal acts" against foreign nationals.

articles.title: Iran warns Israeli attacks in Lebanon and Gaza threaten US ceasefire talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran officials, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, have warned that escalating Israeli attacks in Lebanon and Gaza threaten the ongoing ceasefire negotiations with the United States. They demand a halt to all hostilities, including military operations in Lebanon and Gaza, and insist on full withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory. The Iranian government has suspended text exchanges with US counterparts due to continued hostilities.  President Donald Trump, meanwhile, maintains that Iran wants to make a deal and believes the negotiations will ultimately succeed.

articles.title: Infosys, Tech Mahindra, TCS and other IT stocks jump up to 5%. What’s driving the rally? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty IT index surged to 29,905 on Monday, marking a sharp rebound after a recent AI-driven selloff.  Analysts predict a short-term recovery in the sector as investors capitalize on cheap valuations and anticipate continued demand for customized AI tools.  Technical analysts suggest that if the index sustains above its crucial support zone, it could reach 31,280. However, traders should approach the sector cautiously, as a breach below 28,800 could trigger selling pressure. Infosys, TCS, and other major IT companies saw significant gains on Monday.

articles.title: Aegis Logistics shares rally 4% as Q4 profit rises 45% YoY; Board recommends dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Aegis Logistics reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 413 crore for the quarter ended March 2026, marking a significant increase of 45% year-on-year. Revenue from operations surged 52% YoY to Rs 2,594 crore. The company's earnings per share (EPS) also increased to Rs 11.69 from Rs 8.02 in the previous year. Aegis Logistics recommended a final dividend of Rs 6.70 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at its upcoming AGM.  The company's stock has delivered strong returns over the past three years and is currently trading above all eight of its key Simple Moving Averages (SMAs).

articles.title: Q4 earnings review: Motilal Oswal highlights broad-based beat on estimates, lists 6 sectors that exceeded expectations - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Motilal Oswal Financial Services reported that aggregate earnings of companies under its coverage grew 16% year-on-year in the January-March quarter of FY26, exceeding expectations. The brokerage attributed this growth to strong performance in BFSI, metals, and OMCs sectors, while oil & gas lagged behind.  The Nifty 50 delivered 4% YoY growth in net profit, marking a second consecutive year of single-digit growth. Motilal Oswal cut its FY27 earnings estimates for several largecap companies due to factors like SBI, Reliance Industries, and JSW Steel. The brokerage maintains a positive outlook on the Indian market despite volatility stemming from the West Asian crisis, recommending specific sectors and stocks based on their growth potential.

articles.title: Us Iran Tensions: Fragile ceasefire faces fresh test as missiles keep flying as Iran, US trade new blows: Key details - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for targeting a US military base, while the United States Central Command (CENTCOM) responded with strikes on Iranian radar and command-and-control sites.  The incidents followed the reported shootdown of a US MQ-1 drone over international waters, which Iran disputed. The latest escalation raises concerns about the stability of a fragile ceasefire amidst ongoing diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

articles.title: Explained: NSE extends F&O trading by 10 minutes. What changes for traders? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is extending the closing time for equity derivatives trading by 10 minutes to 3:40 pm, starting August 3, 2026. This change aims to align the cash and derivatives markets during the closing process while maintaining consistency in pricing frameworks. The new system will use a "closing auction session" (CAS) where market participants place buy and sell orders to determine a single closing price for eligible securities through an auction-based mechanism.  The CAS will run from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm, replacing the current VWAP-based methodology. The exchange clarified that any future expansion of CAS will be subject to SEBI guidance and separate operational instructions.

articles.title: Green breakthrough: Mouse eyes performed photosynthesis in a remarkable experiment that could transform eye care | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at National University of Singapore have developed a treatment for dry eye disease using specially designed eye drops derived from spinach leaves. The treatment, called LEAF, uses photosynthetic machinery to generate antioxidant molecules that help reduce inflammation and tissue damage.  The study found that mice treated with LEAF showed significantly better tear production and less corneal damage compared to those receiving saline solution. While the treatment does not make eyes green, it could potentially offer a new non-invasive treatment option for dry eye disease in humans if further research proves successful.

articles.title: Meet Argus: The sea-urchin robot with 20 eyes and legs that has rewritten the rules of how a robot should be built | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A team at Duke University's General Robotics Lab has developed an omnidirectional robot named Argus, challenging traditional robotic design principles.  The robot, designed with a dodecahedron geometry and 20 telescoping legs, scores near-perfect on dynamic isotropy, meaning it can move equally well in all directions without needing to face the world in any particular way.  Argus successfully navigated real-world terrains including forests, sand, and wet surfaces, demonstrating its resilience to damage and adaptability to various obstacles. The research suggests that dynamic symmetry could be a viable alternative to traditional biological templates for robot design, paving the way for more agile and robust machines.

articles.title: Uae Fuel Prices: UAE announces June 2026 fuel prices as petrol jumps 8% to Dh3.95 per litre, highest level in nearly 4 years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE Fuel Price Committee announced another increase in petrol prices for June 2026, pushing fuel costs to their highest levels since August 2022.  Super 98 petrol now costs Dh3.95 per litre, up from Dh3.66 in May, while Special 95 and E-Plus 91 have also increased. Vijay Valecha, Chief Investment Officer at Century Financial, stated that physical oil markets remain tight due to shipping restrictions and broader regional security concerns.  The increase comes shortly after the UAE's historic decision to leave OPEC and OPEC+. Analysts are closely watching how future production policies could influence oil markets.

articles.title: The 10 richest people in the world: Elon Musk, Larry Page and Jeff Bezos lead the global wealth race | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The combined wealth of the world's richest people increased to around $2.9 trillion in the past month, driven by a surge in tech stocks and investments in artificial intelligence. Elon Musk, with his holdings in SpaceX and Tesla, remains the wealthiest person globally at $835 billion.  Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Jeff Bezos, Larry Ellison, Michael Dell, Mark Zuckerberg, Jensen Huang, Bernard Arnault, and Steve Ballmer round out the top ten, with their fortunes largely tied to technology companies and digital services.

articles.title: Explained: NSE extends F&O trading by 10 minutes. What changes for traders? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is extending the closing time for equity derivatives trading by 10 minutes to 3:40 pm, starting August 3, 2026. This change will be accompanied by a shift from a "continuous trading close" to an "auction discovered close," with a 20-minute auction session running from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm for securities eligible for the CAS (Closing Auction Session). The new framework aims to ensure smoother transitions between cash and derivatives markets while maintaining consistency in pricing across segments.  The closing price of eligible securities will be determined through an auction process, with existing methodologies for calculating closing prices remaining unchanged for non-eligible securities.

articles.title: London tube strikes set to go ahead unless last-ditch talks deliver breakthrough | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Transport for London (TfL) and the National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers (RMT) are locked in a dispute over pay, working conditions, and staffing levels.  Union officials say workers deserve fair compensation amid rising living costs, while TfL insists it wants to avoid disruption and find a negotiated solution. The RMT has threatened strikes unless their demands are met, raising concerns about widespread disruption for London's transport network. If no agreement is reached, the dispute could lead to further Tube strikes, impacting millions of commuters and travelers across the city.

articles.title: Scientists discover 5.5 million bees living beneath a New York cemetery for over 100 years and it could help save vulnerable pollinators | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cornell University researchers discovered an estimated 5.5 million mining bees living in a hidden underground aggregation beneath East Lawn Cemetery in Ithaca, New York. The discovery highlights the importance of undisturbed habitats for pollinators and could provide valuable insights into conserving vulnerable bee populations facing threats from habitat loss, pesticides, and climate change.  The site may have existed since the early 1900s due to favorable nesting conditions and limited disturbance, offering a rare glimpse into how native bees can thrive in seemingly ordinary locations.

articles.title: Scientists found a hidden signal beneath the Sun and it may change what we know about solar cycles | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A team of scientists led by Professor William J. Chaplin from the University of Birmingham analyzed nearly four decades of data collected by the Birmingham Solar-Oscillations Network (BiSON), a global network that measures oscillations inside the Sun.  Their findings suggest that structural changes occurring in relation to Solar Cycles 22, 23, 24, and 25 are moving deeper into the outer layers of the solar core, indicating a hidden signal beneath the surface. This discovery challenges traditional methods of gauging solar activity by focusing on sunspots and radio flux, suggesting that the Sun's interior may be far more active than previously thought. The study also highlights the potential implications for future solar activity and space weather phenomena.

articles.title: 2 killed in Mumbai-Pune Expressway crash; Missing Link closed briefly | Cities News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Two people died and two others were injured in a truck crash on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway early Monday morning. The Highway Traffic Police reported that the driver lost control of the truck, causing it to collide with a container carrying rice and cooking oil and an Ertiga near Khalapur Food Mall.  The driver and helper of the truck died at the scene, while Lilabai Satse, driving the Ertiga, sustained serious injuries. The injured driver of the container is in stable condition and was taken to hospital. Traffic on the Mumbai-bound section of the Missing Link was shut down for an hour before being reopened with limited lanes by 7 am.

articles.title: Katrina Kaif shares rare photo of son Vihaan, her quiet life with Vicky Kaushal | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Katrina Kaif shared a photo dump on Instagram showcasing her May life with husband Vicky Kaushal and son Vihaan. The photos included moments of family time, outdoor activities, and cozy coffee breaks.  She also shared glimpses of her reading time with Vihaan and a glimpse into her music playlist featuring a Punjabi track. Fans reacted positively to the post, praising Katrina Kaif's long hair and expressing their love for the family.

articles.title: A Maharashtra BJP pick for MLC polls with connection to Pawars: Who is Arun Lakhani? | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Arun Lakhani, a prominent Maharashtra BJP leader and close associate of Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, has been nominated to represent the Wardha-Chandrapur-Gadchiroli Local Authorities constituency in the upcoming June 18 state MLC elections.  Lakhani's nomination has sparked debate due to his lack of local roots within the constituency, but he is a familiar face within the party and known for his work in infrastructure development and social initiatives. His son, Sarang Lakhani, is engaged to NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule’s daughter, Revati, further adding to the political intrigue surrounding his candidacy.

articles.title: Websites Can Now Spy on You Through Your Hard Drive | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta and Yandex were recently caught engaging in privacy-invasive tracking techniques, and now a new method called FROST has emerged. This technique exploits side channels on solid-state drives to monitor website activity and open applications on a visitor's device. The attack relies on measuring the timing of I/O operations within the OPFS (origin private file system) and uses a convolutional neural network to classify these traces, inferring user activity. While FROST requires no interaction from the visitor, its reliance on large OPFS files and limited applicability to devices using separate SSD drives for apps pose limitations.  However, researchers propose browser makers limit the size of such files and shut down the side channel.

articles.title: 61-year-old Kerala man gets appointment letter for government job 18 years after rank list expired | Trending News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Majeed, a 61-year-old resident of Kerala, received an appointment letter for a part-time junior Arabic teacher position from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) after a 18-year delay.  Majeed had taken the PSC examination in 2005 and his name was recommended on a rank list that expired in 2008.
