The vacancy remained unfilled despite multiple recruitment attempts, prompting social media reactions ranging from admiration to criticism of the Indian government system.

articles.title: Audio clip claims Congress leader Zameer Ahmed helped SDPI candidate in Karnataka bypoll | Cities News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: An audio clip of a purported conversation between Zameer Ahmed Khan, a Karnataka minister, and Mohammed Siraj, a Congress leader, was leaked. The clip suggests internal sabotage during the Davanagere South bypoll, where Siraj claims the results were a matter of honor for Khan.  Both men deny the authenticity of the audio clip, with Khan alleging it was created using AI tools and Siraj suggesting a conspiracy behind its release. The leaked conversation comes amid speculation about Khan's potential appointment as deputy chief minister and amidst controversy surrounding the bypoll, which saw a significant margin for the BJP candidate.

articles.title: The Painful Truth About Long Covid | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Privacy Center currently offers opt-out options for tracking technologies through its Consent Management Platform, but these may vary depending on location and device. The website uses essential cookies to ensure functionality and personalized user experience, while also employing audience measurement cookies to track site performance and traffic.  These cookies do not store personal information and are used solely for aggregated data analysis.

articles.title: JEE Advanced AIR 1 Shubham Kumar’s recipe for success: Dedication, discipline, consistency | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Vidheesha Kuntamalla, a Senior Correspondent for The Indian Express, is known for her investigative reporting on higher education policy, international student immigration, and academic freedom.  Her work often connects policy decisions with lived realities, highlighting the impact of administrative actions, political pressure, and global shifts on students, faculty, and institutions. Recent articles by Kuntamalla have focused on JNU's legal battles with students and faculty, the challenges faced by Indian students in the US due to immigration policies, and the shrinking academic freedom at South Asian University.

articles.title: Can India's Delivery Workers Escape the Trap of Time-Bound Labour?
articles.rephrased_article: Delivery agents employed by food and grocery platforms in Delhi reported working over 84 hours a week to meet incentive thresholds, despite earning only between Rs 25,000 and Rs 30,000 per month. This practice reflects the pressure of time-bound labor within the competitive platform economy, which is built on maximizing profits through speed and constant availability.  The author argues that this exploitation mirrors historical forms of labor control, such as Taylorism and Fordism, and calls for greater protection for workers in this new digital landscape.

articles.title: France Tanker Seizure: ‘International terrorism’: Russia slams France's seizure of Russian-linked tanker, terms it 'illegal' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia strongly condemned France's detention of a Russian-linked oil tanker, the Tagor, in the Atlantic Ocean, calling it illegal and bordering on international terrorism.  The Kremlin stated that the vessel was being used to circumvent Western sanctions imposed over the Ukraine war. French President Emmanuel Macron announced the seizure of the tanker, which departed from Murmansk and was heading towards Cameroon, with support from Britain and other partners. Authorities in France opened a criminal investigation into the vessel for failing to prove its nationality and refusing to comply with orders.

articles.title: Empty Stomach, Waiter Jobs: An Indian Student's Story Of The Falling Rupee
articles.rephrased_article: Divyam Sharma, an Indian student studying at King's College London, has experienced the impact of a weakening rupee on his daily life.  As the exchange rate between the rupee and pound fluctuates, Sharma highlights how it affects his tuition fees, monthly expenses, and overall financial well-being. He notes that while he is not alone in facing these challenges, the situation is particularly difficult for students who rely heavily on currency conversions. Despite the difficulties, Sharma emphasizes that living abroad has taught him valuable lessons about budgeting and appreciating the city's diverse experiences.

articles.title: The Romance Scammer Who Made a Small Fortune Posing as a WWE Superstar | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Barragán's book, "The Yahoo Boys: Love, Deception, and the Real Lives of Nigeria’s Romance Scammers," details Chibuike's journey from a desperate young man in Lagos to a sophisticated romance scammer.  Chibuike began by impersonating the world champion wrestler Cody Rhodes, using prewritten scripts and fabricated stories to convince a woman named Theresa he was the real deal. He skillfully manipulated her emotions and finances, convincing her to send him hundreds of euros through various excuses like "billing" for travel expenses, medical bills, and even gifts. Over four years, Chibuike scammed Theresa out of 78,000 euros, highlighting the devastating impact of online romance scams on vulnerable individuals.

articles.title: Wildlife study first, tree felling later: Court closes PIL against Rs 5,729-crore Guwahati Ring Road project | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Gauhati High Court closed a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the Rs 5,729-crore Guwahati Ring Road project after the Assam government and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) assured that no trees would be felled in the affected sanctuary area until a detailed wildlife impact study is completed. The court noted a communication from the Wildlife Institute of India indicating the institute's role in assessing the project's impact and recommending mitigation measures.  The study, expected to be completed within 90 days, will guide the execution of the project while ensuring the preservation of the sanctuary's wildlife.

articles.title: 'Stressed, Tired': Why Indian Employees Still Don't Use All Their Leaves
articles.rephrased_article: A new analysis by global payroll and HR platform Deel reveals that Indian employees, despite having generous leave entitlements compared to many Asia-Pacific countries, are among the least likely to use them fully. The data shows that only 17.2% of Indian workers exhausted their annual leave entitlement in 2025, with a median leave taken of just 12 days annually. This trend suggests that while employees may not be avoiding time off altogether, they are more selective about how they use it, often opting for shorter breaks.  Experts attribute this to workplace psychology and cultural factors such as the fear of appearing less committed or concerns about being perceived as replaceable. The analysis highlights the need for employers to address the underlying reasons behind underutilized leave, ensuring a culture that encourages employees to fully disconnect and recharge.

articles.title: Noose, Belt, 80-kg Dummy: CBI Recreates Twisha Sharma's Final Moments, Samarth Singh, Giribala Singh
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) recreated the final moments of Twisha Sharma, a Noida-based actor-model who was found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12.  The investigation involved bringing Samarth Singh, Twisha's husband, and his mother, Giribala Singh, to the scene to understand how she was taken down and how Giribala Singh untied the knot around her neck. The agency also tested the strength of the ligature used to recreate the sequence of events.  The CBI arrested Giribala Singh on Thursday after cancelling her anticipatory bail, and both Samarth Singh and Giribala Singh will be in CBI custody until June 2nd.

articles.title: Mango The Sweet Diplomat, From Mughals To Modern India
articles.rephrased_article: Americans are embracing Kesar mangoes, a popular Indian fruit, after a long-standing ban was lifted in 2006. This trend began with then President George Bush's appreciation for the fruit during a visit to India and has continued through subsequent years of diplomatic exchanges between the two countries.  The tradition of gifting mangoes dates back centuries, from Mughal emperors who used them as diplomatic tools to modern-day leaders like Prime Minister Narendra Modi who have received gifts of mangoes from other nations. The practice continues today with President Pranab Mukherjee, Sheikh Hasina, and others using mangoes as a symbol of goodwill between their countries.

articles.title: How India-Oman Trade Pact Opens Alternative Route To Gulf Beyond Hormuz
articles.rephrased_article: The India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) commenced today, offering zero-duty access to a wide range of Indian exports to Oman. This agreement comes amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran conflict, with Oman's strategic location providing an alternative trade and energy gateway for India.  Piyush Goyal, Union Commerce and Industry Minister, highlighted that this deal will boost exports, attract investments, and create jobs, while Ajay Srivastav, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), noted the agreement's significance in ensuring reliable trade even during geopolitical instability.

articles.title: ‘Sexual Chocolate’ Faces Recalls After FDA Tests Reveal Undisclosed Viagra | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several alerts regarding chocolate products marketed for “sexual enhancement” that contain undisclosed drugs, including sildenafil and tadalafil, the active ingredients in Viagra and Cialis.  The FDA advises consumers not to purchase these chocolates due to potential health risks, including interactions with nitrates found in prescription medications. Several brands, including Boner Bears Chocolate and Lovion Chocolate With Ginseng for Men, are being voluntarily recalled by distributors such as Nalpac and Gear Isle. The agency also warns that the products may interact with nitrates found in some prescription drugs, such as nitroglycerin, and may lower blood pressure to dangerous levels.

articles.title: Dead For Years, Active Before Attack: The Phone Trail Behind Pahalgam Attack
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) and the Jammu and Kashmir Police have uncovered evidence suggesting that a 2025 Pahalgam attack was planned for years. Investigations revealed that one of the two mobile phones used by terrorists in the attack was imported into Pakistan in 2021, financed by a Karachi-based bank previously linked to terrorism cases. The phone remained unused for four years before being activated just prior to the attack.  The investigation is now focusing on uncovering networks providing technical and logistical support from Pakistan.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article suggests a long-planned attack financed by a known terrorist entity.

articles.title: A Bachelor's In Rare Earths? China Has Schools For That
articles.rephrased_article: China has established a robust education system for rare earths, with over 40 specialized labs and at least 11 universities enrolling more than 500 students annually in rare earth degree programs. This strong pipeline of talent sustains Beijing's dominance in global rare earth refining.  The US is lagging behind, with limited undergraduate degrees and low mining enrollments. Despite this, the US Department of Energy is investing in domestic mining expertise and international cooperation to bolster its rare earths capabilities.

articles.title: Iran war day 94: US strikes Iranian sites; Kuwait intercepts missiles | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States military conducted "self-defense strikes" on Iranian radar and drone sites, while the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) retaliated by targeting a US base.  Iran has restored gas production at three offshore platforms after Israeli attacks in March. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump stated that Iran is eager to reach an agreement, calling it "a good one for the USA and those that are with us." The conflict escalated as Israel deepened its offensive into southern Lebanon, prompting Hezbollah to shoot down an Israeli drone.  The situation remains tense, with both sides exchanging messages on a potential deal.

articles.title: Washington proposes ‘roadmap’ for de-escalation in Lebanon: US official | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has proposed a "roadmap" for de-escalation in Lebanon, involving Hezbollah halting attacks on Israel in exchange for Israel refraining from further escalation in Beirut. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered military operations in southern Lebanon's Dahiyeh district, claiming the capture of Beaufort Castle marks a "dramatic shift" in the campaign against Hezbollah.  The US official blamed Hezbollah for prolonging the conflict and accused Iran of manipulating it as a mediator. The escalation has resulted in widespread condemnation from countries like France, the United Kingdom, and Qatar, who have called for Israel to halt its military activities in Lebanon.

articles.title: Watch: Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami Speaks Mandarin, Gives Tour Of Indian Embassy In Beijing
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Doraiswami, India's Ambassador to China, is gaining attention for a video tour of the Indian Embassy in Beijing. In the video, Doraiswami speaks fluent Mandarin and introduces himself as "Wei Jiameng," highlighting cultural ties between India and China, referencing Rabindranath Tagore's visit to China over a century ago.  He also showcases various sections of the embassy, including its cultural center, where courses like yoga and dance are offered, and an exhibition area displaying handicrafts from across India.

articles.title: Vinicius brings Maracana curtain-raiser to life as Brazil rout Panama 6-2 | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brazil defeated Panama 6-2 in a friendly match, with Vinicius Jr. scoring two goals and setting up another.  The victory served as preparation for the upcoming World Cup, where Brazil will be without key players like Neymar. The game saw Carlo Ancelotti make significant changes to his starting lineup.  Christian Pulisic scored one goal and created another for Folarin Balogun in a 3-2 win against Senegal, as the USA prepared for their World Cup opener against Paraguay.

articles.title: Political commentators Cenk, Piker say UK bars them over Israel remarks | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker, US political commentators, were denied entry to the UK due to their criticism of Israel.  They allege that British authorities cited their public comments about Israel as the reason for the decision, stating they pose a "serious risk" to public order. The pair also claim that their criticisms of Israel's influence on American politics are being labeled as antisemitic. The Times newspaper reported that UK officials stated Uygur’s presence was not “conducive to the public good.

articles.title: Iran’s IRGC launches retaliatory strike after US attacks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran launched a retaliatory strike on a US base in Kuwait after the US carried out strikes on Iran's communications tower. The attacks came as indirect negotiations between the US and Iran to formalize a fragile ceasefire continue, with reports suggesting mixed signals about whether an agreement will be reached.  The US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated that no US troops were hurt in the attacks, while Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson blamed "lack of trust" and contradictory positions from the US for delays in negotiations.

articles.title: Ethiopia election under way as Abiy Ahmed seeks another term but no voting in Tigray
articles.rephrased_article: The Ethiopian general election is underway, but conflict in parts of the country has prevented many from voting. The northern region of Tigray, which was ravaged by a brutal civil war ending in 2022, is excluded from the poll. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Prosperity Party is expected to win, despite criticism over his government's suppression of dissent and human rights violations.  The election takes place amidst ongoing tensions with neighboring Eritrea and violent insurgencies in Amhara and Oromia regions, raising concerns about potential instability. Many young voters hope the election will bring stability, but some express apprehension about its impact on their lives.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Exclusion of Tigray from elections after civil war raises serious concerns about justice and democratic process.

articles.title: Wildlife study first, tree felling later: Court closes PIL against Rs 5,729-crore Guwahati Ring Road project | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Gauhati High Court closed a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the Rs 5,729-crore Guwahati Ring Road Project after the Assam government and National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) assured that no trees would be felled in the affected sanctuary area until a detailed wildlife impact study is completed. The court noted that the study, expected to be completed within 90 days, will be conducted by the Wildlife Institute of India (WII).  The project, proposed as a 121-km highway, aims to improve traffic management and animal corridor preservation.

articles.title: Donald Trump Mount Rushmore Moment? AI Photo Shows Him With 4 US Presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, Abraham Lincoln
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image on Truth Social that depicts him alongside the faces of four presidents on Mount Rushmore. The post reignited discussions about his long-standing interest in being included on the iconic monument, a sentiment he has previously expressed publicly. Kristi Noem, South Dakota Governor, confirmed that Trump had mentioned his desire to be added to Mount Rushmore during an earlier meeting.  This renewed conversation follows previous public remarks by Trump expressing his interest and even joking about the possibility.

articles.title: Which football rule changes will be implemented during the World Cup? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: IFAB, the international self-regulatory body for football, announced several rule changes to be implemented at the 2026 World Cup. These include red cards for players covering their mouths in confrontational situations and leaving the field of play in protest, as well as a broadened use of VAR technology to review decisions like second yellow card offenses and incorrect corner kick awards. The new rules aim to enhance match tempo, improve player and fan experience, and address discrimination.

articles.title: Shibuya: Japan introduces litter fine in Tokyo's tourist hotspot
articles.rephrased_article: Tokyo's Shibuya Ward has implemented on-the-spot fines of 2,000 Japanese yen for littering in an effort to curb the growing issue. The new penalties, part of a broader anti-littering campaign, aim to address concerns about public cleanliness and tourism impact. Authorities will deploy up to 50 officials to enforce the fines, which can be paid via cash, credit card, or QR codes. This initiative follows a surge in tourism following the Covid pandemic, leading to challenges for local communities and infrastructure.

articles.title: France intercepts sanctioned Russian oil tanker, Macron says
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron announced that France seized a sanctioned Russian oil tanker, the Tagor, with UK support in international waters. The French Navy boarded the vessel after it was found to be flying a false flag and violating international sanctions on Russia's oil exports.  The Kremlin condemned the seizure as "bordering on international piracy" while the UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer previously granted permission for UK military involvement in intercepting sanctioned Russian ships.

articles.title: Cockroach Janta Party founder to return to India on June 6 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, announced plans to return to India on June 6th to launch a peaceful protest demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.  Mr. Dipke called on supporters and students to join him in Delhi, where he will request permission from authorities to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. He cited exam-related controversies and disruptions as reasons for his call to action.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak: DR Congo celebrates recovery of five nurses
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Democratic Republic of Congo's Institute of Public Health are celebrating the recovery of five Ebola patients from a hospital in Bunia, the epicenter of the outbreak.  These recoveries mark an encouraging milestone and highlight the effectiveness of early detection, medical care, contact tracing, and community engagement. Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, emphasized the importance of community collaboration and trust for successful response efforts. The current outbreak has caused over 246 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda.

articles.title: Tirumala Sees Record Surge In Hair Offerings, 1.24 Million Devotees Shave Heads
articles.rephrased_article: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), which manages the world's richest Hindu shrine, recorded over 12.43 lakh hair offerings from devotees in May 2024, surpassing previous years and reaching a peak of 57,580 daily tonsuring on May 23rd. The increase is attributed to summer holidays, weekend rush, and pilgrims from across India and abroad. To handle the high demand, TTD has maintained round-the-clock tonsuring services with over 1,150 barbers working in shifts.  The hair collected is auctioned for use in wig, hair extension, and beauty industries, generating significant revenue for TTD.

articles.title: Tiger Shroff ‘smells’ cake but won’t take a bite, says sis Krishna; expert on extreme discipline | Fitness News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna Shroff, sister of actor Tiger Shroff, shared insights into her brother's disciplined approach to fitness.  She revealed that Tiger Shroff is extremely focused on training and avoids late-night cravings, prioritizing sleep and structured eating habits. Psychologist Rasshi Gurnani explained that while discipline is crucial for achieving fitness goals, an overly rigid approach can be detrimental, leading to anxiety, guilt, and unhealthy relationships with food and exercise.  Gurnani suggests a more balanced perspective where food and movement are viewed as sources of nourishment and pleasure rather than tools for punishment or control.

articles.title: Israel PM orders strikes on Beirut suburbs as Hezbollah conflict escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, ordered strikes on the southern Beirut suburbs in response to attacks on Israeli civilians and violations of a US-brokered ceasefire. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, urged both sides to cease hostilities and pressure Hezbollah to stop its attacks on Israel. Joseph Aoun, the Lebanese president, is relying on US mediation efforts to prevent further civilian casualties. The conflict escalated after Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for an Israeli strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

articles.title: France Tanker Seizure: ‘International terrorism’: Russia slams France's seizure of Russian-linked tanker, terms it 'illegal' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia strongly condemned France's detention of the oil tanker Tagor, calling it illegal and bordering on international terrorism. The Kremlin stated that the vessel was suspected of being part of Russia's "shadow fleet" used to circumvent Western sanctions imposed over the Ukraine war.  The French government seized the tanker in international waters after it departed from Murmansk and was headed towards Cameroon. France has opened a criminal investigation into the vessel for failing to prove its nationality, refusing to comply with authorities, and sailing under a suspected false Cameroonian flag.

articles.title: Iran attacks damage 20 US military sites since start of war, satellite images show
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has damaged 20 US military sites since the start of the war, according to satellite imagery analysis by BBC Verify.  The attacks have targeted key facilities across eight countries in the Middle East, causing millions of dollars worth of damage to state-of-the-art air defense systems, refuelling aircraft and radars. The Pentagon has reported destroying over 13,000 targets in Iran, but analysts suggest that Tehran's counter-attacks have been more precise and extensive than previously acknowledged.  The US is seeking to limit satellite analysis of the conflict by requesting Planet, a major provider, to impose an "indefinite" restriction on new images of Iran and most of the Middle East.

articles.title: US, Iran trade new attacks amid talks: Here’s what we know | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US and Iran have continued to exchange attacks despite a ceasefire that began on April 8. The US military struck Iranian radar and drone sites over the weekend, while Iran retaliated by targeting a US base in the Gulf region.  Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has also claimed responsibility for attacks on Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. Donald Trump claims he is close to achieving a "very good deal" with Iran but negotiations have been strained by recent attacks. The Iranian government maintains that it will not agree to any deal that does not secure full Iranian rights.

articles.title: Wockhardt shares rocket 19% after FDA approval for antibiotic targeting drug-resistant infections. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Wockhardt announced the FDA approval of its antibiotic, ZAYNICH, a fourth-generation cephalosporin that targets multiple penicillin-binding proteins simultaneously. The drug received Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) and Fast Track designations from the FDA, recognizing its potential to address the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance.  The Phase 3 ENHANCE-1 study showed ZAYNICH achieved a higher clinical cure rate compared to meropenem in hospitalized patients with complicated urinary tract infections or acute pyelonephritis. The drug has also been approved by the Drugs Controller General of India and is under review for approval in Europe.

articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet Expansion Live Updates: WB CM Suvendu Adhikari Cabinet Ministers Expansion 2026 Portfolio Wise Minister Oath Ceremony Latest Updates
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, is set to expand his council of ministers today with 35 BJP MLAs taking the oath. The expansion will bring the total number of ministers in the state cabinet to 41, exceeding the constitutional limit by three positions.  The new ministers represent various communities and regions, including North Bengal, women, tribals, and Matuas. Amit Malviya, a senior BJP leader, is among those expected to join the ministry. The expansion aims to solidify the party's support base after its victory in the recent state elections.

articles.title: Japan-Philippines Maritime Talks: China patrols east Taiwan waters ahead of Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China’s coast guard conducted patrols in waters east of Taiwan in response to Japan and the Philippines announcing maritime boundary delimitation talks.  The Chinese government asserts that these waters are under its sovereignty, while Taiwan rejects this claim and insists on its own territorial rights. Beijing has previously expressed disapproval of such discussions and urged Japan and the Philippines to cease any actions that infringe upon China's sovereign rights.

articles.title: Asian Paints shares rally 4% after Q4 results. Here’s what Nomura and Motilal Oswal are saying - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Asian Paints reported a 11% year-on-year increase in total income to Rs 9,418 crore for the quarter ending March 31, 2026.  EBITDA rose by 24.4% to Rs 1,787 crore during the same period. Nomura raised its target price on the company's shares to Rs 3,600, citing strong demand and a favorable product mix. Motilal Oswal maintained a Neutral rating with a target price of Rs 2,750, while JM Financial upgraded the stock to Add with a target price of Rs 2,815.  The brokerage firms expect high single-digit volume growth in FY27 despite significant price hikes and continued inflationary pressures.

articles.title: Rivalry led to Paralympic athlete’s killing in Ghaziabad, say cops; kin ‘wanted to see him win medal for India’ | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A 25-year-old Paralympic athlete, Chirag Tyagi, was shot and killed in Ghaziabad on May 30th.  DCP City and Trans-Hindon Dhawal Jaiswal stated that a rivalry between Chirag Tyagi and another Paralympic athlete preceded the killing. The victim's aunt said he had qualified for the Asian Para Games, which were to be held in October, and was preparing to return home after winning gold and silver medals in the 400 m and 1,500 m races.  The accused is suspected of being a junior athlete who felt Tyagi filed a complaint against him following his disqualification at an event.

articles.title: Nearly 60 out of 80 TMC MLAs skip Mamata meeting, party blames attack on its MPs | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: TMC postponed a meeting with newly elected MLAs after most failed to attend due to ongoing protests and police action following attacks on party leaders.  The party's spokesperson, Kunal Ghosh, stated that the meeting was postponed until later date as the MLAs were assisting arrested party workers. Mamata Banerjee will lead a protest rally in Kolkata on June 1st against the attacks on her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, and other party members.

articles.title: Inox Wind shares crash 8% after Q4 profit drops 45% YoY. Should you buy, sell or hold? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Inox Wind's shares plummeted to their lowest point since April 10, 2023, following a disappointing fourth-quarter earnings report. The company's revenue fell over 2% year-over-year and its EBITDA declined by 6%. JM Financial downgraded the stock rating to "Add" with a target price of Rs 101 per share, while Motilal Oswal maintained a "Buy" rating with a target price of Rs 110 per share.  Despite the challenges in connectivity and PPAs, the brokerage firms remain optimistic about Inox Wind's future prospects.

articles.title: Eating oats every day? A dietitian reveals mistakes that could cancel their benefits | Health and Wellness News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Archana Batra, a clinical dietician, advises against consuming oats as the sole meal component and emphasizes incorporating them into balanced breakfasts. Dr. Batra suggests adding protein sources like yogurt, nuts, or seeds to oatmeal for increased satiety and sustained energy levels.  She cautions against using oat milk as a nutritional replacement for dairy milk due to its low protein content and added ingredients that can alter the nutritional profile.

articles.title: Stalin Wine Cellar: Inside Stalin’s hidden wine cellar in Georgia: 40,000 rare French and Georgian bottles emerge after decades underground | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Georgian authorities opened a secret wine cellar containing approximately 40,000 bottles of rare French and Georgian wines to the public. The collection, believed to date back more than 200 years, was assembled by Josef Stalin, who took an interest in wine during his rule over the Soviet Union.  The government plans to auction parts of the cellar to establish a wine education school, hoping to boost Georgia's international wine market profile. The collection is shrouded in historical intrigue due to Stalin's controversial legacy and the wines' connection to imperial Russia.

articles.title: RCB win IPL: Virat Kohli, Krunal Pandya dance to dhol beats
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) won the IPL final against the Gujarat Titans, securing their second consecutive title.  Virat Kohli and his wife, Anushka Sharma, were seen thanking fans at the stadium, while Krunal Pandya and other players danced in celebration. Fans in Bengaluru took to the streets to celebrate the win, joining the festivities in Hyderabad as well. The team joins Chennai Super Kings and Mumbai Indians as the only franchises to achieve back-to-back IPL titles.

articles.title: Pune Crime Files: How a Bangladeshi woman with 2 Aadhaar cards was deported twice from India | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chandan Haygunde, an Assistant Editor at The Indian Express, is a seasoned journalist specializing in crime, national security, and legal affairs. He has extensive experience covering various high-profile cases, including the Koregaon Bhima violence, Elgaar Parishad investigation, and the Maoist urban link cases.  His investigative reporting often delves beyond official narratives, providing historical context and highlighting systemic issues. Haygunde is known for his balanced coverage of sensitive communal issues and his deep connections within law enforcement agencies.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights potential misuse of Aadhaar and lax border control.

articles.title: NMDC Steel shares jump 18% to record high after returning to profit in Q4, FY26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NMDC Steel returned to profitability in the March quarter, reporting a net profit of Rs 391.91 crore compared to a loss of Rs 473 crore last year. Revenue from operations surged 37% year-on-year to Rs 3,879 crore, driven by strong production and sales volumes. The company also achieved its first profitable full-year performance, posting a net profit of Rs 59 crore in FY26.  Institutional investors increased their stake in the company during the quarter, while foreign institutional investors maintained their holdings at a steady level. Technical indicators suggest continued bullish momentum for NMDC Steel.

articles.title: Gujarat Hardlook | Cyber terror in labour room: Curtains left open, weak passwords, eight hackers, and viral clips | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A group of individuals, including Prajwal Ashok Teli, Praj Rajendra Patil, and Chandraprakash Phoolchand, were arrested for hacking CCTV systems at hospitals, malls, and commercial buildings across India. They sold the footage on closed Telegram groups, earning an estimated Rs 8 lakh before their arrest. The accused used virtual numbers to communicate with hackers in Romania and Atlanta, USA, and accessed restricted data through various hacking tools. Police are investigating how many other victims were affected by this crime.  The Gujarat government is reviewing its cybersecurity protocols following the incident.

articles.title: UP records 90% attendance in B Ed entrance exam; over 4.44 lakh candidates appear | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The B.Ed Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) 2026 was successfully conducted in Uttar Pradesh on Sunday, with 90% of the 4,44,958 registered candidates participating. The exam, overseen by Bundelkhand University, took place at 1,011 centers across 72 districts and utilized advanced technology including AI-based face recognition, fingerprint verification, and real-time attendance systems to ensure fairness.  Uttar Pradesh Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay expressed satisfaction with the exam's successful conduct and highlighted the government's commitment to transparent and secure examinations.

articles.title: 10 darkest regions on Earth where you can get the clearest views of planets, stars and the Milky Way | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Atacama Desert in Chile, the Namib Desert in Namibia, and other locations around the world offer exceptional night-sky conditions for stargazing. These regions are characterized by low population density, minimal light pollution, and high altitudes, creating clear views of celestial objects like planets, constellations, and the Milky Way.  These dark skies are crucial for scientific research and provide a valuable opportunity for people to connect with the natural world.

articles.title: NMDC Steel shares jump 18% to record high after returning to profit in Q4, FY26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NMDC Steel returned to profitability in the March quarter, reporting a net profit of Rs 391.91 crore after a loss of Rs 473 crore in the same period last year. The company's revenue surged 37% year-on-year to Rs 3,879 crore, driven by strong production and sales volumes. NMDC Steel also achieved its first full-year profitability, posting a net profit of Rs 59 crore for FY26.  The company's stock has seen a significant rally, with a market capitalization of approximately Rs 13,076 crore and positive EPS. Institutional investors increased their holdings during the quarter.

articles.title: Commercial LPG Prices Hiked By Rs 42 In Delhi, Rs 53.5 In Kolkata Amid Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Commercial LPG prices in Delhi rose by Rs 42 to Rs 3,113.50 per cylinder from June 1st, marking a nearly doubling of costs since January. This increase follows a series of price hikes throughout the year, driven by disruptions in global energy supply chains due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and tensions around the Gulf region. The rise in LPG prices has also impacted CNG prices, which have increased by Rs 2 per kg.  The government is working to build larger reserves of LPG to mitigate future disruptions and strengthen India's energy security. This will likely impact businesses and consumers as they face higher cooking costs and potential price increases for meals, services, and products.

articles.title: Weather Today LIVE Updates | IMD Weather Forecast Delhi NCR, UP, Noida, Rajasthan Heatwave Updates: Drastic Drop In Temperatures Keeps Delhi Cool
articles.rephrased_article: India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts continued relief from the summer heat in Delhi-NCR as rain and thunderstorms are expected until June 4th.  The IMD also predicts scattered rainfall and gusty winds across the region, keeping daytime temperatures below 40 degrees Celsius through at least June 6th. The western disturbance over Rajasthan and central Pakistan is contributing to these weather conditions. Heavy rainfall is anticipated in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and southern states as the monsoon progresses.

articles.title: Noida Trekker Goes Missing On Uttarakhand's Pindari Glacier Trail, Search On
articles.rephrased_article: State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams are searching for missing trekker Vishesh Chauhan in Uttarakhand's Bageshwar district after he separated from his local porter on the Pindari Glacier route.  Chauhan, who was returning from the trek, failed to reach the base by the scheduled time and prompted a request for SDRF assistance. The team used rope rescue techniques to search a suspected location but Chauhan remains missing.

articles.title: Nepal has encroached on Indian territory as well: PM Balendra Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah sparked a political uproar in Parliament after his comments about border encroachment. The government later clarified that the remarks were due to technical factors related to shifting river boundaries.

articles.title: UP records 90% attendance in B Ed entrance exam; over 4.44 lakh candidates appear | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The B.Ed Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) 2026 was successfully conducted in Uttar Pradesh on Sunday, with 90% of the 4,44,958 registered candidates participating.  Yogendra Upadhyay, Uttar Pradesh Higher Education Minister, expressed satisfaction over the exam's fairness and transparency, which were enhanced by advanced technology including AI-based face recognition, fingerprint verification, and real-time attendance systems. The examination was overseen by a centralized command center with 22,000 CCTV cameras and 5,651 biometric machines to ensure only genuine candidates took the test.

articles.title: IREDA shares drop 4% post Q4 results. What’s spooking investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: IREDA's share price declined on the NSE despite a 14% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,175 crore for Q4FY26. The company announced a final dividend of Rs 0.75 per share (7.5%) and discussed fines levied by BSE and NSE related to board composition.  The company is requesting the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) to expedite the appointment of Independent Directors, including a woman director. IREDA's shares have declined over 8% in 2026 and nearly 27% over the past year.

articles.title: Iran-US war, What To Know As Israel's Lebanon Incursion In 25 Years Complicates Iran Deal
articles.rephrased_article: Israel seized the symbolic Beaufort fort in southern Lebanon, a move that challenges a US-brokered ceasefire and raises concerns from Qatar, Germany, and other countries. The Israeli military claims it is targeting the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group, but Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accuses Israel of "total destruction" and calls for an end to the conflict.  The incursion comes amidst ongoing talks between senior officials from Israel and Lebanon, aiming to address issues like an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon, deployment of Lebanese forces, and Hezbollah disarmament.

articles.title: With departed souls in mind, fans in Bengaluru celebrate another IPL win in the ‘right spirit’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) fans celebrated their team's back-to-back IPL victory in Bengaluru, with police ensuring the celebrations remained peaceful after last year's tragic stampede.  The city's Commissioner of Police, Seemanth Kumar, stated that the police had taken security measures to maintain order and prevent any disturbances.  RCB captain Rajat Patidar celebrated his birthday victory, acknowledging the fans' unwavering support. The team also wore jersey number 11 as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in last year's stampede.

articles.title: 10 darkest regions on Earth where you can get the clearest views of planets, stars and the Milky Way | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have identified ten regions around the world offering exceptional night-sky conditions. These include the Atacama Desert in Chile, known for its dryness and high altitude, as well as the Namib Desert, the Mauna Kea mountain in Hawaii, and the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve in New Zealand. The Kerry International Dark Sky Reserve in Ireland, the Tibetan Plateau, and Cherry Springs State Park in Pennsylvania also offer clear views of celestial objects.  These dark-sky locations are important for scientific research and provide opportunities for stargazing enthusiasts to appreciate the beauty of the night sky.

articles.title: Rajat Patidar and the conversation that predicted RCB’s future | Cricket News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rajat Patidar, after initially being unsure about the captaincy offer from Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), led his state team to victory in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy.  His friend, Abhishek Pathrod, recalls that he took time to consider the decision and only accepted when he felt ready. Patidar's calm demeanor and focus on the present have been key factors in his success as a batsman and captain. He credits former Madhya Pradesh teammate Ishwar Pandey and coach Amey Khurasiya for helping him develop his skills and mental game.  His ability to judge length quickly and execute effectively has earned him praise, particularly after his unbeaten 93 in Qualifier 1 against Gujarat Titans.

articles.title: AP EAMCET 2026 results today: Websites to check | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: APSCHE will release the results for the 2026 AP EAMCET today, May 31st, on their official website, cets.apsche.gov.in. Candidates can also check their results through the APSCHE myCET mobile app by entering their details and selecting the appropriate exam. The exam was held from May 12th to May 20th, 2026, with no negative marking for incorrect answers. Following the release of the results, the counseling process will begin for eligible candidates.

articles.title: What's P2P Lending? Why Banks, RBI Are Watching This Credit Trend Closely
articles.rephrased_article: India's digital lending ecosystem is evolving rapidly, with peer-to-peer (P2P) lending gaining momentum. Fintech platforms are using alternative data to assess credit for underserved borrowers, such as freelancers and gig workers, offering potentially higher returns than traditional debt products.  However, the sector faces challenges like credit risk and liquidity concerns. The Reserve Bank of India has implemented regulations to ensure responsible participation and improve governance standards.

articles.title: What is Lipulekh and why is it at centre of India-Nepal border dispute? Explained | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's new Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, stated that his government has sent a diplomatic note to India regarding the "encroachment" of territories. He asserted that both countries have encroached on each other's land in various locations.  Shah expressed hope for resolving the dispute through dialogue and emphasized the importance of studying facts together as friends. While India has not yet responded, it previously rejected Nepal's objection to the upcoming Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh Pass, stating that the route is long-established and the issue should be addressed through bilateral discussions. The dispute over Lipulekh stems from conflicting claims regarding the location of the Kali River, which is recognized as the natural border between the two countries.

articles.title: Did Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian Resign Over Disagreement With IRGC? A Fact Check
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian authorities have denied reports that President Masoud Pezeshkian has submitted a resignation letter to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.  The Tasnim News Agency, an IRGC-affiliated outlet, reported that Pezeshkian remains in office and continues his duties. The deputy head of communications at the president's office also dismissed the report as misinformation from foreign media outlets.

articles.title: How PSG gave the city of Henry & Mbappe a football club they can be proud of
articles.rephrased_article: PSG, a club once struggling in Ligue One, has transformed into a dominant force in European football.  Under manager Luis Enrique, the team has won back-to-back Champions League titles and established itself as one of the most exciting teams in the world. The squad boasts an impressive blend of individual talent, tactical flexibility, and defensive solidity, with players like Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele leading the charge.  The club's success has brought a new level of global recognition to French football.

articles.title: Malaysia Enforces Social Media Facebook, Instagram, TikTok YouTube Ban For Under-16, Platforms Must Verify Age
articles.rephrased_article: Malaysia began enforcing rules on Monday prohibiting under-16s from owning social media accounts, requiring platforms with 8 million users to verify age and block underage account creation. Companies that fail to comply face fines of up to $2.5 million. The government aims to protect children from harmful content and cyberbullying, but critics argue the law could backfire by driving teenagers away from protected apps into unregulated spaces.  The move comes as governments worldwide grapple with concerns about social media's impact on children's mental health and online safety.

articles.title: Virat, Anushka dance at RCB's championship after party: 'One felt nice, we did twice' | Video | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) won their second consecutive IPL title after defeating the Gujarat Titans by five wickets. Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, who were both present at the celebrations, danced with teammates and family members.  The team secured victory with a clinical chase of 156, with Kohli scoring an unbeaten 75. The win makes RCB only the third franchise to retain the IPL trophy after Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings.

articles.title: ‘I never studied for number,’: Meet Kabeer Chhillar, AIR 2 in JEE Advanced 2026
articles.rephrased_article: Kabeer Chhillar, an IIT Roorkee graduate, secured the second-highest rank in the JEE Advanced 2026 exam with a score of 329 out of 360.  He achieved this despite not focusing on the ranking and instead prioritizing understanding concepts. Chhillar's success was attributed to his disciplined study habits, strong mental fortitude, and passion for learning. He plans to pursue a Computer Science degree at IIT Bombay and potentially further studies at MIT.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet Formation News Siddaramaiah Yathindra DK Shivakumar Cabinet
articles.rephrased_article: Yathindra Siddaramaiah, son of former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah, has expressed hope for a ministerial position in the new cabinet led by DK Shivakumar.  He stated that the party high command has assured him of such a berth. Another Congress MLA, Basavaraj Shivannavar, also seeks a ministerial post and believes his community from North Karnataka deserves representation. The Congress is yet to finalize its cabinet lineup, with speculation about a two-to-three deputy chief minister formula.

articles.title: Delhi ITO fire: Fire breaks out at Education Ministry office building, 8 tenders rushed to spot - Delhi News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out on the second floor of a building housing Ministry of Education offices in Delhi's ITO area on Sunday morning.  Delhi Fire Service received a call at 9:37 am and dispatched eight fire tenders to the scene. Thick smoke was reported, but no injuries or casualties have been reported. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

articles.title: 'My son was so happy': Hours after saying 'I do', Indian-origin newlywed pilot killed in helicopter crash in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A helicopter carrying Dave Fiji, an Indian-origin pilot, and his wife Jesni crashed shortly after takeoff in Georgia on Friday night. The crash claimed the lives of both pilots, while Jesni survived with injuries and is recovering in hospital.  Dave Fiji had been overjoyed on his wedding day and had expressed concerns about poor visibility before the flight. The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Meet JEE Advanced 2026 toppers: AIRs 1, 2, 3 share success strategies - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Shubham Kumar, Kabeer Chillar, and Jatin Chahar secured the top three ranks in the JEE Advanced 2026 exam, with Kumar achieving AIR 1.  These students emphasized consistent study habits over marathon sessions, highlighting the importance of conceptual understanding and reviewing mistakes. Arohi Deshpande, the highest-ranked female candidate, advocated for a relaxed approach to exam pressure and maintained mental stability throughout her preparation journey. The results have sparked attention towards the JoSAA 2026 counselling process, which will determine admissions to various institutes based on the candidates' performance in the JEE Advanced.

articles.title: IPL 2026: How father’s tales of a helmetless Gavaskar forged Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s grit - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a 15-year-old Indian cricketer, made history by becoming the first player in IPL history to sweep five major individual titles in a single season.  He achieved this feat with an unprecedented 776 runs and a record-breaking strike rate of 237.30. Sooryavanshi's success is attributed to his father's bedtime stories about legendary cricketer Sunil Gavaskar, who inspired him to play fearless cricket, even without a helmet.  He has ambitions beyond the T20 format, aiming to represent India in Test cricket and continue honing his skills on the red ball.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet Formation News Siddaramaiah Yathindra DK Shivakumar Cabinet
articles.rephrased_article: Yathindra Siddaramaiah, son of former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, and Basavaraj Shivannavar, a Congress MLA, have expressed interest in ministerial positions within the new DK Shivakumar-led cabinet.  Shivakumar, who will be sworn in as chief minister on Wednesday, has promised to prioritize a power-sharing arrangement that could see a Dalit leader and a minority community leader appointed as deputy chief ministers. The Congress is yet to formally announce its ministerial appointments.

articles.title: Can a 10-year SIP really make you rich? Here’s the truth you need to know - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A 10-year SIP can significantly improve the chances of earning positive returns in equity mutual funds, but it is not a guarantee of riches. Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, explains that long-term investing and rupee cost averaging help investors average purchase costs over time. Historical data shows that Indian markets have weathered various economic cycles and market crashes, suggesting that staying invested through these periods can lead to positive long-term outcomes. However, experts emphasize the importance of fund selection, consistency, and investor discipline as key factors in achieving wealth creation. Abhishek Kumar, a Sebi-registered investment adviser, cautions against oversimplifying the concept of a 10-year SIP, stating that while it can improve chances of positive returns, equity mutual funds remain market-linked instruments with inherent risks.

articles.title: Delhi Gymkhana Club Membership Fees: Why elite clubs across India are sweating - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Elite clubs across India are facing scrutiny after the Delhi Gymkhana Club received an eviction notice from the government. The controversy has sparked concerns about whether these institutions, which occupy prime government-leased land at concessional rates, can continue to enjoy privileges in a country where public land is under pressure.  Mumbai's Marine Drive and Marine Lines belt clubs are reviewing their lease records and seeking changes to annual rent hikes and restrictions on events. Similar discussions are happening in cities like Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, and Varanasi. The Delhi Gymkhana case has raised questions about transparency, accountability, and the balance between heritage and public good.

articles.title: US-Iran war live updates: Iran To Revise Deal Draft After US Changes, US-Iran peace proposal, Iran nuclear programme, israel lebanon latest news
articles.rephrased_article: The United States carried out airstrikes on Iranian radar and drone control sites in response to the shooting down of an American MQ-1 Predator drone. Iran retaliated with its own attacks, disrupting global energy supplies as Iran maintains control over the Strait of Hormuz.  The escalating conflict comes amid Israeli incursions into Lebanon and continued negotiations for a ceasefire extension. The US is awaiting President Trump's decision on a proposed deal to extend the ceasefire while oil prices rose due to the situation.

articles.title: IPL Final: GT players evacuated as team bus breakdown due to short circuit after loss to RCB in Ahmedabad - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Gujarat Titans players and support staff were evacuated from their team bus after a short circuit caused smoke to spread inside the vehicle following the IPL 2026 final in Ahmedabad. All members escaped unharmed, with an alternate bus arranged for them to reach the hotel. The incident occurred while the team was traveling back to their hotel after suffering a five-wicket defeat to Royal Challengers Bengaluru.  The Titans' disappointing end to the season was compounded by this unexpected travel disruption.

articles.title: Delhi, Saket Building Collapse: Research Aspirant Was Celebrating His Interview When Delhi Building Collapsed
articles.rephrased_article: A multi-storey commercial building collapsed near Saket metro station in Delhi, killing at least six people and trapping several others under debris. Among the victims were Kapil, an aspiring BARC candidate, and Nalin, a GATE exam candidate from Bihar. The collapse occurred around 7:30 pm on Saturday evening, sending tonnes of debris crashing onto a tin-shed canteen frequented by students preparing for competitive exams. Witnesses reported hearing cracking sounds before the structure gave way, while locals alleged that their input regarding trapped victims was initially ignored. Rescue efforts continued through the night with multiple agencies involved, and authorities have initiated an inquiry to determine the cause of the collapse.

articles.title: ASI succumbs to accident injuries in Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: An Assistant Sub Inspector (ASI) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police named Karamjeet Singh died at a hospital in Jammu after being hit by a vehicle during an accident in Gangyal.  Singh was admitted to GMCH Jammu in critical condition following the incident, which also injured another person, Rajesh Kumar, who is from Uttar Pradesh. Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation.

articles.title: Rasikh Salam, Virat Kohli star as RCB wins second IPL title
articles.rephrased_article: Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) won their second Indian Premier League (IPL) title by defeating Gujarat Titans (GT) in the IPL 2026 final. RCB comfortably chased down a target of 156 runs, with Virat Kohli scoring an unbeaten 75 and guiding them to victory.  Rasikh Salam was instrumental for RCB with his three wickets, while Rashid Khan had two wickets for Gujarat Titans. The victory marks a memorable night for RCB as they secured their second IPL crown.

articles.title: Picnic Turns Deadly, 2 Teens Drown At Maharashtra Jayakwadi Dam, 1 Body Recovered
articles.rephrased_article: Friends from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra visited the Jayakwadi dam for sightseeing on Sunday. Two teenagers, Aniket Manu Bharti and Sanket Siddharth Kharat, entered the water without realizing its depth or current, leading to their drowning.  Local residents and rescue teams launched a search operation that recovered one body but continued efforts to locate the other teenager. Authorities are urging caution when visiting dams and reservoirs.

articles.title: Caribbean hot sauce producers warn of shortages and higher prices
articles.rephrased_article: Caribbean hot sauce producers are facing shortages and price increases due to a confluence of extreme weather, disease, and pests affecting Scotch bonnet pepper production. The temperamental fruit is crucial for the region's signature sauces, with manufacturers like Walkerswood, Gray's Pepper, and Homebrew Hot Sauce reporting disruptions in supply and increased costs.  The Jamaican government has been working to support farmers, while some producers are exploring alternative peppers or using high-yielding hybrid red chillis.

articles.title: Adityanath urges people to protect nature, links environmental conservation to Sanatan traditions
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, urged citizens to actively participate in environmental conservation, emphasizing its deep connection to Indian culture and tradition. He highlighted the importance of respecting nature through rituals like Vat Savitri fast and festivals like Chhath and Mahakumbh.  Adityanath stressed the need for collective action on World Environment Day, urging people to pledge themselves to protecting nature and conserving resources. The state government has been actively involved in environmental initiatives such as the inclusion of Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary and the "One District One River" program.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: CBI traces Samarth Singh's movements as probe widens in dowry death probe - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is investigating the death of former model and actor Twisha Sharma, who was found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12. The agency has obtained new details from Samarth Singh's interrogation regarding his movements after her death and during his time on the run.  The CBI is now examining potential helpers and medical claims as they reconstruct the sequence of events leading up to Sharma's death, including questioning doctors linked to the case. Officials are also looking into Twisha's consultations with a psychiatrist and investigating possible dowry-related harassment by her in-laws. The investigation has been taken over by the CBI after re-registering a Madhya Pradesh Police FIR that names Samarth Singh and Giribala Singh as accused.

articles.title: Malaysia enforces ban on social media accounts for children younger than 16
articles.rephrased_article: Malaysia began enforcing rules on Monday barring children under 16 from owning social media accounts, joining a global effort to protect young users. The new regulations require platforms with at least 8 million users, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, to implement age-verification systems and block users under 16 from creating accounts. Companies that fail to comply face penalties of up to 10 million ringgit (USD 2.5 million). The government stated the measures are aimed at protecting children from harmful content, cyberbullying, and excessive use features. However, some experts have expressed concerns about the law's effectiveness due to potential loopholes and lack of parent penalties.

articles.title: China's coal mine disaster is a reminder of its darkest days
articles.rephrased_article: A devastating coal mine explosion in Shanxi province killed 82 people and injured over 120 others. The blast at the Liushenyu mine, which was flagged for safety violations before, highlights the ongoing challenges of China's coal industry despite recent safety reforms. Authorities are investigating the cause of the disaster, but experts attribute it to human error, such as management failures and flawed safety systems.  The tragedy underscores the need for continued vigilance in a sector that has historically been plagued by accidents. While China is transitioning towards green energy, coal remains vital for its economy and power grid stability.

articles.title: Palestinian man shot dead by Israeli forces at West Bank barrier near Jerusalem
articles.rephrased_article: A Palestinian man, Imad Haroun Ishtayeh, was shot and killed by Israeli forces while attempting to cross the West Bank barrier into Israel.  The incident occurred in al-Ram town on Sunday, with footage showing his body being carried across the barrier. Ishtayeh, 26, had been trying to enter Israel for work after economic hardship in his village of Salem. His death follows a string of Palestinian deaths at the barrier and increased unemployment in the West Bank since the October 7th attack on Israel by Hamas-led militants.

articles.title: Lucknow Dowry Death: Gave Rs 7 Lakh Dowry, They Wanted Car Too: Lucknow Influencer Found Dead
articles.rephrased_article: Mansi, a social media influencer, was found dead at her in-laws' house in Lucknow. Her family alleges that Sagar Rajput, her husband, and his family members killed her over demands for a car and staged it as suicide.  A dowry death case has been filed against Rajput and five other family members based on the victim's family's complaint.

articles.title: Meji Alabi, Grammy-winning director, explores his Nigerian grandfather’s role in the Biafran war for BBC Africa Eye
articles.rephrased_article: Meji Alabi, a Grammy-winning director, and his uncle Leke Alabi-Isama produced the documentary "Surviving Biafra: Voices from the Nigerian Civil War" for BBC Africa Eye. The film features previously unseen footage of the devastating conflict that lasted from 1967 to 1970.  Survivors recount their experiences during the war, which resulted in an estimated 500,000 to three million deaths and is still relevant today. The documentary also explores the role of Godwin Alabi-Isama, Leke's father and a former army commando who fought for the federal army against the Igbo separatists.  The film aims to encourage Nigerians to confront their shared history with honesty, reflection, and empathy.

articles.title: Pezeshkian Decries IRGC 'Madness,' Seeks Khamenei Meeting Before Quitting | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: President Masoud Pezeshkian has reportedly submitted his resignation to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, citing a power struggle between the civilian government and Tehran's military-security apparatus. The move comes amid mounting tensions between the elected administration and the IRGC, which has increasingly assumed control over key elements of state governance, according to sources familiar with internal discussions in Tehran.  The resignation report coincides with ongoing US-Iran diplomacy aimed at ending a three-month conflict, but significant gaps remain in negotiations for a ceasefire and settlement.

articles.title: Rupee falls 9 paise to 94.94 against US dollar in early trade
articles.rephrased_article: The rupee depreciated 9 paise to 94.94 against the US dollar on Monday, weighed down by elevated crude oil prices and escalating tensions between Israel and Lebanon.  Forex traders cited a strengthening Dollar Index and rising oil prices as contributing factors. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened in the market to prevent the rupee from exceeding 96.00 levels. Despite outflows by foreign institutional investors, the rupee maintained its strength due to the RBI's presence.

articles.title: ‘Before, the land sustained us’: Who benefits from Guinea’s bauxite wealth? | Mining News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Guinea's vast bauxite reserves have fueled economic growth, but at a cost.  Indian, Russian, US, and UAE companies are exploiting the country's resources, leading to environmental degradation and poverty for many residents. While some Guineans benefit from mining jobs, others struggle with contaminated water, lost farmland, and declining agricultural productivity. The government is attempting to reform the mining sector by processing bauxite within Guinea, but power shortages and a lack of infrastructure hinder progress.  The influx of bauxite-related wealth has also led to an increase in migration from Guinea to Spain, where Guinean communities are growing rapidly.

articles.title: 'They're hunting buses': The Ukrainian drivers risking death on the routes of Kherson
articles.rephrased_article: Anatoly Dmytrov, a driver for Kherson municipal transport company, and his colleagues are facing increasing danger on their routes as Russian drones target buses in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson. The attacks, which started last year, have resulted in injuries and fatalities, with at least eight passengers injured in one recent incident.  The attacks have escalated since Russia began using optic fiber cables for drone navigation, making traditional anti-drone measures ineffective. Kherson municipal transport company has taken steps to protect drivers and passengers, including providing helmets and bulletproof vests, but the threat remains significant. Despite the danger, bus drivers continue to work, recognizing their crucial role in transporting essential supplies and people within the city.

articles.title: Weather update: Forecast for Southern cities on 1 June - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department issued weather forecasts for major South Indian cities on Monday, June 1st. Hyderabad will experience partly cloudy skies with the possibility of rain, thunderstorms, or duststorms, while Amaravati is expected to have partly cloudy skies with one or two spells of rain or thundershowers. Bengaluru will have a partly cloudy sky that may become generally cloudy in the afternoon, evening, or night. Thiruvananthapuram will have a generally cloudy sky with a few spells of rain or thundershowers, and Chennai is expected to have partly cloudy skies with the possibility of moderate rain or thunderstorms.

articles.title: Technique, temperament still rule T20 cricket; Kohli proves it again: Sharma
articles.rephrased_article: Virat Kohli led Royal Challengers Bengaluru to victory in the IPL final, scoring an unbeaten 75 runs as they defended their title. His coach, Rajkumar Sharma, praised his technique and temperament, highlighting that power-hitting alone is not enough for success in T20 cricket.  Sharma also noted Kohli's consistent performance across formats and his unwavering commitment to winning, making him a role model for young players.

articles.title: US says ban on AI chip shipments applies to Chinese firms outside China | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Commerce clarified its export control rules regarding advanced AI chips, stating that licensing requirements apply to all businesses with headquarters or parent companies in China. This follows concerns about loopholes in the regime and comes after the Biden administration's scrapped Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, which proposed a global licensing system for AI chip exports. Nvidia, a major chip company, confirmed it has been operating under these clarified rules, while other competitors like AMD and Intel, as well as chip manufacturer TSMC, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Early Morning Blaze Devastates Cuttack's Fish Market; Bank, Over 30 Shops Reduced To Ashes | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: A massive fire broke out at the fish market near Press Chhak in Cuttack, Odisha early Monday morning. The blaze, which started around 2:30-3 am and spread rapidly through shops, godowns, and storage units, caused extensive damage to the market complex and a nearby Bank of India branch.  Firefighters, who deployed multiple fire tenders and a robotic firefighting vehicle from Bhubaneswar, battled the blaze for over six hours. The incident resulted in significant losses for fish traders, with reports indicating the destruction of deep freezers, furniture, stock, and other business assets. Deputy Fire Officer Abani Kumar Swain confirmed that the fire has been brought under control but estimated the total damage to exceed Rs 50 lakh.

articles.title: Air India Ahmedabad crash: One year on, a Mumbai family still waits for answers - and peace
articles.rephrased_article: A year after the Air India Flight AI171 crash, which killed Javed Ali and his family, Imtiyaz Ali, a brother of the deceased, continues to grapple with unanswered questions about the incident.  Air India officials and doctors have been slow to provide updates on the investigation, belongings, and medical support for the grieving family. Despite receiving an interim report shortly after the crash, Imtiyaz Ali feels that the technical details only add to their pain. He believes that the investigation will eventually reveal what caused the crash but finds solace in a recording of his brother's voice from before the accident, where he describes a peaceful dream about angels and roses.

articles.title: ‘I never studied for number,’: Meet Kabeer Chhillar, AIR 2 in JEE Advanced 2026
articles.rephrased_article: Kabeer Chhillar, from the IIT Delhi zone, secured the second-highest rank in the JEE Advanced 2026 results with an AIR of 2.  He scored 329 out of 360 marks, just one mark behind the top scorer, Shubham Kumar.  Chhillar's father, a IIT Kharagpur alumnus, emphasized that his son focused on understanding concepts rather than chasing rankings.  The young student, who has represented Haryana in soccer and enjoys music, plans to pursue CSE at IIT Bombay and further studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

articles.title: TMC MLAs, Abhishek Banerjee attack: Only 20 attend Mamata Banerjee Kalighat meeting - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: TMC General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee was attacked on Saturday, leading to a low turnout at a legislative party meeting called by Mamata Banerjee. Only 20 of the 80 newly elected MLAs attended the meeting at her residence. The absence of nearly three-fourths of the legislators raised concerns, but TMC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh stated that many were protesting against alleged political violence and police action against party workers.  The party announced plans for protests in rural areas and urban wards on Monday, followed by a sit-in led by Mamata Banerjee at Rani Rashmoni Road on Tuesday.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale MLA absence raises concerns about internal party conflict and potential instability.

articles.title: US Strikes Iran's Radar, Drone Control Sites In Goruk And Qeshm Islands
articles.rephrased_article: The United States conducted self-defense strikes on Iranian radar and drone control sites in the Goruk and Qeshm Islands over the weekend, responding to Iran's shooting down of a US MQ-1 drone. CENTCOM stated that fighter aircraft targeted Iranian air defenses, a ground control station, and two one-way attack drones, with no US personnel harmed.  Iran retaliated by targeting an airbase in response to the US strikes, according to reports from Fars news agency. The escalating tensions follow previous attacks between the two nations last week.

articles.title: AIADMK MLAs join TVK: Why the Anti-Defection Law does not apply - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The resignation of four AIADMK MLAs and their subsequent entry into the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has sparked allegations of horse-trading, prompting legal experts to question whether this case falls under the Anti-Defection Law.  While the law does not prevent an MLA from resigning and joining another party, it's unclear if the TVK's actions constitute a breach of the law. Legal experts argue that the current framework lacks effective mechanisms to curb defections, but suggest revisiting the provision allowing mergers involving two-thirds of a legislature party.  Senior journalist RK Radhakrishnan believes the TVK's alleged efforts are driven by financial gain and political immaturity, while writer and activist Aadhavan Dheetchanya suggests the party is building an independent majority as a safeguard against potential policy conflicts with its current allies.

articles.title: Over 56,000 qualify JEE (Advanced) 2026; Shubham Kumar secures AIR 1
articles.rephrased_article: Over 56,000 candidates successfully passed the Joint Entrance Examination (Advanced) 2026, considered one of India's most challenging exams.  Shubham Kumar, from the IIT Delhi zone, achieved the top rank with a score of 330 out of 360 marks. Arohi Deshpande, also from the IIT Delhi zone, secured the highest female ranking with an All India Rank (CRL) of 77. A total of 1,79,694 candidates took part in both papers 1 and 2 on May 17th, 2026.

articles.title: Has Iranian President resigned? Here's the truth after report claims end to Pezeshkian's rule over dispute with IRGC | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Masoud Pezeshkian, the Iranian president, has denied reports that he resigned amid a dispute with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) over decision-making.  Iranian officials have dismissed these claims, stating that Pezeshkian remains in office and will continue to serve the people. The report, published by Iran International, cited an official as saying Pezeshkian submitted a resignation letter to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

articles.title: Odisha Man Strangles Wife With Towel, Buries Body On Riverbank | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: A 29-year-old mason, Malay Kumar Samal, has been arrested for the alleged murder of his 28-year-old wife, Banita Sethi, in Cuttack district, Odisha.  Samal allegedly strangled Sethi following escalating marital conflicts stemming from his alleged extramarital relationship and then concealed her body by burying it on the bank of Mendhakhai Nullah. The crime came to light after Sethi's mother filed a complaint, leading police to the burial site where they seized evidence including a spade and a towel.  Police are investigating further and suspecting another woman involved in the case.

articles.title: Controversial 'Highway to Hel' 666 bus revived in Poland
articles.rephrased_article: FlixBus has revived its "Highway to Hel" bus service, connecting Kraków to the Polish seaside resort of Hel. The new route, previously operated by PKS Gdynia, features a 13-hour journey passing through various Polish cities and towns.  The number 666 was chosen as a marketing tactic, but religious groups opposed the association with the number, which is linked to the "number of the beast" in the Bible.

articles.title: 'Beware of pickpockets': Rahul slams Govt. over CBSE re-evaluation cost - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, criticized the Modi government over the CBSE's re-evaluation process, alleging that errors are not corrected but multiplied due to treating education as a business.  He highlighted the financial burden on students who face costs for scanning, re-totalling, and re-evaluation, with some paying up to ₹2,000 for accurate evaluation of their answer sheets. Gandhi also criticized the centralized nature of the system, claiming it leads to critical failures when one node fails. He shared video clips from a conversation with students who experienced issues with the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system and expressed concern about the financialization of education.

articles.title: CBSE Class 12 OSM website tender row: Rahul Gandhi alleges answer sheets were scanned on phones - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader, has accused the CBSE and its vendor, COEMPT Edu Teck, of using mobile phones to scan Class 12 answer sheets instead of professional equipment.  Gandhi alleges that the tender process was manipulated to favor COEMPT, resulting in compromised security and inaccurate evaluation scores.
