Students are reporting blurred scans, missing pages, and discrepancies between their answers and the uploaded copies. Nisarga Adhikary, an ethical hacker, also exposed vulnerabilities in the OSM portal, raising concerns about data security. The CBSE has acknowledged these issues and is working to address them.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of manipulated tenders and compromised evaluation of student answer sheets raise serious concerns.

articles.title: US bombs Iranian military sites; Kuwait hit by drone, missile fire
articles.rephrased_article: The United States military conducted airstrikes on Iranian radar and drone control sites in response to the downing of an American MQ-1 Predator drone. Iran acknowledged launching a retaliatory strike, while Kuwait reported intercepting incoming drone and missile fire. The attacks highlight the fragility of a weekslong ceasefire in the ongoing conflict between the two countries, which has seen repeated attacks despite efforts to extend it.

articles.title: Iran and US report new wave of air strikes in Gulf
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran resumed air strikes in the Gulf over the weekend, each claiming to have targeted military sites. The US Central Command (Centcom) reported striking Iranian radar, command and control sites for drones, while the IRGC claimed retaliation by targeting an airbase used by US forces.  The latest round of hostilities comes despite ongoing negotiations for a peace deal that could lead to a ceasefire in the region. No American servicemen or women were injured in the US strikes, but the IRGC warned of a "completely different" response if aggression continues.

articles.title: Ex-US Fed Chair Powell warns against politicisation amid Trump’s attacks | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, former US Federal Reserve Chair, warned against the politicisation of monetary policy during his acceptance speech for the 2026 John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award. He stated that the US Congress had wisely insulated the central bank from political pressure and that all advanced economies have similar norms upholding the independence of monetary policy. Powell emphasized that removing Fed officials over policy differences would erode public trust in the institution, potentially damaging its credibility and ability to support a strong and stable economy.

articles.title: 18-year-old Sri Lankan refugee killed in Chennai after group allegedly rams vehicle into two-wheeler - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: An 18-year-old Sri Lankan Tamil refugee woman, Yansi, was killed and a 17-year-old girl injured when a car allegedly rammed into their two-wheeler following a dispute near a private bar in Chennai.  The incident occurred late on Saturday, May 30th, after a quarrel between two groups at the bar escalated onto the road where both groups attacked each other. Police have arrested three people and seized the car involved in the crime.  CCTV footage is being examined as part of the investigation.

articles.title: Voice Behind Odia Classic 'E Banara Chai' Suman Kalyanpur Passes Away At 89 | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Suman Kalyanpur, a renowned playback singer known for her soulful voice across Hindi, Marathi, Odia, and other regional cinemas, passed away at 89 in Mumbai due to age-related health issues.  Born Suman Hemmadi in Dhaka, she began her career in the 1950s with Marathi films before becoming a prominent figure in the 1960s and 1970s. Kalyanpur collaborated with many renowned musicians including Mohammed Rafi, and left an indelible mark on Indian music through her timeless Hindi classics and contributions to Odia cinema.  Tributes have poured in from across the music industry, political leaders, and fans mourning the loss of a golden voice.

articles.title: J&K Chief Justice Arun Palli Elevated to Supreme Court
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre has approved the appointment of five new judges to the Supreme Court, including Justice Arun Palli, Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.  These appointments were announced by Union Minister of State for Law and Justice, Arjun Ram Meghwal. The appointments bring the total number of judges in the Supreme Court to 37 out of 38 sanctioned positions.

articles.title: Iran president Pezeshkian gives resignation letter to supreme leader over IRGC control, says report; official rejects claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian reportedly submitted a letter of resignation to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, citing his exclusion from decision-making processes and control by hard-line factions within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).  An official from the president's office dismissed the reports as baseless and refuted claims that young people lack capacity for governance.

articles.title: Sonakshi Sinha Reveals DIY Flaxseed Gel Hack for Natural Curly Hair
articles.rephrased_article: Sonakshi Sinha, a Bollywood actress, shared a DIY beauty hack for achieving natural curls using flaxseed gel on her YouTube vlog. She collaborated with her mother-in-law to prepare the gel, which is made by simmering flaxseeds in water. Sinha then used the gel to create soft, natural curls overnight by braiding her hair and opening it the next day.  Dr Rimpa Sarkar, PhD, a wellness expert at Sentier Wellness in Mumbai, suggests that intergenerational learning, like beauty tips from mothers-in-law, can strengthen family bonds.

articles.title: Unsung Heroes | How a monkey licking water spilt on road in Bidar sparked a thirst to help wildlife in summer | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Swabhimani Geleyara Balaga, a group of friends in north Karnataka, has been installing and maintaining water troughs in forests to provide drinking water for animals and birds during the summer heat. The group was inspired by an incident where a monkey tried to lick spilled water from the road, prompting them to address the issue of dwindling water sources in the region.  Chandrashekhar Padashetti, president of the Balaga, has led the effort since its formation 12 years ago, focusing on tree planting and recharging the water table. The group now deploys over 40 members to ensure daily refills of water troughs across several forest areas.

articles.title: Delhi Confidential: Mandarin Connect | Delhi Confidential News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Doraiswami, newly appointed Indian ambassador to China, has begun engaging with Chinese social media audiences by introducing the Indian embassy in Beijing and its facilities.  He is using his fluent Mandarin skills, honed during his time in China as a diplomat, to connect with the audience. Meanwhile, Asaduddin Owaisi, chief of the AIMIM party, has warned Shaukat Ali, state unit chief, that he will be removed if the party's performance in Uttar Pradesh does not improve before upcoming elections.

articles.title: No inquiry needed: J-K High Court says President, Governor can terminate govt employees over ‘security of state’ | India News - The Indian Express
articles.sentiment_target: Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court has upheld the dismissal of a police constable, Ghulam Mohammad Tantray, by the then Governor based on Article 311(2)(c) of the Constitution. The court ruled that the President or Governor can remove employees from government service without an inquiry if it is deemed necessary for the security of the state.  The court acknowledged that this provision has a high threshold and requires subjective satisfaction, considering factors like terrorism, espionage, or anti-national conduct. This decision comes amidst criticism of the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor's administration for dismissing 91 employees under Article 311(2)(c) since 2021.

articles.title: Trump Suggests Canceling State Fair Concerts After Artist Boycott
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has called for the cancellation of a series of concerts marking America's 250th anniversary, citing concerns over the event's political ties and the "overpriced" and "boring" lineup. Several performers, including Martina McBride, Young MC, and Bret Michaels, have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 festival.  Despite these withdrawals, acts like Vanilla Ice and Milli Vanilli are still scheduled to perform. Trump has suggested replacing the concert series with a political rally and is considering a "giant MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN RALLY" in place of the fair.

articles.title: A social media connection across LoC: How this ‘intruder’ from PoK found himself in Army custody in J-K | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: An intruder from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) was intercepted by Army troops near Silikote in Uri sector of north Kashmir while attempting to cross the Line of Control. The 22-year-old man, identified as Zeeshan Ahmad, crossed the border to meet a woman he had developed a romantic relationship with through social media. Authorities are investigating whether the love story is a cover-up for something else.

articles.title: US team in Delhi today, urgency to finalise deal | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: USTR officials, led by Brendan Lynch, will begin negotiations with India on Monday to finalize an interim trade agreement.  The talks are being held due to a new US tariffs architecture replacing reciprocal tariffs that were deemed illegal by the Supreme Court in February. While tensions have eased somewhat, India faces challenges from "unconventional US demands" regarding oil and agricultural purchases.  A deal could help restore investor confidence in India, but disagreements remain on issues like agricultural products and Russian oil imports.

articles.title: Maharashtra clears mine project, says not in tiger area; maps show otherwise | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra government exempted an iron ore mining project in Gadchiroli from wildlife clearance, claiming it was not within a tiger corridor. However, the project site is located within forest compartments identified as part of the Tadoba-Indravati tiger corridor, according to official records reviewed by The Indian Express.  The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has previously clarified that corridors identified in approved TCPs should be considered for scrutiny of project proposals under the Wildlife Act. Despite this, the Maharashtra government's Chief Wildlife Warden initially exempted the project and later withdrew his letter after a review.

articles.title: Noida engineer missing near Pindari Glacier: Camera found on riverbank after he told porter to go ahead | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old engineer, Abhishek Chauhan, has gone missing while on a trek from Pindari Glacier in Uttarakhand.  Rescue personnel, including members of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), have been searching for him since Friday, when he failed to meet his porter at a designated point. The search effort has been hampered by heavy rainfall and adverse weather conditions. A drone was deployed to scan the area, but operations were called off on Saturday.  The operation is ongoing with teams from the forest department and police also involved in the search.

articles.title: The good girl who never came home - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The case of Twisha Sharma, a woman who disappeared after her marriage, has sparked widespread discussion about the societal pressures placed on women in India. The author reflects on their own experiences with familial expectations and cultural conditioning that often silence women's voices and perpetuate harmful stereotypes.  They argue that while some cases may involve misuse of legal protections, the larger issue lies in a system that encourages women to prioritize family and societal expectations over their own well-being. This systemic pressure can lead to psychological abuse, silencing, and ultimately, disappearance. The author concludes by expressing their fear of conforming to these societal norms and choosing independence instead.

articles.title: India warm nights: IMD data shows rising minimum temperatures and higher power demand - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: India's nights are experiencing a steady rise in temperature, according to data analysis by the India Meteorological Department.  The increase is particularly pronounced after 2000, with 2024 marking the highest annual average minimum temperature. This warming trend has significant consequences for public health, leading to increased heat stress and disrupted sleep patterns, especially among vulnerable populations like children, elderly individuals, and those living in cramped conditions without proper ventilation.  The rise in nighttime temperatures is also driving up electricity demand, contributing to power outages and strain on the national grid.

articles.title: Delhi crime rate against women highest in 2024, Jaipur tops cities - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi recorded the highest crime rate against women in India in 2024, with a rate of 130.7 cases per lakh women, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.  The city was followed by Telangana, Odisha, Haryana, and Rajasthan.  While some states saw declines in crime rates against women between 2020 and 2024, including Assam, Telangana experienced a significant increase. Jaipur reported the highest crime rate among surveyed cities at 199.6 cases per lakh women, while Chennai had one of the lowest rates.  Major crimes against women declined in 2024, with decreases seen in cruelty by husbands or relatives, kidnapping and abduction, assaults on women, and dowry-related crimes.

articles.title: Siddaramaiah set to hand over baton after record tenure in Karnataka - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Siddaramaiah resigned as Karnataka Chief Minister, paving the way for his deputy, DK Shivakumar, to assume the role. The transition follows a long-running power struggle between the two leaders and comes after three years of Congress rule in the state.  While Siddaramaiah oversaw significant welfare programs and became Karnataka's longest-serving chief minister, the leadership change has also highlighted political instability within the state, with frequent changes in leadership over the years. The transition is seen as a major moment for the Karnataka Congress, who will now need to balance caste equations and factional ambitions ahead of the 2028 Assembly elections.

articles.title: India heatwave deaths study: Five-day spell could cause 30,000 excess deaths - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A new study estimates that a five-day heatwave could cause nearly 30,000 excess deaths in India, concentrated in the poorest and hottest states.  Union Health Ministry recorded about 360 heatstroke deaths between March and July 2023; independent trackers counted 733. Piyush Narang and Ashok Gadgil, authors of the study published in the journal Frontiers in Environmental Health, argue that official statistics substantially under-report heat-related deaths. The five states with the highest death toll from a five-day heatwave are Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Gujarat.  The study highlights an economic divide, as these states have 43% of India's population but only 29% of its GDP.

articles.title: DK Shivakumar career: From student leader to Karnataka CM frontrunner - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: DK Shivakumar, a former student leader, has consistently risen through the ranks of the Congress party in Karnataka over four decades.  He won eight Assembly elections, securing a commanding 75% vote share in 2023. His rise to prominence began in 1981 when he joined the National Students' Union of India and later served as chairman of the Karnataka State Planning Board. Shivakumar also played a key role in organizing the historic campaign yatra that brought SM Krishna's Congress to power, defeating HD Kumaraswamy in Sathanur in 1999. He has held various ministerial positions and led the Congress party's 2023 Karnataka campaign, ultimately becoming deputy chief minister after winning his own seat with a strong majority.

articles.title: Delhi CM visits building collapse site, orders action on all illegal buildings - Delhi News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta visited the Saket building collapse site on Sunday, ordering a criminal case and a magisterial inquiry into the incident.  Following her visit, Gupta directed authorities to inspect dilapidated buildings in the area and take action against unauthorized constructions. The CMO Delhi, along with Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu and Home Minister Ashish Sood, confirmed that rescue teams were continuing operations and providing medical assistance to those affected.

articles.title: Royal Enfield Bullet 650 review: first ride shows it is better than the Classic 650 - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The new Royal Enfield Bullet 650 is a refined update to the classic motorcycle, offering comfort and ease of riding.  It retains the familiar stance and relaxed attitude of its predecessor while incorporating modern features like a smoother engine and improved ergonomics. The Bullet 650's 647.95cc parallel-twin engine delivers ample power for city riding and highway cruising, making it an enjoyable motorcycle for both short trips and longer journeys.  While visually understated compared to the Classic 650, the Bullet 650 offers a more comfortable experience with its single-piece seat and plush suspension. The bike's relaxed nature makes it ideal for leisurely rides, but its performance is still capable of handling twisty roads when needed. Despite being priced at Rs 3.65 lakh ex-showroom, the Bullet 650 feels like the most complete Royal Enfield 650 currently on sale.

articles.title: FPI selling puts June rally at risk, midcaps may march on - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty 50, Nifty 500, Midcap 100, and Smallcap 250 have shown mixed performance over the past decade, with gains in some periods and losses in others.  Analysts suggest that while June typically favors Indian equities, factors like crude prices, foreign selling, and weather conditions could influence market sentiment this month. They also note that July historically has been a positive period for the market, making dips or consolidation in June an opportunity to buy for further gains.

articles.title: Everyone Has Their Targets Set on the MacBook Neo | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Dell and Microsoft are responding to the success of Apple's MacBook Neo with laptops offering similar features at lower prices.  The new Dell XPS 13, starting at $699, mirrors the MacBook Neo's design and premium feel while using an Intel Core 5 processor instead of a more powerful chip. Microsoft has also released two versions of its Surface Laptop for Business PCs, with one model offering 8 GB of RAM and a lower price point. However, Microsoft is facing criticism for downgrading the RAM in its cheaper Surface Laptop option compared to previous models.  The competition between these companies will likely continue to heat up as they navigate the challenges of chip shortages and consumer demand.

articles.title: U.P.'s 'cockroach man' floats CJP spin-off after drawing attention to Yamuna's plight - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Deepak Sharma, a social activist and kathavachak from Uttar Pradesh, dressed as a cockroach to draw attention to Yamuna pollution in Mathura.  Sharma's initiative, the "Common Justice Platform" (CJP), aims to highlight official apathy towards the river. The CJP has gained popularity with over 800 volunteers who identify themselves as cockroaches and are committed to raising awareness about environmental issues. However, some critics view the movement as a political stunt aimed at destabilizing India.

articles.title: Pahalgam: Let the valley remain pristine
articles.rephrased_article: Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam, a popular tourist resort, is facing environmental problems due to unscientific garbage disposal. The landfill site at Sarbal contaminates the Nallah Tulyan stream, which flows into the Lidder river, posing risks to aquatic life and water quality.  Environmental activists like Mushtaq Pahalgami have been advocating for its closure for years, citing concerns about forest land usage and ecological damage. Despite government assurances, no significant action has been taken to relocate the landfill. The issue highlights the need for sustainable waste management practices in tourist destinations to protect fragile ecosystems.

articles.title: Watch: Cuba’s blackouts leave high-rise residents with constant uncertainty - BBC News
articles.rephrased_article: Cuba is experiencing another month of blackouts due to the US fuel blockade, causing significant disruption to residents' lives. Ana Rosa Romero, a 70-year-old widow living in a high-rise building, describes how the power outages have transformed her daily routine.  BBC reporter Will Grant spoke with Romero about the impact of these blackouts.

articles.title: First Health Emergency
articles.rephrased_article: Tahir Ahmad, MDS oral and maxillo-facial surgery, highlights the alarming rise in tobacco addiction as a precursor to substance abuse, particularly among youth in Kashmir.  He emphasizes that World No Tobacco Day 2026 should focus on prevention and protection of young people against tobacco addiction, aligning with the ongoing Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan launched by the J&K Government. He stresses that addressing tobacco consumption is crucial for preventing substance abuse, as research shows a strong association between smoking and later drug use.  He urges institutions to prioritize nicotine awareness in schools, mosques, and community organizations, advocating for a shift away from romanticizing self-destructive habits as symbols of masculinity or modernity.

articles.title: Ladakh: Towards People’s Rule
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre and representatives of the Apex Body of Ladakh (ABL) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) have reached an "in-principle" agreement on restoring democracy in Ladakh, providing constitutional safeguards under provisions similar to Article 371 A, F, and G.  These provisions are applicable in states like Nagaland, Sikkim, and Mizoram. The agreement includes granting legislative, executive, and financial powers to elected representatives through a UT-level Assembly, with the elected head having direct administrative control over the entire UT bureaucracy.  The agreement also safeguards land, environment, culture, and jobs under Article 371.  While both parties expressed optimism about this step forward, they emphasized that further discussions are needed before finalizing the proposal.

articles.title: Healer in exile
articles.rephrased_article: Sachin Razdan, in his book "Healer in Exile," offers a moving portrait of his father, Dr. Sushil Razdan, a renowned neurologist who faced exile and hardship as a Kashmiri Pandit.  The book explores the doctor-patient relationship, highlighting Dr. Razdan's commitment to empathy and service despite personal suffering. The author recounts Dr. Razdan's life journey with honesty and restraint, capturing both the beauty of Kashmir before militancy and the pain of displacement.  "Healer in Exile" is a testament to resilience, ethics, and humanity, reminding readers that true healing extends beyond medicine.

articles.title: Cepeda, de la Espriella advance in Colombia’s presidential election | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abelardo de la Espriella and Ivan Cepeda will face off in a runoff for Colombia's presidency on June 21st after neither candidate secured the required majority in Sunday's election.  De la Espriella, an outsider with a hardline security platform, led the vote count with 43 percent of the ballots cast, while Cepeda, a left-wing senator, trailed behind by over 600,000 votes. The results come after Paloma Valencia, a right-wing senator who was initially considered a frontrunner, dropped out of the race.  Security concerns were a key issue in the election, with de la Espriella focusing on crime and violence while Cepeda advocated for a "Total Peace" approach championed by outgoing president Gustavo Petro.

articles.title: Legendary Broadcaster from Hyderabad
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Rafiq Masoodi, a former Director of Radio Kashmir, shared memories of his interactions with Kabir Ahmed Jaisee, the late renowned broadcaster and academic, who passed away in 2021.  Masoodi met Jaisee during his time as a program executive at Radio Kashmir in the 1980s and was deeply impressed by Jaisee's aura and genuine warmth. He recalled Jaisee's open praise for staff and his understanding of their daily struggles, particularly when Masoodi explained his reliance on taxis to reach the airport.  Jaisee's daughter, Dr. Humera Sultana, wrote a moving tribute to her father in the magazine "A New Chapter" which has been praised by Masoodi for its profound and befitting nature.

articles.title: Commercial LPG cylinder price hiked in Delhi, domestic LPG rates unchanged - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The government has increased the price of commercial LPG cylinders in Delhi and Kolkata, effective June 1st. The price hike for a 19 kg cylinder is Rs 42 in Delhi, reaching Rs 3,113.50, and Rs 53.50 in Kolkata, reaching Rs 3,255.50.  The Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Sujata Sharma, stated that these price increases are part of efforts to strengthen fuel security and maintain adequate reserves. Authorities have also intensified inspections to prevent hoarding and diversion of LPG.

articles.title: Noida engineer missing near Pindari Glacier: Camera found on riverbank after he told porter to go ahead | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old engineer, Abhishek Chauhan, has gone missing while on a trek from Pindari Glacier in Uttarakhand.  Rescue personnel, including members of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), have been searching for him since Friday. His camera was found near the Pindar River, and his porter reported him missing after he failed to meet at a scheduled location. The search has been hampered by adverse weather conditions and inaccessible terrain.

articles.title: Iran war live: Israel’s expanding invasion of Lebanon draws global alarm | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: France requested an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council to address Israel’s expanding invasion of Lebanon, drawing global condemnation.  US President Donald Trump stated he is close to a "very good deal" with Iran, according to US media reports.

articles.title: Staying Safe During Workouts
articles.rephrased_article: Recent years have seen a rise in fitness participation, but safety during exercise is often overlooked. Dr. Mehreen Mustafa, In-charge PMRD Khyber Medical Institute Khayam Chowk Srinagar, highlights that sudden cardiac events, including heart attacks and arrhythmias, can occur during workouts, particularly among young, seemingly fit individuals.  These events are often linked to underlying heart conditions like coronary artery disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or aortic dissection. Dr. Mustafa emphasizes the importance of gradual training, warm-ups, cool-downs, hydration, recognizing warning signs, and consulting healthcare professionals before starting a new workout routine for those with existing health conditions.

articles.title: Trump seeking edits to US-Iran deal, US media report
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has requested further edits to the US-Iran deal, aiming to address concerns related to the Strait of Hormuz and highly enriched uranium. These latest changes follow a framework agreement reached on Thursday, which included a 60-day ceasefire, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and potential sanctions relief for Iran. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator, has stated that any deal must ensure Iranian rights are secured. While US officials have expressed confidence in reaching an agreement, Iran has cast doubt on the White House's messaging and demands the release of frozen assets before substantive nuclear program talks can proceed.

articles.title: Apple Smart Glasses likely to launch in late 2027, will follow Watch playbook - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Apple is reportedly targeting a late 2027 launch for its first smart glasses, with the device expected to compete with Meta and Google. The company aims to position the glasses as a platform for Siri and Apple Intelligence, focusing on practical features like cameras, microphones, speakers, notifications, and walking directions.  Apple is prioritizing design and everyday usability over flashy augmented reality capabilities in its first-generation product.

articles.title: Call for action
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Pir Naseer Ahmad, an advocate at the High Court of Srinagar, argues that awareness campaigns against substance abuse are insufficient without structural reform and decisive action. He criticizes the contradiction between publicly denouncing drug use while allowing tobacco and alcohol to remain widely available.  He proposes a strategy focused on reducing availability through stricter licensing and policy shifts, alongside increased funding for de-addiction centers and community accountability measures. Dr. Ahmad believes that meaningful change requires bold, consistent action from all stakeholders at every level.

articles.title: CUET-UG 2026 exam, rescheduled over Id, conducted smoothly across centres - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) successfully conducted the rescheduled Common University Entrance Test-Undergraduate (CUET-UG) 2026 on May 31, 2026, after postponements due to Id. The examination was held in two shifts across hundreds of centers both domestically and internationally. A total of 54,882 candidates participated in Shift II, with an attendance rate of 67.9%.  The NTA had previously announced the rescheduling of certain tests scheduled for May 28th due to Id.

articles.title: Uri-I Stage-II hydro project enters construction phase
articles.rephrased_article: The NHPC Limited officially began construction on the 240 MW Uri-I Stage-II Hydroelectric Project in Baramulla, Kashmir. The first blast for underground tunnel excavation marked a significant milestone in the project's development, which will involve constructing water-conveyance tunnels and a powerhouse complex.  The project is expected to significantly enhance power generation capabilities in the region and contribute to long-term energy security by increasing hydropower output. Officials emphasized that safety measures are being taken and all necessary approvals have been secured for the project's construction.

articles.title: Colombia leftist faces pro-Trump rival in presidential election runoff
articles.rephrased_article: Colombia's presidential election will proceed to a runoff on June 21st between leftist senator Iván Cepeda and right-wing candidate Abelardo de la Espriella.  Neither candidate secured an outright majority in the first round, with De la Espriella receiving slightly more votes than Cepeda. Both candidates offer contrasting visions for addressing Colombia's ongoing internal armed conflict and its relationship with the US. De la Espriella has advocated a tougher approach to crime, including closer ties with the US, while Cepeda prioritizes dialogue and negotiations with armed groups as part of his "total peace" strategy.  The runoff will be closely watched for its implications on Colombia's foreign policy, particularly its relationship with Ecuador, which has been impacted by drug trafficking.

articles.title: Garlic economy grows in Kashmir as bumper crop boosts trade
articles.rephrased_article: Kashmir’s garlic industry has experienced a significant upswing this year, with farmers reporting strong yields and better market prices. Bashir Ahmad Basheer, chairman of the All Kashmir Fruit Growers Union, stated that nearly 2,000 truckloads of garlic are exported annually from Kashmir, primarily to southern states like Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.  Farmers and traders attribute the success to improved yields, stable demand, and increased market access. They believe this trend can lead to further growth for the Valley's agricultural economy.

articles.title: Tullamulla farmers embrace garlic cultivation, seek better market support
articles.rephrased_article: Garlic cultivation is gaining popularity in the Tullamulla area of Ganderbal district, Kashmir, as farmers seek higher returns.  Farmers are investing time and effort to produce quality garlic, but lack of proper market linkages, storage facilities, and institutional support hinders its sustainability. Local farmers advocate for improved marketing systems, cold storage infrastructure, and value-added processing units to enhance competitiveness and reduce post-harvest losses. They believe that government intervention can significantly improve the viability of garlic cultivation in the region.

articles.title: Trinamool calls off meeting as three-fourths of its MLAs fail to turn up - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A scheduled meeting of newly elected Trinamool Congress legislators was called off after nearly three-fourths of the party's MLAs failed to attend.  The meeting, convened by Sobhandeb Chatterjee, and likely to be addressed by former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, saw only 20 out of 80 attendees present at Banerjee's residence. Kunal Ghosh, a Trinamool spokesperson, attributed the low turnout to the attack on party general secretary Abhishek Banerjee in Sonarpur and ongoing attacks on party leaders and activists.

articles.title: Emergency operation centres activated in district ahead of monsoon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The district administration in Kerala has activated emergency operation centres across all seven taluks as the southwest monsoon is expected to arrive this week. The centers, including the District Emergency Operation Centre (DEOC) and taluk centres, have been operational since a week ago due to pre-monsoon showers causing damage to over 200 houses. These centers will pass information on waterlogging and flooding to relevant departments like police and fire force for prompt action, while cases requiring resident relocation will be handled by local bodies.

articles.title: UAS-B launches new UG programmes in Natural farming, Forestry and Biotechnology - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The University of Agricultural Sciences Bangalore (UAS-B) has launched three new undergraduate programs for the academic year 2026-27: a BSc in Natural Farming, a BSc in Forestry, and a BSc in Biotechnology.  Vice-Chancellor S.V. Suresha stated that these programs were initiated based on student and faculty suggestions and research indicating the growing demand for graduates with natural farming knowledge due to its potential to address environmental concerns and job opportunities in the agricultural sector. The university has limited initial enrollment to 60 students per program, with the Forestry program attracting interest from students across Karnataka who aspire to pursue careers in forestry or the Indian Forest Service (IFS).

articles.title: 2026 Honda City facelift review, first drive: Comfort, efficiency and legacy - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The Honda City facelift, a second update since its 2020 debut, focuses on refinement and efficiency.  Changes include a redesigned grille, updated interior with a new 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment system, and ventilated front seats. The hybrid powertrain remains unchanged but offers impressive fuel economy and smooth transitions between electric and petrol power. While the City retains its comfortable ride quality and reliable performance, it may not appeal to buyers seeking more sporty driving dynamics.  The updated City continues to be a strong contender in the mid-size sedan segment.

articles.title: Bangalore Astronomical Society featured in Mann Ki Baat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Astronomical Society (BAS), a Bengaluru-based non-profit group, was featured in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 134th episode of Mann Ki Baat. The group, founded in 2006, promotes astronomy through workshops and stargazing sessions, particularly targeting rural areas.  The organization has conducted over 1,000 programs, inspiring participants to pursue careers in astronomy. BAS volunteers are passionate about sharing their knowledge freely, providing educational opportunities for students of all ages.

articles.title: “If I can do it, anybody can” Shape of Momo Director Tribeny Rai’s message to aspiring filmmakers - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A 14-year-old Indian-American, Shrey Parikh, won the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee but faced online racist comments. A dust storm in Rajasthan's Churu district caused widespread disruption, plunging parts of the region into darkness and halting daily life.  Ram Charan, Janhvi Kapoor, Boman Irani, and Divyendu spoke to India Today about their roles in the upcoming film "Peddi."

articles.title: Experts discuss hydrocarbon management at webinar in Vijayawada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AvaniXplore LLP, EarthScholar Professional Academy, and MindSpark Learning Hub collaborated to host a webinar on "Untapped Hydrocarbon Frontiers – A Forward-Looking Perspective for India." The session, attended by 160 participants, including students and professionals from various fields, focused on petroleum exploration, basin analysis, resource management, and India's long-term energy outlook.  The event took place amidst growing global concerns about energy security and the need for diversified hydrocarbon sourcing.

articles.title: I never saw my representation on screen: Tribeny Rai on why she made 'Shape of Momo' - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: An alleged attack on TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee during his visit to Sonarpur, West Bengal sparked a major political showdown. Protesters hurled stones and eggs at his convoy, raising "chor chor" slogans, while the incident has drawn criticism from various political parties.

articles.title: Blackmail over private videos leads woman to plot sister-in-law’s murder in Chickballapur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhavya and Lohith Kumar, a 25-year-old woman and her relative, have been arrested for the alleged murder of Bhavya's sister-in-law, Bhagyamma. The duo allegedly smothered Bhagyamma to death with a pillow and stole her jewelry after being blackmailed by Kumar over private videos of Bhavya.  The police investigation revealed inconsistencies in Bhavya's statements and the crime scene evidence pointed towards smothering as the cause of death, leading to their arrest.

articles.title: 'Bakrid Invite' murder accused killed in encounter I Ghaziabad case - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Tribeny Rai, director of the film "Shape of Momo," discussed her experience growing up without seeing people from the Northeast represented in mainstream cinema. The alleged attack on TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee during his visit to Sonarpur, West Bengal, sparked a political showdown after protesters surrounded his convoy and hurled stones and eggs.  The investigation into the death of 17-year-old Surya Pratap Chauhan is ongoing.

articles.title: Three persons killed in accident in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three people, including a 68-year-old lorry driver and two others, were killed in a car accident on the Chennai - Bengaluru Highway near Vellore.  The incident occurred around 3 a.m., when S. Karthi, who was driving with his family members, lost control of his vehicle after it collided with two motorcycles traveling on the wrong side of the road. The car then plunged into a pit and struck a tree. All seven individuals involved escaped injuries, but the accident resulted in the deaths of the three people.

articles.title: Rajat Patidar: From being unsold to back-to-back IPL titles with RCB - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rajat Patidar, the man accused of being involved in the "Bakrid Invite" murder, was killed during an encounter with police in Ghaziabad.  The case has taken a dramatic turn after Patidar's alleged involvement in the murder and subsequent arrest.
articles.civic_flag_reason: An encounter killing raises serious concerns about due process and potential abuse of power.

articles.title: DVAC registers case against Tahsildar, VAO in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Venda, a Tahsildar, and S. Suresh, a Village Administrative Officer (VAO), have been booked by the DVAC for issuing patta for government land in Vellore. Initial investigations revealed that Venda issued patta for 1,700 sq.ft of land allocated for police quarters while creating false entries with VAO Suresh to issue it to R. Umapathy, husband of Veppankuppam panchayat president U. Suganya.  A probe is underway.

articles.title: Sarvam cuts Vision AI prices by 67% after Indians digitise 35 million documents - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Sarvam AI, an Indian AI startup, has reduced the price of its document intelligence platform, Sarvam Vision, by 67 percent after digitizing over 35 million pages. The company cites infrastructure improvements and increased demand as reasons for the price reduction. Sarvam AI says the revised pricing makes the service more affordable for businesses and developers working with large document collections.  The platform focuses on optical character recognition (OCR) and is designed to handle a variety of content formats, including scanned documents and complex page layouts.

articles.title: Padmaja assumes office as Collector of Kallakurichi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J.E. Padmaja assumed office as the new Collector of Kallakurichi district on Sunday, replacing M.S. Prasanth.  Ms. Padmaja, previously an Additional Collector in Villupuram, pledged to expedite grievance redressal and improve inter-departmental coordination for overall district development. She assured that all public petitions would be promptly forwarded and resolved within a defined timeframe.

articles.title: Asus ExpertBook Ultra (2026) review: A serious business ultrabook with premium ambitions - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The Asus ExpertBook Ultra (2026) is a premium business ultrabook designed for professionals on the move. It features a lightweight design, strong performance, long battery life, and a beautiful OLED display. The laptop's keyboard is excellent for typing, and its trackpad is responsive but has occasional issues.  The camera is functional but average, and the speakers are adequate but not impressive. Battery life is outstanding, lasting up to 14 hours with regular use. While the ExpertBook Ultra excels in portability, productivity, and battery life, minor software bugs and a lack of convertible design hold it back from being perfect.

articles.title: Don't act like you're tough: Frances Tiafoe's tiff with opponent at French Open
articles.rephrased_article: Frances Tiafoe defeated Jaime Faria in a heated third-round match at the French Open, winning 4-6, 6-7 (2), 7-6 (4), 6-1, 6-2.  Alejandro Tabilo advanced past Moise Kouame, while Felix Auger-Aliassime secured a victory over Brandon Nakashima. Juan Manuel Cerundolo extended his winning streak with a five-set victory over Martin Landaluce, setting up a match against Matteo Berrettini.  Anastasia Potapova defeated Coco Gauff, ending the American's French Open defense.

articles.title: Pune Uber driver's 4am life-or-death traffic lesson for founder is too real to miss - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Vik Gambhir, a Pune Uber ride founder, shared an eye-opening conversation he had with an ambulance driver during his early morning commute. The driver, who had spent 11 years driving ambulances, suggested that aspiring motorists should spend a week behind the wheel of an ambulance before obtaining a license to gain a deeper understanding of traffic realities.  The driver explained how every delay in an emergency situation could have serious consequences for patients and their families. This sparked online discussion with many users praising the driver's perspective on road safety.

articles.title: Bengaluru traffic cop carries specially-abled man across flooded road - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A Bengaluru traffic constable, Anil Kumar, helped a differently-abled youth cross a flooded road during heavy rain.  The incident occurred in Byatarayanapura on Friday evening as several roads were waterlogged and causing traffic disruptions. Kumar noticed the young man struggling to cross safely and decided to carry him across the flooded stretch himself, ensuring his safety and comfort throughout the process. The video of Kumar's compassionate act has gone viral online, receiving praise for his humanity and highlighting that public service can extend beyond routine duties.

articles.title: Sumukhi Suresh says female comics get cancelled every day: ‘Just read our comments section’ | Web-series News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sumukhi Suresh discussed her experiences as a female comedian, stating that she and other female comics face more negativity than male comedians. She believes the system favors men in comedy, leading to less support for women in the industry. Suresh also spoke about her Netflix stand-up experience and working with fellow comedians like Samay Raina, Vir Das, and Vikramaditya Motwane.

articles.title: Overseas French nationals cast votes to elect councillor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: French nationals residing in Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala participated in elections to elect Councillors for the French living abroad. The election was held at four polling stations across these regions, with voting taking place from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.  Elected by direct universal suffrage for a six-year term, the Councillors represent the French community and sit on the Consular Council, advising on matters such as educational scholarships, social assistance, and support for local French associations. The French Consulate organized these elections, which are held worldwide in 2026.

articles.title: Ruturaj Gaikwad replaces injured Riyan Parag in India A squad for SL tri-series
articles.rephrased_article: The BCCI announced that Ruturaj Gaikwad has been added to the India A squad for the upcoming tri-series in Sri Lanka as a replacement for injured Riyan Parag.  Parag, who was playing with a hamstring injury, will be out for nearly three months. The series will feature Sri Lanka A, India A, and Afghanistan A, and will take place from June 9 to June 21, 2026 in Dambulla.   The team will also play two long-form matches against Sri Lanka A after the tri-series.

articles.title: Nepal PM says India, Nepal ‘encroached’ each other’s territories, triggers row | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah stated that he has learned of potential Nepalese encroachment on Indian territory, suggesting a complex border dispute. Shah emphasized the need for both countries to resolve the issue through diplomatic channels with expert assistance. He also revealed discussions with China and the United Kingdom, highlighting the historical context of the dispute.  However, several former diplomats and experts have questioned Shah's assertion, noting that most border issues have been resolved and cross-border farming arrangements do not constitute state encroachment.

articles.title: Bihar BJP’s Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya mega training campaign-2026 concludes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bihar BJP concluded its "Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Mega Training Campaign-2026" on May 31, 2026. The month-long campaign, which involved nearly 20,000 party workers across all 52 organizational districts, focused on training in organizational, ideological, and political subjects.  Bihar BJP President Sanjay Saraogi, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, and State Training Convenor Mrityunjay Kumar Jha addressed the concluding sessions of the campaign. The training curriculum covered a wide range of topics, including national challenges, government initiatives, organizational structure, and cultural nationalism.  Mr. Jha praised the campaign's success in demonstrating exemplary organizational capability and discipline.

articles.title: I could have become Deputy CM: Premallatha Vijayakant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMDK general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant stated that her party does not seek positions or seats, despite the perception that they "bargain" for them. She claimed the DMDK remains loyal to the DMK alliance and would have been offered a Deputy Chief Minister position had she approached Chief Minister  Edappadi K. Palaniswami. Vijayakant also criticized Palaniswami, alleging he insulted the DMDK and disregarded their contributions, leading to their decision to form an alliance with the DMK.

articles.title: In the Trump era, ‘The Boys’ went from satire to prophecy | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Boys, a TV show originally conceived as satire, has become increasingly prophetic in its portrayal of the Trump era. The show's creator, Eric Kripke, acknowledged that Homelander, the show's most dangerous villain, was inspired by Donald Trump. Parallels between Trump and Homelander include their self-proclaimed godhood and claims to have a quasi-divine sense of mission.  The show's ending highlights the resilience of capitalism and the enduring influence of powerful institutions, suggesting that even defeating villains like Homelander does not alter the system that created them.

articles.title: Gujarat CM participates in toy collection drive for underprivileged children - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel participated in a toy collection drive called "Let Kids Play, Let Kids Bloom" at Aarohi Twins Bungalow in Bopal-Ghuma. The campaign, inspired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, encourages donations of unused toys from well-off families to underprivileged children.  Patel emphasized the importance of play and social responsibility in fostering empathy and compassion among youth. He urged citizens to contribute generously to bring joy to children from economically weaker sections.

articles.title: ‘With my fellow anti-national Soros agents’: Rahul Gandhi’s dig at Centre over CBSE row | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, met with students who alleged they were labeled "anti-nationals" and "deep state agents" for questioning the CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system.  Gandhi expressed support for these students, demanding a bright future for them while criticizing the government's response to their concerns. The CBSE has defended its contract process, stating it followed proper protocols and awarded the contract to Coempt Edu Teck based on a competitive bidding process.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Students labeled 'anti-national' for raising concerns about an educational system raises alarm.

articles.title: Taiwan condemns China after New York Times reporter expelled after presidential interview | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan’s presidential office condemned China for expelling its reporter, Vivian Wang, following an interview with President Lai Ching-te. The New York Times reported that the Chinese government cited the interview as the reason for Wang's expulsion.  Karen Kuo, spokesperson for the Taiwan presidential office, stated that China’s actions are a violation of press freedom and highlight its instability on the world stage. Neither China’s foreign ministry nor the US State Department responded to requests for comment.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Expulsion of a journalist for interviewing a president is a clear suppression of press freedom.

articles.title: ‘Father was a farmer, family hoped he would become a doctor’: Dreams, lives cut short in Saket building collapse | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Ravi Prakash (26) and Nalin (22), both aspiring doctors, were among six people killed when a four-storey building collapsed in Saidullajab, Delhi. The incident occurred on Saturday evening as the victims gathered for dinner at a kitchen adjacent to the structure.  The building's collapse was attributed to illegal construction work that had been ongoing for several months, according to police. Ekta, Alok, and Kapil were also killed in the collapse, along with Parvati, who ran the kitchen where they were dining. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has suspended two engineers responsible for the area's dereliction of duty and negligence.

articles.title: Police step up deployment to manage traffic as schools reopen in city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Ernakulam district have implemented extensive traffic management plans to ensure the safety of students returning to school on Monday.  The plan includes deploying hundreds of personnel, restricting tipper lorry movement during peak hours, and conducting patrols for drunk driving and drug-related offenses. District Police Chief Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar stated that 700 officers will be deployed between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m., and again from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., with additional patrol teams throughout the city.  The Ernakulam Rural Police have also prepared deployment and surveillance plans focusing on school transport safety, including inspections of school buses for permits and fitness certificates.

articles.title: Edappally-Moothakunnam NH widening deadline extended to December - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has set a new deadline of December for completing the six-laning works on the Edappally-Moothakunnam stretch of NH 66.  The project aims to increase vehicle speeds and widen the highway to 45 meters, including service roads, drains, and allied infrastructure. While the newly constructed bridge at Varapuzha is operational, another bridge under construction at Moothakunnam is ready for opening. NGOs, residents’ associations, and people's representatives have renewed their demand for additional underpasses along the stretch to improve safety, particularly in densely populated areas with educational institutions and places of worship.  The NHAI has expressed willingness to provide funds to local bodies for waterlogging prevention measures on the highway.

articles.title: CBSE row: Rahul Gandhi Meets students, takes dig at government | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the Centre over the CBSE On-Screen Marking (OSM) controversy, highlighting a video interaction with students who alleged discrepancies in their answer sheets.  Gandhi expressed support for the students and vowed to ensure they receive a bright future despite facing accusations from the government. He also jokingly referred to them as "anti-national" and "terrorists."

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: Daughters killed for dowry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Giribala Singh, a retired Bhopal district judge, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on May 28th following her daughter-in-law Twisha Sharma's dowry harassment and death case. The arrest followed a six-hour investigation and questioning at her residence.  The arrest came after the Madhya Pradesh High Court quashed the anticipatory bail granted to Singh by a local court, amid allegations of bias and lack of cooperation from the police.

articles.title: Kohli powers Bengaluru to ‘stuff of dreams’ back-to-back IPL titles | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Virat Kohli led Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to their second consecutive Indian Premier League (IPL) title with a five-wicket victory over the Gujarat Titans.  Kohli's unbeaten 75 and inspired bowling, including a disciplined attack from Rasikh Salam, helped RCB chase down Gujarat's total of 155-8. This marks the second consecutive IPL title for RCB, joining a list of elite captains like MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma.

articles.title: ‘Battle of Hogwarts’ memes flood internet as PSG Champions League celebrations turn violent in France | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Social media users compared the violence in Paris following PSG’s Champions League victory to scenes from the Harry Potter films, particularly the Battle of Hogwarts.  The celebrations turned into widespread unrest across France, resulting in 219 injuries, nearly 800 arrests, and one fatality.  French authorities deployed over 22,000 officers to contain the violence after similar disturbances followed PSG’s previous European triumph. Laurent Nuñez, French Interior Minister, confirmed that 57 police officers sustained minor injuries during the clashes between football supporters and police.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: Daughters killed for dowry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CBI arrested retired Bhopal district judge Giribala Singh on May 28th in connection with her daughter-in-law Twisha Sharma's dowry harassment and death case.  Singh was taken into custody following six hours of investigation and questioning, after a Madhya Pradesh High Court quashed her anticipatory bail granted by a local court earlier that day. Samarth Singh, Twisha’s husband and Giribala Singh’s son, is already in CBI custody. Dozens of reporters were present as the team moved from the house where Twisha was found dead to the police station.

articles.title: CBSE row: Rahul Gandhi Meets students, takes dig at government | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, criticized the Centre over the CBSE On-Screen Marking (OSM) controversy. He shared a video of an interaction with students who alleged issues with their answer scripts and claimed they were labeled as "anti-nationals" by the government.  Gandhi stated that he would ensure these students receive a bright future despite facing insults from authorities.

articles.title: ‘Battle of Hogwarts’ memes flood internet as PSG Champions League celebrations turn violent in France | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Celebrations following Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory over Arsenal in Budapest descended into widespread unrest across France, leaving hundreds injured and prompting nearly 800 arrests. The violence began after the Eiffel Tower was illuminated in PSG's colors, escalating to clashes between football supporters and police, vandalism, vehicle fires, and even a fatality on Paris’s ring road.  Social media users responded with humorous comparisons between the chaos in Paris and scenes from the Harry Potter franchise, drawing parallels to battles depicted in films like "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2."

articles.title: Corruption crackdown: Rajasthan government dismisses 20 officials, suspends 332 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan government has launched a zero-tolerance campaign against corruption and administrative negligence, dismissing 20 officials, suspending 332 others, and halting pensions for 17 personnel.  Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma directed strict action against erring officials, emphasizing the need for improved accountability and transparent governance. The crackdown includes investigations into over 577 cases, with further action anticipated.

articles.title: Suman Kalyanpur death: Veteran playback singer dies at 89 in Mumbai - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Suman Kalyanpur, a celebrated Indian playback singer, died on Sunday evening at the age of 89 in Mumbai.  The veteran singer, known for her melodious voice and classical finesse, left behind a rich musical legacy spanning over six decades. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, along with other prominent figures like Sharad Pawar and Eknath Shinde, mourned the loss of the "divine voice" who enriched India's musical heritage.  Her timeless songs in Marathi, Hindi, and several regional languages will continue to resonate with audiences for years to come.

articles.title: Nicaraguan indigenous leader dies after three years in prison
articles.rephrased_article: Brooklyn Rivera, a Nicaraguan indigenous leader and founder of the Yatama movement, died in prison on Sunday. Daniel Ortega's government confirmed his death after 15 hours, refusing to release his body to his family.  The Nicaraguan Ministry of Health attributed Rivera's death to "physical and neurological deterioration" linked to a Covid-19 infection. The US State Department condemned the treatment of Rivera while in custody, calling it "unjust imprisonment." Amnesty International called for Rivera's immediate release, stating his critical health condition while in the government's care confirms the extreme risk he faced.

articles.title: Nicaragua confirms death in custody of Indigenous leader Brooklyn Rivera | Indigenous Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brooklyn Rivera, an Indigenous leader and activist, has died at age 73 in Nicaragua state custody after nearly three years of detention.  His death prompted outrage from human rights advocates who believe his cause of death was directly linked to the conditions of his imprisonment. The United States condemned the government's actions, demanding Rivera's unconditional release and calling for an end to the repression against dissidents in Nicaragua.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Death in custody raises concerns about abuse of power and suppression of justice.

articles.title: Five arrested for attack on TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee; another MP Kalyan Banerjee mobbed at Hooghly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal police arrested five individuals in connection with the attack on Trinamool Congress leader and MP Abhishek Banerjee.  Trinamool Congress leader Kalyan Banerjee was also attacked by a mob while he was on his way to submit a deputation. Mamata Banerjee, the Trinamool Congress chairperson, alleged that hospitals were pressured not to admit her nephew, who suffered injuries during the attack. The incident has sparked accusations of political violence from both sides. BJP leaders condemned the attacks but also claimed they reflected public anger towards the Trinamool Congress.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Politicians being attacked and hospitals pressured is a serious threat to democracy.

articles.title: Assam’s Council of Ministers to be expanded on June 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, Chief Minister of Assam, announced the expansion of the state's Council of Ministers on June 5th.  The expansion will bring the total number of ministers to a maximum of 19, aligning with the constitutional limit of 15% of the Assembly seats. The decision follows Mr. Sarma's previous statement that the government would expand its ministerial team over time.  He did not specify the number of new ministers or their identities.

articles.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court suspends former CBI Court special judge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab and Haryana High Court suspended Rajeev Goyal, a former special judge in the CBI Court, Panchkula, with immediate effect. The suspension order cites potential disciplinary proceedings related to his time as special judge and does not specify a reason.  Goyal is now posted as an additional district and sessions judge in Kaithal, where he will remain under suspension until further notice.

articles.title: Will CM-designate Shivakumar continue to hold charge of Bengaluru Development portfolio? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Will D.K. Shivakumar, the Chief Minister, faces pushback from Congress Ministers in Bengaluru who advocate for a full-time minister for the city's development portfolio.  Senior ministers like Ramalinga Reddy, K.J. George, and Krishna Byre Gowda are mentioned as potential candidates. While Shivakumar is keen to retain the portfolio, some argue his personal involvement has been significant in driving key projects and shaping Bengaluru's governance.

articles.title: ‘Monsoon holiday’ for sand collection begins June 1 along Godavari river - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has implemented a ban on sand excavation and collection along the banks of the Godavari River from June 1st to October 15th as part of its "monsoon holiday" policy. Mines and Geology Deputy Director D. Phanibhushan Reddy stated that the ban applies to semi-mechanized reaches and patta lands.  The East Godavari district authorities have stored 14.57 lakh metric tonnes of sand for distribution across 43 reaches, including Kovvuru, Peravali, Nidadavolu, Sithanagaram, Rajamahendravaram, and Tallapudi.

articles.title: 200 nursing officers attend Florence Nightingale CNE programme at Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Government Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital in Telangana hosted the first Florence Nightingale Continuing Nursing Education (CNE) Programme for ophthalmic nursing officers on May 31st. The program, attended by over 200 delegates from across the state, aimed to enhance professional development and provide recognized academic credits through the Telangana State Nursing Council.  The council awarded 5 credit hour points for participation in the program, which covered topics such as patient management, surgical procedures, and sterile protocols.

articles.title: The Hindu Huddle panel to throw light on AI and its impact - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India is grappling with the implications of AI's growing influence on its workforce and economy. Concerns exist about potential job displacement in technology sectors, while questions arise regarding India's ability to lead AI transformation globally. The government is seeking to address these concerns by ensuring adequate infrastructure and support for AI development.

articles.title: The apex court rings its own chain - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognisance of Twisha Sharma's death, raising concerns about institutional bias and procedural discrepancies. The court registered the case based on media reports and other circumstances, but later requested the media to refrain from recording witness statements. This action highlights a potential conflict of interest as the court simultaneously acts as both consumer and critic of the same source.

articles.title: White Paper on State govt.’s finances is being finalised - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, is finalizing a White Paper on the state's finances, which he promised to release upon assuming office. The document will address the financial situation left behind by the previous DMK government and claims that it was "empty."  Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson stated that the paper would be finalized in two weeks.

articles.title: BJP to host Nepal ruling party delegation in outreach to new govt. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Nepal's ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), led by chairperson Rabi Lamichhane, will visit India at the invitation of BJP president Nitin Nabin. The visit aims to foster political dialogue between the two countries and explore organizational practices, democratic processes, and people-centric outreach.  This follows the cancellation of Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's planned visit to Kathmandu due to a lack of assurance over a meeting with Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

articles.title: Palaniswami did not build a strong alliance to garner anti-incumbency votes, says PT chief K. Krishnasamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. K. Krishnasamy, founder of the Puthiya Tamilagam, believes that the fractured mandate in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly election could have been avoided if the AIADMK, led by Edappadi K. Palaniswami, had built a stronger coalition to address anti-incumbency sentiment. He argues that while the DMK delivered on some promises, people felt it failed to provide good governance and that the AIADMK's internal conflicts hindered its ability to capitalize on this dissatisfaction. Krishnasamy believes that other parties have consistently tried to build an alternative to the two major Dravidian parties, but TVK, led by C. Joseph Vijay, successfully channeled this sentiment and provided a viable option for voters.

articles.title: T.N. government announces zero-tolerance approach towards delays in sanctioning building plan approvals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government has implemented a zero-tolerance policy for delays in building plan approvals.  P. Madhusudhan Reddy, Director of Municipal Administration, issued guidelines requiring all fee payments to be made online and all interactions with applicants to be conducted through the online portal.  Any failure to enforce these protocols will result in disciplinary action. The government has set specific time-based guidelines for issuing "Planning Permission" and "Building Permits", ensuring that approvals are granted within stipulated timelines.

articles.title: Four convicts held for attacking Sulur sexual assault case accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Race Course police formally arrested four convicts, who were undergoing conviction at the Coimbatore Central Prison, for assaulting K. Karthi (35), the main accused in a sexual assault-cum-murder case near Sulur. The arrests followed a complaint filed by a prison officer and were conducted according to due procedures with the jurisdictional magistrate present.

articles.title: Recruitment exam candidates accuse Uttar Pradesh govt of suppressing drive for transparency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students appearing for recruitment exams in Prayagraj accused the Uttar Pradesh government of suppressing a movement demanding transparency in recruitment processes. The Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, a student collective, alleged irregularities, paper leaks, and mismanagement at examination centers. They demanded an independent inquiry into the Lekhpal main exam and called for the release of the UP (SI) examination scorecard. The students also threatened indefinite protests and urged the government to implement a technical monitoring system and establish a grievance redressal mechanism.
