The court emphasized that boys must be held accountable for their actions and warned against continued cruelty towards brides and their families.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee beaten up, TMC MP says ‘my head would have been split in two’; blames BJP for attack — Video | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, TMC MP and nephew of Mamata Banerjee, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal while visiting the family of a party worker killed during post-poll violence.  Videos show the attack, with witnesses alleging that Banerjee was assaulted by individuals throwing bricks and eggs. Banerjee blamed the incident on the BJP, claiming it was orchestrated to intimidate him and his supporters.  The TMC condemned the attack, while political allies like Congress and Samajwadi Party also expressed their condemnation.  BJP leaders have condemned the incident, urging for peace and law enforcement.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against an elected official raises serious concerns about safety and rule of law.

articles.title: Pakistan ISI-underworld module busted in Delhi; 9 arrested for plotting attacks - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's ISI and the Mumbai underworld are suspected of orchestrating attacks on key installations and security personnel in Delhi.  Nine individuals were arrested by the Delhi Police Special Cell, who recovered arms and explosives during a raid. The arrests follow an operation against a suspected sleeper cell linked to Pakistani gangster Shahzad Bhatti, which was busted earlier this week by the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad and Special Task Force.

articles.title: Tello Mobile Plan Review (2026): Low Cost, Reliable Service | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: A consumer is exploring the possibility of saving money on their phone plan by switching to a prepaid mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) from Tello Mobile, which uses T-Mobile's network. The consumer found that Tello's service, while lacking certain perks like international roaming or discounts, provided comparable data speeds and reliable reception to T-Mobile.

articles.title: Fitness Centres in Kolkata | Zumba, pilates, pickleball and more - Kolkata’s fitness culture moves beyond dumbbells and yoga mats - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Kolkata's wellness culture is shifting away from traditional gym routines and yoga, embracing more social and enjoyable activities. Dance fitness classes, run clubs, cycling groups, swimming clubs, and recreational sports like pickleball are attracting people seeking alternative ways to stay active and connect with others.  These trends emphasize the importance of consistency over intensity, making fitness a fun and engaging experience for residents.

articles.title: US green card policy | Trump administration makes U-turn on green card policy not all applicants need to leave US to apply: Report - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) clarified that not all immigrants seeking green cards will be required to return to their home countries. The clarification came after a memo from the US Citizenship and Immigration Services sparked backlash from lawmakers and immigration lawyers who feared it would lead to chaos. While the DHS stated that individual officers have discretion in deciding whether someone should be forced to apply abroad, some immigration attorneys are already questioning applicants about their reasons for seeking green cards within the US. Industry leaders warned that this policy could disrupt technology companies reliant on foreign professionals.

articles.title: Ram Charan on how Peddi changed him as an actor and person - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Ram Charan, in an exclusive interview with India Today, discussed his role as Peddi, a character representing those often unheard and needing recognition. He described the film as his most demanding role, pushing him both as an actor and a person. Charan revealed he suffered a wrist injury during filming that required extensive recovery time but was ultimately able to complete the project. The Telugu drama, directed by Buchi Babu Sana, is set for release on June 4th.

articles.title: Heavy rain, cool breeze turn Chandigarh weather pleasant; max temp drops to 25.3°C - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rain and thunderstorms swept through Chandigarh on Saturday, bringing a dramatic end to a severe heatwave that had plagued the region.  The city experienced a significant drop in temperature, with a maximum of 25.3°C and a minimum of 18°C, both well below normal. The downpour brought relief from the scorching heat, prompting residents to flock to public spaces like Sukhna Lake and Rock Garden. While the IMD predicts below-normal monsoon rainfall for 2026, Saturday's rain provided a welcome respite.  The weather is expected to remain cool and breezy through Sunday and Monday before returning to dry conditions from Tuesday onwards.

articles.title: CBSE OSM Coempt TCS row | CBSE on screen marking row: Rahul Gandhi says ‘rules’ bent to favour Coempt, cites TCS loss in auction - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi criticized the Modi government over the CBSE exam evaluation controversy, alleging that the board lowered technical requirements to favor COEMPT Eduteck Private Limited, a company with a poor track record. He demanded an independent judicial probe into the contract awarding process and accused the government of prioritizing its survival over student well-being.  Piyush Goyal, the Union commerce minister, countered Gandhi's claims, accusing him of "propaganda" while Dharmendra Pradhan, the Union education minister, defended the board's actions. Other prominent figures like Priyanka Chaturvedi and Mohammed Zubair have also raised concerns about potential manipulation and a coordinated campaign to promote the OSM system.

articles.title: Government unveils AI-enabled chatbot to help people lodge complaints - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre on Saturday unveiled an AI-enabled chatbot named 'Samadhan Didi' to help citizens raise grievances against government departments online.  Union Minister of State for Personnel Jitendra Singh called the chatbot a "democratisation of public grievance mechanism" and highlighted its ability to simplify, make accessible, and provide multilingual support. Developed by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) in collaboration with Bhashini, the chatbot is designed to automatically identify the appropriate Ministry, department, category, and sub-category for each grievance.  The chatbot was demonstrated live at the launch event and will be integrated into the CPGRAMS portal to reach citizens across India.

articles.title: Rivalry with Siddaramaiah, succession drama: DK Shivakumar's biography to hit the stands in mid-July
articles.rephrased_article: Rasheed Kidwai, a senior journalist, will publish his biography of D K Shivakumar, titled "Congress's Crisis Manager, Karnataka's Kingmaker," in mid-July. The book chronicles Shivakumar's rise as a prominent politician, detailing his involvement in various crises within the party and his role as a crisis manager.  The book explores Shivakumar's political journey from student leader to a figure of national interest, highlighting his connections with the Gandhi family and his contrasting roles as a strongman and strategist.

articles.title: RTI activist shot dead outside Lovely Professional University gate in Phagwara - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Simranjeet Singh, a Jalandhar-based RTI activist, was fatally shot outside the gate of Lovely Professional University in Phagwara. He had previously survived an attack and was reportedly without police security at the time of this incident.  Singh had been filing petitions against various individuals and organizations for over a decade. A .32 bore pistol and a .12 bore rifle were recovered from a Fortuner parked near the crime scene. Jalandhar Range DIG Naveen Singla confirmed that multiple teams, including Counter Intelligence units, are actively searching for the suspects.

articles.title: Keychron K2 HE Concrete Edition Review: Rock-Solid Typing | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Keychron has released a concrete keyboard, featuring standard plastic keycaps. The company's latest offering is well-made and coherent, despite its unconventional material choice.  The K2 HE's drab gray case, inspired by brutalist architecture, has garnered attention for its absurdity and industrial aesthetic.

articles.title: ‘Foundation stone very soon for Jindal mega industrial park’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Industries and Commerce department secretary N. Yuvaraj directed officials to expedite the foundation stone ceremony for the JSW Industrial Park Limited in S. Kota constituency. Jindal group representatives were consulted, with the Collector assuring action after speaking with them. The initiative comes amid farmer protests alleging unfulfilled promises from the company regarding job opportunities and land allocation.

articles.title: Kashmir witnesses peaceful Eid-ul-Adha celebrations amid heightened security
articles.rephrased_article: Eid-ul-Adha was celebrated peacefully across Jammu and Kashmir with religious fervor. Tens of thousands of devotees gathered at various mosques, Eidgahs, and shrines to offer prayers amid pleasant weather conditions.  Authorities intensified security preparations across the region, deploying personnel at key intersections and public places. Major congregations were witnessed at Hazratbal shrine on the banks of Dal Lake, Eidgah Srinagar, and prominent Eidgahs and Jamia Masjids in districts including Budgam, Anantnag, Baramulla, Shopian, Pulwama, Kupwara, and Bandipora.  The festival passed off peacefully without any major untoward incidents reported from any part of the Valley.

articles.title: Well-Known Educationists Arrested For Plotting Lawyer's Murder In Hyderabad | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Mujahid Alam Khan and his father Mahaboob Alam Khan, owners of educational institutions in Hyderabad, have been arrested for the murder of senior advocate Khaja Moizuddin.  The investigation revealed that long-standing disputes between the families over Waqf properties management issues led to a grudge against the deceased. The accused conspired with associates Hassan Ali alias Chaous and Muneer to hire Kishan alias Pappu who carried out the plan, resulting in Moizuddin's death outside his home.  The police commissioner stated that the Khans believed their legal setbacks were due to the deceased’s involvement in several legal proceedings against them.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Murder of a lawyer due to property disputes raises concerns about justice and safety.

articles.title: Cherry picking gains pace in Ganderbal amid price concerns
articles.rephrased_article: Cherry picking has begun in Ganderbal district, Kashmir, with the harvest season expected to peak over the next two weeks.  The Awwal, Double, and Mishri varieties are being harvested, while growers anticipate a bumper crop despite low market prices. Growers express disappointment as cherry prices remain low, despite the anticipated surplus. The district is known for its high production of cherries, accounting for nearly 60 percent of Kashmir's total output.

articles.title: Orissa HC Quashes Action Against Vigilance Judge, Orders Restoration Of Benefits | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Orissa High Court has quashed disciplinary proceedings and punishment against senior judicial officer Lalit Kumar Dash. The court found the findings against Dash based on presumptions and not backed by evidence.  The bench, comprising Justices Manash Ranjan Pathak and Sibo Sankar Mishra, ordered the restoration of all consequential service benefits to Dash before his retirement in July 2026.

articles.title: Woman doctor of Dera Bassi hospital 'attacked' by 2 men; staff suspend OPD services in protest - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: A woman doctor, Jot Noor, an anaesthetist at the Dera Bassi Sub-Divisional Hospital, was attacked by two unidentified men on Friday morning. The attack occurred after she was questioned about her profession and subsequently assaulted.  Dr Noor filed a complaint with the police, and hospital staff suspended outpatient services in protest of what they described as inaction from authorities and lack of security measures. Dr Dharminder Singh, the Dera Bassi Sub-Divisional Officer (SMO), confirmed a police complaint was filed and a case registered.

articles.title: Truck plunges into gorge at Zojila Pass; driver, conductor escape miraculously
articles.rephrased_article: A truck driver and his conductor escaped uninjured after their 14-wheeler truck plunged into a deep gorge near Zojila on the Srinagar-Leh highway. The accident occurred near Pani Matha in the Zojila sector, when the truck lost control before skidding off the road.  The truck was completely damaged, but both the driver and conductor were unharmed. Police and local authorities responded to the scene to investigate the cause of the incident.

articles.title: Hegseth: America Prepared To Resume Iran Attacks If Agreement Not Reached | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the United States is prepared to resume aerial attacks on Iran if diplomatic efforts fail.  He stated that the US has sufficient munitions and can handle multiple conflicts simultaneously, emphasizing President Trump's commitment to securing a nuclear-free Iran. A 60-day truce extension is being negotiated, with both sides working towards a permanent end to the conflict. The war, launched in February, has resulted in thousands of casualties and global economic strain due to Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Reshwari emerges as popular tourist retreat in Kupwara
articles.rephrased_article: Reshwari, a scenic destination in the foothills of Bangus Valley, has become increasingly popular among locals and tourists. Visitors are drawn to the gushing waters of Nallah Mawer, offering cool breezes and prime trout fishing opportunities.  The Forest Department's Langate Division maintains a rest house at Reshwari, providing accommodation and food facilities for visitors. Locals have reported an increase in tourist footfall, contributing positively to local economic growth.

articles.title: Indian football team gets rousing diaspora welcome in UK
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian men's football team received a warm welcome from the Indian diaspora in London ahead of their third-place match against Zimbabwe. Deputy High Commissioner Kartik Pande welcomed the players, emphasizing the unifying power of sports and highlighting India's progress in football. Kalyan Chaubey, president of the All India Football Federation (AIFF), also spoke about the importance of bilateral ties between India and the UK, particularly in fostering cooperation for football development. The team urged fans to support them at their final Unity Cup match.

articles.title: UAE Carried Out Dozens Of Strikes Against Iran With Support From US And Israel: Report | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) allegedly carried out dozens of airstrikes against Iran with support from the US and Israel, according to a report in The Wall Street Journal. The strikes began early in the war and continued until the April ceasefire, suggesting a deeper involvement than previously known.  The UAE targeted Iranian energy facilities in response to Tehran's attacks on their oil and gas infrastructure, including the Asaluyeh petrochemical complex.  The strikes were coordinated with the US and Israel, who provided intelligence.

articles.title: Rivalry with Siddaramaiah, succession drama: DK Shivakumar's biography to hit the stands in mid-July
articles.rephrased_article: A biography of D K Shivakumar, a prominent Congress leader in Karnataka, will be published in mid-July. The book, titled "Congress's Crisis Manager, Karnataka's Kingmaker," by senior journalist Rasheed Kidwai, details Shivakumar's rise to power and his rivalry with outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.  Kidwai highlights Shivakumar's reputation as a crisis manager, citing examples from his work in the Rajya Sabha election and Maharashtra. The book also explores Shivakumar's personal life and political journey, including his college days and close ties to the Gandhi family.

articles.title: 100 Days Nasha Mukt J&K Abhiyan | Paddar Premier League Cricket Tournament begins in Kishtwar
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Kumar Sharma, inaugurated the Paddar Premier League 2026 Cricket Tournament at Chhatargarh Stadium. The event was organized by the local administration in collaboration with the Department of Youth Services & Sports, Kishtwar, and other stakeholders.  Sharma encouraged youth participation in sports for personal development as part of the ongoing "100 Days Nasha Mukt Jammu & Kashmir Abhiyan." He also held a public grievance redressal meeting and inspected pilgrimage arrangements for the Shri Machail Mata Ji Yatra 2026. The event was attended by ADC Kishtwar Pawan Kotwal, SDM Paddar Dr. Amit Kumar, SDPO Paddar Vijay Bhagat, Tehsildar Paddar Vijay Gupta, and other officers.

articles.title: NMBA: DYSS holds sports activities in Rajouri
articles.rephrased_article: Department of Youth Services & Sports, Rajouri, organized sports and awareness activities as part of the "Nasha Mukt Jammu & Kashmir Abhiyan" in various zones of District Rajouri. The events included cricket and volleyball matches, training sessions, and orientation programs aimed at promoting fitness, discipline, teamwork, and a drug-free lifestyle among youth.  The initiatives witnessed enthusiastic participation from players and spectators, reflecting growing awareness and positive engagement with constructive activities.

articles.title: 8 Held After Violent Clash Inside Police Station In Odisha's Baripada | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Baripada Town police responded to a violent clash between two groups of youths at the police station on Friday evening.  The incident, which involved vandalism and assault, led to the arrest of eight individuals for their involvement in the altercation. Police sources said that the clash stemmed from an argument between youths from Baripada and Dhanpur areas over a car ride.

articles.title: Eid-ul-Adha celebrated with religious fervour across Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: Eid-ul-Adha was celebrated with religious fervor and communal harmony across the Jammu region, with thousands of devotees gathering at mosques and Eidgahs to offer prayers for peace, prosperity, and well-being. Deputy Commissioners, along with senior officers from the civil and police administrations, extended greetings to the Muslim community and visited major congregational sites.  MLA Arjun Singh Raju of Ramban district greeted the people on Eid-ul-Adha, while SSP Arun Gupta and other senior officers were also present. The celebrations passed off peacefully amidst elaborate security arrangements and festive spirit.

articles.title: Muted Celebrations For RCB Fans In Bengaluru Even If Team Wins; Restrictions By Police | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru City Police issued an advisory urging the public to avoid celebrations and disturbances after the IPL 2026 final on May 31st, following a tragic stampede in 2025 that resulted from fan celebrations. The advisory prohibits bursting firecrackers, road celebrations, large gatherings, and the use of dangerous materials. The police also urged people to maintain peace and discipline, follow traffic instructions, avoid consuming alcohol in public places, and refrain from engaging in fights or indecent behavior.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Restrictions on celebrations after a tragic event raise concerns about overreach.

articles.title: Ram Charan on how Peddi changed him as an actor and person - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Ram Charan spoke about his role in the upcoming Telugu film *Peddi*, stating it was a challenging and rewarding experience. He described the character as representing those who are often unheard and needing recognition, which he felt proud to portray.  The actor also revealed that playing the role pushed him further in his craft and left him feeling satisfied both personally and professionally. Ram Charan sustained a wrist injury during filming but persevered through it, ultimately completing the movie ahead of its June 4 release date. Directed by Buchi Babu Sana, *Peddi* also stars Janhvi Kapoor, Boman Irani, and Divyenndu.

articles.title: New Punjab BJP chief Kewal Dhillon won’t be able to deliver: Capt Amarinder - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Capt Amarinder Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister, criticized the appointment of Kewal Dhillon as the new BJP state chief, arguing that organizational capability should have been prioritized over caste considerations.  He expressed concern about the BJP's lack of a strong base in Punjab and suggested an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for electoral success. He also criticized the Aam Aadmi Party government's centralized control and highlighted the state's economic challenges, security concerns, and political instability.

articles.title: Govt committed to responsive governance, grassroots development: Deputy CM
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary conducted a tour of Nowshera, inspecting developmental projects and healthcare facilities. He met with delegations and individuals to address public issues and concerns. During his visit to the Sub-District Hospital Nowshera, Choudhary assessed patient care and directed authorities to improve healthcare services.  He also reviewed ongoing works at the Dak Bunglow Nowshera, emphasizing the need for timely completion and quality standards.

articles.title: Cyber Breach On CBSE Portal Lets Students See Erratic Charges, HDFC Gateway Blamed | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: A malicious attack on the payment system of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)'s revaluation portal, using the HDFC payment gateway, caused erratic fee displays for approximately 50 students. The breach occurred after a period of non-functionality and authorities are investigating the issue with experts from IIT Madras and IIT Kanpur, alongside the Digital Infrastructure Corporation of India.  To address the vulnerability, four public sector banks have been added as alternate payment gateways. Officials also noted infrastructure changes to improve capacity by shifting the portal to Amazon Web Services.

articles.title: Rajouri Encounter Day 7: More reinforcement rushed to encounter site
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing Indian Army operation, "Operation Sheruwali," in the Dori Maal area of Rajouri district, Jammu and Kashmir, has entered its seventh consecutive day.  Security forces have intensified their efforts to neutralize two suspected terrorists hiding in the dense forest area, with intermittent gunfire and explosions reported from the encounter site. Forces have deployed additional reinforcements and maintained a tight cordon around the forest, while round-the-clock surveillance is being conducted.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh man repeatedly slams toddler to ground, kills him to marry child’s mother - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A man, Viraj, has been accused of killing a one-and-a-half-year-old boy named Aarav in Uttar Pradesh's Firozabad.  Viraj, who allegedly wanted to marry the child's mother, Rati, is suspected of repeatedly slamming the toddler onto the ground after taking him from his aunt's house. The incident was captured on CCTV and police have launched a manhunt for Viraj.

articles.title: Over 45000 BLOs Fan Out As Door-To-Door SIR Survey Begins In Odisha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India in Odisha began a comprehensive Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls on Saturday, involving 45,255 Booth Level Officers (BLOs). The process aims to ensure the accuracy of voter lists ahead of future elections. BLOs are visiting households to distribute enumeration forms and assist voters with updating their details.  The SIR will continue until June 28th, with officials requesting all eligible Indian citizens to be included in the voter list while removing ineligible entries. Political parties have been asked to appoint Booth Level Agents (BLAs) for every polling station to ensure transparency. The draft electoral roll will be published on July 5th, and claims and objections can be filed until September 2nd.

articles.title: Congress move to bring Girish Chodankar back to helm Goa unit sparks discontent | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Congress appointed Girish Chodankar as the new Goa Pradesh Congress Committee (GPCC) president, replacing Amit Patkar. This move has sparked discontent among some party leaders who question Chodankar's 2022 performance in Goa and his appointment after a three-year absence from the post.  Patkar, who skipped the event where Chodankar took charge, is reportedly planning to form a new political party with his supporters. The AICC has also appointed three new state working presidents: M K Shaikh, Altone D’Costa, and Carlos Alvares Ferreira.

articles.title: CBSE To Make Answer Scripts Available For Students Through DigiLocker | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Union education ministry is planning a full audit of the Central Board of Secondary Education's (CBSE) on-screen marking system (OSM), from tendering to implementation, following concerns about glitches and evaluation issues.  This comes after students raised questions about answer sheet access, discrepancies in scanned copies, and technical glitches during re-evaluation. The company chosen for the OSM work, Coempt Edu Teck, is based in Telangana and has faced allegations regarding its previous work in the state.

articles.title: Zero Tolerance Towards Corruption: Odisha CM Sacks Former Bhubaneswar Additional Tehsildar | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi dismissed former Bhubaneswar Additional Tahsildar Chittaranjan Pilla from government service for alleged irregularities in land administration decisions. The action follows departmental inquiries into several land-related cases during Pilla's tenure, which revealed significant administrative misconduct.  The state government emphasized its commitment to transparency and accountability in public administration, sending a strong message against corruption within government offices.

articles.title: Bengal News: TMC-allied Tollywood actor Parambrata Chatterjee gets arrest shield as Rograni post bites back - West Bengal News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Actor Parambrata Chatterjee and actress Swastika Mukherjee are facing legal action for social media posts made in 2021 following the West Bengal Assembly elections. The posts, which included a call to "declare World 'Rograni Dibosh' Day," have resurfaced after the BJP won the recent state election, leading to an FIR filed against them.  Chatterjee and Mukherjee are accused of inciting violence by their comments, with authorities citing sections of the Indian Penal Code that pertain to incitement and promoting enmity between groups. Chatterjee sought anticipatory bail from the Calcutta High Court, which granted it for four weeks pending investigation. The case has drawn criticism from BJP leaders who accuse Chatterjee of political opportunism, while some critics have labeled him a "chameleon" for shifting his allegiances.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of power by filing charges for old social media posts after a political shift.

articles.title: Japanese proverb of the day: Money grows on the tree of persistence' | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A Japanese proverb, "Money grows on the tree of persistence," emphasizes that financial success is often achieved through sustained effort rather than instant gratification. The proverb compares wealth to fruit growing on a tree, suggesting that long-term commitment and consistent hard work are essential for achieving significant results. This message is particularly relevant for students, entrepreneurs, and professionals working towards their goals, reminding them that patience and consistency matter more than talent alone.

articles.title: Aam Aadmi Party scores big in Punjab civic elections - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) secured a resounding victory in Punjab's urban local body elections, winning control of five municipal corporations and nine nagar panchayats.  Bhagwant Mann, the Chief Minister, hailed the outcome as "historic" and attributed it to AAP's model of good governance. The party also performed strongly in 19 nagar panchayats, securing a majority in most areas. Manish Sisodia, AAP Punjab affairs in-charge, emphasized the landslide victory as a testament to the people's endorsement of their model.  The Congress finished second, while Independents secured third place.

articles.title: Haryana government has assured to maintain 1,000 cusecs of water supply through Munak Canal: Delhi CM | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Minister Rekha Gupta assured that the state will supply 1,000 cusecs of water to Delhi daily through the Munak Canal.  The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) is currently producing around 900-924 cusecs of water per day, but faces a shortfall of over 300 MGD during peak summer. The DJB has been working to maintain production and ensure minimal disruption for residents, while also addressing complaints related to water scarcity. Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh highlighted the challenges posed by the low Yamuna water level at Wazirabad Barrage, but emphasized efforts to sustain water production.  The CM directed officials to address all water leakage complaints and deploy more tankers in affected areas.

articles.title: Rivalry with Siddaramaiah, succession drama: DK Shivakumar's biography to hit the stands in mid-July
articles.rephrased_article: Rasheed Kidwai, a senior journalist, will publish his biography of D K Shivakumar, titled "Congress’s Crisis Manager, Karnataka’s Kingmaker," in mid-July. The book details Shivakumar's rise as a prominent politician, from student leader to crisis manager for the party, and explores his complex personality.  The book will cover key moments in Shivakumar's life, including his political career, personal experiences, and relationships with influential figures like Ahmed Patel and the Gandhi family.

articles.title: Kerala school principal was suspended 2 days before retirement for ‘insulting’ CM. To his rescue: The CM | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister V D Satheesan directed the general education department to withdraw the suspension of a government school principal, Javad S, who was accused of insulting him on social media. The suspension order alleged that the principal posted an edited photo of Satheesan, which violated service rules and government circulars regarding social media use.  The decision came two days before the principal's retirement on May 31st.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee heckled | TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee allegedly manhandled by agitating locals at Sonarpur in Bengal's South 24 Parganas: Police - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress national general secretary, was physically attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal, while visiting families of post-poll violence victims.  The incident occurred after he arrived to meet the family of Sanju Karmakar, a victim of the violence.  Local residents shouted "thief" slogans and hurled objects at him. Derek O'Brien, leader of Trinamool in Rajya Sabha, condemned the attack and called for action from the police. Opposition leaders across parties, including Samik Bhattacharya (BJP), Mallikarjun Kharge (Congress), Akhilesh Yadav (SP), Arvind Kejriwal (AAP), and Tejashwi Yadav (RJD), condemned the attack on Banerjee and called for an end to political violence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Physical assault on a political leader by a mob raises concerns about law and order.

articles.title: Quote of the day from Moulin Rouge: ‘The greatest thing you’ll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return’ | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Baz Luhrmann's 2001 film *Moulin Rouge!* continues to resonate with audiences for its enduring message of love and its deeply romantic storytelling. The film stars Ewan McGregor as Christian, an idealistic writer, and Nicole Kidman as Satine, a star performer at the famed Parisian cabaret.  The quote "The greatest thing you’ll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return" delivered by John Leguizamo's Toulouse-Lautrec encapsulates the film's central theme of genuine human connection outweighing wealth, status, and ambition. The film explores the transformative power of love through its protagonists' journeys, highlighting both its joys and challenges.  The quote's enduring appeal lies in its universality, reflecting the profound experience of being loved and reciprocated.

articles.title: Reshuffle in Udhampur Police, SHOs, officers transferred
articles.rephrased_article: District Police Udhampur has ordered the transfer and posting of several officers with immediate effect. Inspector Purshotam Kumar was transferred from Rehmbal to Ramnagar, while Inspector Nishant Gupta moved from DPL Udhampur to Chenani.  Inspector Parvez Sajad, currently at DPL Udhampur, will assume charge as SHO of Udhampur after the relieving of the current officer, Abhijeet Sirohi. Other transfers include Inspector Sumit Magotra moving to Rehmbal and PSI Manveer Singh being transferred from Ramnagar to Udhampur.  PSI Varun Sharma has been moved to Battal Ballian as Incharge Police Post, while PSI Ravinder Kumar was transferred from Battal Ballian to Udhampur. The transfers are intended to improve the administration and efficiency of the police department across the district.

articles.title: 7 dead as car gets crushed between two container trucks in Pune
articles.rephrased_article: Seven people were killed and over a dozen injured in a horrific accident on the Mumbai-Bengaluru Highway in Pune city. A car became trapped between two container trucks that caught fire after one lost control due to a suspected brake failure, according to Deputy Commissioner of Police Sambhaji Kadam.  Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar, who visited the scene, said the fire erupted due to the impact of the collision. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced ₹5 lakh ex-gratia for the families of the deceased.

articles.title: PCI invites claims from eligible Associations of Persons for 15th Term Reconstitution
articles.rephrased_article: The Press Council of India has issued a notice inviting claims from eligible associations managing news agencies for its 15th term. The deadline to submit claims is June 19, 2026, and the process follows Section 5(3)(c) of the Press Council Act, 1978.  The Press Council has also completed its 14th term.

articles.title: India Preparing For Operation Sindoor 2.0: Army Chief | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: General Upendra Dwivedi, the Chief of Army Staff, stated that India is preparing for a potential second phase of Operation Sindoor. He emphasized that while the current situation is a temporary cessation of hostilities, the Indian military, including the Air Force and Navy, remains prepared should a fresh operation be necessary.  Dwivedi highlighted the importance of information warfare in uniting the nation behind a common narrative to ensure victory. India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, following a terror attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, which escalated into missile and drone strikes by Pakistan against Indian targets.

articles.title: Keychron K2 HE Concrete Edition Review: Rock-Solid Typing | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Keychron has released a concrete keyboard, featuring a gray case and standard plastic keycaps. The company's latest product aims to bridge the gap between industrial aesthetics and functional design, offering a well-made and coherent typing experience despite its unconventional material.  The K2 HE keyboard is generating buzz for its unique construction and serves as a conversation starter with its stark appearance.

articles.title: Governors cannot sit indefinitely on Bills, says SC, but stops short of fixing timeline
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that neither the Governor nor the President can be subject to fixed timelines for granting assent to Bills passed by state legislatures. The court emphasized that such delays undermine democratic governance and are against the principles of federalism.  The bench, led by Chief Justice BR Gavai, unanimously rejected the "deemed assent" mechanism previously granted in a Tamil Nadu case, stating it encroaches upon the constitutional authority of the Governor or President. While several states argued for specific time limits to address delays, the court emphasized that enforcing such timelines would contradict the Constitution's flexibility and separation of powers.

articles.title: 43 tonnes of cherries from Kashmir transported through SLR, parcel vans
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Railways has transported over 43 tonnes of fresh cherries from Jammu and Kashmir to major markets across the country through special parcel vans and SLR (Seating cum Luggage Rake) coaches. This initiative, facilitated by the Jammu Railway Division, aims to provide efficient and economical logistics solutions for fruit growers and traders in the region. Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal highlighted that this service is a testament to the growing trust in rail services, enabling farmers to reach better prices and consumers with fresh produce.  The railway administration encourages all stakeholders to utilize the rail parcel service and support the marketing of agricultural produce from Jammu and Kashmir.

articles.title: Odisha Gymnastics Apologises After Dead President's Name On Letterhead Sparks Row | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Kumar Sahoo, secretary of the Odisha Gymnastics Association, apologized for continuing to use the late president Samir Dey's name on official letterheads.  Sahoo acknowledged an oversight error and stated that the association is working to rectify it. A complaint has questioned how the OGA secured nearly Rs 98 lakh from the state government for the 2026 National Gymnastics Championships while invoices exceeding Rs 1.96 crore continued to bear Dey's name as president.

articles.title: Industry stakeholders seek balanced expansion of J&K industrial package ahead of high-level review
articles.rephrased_article: Industry stakeholders and experts have expressed concerns about the New Central Sector Scheme (NCSS) for J&K, highlighting a need for a more balanced approach to industrial growth. They suggest that the scheme's current focus on select pockets with better infrastructure could lead to uneven distribution of investments and employment opportunities across the 20 districts of the Union Territory.  They also emphasize the importance of addressing existing industrial units' challenges through revival programs, market support for local enterprises, and a more inclusive policy framework that supports both new and existing businesses. The upcoming review meeting on May 30th is expected to address these concerns and strengthen the industrial policy framework in J&K.

articles.title: Fake Cockroach Janta Party App Spreading Malware, Cyber Security Firm Warns | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: TraceX Labs, a Mumbai-based cybersecurity firm, has warned of a fake Android app mimicking the popular satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that steals personal information. The report, published on May 22nd, reveals the app requests numerous permissions and connects to suspicious websites after installation.  Experts say criminals are exploiting meme culture and political trends to distribute this spyware through unofficial APK links, particularly targeting younger users.  The researchers urged users not to download APK files from unofficial sources and asked Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the CJP platform, to publicly confirm the app's unrelated status.

articles.title: Aadhaar upgrade soon: Update your mobile number in minutes using new app | Aadhaar Updates | How to change your mobile number
articles.rephrased_article: UIDAI is launching a new app that will allow users to update their mobile numbers without visiting an enrollment center. The update, which costs ₹75 and may take up to 30 days to process, can be accessed through the mAadhaar app on Android and iOS devices. Users must align their face within the app's frame, enter their Aadhaar number and OTP, and verify the new number using facial recognition.

articles.title: No free services for IPL final, clarifies BMRCL - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has denied claims of offering free metro travel for Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) fans on May 31st. The corporation stated that it did not authorize any promotion or advertisement for free travel and urged the public to verify information through official channels, as unauthorized posts and messages are circulating online.

articles.title: Dr Jitendra to inaugurate ‘Lavender festival’ at Bhaderwah on June 6: Director CSIR-IIIM Jammu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State in the PMO, will inaugurate the 4th Lavender festival organized by CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM), Jammu. The festival, themed "Lavender goes global," celebrates the success of lavender cultivation and rural entrepreneurship in J&K.  The event, under the mentorship of Dr Jitendra Singh and guidance of Dr N Kalaiselvi, Director General CSIR and Secretary DSIR, will feature startup exhibitions, live demonstrations, and technical sessions on lavender cultivation and aroma-based products. The festival aims to promote agri-based entrepreneurship, sustainable livelihoods, and innovation in the aromatic crops sector.

articles.title: Astrologer's Advice Or Rahul Gandhi's Availability? Reason For June 3 Pick For Shivakumar's Swearing-In | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: DK Shivakumar, the newly elected chief minister of Karnataka, is set to be sworn in on June 3rd.  The date was chosen after consultation with an astrologer, who deemed it auspicious. A delegation led by Shivakumar will meet Governor Thawarchand Gehlot to discuss the ceremony. The swearing-in is expected to be a simple affair and may involve the oath-taking of two deputy chief ministers, along with Yathindra Siddaramaiah, son of the outgoing chief minister Siddaramaiah.

articles.title: Cyclone Ditwah leaves 366 dead in Sri Lanka; rain alert in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry
articles.rephrased_article: Cyclone Ditwah, which has weakened into a deep depression, continues to hover near the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coasts. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin held a review meeting with district collectors to assess the situation, while the Greater Chennai Corporation deployed 103 boats for rescue operations. The IMD predicts further rainfall in the region, leading to disruptions in normal life and damage to crops. Sri Lanka announced a special public-private fund to support recovery efforts after the devastating floods and landslides caused by Cyclone Ditwah, resulting in a death toll of 366 with 367 people still missing. International assistance is pouring in from countries like the UK, China, Australia, and Nepal.

articles.title: Eye on poll, BJP picks Kewal Singh Dhillon as first Jat Sikh Punjab unit chief - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP appointed Kewal Singh Dhillon as the new president of its Punjab unit, a move seen as an attempt to broaden the party's appeal beyond its Hindu-based image.  Dhillon, a Jat Sikh leader with experience in both Congress and BJP, is expected to focus on farmers' welfare and ensure minimum support price (MSP) for crops. The BJP hopes Dhillon will help them gain power in the 2027 Assembly elections. While Sunil Jakhar, who previously held the position, has not been assigned a new role yet, sources suggest he will remain influential in the party's Punjab campaign.

articles.title: BSF to get stronger security grid along borders: Amit Shah
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, the Union Home Minister, praised the BSF for its service in safeguarding difficult borders over the past 60 years. He highlighted the harsh conditions faced by BSF personnel and emphasized the government's efforts to strengthen border security through advanced technology and infrastructure improvements.  Shah also announced the establishment of a center to educate citizens about BSF duties and the development of a "quadrangular security grid" for improved territorial security.

articles.title: Indian Man Paid Traffickers To Assault Minor In US; Sentenced To 10 Years | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Kavankumar Patel, a 27-year-old Indian man working at the AmericInn hotel in Omaha, Nebraska, was sentenced to 10 years in prison for sexually assaulting a minor girl after paying human traffickers. Eduardo Jose Perdomo, Michel Martinez-Gonzalez, and Alfredo Zambrano-Hurtado were also charged with sex trafficking of minors.  The investigation began on January 6, 2025, when police discovered evidence of sex trafficking at the hotel. The Homeland Security Task Force and the Omaha Police Department rescued two minor girls who had been brought to the hotel from out of state for commercial sex.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Sex trafficking of minors is a serious crime and abuse of power.

articles.title: After SCO summit drive, Modi, Putin share car ride again as Russian president begins 27-hour India visit | India News
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president, arrived in New Delhi for a 27-hour visit aimed at strengthening an enduring partnership with India.  The visit, which includes meetings and events focused on trade, defense, and energy cooperation, follows a shared car ride between Modi and Putin after the SCO summit. The two leaders are expected to discuss a range of issues, including India's widening trade deficit with Russia and potential collaboration on small modular reactors.  The visit is significant as it comes amidst strained relations between India and the United States.

articles.title: No ‘double standards’ in fight against terrorism: NSA Doval in Russia
articles.rephrased_article: Ajit Doval, National Security Advisor of India, called for decisive action against terrorism and a rejection of double standards in the fight against it during an international security forum in Russia.  He emphasized the need for reforms to existing structures and institutions established after World War II, ensuring greater representation from the Global South.  Doval also highlighted the importance of safe and uninterrupted trade through critical shipping routes like the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, particularly given ongoing conflicts in West Asia. During his visit to Russia, Doval met with Sergei Shoigu, Secretary of the Security Council of the Russian Federation, to discuss defense, security, energy, and trade-economic ties.  The meeting also served as an opportunity to exchange views on preparations for the upcoming BRICS national security advisers' meeting in New Delhi.

articles.title: Permanent Hormuz Transit Fees To Hit Consumers, Temporary Tolls Negotiable: Qatar | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Qatar's Deputy Prime Minister, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, rejected the idea of a permanent legal levy on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, stating it would ultimately impact consumers. He suggested temporary charges for specific needs like mine-clearing operations could be negotiable.  Sheikh Saoud also emphasized Qatar's desire to maintain diplomatic ties with Iran and called for a unified response from the Gulf Cooperation Council in dealing with Iranian actions.

articles.title: US, China trade journalist expulsions days after Trump visits Xi in Beijing
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration revoked the visa of a Chinese national working for Xinhua, in response to Beijing's expulsion of a New York Times reporter. This reciprocal action follows China's decision to expel Vivian Wang, a China correspondent for the newspaper, over the appearance of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te in a recorded interview at a DealBook Summit. The move has raised concerns among other Western media who might interview Lai and risk losing their reporting abilities within China.  The US State Department previously designated some major Chinese news groups as "foreign missions" and limited visas for journalists working for US media.

articles.title: 550 cancellations and several delays; IndiGo says operations to be normal by February | Onmanorama | India
articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo, the Indian airline, informed the DGCA that it would stabilize its operations by February 10, 2026, following over 550 flight cancellations due to implementation gaps of the new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms. The airline acknowledged misjudgments and planning gaps in implementing the rules, leading to disruptions and a fall in on-time performance. Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu expressed displeasure with the airline's response, while the DGCA will monitor real-time operations and ensure passengers are informed of cancellations well in advance. The airline has sought exemptions from specific FDTL requirements for A320 flights until February 10, 2026, which the DGCA will review.  The DGCA also inspected IndiGo's passenger handling at Delhi airport and instructed the airline to increase manpower and strengthen support services.

articles.title: Nine Nabbed For Links With ISI, Dawood; Had Planned Strikes On Sensitive Locations | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police arrested nine men with links to Pakistan’s ISI, Dawood Ibrahim, and an al-Qaeda-affiliated group, Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind. The suspects were planning attacks in Delhi, Mumbai, and other parts of the country, including targeting vital installations and security personnel.  The arrests followed a period of surveillance and officials are investigating possible cross-border linkages, funding channels, and overseas handlers.

articles.title: India is 'powerful' and 'modernising' its military, says Hegseth
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, US Secretary of War, stated that India is modernizing its military with heavy industrial and logistics capabilities to support high-end operations.  He also emphasized the importance of co-production between the US and India as part of a national manufacturing globalisation of defense. Hegseth discussed the US's defense strategy in the Asia-Pacific region, highlighting its role in maintaining regional security and calling for increased investment in defense by nations globally.  The Shangri-La Dialogue brought together top officials from 44 countries.

articles.title: Many, possibly students, feared trapped as building collapses in Delhi's Saket | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under debris.  The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) responded to the incident and deployed seven fire tenders, while police launched a search and rescue operation. The building housed a coaching institute on the ground floor and construction work was underway on upper floors. Residents are assisting with the rescue efforts, and authorities have not yet confirmed the number of people trapped.

articles.title: India signs BrahMos missile deal with Vietnam, nears pact with Indonesia | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Kumar Singh, India's Defence Secretary, confirmed that an agreement to supply BrahMos cruise missiles to Vietnam has been officially executed.  Singh also stated that a parallel defense contract with Indonesia is nearing completion. He emphasized that India prioritizes sharing advanced defense technologies with trusted strategic allies, particularly within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). This move signifies India's growing influence in Southeast Asia as it strengthens its defense diplomacy and seeks to cultivate reliable alliances and secure maritime domains.

articles.title: ‘Stop construction activities at Cubbon Park’: Walkers’ association stages protest | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Cubbon Park Walkers’ Association protested against construction activities within the protected park in Bengaluru, alleging a violation of the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975. The association claims the structure is an illegal addition and that officials have ignored their concerns.  However, an official from the government museum and Venkatappa Art gallery stated the construction is authorized by a committee headed by the additional chief secretary and is for a restroom to serve visitors.

articles.title: Stage set for DK Shivakumar’s swearing-in as CM on June 3; government, party rejigs on cards | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar, the newly elected leader of the Karnataka Congress Legislature Party (CLP), will be sworn in as Chief Minister on June 3rd.  The CLP unanimously chose him following the resignation of Siddaramaiah, who stepped down to make way for a power-sharing agreement with Shivakumar. The new CM is expected to appoint a new Cabinet and may include several new faces while dropping over half of the ministers from the previous government. K C Venugopal and Randeep Surjewala, both AICC officials, were present at the CLP meeting and confirmed the transition.  The Governor has invited Shivakumar to take oath along with his new ministers.

articles.title: Make dope tests mandatory for individuals joining govt services: Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhu | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu directed all departments to implement mandatory drug testing for government service applicants.  He also requested details on action taken against employees involved in drug trafficking and sought information regarding vacant posts, pending gratuity payments, and applications for compassionate grounds employment. Sukhu emphasized the state's commitment to combatting drug abuse and ensuring timely removal of fallen trees from forest land following recent storms. The meeting was attended by various senior officials including Chief Secretary Sanjay Gupta and Additional Chief Secretaries K K Pant and Onkar Chand Sharma.

articles.title: TMC panchayat member promises to return cut money, villagers blare reminders on loudspeakers - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in West Bengal's Cooch Behar district are using loudspeakers to remind a Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader, Jyotsna Barman, of a promised refund for "cut money" collected from beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.  The villagers allege that they were forced to pay commissions ranging from Rs 5,000 to Rs 25,000 to secure benefits and avoid delays in future installments during the previous TMC regime. The deadline for returning the "cut money" is June 4th, and residents have threatened fresh protests if the promise is not kept.

articles.title: How Iran's Hardliners Are Trying To Sabotage A Peace Deal With US
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's hard-line faction, including members of Parliament and the Supreme National Security Council, is opposing a potential US deal with Iran, using rallies and media to resist compromise.  The opposition argues against any negotiation terms, despite calls for unity from President Masoud Pezeshkian. State TV has been criticized for biased coverage against the talks, deepening political rifts within the country. Ali Bagheri Kani, a hard-line politician who serves as deputy secretary of the National Security Council, attempted to undermine negotiators by urging Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei to impose limits on the team. Despite internal disagreements, Khamenei continues to support the negotiating team.

articles.title: Indian citizenship proof: Can you prove your Indian citizenship? I'm not sure I can - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The author reflects on the complexities of proving Indian citizenship, highlighting the lack of a definitive document.  Despite having various documents like identity cards and voter IDs, they are unable to definitively prove their citizenship status. The author compares this situation to God's non-citizen status, emphasizing the ambiguity surrounding citizenship in India. They argue that while there are numerous definitions and documents claiming the opposite, there is no single document proving Indian citizenship. This lack of clarity highlights a frustrating paradox within the Indian legal system.

articles.title: CUET UG 2026 Exam Chaos: Technical Glitch Strands Thousands, Forces Postponement for 3,765 Students
articles.rephrased_article: National Testing Agency (NTA) and its technology partner TCS iON faced criticism for technical failures that disrupted the morning shift of the Common University Entrance Test Undergraduate (CUET UG) 2026 examination. Thousands of candidates were left stranded at exam centres across multiple cities, experiencing delays of up to two hours before being informed of the issue.  The confusion extended beyond students, with parents expressing concerns about conflicting information and a lack of official communication from NTA. Despite efforts by TCS iON to resolve the technical glitch, many candidates reported spending several hours waiting for clarity on the exam's status.

articles.title: Pete hegseth US Iran War Trump Aide Warns US "More Than Capable" Of Restarting Iran War
articles.rephrased_article: The United States warned it is capable of restarting the war with Iran after President Donald Trump stated his red lines for any potential peace deal, including preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. President Trump and US Central Command (CENTCOM) have signaled continued vigilance in the region while Iran's IRNA state news agency reported Iranian air defenses shot down a drone belonging to the US-Zionist aggressor enemy. Despite ongoing diplomatic efforts, including attempts to stop fighting in Lebanon, competing conditions remain as Iran demands the release of $12 billion before moving forward with negotiations and Trump insists on Iran removing mines from the Strait of Hormuz and ending its closure.

articles.title: From gambling on rains to exchange-traded rain futures, a full circle for Mumbai - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange Limited (NCDEX) will launch India's first weather derivatives on June 1st, based on rainfall deviation data from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). This follows a historical trend of rain-gambling in Mumbai during the late 19th century, where bets were placed on rainfall patterns and their impact on daily life.  The practice was eventually curtailed by authorities but continued to evolve into new forms of gambling like cotton price speculation and later, matka.

articles.title: Mosque, temple and modernisation: Can Kolkata airport become world-class? - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Sourav Sikdar, the BJP MLA from Uttar Dum Dum, and Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu, the Union civil aviation minister, have confirmed plans to relocate a mosque and a temple near Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport for its expansion. The relocation is part of a larger redevelopment project aimed at transforming the airport into a world-class facility with an Aerocity district similar to Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.  The government aims to boost economic benefits for the surrounding region, particularly the Uttar Dum Dum municipality, which currently earns around Rs 86 lakh annually from airport operations. The relocation of the mosque and temple is part of ongoing discussions that have been raised in Parliament since 1998.

articles.title: Bengaluru restaurant sealed for allegedly selling beef as mutton, 2 arrested | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Kayaloram Restaurant, located in Bengaluru, was sealed after police found that the restaurant had been serving beef as mutton to customers.  The incident came to light when a group of customers suspected their order was not mutton and reported it to the police. Avalahalli police arrested two individuals, Jijoo and Shimbu, both from Kerala, while another suspect, Abilash, is still at large. The seized meat samples have been sent for forensic examination, pending which the police will take appropriate legal action.

articles.title: Video: Trinamool Congress Leader Abhishek Banerjee Assaulted During Visit To Party Worker's House
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress leader, was attacked by a crowd in Sonarpur, West Bengal while visiting families affected by post-election violence. The incident occurred after his party's defeat in the assembly elections.  He was reportedly heckled and physically confronted amid heavy police presence. Derek O'Brien, Trinamool Congress national general secretary, condemned the attack and defended Banerjee. The BJP has denied involvement in the incident.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Physical assault on a political leader raises concerns about safety and rule of law.

articles.title: How West Asia crisis keeps analysts, policymakers guessing on volatile rupee - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: The rupee has weakened significantly since the beginning of the West Asia conflict, falling nearly 6% and trading at 95.72 to a dollar on May 27.  This decline is attributed to concerns over the prolonged standoff in the Gulf region and potential escalation of the conflict, which could further pressure the currency. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has attempted to stabilize the rupee by selling dollars, but this action depletes foreign reserves. While some economists advocate for a free-floating rupee, others believe that intervention is necessary to prevent further depreciation.  Experts predict the RBI will maintain its current policy stance on interest rates during its next meeting in June.

articles.title: Rabindranath Tagore on happiness and present moment: 'The butterfly counts not months but moments' | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Rabindranath Tagore, a celebrated Bengali writer, poet, and thinker, is known for his philosophy that happiness comes from enjoying each moment rather than focusing on time. Born in 1861, he received the Nobel Prize in Literature and composed national anthems for India and Bangladesh. His works, including poetry collections like "Gitanjali" and novels like "Ghare Baire," have influenced generations of Indians and continue to inspire readers worldwide.  His legacy extends beyond literature, as his music and philosophy remain influential today.

articles.title: ‘Matthe ke Aloo’: The gut-friendly UP dish nutritionists swear by with a ‘Gen Z’ twist | Health News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A nutritionist shared a recipe for Matthe ke Aloo, a gut-friendly dish popular in Uttar Pradesh.  Pratibha Singh, Professor of Nutrition & Dietetics at Manav Rachna International Institute of Research & Studies, confirmed that potatoes are often misunderstood but offer nutritional benefits when prepared without deep frying or excessive salt. Dr Singh explained that the recipe's ingredients like buttermilk, ghee, methi, hing, and turmeric support digestion and gut health. She emphasized that traditional Indian recipes, like Matthe ke Aloo, can guide future sustainable nutrition practices by combining plant-based foods with healthy fats and fermented dairy.

articles.title: Why archers Jyothi Vennam, Dhiraj Bommadevara are optimistic about Asian Games - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Jyothi Vennam and Dhiraj Bommadevara, India's top compound archer and male recurve archer respectively, secured their spots at the Asian Games after a successful selection trial. Despite the presence of young talent in the squad, they remain optimistic about India's performance.  They are confident that the team can achieve success despite the changes and will focus on building team spirit and improving areas where needed.

articles.title: Why the furore over Rathan Kelkar’s appointment as secretary to Kerala CM Satheesan - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rathan Kelkar, a former Kerala chief electoral officer, has been appointed secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan by the new UDF government. Kelkar was previously praised for his integrity and efficiency during his tenure as chief electoral officer under the previous Left Front rule. The opposition CPI(M) and BJP have questioned this appointment, citing a similar case in West Bengal where the chief electoral officer was appointed as chief secretary. However, Satheesan defends the decision, emphasizing Kelkar's track record and due process.

articles.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court suspends Kaithal’s Additional District and Sessions Judge, assigns no reason | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jagpreet Singh Sandhu, a Senior Correspondent at The Indian Express, based in Chandigarh, has been covering legal, crime, and environmental reporting for over a decade. His recent coverage includes detailed reports on judicial verdicts, financial scams, public health concerns, and the intersection of technology and law enforcement.  Sandhu's work often focuses on victim rights and highlights administrative lapses within various sectors.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Suspension of a judge without stated reason raises concerns about transparency and accountability.

articles.title: PSG vs Arsenal Champions League final: PSG retain title after 4-3 penalty win - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: PSG defeated Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the UEFA Champions League final, retaining their European crown.  The French champions overcame an early Arsenal goal and sustained pressure from the Gunners throughout extra time to secure victory. This marks PSG's second consecutive Champions League title defense, while Arsenal remains without a continental trophy.

articles.title: Video: Trinamool Congress Leader Abhishek Banerjee Assaulted During Visit To Party Worker's House
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress leader, was attacked by a crowd in Sonarpur, West Bengal while visiting families affected by post-election violence. The incident occurred as Banerjee attempted to meet with party workers who were allegedly targeted by political rivals following the party's defeat.  The crowd confronted Banerjee, shouting slogans and throwing eggs at him.  He was taken to Apollo Hospital for treatment, where his aunt, former chief minister Mamata Banerjee, also visited. The BJP has denied involvement in the incident, while Derek O'Brien, a Trinamool leader, condemned the attack and called for police protection for the families affected by violence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a leader suggests a breakdown of law and order.

articles.title: Gujarat hotel worker Kavankumar Patel jailed for 10 years in US for child sex trafficking at Omaha hotel
articles.rephrased_article: Kavankumar Patel, a 27-year-old Indian national, was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison for two counts of sex trafficking of a minor at the AmericInn hotel in Omaha, Nebraska. Judge Joseph F Bataillon imposed the sentence on May 26th after Patel admitted to taking cash from the hotel's front desk drawer to pay traffickers who allowed him and the victims to remain on the property for multiple days. The investigation was conducted by a multi-agency Homeland Security Task Force in coordination with the Omaha Police Department, which rescued two underage girls who had been transported from out of state for commercial sex.  The US Attorney's Office commended the law enforcement efforts and stated that they will continue to work hard to protect vulnerable victims.

articles.title: Who is Jugal Daterao? Indian-origin Walt Disney manager sentenced to 2.5 years in prison in Russia for smuggling | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A Walt Disney Company program manager, Jugal Daterao Sudhir, was sentenced to two years and six months in a Russian penal colony for drug smuggling after THC-infused gummies were found in his luggage.  Sudhir claimed the drugs were prescribed by a doctor in the United States to manage the effects of brain surgery. He arrived in Russia from Qatar earlier this year and was apprehended at Sheremetyevo International Airport. Sudhir, an Indian citizen who also worked for companies like WWE and Viacom, has over 15 years of experience in project management and software development.

articles.title: Mamata Banerjee vs BJP On Abhishek Banerjee Assault: Rulers Became Killers
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, former Bengal chief minister, accused the BJP of orchestrating an assault on her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, in Sonarpur, South 24 Parganas. The BJP vehemently denied any involvement and condemned the attack as unacceptable. Banerjee claimed the incident was pre-planned and that there was no police protection for him or his family.  The Congress also condemned the assault and demanded adequate security for all opposition leaders.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of political violence and lack of police protection raise serious concerns.

articles.title: "Must Erase Every Trace Of Colonial Mindset": J&K Lt Governor Manoj Sinha
articles.rephrased_article: The Kashmir Literature Festival began today, with Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha urging the event to erase colonial mindset and reclaim India's true history.  Sinha highlighted ancient Indian contributions to science, math, and astronomy, emphasizing that modern times saw India lose its habit of writing its own history. He stressed the importance of accurately representing India's "real history" and correcting historical distortions for global audiences.

articles.title: Odisha Vigilance Arrests Cooperative Official For Embezzling Rs 33.80L Govt Funds | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Vigilance arrested a former secretary of the Garhsantri Service Co-operative Society, Patitapaban Majhi, for allegedly misappropriating government funds amounting to Rs 33,80,963.  The embezzlement occurred between 2017 and 2018 while Majhi was responsible for handling daily financial collections and government deposits at the Angul United Central Co-operative Bank (AUCCB) headquarters. A case has been registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, with further investigation underway.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Embezzlement of public funds is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: Two killed as truck plunges into gorge, catches fire near Gangroo in Ramsoo on NH 44
articles.rephrased_article: A truck carrying limestone caught fire and plunged into a gorge near Gangroo in Ramban district, killing the driver, Shakir Ahmed Manhas, and his conductor, Mohammad Iqbal. The incident occurred on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway early Saturday morning.  Police personnel from Ramsoo police station, volunteers of the Himalayan Quick Response Team (QRT) Ramsoo, CRPF personnel, and Fire and Emergency Services responded to the scene and launched a rescue operation.

articles.title: Kejriwal's Claims Of IB Threats Backfire; Call Traced Back To AAP Leader | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its leader Arvind Kejriwal faced embarrassment after allegations of threats by the Intelligence Bureau (IB) and police backfired.  Gujarat Police arrested two men, including the party's Vadodara city unit president, for allegedly making a "threat call" to an AAP worker posing as an IB official. The investigation stemmed from a social media post by Kejriwal, who questioned the harassment of workers in Gujarat. The phone number linked to the alleged threat was traced back to Nitin Dobriya, a labor contractor, and his actions were allegedly orchestrated by Ashok Oza, the Vadodara unit president.  Gadhvi, the Gujarat AAP president, expressed shock at the incident and stated that the party will take appropriate action if connections or responsibilities emerge in Gujarat.

articles.title: Op Sindoor defined India's response to provocation: Army chief
articles.rephrased_article: General Upendra Dwivedi, Chief of Army Staff, praised the graduating cadets of the 150th course at the National Defence Academy (NDA) in Pune. He highlighted the success of Operation Sindoor, India's military exercise against terror infrastructure in Pakistan, as an example of precision and resolve in responding to provocation.  Dwivedi emphasized the importance of jointness and adaptability in today's security environment, urging cadets to uphold the high standards set by Operation Sindoor. He also commended the parade commander and Cheetah Squadron for their achievements.

articles.title: Ministers statements on paddy procurement run contrary to ground reality: BJP State chief N. Ramchander Rao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, BJP State president, criticized the inconsistent statements from Civil Supplies Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and other ministers regarding paddy procurement figures, alleging a lack of clarity from the State government.  He claimed that these inconsistencies highlight the plight of farmers who are facing distress sales due to delayed procurement. Rao also accused the Congress dispensation of misleading farmers with misinformation campaigns.

articles.title: How was FIR lodged 75 minutes before alleged recovery of weapons? J-K High Court seeks answers in terror case
articles.sentiment_target: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court has raised concerns about the timeline of a 2019 terror case, noting that the FIR was filed 75 minutes before the alleged recovery of arms. The court observed that the original FIR was missing from the trial record and directed the government to inform it whether the investigating officer remains in service.  The court also requested the petitioner's counsel to provide a chronology of prosecution witnesses. Sabeel Ahmad Baba, along with two co-accused, remain under arrest as they seek bail in this case.

articles.title: Odisha Govt Sanctions Rs 1.08 Cr For Sital Sasthi Festival In Sambalpur | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Odisha government has approved a grant of Rs 1.08 crore for the celebration of the Sital Sasthi festival in Sambalpur district.  This decision, authorized by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, will be disbursed through the Odia Language, Literature & Culture Department. The funding will support 21 committees organizing the festival and reflects the state government's commitment to promoting Odisha's cultural heritage and giving its major festivals and pilgrimage sites wider global recognition.

articles.title: As The War Rages In Iran, Tensions Brew In Other Parts Of The World
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea rejected calls for denuclearization, asserting its right to nuclear weapons and calling the Quad a US-led bloc.  China expanded its nuclear silo network, signaling increased military capabilities, while Russia launched a drone strike in Romania, prompting NATO to defend its territory. Kazakhstan offered to store Iran's uranium stockpile, highlighting the emergence of central Asia as a potential diplomatic buffer zone. This confluence of events underscores a shift from post-Cold War non-proliferation strategies towards consolidation and survival amid expanding arsenals, with global alliances struggling to maintain equilibrium.

articles.title: Break colonial mindset, India must reclaim its true history: LG Sinha at Kashmir Lit Fest
articles.rephrased_article: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha inaugurated the two-day Kashmir Literature Festival-2026, emphasizing the power of writers and scholars in shaping civilizations. He called for breaking colonial mindsets and reclaiming India's "real history," drawing parallels to Indian mythology and highlighting the importance of recognizing the depth of the country's civilisational knowledge. Sinha also rejected the notion that reading culture is declining, citing global book publication figures as evidence of a growing literary landscape.

articles.title: MP And TMC National GS Abhishek Banerjee Assaulted Near Kolkata; Stones, Shoes And Eggs Hurled | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress national general secretary, was allegedly assaulted by a mob in West Bengal's Sonarpur area while visiting families of post-poll violence victims. The incident involved stones, shoes, and eggs being hurled at him, with people shouting "thief" slogans.  Banerjee claimed the attack was pre-planned and demanded police protection for the victims' families. The Kolkata Municipal Corporation had previously issued notices regarding his properties.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Politically motivated violence against a national leader raises serious concerns about safety and rule of law.

articles.title: Ministers statements on paddy procurement run contrary to ground reality: BJP State chief N. Ramchander Rao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Ramchander Rao, BJP State president, criticized the inconsistent statements made by Civil Supplies Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and other ministers regarding paddy procurement figures, alleging a lack of clarity from the State government.  He claimed that farmers were forced to sell their produce at below market prices due to delayed procurement and accused the government of misleading farmers with misinformation campaigns against the Centre. He demanded immediate purchase of all remaining paddy and maize stock and compensation for farmers affected by unseasonal rains.

articles.title: Will Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Replace Sachin Tendulkar As Team Indiaâs Youngest Player? | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a 15-year-old cricketer from Bihar, has been making waves in the cricketing world.  He is already an U-19 World Cup winner and has been named in India A's squad for a Tri-series in Sri Lanka. The selectors have included him on their 30-member list of probables for the Asian Games in September, where he will compete in T20 competition.  If Sooryavanshi makes the cut, he could become the youngest cricketer to play for Team India this year.

articles.title: Police attach properties worth Rs 2 crore under NDPS Act in Srinagar
