articles.rephrased_article: Srinagar Police attached multiple immovable properties worth approximately 2 crores rupees belonging to individuals involved in narcotics-related activities as part of the ongoing 'Nasha Mukt Jammu & Kashmir Abhiyan'.  The Police Station Bemina attached a double-storey residential house and approximately 04 marlas of land worth ₹1.5 crore belonging to Mudasir Ahmad Pir alias Sahil alias Doge, while another property valued at ₹50 lakhs was attached in connection with Case FIR No. 10/2024 registered under Sections 8/21-29 of the NDPS Act at Police Station M.R. Gunj.  The properties were attached under Section 68F(1) and 68-F of the NDPS Act, respectively, after obtaining confirmation from the Competent Authority SAFEMA, Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue, New Delhi.

articles.title: Jacqueline Fernandez, Conman Sukesh Face Charges In Money Laundering Case
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court has ordered charges to be framed against Jacqueline Fernandez, Sukesh Chandrashekar, and 15 others in a Rs 200-crore money laundering case. The prosecution alleges that the accused, including Chandrashekhar, who was arrested for bribery, used spoofed calls and fabricated identities to extort money from individuals. They are accused of concealing proceeds of crime through various channels, using them to purchase property, luxury vehicles, and gifts.  The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has collected digital evidence, including mobile phone records and financial transactions, linking the accused to the alleged money laundering scheme.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of large-scale financial fraud and abuse of power warrant urgent attention.

articles.title: CUET-UG delayed at some centres due to technical glitch, afternoon timing revised: NTA
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) announced a technical glitch delayed the commencement of the CUET-UG 2026 exam at some centers on Saturday. The issue was resolved, and the exam is now being conducted with full compensatory time to ensure no candidate is disadvantaged. TCS, which hosted the exam, reported the delay.  The NTA regrets any inconvenience caused and has provided a helpline and email support for assistance.

articles.title: Ranveer Singh Contacts Farhan Akhtar Amid âDon 3â Controversy, Expresses Interest In Another Film: Report | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ranveer Singh has reached out to Farhan Akhtar to potentially collaborate on a future project, offering to work on another film with him or his sister Zoya Akhtar.  Neither Farhan nor Zoya are currently interested in working with Ranveer again. This follows reports of Ranveer's exit from the film "Don 3" due to creative disagreements and production delays, which led to a legal dispute between Ranveer and Excel Entertainment, Farhan's production company.  Salman Khan reportedly intervened in the conflict, encouraging both sides to prioritize the film industry's interests.

articles.title: Gen Chauhan wraps up 'very satisfying' tenure as CDS; Lt Gen Subramani to take charge Sunday
articles.rephrased_article: Gen Anil Chauhan, the outgoing Chief of Defence Staff, concluded his three-year and eight-month tenure with a ceremonial tri-services guard of honor. He focused on enhancing military synergy among the three services during his time as CDS, playing a key role in Operation Sindoor and the theaterization model. Lt Gen NS Raja Subramani (retd) will succeed him as the next Chief of Defence Staff.  Chauhan expressed gratitude for his tenure and bid farewell to colleagues before transitioning to civilian life.

articles.title: Pre-Admission Medical Tests Included In Ayushman Package In Odisha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Mukesh Mahaling, Health and Family Welfare Minister of Odisha, announced that diagnostic tests conducted up to three days before a patient's admission will now be covered under the Ayushman Bharat Health Insurance Scheme.  Hospitals failing to comply with this rule face strict action, including potential fines or legal repercussions. The government has established a high-level committee to monitor implementation and conduct inspections across hospitals to ensure compliance.

articles.title: India's Exercise PRAGATI: Troops From Many Nations Train To Fight Together
articles.rephrased_article: India hosted a joint military exercise, PRAGATI 2026, involving soldiers from 13 countries including Bhutan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam. The two-week training focused on counter-terrorism, jungle warfare, rappelling, and casualty evacuation drills, with troops operating in mixed groups to enhance coordination for real-time emergency responses.  The exercise highlighted the shared security challenges faced by these nations, including terrorism, crossborder crimes, maritime threats, disaster management, and regional instability.

articles.title: PSG vs Arsenal Champions League final: PSG retain title after 4-3 penalty win - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: PSG successfully defended their UEFA Champions League title, defeating Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a tense 1-1 draw in the final.  The French champions overcame an early Arsenal goal and maintained pressure throughout the match, ultimately securing victory despite injuries and inconsistent results during the season. This marks PSG's second consecutive European crown, while Arsenal remains without a Champions League title.

articles.title: Why Interest Keeps Adding Up During Education Loan Moratorium
articles.rephrased_article: Banks in India offer a moratorium period on education loans, which covers the duration of studies plus six months to one year after completion. However, interest continues to accrue during this time, compounding and increasing the loan balance significantly. The article explains that while the moratorium provides a temporary break from EMIs, it doesn't stop the accumulation of interest, which can lead to borrowers owing more than their original loan amount by the time they start repaying.  Therefore, understanding how interest accrues during this period is crucial for managing student loans effectively and avoiding financial surprises.

articles.title: Celina Jaitlyâs Estranged Husband Peter Haag Sends Legal Notices, Seeks Public Apology Over Alleged Defamation | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Celina Jaitly's estranged husband, Peter Haag, and his father, DI Wolfgang J. Haag, have sent legal notices to her demanding a public apology and withdrawal of defamatory statements made against them. The Mumbai-based law firm Semwal & Co. represents the couple and claims that Celina has circulated false allegations through interviews, social media, and media interactions in India and overseas.  The family asserts that these allegations are unsubstantiated and have been used to damage their reputation despite ongoing legal proceedings regarding custody and domestic violence.

articles.title: Indian Navy confined entire Pak Navy to its ports during Operation Sindoor: Rajnath
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addressed the inauguration of the 'Nausena Shaurya Vatika', an open-air naval museum in Lucknow, highlighting the Indian Navy's role in Operation Sindoor.  The operation, launched to avenge the Pahalgam terror attack, saw Indian Navy Chief Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, and deputy chief ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya also present. The museum showcases the legacy, operational capabilities, and maritime achievements of the Indian Navy. Singh emphasized that maritime security is vital for India's economy and that the navy plays a crucial role in safeguarding national interests.  The museum was developed jointly by the Indian Navy and the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department.

articles.title: Five-storey building crashes down in South Delhi's Mehrauli, 10 rescued from debris - Delhi News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket Metro station in South Delhi, triggering a large-scale rescue operation. Delhi Fire Service led the initial response and scaled up operations after confirming the structure's collapse. At least 10 people have been rescued so far, but officials fear several others may still be trapped under the rubble.  Deputy Chief Warden (Headquarters) of Civil Defence Dharamvir Sejwal stated that five to six people are believed to be trapped beneath the debris and that irregularities in the building's construction could have contributed to the collapse. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta expressed concern over the incident and confirmed that all relevant agencies were mobilized, including the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police, Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), and Civil Defence teams. Rescue efforts continue into the night.

articles.title: Intense Thunderstorm, Hail Likely In Odisha For 3 Days; Temp To Rise Again By 2-3Â°C | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued warnings of severe thunderstorms for several districts in Odisha over the next five days. The southwest monsoon is expected to advance further into more areas, bringing intense rainfall, hailstorms, and high winds.  Orange warnings have been issued for specific districts, with heavy rainfall and strong thunderstorms predicted, while yellow warnings cover other coastal and interior regions. Fishermen are advised to avoid the sea during this period due to rough seas.

articles.title: Gujarat hotel worker Kavankumar Patel jailed for 10 years in US for child sex trafficking at Omaha hotel
articles.rephrased_article: Kavankumar Patel, a 27-year-old Indian national, was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison for two counts of sex trafficking of a minor at the AmericInn hotel in Omaha, Nebraska. Judge Joseph F Bataillon imposed the sentence on May 26th after Patel admitted to taking cash from the hotel's front desk drawer to pay traffickers who allowed him and the minors to stay on the property. The investigation began in January 2025 when Omaha Police Department officers discovered evidence of human trafficking, leading to the rescue of two underage girls.  The case is part of a larger investigation into Indian-origin nationals involved in hotel-based trafficking schemes in Nebraska.

articles.title: 5-Storey Building Collapses In South Delhi, Several Feared Trapped
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in south Delhi on Saturday evening, flattening into a massive mound of rubble. Delhi Fire Services received the call at 7:44 pm and sent seven fire tenders to the scene. The building housed a coaching institute on the ground floor and construction work was underway on upper floors, with authorities suspecting students may be trapped. Rescue operations are ongoing as officials try to determine the number of people potentially trapped under the debris.

articles.title: Former M&S chief appointed to tackle UK youth unemployment crisis | Young people | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marc Bolland, former chief executive of Marks & Spencer, has been appointed as a government jobs adviser to tackle youth unemployment.  He will lead a summit of business leaders and advise the work and pensions secretary, Pat McFadden, on how to respond to warnings that one in eight young people are not in education, employment or training. Bolland's appointment comes amid concerns about a "lost generation" of young people, with an interim report by former health secretary Alan Milburn highlighting the rising number of Neets (not in education, employment or training). The government has pledged to work with charities supporting disabled young people and businesses to create clear routes into work.

articles.title: Amit Shah chairs security review meeting on border-related issues
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, chaired a security review meeting in Bhuj, Gujarat, focusing on border and coastal district security.  The meeting included Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister of Gujarat, along with other senior state government officials, District Magistrates, Superintendents of Police, and representatives from the BSF, Coast Guard, Income Tax Department, Enforcement Directorate (ED), and Lead Bank Manager.  Shah emphasized the need for robust border management, including strict enforcement of laws, vigilance against infiltration, and coordination between agencies to combat financial crimes and narcotics trafficking. He also stressed the importance of maintaining close watch on centers of radicalization and demographic changes in border districts.

articles.title: Doctors remove glass shard lodged in man's food pipe after 15 days of severe pain | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A 40-year-old man experienced two weeks of persistent throat pain and difficulty swallowing before being diagnosed with a glass shard lodged in his esophagus. Dr Apurva Pande and Dr Sanjeev Chopra, from the Yatharth Super Speciality Hospital, successfully removed the glass fragment using endoscopic techniques. Doctors warned that such cases can lead to severe complications if left untreated, emphasizing the importance of seeking medical attention for persistent symptoms like throat pain or difficulty swallowing.

articles.title: Oppn. accuses Kochi Mayor of ‘abuse of power’ over extension of biomining agreement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) accused Mayor V.K. Minimol of illegally extending a biomining agreement with Bhumi Green Energy, without council approval, and criticized the governing committee for pre-monsoon work failures. The LDF parliamentary party leader, V.A. Sreejith, alleged that the decision was made after the National Institute of Technology-Calicut (NIT-C) survey and legal opinion were disregarded. Mayor Minimol defended the extension, citing a reduced biomining rate and favorable monsoon timing.

articles.title: PSG edge Arsenal on penalties to retain Champions League title - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PSG defeated Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the Champions League final.  The victory marks Luis Enrique's third Champions League triumph and makes PSG the second team besides Real Madrid to win the competition in consecutive years.  Eberechi Eze missed a penalty for PSG, while Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya made several crucial saves.

articles.title: First-Ever Standalone Policy For Single Women To Be Introduced In This State | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: The Mahayuti government in Maharashtra has approved the formation of a draft committee to develop a "Single Women Policy." The policy, spearheaded by Women and Child Development minister Aditi Tatkare, aims to empower single women across the state through access to government welfare schemes and addressing their unique concerns.  The policy will benefit widows, divorced, deserted, and unmarried women who often face social and economic challenges due to a lack of support systems. The committee will be chaired by the Commissioner of the Women and Child Development Commissionerate, Pune, and include representatives from various state departments.

articles.title: Amalgamate banks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Economic Times reports that India needs more banks and innovative approaches to financial inclusion, particularly in rural areas. The newspaper suggests consolidating the existing number of banks with more branches nationwide to improve access for citizens in semi-urban and rural regions.  This is echoed by the Narasimhan panel's recommendations, which advocate for fewer but larger banks to better serve diverse communities.

articles.title: FM must rethink - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: D B Naik, a Mumbai-based economist, has criticized the government's tax policy and medium-term debt-to-GDP target. He argues that cutting income tax rates will lead to revenue loss and that high borrowing levels, coupled with tight monetary control, will hinder private investment.  Naik also suggests that oil price increases may necessitate higher fuel prices and additional borrowing.

articles.title: Cairn: Vedanta plunges 5.59 per cent on LSE amid talks to buy Cairn stake - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta Resources Plc's stock experienced a significant decline on the London Stock Exchange, dropping 5.50% to close at 20.61 pounds. The broader market also weakened, with the FTSE 100 down 0.32%. In contrast, Cairn Energy Plc and its Indian subsidiary, Cairn India, saw gains.  Vedanta Group firm Sterlite Industries fell over 4% in India, while Cairn India reached a record high on the Bombay Stock Exchange. A potential acquisition of Cairn India by Vedanta Resources Plc is being negotiated, with a deal potentially announced as early as Sunday evening or Monday.

articles.title: Cairn India hits record high on BSE amid stake sale talks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay Stock Exchange saw a surge in trading activity, with the stock of Vedanta Resources Plc closing up 4.36 percent at Rs 355.45. This positive performance was attributed to reports that Vedanta is in talks to acquire a 51 percent stake in Cairn India from its parent firm, Cairn Energy. Analysts believe the deal, estimated at between USD 8-8.5 billion, will value Cairn India at USD 15.7 billion and could lead to a rally in Cairn India's stock price upon official announcement on August 16th.

articles.title: Old Fox has dream run on Dalal Street - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SpiceJet, Bombay Dyeing, and Godrej Properties experienced significant gains on Friday, with SpiceJet reaching a 52-week high of Rs 68.45 before closing at Rs 66.05, up 8% over the previous close. Bombay Dyeing also hit a 52-week high of Rs 684.85 before closing at Rs 661.55, up 12% over its previous close.  Godrej Properties rose 3% to close at Rs 776.40.

articles.title: Indian firms slip in global ranking; four move out of Top-500 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The global rankings of Indian companies have declined significantly in the first quarter of 2008, with 13 out of 14 firms present on the latest Financial Times Global 500 list seeing a drop in their rankings.  Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Petroleum, state-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC), realty major Unitech, and housing loan giant HDFC have completely exited the league. The market value of these 14 companies has fallen by $150 billion since December 2007, dropping to about $440 billion.  The US remains at the top with 169 companies worth a total of $9.6 trillion, followed by the UK, China, France and Japan.

articles.title: Six Indian cos among BusinessWeek's top 100 Infotech firms - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BusinessWeek has released its annual "The Infotech 100" list, ranking Reliance Comm, Bharti Airtel, and other Indian firms among the top global performers in information technology. The list, based on shareholder return, return on equity, total revenues, and revenue growth, is topped by US companies Amazon.com and Apple.  Other Indian firms included on the list are Wipro, Satyam, and HCL Technologies.  South African telecom firm MTN Group also ranked highly at 12th place.

articles.title: Wait for more signals before turning positive - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex has experienced a sharp rally since its low of 12514 points, but analysts caution against interpreting this as a sustained uptrend.  The author, VP of technical research at Darashaw, highlights that the recent bullish "Island Reversal Gap" on the daily charts may be negated if the Sensex closes below 14104 pts, potentially leading to a downward movement of 13513 points. However, further confirmation is needed before turning positive on the medium-term outlook as the resistance between 15026 pts and 15390 pts remains strong.  The Sensex may test higher levels if it decisively overcomes these resistances.

articles.title: Weak rupee takes its toll on cos with huge foreign debt - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel, Tata Motors, and Tata Chemicals are among several Indian companies facing potential losses due to accounting rules requiring mark-to-market provisions for foreign currency loans. The rupee's depreciation has increased the value of their foreign currency liabilities, leading to estimated losses of around Rs 344 crore, Rs 311 crore, and Rs 187 crore respectively. While this is only an accounting entry and does not affect cash flows, it could negatively impact stock market valuations. Companies like Reliance Communication, Reliance Industries, and Bharti Airtel are less impacted as they follow a different accounting standard.

articles.title: Fin Crisis: Too late and too little done in US - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Arun Kumar, professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, stated that the US financial crisis is too severe to be addressed with bailout packages. He attributed the collapse to deregulation under Alan Greenspan, which led to a lack of trust in the financial system and interconnectedness within banks.  He warned that countries like Japan, China, Iceland, Ukraine, and others are facing economic difficulties due to the US crisis. Kumar emphasized the need for an "out-of-the-box" restructuring of the $600 trillion financial sector and urged international coordination through initiatives like the G-20.

articles.title: Prabhudas Lilladher has a ‘reduce’ rating on Infosys - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prabhudas Lilladher has downgraded its rating on Infosys Technologies to "reduce" due to a weak outlook for the software industry and pressure on pricing power. The brokerage firm expects Infosys' earnings growth to be limited, with a two-year CAGR of 10-15% unlikely.  They anticipate weakness in the BFSI domain spreading to retail and manufacturing sectors, potentially impacting Enterprise Solutions the most. Infosys is also expected to announce another reduction in US dollar guidance.

articles.title: 'Don't bank only on price-to-earning ratio' - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Many financial experts caution against relying solely on price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios to assess the market or individual stock valuations. While P/E ratios can be useful indicators, they don't capture the full picture of a company's growth potential and future earnings.  Mukesh Dedhia, director at Ghalla & Bhansali Securities, emphasizes that there is no single "right" valuation for a stock, as it depends on various factors like growth rate, capital requirements, and market conditions. Rajiv Thakkar, CEO of Parag Parikh Financial Advisory Services, agrees that P/E ratios alone are insufficient for making investment decisions, urging investors to consider other aspects such as sustainability and future prospects.  Devendra Nevgi, founder & principal partner at Delta Global Partners, believes the current high valuations may be justified by foreign investor confidence in Indian companies' growth potential.

articles.title: Market may trade in a range, but FIIs seen sold on India - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dalal Street is expected to experience range-bound trading this week due to a lack of significant domestic or global triggers.  Analysts predict the market may open with a negative bias on Monday, but foreign institutional investors are still bullish about India's growth story and expect fund inflows to support a rebound. Geojit BNP Paribas research head Alex Mathews highlights that global parameters will be crucial in determining the direction of the domestic market. The IIP figures for June, which are due this week, will also be closely watched.

articles.title: Seven out of top 10 Asian small-cap funds are Indian - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: DSP BlackRock Micro Cap Fund, managed by Vinit Sambre, led the pack with an 82% return over the past year, outperforming the BSE Small-Cap Index and other small-cap funds.  The fund's success is attributed to its holdings of credible, high-return companies, a closed-ended structure that helped weather market turbulence, and a cash reserve to capitalize on opportunities. Value Research, a mutual fund tracking firm, praised the fund for its strategy, while experts caution investors to maintain a limited exposure due to the volatility associated with small-cap investments.

articles.title: Nifty may find support at 5300 level - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty closed the day at 5400, with trading volumes increasing in the final hour.  Open interest in futures reached a record high, indicating hedging activity and a bullish bias among participants. Bhavin Desai, Manager (derivatives) at Motilal Oswal Securities, suggests a bear ratio spread strategy for traders to hedge their long positions while capturing potential upside.

articles.title: Traders bet on calendar spread as Nifty moves in a tight range - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Girish Patil, manager-derivatives at Antique Stockbroking, suggests a trading strategy involving selling current month options and buying the next month's, as volatility is expected to remain low.  Shailesh Kadam, an AVP-derivatives at PINC Research, agrees that this strategy could be profitable due to the anticipated range-bound movement of the Nifty 5000 index in the August series. The current market environment has seen limited volatility, making calendar spreads a potentially lucrative option for traders.

articles.title: Implementation of 'guarantees', decline of BRS favour Congress in Telangana, BJP aiming for better show - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Lok Sabha elections are expected to be a tight race between the Congress and the BJP, with both parties aiming for victory. The Congress, riding high on its recent Assembly election win, is banking on the implementation of its campaign promises and the popularity of CM Revanth Reddy to secure votes. The BJP, which saw its vote share double in the 2023 Assembly elections, aims to capitalize on this momentum and secure a significant portion of seats.  The BRS, facing a morale slump after its defeat, is expected to struggle against these two major contenders.

articles.title: Modi charisma key factor in BJP's bid to retain all 26 seats in Gujarat - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Lok Sabha elections in Gujarat are expected to be influenced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's charisma, as he is a prominent figure for the state.  Anti-incumbency sentiment, unemployment, inflation, education and healthcare facilities are also key issues that will shape voter decisions. The ruling BJP aims to retain all 26 seats it won in 2019. The opposition parties will likely capitalize on these concerns to challenge the incumbent government. Gujarat is a crucial state for determining the outcome of the Lok Sabha elections.

articles.title: Lok Sabha election 2024: Maharashtra get interesting after splits in Shiv Sena, NCP - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Lok Sabha elections in Maharashtra will be influenced by splits within the Shiv Sena and NCP, along with traditional issues like unemployment and farmer suicides. The BJP-Shiv Sena alliance won 41 of the 48 seats in 2019, but the split has shifted the political landscape.  Eknath Shinde leads the ruling alliance in Maharashtra, while Ajit Pawar joined the alliance after splitting from the NCP. Manoj Jarange, a Maratha quota activist, is gaining traction in Marathwada. The region will be crucial to watch as it has traditionally been a stronghold for the BJP-Shiv Sena.  The elections are scheduled across five phases between April 19 and May 20 with counting on June 4. Over 9.2 crore citizens are eligible to vote, an increase of 34 lakh from 2019.

articles.title: BJP accuses Kejriwal of sending voters hoax calls to mislead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP accused Arvind Kejriwal, leader of the AAP, of orchestrating hoax calls to mislead voters and distribute money in slum areas.  Parvesh Verma, a BJP MP, played an audio recording of one such call, alleging that the AAP is attempting to manipulate voters. The BJP also claimed the AAP has accessed confidential voter data and accused them of supporting activities that shield terrorism. Sudhanshu Trivedi, a BJP spokesperson, welcomed the US Supreme Court's decision to extradite Tahawwur Rana, an accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks.  The BJP demanded an investigation into these allegations.

articles.title: Rare 'intensive' revision in Bihar four months before polls - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has ordered a special summary revision of electoral rolls in Bihar, marking a departure from its usual practice.  This revision differs from previous intensive revisions by utilizing the 2002-03 electoral roll as a base and incorporating a new pre-printed enumeration form for house-to-house verification. The ECI's decision to conduct this revision ahead of the assembly elections in October 2025 is unusual, as it has rarely ordered full state-wide intensive revisions so far out from the scheduled polls.  This move follows a pattern of the ECI conducting 'intensive' revision in specific areas of states based on various factors like population changes or electoral irregularities.

articles.title: 'Done deal': CM Himanta Biswa Sarma on NDA seat-sharing for Assam polls - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that the seat-sharing arrangement within the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) for the upcoming Assam assembly elections is finalized. The alliance includes the BJP, Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), United People's Party Liberal (UPPL), and the Bodoland People's Front (BPF), along with other parties like Rabha Hasong Joutha Sangram Samiti (RHJSS) and Janashakti Party (JP). Sarma confirmed that after the completion of all processes, the state leadership will meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to present a list of probable candidates.  The elections are expected in March-April following the delimitation exercise in 2023.

articles.title: Italy bans Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts amid security fears and protest concerns | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Travis Scott and Kanye West have had their concerts in Italy cancelled after local authorities raised concerns about public safety, security, and the potential for protests. The decision was made by Reggio Emilia prefect Salvatore Angieri, who cited the expected influx of thousands of spectators and the possibility of demonstrations as reasons for prohibiting the events.  The cancellations follow a series of controversies surrounding both artists, including antisemitic remarks from Kanye West and safety concerns related to Travis Scott's 2021 Astroworld Festival tragedy.

articles.title: Iranian ballistic missile strike in Kuwait injures US citizens as Washington-Tehran peace deal hangs in balance | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A missile attack on a military base in Kuwait, targeting a US military base, injured five people, including military personnel and contractors. The attack caused damage to two MQ-9 Reaper drones, each valued at approximately $30 million. While negotiations for an extension of the ceasefire with Iran concluded without a clear outcome, US officials have expressed varying signals regarding potential compromises on issues such as the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program, and sanctions relief.  The developments underscore the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the prospects of a deal with Iran.

articles.title: Ukrainian drones ignite more Russian oil depots as strike campaigns intensify | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) targeted multiple Russian oil infrastructure locations overnight, causing fires at storage sites and cargo vessels in Taganrog and an oil facility in Armavir. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine confirmed the attacks on social media, stating that they were part of a larger offensive against Russia's energy sector.  These strikes follow a pattern of escalating attacks by Ukraine on Russian energy assets, which Moscow retaliates against with long-range ballistic missiles targeting civilian infrastructure in Ukraine. The incidents underscore growing tensions between Russia and the West over the conflict.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak: WHO chief visits epicentre Bunia in eastern Congo, urges countries to reconsider travel bans | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited Bunia, Congo, to assess the rapid spread of a rare Ebola strain. He emphasized community trust and safe burials as crucial for curbing the outbreak, urging nations to reconsider travel restrictions that hinder transparency.  The WHO reported 906 suspected cases and 223 deaths in the DRC, with neighboring Uganda also reporting nine cases. MSF warned of inadequate response efforts, calling for expanded testing and aid deployment. The US has committed over $112 million in aid and is establishing quarantine facilities for Americans exposed to the virus.

articles.title: California murder-suicide: Six-day-old baby girl among four found dead; here's what we know | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) responded to reports of gunshots at a North Hills residence on Wednesday evening and found four people dead from apparent gunshot wounds.  The victims included a man identified as 31-year-old Khajag Basmajian, a two-year-old boy named Alec Basmajian, a six-day-old baby girl named Ella Basmajian, and a woman in her 30s whose identity has not been released. Evidence suggests the woman shot the man and children before turning the gun on herself, according to law enforcement sources.  The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner (LACME) is conducting autopsies to determine the cause of death.

articles.title: Kelly Curtis, actress and elder sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, dies at 69 | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Kelly Curtis, the elder sister of actress Jamie Lee Curtis, passed away at age 69 on Saturday.  She was a talented actress who appeared in films like "Trading Places" and "The Devil's Daughter," as well as television series such as "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine."  Curtis is survived by her husband, playwright Scott Morfee.  Tributes have poured in from colleagues, fans, and members of the entertainment industry.

articles.title: Govt may keep Rs 7,500 cr outlay for IT hardware manufacturing under PLI scheme - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government is planning to allocate Rs 7,500 crore for a production-linked incentive scheme for IT hardware products like personal computers and laptops. Foreign companies seeking incentives will need to invest Rs 500 crore over four years, while domestic firms are likely to face a threshold of around Rs 20 crore over five years. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Meity) is expected to finalize the detailed guidelines soon and aims to launch the scheme in the next financial year. This initiative follows the government's broader strategy to encourage domestic manufacturing across various sectors, with a cumulative production-linked incentive of Rs 2 lakh crore for ten key industries.

articles.title: Drone Hits Nuclear Facility as Kyiv, Moscow Trade Strikes | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine and Russia engaged in aerial attacks on Saturday, with a Ukrainian drone strike causing damage to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant.  The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that the plant lost all off-site power for the 16th time since the invasion of Ukraine. Russia claimed to have targeted military infrastructure and energy facilities in Ukraine, including an oil terminal on the Crimean peninsula. Ukraine's air defense unit shot down most of the incoming missiles and drones, but also reported damage to a railway station in Shostka.  President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a meeting with top aides to discuss next steps for the conflict.

articles.title: Twitter's India policy head, Mahima Kaul, to step down; will transition in March - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Twitter has announced that its Public Policy Director for India and South Asia, Mahima Kaul, is resigning to pursue other interests.  Kaul will continue in her role until the end of March and support the transition. The company has also advertised a position for public policy director - India. Monique Meche, VP, Public Policy at Twitter, stated that Kaul's departure is not related to recent controversy surrounding the blocking and unblocking of certain handles tweeting about farmer protests.

articles.title: Trump calls himself 'number one attraction in the world', considers replacing artists at 250th anniversary event | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump responded to cancellations of artists scheduled for Washington's 250th anniversary celebrations by suggesting himself as a replacement. He proposed an "America Is Back" rally on Wednesday, stating he would bring his "popularity and success" to the event. Freedom 250, the group organizing the events, has faced criticism from some artists who felt the celebration was more political than initially presented.  Despite these cancellations, Freedom 250 continues to move forward with the program, announcing additional performers and speakers in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Despite transatlantic 'love fest', EU charts third way in ties with US and China - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: EU envoys expressed cautious optimism about a new strategy for the bloc's relationship with China, but remain wary of a US-led approach that they perceive as overly hawkish. The EU aims to establish a more independent security presence in the Indo-Pacific region, including increased military cooperation and development aid, while also seeking closer ties with countries like India, Japan, and Australia.  Despite concerns about potential conflict arising from a united front against China, the bloc sees the Indo-Pacific as crucial for its future economic and geopolitical interests.

articles.title: Apple faces Indian engineer’s bias lawsuit - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Apple Inc. lost an early round in a discrimination lawsuit brought by Anita Nariani Schulze, a female engineer from India, who alleges her managers treated her as they would in their own countries.  Santa Clara County Superior Court Judge Sunil R. Kulkarni rejected Apple’s request to dismiss the case, finding that Schulze adequately supported her legal claims. The judge also denied her request to represent a class of female employees who suffered job discrimination over the last four years. Meanwhile, Cisco Systems Inc. is facing a suit brought by California's civil rights agency alleging bias against a Dalit employee based on caste.

articles.title: Thousands of farmers halt trains in Rajasthan as wheat procurement row escalates | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of farmers in Rajasthan's Hanumangarh district blocked the Bikaner–Hanumangarh railway track on Saturday, protesting against a reduced wheat procurement period and lower procurement targets. The protest escalated after farmers met with local officials who assured them that Hanumangarh would receive 8 lakh bags of wheat procurement capacity while neighboring Sriganganagar would receive 11 lakh bags.  The farmers' agitation is ongoing as they demand an extension to the procurement period and a higher target, citing increased wheat production in the district. The Indian Express reports on this story with coverage by Principal Correspondent Parul Kulshrestha.

articles.title: Panghal sidesteps Phogat show to book Asian Games ticket
articles.rephrased_article: Antim Panghal reclaimed her standing in the 53 kg category after defeating Meenakshi Goyat in the Asian Games trials final at the IG Indoor Stadium. WFI reviewed the bout and confirmed Antim's victory, despite Meenakshi's protestations.  Antim, who had lost to Meenakshi earlier this year, employed a defensive strategy that proved successful against her opponent. The win puts Antim in good position for the upcoming Asian Games where she is expected to be one of India's top medal contenders.

articles.title: Wife of key accused held from Ahmedabad airport; ‘had flown in from Dubai’ | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Bhumi Patel, wife of key accused Utpalkumar Raman Patel, was arrested at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad after landing from Dubai.  The arrest followed a probe into the multi-crore investment fraud by Shootspace Digital Private Limited. The company, based in GIFT City, had allegedly promised investors false profits and diverted their money to other companies like CloudG Technology Limited, Harry Hospitality and Leisure Limited. A special investigation team (SIT) is investigating the case.

articles.title: Several feared trapped as five-storey building reduced to rubble in Delhi’s Saket
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in south Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under the debris.  The structure housed a coaching institute and construction work was underway on upper floors. Rescue efforts are ongoing with seven fire tenders dispatched to the scene, but authorities have not yet confirmed the number of trapped individuals.

articles.title: Massive Sandstorm Engulfs Bikaner, A Sight Straight Out Of 'Dune' Universe
articles.rephrased_article: A massive dust storm hit Bikaner, Rajasthan, on Saturday afternoon, causing severe visibility reduction and disrupting city life. The strong winds snapped tree branches, caused power outages, and led to panic among residents as the storm blanketed the city in a dense haze.  The Meteorological Department advised caution and urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel during adverse weather conditions.

articles.title: Analysis: Amit Shah's Blueprint To Secure Porous India-Bangladesh Border
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP government in West Bengal has shifted focus to border security, aiming for a more practical and diplomatic approach than previous rhetoric.  Union Home Minister Amit Shah has instructed officials to handle infiltration with careful identification and documentation before handing over suspected infiltrators to Bangladeshi authorities through official channels. The government is prioritizing land acquisition and infrastructure development, including fencing projects, but acknowledges the complexity of the task due to terrain challenges, legal disputes, and diplomatic considerations. Despite these hurdles, the new administration has accelerated fencing work in key areas like Phansidewa, aiming for a phased approach that balances security with humanitarian concerns.  However, experts warn that achieving complete border control within a short timeframe is unrealistic.

articles.title: Best road trips near Mumbai to take this June for misty hills, beaches, and quick escapes | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mumbai residents seeking a monsoon escape can consider several road trip options within driving distance. Lonavala, known for its waterfalls and misty views, is a popular choice for spontaneous weekend breaks.  Matheran, India's only automobile-free hill station, offers peaceful retreats with red mud trails and scenic viewpoints. Alibaug provides coastal drives, beaches, and relaxed vacation energy, while Igatpuri boasts lush landscapes and dramatic valley views. Nashik offers vineyard getaways, temple visits, and local food.  For those willing to travel further, the Satara belt presents waterfalls, ghats, and scenic roads.

articles.title: At Norway Chess, the Armageddon exhausts the players and thrills the crowd | Chess News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Divya Deshmukh, after a grueling four-day run in the Armageddon tiebreaker format at Norway Chess, emerged exhausted but victorious.  The Indian player's tears were not from joy, but from the sheer mental strain of playing this intense format for four consecutive days. Magnus Carlsen, the tournament's host and reigning world champion, acknowledged the intensity of the Armageddon, stating it is "pretty exhausting" for players due to its fast time controls.  Norway Chess has incorporated the Armageddon since 2019, making it a defining feature of the tournament.

articles.title: A.P. primary teachers body elects new office-bearers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Primary Teachers’ Association (APPTA) State Executive Council elected new office-bearers, including Kaki Prakash Rao as president and M.G. Mehdi as general secretary. The committee resolved to urge the State Government to address pending dues, appoint the PRC chairman, and provide interim relief.  The committee also threatened a sustained protest if their demands were not met.

articles.title: At Norway Chess, the Armageddon exhausts the players and thrills the crowd | Chess News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Divya Deshmukh's dramatic Armageddon victories in the Norway Chess tournament, despite her exhaustion after four consecutive days of play, have captivated audiences. The format, introduced in 2019, has become a defining feature of the event, with 19 out of 24 games decided by the tiebreaker. Magnus Carlsen, a renowned player himself, acknowledged the intense nature of the Armageddon, but also its entertainment value.  The tournament's unique format and Deshmukh's resilience have made it a captivating spectacle for viewers.

articles.title: 63% students pass SSLC exam-2 - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB)
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB) announced the results of the Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) exam, with a pass percentage of 62.98%.  49,351 students appeared for exam-2 out of which 31,080 passed. 70.57% of the students who took exam-2 to improve their scores achieved success. The overall SSLC exam result this year reached 98.08%, an improvement of 18.04 percentage points compared to 2025.

articles.title: Salman Khan Only Owns One Rolex—But His Real Collection Is Worth Crores
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Khan has a significant watch collection, including a Rolex Rainbow Daytona valued at ₹5.13 crore and a Jacob & Co. "Ram Janmabhoomi" timepiece gifted by his mother. He collaborated with Jacob & Co. to create the "Billionaire III," featuring 714 diamonds, which is a tribute to his father's legacy. The actor has showcased various watches over the years, including a limited-edition "Epic X Ram Janmabhoomi Titanium Edition 2" from Jacob & Co., valued at ₹34 lakhs.

articles.title: Congress will face setback in 2028 Assembly elections: Former BJP MLA Narasimha Naik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Narasimha Naik, a former BJP MLA, stated that the Congress will face a setback in the 2028 Assembly elections without outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.  He expressed disappointment over Mr. Siddaramaiah's resignation and believes it will be a challenge for the new leader, D.K. Shivakumar, to lead the party effectively. Naik compared this situation to former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa's resignation, suggesting that the Congress will face similar consequences.

articles.title: True Gen-Z defined by both its culture and contribution towards nation building: BJP president Nitin Nabin | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: BJP national president Nitin Nabin addressed concerns about India's Gen Z, calling for an open debate on its definition and contribution to nation building.  He emphasized the need to guide this energy in a positive direction, citing examples of youth-led movements in neighboring countries that have led to instability. Nabin also cautioned against labeling young people as "anti-establishment" and highlighted the importance of nurturing their potential for progress. He stressed the role of the government in providing direction and support for India's youth, particularly in areas like employment and education.

articles.title: Obsession takeover: A Rs 7 crore horror film just exposed Bollywood’s biggest issue - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A low-budget horror film, "Obsession," directed by Curry Barker and starring Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, has become Hollywood's biggest ROI story of 2026.  The film, made for a reported budget of $750,000 to $1 million (roughly Rs 6–8 crore), grossed over $100 million worldwide, earning nearly 80 to 100 times its production cost. This success highlights the shrinking space for mid-budget theatrical films in Bollywood, where studios increasingly prioritize large-scale spectacles and franchise universes.  The film's low-risk, high-concept storytelling model contrasts with the escalating budgets of recent blockbuster releases like "RRR" and "Dhurandhar: The Revenge," which have also achieved significant box office success but rely on massive production costs.

articles.title: IPL 2026: 'Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the world's best batter right now,' says GT and India captain Shubman Gill - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Shubman Gill, captain of the Gujarat Titans, praised Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a 15-year-old wonderkid from the Rajasthan Royals, as the world's best batter after their Qualifier 2 match.  Gill was impressed by Sooryavanshi's fearless approach and technical brilliance, calling him one of the best batters in the world. The young prodigy shattered records during his impressive innings, becoming the fastest player to reach 1,000 IPL runs and the second-fastest in terms of innings. Following a successful debut season, Sooryavanshi has been called up to the India A squad for a tri-series in Sri Lanka.

articles.title: IPL 2026 Final: Storm delays Gujarat Titans' arrival in Ahmedabad before RCB clash - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Gujarat Titans were forced to alter their travel plans due to stormy weather, delaying their arrival in Ahmedabad until Saturday evening. The team's preparations for the IPL 2026 final against Royal Challengers Bengaluru have been disrupted, leaving them with less than 24 hours to prepare.  RCB, on the other hand, arrived in Ahmedabad earlier and has had more time to recover. This is the first time an IPL finalist has had to travel on the eve of the final due to the BCCI's decision to host playoffs across three venues.

articles.title: Congress will face setback in 2028 Assembly elections: Former BJP MLA Narasimha Naik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Narasimha Naik, former BJP MLA, claims that the Congress will face a setback in the 2028 Assembly elections without outgoing Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.  He argues that Siddaramaiah's forced resignation weakens the party and presents challenges for new leader D.K. Shivakumar. Naik believes this situation mirrors the impact of former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa's resignation, suggesting a potential victory for the BJP in 2028.

articles.title: Rajat Patidar and Shubman Gill talk T20I selection chances before IPL 2026 final. And it’s not straightforward responses - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rajat Patidar and Shubman Gill, captains of their respective teams in the IPL final, have provided insights into their T20I selection prospects. Both players have delivered impressive performances this season, with Patidar's explosive innings against Gujarat Titans and Gill's consistent scoring across formats. The outcome of the final will significantly impact their chances for a spot in the upcoming T20I series against Ireland and England.  The selectors will meet shortly after the game to finalize the squad.

articles.title: Firing incident indicates deteriorating law and order, says Pralhad Joshi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi expressed concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in Dharwad, citing a recent firing incident as an example. He alleged involvement of high-level officials, including police officers, in the case due to their failure to arrest the prime suspect, Sundar Pal.  Joshi also criticized the police for not including the accused's name in the FIR until media reports prompted action.

articles.title: Hantavirus Quarantine to End for Some US Cruise Passengers | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is monitoring 18 Americans at the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s National Quarantine Unit in Omaha for hantavirus symptoms.  Two New Yorkers are expected to be released from isolation next week, while another will remain in Nebraska until June 22nd. The remaining passengers' details haven't been released. The CDC continues to work with state and local health departments during the 42-day monitoring period.

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Revival In Bengal? Support For Mamata Banerjee Over Nephew's Assault
articles.rephrased_article: Despite losing the Bengal election, Mamata Banerjee's stature within the INDIA bloc remains strong. Opposition leaders condemned the assault on her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, by a mob in Sonarpur, South 24 Parganas.  Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, and Arvind Kejriwal accused the BJP of fostering political violence, while the ruling party denied involvement and blamed the TMC for mischaracterizing public anger. The incident has led to calls for stronger law-and-order measures in West Bengal.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a prominent politician is a serious concern.

articles.title: IPL Final, RCB vs GT: RCB captain Rajat Patidar pre-match press conference - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rajat Patidar, captain of Royal Challengers Bengaluru, has the opportunity to become only the third captain in IPL history to successfully defend an IPL title if his team beats Gujarat Titans on Sunday.  Despite this historic achievement, he insists that he is focused on leading his team in his own way and not comparing himself to past captains like MS Dhoni or Rohit Sharma.

articles.title: Three boys drown in tank in Dharwad taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three boys, aged 11, 13, and 15, drowned in a village tank in Dharwad taluk on Saturday while swimming. The incident occurred at Kariyammana Kere (Tank) in Singanahalli village.  Police Superintendent Gunjan Arya, Deputy Superintendent of Police Vinod Muktedar, and other officials responded to the scene and recovered the bodies with assistance from expert swimmers.

articles.title: No Ambulance Or Doctor In Jammu And Kashmir Village, Pregnant Woman Carried On Shoulders, Baby Dies
articles.rephrased_article: A pregnant woman, Shaista Begum, lost her baby in the mountainous Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir after a difficult journey to medical care.  Her family carried her for miles due to lack of roads and ambulances before reaching a primary health center with no gynaecologist on duty. The family then embarked on a 120-kilometer journey to the Government Medical College in Anantnag, where the baby died during the journey. Villagers are demanding improved healthcare facilities in Marwah, including a gynaecologist and a 24-hour ambulance.

articles.title: Punjab civic polls: Early edge to Congress as counting proceeds amid tight security - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Congress is surging ahead in the early stages of counting for Punjab's civic body elections, with strong performances in several municipal wards.  The counting process began on Friday amidst heavy security deployment at multiple counting centers across the state. The AAP, BJP, and SAD are also contesting the elections, which are being viewed as a key indicator of the political mood ahead of next year's Assembly elections. A total of 7,555 candidates contested the election, with Congress leading in several wards.  The outcome is expected to serve as an important indicator of the political mood in Punjab ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

articles.title: Congress’s message to Siddaramaiah as DKS takes charge: Won’t allow you to rest - Karnataka News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary KC Venugopal declared that the party will not allow former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to rest, urging him to continue playing an active role in both state and national politics.  After Siddaramaiah's resignation, DK Shivakumar was unanimously elected as the new CLP leader and formally named Karnataka’s next Chief Minister.  Siddaramaiah congratulated Shivakumar and called for a "second freedom struggle" to protect the country's unity and integrity. The Congress leadership expressed confidence that under Shivakumar's leadership, they will return to power in the 2028 elections.

articles.title: 'Enhancing Capabilities For China, Pakistan's 2-Front Challenge': Navy Chief
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Navy has enhanced its anti-submarine warfare capabilities, underwater surveillance, and network-centric operations to counter potential threats from China and Pakistan.  Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, the Navy Chief, stated that these efforts are not directed at any specific nation but aim to secure India's maritime interests. The Indian Navy is focusing on credible deterrence through technological integration, sustained presence, and operational readiness, including the acquisition of six stealth submarines under Project 75(I).  The Navy is also committed to achieving self-reliance in defense by building its own platforms and industrial capabilities.

articles.title: Odisha Private Bus Owners Threaten Strike Over Fare Hike Demand, Give 10-Day Deadline | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha State Private Bus Owners Association issued a 10-day ultimatum to the state government, threatening an indefinite strike if demands for fare revision and increased maintenance charges are not addressed. The association argues that rising operational expenses have made it difficult to sustain services under the current fare structure and maintenance provisions.  The association also resolved to submit a memorandum to the government urging immediate action. If the proposed strike occurs, private bus services across the state could be disrupted, impacting thousands of commuters.

articles.title: SF Campaign: Andhra has more obese men among large states, Kerala tops among women - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) revealed that Andhra Pradesh has the highest prevalence of overweight or obese men among large Indian states, with 47.9% of men aged 15 to 49 years classified as such.  Kerala leads in female obesity prevalence, with 46.7% of women in that age group classified as overweight or obese. The survey highlights a growing obesity burden across southern states, with rising prevalence in both urban and rural areas, raising concerns over lifestyle-related diseases. Public health experts have warned that obesity is becoming a widespread challenge across rural India as well.

articles.title: Donald Trump’s daughter visits Taj Mahal
articles.rephrased_article: Tiffany Trump, daughter of Donald Trump, visited the Taj Mahal with her husband, Michael Boulos, on Saturday.  She toured the monument extensively and expressed interest in its history and architecture. Security was heightened for the visit, with a high-security corridor established from the airport to the Taj Mahal. After leaving the monument, she returned to her hotel with Boulos and will continue their India trip.

articles.title: DK Shivakumar To Be Sworn In As Karnataka CM On June 3 | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Siddaramaiah resigned as chief minister of Karnataka, paving the way for DK Shivakumar to become the new leader of the Congress Legislative Party.  The formal election took place on Saturday with Shivakumar being elected by a unanimous vote from the CLP. He will be sworn in as the next Karnataka chief minister on June 3rd. The focus now shifts to selecting deputy chief ministers under Shivakumar.

articles.title: Three boys drown in tank in Dharwad taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three boys, aged 11, 13, and 15, drowned in a village tank in Dharwad taluk on Saturday. The incident occurred at Kariyammana Kere (Tank) in Singanahalli village, where the boys were swimming with others. Superintendent of Police Gunjan Arya, Deputy Superintendent of Police Vinod Muktedar and other officials responded to the scene and recovered the bodies with the help of expert swimmers.

articles.title: Vinesh Phogat’s return to wrestling: What a mess - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Vinesh Phogat, one of India's greatest-ever wrestlers, returned to the wrestling mat in a bid to qualify for the 2026 Asian Games. However, her comeback was marred by conflict with the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI), which imposed restrictions on her weight class and created an atmosphere of tension throughout the competition. Despite facing challenges like being denied entry into the stadium and experiencing biased officiating, Phogat persevered but ultimately lost in the semi-final. The WFI's actions sparked outrage from fans and athletes alike, highlighting a systemic issue within the federation that needs to be addressed.

articles.title: US Aircraft Fires Missile At Gambia flagged Ship For Iran Blockade Violation
articles.rephrased_article: US Central Command (CENTCOM) disabled a Gambia-flagged cargo ship, the M/V Lian Star, attempting to sail to an Iranian port by firing a Hellfire missile into its engine room on May 29. The strike followed over 20 warnings issued to the vessel's crew, who failed to comply.  The ship is no longer transiting to Iran and the US has disabled five commercial vessels in an effort to enforce a blockade of Iranian ports as part of a ceasefire with Tehran.

articles.title: The poet who shaped a filmmaker: Vishal Bhardwaj recalls a lifetime of friendship with Bashir Badr
articles.rephrased_article: Vishal Bhardwaj, a renowned filmmaker, mourns the passing of Bashir Badr, a celebrated Urdu poet.  Badr, who died at 91, was known for his profound impact on Bhardwaj's life and career. The two shared a deep bond that began in Meerut, where Bhardwaj was a student and Badr taught. Their friendship spanned decades, during which Bhardwaj learned from Badr's poetry and became a successful filmmaker.  Bhardwaj has honored Badr through his work, including incorporating his poems into films like "Dedh Ishqiya" and composing ghazals based on Badr's verses.  The two remained close even as Bhardwaj's career flourished in Mumbai, with Badr visiting him often and offering encouragement.

articles.title: 'Dhobi' on mortuary duty: HR crisis dogs busy medical college in Kerala - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The Government Medical College (GMC), Manjeri, is facing severe staffing shortages despite its growing role as a major tertiary-care teaching hospital.  Malappuram, with its unprecedented political influence in the new UDF government, has sparked hopes that long-pending issues at the medical college will be addressed. The institution struggles with chronic staff shortages, vacant specialist posts, and administrative bottlenecks, leading to employees taking on responsibilities far beyond their designated roles. The GMC faces a shortage of 271 permanent positions and 32 vacancies under the Health Department.  A study conducted by the Personnel and Administrative Reforms Department revealed that outsourced workers are handling crucial duties due to staff shortages, highlighting the urgent need for additional personnel. The institution recommends converting all 40 outsourced posts into permanent ones and creating six new posts to address the growing workload.

articles.title: Utensils Washed In Train Toilet; IRCTC Receives FSSAI Notice | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: IRCTC has been notified by the FSSAI after a video surfaced showing catering staff washing utensils in a train toilet. The FSSAI expressed concern over the unhygienic practices, which violate food safety regulations and could pose health risks to passengers.  The IRCTC has been asked to provide details on the incident, including the contractor's license and corrective measures taken.

articles.title: Audit of fundamental rights’ effectiveness could yield ‘uncomfortable’ findings: J. Chelameswar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J. Chelameswar, former Supreme Court judge, expressed concerns about the effectiveness of constitutional rights in protecting common people during a conference on legal education. He suggested an audit could reveal "very uncomfortable" findings and emphasized that the system's progress should be examined by the judicial fraternity. K. Chandru, former judge of the Madras High Court, also spoke at the event, questioning the need for an "Indianised jurisprudence" while advocating for legal studies to address contemporary issues like poverty and caste.

articles.title: Naga Chaitanya Approaches Delhi HC Over Defamatory Content Alleging He Cheated On Samantha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Naga Chaitanya, an actor, has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against online content and defamatory claims alleging he cheated on his ex-wife Samantha Ruth Prabhu. The actor's legal team argues that unauthorized use of his name, image, and persona across various platforms is damaging his reputation.  Justice Jyoti Singh acknowledged the vulnerability of public figures but stressed limitations to scrutiny. The court will examine Chaitanya's plea for legal protections against such online misuse.

articles.title: Kulgam Police attach houses worth over Rs 1 crore in anti-drug crackdown
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Kulgam district, south Kashmir, attached two residential properties worth over ₹1 crore, alleging they were acquired through proceeds from illegal drug trafficking. The first property, a house valued at ₹50 lakh belonging to Imtiyaz Ahmad Mir, was attached in connection with an FIR registered at Yaripora police station. A second property, a single-storey house worth ₹52 lakh owned by Feroze Ahmad Khan, was also attached under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after obtaining approval from the competent authority under the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act (SAFEMA). The authorities stated that all legal formalities were followed.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee Sonarpur attack: TMC leader alleges BJP wanted to kill him; shirt torn, specs broken, Stones, eggs and 'chor chor' chants - West Bengal News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, TMC national general secretary, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal while visiting the family of a man allegedly killed in post-poll violence. The incident involved stones, eggs, and verbal abuse, with protesters accusing him of corruption and demanding security for the area. Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister of West Bengal, visited him at the hospital and blamed the BJP for orchestrating the attack.  Derek O'Brien, a Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP, questioned the withdrawal of security during the visit and called for an investigation. The BJP condemned the violence but denied any involvement in the attack.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a high-ranking official is a serious threat to democracy.

articles.title: Reported spousal violence declines across India, but rises sharply in Kerala: NFHS-6 - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) reveals a mixed picture of spousal violence against married women in India. While the national rate declined from 29.2% to 22.3%, Kerala saw a sharp increase, while Telangana remained among the worst-affected states with 30.8% reporting abuse.  Karnataka recorded one of the steepest declines, falling from 44.4% to 14.1%. The survey also found a rural-urban divide in domestic violence, with higher rates in rural areas across most states. Despite improvements nationwide, Telangana, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh continue to have alarmingly high levels of spousal violence.  The survey also examined sexual violence before the age of 18 among young women aged 18-29, revealing a national decline from 1.2% to 0.7%.

articles.title: Bengal CID Serves Summons To Abhishek Banerjee In 'Fake Signature' Probe
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal CID served a notice to Abhishek Banerjee, TMC national general secretary, requesting his presence for questioning in a probe into alleged forged signatures on a letter supporting Shobhandeb Chattopadhyay as the Leader of Opposition. The notice was delivered after officers waited at Banerjee's residence and were directed to his alternative residence before finally serving him the summons.  The CID is investigating discrepancies in the signatures on a May 19 letter submitted by the TMC to the Assembly Secretariat, which some MLAs signed endorsing Chattopadhyay as the LoP. The probe has also questioned several TMC MLAs, including Nayna Banerjee and Kunal Ghosh.

articles.title: Vinesh Phogat Loses In Asian Games Qualifiers; âI Have Not Failed... I Am Fighting Whole Systemâ | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Vinesh Phogat, a three-time Olympian and Indian female wrestler, lost in the 53 kg semifinal of the Asian Games selection trials. Despite the defeat, she remains determined to return to elite competition after becoming a mother ten months ago. Vinesh asserts that her victory lies in defying the system that tried to keep her away from competition. She plans to continue training and compete in the upcoming 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

articles.title: LG directs Ladakh Admin to adopt austerity measures as per PM's call
articles.rephrased_article: Vinai Kumar Saxena, the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, has issued directives to all departments to promote austerity and sustainable practices in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for a greener future. Saxena directed departments to reduce government expenditure, cut fuel consumption, promote renewable energy, encourage local products, and enhance environmental sustainability. He also emphasized the need for greater domestic tourism, natural farming, and efficient resource utilization across sectors. All departments have been asked to submit an action plan report within 30 days and launch public awareness campaigns on various sustainable initiatives.

articles.title: Former YSRCP Vinukonda MLA among absconding accused in ₹1,000-crore land scam - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: Bolla Brahma Naidu, a former YSRCP MLA from Vinukonda, and his relative Bolla Ramesh are key suspects in an alleged ₹1,000-crore government land fraud involving forged government orders (GOs) and the illegal sale of government land in Gandipet.  The case was initiated after a complaint filed by Gandipet Tahsildar Srinivas Reddy, alleging that five fabricated GOs were circulated falsely claiming 10 acres of government land had been regularized and allotted to private individuals. The Nimmala family, who have been pursuing legal remedies since 2012, allegedly entered into an agreement with Brahma Naidu and Ramesh to sell the land at ₹3.5 crore per acre.  Police seized bank records, fake MoUs, mobile phones, and a laptop from the arrested accused during their investigation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale land fraud involving forged documents raises serious concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Indian student drowned at Wisconsin dam as he jumped to save three friends; feet got stuck in fishing wire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anurup Reddy Koduru, a 22-year-old Indian student who recently graduated from the University of North Texas, drowned at Toledo Bend Reservoir on May 29th.  He was swimming with friends when he became entangled in fishing wire and was pulled under water. The incident involved multiple agencies including the South Sabine Fire District, LA Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, North Sabine Fire District, Sabine River Authority, Acadian Ambulance, Life Air Rescue, and the Sabine Parish Sheriff Dive Team. Ashtrith Reddy Koduru, his brother, has set up a fundraiser to help with repatriation and funeral expenses.

articles.title: D K Shivakumar elected Cong Legislature Party leader, set to be new Karnataka CM
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar was elected leader of the legislature party in Karnataka, paving the way for him to become the state's next chief minister.  Siddaramaiah, the outgoing chief minister, proposed Shivakumar's name and the meeting unanimously endorsed it.  The CLP meeting took a ten-minute break with top leaders including Siddaramaiah, KC Venugopal, and Randeep Singh Surjewala in a separate room.  Shivakumar will be sworn in as the new CM on June 3rd.

articles.title: âHe Was A Magical Human Beingâ: Pooja Bhatt On Her Relationship With Bobby Deol | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Pooja Bhatt reflected on her past relationship with Bobby Deol, calling it a "magical time" in her life.  She emphasized the importance of maintaining dignity and grace, stating that discussing the reasons for their separation would be inappropriate. Deol is currently married to Tanya Deol and has two sons. Pooja Bhatt is married to Manish Makhija, and they separated after 11 years of marriage.

articles.title: Six dalits hacked over banner dispute in Tenkasi; Residents protest seeking justice - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: A masked gang attacked six members of the Devendra Kula Vellalar community in Tenkasi district, Tamil Nadu, on May 29th during a wedding celebration. The victims sustained severe injuries and were hospitalized.  P. Uchimakali, CPI(M) Tenkasi district secretary, claims the attack was caste-driven and stems from a dispute over a banner erected for the wedding. Police have detained eight individuals in connection with the incident, including three juveniles. Investigations are ongoing.

articles.title: CUET-UG exam hit by technical glitch; NTA orders probe, announces retest for 3765 candidates
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of candidates taking the Common University Entrance Test Undergraduate (CUET-UG) 2026 in India faced disruption on Saturday due to a technical glitch at several examination centres. The National Testing Agency (NTA) ordered an investigation into the issue and announced a special re-examination for affected students. Nearly 95% of candidates completed their exams after services were restored, but 3,765 chose to leave before the test resumed.  The NTA will reschedule the exam for these candidates through a one-time special examination with details to be announced on the official CUET website.

articles.title: Audit of fundamental rights’ effectiveness could yield ‘uncomfortable’ findings: J. Chelameswar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J. Chelameswar, former Supreme Court judge, expressed concerns about the effectiveness of constitutional rights in protecting common people during a national conference on legal education. He suggested that an audit could reveal "very uncomfortable" findings and emphasized the need for understanding the limitations of the system to innovate law. K. Chandru, former judge of the Madras High Court, also spoke at the event, questioning the argument for an "Indianised jurisprudence" while advocating for incorporating topics like poverty and caste into legal studies.

articles.title: Ukraine Is Using Soldiers That Don't Need Food Or Water To Kill Russians
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's war effort is increasingly reliant on drones and robots, replacing traditional frontline soldiers.  These unmanned systems are used for attacks, reconnaissance, and even medical evacuation, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky highlighting the success of using them to capture Russian positions. The use of these machines has been accelerated by a manpower shortage and uncertainty over Western support, giving Ukraine a technological advantage against a larger Russian force.  The rapid adoption of this technology is transforming warfare, as seen in the nickname "silent death" given to robotic bomb carriers by captured Russian soldiers.

articles.title: Mahima Chaudhry Reacts To Daughter Arinaâs Resemblance To Hollywood Actor Mika Abdalla | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Mahima Chaudhry's daughter, Arina, has been drawing comparisons to Hollywood actor Mika Abdalla.  The resemblance has led to online discussions about Arina potentially making her acting debut. Chaudhry revealed that she has received numerous messages and calls regarding the comparison, finding it flattering. She expressed a desire for her daughter to pursue a career in entertainment.

articles.title: From blacklisting clauses to technical criteria: Class 12 student exposes Coempt Eduteck tender - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: A 12th-grade student, Sarthak Sidhant, alleges that the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) revised tender conditions to favor Coempt Eduteck, a company with a history of operational failures.  The changes included removing disqualification provisions for past performance issues and lowering turnover requirements.  Sidhant claims these alterations allowed Coempt to qualify despite its previous track record and benefited from other modifications like relaxed software ownership requirements and penalties related to delivery timelines.  Rahul Gandhi has demanded an independent judicial inquiry, while KTR, former Telangana Minister, criticized the CBSE's actions and called for accountability from the Union Government.

articles.title: Short: Indian Navy confined entire Pak Navy to its ports during Operation Sindoor: Rajnath
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated the 'Nausena Shaurya Vatika', an open-air naval museum in Lucknow, highlighting India's maritime security and advancements in defence manufacturing. The museum showcases the Indian Navy's legacy, operational capabilities, and achievements, including the decommissioned warship INS Gomati. Singh emphasized the importance of maritime security for national well-being and praised Uttar Pradesh's economic growth under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.  The museum aims to inspire future generations and educate the public about the value of freedom and security.
