The incident occurred near a key security post on the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border, which is part of a nationwide network established to combat smuggling and other criminal activities. Sardar Marwan Khan, District Police Officer, and Rao Atif Raza, Deputy Commissioner, were present at the scene as authorities began investigating the incident.

articles.title: Drug gang attacks ‘force hundreds of Indigenous families to flee’ in Mexico | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Indigenous families in Guerrero state, Mexico have been forced to flee their homes due to intense attacks by the criminal group Los Ardillos. The attacks include drone bombings and gunfire, resulting in at least four deaths and forcing between 800 to 1,000 families to seek refuge elsewhere.  The violence has escalated significantly over the past week, prompting calls for increased government intervention and protection from both local officials and drug cartels. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, acknowledged the situation and pledged support for displaced families while emphasizing the need to address the root causes of the violence.

articles.title: Modi’s austerity drive is an admission of failure on economic and foreign policy fronts, alleges Akhilesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for austerity in light of the Iran conflict, accusing the BJP government of failing on both economic and foreign policy fronts.  Yadav argued that the appeal was an admission of failure and that the restrictions imposed were disproportionate to the perceived crisis. He also accused the BJP of fueling political unrest with electoral fraud and social discord.

articles.title: Muslim Votes Matter says anonymous bid to create political party under same name an attempt to ‘mislead’ voters | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Muslim Votes Matter (MVM) has lodged a complaint with the Victorian Electoral Commission alleging that an anonymous group is attempting to register a political party under their name. MVM, a grassroots advocacy movement focused on Muslim and minority representation in Australia, claims this move is intended to mislead voters by exploiting the existing group voting ticket system (GVT). The attempt to register a party with the same name as MVM has been criticized by MVM spokesperson Ghaith Krayem who believes it risks confusing voters at the ballot box.  The Victorian Electoral Commission has not confirmed receiving the complaint but will be unable to process applications until after the Nepean byelection writ is returned on or before May 23rd.

articles.title: Q1 fuel losses may eliminate entire fiscal-year earnings of Indian OMCs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) have been running record high under-recoveries due to the sustained low prices of petrol, diesel, and cooking gas LPG despite soaring global crude oil prices. The combined daily losses are estimated at Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 1,200 crore, with ICRA Ltd estimating losses of around Rs 1,000 crore per day on the sale of auto fuels and domestic LPG.  The government has intervened by reducing excise duty on petrol and diesel to absorb some of the fuel cost burden.

articles.title: 6 most snake-filled places around Ontario’s waters | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ontario's diverse waterways, from Lake Erie to Rice Lake, support a variety of snake species.  Northern water snakes are commonly spotted in areas like Lake Erie and Georgian Bay, while Eastern fox snakes inhabit the wetlands around Lake Huron.  The St Lawrence River provides shelter for northern water snakes and other species, including milksnakes and garter snakes.  These reptiles are often found near marshes and shorelines.  Despite their presence in many areas, most snake species in Ontario are non-venomous.

articles.title: Karnataka: Deficit pre-monsoon rainfall in 11 districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eleven districts in Karnataka, including Bengaluru Urban and Tumakuru, experienced deficit pre-monsoon rainfall between March 1 and May 11.  The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) reported that these districts received rainfall below the normal range of +19% to -19%.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts a below-normal monsoon season for most of Karnataka, with some regions in northeast and southeast-interior Karnataka expected to receive above-normal rainfall.

articles.title: Skipper Shanto extends Bangladesh lead by 179 runs in first Test against Pakistan - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh extended their lead over Pakistan to 179 runs on the fourth day of the first Test match in Dhaka.  Najmul Hossain Shanto hit an unbeaten half-century, while Mominul Haque reached a fifty before being dismissed. The hosts were 152-3 at stumps with Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim remaining unbeaten. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan failed to hold on to a catch, but the afternoon session was washed out by heavy rain.  The final day promises to be an exciting one for fans as both teams battle for victory.

articles.title: Cole Allen pleads not guilty to attempted Trump assassination | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, 31, of California, pleaded not guilty to charges including attempted assassination of President Donald Trump at a White House reporters gala.  His legal team argues that US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who was present at the event, and other Department of Justice officials should be disqualified from prosecuting him due to potential conflicts of interest stemming from their friendship with Trump. Allen is also accused of assaulting a federal officer and possessing firearms illegally. The case will continue before Judge Trevor McFadden on June 29th.

articles.title: Early Lenskart investor Alpha Wave trims stake by 2.5% in open market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Alpha Wave Ventures II and its affiliates have reduced their stake in Lenskart, selling 4.3 crore shares, representing a significant secondary transaction in the company.  The sale lowered their combined holding to 4.67% of the omnichannel eyewear retailer's equity capital. The move comes despite Motilal Oswal projecting strong growth for Lenskart, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25%/53% in revenue and pre-IND AS EBITDA.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's will stipulated that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet, with strands sent to family members and close associates. This practice was common in the 19th century as a way of mourning after death, and Napoleon's hair became a significant relic for both sentimental and historical reasons. The decision to preserve his hair before dissection ensured its survival, contributing to ongoing debate about his death.  The preserved locks have become part of historical collections and continue to fuel fascination over the circumstances surrounding his demise.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan Tamil Nadu’s CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, was unable to secure support for himself as the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu despite a last-minute attempt by DMK and AIADMK.  The move was prompted by difficulties securing an AIADMK government with DMK support, leading to negotiations between the VCK, CPI, CPI-M, and the Left parties. Ultimately, Thirumavalavan decided against the proposal after discussions with senior DMK and AIADMK leaders.

articles.title: Senators decry hike in petroleum prices, accuse govt of 'economic oppression' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senators in Pakistan's Senate criticized the recent hike in petroleum prices and costly energy, accusing the government of economic oppression.  They demanded an exit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program and called for immediate withdrawal of the fuel hike.  Barrister Syed Ali Zafar, a PTI leader, argued that the government was collecting more than the agreed-upon limit on petroleum levies, while Aamir Waliuddin Chishti, a MQM-P senator, warned that Pakistan's high energy costs and low exports would keep it in debt to the IMF.  Senator Kamran Murtaza raised concerns about Senator Abdul Shakoor being placed on the Fourth Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. The bill seeking to extend blue passport eligibility for senators' children was met with opposition from the Ministry of Interior.

articles.title: Who could challenge Keir Starmer for the UK PM’s job? Meet the candidates | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has pledged to prove his doubters wrong as he faces pressure to resign following disastrous local election results and mounting discontent within the Labour Party.  While some, like Angela Rayner, have been suggested as potential challengers, others, such as Wes Streeting, are also seen as possible contenders. The possibility of a leadership contest hinges on whether more than 20% of Labour MPs support a new candidate, which could be triggered if Starmer refuses to step down.  However, none of the potential challengers have yet publicly declared their intention to challenge Starmer.

articles.title: Victorian politics still exposed to ‘dark money’ and foreign donations as MPs struggle to agree on urgent reforms | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria is facing a political donation crisis after the high court struck down its laws, leaving the state vulnerable to unlimited dark money. Labor, Liberals, and Greens are in negotiations to reintroduce donation caps, disclosure requirements, and public funding arrangements but remain divided on key details. The lack of legislation has raised concerns from Animal Justice Party, Libertarian MP David Limbrick, and civil society organizations who advocate for a retrospective approach and independent review.

articles.title: Groww stake sale: Peak XV, Sequoia, others to sell equity worth Rs 4,750 crore; floor price at Rs 177/share - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, YC Holdings II, LLC, and Ribbit Capital V L.P. are selling shares of discount broker Groww. The transaction will be executed through a vendor sale on the Indian stock exchanges' screen-based trading platform.  The stock price dropped 5.37% to Rs 204.70 after the announcement. Groww was established in 2016 and offers brokerage services for equity, IPOs, and mutual funds. The company went public in November 2025 with a market capitalization of Rs 6,632.30 crores.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's final will instructed that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet for distribution to family members. This practice, common in the 19th century, was a way of holding on to someone physically after death.  The request led to the preservation of authentic locks from Napoleon's head, which have been used as historical artifacts and continue to fuel debate about his death. The hair also became a sentimental keepsake for those closest to him.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalvan, leader of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), was unable to secure the support needed for him to become the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu. The attempt faced opposition from both the DMK and the AIADMK, who were reportedly concerned about potential backlash and criticism.  Despite support from the CPI, CPI(M), and the VCK, Thirumavalvan ultimately decided against the proposal after backroom negotiations failed to garner sufficient consensus among the parties involved.

articles.title: Two years on, over a third of General Elections 2024 petitions await disposal - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Election tribunals across Pakistan have yet to dispose of nearly a third of election petitions filed following the February 2024 general elections.  While Free and Fair Election Network (Fafen) reports that 66% of cases have been decided, with most decisions favoring dismissed candidates, the pace of disposal has slowed in recent months. The delay is attributed to legal challenges and appointments issues, particularly in Punjab where only two tribunals functioned until October 2024.  The Supreme Court has overturned one election result, but many appeals remain pending.

articles.title: Philippine presidential hopeful Sara Duterte impeached for second time | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Duterte, the Philippine vice-president, was impeached by an overwhelming majority of lawmakers in the House of Representatives. The accusations against her include misuse of public funds, unexplained wealth accumulation, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, Louise Araneta-Marcos.  Duterte has denied all wrongdoing and will now face a trial in the Senate. If found guilty, she could be banned from public office, jeopardizing her presidential ambitions for 2028. The case is further complicated by Duterte's family ties to former president Rodrigo Duterte, who faces charges of crimes against humanity at the International Criminal Court.

articles.title: BSE launches F&O trading on IT index; debut day turnover at Rs 148 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE launched derivative contracts for its Focused IT Index, a benchmark representing India's influential technology sector. The new derivatives offer investors hedging and risk management tools, with cash-settled contracts available across three monthly expiries.  The launch saw active participation on the first trading day, with 172 members contributing to a turnover of Rs 148 crore. BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy stated that the new product complements existing index derivatives and enhances risk management for investors.

articles.title: From sleeping in a car to Ivy League: California teen earns admission to 65 elite colleges with 4.4 GPA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lamont Newell, a 17-year-old student from South Los Angeles, has garnered national attention for his remarkable feat of earning admission to 65 colleges while overcoming homelessness and family hardship.  He graduated with a 4.4 GPA from Verbum Dei Jesuit High School and will attend Columbia University on a full scholarship to study industrial engineering. Newell's journey began when he discovered coding at a summer camp, sparking his interest in STEM education and leading him to pursue a future in the field. Despite facing financial instability and challenges due to gang violence and incarceration within his family, Newell persevered, ultimately achieving his goal of graduating high school and securing admission to prestigious institutions.  His story has inspired many online, highlighting the importance of mentorship, educational access, and community support in overcoming adversity.

articles.title: Summit highlights urgency of aligning education with future job markets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo University, Chittoor and the University of Leicester jointly hosted the second edition of the Apollo-Leicester Education Summit-2026 in Vijayawada. The summit brought together diplomats, academic leaders, and industry experts from both countries to discuss how students can prepare for careers in 2030 and beyond.  Daniel Ladley, Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Leicester School of Business, emphasized the importance of globally relevant, employability-focused education. Gareth Wynn Owen, British Deputy High Commissioner for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, highlighted the growing collaboration between India and the UK in education, innovation, and careers.

articles.title: SBI sheds over $11 billion in market value in 2 sessions on margin squeeze, disappointing earnings - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shares of SBI, India's largest lender by customers, experienced a significant drop on Monday, falling 4.5% to a year-to-date low. This selloff followed Friday's near-7% decline and wiped out $11.3 billion in market value. Analysts cited narrowing net interest margins as a key factor contributing to the stock's weakness, with concerns about earnings momentum moderating in the coming quarters. Despite this short-term setback, analysts maintain a constructive long-term outlook for SBI, citing its strong balance sheet and market leadership.

articles.title: New Jersey man sentenced to 18 months for transporting 9 Irish nationals across US-Canada border into Vermont - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyshan Murray, a 44-year-old man from Elizabeth, New Jersey, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for transporting nine Irish nationals who had illegally crossed the US-Canada border into Vermont. The incident occurred on September 8, 2024, near Drew Road in Richford, Vermont.  US Border Patrol agents apprehended Murray's SUV after receiving reports of an unlawful crossing, finding three adults and three young children inside. Prosecutors argued for a 33-month sentence, citing Murray's criminal history and the potential danger to the children.

articles.title: Two children charred to death in accidental fire in makeshift tent in Kothanur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at a temporary labor shed in Bengaluru tragically killed a five-year-old boy and his three-year-old sister. Arjun (5) and Asha (3), children of Durgappa and Savitri, were found dead after the fire broke out while their grandmother was away. The cause of the fire is under investigation, but authorities suspect asphyxiation from smoke before burn injuries.  The incident occurred on Monday afternoon near Kothanur in northeastern Bengaluru.

articles.title: NA passes unanimous resolution hailing military's 'befitting response' to India in May conflict - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly unanimously approved a resolution praising the armed forces' response to India's unprovoked military aggression during last year's conflict. The resolution, led by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, highlighted Pakistan's successful Operation Bunyanum Marsoos and condemned India's false accusations against Pakistan.  The National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq commended the bravery of the armed forces and emphasized that Pakistan remains committed to peace while condemning India's continued aggression and attempts to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty.

articles.title: Iran war effect: Why is Modi asking Indians to avoid foreign trips, gold? | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, urged citizens to work from home, avoid international travel, and refrain from buying gold during the ongoing global energy crisis caused by the war on Iran.  He emphasized these measures to conserve foreign exchange reserves, which have been depleted due to increased oil and gold imports, as well as rising fertilizer costs. The war has significantly impacted global oil and gas supplies, leading to a surge in fuel prices and impacting India's economy.

articles.title: Chicago teen who pushed for parents’ release from ICE custody dies of cancer | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin González, an 18-year-old US citizen who was battling terminal stage four colon cancer, died on Sunday afternoon in Mexico after reuniting with his parents. Isidro González Avilés and Norma Anabel Ramírez Amaya, Kevin's parents, had been detained by ICE in Arizona after crossing the border without permission to see him.  Democratic US congressman Jesús “Chuy” García expressed condolences for Kevin’s passing, vowing to continue fighting for a humane immigration system.

articles.title: BofA settles allegation of insider trading rule violation with Sebi - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SEBI has ordered a settlement from BofA Securities India, alleging the firm failed to maintain a required digital database for insider trading regulations. The firm declined to comment on the settlement or allegations.  The regulator's investigation stemmed from a 2024 share sale in which BofA Securities India allegedly breached insider trading rules and internal "Chinese wall" norms by contacting potential investors with unpublished price-sensitive information.

articles.title: New Jersey man sentenced to 18 months for transporting 9 Irish nationals across US-Canada border into Vermont - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyshan Murray, a 44-year-old man from Elizabeth, New Jersey, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for transporting nine Irish nationals who had illegally crossed the US-Canada border into Vermont. The incident occurred on September 8, 2024, near Drew Road in Richford, Vermont, where US Border Patrol agents stopped Murray's SUV after receiving reports of an unlawful crossing. Prosecutors argued that Murray recklessly endangered the children by transporting them without proper restraints and cited his lengthy criminal record.

articles.title: Govt. to bring reforms in AYUSH sector to enhance quality: Health Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government of Andhra Pradesh is implementing reforms in the AYUSH sector to enhance healthcare services and combat the distribution of fake drugs. Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav announced the establishment of three committees – an expert committee, a stakeholders committee, and a technical committee – to develop new guidelines. The committees will consult experts, gather public feedback, and study best practices from other states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu before submitting their recommendations.  The aim is to strengthen the regulatory framework for AYUSH clinics and hospitals, ensuring all practitioners are qualified and services meet national standards.

articles.title: Six people found dead inside train car at rail yard near Texas-Mexico border | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Union Pacific employees discovered six deceased individuals inside a boxcar at a yard near the Mexican border in Laredo, Texas. The Laredo police department, working with US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), are investigating the cause of death.  The incident echoes a 2024 rescue of 20 migrants found dehydrated in a similar compartment.  Union Pacific is cooperating with authorities and has expressed sadness over the event. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: MCX shares jump 4% despite overall market weakness. Here's why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX, India's largest non-agri commodity exchange, reported a significant surge in net profit and revenue for the January-March quarter of FY26. The company's net profit reached Rs 530 crore, a 291% increase from the previous year, driven by strong revenue growth to Rs 889 crore. MCX also announced a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The company's stock price experienced fluctuations but ended the day with gains.

articles.title: Telangana BJP distances itself from POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son, calls it legal issue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Telangana distanced itself from a POCSO case involving the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The state BJP president, N. Ramchander Rao, stated that the party has no connection to the matter and will investigate if any family member is involved.  Rao also addressed allegations of discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted during the recent Assembly elections, claiming it was a clean-up exercise approved by the Election Commission and Supreme Court. He asserted that the SIR aimed to eliminate "bogus" voters and that the results reflected the mandate of genuine voters.

articles.title: Uk Homeless Man: ‘Adds a little brightness to my day’: Heartfelt note left by homeless man in UK village library goes viral | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of seasoned journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers. The organization is committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering international affairs information.  Their goal is to keep readers informed about the ever-evolving world.

articles.title: Julian Ingram: Police find body believed to be of Australian fugitive
articles.rephrased_article: Police in New South Wales believe the body found beside an abandoned ute is that of Julian Ingram, a man wanted for the January murders of his ex-partner and her friends.  Ingram was on bail at the time for domestic violence offenses, and police say he was last seen on January 22nd. The discovery of the body by wildlife officers brings closure to the investigation and offers some solace to the town.

articles.title: Bank of Baroda shares gain over 2% after Q4 results. Should you buy, sell or hold? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bank of Baroda's net interest income rose 9% year-on-year to Rs 12,494 crore in Q4FY26.  Despite a decline in non-interest income, asset quality improved with gross and net NPAs declining. Citigroup maintained its "Buy" rating on the bank's share price, while Motilal Oswal kept its "Neutral" rating with a target price of Rs 300.  Elara Capital also maintained an "Accumulate" rating but lowered its target price to Rs 314. Goldman Sachs included Bank of Baroda in its basket of "alpha" ideas, citing attractive valuations and potential for outperformance.

articles.title: Vijay, Udhayanidhi, Palaniswami take oath as MLAs in Tamil Nadu; J.C.D. Prabhakar nominated for Speaker post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, and his cabinet colleagues took their oaths in the 17th Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on Monday, May 11, 2026.  The assembly's strength is now 233 following the resignation of Vijay from a second seat.  M.V. Karuppaiah, the Pro-tem Speaker, administered the oath to Vijay and other members. The election for Speaker and Deputy Speaker will be held on Tuesday, May 12, 2026.

articles.title: Philippine House Impeaches VP Sara Duterte Amid Graft Allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte, sending the impeachment complaints to the Senate for trial. The vote, with 255-26 in favor and nine abstentions, followed allegations of graft, corruption, misuse of state funds, and an alleged assassination threat against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.  The Senate elected Senator Alan Peter Cayetano as its new president shortly before the vote, a development that could influence the impeachment trial's outcome. A guilty verdict would remove Duterte from office and bar her from holding any government position for life.

articles.title: Sara Duterte: Philippines house impeaches VP for a second time
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted to impeach Vice-President Sara Duterte for a second time, advancing the case to the Senate for trial. The vote, with 257 lawmakers in favor, was more than the required one-third majority to proceed.  If convicted, she would be disqualified from holding public office. This follows allegations of misuse of public funds and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.  The case will now move to the Senate for a trial where a conviction is uncertain given the political landscape.

articles.title: Canara Bank Q4 Results: PAT drops 10% YoY to Rs 4,506 crore; NII up 4% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Canara Bank's net interest income (NII) increased 4% to Rs 9,808 crore in Q4FY26, while profit after tax (PAT) fell 13% sequentially. The bank's shares dropped 7% following the earnings announcement. Despite this, the lender reported a 13% year-on-year increase in full-year net profit to Rs 19,187 crore and saw growth in domestic deposits, gross advances, and retail lending portfolio. Asset quality improved with lower GNPA and NNPA ratios, while capital adequacy remained strong at 17.04%.  The bank has a vast network of branches and ATMs across India and overseas.

articles.title: Jockeying for the KPCC president’s post gains momentum, even as uncertainty looms over the party’s Chief Minister choice - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sunny Joseph, the current KPCC president, is expected to relinquish his position to join the upcoming UDF government.  Several prominent figures, including Benny Behanan, Kodikunnil Suresh, Anto Antony, and Shafi Parambil, are vying for the vacant post of KPCC president.  The AICC will likely choose a leader based on age, demographics, and political merit. The INTUC has also entered the fray, with its leader objecting to K.C. Venugopal's candidacy for Chief Minister.

articles.title: Philippine House Impeaches VP Sara Duterte Amid Graft Allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte, sending the impeachment complaints to the Senate for trial. The vote was 255-26 with nine abstentions, largely due to Marcos allies in the chamber.  Senator Alan Peter Cayetano was elected as the new Senate president shortly before the vote, a development that could influence the outcome of the impeachment trial. A guilty verdict would remove Duterte from office and bar her from holding any future government positions. The articles of impeachment include allegations of graft, corruption, bribery, misuse of state funds, and an alleged assassination threat against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

articles.title: Why a ministerial vacancy nearly delayed Class 12 Board exam results in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The School Education Department of Tamil Nadu postponed the release date for Class 12 State Board exam results due to a lack of a Minister to authorize the announcement. This decision caused significant disappointment among students, teachers, and parents as it disrupted their preparation plans.  After facing backlash from various stakeholders, including child rights groups and educationists, the department reversed its decision and released the results on May 8th, as scheduled. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar urged the department to release the scores without delay.

articles.title: Nifty Bank crashes 900 points as SBI, IndusInd, Yes Bank, other lender stocks tumble up to 4%. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Bank index declined nearly 2% on Monday, with losses led by SBI, which fell over 4% after reporting margin pressure and weaker operating performance.  Analysts at Bajaj Broking predict the index will continue trading within a range of 54,000-56,500 in the coming sessions, with potential for further gains above 57,500 or consolidation below 54,650. Technical analysts like Rajesh Bhosale at Angel One see support levels around 54,800 and 54,500 on the downside, and resistance levels around 55,800 and 56,300 on the upside.

articles.title: Hantavirus: US Passenger Evacuated from Hantavirus-hit Cruise Tests Positive but Asymptomatic | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An American passenger evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, MV Hondius, has tested positive for the virus but is asymptomatic and will be transferred to a Nebraska Biocontainment unit.  The infected individual is one of 17 US citizens evacuated from the ship, which arrived in Tenerife, Spain after a deadly outbreak left three people dead and at least five more infected. The World Health Organization (WHO) has reassured that the risk to the public is low, but countries receiving passengers have been advised to conduct active daily health monitoring and quarantine measures.

articles.title: Justice Aurangzeb calls for encouraging alternative dispute resolution, says SC to establish mediation centre - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb, of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, urged the judiciary to encourage alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and highlighted the Supreme Court's efforts in establishing a mediation center.  He emphasized the need for more judges to be trained as mediators, with financial assistance from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), to make mediation accessible to all parties. Justice Aurangzeb also noted that while there is no shortage of mediators in Pakistan, they must be compensated fairly for their expertise and services. He stressed the importance of a well-equipped and comfortable mediation center to encourage its use.  The Supreme Court's initiative follows previous calls from Syed Mansoor Ali Shah, former senior puisne judge, for adopting ADR mechanisms to address the growing backlog of cases.

articles.title: Philippine Congress poised to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives is poised to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte for the second time. The impeachment complaint, which includes allegations of misuse of confidential government funds, failure to disclose wealth, bribery, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., has already garnered enough votes to proceed to the Senate trial.  If convicted by the Senate, Duterte would be removed from office and permanently barred from holding any government position.

articles.title: Bandi Bhagirath’s case takes serious turn with Telangana CM ordering special team for comprehensive probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, has demanded an immediate investigation into allegations of sexual harassment against the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Bandi Bhagirath.  The Chief Minister, who is also the Home Minister, instructed the Director General of Police (DGP), C.V. Anand, to launch a probe into the case registered at Pet Basheerabad Police Station. The investigation follows allegations that the police have been slow to act on the complaint lodged by the alleged victim on May 8th.

articles.title: Hyundai shares jump 5% despite 22% YoY fall in Q4 net profit to Rs 1,256 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hyundai Motor India reported a 2% increase in revenue for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, despite a 4% decline in net profit. The company's board recommended a dividend of Rs 21 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Nomura and Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintained their "Buy" ratings on the stock, citing strong export guidance and a robust launch pipeline for new models.  Hyundai shares rose nearly 5% after the results.

articles.title: Why are Greek island houses painted blue and white: The surprising history has more to do with survival than beauty | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The iconic blue and white houses of the Cyclades islands were originally painted white to combat cholera outbreaks in the 1930s. Ioannis Metaxas, the Greek administration at the time, mandated that islanders use lime paint on their homes due to its disinfectant properties. This practice transformed the islands' appearance into the bright white landscape we recognize today.  The blue color for doors and windows was a result of using affordable "loulaki" blue laundry powder mixed with lime. The government later enforced these colors as a symbol of national unity and pride, ensuring architectural consistency and attracting tourists.

articles.title: UK’s Keir Starmer battles for political survival after election defeat | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing calls to resign from Labour Party MPs following the party's significant losses in local elections. Over 30 MPs have called for his departure, with some arguing he has lost the country’s trust.  Starmer plans to address the public and his party on Monday, attempting to convince them of his leadership. He acknowledged responsibility for the results, stating that the Labour Party has not sustained the public's trust.

articles.title: Iran war: PM Modi urges Indians to work from home, limit foreign travel
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Indians to embrace working from home, limit foreign travel, and reduce fuel consumption due to the ongoing crisis in the Middle East.  His appeal, made at a public event in Hyderabad, aims to conserve foreign exchange as India heavily relies on imports for oil. The measures are reminiscent of those implemented during the Covid-19 pandemic, with Modi suggesting public transport usage and carpooling to reduce fuel use.  Analysts suggest these actions may be part of a government directive to curb energy consumption and potentially raise petroleum prices. Opposition leaders criticized Modi's remarks as an attempt to shift responsibility onto citizens rather than address the underlying issues.

articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses PIL challenging women’s right to divorce over non-cohabitation under Hindu law - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court dismissed a plea challenging the constitutionality of a provision in the Hindu Marriage Act that grants only wives the right to seek divorce if cohabitation has not resumed for one year or more after a maintenance decree against the husband. The court, led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, found the petition lacking merit and questioned the petitioner's motivations, stating it was a personal vendetta disguised as a public interest litigation.  The court emphasized that the legislature is empowered to enact special provisions for women and children under the Constitution.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares jump 8% to 4-month high. What’s driving the rally amid stock market crash? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Plc, a UK-based telecommunications company, is considering transferring part of its stake in Vodafone Idea to the Indian telco itself. This move aims to improve Vodafone Idea's balance sheet and debt management, potentially allowing it to pay government dues and invest in future growth. The transfer would be an alternative to further cash injection from Vodafone Plc.  The decision comes as Vodafone Idea, a joint venture between the Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group, faces financial challenges due to rising AGR dues and competition from Reliance Jio.

articles.title: Dubai Smart Bus Station: Dubai launches first AI-powered smart bus station at Mall of the Emirates with 24/7 digital services | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) unveiled its first fully integrated smart bus station at Mall of the Emirates, combining AI, sustainability, and digital services to enhance commuting experiences. The station directly connects with the Metro and serves 11 routes across Dubai, including feeder buses for residential, commercial, and tourist areas. Passengers can track buses in real-time using the RTA's S’hail app and enjoy air-conditioned waiting areas, live travel updates, AI-assisted crowd management, and quicker connections. The station is part of Dubai’s larger plan to modernize public transport through digital technology and smart infrastructure.

articles.title: IT exports expected to reach $4bn during current fiscal year, PM told - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed that Pakistan's IT exports are expected to reach between $4.5 billion and $4.6 billion this fiscal year, according to the Prime Minister's Office. The meeting also discussed the growth of domestic internet connections, with numbers increasing from 1.9 million in 2024 to 5.1 million by 2026.  The recent 5G spectrum auction generated $509 million in revenue, and efforts were made to promote artificial intelligence through events like "Indus AI Week". The meeting also highlighted initiatives such as fiber connectivity for government schools and health units in Islamabad, free internet hotspots, and e-learning pods in certain areas.

articles.title: Body believed to be alleged triple murderer Julian Ingram found near abandoned ute in ‘decomposed state’ | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police believe a body found near an abandoned ute in remote New South Wales is that of Julian Ingram, 37, suspected of killing his pregnant former partner and her relatives.  Ingram was last seen driving a Ford Ranger with council signage on January 22nd. The discovery comes after a four-month manhunt for the gunman, who was on bail at the time for alleged domestic violence offenses against Quinn. Police are still investigating the cause of death but hope this discovery will bring closure to the case and the community.

articles.title: Titan shares crash 6% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, other brokerages saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Titan Company's total income surged 46% to Rs 20,300 crore in Q4FY26, driven by strong performance across its jewellery, watch, and eyecare businesses. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Bernstein maintained their positive ratings on the company's stock, citing robust growth prospects and attractive valuations.  The brokerage firms attributed the impressive results to elevated gold prices and a growing consumer base for discretionary spending.

articles.title: 1998 Pokhran nuclear tests reflected India's scientific excellence: PM on National Technology Day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted the nation on National Technology Day, commemorating India's successful nuclear tests at Pokhran in 1998. He emphasized technology as a key pillar for building a self-reliant India and highlighted its role in accelerating innovation and national growth. Mr. Modi praised the scientists who led these landmark events, stating they are the true architects of the nation's pride and self-respect.

articles.title: US widens drive to revoke citizenship of foreign-born Americans - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is expanding its efforts to revoke the citizenship of naturalized citizens, filing denaturalization cases against individuals accused of fraud, terrorism links, and financial crimes. The Justice Department alleges that some individuals concealed material facts during their immigration proceedings or engaged in conduct disqualifying them from US citizenship.  These cases include an Indian-origin businessman, Debashis Ghosh, accused of orchestrating a $2.5 million investment fraud scheme. Civil liberties groups are concerned about the potential impact on immigrant communities and fear increased uncertainty.

articles.title: Antony Catalano: media mogul accused of assaulting wife excused from attending court due to fears over press scrutiny | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Antony Catalano, 59, a media mogul and co-owner of Australian Community Media, was granted leave to appear via video link in Melbourne magistrates court due to concerns about the detrimental impact of media scrutiny on his mental health. He faces charges of assault, false imprisonment, and making threats to kill stemming from an incident with his wife, Stefanie Catalano.  Catalano's lawyer, Tony Hargreaves, requested the absence due to the intense media attention surrounding the case, including an image taken during his rehabilitation. The case has been adjourned until June.

articles.title: Urban Company shares tank 9% after Q4 net loss swells to Rs 161 crore despite a sharp revenue uptick - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The professional services platform reported a 43% year-on-year increase in revenue for Q4FY26, reaching Rs 426 crore.  Revenue grew 11% sequentially from the previous quarter. The company's losses widened significantly, increasing nearly eightfold to Rs 98 crore. Despite this, the platform saw a 42% year-on-year rise in net transacting value (NTV) to Rs 1,148 crore and an improvement in margins.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Trying to ruin the life of Erika": Laura Loomer accuses Candace Owens of pushing “bankrupt” lies while harassing Erika Kirk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens and Laura Loomer engaged in a heated online feud, escalating from accusations about finances to personal attacks on each other's mental health.  Loomer accused Owens of living a lavish lifestyle while claiming bankruptcy, prompting Owens to respond with insults regarding Loomer's mental health and social standing. The feud further intensified when Loomer brought up Erika Kirk, accusing Owens of harassing her.  The exchange drew significant attention online as users dissected the accusations and personal attacks.

articles.title: Kerala Government formation LIVE: Impasse over chief ministerial candidate in Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leadership held marathon discussions in New Delhi with the three main contenders for Kerala's Chief Minister position, K.C. Venugopal, Ramesh Chennithala, and V.D. Satheesan, and KPCC president Sunny Joseph.  The consultations, attended by observers Ajay Maken and Mukul Wasnik, have failed to reach a decision on the selection of a new Chief Minister despite discussions lasting over three hours.

articles.title: Thaksin Shinawatra: Thailand's ex-PM is out of jail, but is his era over?
articles.rephrased_article: Thaksin Shinawatra, former prime minister of Thailand, was released from prison after serving part of a one-year sentence for corruption and abuses of power. His release sparked jubilant scenes as supporters cheered his return to Thailand. Pheu Thai, his political party, insists he will remain in the background but speculation remains about his future role in Thai politics. The court rulings against his allies and violent clashes during his tenure have shaped Thailand's political landscape for decades.  His continued popularity suggests a potential comeback, although the conservative establishment has shown little willingness to accommodate him.

articles.title: Swiggy shares plunge 7% after Q4 results. What are Nomura, Citi and others saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Swiggy reported a 45% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 6,383 crore in the January-March quarter of FY26. The company's food delivery business saw its strongest growth in 15 quarters, with gross order value rising 23% YoY and monthly transacting users growing 21% YoY. Swiggy’s quick commerce arm, Instamart, experienced a 68.8% YoY increase in gross order value.  Nuvama, Nomura, and Citi maintained their Buy ratings on Swiggy shares with target prices ranging from Rs 473 to Rs 477 apiece, citing strong earnings growth and improving operating metrics.

articles.title: Amos Yee: Who is Amos Yee? Controversial Singapore YouTuber assaulted by Yuji Itadori cosplayer outside anime convention - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amos Yee, a 27-year-old Singaporean content creator, was assaulted outside the Doujima anime convention in Singapore on May 9th.  Videos of the incident show a teenager dressed as Yuji Itadori punching and kicking Yee. The attack reignited debate around Yee’s controversial past which includes multiple arrests in Singapore for provocative online commentary and child-related offenses. While some condemned the assault, others pointed to his history of scandals. Organisers of the convention had previously banned Yee from attending due to his problematic reputation.

articles.title: ‘Compromised PM’ no longer capable of running country: Rahul slams Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for urging citizens to make sacrifices during the West Asia conflict, calling it evidence of failure.  Gandhi argued that these measures are shifting responsibility onto the public and highlight the government's inability to address the crisis. The Congress also condemned Modi's call for reducing fuel consumption and postponing gold purchases, claiming it is reckless and immoral.  The Prime Minister, meanwhile, urged citizens to use petroleum products judiciously, postpone gold purchases, and adopt alternative modes of transport to strengthen the economy amidst the global crisis.

articles.title: ‘Never, ever’: Tim Wilson walks back comments on potential One Nation rightwing alliance | Liberal party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tim Wilson, the shadow treasurer, has walked back previous comments suggesting a potential coalition government with One Nation.  He and other senior Liberal figures have rejected any partnership with the rightwing populist party, despite One Nation's recent victory in the Farrer byelection. While acknowledging the challenges posed by the party's surge in popularity, Wilson emphasized the need for the Coalition to focus on its own vision for the future. Anthony Albanese, the prime minister, has acknowledged the concerns of voters who feel the system is not working for them and expressed his respect for their right to vote but cautioned against One Nation's lack of real-world solutions.

articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant praised Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's new books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous anecdotes from the courtroom.  Kant suggested that Mehta likely wrote the books during downtime in court or while waiting for slow-moving files to be read.  Home Minister Amit Shah also attended the book launch.

articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant praised Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous courtroom anecdotes.  Kant suggested that the books were filled with comical tales from the Indian legal system, noting that there was ample material in Delhi alone to fill a library. Shah, the Home Minister, also attended the launch event.

articles.title: Mamata created false narrative on BJP restricting consumption of fish: Dilip Ghosh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dilip Ghosh, newly sworn-in West Bengal minister, attended a fish festival on Sunday (May 10, 2026) and refuted Mamata Banerjee's claims that the BJP would restrict consumption of fish and meat if it won the Assembly polls.  He accused Ms. Banerjee of spreading falsehoods during her campaign and claimed the BJP government will promote self-sufficiency in fish production.  Echoing Mr. Ghosh, Tapas Roy, the BJP MLA-elect from Maniktala, stated that the previous TMC regime failed to develop the pisciculture sector.

articles.title: Collector declares public holiday on May 15 in Vellore for annual ‘Sirasu’ festival - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Collector V. R. Subbulaxmi declared a public holiday on May 15th for the annual `Sirasu’ festival of Arulmigu Gangaiamman Temple in Gudiyatham town, Vellore.  The festival will be held on the first day of the Tamil month, Vaikasi and will include crowd management measures such as designated routes with shelters, drinking water facilities, sanitation help desks, and temporary shop restrictions to prevent overcrowding. Superintendent of Police U. Sivaraman attended a preparatory meeting at the Collectorate to discuss these preparations.

articles.title: The emerging Rahul Gandhi-Vijay political partnership - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader, attended the swearing-in ceremony of C. Joseph Vijay's new Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government in Chennai. The event signaled a potential shift in the political landscape between the Congress and the DMK, with Gandhi expressing support for Vijay and their relationship mirroring that shared by former allies M.K. Stalin and Gandhi.  The TVK's success may bolster the Congress's influence in southern India.

articles.title: Congress’ wait to join the Tamil Nadu Cabinet continues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi attended the swearing-in ceremony of C. Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on Sunday (May 10, 2026). However, despite the Congress's request for both of its MLAs to be sworn in as Cabinet Ministers at the same time, the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) opted to delay the swearing-in. The TVK is planning to include members from other coalition partners like the AIADMK in the cabinet expansion.  The decision not to immediately swear in the Congress MLAs was seen as a missed opportunity by some party leaders who felt it would have sent a strong message of unity.

articles.title: CREDAI Tamil Nadu calls for transparent governance, faster urban development - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CREDAI Tamil Nadu congratulated C. Joseph Vijay on becoming Chief Minister and urged for systems that promote transparency, eliminate corruption, and improve governance. The organization's president, Habib W.S., emphasized the need for urban development, infrastructure expansion, and ease of doing business to sustain Tamil Nadu's economic growth.  CREDAI Chennai president, Mehul H. Doshi, also congratulated R. Kumar, a member of their organization, on his victory in the Velachery constituency.

articles.title: CM selection a democratic process: Chennithala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ramesh Chennithala, a senior Congress leader, criticized the BJP for its alleged delay in selecting a Chief Minister after the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. He defended the Congress's democratic process and emphasized that decisions are made through discussions within the party.  Chennithala stated that five days is not an unreasonable time frame for such a decision, especially considering the complexity of the selection process. The Congress leadership has been meeting with various leaders to arrive at a consensus on the next Chief Minister.

articles.title: Biogas association calls for blending of organic manure with fertilizers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Biogas Association (IBA) has called for a 10% mandatory blending of fermented organic manure with chemical fertilizers by 2030, arguing it can save $2 billion annually in fertilizer imports. The IBA's white paper, released by New and Renewable Energy Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi, proposes integrating this approach into existing government programs like the Soil Health Card scheme and Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana.  The association emphasizes that such a mandate will create stable market demand for fermented organic manure, strengthen fertilizer distribution networks, and enable region-specific nutrient solutions.

articles.title: Experts call for UK four-day week as study links long work hours to obesity | Obesity | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: International research, presented at the European Congress on Obesity, found a correlation between longer working hours and higher obesity rates in 33 OECD countries.  The study suggests that reducing annual working hours by 1% could decrease obesity rates by 0.16%. Dr Pradeepa Korale-Gedara, of the University of Queensland, Australia, attributes this to increased stress levels from long work hours leading to fat storage and a lack of time for exercise. While researchers acknowledge the need for further investigation, experts advocate for a four-day work week as a potential solution to combat obesity in the UK.

articles.title: Crumbling of Awadh’s heritage amidst monument encroachments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) highlights the concerning state of protected monuments in Uttar Pradesh. The report found that 31 centrally protected monuments are untraceable, with only 31 monuments having proper ownership documentation and 96 being encroached upon. Heritage activists express worry over the disappearance of these historical sites and the potential loss of Awadhi culture, which is intertwined with the architecture and traditions of these structures.  The report also found that the ASI has not been adequately enforcing existing laws and regulations, leading to inadequate planning and documentation for conservation efforts. Experts advocate for stronger legislation, including a state heritage law, to address this issue and protect these valuable cultural assets.

articles.title: Bandi urges BJP workers to not believe allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, addressed allegations against him and his family, stating he would never engage in actions that harm the BJP.  He urged his supporters to disregard the accusations made by the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS).

articles.title: D. Sudhakar: A politician who vouched for rainwater harvesting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sudhakar, a late Minister, was known for his commitment to rainwater harvesting, both personally and publicly advocating for its adoption.  He installed systems at his residences in Challakere and Bengaluru, using only rainwater for drinking due to its superior quality. N.J. Devaraja Reddy, a hydrogeologist who promotes rainwater harvesting, stated that Sudhakar's system was designed for 50,000 liters capacity and had been in place for over two decades.  Sudhakar also initiated rainwater harvesting projects at schools in his constituency while serving as Social Welfare Minister.

articles.title: ​No detours: On the Tamil Nadu elections, post-poll outcome - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by C. Joseph Vijay, formed a government after securing the support of Congress, CPI(M), CPI, VCK, and IUML parties, despite falling short of a majority. The Governor's decision to disregard the Sarkaria Commission framework and Supreme Court rulings regarding the strength of a ministry was criticized.  The Congress's alliance with the TVK is seen as opportunistic, potentially jeopardizing their decades-long alliance with the DMK.

articles.title: ‘Not like Covid’: Indian-American scientist says there is no need to panic over Hantavirus in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jay Bhattacharya, acting US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Director, addressed concerns about a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship near Spain's Canary Islands. He stated the situation is not COVID-19 and that existing protocols have been successful in containing past outbreaks.  The outbreak has resulted in three deaths and five serious illnesses among passengers aboard the MV 'Hondius', with 17 Americans reportedly onboard. The CDC is monitoring the situation, offering quarantine options for those returning to the US, and following a similar strategy used during the 2018 Andes hantavirus outbreak.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to chair first Cabinet meeting on May 11, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the newly elected Chief Minister of West Bengal, will hold his first cabinet meeting on Monday, May 11, at Nabanna.  The meeting will see the allocation of portfolios to five ministers who were sworn in with him on Saturday. The cabinet is expected to establish inquiry commissions into atrocities against women during the Trinamool Congress regime. Adhikari also plans to meet with top officials from various departments including the police and district magistrates.

articles.title: Australia politics live: budget funds to speed up environmental approvals; government repatriates passengers from hantavirus ship | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Barnaby Joyce and One Nation celebrated their victory in the Farrer byelection, with Joyce stating they will "go for government" after securing their first federal lower house win.  Albanese defended breaking promises to not touch negative gearing and CGT, arguing that intergenerational inequality needs to be addressed. The Liberal party suffered a devastating loss, with Taylor and Canavan criticized for adopting "lite" policies that legitimized One Nation. Hume acknowledged the party's lost trust but emphasized rebuilding a policy platform.  The government will use all levers at its disposal to accelerate housing supply, including reforming negative gearing and capital gains tax in tomorrow's budget.

articles.title: Andhra GST officials urged to support tech-driven tax reforms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chowdary Purushottam Naidu, president of the Andhra Pradesh GST Officers and Employees Association, urged officials to support tax reforms and technology usage, criticizing those who oppose them.  He claimed that a few officials are hindering the government's efforts by creating unrest over promotions denied due to procedural issues. Babu Ahmed, Chief Commissioner of the AP GST wing, has been praised for his role in maximizing tax collections through technology. The APNGOs Association pledged support for effective tax collection while refraining from interfering with government policies regarding transfers and other matters.

articles.title: I-PAC emerges as Trinamool’s fall guy after West Bengal Assembly poll debacle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Trinamool Congress leaders are blaming I-PAC, a political consultancy firm, for the party's loss in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. Senior leader Kalyan Banerjee stated that the reliance on I-PAC had detrimental effects on the party's organization and that Abhishek Banerjee's dependence on the firm was not well received.

articles.title: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay chairs meeting to take stock of law and order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, began his tenure by reviewing law and order with senior officials including Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar and Director-General of Police Sandeep Rai Rathore. The meeting focused on safety measures for women and combating illegal drugs and psychotropic substances.  Vijay also paid respects to social reformer 'Periyar' E.V. Ramasamy at Periyar Thidal and met with Dravidar Kazhagam president K. Veeramani.

articles.title: Anger, confusion as Louisiana Republicans move to erase majority-Black US House dist - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Leona Tate, a former student who desegregated schools in the deep South, testified before a Louisiana state senate committee that the proposed redistricting plan to dismantle majority-Black congressional districts brought back memories of racial slurs and threats.  Over eight hours, Black members of Congress, pastors, activists, and voters delivered emotional testimony against the proposal, which Republicans argue will benefit their party. The hearing was marked by protests and security issues as Mike McClanahan, president of the NAACP, was blocked from entering the room.

articles.title: Apollo Hospitals launches centre for venous disorders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo Hospitals has opened a Centre for Venous Disorders at its Greams Road hospital in Chennai. The centre, focusing on conditions like varicose veins and deep vein thrombosis, aims to provide comprehensive treatment through specialized care from vascular surgeons, radiologists, dermatologists, and wound care specialists.  The launch was attended by Ilankumaran Kaliamoorthy, CEO of the Chennai Region, along with vascular surgeons Balaji and Rajarajan Venkatesan and Naveen, CEO of Apollo Hospitals, Greams Road.

articles.title: Non-binary Indian on student visa elected to Scottish Parliament - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Q Manivannan, an Indian national and non-binary transgender individual, became the first foreign citizen elected as a Member of the Scottish Parliament (MSP) on Friday.  They won the Edinburgh & Lothians East seat for the Scottish Greens. While their election has sparked controversy, Manivannan will receive an annual salary of £77k despite not having a permanent visa to live in the UK. They are currently crowdfunding to raise money for a graduate visa that would allow them to remain in Scotland for three more years.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Minister K.G. Arunraj interview | 'Dravidian parties got trapped in vicious cycle of cash-for-votes and corruption' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.G. Arunraj, a former IRS officer and newly appointed Minister in the Tamil Nadu government, criticized DMK and AIADMK for losing their initial idealism due to corruption.  He stated that these parties were unable to act on their good intentions because they had become entangled in a cycle of cash-for-votes and corruption.

articles.title: Israel operated from Iraq's Najaf desert during war: Reports - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces established a makeshift base in the Najaf desert of Iraq, using an abandoned airstrip built by Saddam Hussein, according to two security officials. The base was reportedly used for logistical support during the war against Iran and was coordinated with the US.  The presence of Israeli troops in the desert was first reported by a shepherd who alerted authorities after detecting military activity.

articles.title: TDP to adorn NHs in yellow ahead of ‘Mahanadu’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TDP leaders have instructed their cadre to decorate the National Highway in SPSR Nellore district with yellow flags and banners ahead of the party's annual conclave, "TDP Mahanadu," scheduled from May 27 to 29, 2026.  The meeting was held at IFFCO Kisan SEZ, the venue for the event, and included Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, Beedha Ravichandra, and other party leaders. The various Mahanadu committees will formally meet on May 13th.

articles.title: Bangladesh HC rejects detained Hindu monk's bail plea - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Bangladesh High Court rejected the bail petition of Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das, who is facing trial for the 2024 lawyer's murder in Chittagong. The court set a hearing date for Monday on bail petitions for four other cases against Das.  Das's lawyer argued that the monk has been incarcerated for an extended period with health issues and sought bail. Prosecutors allege 39 people are accused of murdering junior government prosecutor Saiful Islam Alif, while 23, including Das, are in custody to stand trial.

articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the Kerala Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected UDF government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the LDF.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, K.N. Balagopal, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

articles.title: PIL in SC for reviewing wages of priests, sevadars and temple staff in govt.-controlled temples - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An advocate, Ashwini Upadhyay, has filed a plea in the Supreme Court seeking direction for the Centre and State governments to establish a judicial commission or expert committee to review wages and benefits provided to priests, sevadars, and temple staff in state-controlled temples. The petition argues that these individuals are employees under the Code on Wages, 2019, and that denying them dignified wages violates their right to livelihood guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution.  Upadhyay cites instances of protests in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana demanding minimum wages for priests and temple staff who are not receiving even the minimum wage prescribed by the State. The plea also highlights a circular issued by a Tamil Nadu department prohibiting priests from accepting 'Dakshina' in 'aarti plates', further highlighting the precarious nature of their livelihood.

articles.title: Tripura pharmacists to join strike on May 20 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists is calling for a strike on May 20th, affecting health services in Tripura. The strike demands the cessation of online medicine sales, corporate-run industry deep discounts, and the halt of spurious medication sales.  The Tripura Chemists and Druggists Association, affiliated with the national body, will join the strike, resulting in approximately 3,000 pharmacies remaining closed. The State Health and Family Welfare Department and the State Drug Control Authority are reportedly taking steps to mitigate the impact of the strike.

articles.title: Kochi Port on alert after hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Port authorities are maintaining heightened vigilance following the deaths linked to hantavirus infection aboard a Dutch cruise ship, MV Hondius.  The outbreak of the Andes virus strain has been contained within the vessel and no national-level guidelines or advisories have been issued. The port is currently monitoring passengers and crew arriving at the port with a risk-based approach, requiring health declarations and initiating appropriate measures if symptoms are suspected.

articles.title: Man held on charge of attacking another with hammer in Pudukad in Thrissur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyril, a 36-year-old man from Potta, was arrested for attempting to murder Deenas Davis, a 37-year-old native of Marathakkara.  The attack occurred near a gym in Thrikkur village on Saturday evening when Cyril struck Davis with a hammer after waiting outside the gym. The police launched an investigation and identified Cyril through surveillance and scientific evidence, leading to his confession that he planned to kill Davis to be with his wife.

articles.title: Governor’s role in government formation | Explained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) secured a majority in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, but the Governor invited the party's chief to form the government.  C. Joseph Vijay, the TVK leader, was sworn in as Chief Minister after securing letters of support from 120 members. The Governor's discretion in appointing the Chief Minister is based on constitutional provisions and previous recommendations by commissions, but there have been instances where Governors have appointed a Chief Minister without following these guidelines.  The Supreme Court has emphasized that the "floor of the House" is the appropriate forum to determine majority support for a government.

articles.title: India-Trinidad archival pact to help diaspora trace ancestral roots: Jaishankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar highlighted the importance of preserving the legacy of the Girmitya community during his visit to Trinidad and Tobago, emphasizing India's efforts to connect descendants with their roots.  He underscored the significance of a new archival cooperation agreement between India and Trinidad and Tobago, which aims to help individuals trace their ancestry and reconnect with families in India. The agreement, along with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's directive for a dedicated Girmitya Studies Centre, reflects India's commitment to preserving this historical legacy.  Mr. Jaishankar also noted the growing number of applications for Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) cards following Mr. Modi's announcement of extended eligibility.

articles.title: Move to secure technical sanction for STP in West Hill sparks protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Snehil Kumar Singh directed officials to obtain technical sanction for a sewage treatment plant (STP) in West Hill division, despite protests from residents under the aegis of the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Protection Committee. The committee argues that the project violates constitutional rights and should not be implemented in Shanti Nagar, where hundreds of families live. Satheesh Parannur, patron of the committee, stated opposition to the project and called for its withdrawal.  West Hill Ward councillor K. Saritha expressed doubts about the STP's operation and questioned whether treated water would be discharged into the sea.

articles.title: Police rescue 42 cattle, seize two vehicles in separate incidents in Peddapalli - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sultanabad police rescued 42 bulls and cows from two separate vehicles in Peddapalli district on Sunday.  A Hyderabad-bound container lorry carrying 33 bulls was seized at a check post near Dubbapalli, while a van with 9 cows destined for an undisclosed location in Karnataka was intercepted at the same location. The police registered a case against the van's crew, Syed Shabad and Moiuddin, and transferred the rescued animals to a nearby goshala.

articles.title: AAP holds protests against BJP over ED action against Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) held protests across Punjab against the BJP following the ED's arrest of Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora on charges of GST fraud. The protests, led by AAP leaders including Hardip Singh Mundian and Mohinder Bhagat, escalated into clashes with BJP workers in Ludhiana and Bathinda.  The BJP accused AAP workers of attacking their activists while the AAP condemned the police's alleged inaction.

articles.title: 488 booked in Hyderabad, Cyberabad for drunk driving - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad and Cyberabad traffic police conducted special enforcement drives over the weekend, resulting in 488 motorists being booked for drunk driving.  Hyderabad police arrested 351 drivers during a two-day operation, with the highest BAC levels recorded at 300 mg or higher. Cyberabad police also reported arrests of 137 motorists, with BAC levels ranging from 36 mg to 550 mg. All offenders will be prosecuted and face potential penalties including imprisonment.

articles.title: Congress claims Instagram blocked Rahul Gandhi's reel and photo post featuring Vijay due to MeitY rules - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's post featuring him and actor-politician Vijay after the Tamil Nadu chief minister's oath-taking ceremony was mistakenly flagged for blocking by Instagram, according to Congress aide Srivatsa.  He claimed that the action is due to Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) rules, but MeitY sources denied this, stating it was a platform error. The post had garnered millions of views before being restored.

articles.title: Sub-inspector suspended - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mujeeb H., a sub-inspector at the Elamakkara police station, was suspended on Sunday after being booked in two separate cases for sexual harassment, intimidation, and attempted extortion. The alleged incidents occurred in 2025, involving misuse of a narcotics investigation to obtain a woman's phone number and make sexual advances. H. is currently absconding.

articles.title: Maritime safety and security is of primordial importance to Indian Ocean Region: Secretary-General - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India will chair the 23-nation Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) next year, with a focus on maritime security in the wake of the war in West Asia.  The government plans to raise the profile of IORA and address specific challenges such as violence in the region and blockades of the Hormuz Strait by Iran and the **U.S.

articles.title: Prisoners in Kerala to get a wider variety of fish with Jail department entering into tie-up with Matsyafed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's Jail department has partnered with Matsyafed to supply a wider variety of fish to 56 prisons across the state. The agreement, beginning in May, will replace local procurement and ensure consistent fish availability for inmates.  The new system will provide prisoners with sardine, mackerel, tuna, and other commonly available fish, cut into curry-sized pieces, daily. This change aims to address complaints from prisoners regarding limited fish options.

articles.title: Congress government spending more time to solve its internal dispute rather than people’s problems, says Prime Minister Narendra Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized the Congress government in Karnataka during a speech on Sunday, stating that it has been preoccupied with internal disputes instead of addressing the needs of its citizens. He questioned the future leadership and power dynamics within the state government, suggesting an unresolved situation.

articles.title: Karnataka minister D Sudhakar passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sudhakar, the Minister for Planning and Statistics of Karnataka, passed away on Sunday at a private hospital in Bengaluru after battling a lung infection following a knee operation. He was 66 years old.  The government has declared a three-day mourning period and a holiday for schools, colleges, and government establishments on Monday. Prominent leaders across party lines have expressed condolences, including Randeep Singh Surjewala, the AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka, and Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister of Karnataka.

articles.title: What was hidden inside the Great Wall for 400 years: Secrets buried beneath centuries of silence unearthed | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in the Jiankou section of the Great Wall near Beijing have uncovered a massive Ming dynasty cannon dating back to 1632, suggesting possible military technology exchange between China and Western powers during the late Ming era. The discovery also revealed everyday life within the wall's watchtowers, including heated brick beds, stove remains, and an immigration monument from 1573 CE.  The excavation unearthed traces of crops, medicinal plants, animal bones, and even personal inscriptions hinting at the daily lives and struggles of those who built and lived on the Great Wall.
