articles.title: BJP’s victory in Bengal will plug a big hole in national security, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, stated that the BJP's victory in West Bengal was significant for national security, as it plugs a major hole and will make infiltration and cattle smuggling impossible. He emphasized that this victory signifies ideological continuity for the party, marking its presence across all states from Gangotri to Gangasagar.  Shah also highlighted the importance of the victory in light of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 150th birth anniversary and thanked voters for their support. The BJP Legislature Party leader, Suvendu Adhikari, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister on May 9th.

articles.title: Texas woman running for Governor mocks Indians, says her new name is 'Pria' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kelly Smith, a write-in candidate for Texas governor, sparked controversy with a photo of herself in Indian attire and claiming to be "Indian" while stating she would continue to eat hamburgers. Smith's comments drew backlash from the Indian community and accusations of anti-India sentiment, despite her assertion that she is a lifelong Texan. She has only received 14 donations for her campaign and faces an uphill battle in the November election.

articles.title: 2026 elections mapped: how Labour lost ground in different directions | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labour suffered significant losses across England, Scotland, and Wales in the recent local elections. The party lost ground to opponents on both the left and right, including Reform UK, the Greens, and the Scottish National Party.  In England, Labour saw record drops in seat share, pushing it into its lowest representation since the 1970s. This fragmentation of the political landscape has resulted in a significant loss of power for Labour in Wales and a swathe of councils in England. The results have been particularly damaging to the Conservatives, who lost strongholds such as Hampshire and eastern England.

articles.title: AMMK chief Dhinakaran slams TVK for submitting ‘forged’ letter to Governor claiming his party’s backing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.T.V. Dhinakaran, leader of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam, accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) of submitting a forged letter claiming support from his party's lone MLA-elect, S. Kamaraj.  Dhinakaran stated that the TVK submitted a photocopy of a WhatsApp letter to the Governor and will lodge a police complaint. Dhinakaran also previously submitted a letter to the Governor extending support to Edappadi K. Palaniswami urging him to form the government.

articles.title: ‘Eight-pointed star’ seen in UFO files as Pentagon teases ‘even cooler information’ to come - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon released a video of an unidentified object in the sky, captured in 2013 by US Central Command personnel. The infrared footage shows a glowing object with a star-like shape that drifts and streaks across the air.  While officials have not identified what the object is, they have stated the description accompanying the footage is only meant to provide context and should not be interpreted as proof of anything unexplained. President Donald Trump ordered the release of these files through the Pentagon's newly launched website dedicated to UFOs and unexplained aerial incidents.

articles.title: Could Labour and Conservative party dominance in UK politics be ending? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, leader of the Labour Party, faced calls to resign following significant losses in local elections despite his parliamentary majority. The results raise questions about the future of party dominance in UK politics and have prompted challenges from both the left and right.  Experts on political dynamics, including Peter Geoghegan and Lesley Riddoch, discussed the significance of these local election outcomes.

articles.title: Plaid Cymru wins Welsh Senedd elections, ending 100 years of Labour control | Welsh politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Plaid Cymru has won the Welsh Senedd elections, ending 100 years of Labour dominance in Wales.  The party's leader, Rhun ap Iorwerth, said he is ready to become first minister and form the next Welsh government. Reform UK came second, pushing Labour into third place.  Eluned Morgan, who took over Welsh Labour in 2024, has resigned as party leader after a catastrophic result for the party.  The shift marks a seismic change in Welsh politics and signals the end of two-party dominance.

articles.title: Participation in democracy should go beyond voting, says T.M. Krishna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.M. Krishna, a Carnatic singer and author, urged for everyday engagement with politics beyond voting day to foster a "cultural habit of democracy." He emphasized that questioning the State is crucial for its well-being, as political parties often control the questions citizens are asked. Krishna also highlighted inaccuracies in historical narratives surrounding India's national symbols, arguing they can represent both individual independence and collective identity.

articles.title: 'Is the fight for Green Card worth it?' H-1B visa holder says he has decent money but can see parents once every two years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Redditor who obtained an H-1B visa to work in the US is questioning the value of the journey after experiencing limited social life, financial stress, and long working hours.  The user's post sparked a debate on Reddit, with many users suggesting that waiting for a Green Card may not be worth it due to the visa stress and potential job insecurity. Some suggested Canada as an alternative option while others highlighted the importance of factors like financial stability and opportunities in one's home country when making such decisions.

articles.title: Reform wins across northern England overturn decades of Labour control | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party secured a resounding victory in local elections across several Labour-held areas, including Sunderland where they won 58 of the 75 seats. The results marked a significant shift in political control, with Labour losing its grip on key council seats in Sunderland, Gateshead, and South Tyneside.  The party’s losses were attributed to voters disillusioned with Labour’s performance and dissatisfaction with issues such as taxes and local services.  Several prominent figures within the Labour Party, including education secretary Bridget Phillipson, called for a change in leadership.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: CPI, CPI(M) extend unconditional support to TVK; VCK may follow suit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), is seeking to form a government in Tamil Nadu after receiving support from the Communist Party of India and CPI(Marxist).  The VCK remains undecided on backing the TVK, while T.T.V. Dhinakaran, leader of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK), has accused his party's lone MLA-elect of forging a letter of support for the TVK. The Governor is yet to issue a decision on the request for forming the government, with the possibility of President’s Rule looming if no government is formed by May 10th.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Queen Victoria: “Then, dear Mamma, I hope you will grant me the first request I make to you, as Queen. Let me be by myself for an hour.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Queen Victoria's famous quote, "Then, dear Mamma, I hope you will grant me the first request I make to you, as Queen. Let me be by myself for an hour," reveals her need for solitude after becoming queen at 18.  The quote, which reflects a desire for privacy and time to process the immense responsibility of ruling the British Empire, resonates with people today because it captures a universal human experience of needing quiet reflection during times of change. This simple request underscores Victoria's emotional maturity and self-awareness, demonstrating that even powerful figures can feel overwhelmed by life-changing events.

articles.title: Thalassemia awareness walk organised on Necklace Road - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha flagged off a two-kilometer awareness walk on Necklace Road to commemorate International Thalassemia Day. The event, organized by the Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Society (TSCS), aimed to promote thalassemia prevention, early screening, and accessible healthcare support.  Dr. Chandrakant Agarwal, President of TSCS, emphasized the importance of timely screening, awareness, and genetic counselling for preventing thalassemia.

articles.title: ‘CIA knew Iran would shut down Strait of Hormuz if US attacked’: Former counterterror chief Joe Kent makes bombshell claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Joe Kent, former director of the National Counterterrorism Center, has claimed that US intelligence agencies, including the CIA, agreed before the Iran war that Tehran was not developing a nuclear weapon. He argues that intelligence officials warned that targeting Iran's leadership would strengthen the regime and embolden hardliners, but these warnings were ignored in favor of a narrative pushed by Israel. Kent resigned from his position over disagreements about the conflict and has been criticized for spreading false claims.  President Donald Trump, who authorized the military action, maintains that he acted based on strong evidence that Iran posed an imminent threat and was preparing to strike Americans first.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress MLAs camping in Hyderabad amid uncertainty in government formation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Five Tamil Nadu Congress MLAs are currently in Hyderabad after arriving on Thursday, May 7th, 2026. The MLAs were initially planning to leave after Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar asked Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam chief Vijay to form the government. However, they postponed their return due to new developments in Tamil Nadu that cast a shadow on the swearing-in ceremony.

articles.title: Quote of the day by James Watson: “Worrying about complications before ruling out the possibility that the answer was simple would have been damned foolishness.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Watson, co-discoverer of the double helix structure of DNA, emphasized the importance of simplicity in problem-solving. His quote, "Worrying about complications before ruling out the possibility that the answer was simple would have been damned foolishness," highlights the value of clarity and logical thinking in scientific discovery and everyday life.  Watson's approach, which involved seeking simpler explanations before assuming more complicated ones, revolutionized biology and continues to inspire scientists and readers today.

articles.title: US religious freedom commission calls for India to be listed as ‘country of particular concern’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) urged the US State Department to designate India as a "country of particular concern" for its ongoing, systematic, and egregious religious freedom violations. The commission cited concerns about discriminatory legislation, arbitrary detention, attacks against religious minorities, and transnational repression targeting critics abroad.  US House of Representatives member Chris Smith, Stephen Rapp, and scholars like Angana Chatterji and Raqib Naik all testified to the deteriorating situation for religious minorities in India.

articles.title: Four convicted in US related to killing of Haitian President Jovenel Moise | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Four individuals, Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages, were found guilty in the United States for their roles in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moise. The defendants were convicted on charges of conspiracy to kill or kidnap Moise, as well as providing material support for the plot. Prosecutors argued that the Florida-based group served as a central hub for planning and funding the assassination, while defense attorneys claimed their clients were scapegoats involved in a plan to serve an arrest warrant. The case has been linked to ongoing political instability and security crises in Haiti following Moise's death, which left a power vacuum and triggered a series of natural disasters and violence.

articles.title: Man pleads not guilty to threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Jenkinson, 39, pleaded not guilty to threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor with intent to cause fear or provoke violence.  The former prince was walking his dogs near his home in Norfolk when the alleged incident occurred on Wednesday evening.  Mountbatten-Windsor is expected to give evidence via videolink at a trial scheduled for July 29th. Jenkinson also faces charges of threatening another man, Stephen Terry, in May. He was granted conditional bail with restrictions against contacting Mountbatten-Windsor, entering Norfolk, or approaching royal residences.

articles.title: AI market crash coming soon? Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones says the bulls have another two years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jones, a macro trader, warns of potential market crashes similar to the dot-com bubble in the early 2000s, citing parallels with the current AI bull market. While acknowledging the excitement surrounding AI's rapid growth, Jones emphasizes the need for government regulation to prevent potential harm to humanity. Despite this caution, Jones has invested in AI stocks and believes that historical precedents can help guide investors.  The S&P 500, Nasdaq, Nikkei, and Kospi all reached record highs this week, driven by strong earnings from companies like Advanced Micro Devices, while India's IT sector experienced a decline due to concerns about the impact of AI on its services industry.

articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lalit Jain, Director of Census Operations (DCO), Haryana, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

articles.title: Passenger from 'Hantavirus' cruise visited school on remotest island Tristan de Cunha, believed to be infected - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A passenger from the infected MV Hondius visited Tristan da Cunha, a remote island in the South Atlantic Ocean, after the ship stopped off on April 14th, 2026. The UK Health Security Agency has identified this individual as a new suspected case of hantavirus.  The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) activated its Emergency Operations Centers and classified the outbreak as "Level 3", while local officials in Tristan are concerned about the infections on the ship.

articles.title: Badenoch claims Tories ‘coming back’ despite widespread losses in local elections | Conservatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative MP, claimed that her party is "coming back" despite significant losses across England in Thursday's local elections.  While the Tories won back Westminster and Wandsworth councils, they suffered losses in Essex, Suffolk, Brentwood, North East Lincolnshire, Hampshire, and Staffordshire. Reform, a rival party, gained ground in these areas, particularly in Havering where they now hold 39 of the 55 seats.  Prof Tony Travers, a local government expert at the London School of Economics, noted that the strong showing by both Labour and the Liberal Democrats in London suggests voters are seeking less radical change than elsewhere. Political analyst Peter Kellner stated that while the Conservatives' performance is better than last year, it still falls short of historical standards.

articles.title: MCX Q4 Results: Cons PAT soars 291% YoY to Rs 530 crore, revenue triples; Rs 8 per share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX, India's largest non-agri commodity exchange, reported a significant increase in revenue and profit for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. Revenue surged by 205% to Rs 889 crore, driven by a 34% quarter-on-quarter growth in topline.  The company's bottom line also grew substantially, with PBT reaching Rs 682 crore compared to Rs 168 crore in the previous year. The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share for FY26.

articles.title: Plea in Supreme Court says Governor is ‘duty-bound’ to invite TVK to form government in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A writ petition was filed in the Supreme Court on May 8, 2026, arguing that Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Arlekar should invite C. Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party, to form the government as the single largest party. The petition claims this action would violate the mandate of the electorate and the constitutional sequence established by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Inmate boasted after fatal prison attack on singer Ian Watkins, prosecutors tell UK court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rico Gedel, accused of murdering former Welsh singer and songwriter Ian Watkins inside HMP Wakefield, allegedly boasted about his "fame" after the attack.  Prosecutors claim Gedel stabbed Watkins with a homemade blade, inflicting severe injuries, while fellow inmate Samuel Dodsworth allegedly concealed the weapon. The prosecution alleges that both men planned the attack together, although Gedel is accused of carrying out the stabbing himself. Watkins, serving a 29-year sentence for child sex offences, was pronounced dead shortly after the attack.

articles.title: Court fight with Pentagon raises Senator Mark Kelly’s White House profile - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Mark Kelly, a former US Navy combat pilot and astronaut, is facing legal challenges from the Pentagon over remarks urging troops to refuse illegal orders. A federal appeals court expressed skepticism about the government's case, questioning whether it could withstand constitutional scrutiny. The case has gained national attention as Democrats seek candidates capable of challenging President Trump's agenda.  Kelly, who has raised millions in recent months and is viewed by some as a potential presidential contender, maintains his right to express constitutional views.

articles.title: Sebi approves over $1 billion Zepto IPO; 5 other companies also get nod - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zepto, a Bengaluru-based quick commerce company, is preparing for a public market debut that could raise around $1.3 billion, making it potentially the youngest venture-backed Indian startup to list on the stock exchange.  The company's IPO is expected in the July-September quarter of 2026 and will include a fresh issue of Rs 11,000 crore along with an offer-for-sale by early investors. Zepto has been aggressively expanding its customer base and market share in India's competitive quick commerce space, competing with established players like Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and newer entrants such as Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now.  Investment banks including Morgan Stanley, Axis Capital, HSBC, Goldman Sachs, JM Financial, IIFL Securities, and Motilal Oswal are working on the IPO.

articles.title: SC takes cognisance of resolution about HC judge sending advocate to custody - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court will hear a case on May 15th regarding an incident where an Andhra Pradesh High Court judge allegedly sent a young advocate to judicial custody for a procedural lapse. The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) and the Bar Council of India (BCI) have both expressed concern over the incident, urging the Chief Justice to intervene.

articles.title: 'I’d rather die in my country': Why immigrants are choosing voluntarily departure over detention or asylum in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has seen a surge in voluntary departures by immigrants, with over 80,000 orders issued between January 2025 and March this year. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) did not directly address the rise but stated that the administration is enforcing immigration laws more strictly.  Experts say the policy shift has changed how people experience the system, with many immigrants choosing voluntary departure as an alternative to detention due to harsh conditions and long stays in custody.

articles.title: Need for unified quality and reliability framework for aerospace stressed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A national conference on aerospace quality and reliability, organized by the Society for Aerospace Quality and Reliability (SAQR) and the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), highlighted the need for a unified framework to bridge research and development, certification authorities, and production agencies.  VSSC Director A. Rajarajan emphasized the use of advanced quality tools like predictive AI for an Atmanirbhar aerospace system. SAQR President S. Somanath urged start-ups to cultivate a quality culture in the evolving ecosystem.

articles.title: US town mayor fires entire police department for upsetting his wife, says he won't block paychecks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mayor Ron Shinnick of Cohutta, Georgia fired the entire police department after a dispute with his wife, Pam Shinnick, who was a former city council member.  The mayor claimed it was a personnel change similar to a coaching decision and that he appreciated their service. However, former officers are refusing to relinquish equipment until proper procedures are followed.

articles.title: Virginia Supreme Court strikes down Democrats’ redistricting plan in US | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Virginia Supreme Court ruled that the state's Democratic-led legislature violated procedural requirements when it placed a constitutional amendment on the ballot authorizing mid-decade redistricting. This invalidated the April 21 referendum, which voters narrowly approved to flip four Republican-held US congressional seats to Democrats. The ruling is a victory for Republicans, who now have an advantage in the upcoming midterm elections and could potentially gain as many as 10 House seats nationwide.  The decision comes after recent rulings by the US Supreme Court that weakened the Voting Rights Act, further empowering Republicans' efforts at gerrymandering.

articles.title: Robert Jenrick’s rancorous relationship with former Tory colleagues aired live on BBC | Robert Jenrick | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Atkins, shadow environment secretary, accused Robert Jenrick, former Conservative MP and now Reform UK leader, of abandoning their friendship after his defection in January.  Atkins expressed anger over the lack of communication between them since Jenrick left the party, suggesting it reflects poorly on his trustworthiness.  Jenrick attempted to shift the focus to the Conservatives' record, arguing they broke trust with voters by failing to secure borders.

articles.title: Need for unified quality and reliability framework for aerospace stressed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A national conference on aerospace quality and reliability focused on bridging the gap between research, development, and production. Society for Aerospace Quality and Reliability (SAQR) and the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) jointly organized the summit, which emphasized the need for advanced tools like predictive AI for an Atmanirbhar aerospace system.  Somanath, president of SAQR, urged start-ups to cultivate a quality culture, while Vombatkere delivered a keynote address on cyber resilience in quality and reliability.

articles.title: 'Deeply troubling': Elon Musk’s DOGE mass cancellation of grants based on race and gender criticised by US judge - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A US District Judge ruled that the mass cancellations of grants from the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) under Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) were unlawful and discriminatory.  Judge Colleen McMahon found that DOGE staff lacked authority to make the decisions, ignored established procedures, and improperly used protected characteristics during the review process. The ruling blocks the Trump administration from enforcing the grant terminations and criticizes the method used by DOGE as discriminatory. Non-profit organizations who challenged the cuts welcomed the decision, calling it an important defense of cultural and academic work.

articles.title: Senators alarmed by ‘surge’ in violence against women; 5pc conviction rate termed ‘systemic failure’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senators expressed alarm over a surge in violence against women, including honor killings, and called for stronger measures to improve conviction rates.  The presiding officer of the Senate, Sherry Rehman, stated that the current five percent conviction rate reflected a "systemic failure" and urged the Senate Human Rights Committee to investigate cases like Rubina Chandio's murder. Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, assured support for parliamentary committees working on women's rights and pledged government assistance.  Maulana Atta ur Rehman, a JUI-F Senator, also raised concerns about insecurity in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, citing the targeted killing of Maulana Muhammad Idrees and alleged administrative obstruction of protests.

articles.title: ‘Make up their own minds’: Pentagon releases first tranche of UFO files | Space News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Defense released the first tranche of previously classified files on unidentified flying objects (UFOs) following an order from US President Donald Trump in February. The release, which included 162 documents dating back decades and sourced from various government agencies, was accompanied by a new website for public access.  While the Pentagon did not draw any conclusions about the content of the files, they stated that many had only been screened for security purposes and "have not yet been analyzed for resolution of any anomalies." The release has sparked debate, with some praising Trump's focus on transparency while others criticize it as a distraction from other issues.

articles.title: Early England election results make it clear: we are in an era of five-party politics | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The English local election results show a complex picture with Labour experiencing significant losses and Reform UK gaining ground. While the Greens have made notable gains in some areas, the overall trend suggests a shift towards a more fragmented political landscape.  Early results indicate that these changes may pose challenges for both Labour and the Conservatives as they seek to form coalitions. The election results defy simple explanations and highlight the growing influence of smaller parties like Reform UK and the Green party.

articles.title: Class 12 State Board exams: Tamil Nadu registers 95.2% pass rate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Class 12 State Board examination results showed a marginal increase in pass percentage to 95.2%, with Erode district achieving the highest rate of 98.8%.  A total of 7,91,654 students sat for the exams, with girls outperforming boys at 97% compared to 93.19% for boys. School Education Secretary B. Chandra Mohan announced provisional certificates will be available from May 13th and supplementary exams for Class 12 will begin on June 29th.  The outgoing Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin, congratulated the students and urged them to pursue higher education.

articles.title: Glow hard: Donald Trump's nuclear threat grows darker in face of Iranian defiance - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump continued his volatile approach towards Iran, escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz with renewed missile exchanges and naval skirmishes. Despite a ceasefire agreement, Trump issued veiled nuclear threats against Iran, warning it would face "a lot of pain" if it didn't sign an agreement quickly. Intelligence reports suggest that Iran is more resilient than previously believed, capable of withstanding a US blockade for months and retaining significant missile capabilities.  The situation has raised concerns about the US's ability to deter Iran, potentially weakening its deterrence posture in the Pacific, according to analysts close to China.

articles.title: South Africa’s top court revives impeachment inquiry against president | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The South African Constitutional Court has ruled that parliament's decision to block an impeachment inquiry into President Cyril Ramaphosa is inconsistent with the constitution. The court ordered the referral of the independent panel's report to an impeachment committee, which will review evidence against Ramaphosa before deciding whether to recommend formal proceedings.  The ruling comes after allegations surfaced in 2022 that Ramaphosa attempted to cover up the theft of a large sum of foreign currency from his farmhouse. The Economic Freedom Fighters and the African Transformation Movement brought the case, calling for Ramaphosa's resignation.

articles.title: Nigel Farage dodges questions on £5m gift from crypto billionaire | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, has refused to answer questions about a £5 million gift from billionaire Christopher Harborne, which was not declared before his announcement of the 2024 general election candidacy. The Electoral Commission is considering an investigation into the undisclosed gift, while Reform UK chair David Bull claims it has not been raised by voters.  The party has also written to the parliamentary commissioner citing rules requiring MPs to declare personal benefits received within a month of being elected.

articles.title: US job growth beats expectations in April; unemployment rate steady at 4.3% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. economy added 115,000 jobs in April, exceeding expectations and keeping the unemployment rate at 4.3%.  Economists attributed the volatility to adjustments in the birth-and-death model used to estimate job creation. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its current interest rate policy for some time due to this resilient labor market.

articles.title: Nellore Rural MLA announces launch of 168 development works worth ₹17 crore on May 15 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nellore Rural MLA Kotamreddy Sridhar Reddy announced the launch of 168 development works worth ₹17 crore in his constituency on May 15th.  The projects, supported by Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, are part of a larger effort to improve infrastructure and services in the area. The event will feature foundation stone laying by local residents and participation from leaders of various political parties.

articles.title: ‘I wouldn’t pay it either’: Donald Trump slams sky-high World Cup ticket prices that fans must pay to attend | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed his desire to attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup but stated he wouldn't pay $1,000 for a ticket.  He expressed concern that working-class supporters could be priced out of attending matches during the tournament. FIFA President Gianni Infantino defended the high prices, arguing that the market justifies the cost and that many tickets are available at lower prices. He also noted that the resale market has driven up prices further.

articles.title: Steve Hilton: British strategist becomes unlikely frontrunner for California governor | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Hilton, a controversial strategist known for his unorthodox approach and "zany" policy ideas, has emerged as an unlikely frontrunner in the California gubernatorial primary.  Hilton, who gained prominence in the UK for modernizing the Conservative party and was Cameron's director of strategy, is now seeking to disrupt the political landscape in California. While some question his ability to navigate the complexities of American politics, others believe his disruptive style and unconventional thinking could resonate with voters.

articles.title: Bank of Baroda Q4 results: PAT grows 11% YoY to Rs 5,616 crore; NII up 9% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The bank's non-interest income fell 16% to Rs 3,967 crore in the quarter under review. Deposits increased significantly, with global deposits rising by 7.5%, and domestic deposits growing by 13%.  Global advances also saw growth, increasing 16% to Rs 14.29 lakh crore. Operating profit rose 11.5% to Rs 9,069 crore while gross NPAs fell 37 bps to 1.89%. However, the bank's Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) declined by 137 bps to 15.82%.

articles.title: A.P. police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, says NCRB report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, a decrease from the previous years.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reported that 17,149 individuals were arrested for these crimes and chargesheets were filed in 94.4% of the cases. The report highlighted various types of offenses, including harassment by husbands or relatives, sexual harassment, rape, attempted rape, stalking, kidnapping, assault, and murder.  A significant number of kidnapping cases remain pending with 865 cases unresolved at the end of 2024.

articles.title: Fbi: Kash Patel orders lie detector tests for FBI staff to identify alleged leaks behind negative stories of his leadership: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kash Patel, the FBI director, has ordered polygraph tests for over two dozen current and former members of his security detail as he investigates alleged leaks within the agency. This follows a wave of negative media coverage regarding Patel's conduct in office, including claims of excessive drinking, misuse of resources, and demanding expensive travel.  The move has raised concerns among some FBI officials about Patel's level of involvement in key investigations and national security matters. Ben Williamson, an FBI spokesman, denied the allegations of Patel's withdrawal from senior staff meetings but declined to comment on the polygraph testing.

articles.title: Cyril Ramaphosa: South Africa president faces call to resign after court ruling
articles.rephrased_article: The Constitutional Court ruled that parliament violated the constitution by blocking impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa in 2022.  This decision, following a legal challenge by opposition parties including Julius Malema's Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), could lead to fresh impeachment proceedings. The ruling stems from allegations of financial impropriety surrounding a $500,000 theft from Ramaphosa's rural home in 2020.  The ANC, which currently governs in coalition, has welcomed the court's decision and will hold internal meetings to consider its implications.

articles.title: UK’s ‘first gay dad’ Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and husband charged with rape, sex trafficking | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and his husband Scott Hutchison have been charged with multiple serious sexual offences, including rape, sexual assault, and modern slavery trafficking for sexual exploitation. The charges follow police raids at properties in Danbury, Maldon, and Braintree, which were part of an investigation led by Essex Police.  The pair are due to appear before Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court on Friday.

articles.title: Telangana Govt issues detailed guidelines for Musi rejuvenation Phase-I; December 2027 deadline for project completion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Government is moving forward with the ambitious Musi Riverfront Development Project, emphasizing its social responsibility and stakeholder engagement.  A Cabinet sub-committee has outlined guidelines for Phase I of the project, which involves a 5 km stretch from Himayatsagar to Bapughat, with an estimated ₹7,055 crore in funding from the Asian Development Bank. The project aims to revitalize the riverfront while minimizing impact on residents' properties. Officials have been directed to address public concerns and ensure minimal disruption during construction.

articles.title: Benazir programme cuts child stunting rates: study - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has seen significant improvements in child stunting rates under the Benazir Nashonuma Programme (BNP), according to an evaluation by Aga Khan University. The study found a 22% decrease in stunting at six months and 18% lower rates at one year of age.  The program, which has reached over 4.5 million women and children across 157 districts, is credited with reducing low birth weight cases, premature births, and weak newborns. Senator Rubina Khalid, BISP Chairperson, highlighted the importance of maternal and child health for national development.

articles.title: Market Wrap: Sensex drops 516 points, Nifty closes below 24,200 amid fresh Iran-US escalations, smallcaps outperform - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 experienced significant declines on Thursday, driven by concerns over geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.  SBI shares plummeted after disappointing earnings, while other banking and IT stocks also fell. However, some sectors like Titan and Asian Paints saw gains. Oil prices rose despite recent volatility, adding to market uncertainty. Foreign investors remained net sellers of Indian equities, contributing to the overall downturn.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Carl Jung: “Loneliness does not come from having no people about one, but from being unable to communicate the things that seem important to oneself, or from holding certain views which others find inadmissible.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carl Jung, a Swiss psychiatrist and psychoanalyst, believed loneliness stems from the inability to communicate one's true thoughts, beliefs, or emotions.  He argued that emotional isolation can occur even when surrounded by people due to a lack of meaningful connection. This quote resonates today because it highlights the psychological reality of feeling disconnected despite social interaction. Jung emphasized self-awareness and honesty as key to overcoming loneliness, suggesting that suppressing emotions can lead to feelings of isolation. His ideas continue to influence psychology, literature, philosophy, and pop culture, reminding us that true human connection involves being heard and understood.

articles.title: From political defection to murder: Jayakanthan’s story on shifting loyalties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jayakanthan's novella, *Illathavarakal*, explores the volatile political landscape of Tamil Nadu through the story of Tony, a party cadre driven to murder after his leader defects.  Tony, enraged by the change in party flag and fueled by his friends, clashes with rival supporters, resulting in a stabbing that leaves one man dead. The police apprehend Tony, highlighting the consequences of shifting loyalties in the wake of political defections.

articles.title: Constable killed after abduction by unidentified assailants in KP’s Bajaur: police - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A police constable was killed in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after being abducted by unidentified assailants. The 50-year-old officer's body was found on a mountain with signs of torture, prompting an investigation into the incident.  The district police spokesperson confirmed the postmortem report and stated that an official case has been registered against the attackers. This follows a recent surge in violence in the region, including attacks by militants and cross-border shelling.

articles.title: Tata Consumer Products Q4 Results: Profit rises 21% YoY to Rs 419 crore, revenue up 18% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Board of Directors of the company has recommended a dividend of Rs 10 per share for fiscal year 2026, if approved by shareholders. The dividend would be paid/dispatched on or after June 15, 2026, subject to tax deduction at source.

articles.title: Is Vinícius Júnior leaving Real Madrid? Crisis deepens amid training-ground fight and player hospitalisation | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde suffered a concussion after an altercation with teammate Vinícius Júnior, potentially jeopardizing his participation in Sunday's El Clásico against Barcelona.  Amidst the growing tension within the squad, reports suggest that Vinícius Júnior is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, including Manchester City, who view him as a rare market opportunity. The Brazilian forward's contract negotiations with Real Madrid have stalled, and if no new agreement is reached, he could be sold.  Despite the uncertainty surrounding his future, Vinícius Júnior has continued to perform well for Real Madrid.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh government scraps smart prepaid meter system; shifts all consumers to postpaid mode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to discontinue the smart prepaid electricity meter system and convert all existing devices to postpaid mode.  Energy Minister A.K. Sharma announced this decision, citing consumer convenience and grievances following growing protests over alleged billing irregularities. The new arrangement will see consumers receive bills after consumption, with bills for May 2026 issued in June. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission Advisory Committee member Avadhesh Kumar Verma, who represents the Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut Upbhokta Parishad, welcomed the decision but criticized the delay and alleged that the state government was pressured by the central regulatory body into taking action.

articles.title: Senate lauds courage, sacrifices of armed forces - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Senate of Pakistan passed a resolution praising the armed forces, security institutions, and the nation for their sacrifices during last year's conflict with India.  Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stated that India had requested a ceasefire through the US but Pakistan only agreed to a truce after "teaching them a lesson." The Information Minister, Attaullah Tarar, asserted that Pakistan shattered India’s dreams of regional hegemony in just a few hours and highlighted the nation's unity in defense.

articles.title: Titan Q4 Results: Cons profit jumps 35% YoY to Rs 1,179 crore; Rs 15/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Titan Company Ltd. reported a 28% increase in Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT) to Rs 1,875 crore for the quarter ending December 31, 2023. The company's jewellery business saw strong growth with a 50% year-on-year increase in revenue, driven by robust demand for gold and studded products.  Titan also announced a dividend of Rs 15 per equity share, payable within seven days after the annual general meeting.

articles.title: Most expensive ticket ever? World Cup final seat listed for $11.5 million despite being one of the worst in stadium | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A standard ticket for the 2026 FIFA World Cup final has been listed online for $11.5 million (£8.5 million), a price that has drawn criticism for its exorbitant cost despite offering no additional perks beyond a regular seat. FIFA president Gianni Infantino defended the pricing, stating it reflects the American entertainment market and that resale prices are often higher than official ticket prices.  The 2026 World Cup will be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

articles.title: Smacks of low political opportunism: Mani Shankar Aiyar slams Congress’ TVK tie-up decision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Veteran Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar criticized the party's decision to ally with the TVK in Tamil Nadu, calling it "low political opportunism" and a betrayal of its longstanding partnership with the DMK.  Aiyar argued that this move would facilitate the entry of a communal BJP into Tamil Nadu's Dravidian ethos, making it the worst own goal in political history. He expressed deep unease with the Congress' decision to abandon a tried and tested ally, citing Mahatma Gandhi's principles of morality and self-sacrifice. The Congress' decision to join forces with the TVK has been met with disapproval from the DMK, who described it as "backstabbing."

articles.title: Kalyan Jewellers Q4 Results: Cons PAT soars 118% YoY to Rs 409 crore; revenue jumps 66% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kalyan Jewellers India reported a significant increase in revenue and profitability for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. Revenue from operations surged by 66.2% to Rs 10,274.9 crore, driven by strong growth in both domestic and international markets. EBITDA also saw substantial growth, increasing by 84.2% to Rs 735.7 crore, while the company's EBITDA margin improved to 7.2%. The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 2.50 per equity share, subject to shareholder approval.

articles.title: How black holes become cosmic monsters: Scientists uncover the violent merger chain behind giant space objects | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new study suggests that black holes, particularly the largest ones detected so far, may not form from a single star collapse but instead grow step-by-step inside dense star clusters. Researchers analyzing gravitational-wave data from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA found a clear split between two types of black holes: lower mass and slower spinning, likely formed from ordinary stellar collapse, and heavier, faster-spinning black holes that might have been built through multiple mergers within these clusters. This finding challenges long-standing models of stellar evolution and suggests that repeated black hole mergers could be the engine behind these giants.  The study's findings contribute to a growing understanding of black hole growth and their potential role in cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Maharashtra Class 10 results out; over 92% students pass, girls outperform boys again - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) announced the Class 10 results, with an overall pass percentage of 92.09%. Girls performed better than boys, achieving a 94.96% pass rate compared to boys' 89.56%. The Kokan division topped the list with 97.62%, while the Chatrapati Sambhajinagar division recorded the lowest pass percentage at 88.41%.

articles.title: PTI walks out of Senate to protest Bushra’s ‘secret’ hospital visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI senators walked out of the Senate after Syed Ali Zafar, the party's parliamentary leader, raised concerns over the "sudden and suspicious" transfer of Bushra Bibi, former PM Imran Khan's spouse, from Adiala jail to a hospital. Zafar demanded immediate disclosure of her medical test results, permission for personal doctors to examine her, unrestricted family meetings, and her transfer to Shifa International Hospital. He also called for an independent medical board, access for human rights organizations, and a Senate committee visit.  Rana Sanaullah, the PM's aide, advised the party to pursue the matter through legal channels.

articles.title: India-Pakistan: One year after military conflict, ceasefire holds - but little else does
articles.rephrased_article: One year after the four-day India-Pakistan conflict, a fragile equilibrium has replaced the dangerous escalation. The region's diplomatic ties remain frozen, trade is suspended, and cricket ties are severed. India and Pakistan have both made strategic gains in the wake of the conflict, but analysts caution against overstating their newfound influence.  The conflict also highlighted the evolving nature of warfare, with both countries investing heavily in drone technology and modernizing their militaries. While a complete diplomatic freeze is unlikely, the future depends on the willingness of Prime Minister Modi and Field Marshal Asim Munir to pursue diplomacy.

articles.title: Keir Starmer’s leadership on line after Labour’s disastrous election night | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer's leadership is facing renewed scrutiny after Labour suffered heavy losses in local elections, including the loss of every council seat contested in Hartlepool.  Jonathan Brash, the local Labour MP, called for Starmer to resign, while David Lammy, the deputy prime minister, urged colleagues to remain loyal. Reform UK emerged as a significant winner, gaining seats across former Labour heartlands like Wigan and Bolton. The results are seen as a major setback for Labour, with experts predicting further losses in other areas where prominent figures like Angela Rayner and Wes Streeting have local influence.

articles.title: Delhi HC to pass interim order protecting Shashi Tharoor’s personality rights over deepfake videos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court issued an interim order to protect the personality rights of Shashi Tharoor, a Congress leader, after he filed a suit against deepfake videos falsely attributing statements to him.  Tharoor's lawyer argued that the videos were circulating online and being misused by foreign states, damaging his reputation. The court also issued notices to social media platforms such as X and Meta, owner of Instagram.

articles.title: Sandip Sabharwal remains bullish on FMCG, retail and defence themes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors are closely watching whether the rally in Indian equities can sustain itself amid elevated crude oil prices, mixed global cues, and uncertainty around the West Asia conflict. Sabharwal, a market analyst, believes that strong earnings momentum and consumer revival will drive further gains if geopolitical tensions ease and oil prices moderate.  He notes that while India's economy appears "pretty well placed," sustained inflation could impact consumer spending power.

articles.title: Caleb Burke: D4vd’s brother Caleb Burke breaks silence after TMZ claims and Celeste Hernandez backstage rumors explode - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Caleb Burke, younger brother of singer D4vd, has denied claims that he helped Celeste Rivas Hernandez get backstage at one of his concerts. Burke stated in Instagram stories that the rumors are false and he was not close to his brother growing up. He also refuted accusations that he is using the situation for attention, emphasizing his focus on justice for Celeste.  Caleb Burke explained that he had been sharing music online for years before the controversy surrounding his brother's legal troubles arose.

articles.title: NAB freezes four more Bahria Town properties in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) in Karachi has frozen four high-value properties of Bahria Town, including the Bahria Icon Tower and the Bahria Town Tower on Tariq Road, due to investigations linking them to the laundering of crime proceeds. The bureau attached these assets under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, as well as significant land holdings in Sheikhupura and Peshawar owned by front companies used for illicit funds. Legal proceedings are underway regarding these properties.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: Lone TVK cadre stages protest outside Lok Bhavan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party cadre, identified as Suresh, was apprehended by police near Lok Bhavan in Chennai on Friday after staging a protest demanding the Tamil Nadu Governor invite party leader C. Joseph Vijay to form the government.  Suresh is an assistant of film director S.A. Chandrasekar, father of Mr. Vijay. Police warned him against future protests in the prohibited area and advised him to obtain permission before doing so.

articles.title: Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, other bank stocks drop up to 2%, Nifty Bank falls 440 points. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Bank index fell 0.8% to 55,611 as of 10:45 am due to the ongoing political situation in West Asia and FII selling that pushed the rupee down.  Shares of HDFC Bank, India's largest private bank, declined nearly 2%, following Chairman Atanu Chakraborty's exit citing "incongruence" between his personal values and bank practices. Other banks like Axis Bank and Federal Bank also saw declines, while SBI and Bank of Baroda are expected to release their quarterly results later today.  Technical analysts suggest support levels for the index at 55,720 and 55,400, with resistance at 56,280 and 56,550.

articles.title: NASA captures a sea of spinning clouds over Antarctica’s remote volcanic island | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA, using its Landsat 8 spacecraft, captured an extraordinary aerial photograph of a "sea of rotating clouds" near Peter I Island in Antarctica. This phenomenon, known as the Von Kármán vortex street effect, is caused by airflow deflecting and spinning into eddies around obstacles like islands. The winds in this area are known for their strength, allowing atmospheric events to form clearly over the water. These vortices provide valuable scientific insight into atmospheric processes and can be used to study climate change and weather patterns.

articles.title: India pushes for inclusive migration, stronger anti-trafficking laws at United Nations General Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Union Minister Kirti Vardhan Singh emphasized the country's commitment to building an inclusive and humane framework for migration at the United Nations General Assembly.  Singh highlighted India's large diaspora, significant remittances, and bilateral agreements aimed at creating sustainable pathways for safe and ethical migration. He also discussed strengthening consular protection through initiatives like the 'MADAD' portal and Migrant Resource Centres. India has been a top remittance-receiving country since 2010, receiving billions of dollars annually from its citizens working abroad.

articles.title: Coforge shares surge 6%, rally 16% in three days post Q4 results. What's ahead for investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coforge reported a significant increase in net profit and revenue for the January-March quarter of 2026, exceeding expectations.  The company's CEO, Sudhir Singh, attributed the strong performance to solid deal wins and improved margins. Jefferies, Nomura, and other international brokerages have issued "Buy" ratings on Coforge shares, citing its robust order book, acquisition of Encora, and projected growth in FY27.

articles.title: Real Madrid in crisis? Valverde ruled out of El Clásico ahead of Barça clash after training-ground fight | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde has been ruled out of Sunday's El Clásico against FC Barcelona after sustaining a head injury during an altercation with teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni. The incident, which occurred at Real Madrid's Valdebebas training complex, followed an earlier confrontation between the two midfielders on Wednesday.  The clash escalated into a physical fight and required Valverde to seek medical attention. Head coach Álvaro Arbeloa called an emergency meeting to address the escalating tensions within the squad, adding further pressure ahead of the crucial match against Barcelona.

articles.title: Dabur shares jump 4% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Nomura saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dabur India's revenue for Q4FY26 increased by 7.3% year-on-year to Rs 3,038 crore, driven by strong performance in its domestic FMCG segment and underlying volume growth of 6%. Operating profit rose 12.5%, supported by the company's execution and pricing strategies. Morgan Stanley maintained an 'Underweight' rating on Dabur India with a target price of Rs 412, citing continued seasonality and weather-related risks despite near-term earnings support.  However, Nomura maintained a 'Buy' rating on Dabur India with a target price of Rs 600, highlighting the company's pricing measures to protect margins.

articles.title: Dinosaur Skull Discovery: One of the rarest 150-million-year-old dinosaur skulls ever found has been uncovered in Spain | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Palaeontologists in Teruel, Spain, unearthed a nearly complete skull of the armoured dinosaur *Dacentrurus armatus*, dating back 150 million years to the Late Jurassic period. This discovery is significant as it's the most intact stegosaur skull ever found in Europe and provides crucial information about these ancient plant-eaters' cranial structure. Researchers used advanced 3D modelling and comparative anatomy techniques to discover previously unknown features of the Riodeva skull, formally defining a new evolutionary group called ‘Neostegosauria’. This finding clarifies stegosaurs' lineage on the Iberian Peninsula and offers fresh insights into how these iconic plated dinosaurs evolved across different continents long ago.

articles.title: Bottom 50% of Nagaland households receive only 18% of total income, says report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Secretary Sentiyanger Imchen released a report on income disparity in Nagaland, revealing that the top 5% of households earn nearly 21% of the state's gross income, while the bottom 50% receive only 18%. The report, based on a field survey conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the University of Hyderabad, found a Gini coefficient of 0.46 for Nagaland, indicating high income inequality.  The study also highlighted that rural areas had a higher income disparity than urban areas.

articles.title: HFCL shares drop 2% after skyrocketing 92% in one month. Time to buy or better to wait? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL's share price experienced a significant rally this year, surging nearly 147% in just 16 weeks to reach a fresh 52-week high. The company's strong order book and recent acquisitions have bolstered its revenue visibility and future prospects. Geojit Investments maintains a "Buy" call for the stock, projecting an upside potential of nearly 3%.  The brokerage highlights HFCL's growth in data centers, defense sector, and expanding manufacturing capabilities as key drivers for long-term success.

articles.title: Romania History: A newly discovered 6,000-year-old mega-structure in Romania is rewriting Europe’s prehistoric history | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Romania have uncovered a monumental mega-structure dating back 6,000 years. The structure, known as 'Building 43', is almost four times larger than typical dwellings from the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture and was constructed using sophisticated timber-frame techniques and large quantities of clay.  The building's intentional burning at its end suggests a planned ritualistic function, possibly serving as a social center or hub for shared experiences. The lack of luxury items found within the structure indicates that this society operated without a central leader, instead achieving impressive engineering feats through community collaboration.

articles.title: 'Too much at stake to accept ignorance': Lawmakers challenge US ambiguity over Israel’s nuclear capability - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article:
Congressman Joaquin Castro, a senior Democratic lawmaker, and nearly 30 other Democratic lawmakers sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the US government to address its longstanding ambiguity regarding Israel's alleged nuclear weapons program. The lawmakers argue that this secrecy is untenable given the ongoing war with Iran and that Congress has a constitutional responsibility to be fully informed about the nuclear balance in the Middle East. They directly asked for information on Israel's nuclear capabilities, including warheads, launch systems, fissile material production, and possible thresholds for nuclear use. The letter also questioned whether the US administration has received assurances from Israel regarding the non-use of nuclear weapons. 
The lawmakers cited public statements and declassified intelligence assessments to argue that Israel's nuclear capability is already widely understood within official circles.

articles.title: One Nation candidate David Farley sought involvement with independent ‘Voices’ movement | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Farley, a candidate for the One Nation party in the Farrer byelection, had previously engaged with the independent "Voices" movement before endorsing Michelle Milthorpe.  Farley's political history has been scrutinized due to his past affiliations with Labor and his involvement with the Voices movement. He has also been accused of shifting allegiances for personal gain. The One Nation party claims Farley's journey reflects a desire for a party that represents Australian values, while critics point to inconsistencies in his political stances.

articles.title: West Bengal government formation LIVE: Amit Shah arrives in Kolkata for BJP legislature party meet to elect new CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP legislature party will meet in Kolkata on Friday, May 8, 2026, to elect its leader with Suvendu Adhikari emerging as the frontrunner.  Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the TMC’s 15-year rule, Mamata Banerjee, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

articles.title: Shakti Pumps shares tumble 7% as Q4 profit drops 65% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shakti Pumps' revenue increased 28.9% year-over-year to Rs 857.8 crore, but rising costs led to a significant drop in EBITDA and profit margins. The company’s basic EPS fell 66.3% to Rs 3.1 per share. Despite the muted earnings performance, the board recommended a final dividend of Rs 1 per equity share. Institutional investors reduced their holdings during the quarter, while stock performance has declined nearly 36% over the past year.

articles.title: Rare ‘Earth Mango’ found in Kerala: The hidden fungus locals call Nilamanga has returned again | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A farmer in Kerala's Palakkad district unearthed several unusual mushroom-like structures, identified as Sclerotium stipitatum, a rare subterranean fungus locally known as "Nilamanga" or "Earth Mango".  Researchers believe this discovery highlights the need for greater study of underground fungi, which are often poorly documented and may be disappearing before scientists can document them. The fungus's medicinal potential is attracting interest, but experts caution that further research is needed to confirm its effectiveness in treating medical conditions. Scientists are also investigating the fungus's relationship with termite-rich soil environments and its dependence on wet soil conditions during Kerala's monsoon season.

articles.title: J&K Lieutenant Governor given telecom control powers during public safety events - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The President of India has authorized the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor to exercise powers related to telecom services in the Union Territory during public safety events or national emergencies. These powers include interception of signals, suspension of service, and decryption of messages, as outlined in the Telecommunications Act, 2023. The order was published in the gazette on Thursday (May 7, 2026).

articles.title: Communications minister Anika Wells repays $10,000 in incorrect travel expenses | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anika Wells, the communications minister, repaid over $10,000 in incorrect travel claims identified by an audit. The audit found four mistakes dating back to 2022, totaling $8,092.89, and she has paid a 25% penalty loading for the errors.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended Wells, stating she had referred herself to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority and repaid the money in accordance with the rules. He also noted that Wells apologized for the mistakes.

articles.title: Silver gains Rs 2,361, gold near Rs 1.53 lakh amid hopes of Iran peace talks. What should investors do? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump made statements on Truth Social regarding the U.S.-Iran confrontation, claiming that U.S. forces had destroyed Iranian targets and warned of further military action if a nuclear agreement is not reached.  The situation influenced precious metal markets, with spot gold rising 0.7% to $4,719.85 per ounce and silver climbing 1.6% to $79.74 per ounce. Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart suggested that gold and silver prices remain volatile due to factors like the dollar index, crude oil prices, and upcoming U.S. non-farm payroll data.

articles.title: Akaash Singh: Why did Akaash Singh leave Flagrant? Andrew Schulz confirms heartbreaking podcast exit after nine years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Akaash Singh is stepping away from the Flagrant podcast after a decade, focusing on his stand-up comedy career.  Andrew Schulz, Singh's longtime friend and co-host, announced the decision during the May 6, 2026 episode, noting that Singh had recently achieved significant success with sold-out tours and performances. Schulz expressed bittersweet emotions about Singh's departure but acknowledged his friend's desire to prioritize his dream of becoming a successful stand-up comedian.

articles.title: T.N. Government formation LIVE: CPI, CPI(M), VCK hold the key to any further churn in State politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, the Tamil Nadu Governor, informed C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), that the requisite majority support for forming a government has not been achieved in the state assembly.  Vijay and senior party leaders have reached out to DMK allies, including the Communist Party of India, CPI(M), and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, who hold the key to further political developments. M.K. Stalin, the outgoing Chief Minister, reportedly met with these parties to discuss the possibility of supporting an AIADMK-led government.

articles.title: BSE shares fall 3% despite Q4 profit surge. Should you buy, sell or hold India’s oldest stock exchange? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BSE's Q4FY26 revenue surged 85% year-on-year to Rs 1,564 crore, driven by a significant increase in transaction charges.  The company reported a 32% sequential profit growth, reaching Rs 602 crore from the previous quarter. BSE's EBITDA margin stood at 48%, while they expect continued growth in monthly contract volumes and larger contract sizes to help lower clearing charges.  Nuvama Institutional Equities maintains a "Buy" rating on BSE, projecting an upside potential of 15%.

articles.title: Us Iran Ceasefire: US, Iran weigh 30-day ceasefire plan, reopening Strait of Hormuz; n-talks still in limbo - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the US are discussing a temporary framework that would pause hostilities, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and create space for broader nuclear negotiations. The proposed framework includes lifting the US blockade on Iranian shipping, reopening the Strait to commercial traffic, and ending military hostilities under a ceasefire agreement.  Discussions remain ongoing with negotiators exchanging proposals on a long-term agreement, but key sticking points include sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program, and the release of frozen assets.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results: How to check? - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Government Examinations, Tamil Nadu, announced the Class 12 examination results on May 8, 2026. Students can access their results online through tnresults.nic.in and dge.tn.gov.in.  They can also check their results via WhatsApp by saving the number +91-7845252525 and sending a "Hi" message with their registration number and date of birth. Additionally, students can download their marksheets through DigiLocker by following specific steps outlined in the article.

articles.title: Several drugs consignments recovered along Gujarat coast - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Security agencies and police in Gujarat have recovered several consignments of suspected charas from coastal areas, prompting intensified surveillance along the state's maritime border.  The BSF, a security force, recovered ten packets of contraband in Kutch on Wednesday (May 6, 2026), while police found around 4 kg of charas near Kalyanpur in Devbhumi Dwarka district. Officials suspect smugglers abandoned these packages after increased patrols and investigations are underway to identify those involved.

articles.title: 'We’ll knock them out harder': Trump warns Iran of harsher military action after 3 US ships came under fire in Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claimed that three US naval destroyers, while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz, came under fire from Iranian forces but suffered no damage.  He warned Iran of stronger military action if it does not agree to sign a deal quickly. The incident followed reports of military exchanges in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where US Central Command stated American forces targeted Iranian facilities responsible for attacks against US warships.

articles.title: ICE in Minnesota: 'I'd rather live in hiding,' Somali man at risk of deportation tells BBC
articles.rephrased_article: Following the end of a surge in immigration enforcement operations in Minnesota, fear remains among the Somali community. Abdi, a 23-year-old man who fled Somalia due to threats from al-Shabab, fears ICE raids and is living in hiding. The operation, which targeted undocumented immigrants, has led to the detention of some US citizens with Somali heritage and sparked criticism from lawmakers like Ilhan Omar and Jim Abeler.  The Trump administration's efforts to end Temporary Protected Status for Somalis have further exacerbated tensions, prompting concerns about the safety of those living in the country. Despite efforts by community leaders and faith groups to provide support and warn residents of potential raids, many remain fearful of ICE agents.

articles.title: Foreign remittances to Kerala stay resilient despite West Asia crisis - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Federal Bank and South Indian Bank reported quarter-on-quarter growth in non-resident deposits inflow, indicating the stability of Kerala's economy despite the Iran war. The rise is attributed to a 5.4% rupee depreciation between January and March, leading to higher remittances on the same base amount. While experts predict continued inflows due to people seeking to protect their finances, they warn that prolonged conflict could negatively impact these flows in the long run.

articles.title: Congress blocks Agra-Mumbai highway in Indore over farmers’ issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress workers blocked the Agra-Mumbai National Highway in Indore, Madhya Pradesh on Thursday as part of a state-wide protest demanding attention to farmers' issues. Vikrant Bhuria, national president of the Adivasi Congress, accused the BJP government of neglecting farmer concerns and failing to guarantee minimum support prices (MSP). He also alleged irregularities within the soybean 'Bhavantar Yojana' and claimed that market yards were dominated by corporations.  The protest is expected to continue in phases.

articles.title: Fact check: Was Candace Owens arrested on harassment charges after alleged Facebook threats? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens escalated their online rivalry into a personal attack after Loomer resurfaced an old newspaper clipping alleging Owens faced harassment charges as a teenager. Loomer accused Owens of hypocrisy, while Owens countered with accusations of stalking and doxxing. The feud has expanded to include family members and legal threats, highlighting the blurring lines between political debate and personal warfare in the digital age.

articles.title: Retail stake cut in 284 BSE 500 companies in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Retail investors reduced holdings in 65% of companies with a market cap of ₹25,000 crore or more and 60% of those below this threshold during the March quarter of FY26. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) increased stakes in 201 companies, surpassing the previous quarter's reading, while domestic funds also saw an increase in holdings. Company promoters joined institutional investors by raising their shareholding in 42 companies, marking a high point in at least 12 quarters.

articles.title: Ally Cong. seeks ‘better coordination over crucial public issues’ with ruling NC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders in J&K have called for improved coordination between the party and the National Conference (NC), emphasizing the importance of mutual understanding and cooperation for effective governance.  Following disagreements over Statehood restoration, Ghulam Ahmad Mir, a senior Congress leader, stated that concerns and aspirations of the party must be respected to ensure the coalition's continued relevance. This comes after Dr. Farooq Abdullah, president of the NC, accused the Congress of not doing enough to restore Statehood.

articles.title: "He just kissed me": IShowSpeed left horrified as chaotic livestream moment explodes across social media - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed's Dominican Republic livestream was marred by a viral incident when a fan attempted to kiss him uninvited. Security intervened, and the moment sparked online debate about personal boundaries in streaming. The clip quickly spread on Reddit and X, with viewers discussing the streamer's reaction and security team's response. Fellow streamer xQc raised questions about unusually high concurrent viewership numbers for the stream, suggesting potential bot activity but not accusing IShowSpeed.

articles.title: Foreign investors continue to pull out of financials in second half of April - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign investors withdrew a significant amount of money from the Indian stock market in April, particularly from the banking sector.  The outflows totaled ₹28,301 crore across 15 sectors during the second half of the month, with over 41% coming from financial institutions. Saurabh Patwa, head of equities and portfolio manager at Quest Investment Managers, attributed this trend to strong power demand driven by AI investments and the sector's resilience in times of uncertainty.

articles.title: Mumbai family deaths: Rat poison ingredient zinc phosphide found in viscera and watermelon sample - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four members of the Dokadia family, residents of south Mumbai, died last month after consuming rat poison found in a watermelon. The Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) confirmed the presence of zinc phosphide in their viscera and stomach contents.  The police are investigating whether the family intentionally ingested the poison or if it was accidental. Further investigation is being conducted by the JJ Marg police station, which has recorded statements from family members and neighbors.

articles.title: “You will be dead forever”: Sneako posts disturbing messages after Australia reportedly issues lifetime ban against streamer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nico ‘Sneako’ Kenn De Balinthazy, a controversial streamer, has sparked concern with a series of death-themed posts on X following his ban from Australia.  Australian officials banned Sneako after reports claimed he spread hate speech and was allegedly trying to incite violence. The streamer denied these claims, stating he returned to the United States voluntarily.  His recent posts have fueled speculation about his mental state, with some interpreting them as a cry for attention amidst controversy surrounding his Australia visit.

articles.title: Two Islamic-State linked Australian women charged with crimes against humanity
articles.rephrased_article: Two Australian women, Kawsar Ahmad and Zeinab Ahmad, were charged with crimes against humanity after returning from Syria. They are accused of keeping a female slave in their home and complicity in the purchase of the woman for $10,000. Janai Safar, another Australian woman, was also arrested and charged with entering a declared conflict zone and joining IS.  The Australian Federal Police (AFP) allege that these women travelled to Syria between 2014-2015 and are part of a larger group of Australians who were returned to the al-Roj camp in Syria after attempting to return to Australia. The AFP is continuing its investigation into all Australians who traveled to declared conflict areas.

articles.title: NASA’s new plasma engine could reduce travel time to Mars | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) successfully tested a lithium-fed magnetoplasmadynamic (MPD) thruster, achieving 120 kilowatts of power output.
