The cement giant saw total sales volume grow by 11% year-on-year, with a 27% rise in revenue from operations compared to the previous year's quarter. Nomura, JM Financial, and Elara Capital all maintained their positive ratings on the company's stock, citing strong performance and growth potential.

articles.title: TVK makes inroads into AIADMK’s core voter base in Tamil Nadu | Data - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has significantly altered the political landscape of Tamil Nadu, posing a threat to the AIADMK's core vote bank.  AIADMK lost significant support in several regions, particularly central and south, while DMK retained its base despite experiencing a decline in some areas. The TVK's success was linked to a negative correlation with the AIADMK, suggesting voters shifted their allegiance due to anti-incumbency or preference for new political entities.  This shift has led to a larger swing for the DMK compared to 2021 despite the AIADMK losing votes overall.

articles.title: Gas companies will be forced to set aside local supply under major Labor shakeup | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The federal government announced a reservation scheme requiring gas companies to set aside 20% of exports for domestic use on the east coast, starting July 1, 2027. This policy aims to address supply concerns and lower gas prices. The scheme will apply to contracts signed after December 22, 2022, while existing contracts are exempt. Climate change and energy minister Chris Bowen stated that the measure would provide a "modest oversupply" of gas into the east coast market, helping to avert shortages and put downward pressure on prices.

articles.title: Godrej Consumer shares tumble 6% despite Q4 show. Should you buy, sell or hold the stock? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Godrej Consumer Products reported a 11% increase in revenue for the quarter, reaching Rs 3,900 crore.  The company's EBITDA also rose 11%, to Rs 841.4 crore. Morgan Stanley and Motilal Oswal maintained their positive ratings on the company, citing strong domestic growth and potential upside in international markets.  Despite near-term risks from crude oil and palm oil inflation, management expressed confidence in sustaining profitability momentum in FY27.

articles.title: Vienna plumber becomes millionaire after tugging a rope and finding 66 pounds of hidden gold in Austria | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A plumber in Vienna's Penzing district discovered a hidden treasure of 66 pounds of gold coins worth approximately $2.4 million while renovating a basement. The find, according to Austrian law, is shared equally between the finder and the property owner, making the plumber a millionaire. This unexpected discovery sheds light on how wealth was secretly kept in Austria during the mid-20th century.  The coins were hidden under the floor in the 1930s or early 1940s, likely to protect them from wartime loss.

articles.title: Doctors’ body seeks review of SC ruling on liability of deceased doctors’ families - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA), Telangana expressed concern over a recent Supreme Court ruling that allows compensation proceedings in medical negligence cases to continue even after the death of a doctor, implicating legal heirs. The association argued that extending litigation to family members not involved in patient care could cause distress and discourage young doctors from entering high-risk specialties. They urged the Union Government, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and other stakeholders to reconsider the judgment's implications for healthcare delivery systems in India.

articles.title: Polycab shares jump 6% as post-earnings target prices go up to Rs 10,500. Should you buy now? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Following strong Q4 financial results, Polycab saw analysts raise target prices and maintain bullish ratings. The company's revenue and EBITDA grew despite geopolitical disruptions and raw material volatility.  Analysts highlight Polycab's market share gains in the organized cables and wires sector, driven by execution quality and a robust FMEG segment.  They anticipate continued growth fueled by extra-high voltage capacity expansion and aggressive capital expenditure plans.

articles.title: South Korean court reduces Han Duck-soo’s prison term in martial law case | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A South Korean appeals court reduced the prison sentence of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo to 15 years for crimes related to ex-President Yoon Suk Yeol's declaration of martial law. The court acknowledged Han's long public service and lessened penalties, citing a lack of evidence demonstrating his active role in the insurrection.  Han, who has been imprisoned since January, maintains he did not agree to or help with the declaration but regrets not being able to stop it.

articles.title: Jeffrey Epstein: 'They found nothing': Jeffrey Epstein's alleged suicide note released - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US District Judge Kenneth Karas unsealed a handwritten note purportedly written by Jeffrey Epstein, discovered by his former jail cellmate, Nicholas Tartaglione. The note, which was submitted in connection with Tartaglione's criminal case, includes the line "It is a treat to be able to choose ones time to say goodbye" and suggests that Epstein felt he had control over his death.  The judge ruled that there were no legal reasons to keep the note sealed despite questions about its authenticity or chain of custody.

articles.title: One year of Operation Sindhoor | PM Modi says Indian forces gave fitting response to terrorism - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor, a military strike launched in response to a terror attack on civilians in Pahalgam, Pakistan.  He praised the armed forces' courage and precision during the operation, highlighting its success in safeguarding national security. Modi also emphasized India's commitment to defeating terrorism and dismantling its supporting infrastructure.

articles.title: 18 Russian medical varsities to take part in education fair - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Russian universities will participate in an All India Russian Education Fair across Tamil Nadu this month, offering 10,000 MBBS seats to Indian students. The fair is open to those who have cleared the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test and scored at least 50% marks in relevant core subjects. Russian Consul General Valerii Khodzhaev stated that Russia aims to attract 5,00,000 foreign students by 2030. The fair will be held across several cities in Tamil Nadu from May 9th to 14th and offers full scholarships to about 220 Indian students.

articles.title: In a first, world’s smallest wild cat snapped with kitten in Faridabad; confirms breeding outside protected areas, say researchers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers, including wildlife photographer Yatin Verma, have documented the first confirmed breeding of a rusty-spotted cat in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and Haryana.  The discovery was made during routine field surveys conducted since August 2022. The adult cat and its kitten were observed perched on a False Ashoka tree in Kot village, confirming active reproduction outside protected areas. This finding highlights the importance of the Aravalis mountain system for wildlife conservation, including the rusty-spotted cat, which is listed as 'Near Threatened' on the IUCN Red List.  The research paper documenting this discovery was published in Zoo’s Print.

articles.title: RBI introduces specific turnover thresholds for money changers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released revised guidelines for money changers, requiring a turnover threshold of ₹10 crore and regulatory approval for management changes exceeding 50% ownership. The central bank is shifting oversight to principal authorized dealers, strengthening accountability in areas like cross-border retail forex transactions.  These new rules also introduce AD Category-III licenses for entities dealing with forex incidental to their business or offering innovative products and services, requiring a minimum net worth of ₹2 crore. Entities with revoked, surrendered, or previously rejected licenses face a one-year cooling-off period before reapplication.

articles.title: Congress leader Varsha Gaikwad writes to Maharashtra Governor, seeks immediate enactment of Shakti Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Varsha Gaikwad, Mumbai Congress president and MP, has written to Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma urging urgent action on rising crimes against women in the state.  Gaikwad requested the Governor's intervention regarding the Shakti Criminal Laws (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2020, which awaits presidential assent, and urged the government to take strict action against atrocities against women. The letter comes amid protests following a four-year-old girl's alleged rape and murder in Pune district.

articles.title: Canara Bank invites bids for Rs 509 crore loan of Rajesh Exports - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Canara Bank is seeking bids for its loan to Rajesh Exports, one of India's largest gold jewelry producers, as it awaits directions from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) on its bankruptcy petition. The bank aims to avoid prolonged litigation by selling the loan if a suitable offer is received.  Interested parties must submit expressions of interest this week.

articles.title: CEC directs West Bengal officials to ensure zero post-poll violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar directed West Bengal authorities to ensure zero tolerance for post-poll violence following three deaths linked to alleged incidents since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026. Kumar instructed authorities to immediately arrest those responsible for inciting violence and vandalism, with increased vigilance across districts by police and central forces. The West Bengal Assembly polls were held in two phases on April 23 and 29, with the BJP securing victory.

articles.title: Bulls return to D-Street as falling oil prices ease geopolitical jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE Nifty 50 and S&P BSE Sensex both rose on Wednesday, boosted by a decline in Brent crude futures prices.  US President Donald Trump warned of renewed bombing if Iran doesn't meet US demands, but the fall in oil prices improved global sentiment. The India VIX, a measure of market volatility, dropped to its lowest level since the start of the conflict, signaling lower near-term risk expectations.

articles.title: NC, PDP in war of words over Rajya Sabha polls, closure of seminary, ‘sidelining’ Urdu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, J&K Chief Minister, inaugurated a sports complex in Tangmarg, while Mehbooba Mufti, PDP president, criticized the NC for using the Rajya Sabha election results and the closure of the Siraj-ul-Aloom school as political tools. The NC accused the PDP of not appointing polling agents during the Rajya Sabha elections, while the PDP claimed the NC was diverting attention from substantive concerns like the Urdu language erasure and the Waqf Bill.

articles.title: Companies look to shrink issue sizes to get IPOs pass through - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) recently relaxed rules allowing companies with IPO approvals to adjust issue sizes by up to 50% without re-filing documents. Companies in sectors like non-banking finance, jewellery, food, packaging, healthcare, and steel are considering trimming their IPO sizes due to volatile market conditions and investor appetite.  This flexibility could help companies avoid under-subscription or pricing pressure while still securing funding for their businesses.

articles.title: Slain Chandranath Rath: From air force serviceman to Suvendu’s trusted troubleshooter - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandranath Rath, a close aide of Suvendu Adhikari, the leader of the opposition in West Bengal, was shot dead on Wednesday night.  Rath had served in the Indian Air Force for nearly two decades before transitioning into political coordination and administrative roles. He joined Adhikari's inner circle around 2019 after a brief stint in the corporate sector. Rath played a key role in several high-profile political battles, including the BJP’s Bhabanipur campaign, and was considered a trusted confidant of Adhikari.  His death has sparked strong reactions in Bengal and heightened tensions following the Assembly election results.

articles.title: RBI may have to bear forex risk to boost foreign money inflows - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nomura's Sonal Varma predicts a large balance of payment (BOP) deficit of $68 billion in FY27, potentially requiring the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to implement a forex deposit scheme.  The rupee has experienced significant depreciation recently, prompting concerns about overseas fund outflows. The central bank is exploring options such as reviving a similar program from 2013 or eliminating withholding tax on foreign government bond investors. However, some economists like Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis argue that attracting dollar inflows without rising remittances and NRI deposits will be challenging.

articles.title: Federal authorities arrest 18 people in Los Angeles park in drug crackdown | Los Angeles | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federal authorities arrested 18 people in Los Angeles as part of a crackdown on drug trafficking in MacArthur Park. The Department of Justice, working with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and local law enforcement, conducted surveillance operations and undercover purchases to identify distributors.  The investigation alleges that two defendants are key suppliers of fentanyl and methamphetamine, potentially linked to the 18th Street gang, who distribute drugs to street-level dealers in the area. The suspects are expected to appear in court on Thursday.

articles.title: 65% of newly elected Bengal MLAs face criminal cases; 61% are ‘crorepatis’: ADR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) reported that 65% of newly elected legislators in the West Bengal Assembly have declared criminal cases, a significant increase from previous elections.  Of these, 58% face serious charges, including murder and attempt to murder. The report also found that 74% of winning candidates from the Bharatiya Janata Party and 43% from the All India Trinamool Congress have declared criminal cases.  The total assets of all winning candidates stand at ₹1,091 crore, with an average asset of Rs 3.73 crore per MLA. The report also highlighted concerns about the rising wealth among elected representatives and under-representation of women in the legislature.

articles.title: Rising costs, EV push may pressure Hero MotoCorp margins despite strong Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hero MotoCorp reported a 30 basis point expansion in its operating margin to 14.7% for FY26, despite rising input costs and increased advertising expenses. The company expects the cost pressure to be transitory and maintains its medium-term guidance of 14-16% Ebitda margin.  While Hero MotoCorp's electric vehicle (EV) division continues to operate at a lower margin than its internal combustion engine (ICE) operations, the company anticipates narrowing losses on a per-unit basis as volumes increase and benefits from incentive schemes grow. The two-wheeler industry is expected to grow in high single digits in FY27, with scooters outpacing motorcycles.

articles.title: Tyler “sym” Porter cause of death: Twitch streamer and TSM Valorant pro killed during birthday trip - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyler "sym" Porter, a rising star in the Valorant esports scene, tragically died at 21 years old after a car accident while celebrating his birthday with friends.  He was known for his aggressive Jett plays and charismatic personality, earning him a large following on social media. TSM, where he played a key role in elevating their academy program, released an emotional statement mourning his loss alongside fellow player Austen. Porter's impact extended beyond tournament wins, as he was admired for his work ethic and ability to uplift struggling teams.  Tributes poured in from across the esports world, highlighting his positive influence on teammates and friends alike.

articles.title: Gram Sabhas that gave nod to Nicobar project did not have mandatory 50% quorum - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration claims to have achieved the required quorum for the Great Nicobar Island project, despite attendance figures ranging from 2% to 15% of the population. The administration argues that this constitutes proper quorum under the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rules. However, petitions before the Calcutta High Court challenge the process, alleging violations and arguing that the Tribal Council should have been consulted instead of the Gram Sabhas.  The Central government has also requested time to demonstrate consent from tribal people.

articles.title: 516 cases booked for footpath encroachments, traffic obstructions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Malkajgiri Traffic Police conducted a special enforcement drive targeting footpath encroachments and carriageway obstructions, resulting in 516 cases booked and ₹74,900 in fines imposed. The drive, coordinated with civic authorities, focused on unauthorized occupation of footpaths by vendors, illegal parking, and other obstructions that disrupt pedestrian movement and traffic flow.  Authorities emphasized the importance of restoring access for pedestrians and easing congestion to improve safety and traffic flow.

articles.title: Kadambrayar pollution: PCB yet to fix environmental compensation on violators - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala State Pollution Control Board (PCB) has not yet complied with a National Green Tribunal (NGT) order to assess environmental compensation for pollution of the Kadambrayar river in Ernakulam. The NGT's February 19, 2026 order directed the PCB to determine compensation payable by violators and ensure compliance with the LSGD's action report on the matter.

articles.title: Enhanced security cover given to Vijay withdrawn - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu police withdrew the security protocol given to C. Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, after he requested it. The security scale previously matched that of the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister was reduced to minimal levels following early election results indicating a significant victory for the TVK party.  The police had increased security at Mr. Vijay's residence and office in anticipation of large crowds, but these measures were subsequently withdrawn.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant shot dead - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandranath Rath, personal assistant to Suvendu Adhikari, the BJP leader, was shot and killed in Madhyamgram, West Bengal on Wednesday (May 6, 2026).  The incident occurred during post-poll violence in the state. Samik Bhattacharya, the West Bengal BJP president, and Adhikari urged party supporters to avoid violence. The Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar directed authorities to ensure zero tolerance towards post-poll violence and arrest those involved.  The Trinamool Congress condemned the deaths of Rath and other TMC workers killed in violence across the state.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: DMK rejects overtures from AIADMK, sources say - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AIADMK has reached out to the DMK seeking support to form a government in Tamil Nadu following the inconclusive election results. The DMK, however, rejected the proposal and stated its intention to remain in opposition, citing respect for the people's mandate.  DMK MP Kalanidhi Veeraswamy emphasized that the party will function as an effective opposition despite potential betrayals from other parties.

articles.title: Overseas scholarship forAdi Dravidar, tribal students - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department
articles.rephrased_article: The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department has announced the application period for scholarships under the Annal Ambedkar Overseas Higher Education Scholarship Scheme, open to students from the Adi Dravidar community, Adi Dravidar converts to Christianity, and tribal communities.  Applicants must have been admitted to a Master's or PhD program at a foreign university ranked within the top 1000 by QS World University Rankings and have an annual family income of no more than ₹12 lakh. The deadline for applications is June 5, 2026. Eligible candidates can apply online through the department's website between May 5 and June 5.

articles.title: Nearly 50 died on railway tracks Between Alappuzha and Thrissur this year - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nearly 50 people have died on railway tracks in central Kerala's three districts between January and April, according to railway enforcement agencies. The majority of the fatalities occurred between Kalamassery and Vallathol Nagar, where a lack of safety awareness and illegal pedestrian crossings are cited as contributing factors.  The Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Government Railway Police have stepped up safety measures including barricading entry points and conducting awareness drives to reduce these deaths.

articles.title: Online process to join arts and science colleges begins today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students seeking admission to first-year undergraduate degree programs in government arts and science colleges in the state for the 2026-27 academic year can register online starting May 7th. The application fee is ₹48, with a waiver for students from SC and ST communities.  The last day for registration is May 29th. Students can find more information on the website www.tngasa.in or contact the Directorate of Collegiate Education help center at 044-24343100 and 24342011 between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. weekdays.

articles.title: Kauvery Hospital, The Hindu to organise webinar on post-partum care - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kauvery Hospital and The Hindu are hosting a webinar on "Post-partum Care for Mothers" to commemorate Mother's Day. The session, moderated by journalist Soma Basu, will feature K. Thendral, Clinical Lead and Senior Consultant, Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Kauvery Hospital, Radial Road; P. Sathya Sudhakar, Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist at Kauvery Hospital Salem; and Manjeswari G., Psychologist and Sexual Health Therapist at Maa Kauvery, Trichy.  The webinar will be held on May 8th at 11:30 a.m. and registration is available through the link https://newsth.live/ THKMOE.

articles.title: Man charged in DC shooting was walking near JD Vance’s motorcade, agent says | Washington DC | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Marx, a 45-year-old man from Midland, Texas, was shot multiple times by officers after he fired at law enforcement near the Washington Monument.  Marx had allegedly made vulgar remarks about the White House and threatened to be killed while in possession of a firearm. Jeanine Pirro, US attorney, stated that her office will pursue the most serious charges against Marx for bringing gun violence to their streets. The incident occurred during JD Vance's motorcade, prompting a Secret Service investigation into Marx's presence near the White House complex with a concealed firearm.

articles.title: “Pretty easy to clear up”: Candace Owens questions Blake Neff over Erika Kirk TPUSA leadership video after Charlie Kirk death - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens and Blake Neff, producer for Turning Point USA, engaged in a public dispute on X after Neff criticized Owens' online content targeting Charlie Kirk and his widow, Erika Kirk.  Owens questioned why TPUSA had not released a video where Kirk allegedly named Erika as the future CEO and chairman. Neff countered by accusing Owens of ignoring evidence and engaging in conspiracy-driven attacks. The public disagreement is part of a larger split within conservative media circles following Kirk's death, with both sides continuing to trade accusations online.

articles.title: Rise in cybercrime but overall crime rate dropped in 2024, says latest NCRB report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reported a 6% decline in overall crime in India for 2024, but cybercrime cases surged by over 17%.  NCRB data revealed that fraud constituted the majority of cybercrime cases, followed by sexual exploitation and extortion. The report also highlighted a rise in crimes against the state, with The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act being the most frequently cited law. Suicide rates increased significantly in 2024, particularly among agricultural workers, unemployed individuals, daily wage laborers, and students.

articles.title: What’s behind the secessionist movement in the Canadian province Alberta? | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Alberta secessionists have submitted nearly 302,000 signatures to election authorities, exceeding the required number for a referendum on independence from Canada.  The move comes after years of frustration with federal power in Ottawa and concerns over environmental regulations impacting the province's oil industry. While a vote could take place as soon as October, legal challenges from Indigenous groups and questions about voter support remain. The potential secessionist movement has drawn criticism, including from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who suggested that Alberta would be a "natural partner" for the US.

articles.title: Chennai Outer Ring Road best positioned to address all problems of a home buyer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Casagrand, ANAROCK Property Consultants Private Limited, and Super Chennai representatives discussed the potential of the Outer Ring Road (ORR) for housing development in Chennai.  Gautam Agarwal, Casagrand's Chief Operating Officer, highlighted the ORR's ability to address home buyer concerns regarding land availability and flooding risks.  Sanjay Chugh, ANAROCK Property Consultants Private Limited's City Lead and Director, emphasized the need for social infrastructure development on the corridor beyond its existing road network. Karthik Nagappan, CEO of Super Chennai, discussed the ORR's potential to create a 30-minute city with improved work-life balance and better access to amenities.  Vidhya Mohankumar, Founder and Principal of Urban Design Collective, highlighted the advantages of ORR being a greenfield development, while also acknowledging the need for addressing infrastructure shortcomings that exist in other areas like OMR.

articles.title: Mexico City is slowly sinking: NASA radar reveals hidden land collapse driven by groundwater loss and a deepening water crisis | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico City has been experiencing alarming ground subsidence, with satellite images revealing a rate of up to 0.8 inches per month in certain areas. The phenomenon is linked to the city's reliance on groundwater for drinking water and its historical foundation on an old lake basin. This depletion weakens soil structure, causing cracks, tilts, and infrastructure strain. NASA radar technology has provided detailed insights into these changes, highlighting the need for sustainable urban development plans and new water management policies to address the issue. The city's water deficit, exacerbated by groundwater extraction, further complicates the situation, raising concerns about "Day Zero" – a potential scenario where water supply ceases.

articles.title: Outer Ring Road belt is emerging as a strategic hotspot for investment, say experts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: JLL, Casagrand, and other real estate experts gathered for a roundtable discussion on the future of urban expansion in Chennai, focusing on the Outer Ring Road (ORR).  Experts like Jerry Kingsley from JLL highlighted how ORR development has led to similar booms in cities like Hyderabad and Beijing. Diptakirti Chaudhuri, CMO of Casagrand, emphasized the need for a lifestyle shift towards suburban living with access to nature and quality infrastructure, citing their upcoming Thirumudivakkam project as an example.  Karthik Bhatt, historian and author, discussed the city's historical growth patterns, while Janakarajan, President of SaciWATERs, stressed the importance of understanding hydrology and engineering for successful urban development.

articles.title: Stunning ‘rainbow clouds’ spotted over Indonesia: Scientists explain the rare phenomenon | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Residents in Jonggol, Indonesia were surprised by vibrant "rainbow clouds" that appeared in videos circulating on social media. Scientists confirmed the phenomenon as cloud iridescence, a rare optical effect caused by sunlight interacting with tiny water droplets or ice crystals within thin clouds. This effect creates pastel shades and rainbow-like patterns, highlighting how Earth's atmosphere can produce visually stunning phenomena.  However, the vivid colors led some to believe the footage was AI-generated, reflecting growing skepticism about online visuals.

articles.title: The roller-coaster relationship between the DMK and Congress finally derails - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The DMK and Congress, after a two-decade alliance, have officially ended their partnership.  This decision comes after years of strained negotiations over seat-sharing during elections, culminating in the 2026 Assembly polls where the DMK secured victory. The relationship was marked by tensions and disagreements, particularly regarding portfolio distribution and the treatment of local Congress leaders. Despite a history of shared power and opposition to the BJP, the two parties ultimately decided to part ways.  This move is seen as potentially impacting Tamil Nadu's political landscape, with concerns about the emergence of TVK actor Vijay and its potential impact on the BJP's rise in the state.

articles.title: Stanford’s tiny chip could make your internet 100x faster while using less power | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Stanford University researchers have developed a fingertip-sized optical amplifier that uses a 'racetrack-shaped' resonator to boost light signals by 100 times while consuming minimal power. This innovation could significantly impact high-speed data communications, potentially enabling advanced photonics in portable devices like smartphones and remote sensors. The chip, built on lithium niobate, offers a more energy-efficient alternative to traditional amplifiers, which are large and consume significant power.  This advancement aligns with the Department of Energy's 'Green ICT' objectives by reducing heat generation during data transmission and enabling battery-powered applications for future 6G networks and sensors.

articles.title: Police announce arrest in Oklahoma lake party shooting that left 1 dead, 22 injured | Oklahoma | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Edmond police announced the arrest of 18-year-old Jaylan A Davis on Wednesday in connection with a mass shooting at Arcadia Lake that left one woman dead and 22 others wounded. The incident, which began as an argument between two women, escalated into gunfire involving multiple individuals, according to Edmond Police Chief JD Younger.  Davis was charged with assault with a deadly weapon and is being held on a $1 million bond. Police believe there may be additional suspects involved in the shooting.

articles.title: ​Back in the saddle: On the Congress win in the Kerala Assembly polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) won a landslide victory in the Kerala state assembly elections, ending 10 years of opposition. The UDF capitalized on anti-incumbency sentiment against the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) and secured 102 seats.  The BJP made gains, securing three seats while drawing a substantial share of votes in various regions. The LDF faced criticism for its governance, with some accusing it of nepotism and overbearing leadership.

articles.title: Foreign students on F-1 visas could face four-year stay cap under White House plan, J-1 also affected - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The White House is nearing a decision on a proposed rule that would limit the duration of stay for foreign students on F-1 visas. The plan, currently under review at the Office of Management and Budget, would replace the existing "duration of status" system with fixed limits, generally capping F-1 visa holders at four years in the US before requiring renewal. This proposal, identified as RIN: 1653-AA95, has faced opposition from universities and healthcare organizations who argue it could disrupt student progress and create administrative burdens. The rule was sent to OMB's Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs on Tuesday and is expected to be finalized within the next two months.

articles.title: Delhi to host 2026 Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi will host the 22nd Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship in July and August of 2026, with over 35 countries expected to participate. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced the event at the Delhi Secretariat, stating that the city has a strong history of hosting international sporting events. The seven-day championship will be held at the Thyagraj Stadium and feature competitions across multiple categories, culminating in finals on August 2nd.  The tournament is being organized jointly by the Delhi government and the Table Tennis Federation of India, with officials anticipating participation from countries like England, Australia, and Canada.

articles.title: Jasontheween: JasonTheWeen, Marlon, StableRonaldo under fire for running red light and stop sign on stream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: JasonTheWeen, Marlon, and StableRonaldo are facing backlash online after a clip from their recent IRL stream showed them riding motorized two-wheelers without following traffic rules. Viewers criticized the group for ignoring red lights, failing to stop at stop signs, and not wearing helmets. Some fans defended the group's actions, but others pointed out that traffic laws apply to all vehicles, including bikes, and safety is paramount in shared spaces. The incident has sparked a debate about the accountability of content creators and the importance of prioritizing safety during live streams.

articles.title: In rare push, US lawmakers demand transparency on Israel nuclear capability | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A group of US Democrats have called on the State Department to provide transparency regarding Israel's nuclear capabilities, citing the US-Israel war on Iran as a reason for increased clarity. The letter, signed by 30 members of Congress, requests information about Israel's nuclear weapons program, including its warheads and launchers, and whether it has articulated any "nuclear doctrine" or "thresholds for nuclear use." This request comes amidst growing concerns among lawmakers regarding the US relationship with Israel, particularly in light of the ongoing conflict with Iran. The letter highlights the public record supporting the conclusion that Israel possesses nuclear weapons and calls into question why Israel's development of such weapons is not subject to the same scrutiny as efforts to prevent Iran from acquiring them.

articles.title: Keir Starmer makes late pitch to voters turning to Greens and Reform | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labour is facing a potential record-breaking defeat in Thursday's local elections, which could significantly impact Keir Starmer's leadership.  The party faces losses of over 75% of its seats and may lose power in Wales to Plaid Cymru. The results are expected to be decisive for the party's future, with some MPs calling for a change of leadership.  However, Starmer is reportedly considering his next steps before the King's speech next week.

articles.title: Dutch frigate arrives in Kochi as part of efforts to strengthen maritime cooperation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Netherlands Navy ship HNLMS De Ruyter arrived in Kochi, India on May 4th as part of a five-month Indo-Pacific deployment. The visit coincided with a high-level Dutch delegation led by Deputy Commander of the Royal Netherlands Navy, Rob De Wit, and Marisa Gerards.  The delegation met with Rear Admiral Prakash Gopalan, Chief of Staff of the Southern Naval Command, to discuss maritime cooperation and training opportunities. During the visit, the delegation also laid wreaths at the SNC War Memorial and observed advanced simulators and modern training infrastructure at key training establishments.

articles.title: What pushed Australia to reportedly cancel Sneako’s visa? streamer responds with bold clarification - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nico Sneako De Balinthazy, known online as Sneako, denied reports that he was deported from Australia after his visa was cancelled by Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke.  The cancellation stemmed from comments and content authorities deemed hateful. While some questioned how Sneako entered the country in the first place, Sneako clarified that his trip had ended naturally and he did not face deportation. Australian officials have not released additional information about a potential lifetime ban.

articles.title: RBI issues revised norms for entities dealing in forex - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced new regulations, the Foreign Exchange Management (Authorised Persons) Regulations, 2026. The regulations aim to streamline the authorization and renewal process for authorized persons while maintaining checks and balances in foreign exchange transactions. Entities seeking authorization must meet specific criteria, including being incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, and having a minimum net worth requirement.  The new rules also categorize different entities based on their activities and forex turnover.

articles.title: Ted Turner and the legacy of WCW: How he revolutionized wrestling, created nWo, and challenged Vince McMahon | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ted Turner, the media executive who revolutionized professional wrestling by turning WCW into a national rival to Vince McMahon's WWF, died at age 87.  Turner acquired Jim Crockett Promotions in 1988 and transformed it into WCW, challenging WWF for dominance in the television ratings during the Monday Night Wars. The competition led to the launch of WCW Monday Nitro in 1995, a direct competitor to WWF Monday Night Raw. Turner's influence extended beyond wrestling, as he built one of television's most influential modern empires with CNN, TNT, TBS, and Cartoon Network.  Eric Bischoff, former WCW executive, credits Turner for shaping his life and career.

articles.title: ​Cost of success: On the BJP’s victory in Assam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, the BJP's leader in Assam, is expected to be sworn in as Chief Minister after leading the party to victory.  Sarma, who previously served as a Congress leader, has been instrumental in reshaping the state's political landscape through organizational prowess and communal rhetoric. The BJP's landslide win has significantly altered power dynamics within the party nationally, with Sarma being perceived as close to Amit Shah, the Union Home Minister. However, the party's victory has also sparked concerns about its impact on Assam's social fabric, particularly its divisive policies towards Bengali-speaking Muslim communities.

articles.title: Influencer Clavicular faces charges in Florida tied to alligator shooting video | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a controversial social media influencer known for "looksmaxxing", is facing charges of unlawfully discharging a firearm in a public place or residential property after a live stream showing him shooting an alligator in the Everglades. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is investigating the incident, which also resulted in charges against Andrew Morales and Yabdiel Anibal Cotto Torres. Clavicular's attorney claims he followed the instructions of a licensed airboat guide and that no animals or people were harmed.

articles.title: Paytm Q4 Results: Co turns to black, logs profit of Rs 184 crore vs loss a year ago - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Paytm reported a 18% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2,264 crore for the quarter. The company's EBITDA turned positive at Rs 132 crore, up from a loss of Rs 88 crore last year. Paytm attributed this growth to its payments business, which saw a 21% rise in revenue, and financial services distribution, which grew by 38%.  The company also reported an increase in monthly transacting users and contribution profit for the quarter.

articles.title: 'Comparing H-1B workers to entire workforce': Row over US entrepreneur’s claim visa holders are less than 0.5% of jobs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Blunt, a US entrepreneur, sparked debate online by claiming that H-1B visa holders comprise less than 0.5% of the American workforce.  His chart comparing the number of H-1B workers to the total US workforce was met with criticism for its misleading presentation and lack of source information. Hany Girgis, an edtech entrepreneur and co-founder of SkillStorm, challenged Blunt's interpretation, arguing that H-1B workers are concentrated in high-skill sectors like tech and IT, impacting job distribution rather than overall workforce share.  The debate highlights the ongoing controversy surrounding H-1B visas and their impact on American jobs.

articles.title: Nitish Kumar’s son Nishant Kumar may join Bihar cabinet on May 7 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitish Kumar's son, Nishant Kumar, is a subject of speculation regarding his potential inclusion in the new Samrat Choudhary-led NDA government cabinet.  Senior JD(U) leaders met with Nitish Kumar and held meetings in Patna ahead of the Cabinet expansion scheduled for Thursday. The event will be attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Narendra Modi, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and other senior NDA leaders, but no official confirmation has been made regarding Nishant Kumar's inclusion.  The administration is preparing for the ceremony at Gandhi Maidan with security personnel, police dogs, and waterproof tents to ensure a smooth event despite weather warnings of hailstorms and rain.

articles.title: Howard Lutnick answers questions from US House over Jeffrey Epstein ties | Jeffrey Epstein | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Howard Lutnick, the US commerce secretary, appeared before the House oversight and reform committee on Wednesday to answer questions about his past ties to Jeffrey Epstein.  The committee released millions of documents related to Epstein, including those showing that Lutnick continued correspondence with Epstein after the financier's conviction for soliciting prostitution from a minor.  Democrats criticized Lutnick's performance, calling it evasive and dishonest. Republicans defended Lutnick, stating he answered substantive questions and was transparent. The hearing follows previous revelations about Lutnick's contact with Epstein, including visits to his private island in 2012.  While Lutnick maintains he had limited interactions with Epstein after 2005, the committee is seeking further clarification on his relationship with the disgraced financier.

articles.title: Follow the money: How far-right Reform UK built a global network | The Far Right News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, is experiencing a surge in popularity, but its financial ties to individuals and organizations beyond the United Kingdom raise concerns. The party relies heavily on donations from wealthy individuals, including Christopher Harborne, a British-Thai billionaire, who has become the largest single donor in UK political history.  Farage has also accepted significant gifts from Harborne, such as a 5 million-pound donation that was not initially declared, prompting investigations into potential breaches of electoral law. The party's international travel arrangements, including trips to Abu Dhabi and the Maldives, have also been funded by individuals with connections to controversial organizations. Experts argue that these donations, coupled with weak lobbying rules and limited transparency, undermine British democracy and allow a small number of wealthy donors to exert undue influence on political processes.

articles.title: Bajaj Auto announces Rs 5,633 crore share buyback via tender route, sets price at Rs 12,000 apiece - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bajaj Auto announced a dividend of Rs 150 per share and a share buyback program, totaling up to Rs 9,825 crore. The company reported a strong Q4 FY26 with a standalone net profit of Rs 2,746 crore, a 34% year-on-year increase, driven by a 24% rise in volumes and a 25% jump in exports.  Bajaj Auto's revenue from operations also rose 32% to Rs 16,006 crore during the quarter. The company attributed its growth to a strong domestic market performance and robust export sales.

articles.title: Clavicular Shooting Incident: Clavicular charged in shocking Everglades shooting stream, faces up to 1 year in jail - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a popular streamer whose real name is Braden Eric Peters, faces criminal charges after his viral livestream showed him and others firing at an alligator in the Florida Everglades. The Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office filed a charge of unlawfully firing a gun in a public place against Peters, who was joined by other streamers including Cuban Tarzan.  The incident occurred at the Francis Taylor Everglades Wildlife Management Area, and is considered a first-degree misdemeanor under Florida law, potentially leading to up to one year in jail. A court hearing is scheduled for May 20th. The case highlights the potential consequences of live streaming actions.

articles.title: CBI files charge sheet in builder-bank nexus case - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Bank of India, ICICI Bank, UCO Bank
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a charge sheet against several individuals and companies, including AVJ Developers, Kesar Builders, and their directors, along with officials from Bank of India, ICICI Bank, and UCO Bank, for alleged involvement in a builder-bank nexus case. The agency alleges that the accused conspired to induce homebuyers and investors through false assurances and fraudulent representations, abused their official positions to facilitate illegal acts, and caused financial institutions and homebuyers wrongful loss.  The CBI is currently investigating 50 such cases.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq notch records; AMD results spark AI stock rally - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Advanced Micro Devices shares soared to an all-time high after forecasting quarterly revenue above expectations, while Intel and the PHLX chip index also saw gains. Global stocks surged and oil prices fell as Iran reviewed a new U.S. proposal for ending the war, with sources suggesting a one-page memorandum was being finalized. The S&P 500 gained 1.45% to close at 7,364.72 points, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 2.01% to 25,834.88.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average increased by 1.22% to 49,909.55.

articles.title: Who is Jane Fonda? CNN founder Ted Turner’s ex-wife who once called him her 'favorite ex-husband' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ted Turner, the founder of CNN, died at 87 after a battle with Lewy body dementia.  He was remembered by Jane Fonda as a "favorite ex-husband" and a supportive partner in their shared work for charitable causes like the Georgia Campaign for Adolescent Power and Potential. Turner built a media empire that revolutionized global news, including CNN's 24-hour coverage. He also left a legacy of philanthropy and conservation through organizations he founded.

articles.title: Rubio to visit India for bilateral talks; Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting May-end - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to visit India from May 24 to 26, his first since taking office last January.  He will meet with Indian officials including External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, as well as Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The visit aims to strengthen ties between the two countries following recent ups and downs related to tariffs and sanctions. Rubio will also attend the Australia-India-Japan-U.S. Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (FMM) on May 26 with counterparts from Australia, Japan, and India.  The meeting is expected to discuss a potential date for the Quad Summit later this year. The visit follows a visit to Beijing by U.S. President Donald Trump tentatively scheduled for May 14-15.

articles.title: West Bengal CM refuses to resign after poll defeat - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, the chief minister of West Bengal, refused to resign after her party lost power in state elections to the BJP.  The BJP secured over two-thirds of the seats, marking a significant political milestone for the party. Banerjee claimed that 100 seats were "forcibly taken" from her party and accused the Election Commission of bias. The Chief Electoral Officer, Manoj Kumar Agarwal, dismissed these allegations as baseless.  The state's governor can demand Banerjee's resignation or wait until her term ends, at which point a new government will be formed.

articles.title: District Legal Services Authority urges litigants to utilise Special Lok Adalat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The District Legal Services Authority has urged litigants and advocates to participate in the Special Lok Adalat, scheduled for August 21-23, 2026, as part of the "Samadhan Samaroh" initiative.  This event aims to resolve pending cases through mediation and mutual settlement. Litigants are requested to submit details by May 31st via a Google Form available on the Supreme Court website.

articles.title: US shuts Peshawar consulate despite soft talk on Pakistan - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department announced the closure of its Peshawar consulate, citing safety concerns and logistical needs. This decision marks the first permanent closure of an overseas US diplomatic mission under President Trump's second term. The move comes amid a broader downsizing of the US diplomatic corps, with over 200 career diplomats laid off, including those specializing in human rights and democracy promotion.  The administration has shifted towards relying on political loyalists for key negotiations, particularly those involving Iran's nuclear program, raising concerns about strategic coherence.

articles.title: Nigel Farage’s income since being elected MP has hit £2m, analysis shows | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage's income since becoming an MP has reached £2 million, according to analysis of the register of MPs. This figure comes amid scrutiny of his wealth after a £5 million gift from party donor Christopher Harborne was revealed and he did not declare it on time.  The Electoral Commission is investigating a complaint from the Conservative party about the money. Farage maintains that the gift was personal and not political, using it to pay for security arrangements. The news has sparked concerns about potential conflicts of interest and calls for greater transparency in MP finances.

articles.title: T.N. Governor asks TVK chief Vijay to produce proof of support of majority MLAs; Congress says ‘yes’ but AIADMK ‘no’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, the Tamil Nadu Governor, requested C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), to provide evidence of support from 118 MLAs to form a government. The TVK won 108 seats in the recent election and needs additional support from seven legislators to reach the majority mark.  The Congress, which previously had an alliance with the DMK, has extended its support to the TVK, hoping for two Cabinet positions. Edappadi K Palaniswami, a senior leader of the AIADMK, refuted reports that his party would support the TVK. The DMK's allies, including the CPI and CPI(M), are yet to decide on their stance.

articles.title: 'Don't let him die': Teacher accused of murdering baby begged medics to save son, UK court hears - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jamie Varley, a 37-year-old teacher, is facing charges of murder, sexual assault, and child cruelty in connection with the death of his 13-month-old adopted son, Preston. Preston Davey was found unconscious at Blackpool Victoria Hospital on Tuesday after suffering severe mistreatment during his time with Varley and his companion, John McGowan-Fazakerley. Medical professionals testified that Preston showed no signs of water inhalation in his lungs, contradicting Varley's account of leaving the child alone in a bath. The prosecution alleges that Varley abused the child physically and sexually, while McGowan-Fazakerley also faces charges related to child cruelty and sexual assault.  The case has garnered significant public attention due to its serious nature and the potential implications for adoptive care arrangements.

articles.title: Indiana, Ohio primaries draw midterm battle lines, reinforce Trump’s pull | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Trump’s continued influence over the Republican Party was evident in Indiana and Ohio's primaries, where he backed candidates who won. In Ohio, Jon Husted will face off against former Senator Sherrod Brown, while in Indiana, Vivek Ramaswamy secured the GOP gubernatorial nomination.  These results solidify key battle lines for the November midterm elections, with Democrats facing an uphill climb to regain control of the Senate.

articles.title: Cameo, speeches, pushing gold bullion: how Farage has made millions since becoming an MP | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, has amassed a significant personal fortune since entering parliament. He has generated income through various avenues including speeches, writing articles, and promoting gold bullion.  He also received a multimillion-pound donation from Christopher Harborne, which he claims was for his security. This wealth allows him to travel extensively, engage in high-profile events, and maintain a luxurious lifestyle. Farage's financial disclosures have been scrutinized due to the £5 million gift from Harborne and prior breaches of the MPs’ code of conduct regarding unreported income.

articles.title: TVK’s victory in Tamil Nadu polls: The rise of an apolitical polity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. K. Stalin, the outgoing Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, suffered a surprising defeat in the Kolathur constituency despite campaigning across the state for his party's victory.  This loss marks the fourth time a sitting Chief Minister has been defeated in Tamil Nadu history and makes Stalin the latest to experience this setback. The constituency, which he had nurtured with significant development projects, became a symbol of his political legacy.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Pythagoras: “The oldest, shortest words— ‘yes’ and ‘no’— are those which require the most thought.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pythagoras, a philosopher and mathematician, famously stated that "the oldest, shortest words— ‘yes’ and ‘no’— are those which require the most thought."  His quote emphasizes the importance of careful consideration when making choices, as even seemingly simple words like "yes" or "no" can have significant consequences. He believed that saying "yes" requires responsibility for commitments made and that saying "no" is a necessary tool for setting boundaries and protecting oneself. This timeless wisdom reminds us to pause before responding and consider the implications of our decisions, regardless of their size.

articles.title: PTI's Raja says there will be no discussion on party's Punjab coordination and monitoring committee - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Akram Raja, secretary general of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), stated that the formation of a Punjab Coordination and Monitoring Committee would not be discussed at the upcoming party meeting.  However, some party leaders believe the committee is an attempt to "occupy" the party in Punjab and oppose its composition, particularly the nomination of Amjad Khan Niazi as convenor. The committee's terms of reference include coordinating organizational matters between Punjab's four regions through engagement with their presidents and general secretaries.

articles.title: Diageo springs a surprise, sales climb on Africa, Latin America - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Diageo, the maker of Johnnie Walker whisky and Guinness stout, reported organic net sales growth of 0.3% for the period, exceeding analyst expectations of a 2.3% decline. Despite this positive result, Diageo maintained its guidance for this fiscal year, anticipating organic net sales to decrease between 2% and 3%. The company is facing challenges from weak demand for beer and spirits in key markets, as well as consumer concerns about health and rising living costs.

articles.title: In topsy-turvy Haryana politics, Sonipat latest amphitheatre for BJP-Cong. fight - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Jain, the BJP nominee for the Sonipat Municipal Corporation mayoral election, visited a religious gathering at Nirankari Bhawan before beginning his campaign.  He is facing off against Congress's Kamal Dewan, who claims he has the support of sanitation workers and fire brigade employees.  Deepender Hooda, the Congress MP from Rohtak, has been canvassing in the area while Manoj Tiwari is campaigning among Purvanchali voters. The election will be decided by the votes of Punjabis, according to realtor Praveen Arora.

articles.title: JPMorgan offered $1 million, Chirayu Rana demanded $20 million in sexual harassment lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: JPMorgan Chase is facing a legal battle with former banker Chirayu Rana, who has accused senior executive Lorna Hajdini of sexual abuse.  Rana allegedly demanded $20 million from the bank before filing his lawsuit, which alleges drugging, forced sexual encounters, and racist abuse. The bank offered him $1 million to settle but he counter-offered $11.75 million. While JPMorgan maintains there is no evidence of wrongdoing, Rana's lawyer claims the allegations will be supported by evidence as the case progresses.

articles.title: What does the BJP’s victory in West Bengal mean for India’s democracy? | Elections | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won the West Bengal state assembly elections, marking a significant shift in Indian politics.  Critics argue that controversial electoral roll changes played a role in the BJP's landslide victory, raising concerns about the future of democracy and its impact on India's Muslim population. The outcome could reshape national politics for 200 million Muslims.

articles.title: UK voters need to hear battle over bills and climate crisis are linked, green experts say | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Greenpeace UK, Friends of the Earth, and VoteClimate warn that voters should consider the links between inflation and fossil fuels when making their choices in local elections.  The organizations emphasize that boosting renewable energy generation offers a better solution to address soaring energy costs, while also improving affordability, security, and environmental quality. They highlight concerns about water and air pollution, housing affordability, and access to green spaces as key issues for voters. Nigel Farage, leader of the Reform party, has pledged support for fracking and opposes renewable energy sources, while the Conservatives have embraced more drilling in the North Sea but downplayed the climate crisis.

articles.title: Vellore Corporation begins removal of dumped wastes along Palar river - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vellore Corporation has begun a project to remove accumulated wastes from the Palar river, off the Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48). The project aims to restore free flow of rainwater during monsoon and prevent flooding in residential areas. R. Lakshman, Commissioner of Vellore Corporation, inspected the first biomining operation on Wednesday.  The project will cost ₹11.50 crore and is expected to be completed by mid-2027.

articles.title: Dual-national baby stranded abroad after new UK passport rule blocks return from Spain - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A family from Aberdeenshire was denied boarding on a Ryanair flight back to Scotland after their 10-month-old daughter, Lily, who holds both British and Austrian nationality, was deemed ineligible to travel under new UK border rules for dual nationals. The family was informed that they lacked the necessary documentation, despite believing Lily could travel using her Austrian passport.  The Home Office has stated that airlines cannot verify citizenship without proper documents, leading to boarding denials. The situation caused significant distress and resulted in the family being stranded abroad while they apply for a British passport for Lily.

articles.title: ‘Defeated by conspiracy’: West Bengal chief minister refuses to resign after election loss | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, India's most powerful female politician, has refused to resign as chief minister of West Bengal despite the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) winning a landslide victory in state elections.  Banerjee claims the election was "looted" by conspiracy and that she will not step down. The governor of West Bengal has threatened to send police if Banerjee does not voluntarily relinquish her position, potentially leading to legal challenges. The BJP has responded with accusations of "constitutional blasphemy" and a ban on advisors appointed by Banerjee from entering their offices.  Banerjee's refusal to step down could lead to further political turmoil in the state.

articles.title: Three IT employees held with MDMA in Hayathnagar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three IT employees, Anjad, Hemant, and Harish, were arrested in Hayathnagar for possession and alleged sale of MDMA. The Excise State Task Force seized 7.44 grams of the drug during an operation that was led by CI Biksha Reddy and SSI Balaraju.  The accused allegedly procured MDMA from Bengaluru and sold it in Hyderabad at varying prices, with Hemant financing the operation. Further investigation is underway to identify other individuals involved in the supply network.

articles.title: ‘Brown Indian-American who is more America First’: MAGA reacts to Vivek Ramaswamy Ohio primary win - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vivek Ramaswamy, an Indian-American entrepreneur and close ally of Donald Trump, won the Ohio Republican primary, securing his nomination for governor.  His victory was celebrated by supporters within the MAGA movement, including Trump, who praised him as "SPECIAL," while online commentators sparked debate about his background and political stances. Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee, will face Ramaswamy in November's general election.

articles.title: Malkajgiri CP goes undercover at midnight to assess women’s safety - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B. Sumathi conducted an undercover operation to assess women's safety in Dilsukhnagar, posing as a civilian and observing real-time conditions. During the exercise, she encountered a group of young men who engaged in inappropriate conversations with her, prompting police intervention. Instead of immediate arrests, officers counselled the youths about legal consequences and emphasized respect for women in public spaces. The operation was intended to assess safety concerns beyond harassment, including substance abuse and vulnerability among minors.

articles.title: 'Crocodile Bridge' on Mars: NASA’s Perseverance rover captures a mysterious ancient region on the Red Planet | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA’s Perseverance rover has captured a 360-degree panorama of the “Crocodile Bridge” region on Mars, revealing one of the oldest known landscapes on the planet. The panoramic image, created using the Mastcam-Z camera system, combines 980 images taken across multiple Martian days and was processed to resemble how the human eye would see the Martian surface. Scientists are interested in this area because the rocks around Jezero Crater’s rim are believed to be among the oldest preserved anywhere in the solar system. The rover is expected to explore the region for several months, as part of its mission to search for signs that microbial life may have once existed in these ancient habitats.

articles.title: JUI-F holds protest rallies across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over killing of Maulana Idrees - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) held protest rallies across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday against the killing of prominent cleric Maulana Muhammad Idrees.  The party demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible and accused the government of implementing an international agenda by targeting religious scholars. Maulana Fazlur Rehman, JUI-F chief, called for nationwide protests, while Abdul Jalil Jan, JUI-F provincial spokesperson, led rallies in various districts. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi expressed grief over Idrees's death.

articles.title: Infant kidnapped in Suraram rescued within 48 hours; five arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sridevi, 35, and four others, including two juveniles, were arrested in connection with the abduction of a six-month-old infant from Suraram.  The accused, all natives of Karnataka residing in Hyderabad, planned the kidnapping to procure a baby for Sridevi's sister-in-law who was struggling with infertility. The crime was premeditated and the infant was rescued after police tracked them down to a function hall in Rajendranagar.

articles.title: The ‘ghost lake’ returns: California’s largest lost water body resurfaces after 130 years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulare Lake, once a vast freshwater lake, has unexpectedly resurfaced in 2023 due to record snowfall and extreme weather events. The California Department of Water Resources reports that the basin's natural topography allowed water from the Sierra Nevada to flow back into the lake, exceeding the capacity of man-made canals and dams.  The return of Tulare Lake has sparked ecological revival, attracting migratory birds and renewing indigenous cultural areas.

articles.title: Paigham-i-Islam Conference awards title of ‘Greatest Victorious General of the Century’ to CDF Asim Munir - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sixth International Paigham-i-Islam Conference awarded Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir with the titles of “Leader of Peace” and “Greatest Victorious General of the Century.” The conference, organized by the International Tazeem-i-Haramain Sharifain Council and Pakistan Ulema Council, condemned attacks on Iran by the United States and Israel, calling for national security, unity of the Muslim world, and enhanced interfaith harmony.  The conference also recognized Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif with a shield of appreciation for his stance on international issues, particularly Palestine, while Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was honored for contributions to defense cooperation and peace in the region.

articles.title: Ex-Scottish council leader Jordan Linden jailed for 18 months over sex crimes against boys, young men - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jordan Linden, a former Scottish National Party (SNP) council leader, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for multiple sexual offenses against boys and young men.  Linden was convicted of ten offences including sexual assault, stalking, and inappropriate sexual communication after a trial earlier this year. The court rejected a plea for leniency from Linden's defense lawyer, citing his difficult teenage years and autism diagnosis. David Moggach KC, Linden's lawyer, argued that the offenses were not as serious as they appeared.  The case has sparked political controversy with questions raised over how prior complaints were handled within the party and youth organizations.

articles.title: North Kerala districts could get fair representation in UDF Cabinet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: UDF is expected to form a Cabinet in the coming week, with high chances of representation for six districts in north Kerala.  The Congress, IUML, and two Independents secured 21 candidates each from Kasaragod, Wayanad, Kannur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, and Palakkad districts. Several prominent figures within the Congress and other parties are potential nominees for ministerial positions, including Sunny Joseph, K.K. Shailaja, and A.P. Anil Kumar.

articles.title: Indian national accused of laundering $7 million from illegal tobacco trade, submitting fraudulent residency papers in Australia - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian national, 33 years old, is facing multiple charges in Brisbane, Australia for allegedly laundering over $7 million linked to an illegal tobacco network and providing false information to immigration authorities. The Australian Federal Police (AFP) conducted a search warrant operation on April 27th at a Kuraby property with support from the Australian Border Force (ABF) and Queensland Police Service (QPS), seizing cash, mobile phones, business records, and vaping products.  The man is scheduled to appear in court on June 26th, 2026.

articles.title: CJI was only meant to have a say in CEC/EC appointments till Parliament brought a law: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that the Chief Justice of India's involvement in the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) was temporary, pending a law from Parliament. The court addressed petitions challenging the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister in the committee responsible for CEC appointments.  The petitioners argued that the Act effectively reversed the independence of the Election Commission by giving the Executive exclusive control over appointments. Arguments continued on Thursday.

articles.title: India says Pakistani players can visit for multilateral events but bilateral competitions ​remain off table - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India’s sports ministry announced that Pakistani players and teams will be allowed to participate in multilateral events hosted by India but bilateral events remain off-limits. The ministry also stated that the visa process for sportspersons and officials will be simplified, while office bearers of international sports governing bodies will be granted multi-entry visas.  India’s decision comes as they are set to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and bid for the 2036 Olympics and the 2038 Asian Games. The ministry's statement reflects India's growing role as a credible venue for international sports events, while acknowledging the strained relationship between the two countries.

articles.title: German police raid neo-Nazi criminal youth groups
articles.rephrased_article: German police conducted raids targeting individuals suspected of involvement in far-right criminal youth groups, "Jung & Stark" (JS) and "Deutsche Jugend Voran" (DJV). The raids, which took place across 12 states, focused on individuals suspected of organizing violence through social media and forming nationwide networks. Prosecutors stated that the suspects are believed to have attacked left-wing figures and alleged paedophiles.  The groups operate openly online and have been linked to a rise in violent attacks against political opponents and LGBT communities.

articles.title: Timothée Chalamet shocks football fans with surprise Adidas World Cup teaser featuring Messi, Zidane, Beckham, Yamal and Bad Bunny | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Timothée Chalamet unexpectedly unveiled a teaser for Adidas’ upcoming 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign on Instagram, featuring a star-studded lineup of footballers, musicians, and Hollywood figures. The teaser showcases appearances from Lionel Messi, Zinedine Zidane, David Beckham, Bad Bunny, and other prominent names across generations of the sport.  The campaign aims to expand football's reach into mainstream pop culture, with Adidas leveraging the involvement of celebrities like Chalamet to promote the tournament.

articles.title: Srisailam EO reviews amenities, aims for 90% devotee satisfaction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Srinivasa Rao, Executive Officer of the Srisailam temple, held a meeting with temple staff and officials to improve devotee satisfaction with temple facilities. He emphasized a 90% positive response in areas like darshan arrangements, drinking water, annaprasadam, sanitation, and restroom maintenance. SITA training programs for cooks were conducted, ensuring adherence to standard operating procedures and the use of fresh ingredients.

articles.title: Who is Zack Polanski, UK Greens leader and rising political star? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zack Polanski, the leader of the United Kingdom’s Green Party, is a rising political star banking on significant gains in this week's local elections.  His party, which has expanded beyond its environmental focus to include socialist policies like wealth taxes and stronger worker rights, is expected to perform well in London and other major cities.  Polanski, who has been praised for his communication skills and progressive stances, faces accusations of antisemitism following a controversy involving a social media post criticizing police officers' actions during an incident in Golders Green. Despite these controversies, polls suggest the Green Party could consolidate its position as an alternative to Keir Starmer’s Labour party.

articles.title: Coalition considers plan to slash net overseas immigration by nearly half its current rate, leaked documents reveal | Coalition | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Angus Taylor is preparing a hardline immigration strategy for the Coalition, aiming to cut Australia's annual net overseas migration levels to 150,000-200,000. This plan, outlined in a confidential policy roadmap, aims to minimize budget and economic impacts while strengthening social cohesion. The document indicates Taylor wants to be prepared for an early election and avoid the chaos that plagued Peter Dutton's campaign.  The Coalition is also focusing on other key areas like productivity, housing affordability, government services, and families.

articles.title: AMD shares jump 13% as AI chip demand lifts strong results - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AMD's second-quarter revenue projection of $11.2 billion exceeded Wall Street estimates, driven by strong demand for AI chips and a growing data center business. The company guided for adjusted gross margins of 56%, surpassing analyst expectations. AMD is benefiting from the expansion of cloud computing giants' spending on AI infrastructure and its position as a key supplier to companies like Meta Platforms and OpenAI.  Despite competition from Intel, which is ramping up in-house manufacturing, AMD has seen significant stock gains this year.

articles.title: This children’s village stays cool without air conditioning in one of the world’s hottest regions — here’s how | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Urko Sanchez Architects, for SOS Children’s Villages International, designed the SOS Children’s Village Tadjourah in Djibouti, a coastal city with extreme heat and arid conditions. The village utilizes traditional climate-responsive design principles from North Africa and the Middle East to create a naturally cool environment.  The architects incorporated wind-catching towers, reflective surfaces, vegetation, and carefully planned airflow to regulate temperatures without relying on mechanical cooling systems. This approach reduces energy consumption and promotes social interaction within the village.

articles.title: PM to visit Bengaluru on May 10 to address 45th anniversary of Art of Living; BJP to offer reception at HAL Airport - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bengaluru on May 10 to attend the 45th anniversary celebrations of The Art of Living and the 70th birthday of its founder, Sri Sri Ravi Shankar. The BJP State unit is preparing a reception for the Prime Minister upon his arrival at HAL Airport.  He will deliver a speech at a public event followed by an address at the Art of Living International Centre campus where he will inaugurate new facilities and participate in various programs including a meditation session for World Peace led by Sri Sri Ravi Shankar.

articles.title: Four killed in post-election violence in India’s West Bengal | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following the Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sweeping victory in West Bengal's state election, at least four people have been killed in political unrest. The BJP claimed two of its workers were killed while the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) party reported two of their workers being beaten to death.  The violence erupted after the results were announced and included clashes between rival supporters in Kolkata and other districts, with allegations of vandalism and attacks on party offices from both sides. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed state officials to enforce “zero tolerance” towards post-poll violence.

articles.title: With 300 elephants outside forests, Karnataka fast-tracks rehab plan - The Hindu
