Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), has emerged as a frontrunner in the 2026 Tamil Nadu State Assembly elections, capitalizing on voter dissatisfaction with established parties like the DMK and AIADMK.  His independent campaign strategy, appealing to voters through spectacle and simple messaging, has resonated strongly. The upcoming election will focus on traditional political themes such as social justice versus authoritarianism, corruption versus promises of good governance.

articles.title: Hormuz tensions push ceasefire to the brink as Trump threatens Iran | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump renewed threats against Iran, stating that the country would be "blown off the face of the Earth" if it attacked US ships. The US military implemented a plan to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz, but ship-tracking websites show limited traffic.  Iran claimed responsibility for attacks on UAE vessels and facilities, while South Korea reported an explosion and fire on one of its ships in the region. Tensions remain high as both sides accuse each other of escalating hostilities.

articles.title: ‘A test of our values’: Starmer to call for whole-society response to rising antisemitism | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer will call for a whole-of-society response to rising antisemitism at Downing Street on Tuesday, emphasizing the need for action beyond mere condemnation.  He will convene representatives from various sectors including business, charities, and law enforcement to discuss ways to combat this issue. Sarah Sackman, Labour MP for Finchley and Golders Green, has criticized a lack of vocal solidarity from some anti-racist organizations and called for increased support for Jewish communities. The government is allocating additional funding for enhanced security measures at synagogues, schools, and community centers in response to recent incidents of violence against Jewish people.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana took leave for dad's death in 2024 but his father is alive; says he doesn't know anything about JP Morgan row - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, who filed a civil lawsuit against JPMorgan executive Lorna Hajdini, claims his father died in November 2024, prompting him to take leave from work.  However, sources close to the case say that Chaitanya Rana, Chirayu's father, is alive and well. The report also states that Rana used a string of leave allowances between March and May 2024 while claiming his father was seriously ill. JPMorgan denies Rana's claims and says he never reported to Hajdini.

articles.title: With defeat in Kerala, Left out of power for first time since 1977 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] lost the Kerala Assembly election, marking the first time since 1977 that they are not in power in any state.  Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, accused the CPI(M) of collaborating with the BJP, a claim the party's general secretary M.A. Baby dismissed as a "deliberate" and "distorted" attempt to damage its reputation.

articles.title: Gun scare near White House: Person shot by law enforcement at Washington Monument; lockdown briefly imposed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Secret Service confirmed an officer-involved shooting near the Washington Monument on Monday, prompting a brief security lockdown at the White House. Emergency responders transported an adult male to a hospital and a teenage male was treated for minor injuries. The incident occurred not far from President Donald Trump's small business event, where security protocols were briefly activated but did not disrupt his speech.

articles.title: With defeat in Kerala, Left out of power for first time since 1977 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has lost its power in Kerala for the first time since 1977, marking a significant setback for the party.  Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, accused the CPI(M) of colluding with the BJP during the campaign. M.A. Baby, the CPI(M)'s general secretary, refuted these accusations, stating they were intended to damage the party's image and that the CPI(M) supports all sections of society regardless of religion or caste.

articles.title: 'Force v Geography' Trump's Project Freedom meets Iran's residual firepower - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran are escalating tensions in the Gulf after Iran attacked UAE with drones and missiles in response to US efforts to escort commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.  Despite Trump's claims that the operation, dubbed "Project Freedom," was a humanitarian intervention aimed at freeing ships trapped in the strait, most vessels opted for an Iranian-controlled traffic separation scheme instead of a US-proposed corridor. The attacks highlight the limitations of US military power in the region and the effectiveness of Iran’s asymmetric tactics.  The conflict has disrupted global energy markets and caused gas prices to surge in the US.

articles.title: 150-million-year-old soft tissue fossil discovery strengthens Darwin’s theory of evolution | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 150-million-year-old fossil containing soft tissue has been discovered, providing new evidence for Darwin's theory of evolution. This discovery challenges the long-held belief that the fossil record is incomplete and supports the idea that gradual evolutionary changes can be observed through fossilized remains.  The findings are significant because they allow scientists to study microscopic tissues and potentially molecular remnants, offering a deeper understanding of extinct organisms' appearance, behavior, and physiology.   This evidence strengthens the theoretical basis of evolutionary science and highlights the potential for future discoveries to further validate Darwin's theory.

articles.title: AI platforms reference Nigel Farage more than other leaders when prompted on UK politics, study shows | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Peec AI, an analytics firm, found that Nigel Farage was referenced more frequently than any other UK leader in responses from leading AI models like ChatGPT and Google's AI Overview when prompted about British politics. The research analyzed over 280,000 data points across various prompts related to British politics, including immigration, healthcare, and crime. While Reform UK appeared prominently in these responses, particularly on issues related to immigration and council tax, the visibility of other parties like Labour and the Liberal Democrats varied depending on the specific topic. The study highlights the growing influence of AI platforms in political messaging and their potential susceptibility to manipulation by misinformation sources.

articles.title: 'Buy Spirit Airlines' website crashes as everyone wants in: 'Movement overwhelmed our servers' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Spirit Airlines, facing financial difficulties due to rising fuel prices, announced its closure.  A website created by TikToker Hunter Peterson to crowdfund the airline's revival crashed due to overwhelming support from people wanting to save it. The site, letsbuyspiritair.com, allowed users to pledge an interest in owning Spirit Airlines, with over 124,000 patrons pledging a total of $88 million by May 4th.  Peterson is seeking developers, public relations professionals, lawyers and airline executives to help realize the plan.

articles.title: US releases Touska container ship crew: Why it matters | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States released 22 crew members from the Iranian container ship, the Touska, to Pakistan in a move described as a "confidence-building measure" by Pakistan's foreign ministry. The release comes amid escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz following the US seizure of the vessel and its subsequent transfer to Pakistan.  The incident is seen as a potential step towards de-escalation, but analysts warn that it may not be sufficient to resolve the broader conflict between Iran and the United States.

articles.title: Failed H-1B lottery 7 times, moved to Canada: Indian-origin Microsoft techie gets Green Card through EB-1 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aishani B, an Indian-origin Microsoft techie, shared her experience of obtaining a Green Card through the EB1 visa category after seven years of unsuccessful H-1B visa applications.  She described the emotional toll of repeated rejections, noting that while initial disappointment is understandable, it eventually transforms into a quiet erosion of certainty. Despite facing numerous setbacks, B persevered and ultimately found success in her immigration journey. Her story emphasizes that the number of rejections does not define one's potential but rather the resilience and determination to overcome challenges.

articles.title: US Supreme Court temporarily lifts ban on abortion pill mail delivery | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court temporarily lifted a ban on mail-order delivery of the abortion pill mifepristone, restoring telehealth access for at least one week. The court's "administrative stay" was issued by Justice Samuel Alito and allows manufacturers to continue providing the medication via telemedicine and mail while legal challenges play out.  The decision comes as abortion rights remain a contentious issue in the US following the overturning of Roe v. Wade, with Democrats emphasizing access to reproductive healthcare and Republicans calling for restrictions on the procedure.

articles.title: “Bizzare attacks against me”: Candace Owens alleges Ben Shapiro lawsuits as Laura Loomer responds with strong criticism - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens and Laura Loomer have escalated their public feud, with Owens accusing Shapiro of orchestrating attacks against her and her family. Loomer countered by challenging Owens's denial of her claims and accused her of spreading false information about Kasparian. The situation has drawn in other figures like Ana Kasparian and organizations such as Turning Point USA, with both sides making serious allegations without concrete evidence.

articles.title: PTI accuses govt of ‘unprecedented economic crisis’, slams claims of stability - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party accused the current government of driving Pakistan into an economic and governance crisis, citing high inflation, soaring fuel and electricity prices, and food insecurity.  Sheikh Waqas Akram, PTI's Information Secretary, criticized the government's policies on wheat movement, energy sector debt, and tax policy, calling them "punish the documented, protect the powerful" and blaming the government for failing to address issues like circular debt and theft. He argued that without a focus on democratic governance, strong institutions, and merit-based decision-making, Pakistan will continue to lose opportunities and dignity.

articles.title: Cabinet ministers warn mutinous MPs about trying to oust Keir Starmer | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cabinet ministers have warned Labour MPs against attempting to oust Keir Starmer after the potentially disastrous election results. While some cabinet members acknowledge the current mood on the backbenches is febrile, they believe any attempt at a leadership challenge would be detrimental to the party and unlikely to succeed.  Several ministers expressed concern about unintended consequences of such an action, emphasizing that it's premature for a leadership contest or timetable for Starmer’s departure.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks fall from record high on Middle East worries - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record highs last Friday, but renewed concerns about the Middle East conflict have led to market declines.  Investment strategist Ross Mayfield of Baird Private Wealth Management noted that with markets at all-time highs, there is a risk of "big asymmetric" events impacting the market negatively.  The S&P 500 lost 28.37 points on Friday, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 43.78 points.   Shares of GameStop tumbled after proposing to buy eBay, and FedEx and United Parcel Service declined after Amazon.com expanded its logistics network.

articles.title: Governance is the ultimate currency in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala has elected the United Democratic Front (UDF) to power in the 2026 Assembly elections, marking the end of the Left Democratic Front’s (LDF) decade-long rule. The UDF secured a decisive victory with 97 seats, while the LDF received 35 and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) garnered 3 seats. This trend reflects previous electoral successes for the UDF in both the Lok Sabha elections of 2024 and local body elections of 2025.

articles.title: Viral Video Ishowspeed: Viral clip shows IShowSpeed landing punch on fan during Puerto Rico appearance - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular streamer, was involved in a playful boxing-style interaction with a fan during a public appearance in Puerto Rico. The video, which quickly went viral online, showed Speed landing a punch that caused the fan to stumble backward.  While the clip was shared with dramatic captions suggesting a knockout, there is no evidence of serious injury. This incident occurred during Speed's ongoing travel content tour where he engages in unpredictable live activities with fans.

articles.title: Narendra Modi’s BJP wins election in West Bengal for the first time | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won a resounding victory in West Bengal, marking the first time the party has held power in the state. This significant win expands the BJP's control over Indian state and central governments, further solidifying its dominance under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The victory is attributed to factors like anti-incumbency against the ruling Trinamool Congress (TMC) and a strong Hindu vote, despite controversies surrounding the BJP's electoral roll revision exercise.  The results also signal a return to the BJP's dominant position in Indian politics, potentially impacting the 2024 general election.

articles.title: UK weather forecast: Temperatures to fall after bank holiday warm spell across regions - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Met Office and BBC forecast cooler temperatures across the United Kingdom in the first week of May, transitioning from a period of warm settled weather. The change is attributed to shifts in pressure patterns and northerly winds, resulting in occasional showers, frost, and fog in some regions.  Northern Ireland experienced largely dry and sunny conditions while England and Wales saw varying cloud cover with some sunshine.

articles.title: BJP-led NDA scores hat-trick in Assam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured a historic victory in the Assam Assembly elections, winning 102 of 126 seats to retain power for a third consecutive term. The BJP's regional allies, the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) and the Bodoland People’s Front (BPF), also performed well, winning 10 and 10 seats respectively.  The Congress party suffered its worst performance since losing power in 2016, winning only 19 seats. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who retained his Jalukbari seat, is now considered one of the BJP's most prominent leaders in Assam.

articles.title: xQc ignites online storm with bold gender dynamics take on female police officers during livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: xQc Lengyel, a popular streamer, sparked debate on social media after sharing his opinion during a livestream about gender roles in policing.  He stated that he believes men are better suited to give orders in certain situations, citing the perceived "commanding voice" as a factor. This comment drew mixed reactions from viewers, with some supporting his viewpoint and others criticizing it for potentially perpetuating harmful stereotypes. xQc later clarified that his views were not absolute but rather based on how different situations may require different approaches, including acknowledging the potential effectiveness of women in de-escalation situations.

articles.title: West Bengal election results: Split in Muslim votes spells doom for Trinamool Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Trinamool Congress lost power in the 2026 Assembly elections due to a split in the Muslim vote bank, which favored the BJP and its candidates.  Several factors contributed to this shift, including discontent among Muslim voters over issues such as temple construction and lack of development in minority-dominated areas. The Left Front, Congress, and AJUP also benefited from this division, securing seats in Malda and Murshidabad districts where the Muslim population is significant.  The BJP's success was particularly pronounced in these areas with a majority of Hindu voters.

articles.title: NAB recovers 80 acres of govt land illegally allotted to Bahria Town - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) Karachi recovered 80 acres of government land illegally allotted to Bahria Town in Hyderabad's Deh Ganjo Takkar. The land, worth Rs6 billion, was intended for a university but was given to Bahria Town for a paltry sum of Rs383 million.  The HDA cancelled the allotment and forfeited the partially paid amount after NAB intervened. Last week, an accountability court issued arrest warrants against Malik Riaz, his son, and others involved in the land grab case.

articles.title: Tata Chemicals Q4 results: Cons loss widens YoY to Rs 2,132 crore on exceptional items; revenue drops 2% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Chemicals reported a significant net loss of Rs 93 crore in Q3FY25, driven by weak pricing across regions and impairment charges in the US business. The company's profit after tax before exceptional items and NCI stood at Rs 279 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 12 crore for the same period last year.  R. Mukundan, Managing Director & CEO of Tata Chemicals, highlighted the oversupplied global soda ash market and geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East as key factors impacting pricing. Despite these challenges, the company remains focused on long-term growth initiatives like expanding its specialty chemicals portfolio and enhancing salt capacity.

articles.title: Olivia Henderson: Viral TikTok DoorDash driver Olivia Henderson hit with felony charges, pleads not guilty - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olivia Henderson, a DoorDash driver from New York, faces felony charges and a misdemeanor for recording and sharing a video of a customer inside his home without permission. DoorDash removed her from the platform after the company stated she was not fired for reporting a safety issue but for violating their policy. The case has sparked debate about privacy rights and the use of surveillance technology. Henderson has pleaded not guilty to the charges, which could lead to serious consequences if found guilty.

articles.title: West Bengal election results: Split in Muslim votes spells doom for Trinamool Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Trinamool Congress lost power in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections due to a split in the Muslim vote bank.  A combination of factors, including discontent over development and alleged lack of support for restoring voter names, led voters to choose alternative parties like the Left Front, Congress, and the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP). The BJP benefited from this split, winning or leading in several seats with large Muslim populations.

articles.title: Spain seizes record amount of cocaine in Atlantic Ocean, authorities say
articles.rephrased_article: Spanish police have seized a record amount of cocaine, estimated between 30,000 and 45,000 kilograms, from a freighter intercepted off the Canary Islands. The Civil Guard, in collaboration with the AUGC union, arrested around 20 individuals on board the vessel which was traveling from Sierra Leone to Libya.  Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska described the seizure as "one of the biggest, not only nationally but internationally."

articles.title: CSB Bank Q4 profit rises 6% on lower provisions, growth steady - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Manappuram Finance reported a 9.6% decrease in its standalone net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26, reaching Rs 497 crore compared to Rs 550 crore in the previous year. The decline was attributed to higher finance costs and provisions against bad loans.  The bank's gross non-performing assets ratio improved sequentially but deteriorated year-on-year, while its net interest margin increased. Manappuram Finance also proposed a dividend of Rs 0.50 per equity share.

articles.title: Olivia Henderson: Viral TikTok DoorDash driver Olivia Henderson hit with felony charges, pleads not guilty - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olivia Henderson, a DoorDash driver from New York, is facing felony charges and a misdemeanor for recording and sharing a video of a customer inside his home without permission.  The incident began when Henderson called 911 claiming the customer was asleep without pants in an open door. Police determined no crime had been committed, but Henderson was later arrested and charged with unlawful surveillance and sharing the video. The case is ongoing as she pleads not guilty to the charges.

articles.title: Assam’s mandate of assertion and polarisation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) is set to form the government in Assam for a third consecutive term, securing a significant increase in both seats and vote share.  This victory reflects a renewed dominance of the BJP in the state, which has historically seen shifts between Congress and regionalist parties. The current mandate signifies an ongoing political shift towards the BJP's ideology.

articles.title: Six Indian nationals among sailors rescued by navy, maritime security agency in Arabian Sea: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Navy and the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (PMSA) provided humanitarian assistance to six sailors aboard an Indian offshore tug and supply vessel, the MV Gautam, after a technical fault stranded them in the Arabian Sea. The Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre in Mumbai requested assistance from Pakistani authorities who deployed the PMSS Kashmir for rescue operations. Emergency aid, including food, medical supplies, and technical support, was provided to the crew of the MV Gautam, with ongoing support efforts.

articles.title: Gangland wars killing dozens of bystanders, report Swedish police | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Swedish police report that 23 innocent people have been killed and 30 wounded in gangland shootings over the past three years. The violence, primarily linked to drug market disputes, has led to a surge in bystander casualties due to young perpetrators with limited experience in violent crime. Alexander Wallenius, operations coordinator at the Swedish police’s department of national operations, attributes this trend to the involvement of minors who are often recruited through social media and encrypted apps. The government is currently working on legislation requiring social media platforms to remove gang-related posts within an hour or face fines.

articles.title: Victoria state budget 2026: state back in black forecasting two back-to-back surpluses | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria is projected to achieve a $700 million operating surplus in the 2025-26 financial year, marking its first surplus since before the COVID-19 pandemic. Jaclyn Symes, the state's treasurer, announced this surplus and projected another $1 billion surplus for the 2026-27 fiscal year. However, Jess Wilson of the opposition Liberal party criticized the government's claim of a "real" surplus, highlighting the significant infrastructure spending that is not included in the operating surplus figures. The budget also includes funding commitments for various initiatives such as car registration refunds, public transport extensions, school infrastructure upgrades, and healthcare programs.

articles.title: Hantavirus scare: All you need to know about Atlantic cruise ship outbreak that killed 3 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: WHO and CDC are investigating an alleged hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise liner, which has resulted in confirmed and suspected cases among passengers. Hantavirus is a virus transmitted to humans by rodents through airborne particles from their droppings, urine, or saliva. The disease can cause serious respiratory problems, including death, and there are two main forms: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome.  Early diagnosis and supportive care are crucial for managing the infection.

articles.title: Tata Technologies Q4 Results: Cons PAT rises 8% YoY to Rs 204 crore, revenue rises 22% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company's total operating revenue reached Rs 1,572 crore in Q4FY26, a 22% increase from the previous year. This growth was driven by a 15% quarterly revenue increase and a strong performance in the services segment, which generated $132.6 million in revenue. The company's EBITDA rose to Rs 252 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 16%. The company also announced a final dividend of Rs 8.35 per share and a one-time special dividend of Rs 3.35 per share for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

articles.title: Meto Komori and Yuhi Chito suspension shocks fans as VSPO! hides details behind contract violation claims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: VSPO!, a VTuber agency, announced that creators Meto Komori and Yuhi Chito will be suspended for two months due to "conduct that partially violated their contracts."  The company declined to disclose specifics but stated the suspension is intended for reflection and behavior re-examination. Both creators apologized to fans without going into detail about the situation, fueling speculation among viewers.

articles.title: Thalapathy government? Why Vijay's historic rise in India's industrial powerhouse state matters for stock market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu, a major manufacturing and export hub for India, is expected to see a measured market reaction following the election of Vijayakanth as Chief Minister.  Analysts predict that his focus on welfare and social justice may initially raise concerns about fiscal spending and regulatory oversight. However, they also believe his clean image and promises around job creation could improve governance perception if implemented effectively. Investors will be closely watching for policy clarity on ease of doing business and industrial incentives in the coming weeks. Sectors such as auto and electronics manufacturing, industrial parks, logistics, renewable energy, and grid infrastructure are expected to remain in focus.

articles.title: Giuliani recovering from pneumonia and 'now breathing on his own'
articles.rephrased_article: Rudy Giuliani, the former New York City mayor, is recovering from pneumonia and is now breathing on his own after being hospitalized.  His spokesman, Ted Goodman, stated that Giuliani has had restrictive airway disease since the 9/11 terror attacks, which led to complications when he contracted the virus.  Giuliani remains in critical but stable condition. The former mayor, known as "America's Mayor", was a key figure in Donald Trump's presidential campaigns and later became his personal lawyer. He has faced legal consequences for making false claims about the 2020 election.

articles.title: Two killed and several hurt after car ploughs into crowds in German city of Leipzig | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A driver in an SUV plowed into a crowd of shoppers and cafe patrons in Leipzig, Germany, killing at least two people and injuring several others. The incident occurred around 4:45 pm on Monday in the city's pedestrian zone.  The driver was apprehended by police, and authorities have cordoned off the area to allow for an investigation. Mayor Burkhard Jung expressed his solidarity with the victims' families and stated that everything else will depend on the work of the police and investigating authorities.

articles.title: 'Can a neighbor hear a gunshot?': Chilling forensic details emerge in murders of two Bangladeshi students in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh, a roommate of missing student Zamil Ahmed Limon, has been charged with the murders of both students. Bristy's body was found in Tampa Bay, and Limon's remains were discovered on the Howard Frankland Bridge.  Forensic evidence revealed that Abugharbieh planned and executed the killings, removing all traces. The investigation is ongoing as the bodies are being sent to Bangladesh for burial.

articles.title: Adani Ports, Tata Motors and Siemens Energy witness block deal action on Monday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Capital Group International All Countries Equity Trust, Capital Income Builder, and Europacific Growth Fund acquired shares in APSEZ, indicating a significant transfer of institutional holdings.  BNP Paribas purchased shares in TMCV from Goldman Sachs.  The Indian stock market closed higher, with gains driven by financials, pharma, and metal sectors. The Nifty index gained 0.51% to finish at 24,119.30, while the Sensex rose 0.46% to settle at 77,269.40.

articles.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a protest against India after the country announced the resumption of a religious pilgrimage through the Lipulekh Pass, which is claimed by Nepal based on a 1816 treaty.  India maintains that the pass has been used for pilgrimages since 1954 and disputes Nepal's territorial claims. The dispute reignited after India agreed with China to resume the pilgrimage, which was suspended in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Leipzig: Two killed and many injured after car driven into crowd
articles.rephrased_article: A car driven into a crowd in Leipzig, Germany on Monday afternoon resulted in the deaths of two people and numerous injuries.  The suspected driver was apprehended by authorities who are currently investigating the incident's motivation. Mayor Burkhard Jung confirmed that 22 individuals were injured, with two suffering serious injuries. Firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, along with police, who secured the area after the suspect was taken into custody.

articles.title: Nigerian refinery accused of sacking union members is key to UK plan to tackle jet fuel shortage | Airline industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government is seeking to alleviate a jet fuel shortage by importing more fuel from the US and west Africa, including fuel produced at the Nigerian refinery owned by Aliko Dangote.  This refinery has been accused of union-busting practices after firing workers who joined the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (Pengassan) union. The Nigerian government intervened in a dispute last year, but the company denies dismissing workers for union membership. Despite the controversy, the refinery is now producing aviation fuel at its maximum capacity to meet increased demand from the UK.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: P. Rajeeve fails to survive anti-incumbency wave in Kalamassery - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.E. Abdul Gafoor, of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), won the Kalamassery constituency seat in Kerala, defeating outgoing Industries Minister P. Rajeeve of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)].  Gafoor secured a significant victory with 80,606 votes compared to Rajeeve's 64,294. The LDF, which had pinned its hopes on Rajeeve's performance as a minister, suffered setbacks across several municipalities in the region.  Rajeeve conceded defeat and acknowledged the anti-incumbency wave affecting the Left camp.

articles.title: Built for future: Florida town that runs entirely on sunlight and produces more power than it uses | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Babcock Ranch, a Florida town developed by Kitson & Partners in partnership with Florida Power & Light, is an innovative model for sustainable urban living. The community, spanning 17,000 acres, generates more electricity than it consumes through a large solar installation and energy-efficient design.  This system, coupled with preserved natural habitats and smart grid technology, allows the town to operate as an energy-positive entity while reducing reliance on traditional infrastructure. Babcock Ranch serves as a blueprint for future urban development by demonstrating how clean energy, efficient design, and environmental balance can be integrated into everyday life.

articles.title: Security lapses at Parliament Lodges a 'serious threat', says Senate deputy chairman - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Syedal Khan Nasar, Senate Deputy Chairman, summoned Capital Development Authority (CDA) and security officials to address security lapses and poor facilities at the Parliament Lodges.  He expressed displeasure over unauthorized entry, delays in renovation, and a lack of progress on 104 new blocks. Nasar ordered a comprehensive report within three days, demanding details of complaints, action taken, and an inquiry into a video showing an unrelated woman entering the lodge. The deputy chairman also directed immediate repair work and resolution of complaints.

articles.title: Modi’s party poised for big wins in Indian state elections | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is expected to win two of four crucial state elections in India, strengthening its position and weakening key rival Mamata Banerjee.  The BJP's lead in West Bengal and Assam suggests a significant boost for Modi as he seeks to tackle economic challenges. Opposition parties like the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) are facing setbacks, potentially weakening their opposition against Modi in future elections. The results of these state elections will have long-lasting implications for Indian politics, with analysts predicting a significant shift in power dynamics.

articles.title: NSW to criminalise secret GPS tracking after report highlighting number of devices bought by DV offenders | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A man in New South Wales fatally shot his wife after using a GPS tracking device to monitor her movements for months, prompting the NSW government to introduce new legislation. The changes aim to criminalize secretly monitoring someone without their knowledge, as well as directing third parties to engage in stalking or promoting unlawful surveillance device use.  The NSW Crime Commission's Project Hakea report found that tracking devices were increasingly used by domestic violence perpetrators and organized crime networks, highlighting the need for stronger laws to protect victims from such abuse.

articles.title: Four killed, two injured as ambulance rams into stationary truck near Srikalahasti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four people were killed and two others injured in a road accident near Srikalahasti town of Tirupati district on Monday (May 4, 2026).  An ambulance rammed into a stationary truck from behind, resulting in the deaths of four passengers traveling in the vehicle. The injured individuals were transported to a nearby hospital for treatment. The cause of the crash is under investigation by police.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos secretly selling $500 million superyacht that has sculpture of Lauren Sanchez as mermaid because... - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeff Bezos is selling his $500 million superyacht, Koru, due to its size. The 417-foot vessel, which has a support ship called Abeona, was designed with a sculpture of Lauren Sanchez, his wife, and symbolizes new beginnings for the couple.  The sale comes after Bezos faced difficulties docking Koru in various locations, including Monaco and the Florida Everglades.

articles.title: PSL 11’s highest scorer Babar Azam named captain of the edition’s Team of the Year - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced the Team of the Year for the 11th HBL Pakistan Super League edition, with Babar Azam leading the side after scoring the most runs.  The team was selected by a five-member committee from the commentary team and included players like Kusal Mendis, Fakhar Zaman, and Shan Masood.  Sufyan Muqeem won the Best Bowler award, while Shadab Khan earned the title of Best All-rounder.

articles.title: India loses its last left-wing government after five decades | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India's left-wing parties have lost their grip on power, with the United Democratic Front winning the Kerala state elections. This marks the first time in over half a century that no Indian state is ruled by the left. The decline of the left's influence is attributed to factors such as its inability to address issues like caste and gender inequality and its perceived lack of relevance in the face of changing economic realities. Experts suggest that while the left may not be in power, it remains an important opposition force capable of influencing policy debates.

articles.title: Albanese won’t bring in a gas export tax next week – but he’ll struggle to hold off pressure forever | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hosted Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Canberra for annual leaders' talks, solidifying a strong relationship between the two countries.  The meeting coincided with the 50th anniversary of a landmark treaty between Australia and Japan. Meanwhile, independent Senator David Pocock addressed Labor-aligned union rallies in Gladstone, advocating for a new gas export tax to address concerns about rising living costs. Labor's Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) president Michele O’Neil also expressed support for the idea, arguing that multinational corporations should pay their fair share of taxes.  The government is currently facing internal pressure to consider a gas export tax in the future.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: IUML enters new era as Fathima Thahiliya becomes first woman MLA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fathima Thahiliya, a former Haritha leader and practicing lawyer, has become the first woman from the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) to be elected to the Kerala Assembly.  She defeated T.P. Ramakrishnan, the LDF convener, by a significant margin of 5,087 votes. This victory marks a turning point for the IUML, which had previously faced criticism for its lack of female representation in public life. The party's leadership has increasingly embraced women's participation in politics, as evidenced by their decision to field two women candidates this election.  While Ms. Thahiliya's win is a significant step forward, it also signals the potential for broader acceptance of women within the IUML's electoral framework.

articles.title: It was not racist: New Zealand woman says police came to her house for her 'Welcome to New India' FB post - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Renee-Rose Schwenke, a New Zealand woman, claims she was contacted by the police after posting a Facebook photo with a caption that mocked Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's recent trade agreement with India.  Schwenke maintains her post wasn't racist but was instead met with abusive comments and subsequently reported to authorities who questioned her about it. She alleges the police officer she spoke with was biased and unprofessional in his response. Schwenke doubled down on her views, stating that she won't be silenced for expressing them.

articles.title: Vedasandur, a bellwether Assembly segment since 1957, bucks the trend - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, DMK won the Vedasandur Assembly segment in Dindigul district, a traditionally bellwether seat. However, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) emerged as the single largest party in the state, with candidates winning in both the Vedasandur and Sholavandan segments.  T. Saminathan of the DMK won the Vedasandur segment by a margin of 10,063 votes, while M.V. Karuppaiah of the TVK won the Sholavandan segment by a margin of 2,678 votes.

articles.title: '20 years on H-1B': Major row over Indian man's viral post on not getting to see dying mother - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Dey, an H-1B visa holder living in the US, faced backlash after his LinkedIn post detailing his inability to travel to India to see his dying mother due to consular issues. Many criticized Dey for choosing a life in the US over his family and questioned why he had not become a permanent resident after 20 years. Sam Peak, an immigration policy analyst, defended Dey, stating that there could be many factors contributing to his visa difficulties.  Vijay Thirumalai, an Indian-origin entrepreneur, argued that Dey's situation was unfair due to the US's restrictive immigration system and called for focusing on illegal immigrants instead of honest H-1B holders.

articles.title: India's Modi celebrates 'record' win in opposition-held West Bengal - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister, claimed a record victory in the West Bengal state elections for his Hindu nationalist party, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The BJP secured a majority of seats and is expected to strengthen its position ahead of the 2029 general election.  The results were met with celebrations by party leaders and supporters, while scuffles broke out at some counting centers. In Tamil Nadu, veteran politician MK Stalin lost his seat to a new party led by actor-politician C. Joseph Vijay. The Congress party won in Kerala, ousting the ruling Communists.

articles.title: Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso quit ADC and join NDC in major Nigerian political shake-up
articles.rephrased_article: Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, who finished third and fourth in the 2023 presidential election, have joined the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). This move comes after a short stint in the African Democratic Congress (ADC) where they were previously aligned with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The defections are seen as a potential threat to the opposition's unity and could reshape Nigeria's electoral landscape, especially if Obi is chosen as the NDC's presidential candidate.  The Nigerian presidency has downplayed the significance of the defections.

articles.title: France’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon announces 2027 presidential bid | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the radical left leader of La France Insoumise, announced his intention to run for president again in 2027, citing a need to counter the far-right. He argued that his radical left economic program could defeat the National Rally and called for a united front against war in the Middle East with Spain.  Despite his experience, Mélenchon faces challenges from a polarized electorate and accusations of antisemitism. Other prominent figures like Edouard Philippe have also declared their candidacy.

articles.title: Pawan Kalyan steps in to rescue stranded woman worker in Muscat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan responded to a viral video of an immigrant worker from Valmikipuram, Shehnaz, pleading for help in Muscat after being allegedly assaulted and denied basic necessities.  Mr. Pawan Kalyan directed officials to coordinate with the Ministry of External Affairs and the Indian Embassy in Oman to ensure her safe return. Officials are working with her family and local recruitment agents to facilitate her repatriation.

articles.title: ‘All British people should die’: Irish woman convicted after ‘anti-english’ rant at UK hotel | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 40-year-old Irish woman, Cait O’Halloran, was fined £614 and ordered to pay costs after being convicted of racially aggravated harassment in Cheshire.  She verbally abused hotel staff at a Holiday Inn in Runcorn on January 17th while intoxicated, making anti-English remarks and threats against British people. The court heard that O'Halloran admitted the offense and expressed remorse for her actions, which were linked to alcohol consumption. Her solicitor stated that this was out of character for her and that she is mortified by her behavior.

articles.title: Srinagar again ‘full-fledge capital’ of J&K after hiatus of six years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Srinagar functioned as the full-fledged summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, May 4, 2026, after a six-year hiatus.  Chief Minister Omar Abdullah received a ceremonial guard of honor at the Civil Secretariat, marking the resumption of the annual Darbar Move tradition. The move, abolished in 2020 by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, sees over 151 government departments shift offices between Jammu and Srinagar. To accommodate employees, the J&K government inaugurated 368 residential units for them at Sempora, Pampore.

articles.title: "Easily killed an innocent person": Candace Owens and Laura Loomer feud turns ugly as feud spirals out of control - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens and Laura Loomer have engaged in a heated online feud, escalating from initial criticism to personal attacks.  Owens shared a video clip alleging that Loomer advises Donald Trump on foreign policy, while Loomer countered by focusing on Owens' husband's alleged DUI incident. The dispute has drawn significant attention and sparked debate about the boundaries of online discourse and the weight given to perceived political proximity. Neither side appears willing to back down, making it unlikely that the feud will subside soon.

articles.title: Chiranjeevi, Mahesh Babu, Nani, Vijay Deverakonda react to actor Vijay TVK win in Tamil Nadu poll - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Chiranjeevi, Mahesh Babu, and other Telugu film stars congratulated actor-politician Vijay on the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam's (TVK) strong showing in the Tamil Nadu Assembly election.  The actors expressed their well wishes for Vijay's public service to the state of Tamil Nadu and its people.

articles.title: Plane hits truck while landing at Newark airport, chilling dashcam video shows what happened - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A United Airlines Boeing 767, en route from Venice to Newark, experienced a collision with a streetlight and a tractor-trailer on the nearby highway during its landing. The incident occurred after the plane's landing gear tires struck the truck, causing damage to both vehicles.  The truck driver sustained non-life-threatening injuries but was transported to a hospital. United Airlines stated that the aircraft landed safely with no passengers or crew injured and the pilot and air traffic control did not appear to be aware of the incident upon landing.

articles.title: ‘Hegemonic power’: How Modi’s BJP won India’s Bengal for the first time | Elections | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the West Bengal state elections, marking a significant shift in Indian politics. The party's victory was attributed to factors including religious polarisation and anti-incumbency against the incumbent All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) party, led by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.  The BJP leveraged this strategy while also benefiting from a record voter turnout, with nearly 68.2 million people casting ballots. The TMC's loss is seen as a major setback for Banerjee's hopes of becoming a national challenger to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This victory strengthens the BJP's position within India and could impact future elections.

articles.title: West Bengal: Modi's BJP conquers one of India's toughest political frontiers
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive victory in West Bengal, marking a significant breakthrough for Narendra Modi and his 12-year reign.  This unexpected outcome comes after years of the party's struggle to gain traction in the state, which has traditionally been dominated by the Trinamool Congress (TMC). The BJP's success is attributed to a combination of factors, including its aggressive welfare pitch, sharpened Hindu consolidation efforts, and a focus on alleged corruption within the TMC. This victory will likely have far-reaching implications for the BJP's future trajectory, potentially solidifying Amit Shah's position as Modi's successor.

articles.title: Karnataka bypolls results 2026: Congress retains Bagalkot constituency, faulty EVMs delay counting in Davanagere South - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Umesh Meti of the Congress won the Bagalkot Assembly constituency by a margin of 22,332 votes in Karnataka's by-election.  The counting of votes for the Davangere South constituency has been delayed due to technical glitches on three EVMs. The results are expected after the completion of the VVPAT tallying process. Security arrangements have been made at both counting centers to ensure a smooth and secure election outcome.

articles.title: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope detects ‘little red dots’: New X-ray data hints at hidden supermassive black holes | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The James Webb Space Telescope has detected faint, distant objects known as "little red dots" that exhibit unusual characteristics.  These objects, which are compact and reddish in color, appear to contain rapidly growing supermassive black holes hidden within dense gas clouds. Data from the Chandra X-ray Observatory supports this hypothesis, revealing X-ray emissions emanating from these locations. While intriguing, scientists remain cautious as further research is needed to confirm the presence of a black hole and rule out other potential explanations for the observed phenomena.

articles.title: Shipping bosses nervous over Trump plan to guide vessels from strait of Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US has launched "Project Freedom" to guide ships trapped in the Gulf by the Iran war through a southern route of the Strait of Hormuz.  While Iran insists any such transits must be coordinated with its armed forces, the US Central Command will support the project with military resources. The initiative comes amid uncertainty over its effectiveness and potential for conflict.  The US has been approached by countries seeking assistance in freeing their ships and crews from the Gulf, and President Trump claims positive discussions are underway with Iran. However, Iran maintains that any unauthorized transit of the strait will be considered a violation of the ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Dubai-based Indian to approach embassy over travel ban - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court declined to grant relief to Asif Azad, an Indian engineer who alleged harassment by local authorities in Dubai.  Mr. Azad, appearing via video conference from a Dubai mall, claimed he was wrongfully subjected to a travel ban due to a case against him in Kerala. The court directed Mr. Azad to seek assistance from the Indian Embassy in the UAE.

articles.title: Earth’s origin mystery cracked? Meteorites may hold the secret to life’s ingredients | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists have been studying the origins of Earth's building blocks, particularly through the analysis of meteorites and isotopic compositions.  These studies suggest that carbonaceous chondrites, considered primitive materials from the outer solar system, played a significant role in providing carbon, water, and volatile elements necessary for life on Earth. Isotopic fingerprints found in Earth's mantle, such as those of molybdenum, indicate genetic links between Earth and these meteorites, suggesting a common source for both.  This research challenges the traditional view that comets were solely responsible for delivering water to Earth.  Further investigation into this process will provide more insight into the origins of life and planetary formation within our solar system.

articles.title: Rudy Giuliani in critical condition in hospital
articles.rephrased_article: Rudy Giuliani, the former New York City Mayor and a long-time supporter of President Donald Trump, is in "stable but critical condition" at a hospital following an accident last year. Trump praised Giuliani's efforts in contesting the 2020 election, which was won by Democrat Joe Biden.  Goodman, Giuliani's spokesman, requested prayers for his health. The former mayor has faced legal repercussions for false claims about the 2020 election and received a $148 million defamation judgment from a jury.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Dubai-based Indian to approach embassy over travel ban - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court declined to grant relief to Asif Azad, an Indian engineer who alleged harassment by Dubai authorities and a wrongful travel ban.  Mr. Azad appeared via video conferencing from a Dubai mall, claiming he was entrapped and implicated in a case against him in Kerala. The court directed Mr. Azad to seek assistance from the Indian Embassy in the UAE.

articles.title: 12,000-year-old Karahantepe discovery reveals massive statues and an unexpected prehistoric diet | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Excavations at Karahantepe, a Neolithic site in southeastern Türkiye, have revealed evidence of a complex society that practiced 'pre-domestication' cultivation.  The site, dating back around 12,000 years, produced over-life-sized human statues and detailed carvings of animals, as well as plant remains indicating a semi-managed diet including wild legumes. Professor Necmi Karul, leading the excavations, found numerous T-shaped pillars and highly detailed human figures, while bioarchaeological research revealed consumption of gazelle, wild sheep, and various legumes like bitter vetch and lentils. This evidence challenges the traditional view known as the 'Agriculture First' theory by demonstrating that hunter-gatherers formed stable communities with permanent buildings and communal feasting well before wheat became domesticated.

articles.title: 'Not a nation that bows': Bilawal hails Pakistan's victory against India during Marka-i-Haq - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah addressed a commemoration event for Marka-i-Haq, marking the 2025 conflict with India.  Bilawal emphasized Pakistan's "victory" against India, highlighting its resilience and unity in the face of pressure. He stressed that victory was measured by dignity preserved and sovereignty defended, not territorial gains or military victories. Bilawal called for a focus on building a stronger Pakistan through investment in people, education, and economic growth, while advocating for just and dignified peace.  The event commemorated the conflict's impact and its significance for future generations.

articles.title: Assam election results LIVE: Trends show NDA inching towards majority mark - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The counting of votes for the Assam Assembly elections began on Monday, May 4, 2026. Election Commission of India early trends show the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) leading in over 70 seats. The ruling NDA is seeking a third consecutive term while the Congress-led Opposition alliance hopes to regain power with the Asom Sonmilito Morcha (ASM).  Counting is taking place at 40 centers across all 35 districts.

articles.title: Who is Charles Lieber? Convicted Harvard scientist now leading China’s research to link the brain with computers | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charles Lieber, a former Harvard chemistry professor, was convicted in 2021 of making false statements and tax-related offenses tied to payments from China. He now leads the i-BRAIN institute in Shenzhen, where he is researching brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for medical applications. The move has drawn attention due to Lieber's past conviction and China's focus on BCIs as a strategic priority.  Lieber's expertise in nanotechnology and neural interfaces could accelerate BCI research, but his involvement raises concerns about the intersection of science, geopolitics, and technological competition.

articles.title: Former NYC Mayor Giuliani hospitalised in ‘critical condition’ | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rudolph Giuliani, former New York City mayor and advisor to President Donald Trump, was hospitalized in critical but stable condition. His spokesperson said he is a fighter who has faced every challenge with unwavering strength. Trump hailed Giuliani as a "true warrior" and praised his resilience despite recent legal troubles.  The 81-year-old Giuliani coughed during his nightly online show, prompting concern about his health.

articles.title: Kerala Election Results 2026 LIVE: UDF leads in the State, CM Pinarayi Vijayan trails in Dharmadam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress-led UDF is on track to secure a majority in the Kerala Assembly elections, with trends indicating they will surpass their target of 100 seats.  As counting progressed, the UDF held a commanding lead in over 100 constituencies while the CPI(M)-led LDF lagged behind in under 40. The BJP-led NDA secured only two seats according to early results.  Congress MLA Chandy Oommen won his constituency by a significant margin.

articles.title: Hidden for 1,000 years: Massive Viking silver coin hoard containing 3,000 coins discovered in Norway | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Norway have unearthed a remarkable Viking Age coin hoard, estimated to contain around 3,000 silver coins. The discovery, made near Rena in the Østerdalen region, dates back to the late 10th and early 11th centuries, during the peak of the Viking era.  Experts believe the hoard may have been buried around 980-1040 CE and originated from various European regions, including England and Germany. The coins exhibit elements from different minting systems, suggesting extensive trade links across Europe. While the exact purpose of the hoard remains unclear, researchers believe it could be linked to the iron industry in the area.  The discovery is considered significant for its historical value and insight into Viking trade and economy.

articles.title: Markets likely near bottom range; stay invested: Devina Mehra - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mehra, a prominent investment advisor, maintains her view that the current market is around its bottom range and advises investors to remain invested. She believes 2026 will be a better year than 2025, despite acknowledging near-term disruptions in earnings growth and valuation concerns.  While she highlights sectors like power generation and equipment as promising, she cautions against overreliance on index-level PE multiples and emphasizes the need for selective exposure within sectors. Mehra acknowledges the impact of rising crude prices but believes it is manageable and not a structural disruption. She also expresses cautious optimism about the IT sector despite acknowledging AI risks and employment concerns.  Despite some cooling in valuations, she doesn't see enough compelling reasons to make aggressive bets on the sector.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly election results: Congress’ Chandy Oommen wins in Puthuppally with huge margin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandy Oommen, son of former Kerala Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, won the Puthuppally by-election with a significant margin, securing 84,031 votes. His victory came after a campaign focused on environmental sustainability and door-to-door canvassing using bicycles.  The Communist Party of India (Marxist)'s K. M. Radhakrishnan received 31,124 votes. The Kerala Assembly elections were held on April 9th.

articles.title: Deadly Hantavirus scare on Atlantic Cruise Ship leaves 3 dead, British passenger critical | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A luxury cruise ship, the MV Hondius, travelling from Argentina to Cape Verde has been hit by a suspected hantavirus outbreak that has resulted in three deaths and several others being seriously ill. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed one case of hantavirus and authorities are working with South African and Dutch health officials to contain the crisis.  Authorities are coordinating efforts to evacuate affected passengers, repatriate bodies, and monitor potential exposure cases. The outbreak has raised concerns about cruise ship health risks and the difficulty in managing outbreaks in remote locations.

articles.title: IHC rejects Imran, Bushra's pleas seeking suspension of sentences in £190m graft case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court rejected the petitions of former prime minister Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi seeking suspension of their sentences in the £190 million corruption case. The court observed that their main appeals were already scheduled for hearing on May 7th, making the suspension applications infructuous.  Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir also heard a petition by Bushra's daughter seeking access to her mother and permission for a family meeting. Aleema Khanum, Imran’s sister, urged PTI leaders to pressure the government for access to Imran and his family at Adiala jail.

articles.title: Queensland government in ‘integrity crisis’ over alleged undisclosed affair between two ministers, opposition says | Queensland politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queensland’s opposition has accused the LNP government of an “integrity crisis” over a personal relationship between two ministers, Tim Mander and Amanda Camm. The pair issued statements claiming their relationship began in June 2023 and ended in May 2024, but media reports have questioned the timeline and raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest.  Deputy opposition leader Cameron Dick has called on the premier to release relevant documents, while political commentator Paul Williams believes Labor’s attack strategy may backfire as voters are more concerned with pressing issues like housing and cost of living.

articles.title: Markets may be approaching near-term exhaustion after strong rally: Rohit Srivastava - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rohit Srivastava, Founder of Strike Money Analytics & Indiacharts, suggests the market's rally may be nearing its end. While momentum indicators suggest a cooling pace, he notes that the Nifty faces resistance at 24,300 and could retest 23,500 if it fails to break through.  Real estate is emerging as a standout performer, with the Nifty Realty index surging sharply after a prolonged downtrend. However, experts caution that oversupply concerns remain, and further catalysts like rate cycle changes are needed for a sustained turnaround.

articles.title: Puducherry election results 2026 LIVE: Ruling AINRC leads the race; CM Rangasamy secures comfortable majority in Thattanchavady - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AINRC has secured 9 seats in the Puducherry Assembly elections, with N. Rangasamy winning his constituency. The BJP won Mannadipet and Neravy-T.R. Pattinam, while DMK took Nellithope from the BJP. Counting of votes is ongoing at six centers across the Union Territory.

articles.title: Which is the most common type of planet in the galaxy? Scientists reveal ‘super-Earths’ | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kepler observations have revealed that super-Earths, planets larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune, are the most abundant type of planet in the Milky Way. These planets, with sizes ranging from 1 to 4 times Earth's radius, vary in composition and orbit different stars.  The NASA Kepler Space Telescope, through its transit method, has discovered thousands of exoplanets, including super-Earths, which are particularly common due to their formation process being less stringent compared to gas giants. The abundance of these planets suggests that the galaxy contains many diverse planetary systems beyond our own.

articles.title: Oil prices flat as Trump’s plan for Strait of Hormuz fails to calm market | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices remained largely unchanged on Monday following President Donald Trump’s announcement of a plan to guide vessels out of the Strait of Hormuz.  While US Central Command stated it would support vessels seeking to transit the waterway, senior Iranian officials have warned against any “American interference” in the strait, casting uncertainty over the fragile ceasefire between the sides. Despite Trump’s plan and efforts by the United Kingdom’s military, maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly reduced due to ongoing threats from Iran.  Analysts suggest oil prices may remain elevated for some time after any peace deal is reached, as a backlog of unloaded energy supplies and damaged infrastructure persist.

articles.title: Jim Chalmers rules out fuel excise extension and downplays hopes for tax relief in ‘most responsible’ budget yet | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jim Chalmers, the Treasurer of Australia, stated that his upcoming budget would be "responsible" and focus on addressing inflation, despite previous promises not to touch negative gearing rules.  He ruled out extending the fuel excise cut beyond June and emphasized that the government would prioritize spending on essential programs like the fuel tax cut and standard deduction.  Anthony Albanese, the Prime Minister, has also faced criticism for breaking a pre-election promise regarding negative gearing. Chalmers acknowledged this but reassured Australians that the government is taking necessary steps to address community concerns about intergenerational fairness.

articles.title: Large and midcaps better placed than smallcaps in current phase: Shibani Sircar Kurian - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kurian, CEO of Kotak Mahindra Bank,  acknowledged the current market volatility, but emphasized that valuations remain reasonable and earnings expectations are intact. She highlighted the banking sector's strong performance, driven by credit growth and stable asset quality, with private banks showing particular promise due to their favorable valuations compared to historical averages. The outlook remains cautious yet optimistic, encouraging investors to be selective and capitalize on market corrections for gradual portfolio expansion.

articles.title: More Strait talks: Trump rolls out 'Project Freedom' to guide ships through Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump unveiled "Project Freedom", an initiative to assist commercial vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz amidst rising tensions.  He stated that countries worldwide, not involved in the Middle Eastern conflict, have requested US assistance to safely move their ships out of the waterway. The initiative will begin on Monday and aims to ensure safe passage for affected vessels while also highlighting concerns over supply conditions onboard. Trump emphasized that the movement is humanitarian in nature, intended to free up those who are victims of circumstance. He warned against interference with the operation and suggested potential diplomatic progress with Iran.

articles.title: Nifty’s 2 pillars now facing structural headwinds: Ravi Dharamshi's warning on IT & consumption - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ValueQuest, a financial firm, is advising investors to move away from traditional sectors like IT services and consumption-oriented businesses due to structural changes driven by AI and geopolitical factors. Dharamshi, the firm's head, warns that India's economic growth may be hampered by rising crude oil prices, supply chain disruptions, and a slowdown in IT employment.  He suggests investing in energy transition, defense, aerospace, AI infrastructure enablers, and grid capex plays as these sectors are likely to benefit from a more fragmented and security-conscious world. He believes that earnings dispersion will drive returns in the medium term, not just index-level performance.

articles.title: Israel issues evacuation warning; kills 1, hurts 4 in Lebanon strikes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon resulted in the deaths of at least one person and injuries to four rescuers, according to Lebanon's health ministry.  The strikes targeted several villages including Arabsalim, Srifa, and areas beyond the area Israel occupies. The Lebanese government condemned these attacks and reiterated the Geneva Convention's requirement for safe medical facilities during conflict.  Israel issued evacuation warnings for over 10 villages in southern Lebanon, citing threats from Hezbollah.

articles.title: Resurgent in April, can bulls defy 'Sell in May' maxim? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nifty and Sensex experienced strong gains in April, but analysts predict a more moderate performance in May.  While historical data suggests average returns of 1.84% for May, rising crude prices and uncertain economic conditions may limit upside potential.  Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, Elios Financial Services, and IIFL Capital Services anticipate a range-bound market with small- and mid-cap stocks outperforming large caps.

articles.title: NASA scientists reveal a 2.5-billion-year-old hidden structure within the Great Dyke of Zimbabwe | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA researchers, using satellite imagery and geophysics mapping, have discovered a hidden internal structure within the Great Dyke of Zimbabwe, estimated to be 2.5 billion years old. This feature, formed during the Archaean Eon, provides valuable insights into early Earth geology, magma systems, and continental formation. The discovery highlights the importance of modern satellite technology in revealing subsurface geological formations and processes.  This finding has implications for refining theories about the formation of terrestrial planets and understanding mineral deposits within the Great Dyke.

articles.title: AJK PM grants land ownership to 1,000 families displaced by LoC shelling - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Raja Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Prime Minister, announced the grant of ownership rights to over 1,000 families displaced from the Line of Control who have been living on government land near Mirpur since 2006.  Rathore, while acknowledging the hardships faced by these individuals due to cross-border shelling in 1998, stated that the government would continue to prioritize their rights and welfare. He also announced a dispensary for the area and plans for development initiatives in Kharri Sharif. Rathore expressed confidence in his party's success in the 2026 elections and asserted that the PPP was committed to safeguarding public rights.

articles.title: Tensions intensify at Strait: Cargo ship sailing near Hormuz attacked by Iran | India News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Britain’s Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that a bulk carrier was attacked by multiple small craft near Sirik, Iran. All crew members were unharmed and there was no environmental impact. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced it will begin guiding ships through the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday.  US President Donald Trump stated this operation involves guided-missile destroyers, aircraft, and service members but is not an escort mission. Iranian officials, including Ebrahim Azizi, warned that any US interference in the Strait's maritime regime would violate the ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election results 2026 LIVE: Counting of votes begins; all eyes on Vijay's TVK as DMK seeks second consecutive term - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu is awaiting the results of its State Assembly elections, with counting scheduled for Monday, May 4th, 2026.  The Election Commission of India reports a voter turnout of 85.1% and over 4.8 crore votes cast. The three-cornered battle involves the ruling DMK, the AIADMK, and the new entrant Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by actor C. Joseph Vijay.  Exit polls suggest a potential victory for TVK, with Axis My India predicting a massive 98-120 seat advantage for the party.

articles.title: Pharma Q4 outlook mixed: Hospitals steady, generics face revlimid drag - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sun Pharma is expected to benefit from strong growth in India and Europe, driven by specialty products. Aurobindo Pharma will report single-digit revenue growth due to a decline in US sales, while Dr Reddy's faces challenges from reduced gRevlimid business. Lupin is projected to see strong US revenue growth, offset by pressure on margins. Cipla and Apollo Hospitals are expected to experience declines in sales, driven by competition and supply disruptions.  Overall, the Indian pharmaceutical sector is anticipated to show significant growth with a focus on specialty products and emerging markets.

articles.title: Middle East crisis: Iran proposes 30-day plan to end war, says it has received US reply - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran received the US response to its 14-point proposal for peace talks, calling for an end to hostilities within 30 days. The proposal also included demands for sanctions lifting and the withdrawal of US forces from the region. President Donald Trump is reviewing the proposal but expressed doubt it would lead to a deal, stating that Iran has not paid "a big enough price" for its actions.  The US and Israel have suspended their bombing campaign against Iran, but attempts to set up further meetings have failed so far.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 results: Counting of votes begins across five States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Counting of votes for the Assembly elections in five states, including Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and West Bengal, is underway.  Election Commission of India (ECI) officials are overseeing the process at designated counting centers across the country. Early trends suggest a tight race in several constituencies with the DMK seeking to retain power in Tamil Nadu, while the AIADMK and independent candidates like Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam are vying for victory. In Kerala, the ruling Left Democratic Front faces competition from the Opposition United Democratic Front (UDF) and Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).  Security arrangements have been tightened across all states to ensure a smooth and peaceful counting process.

articles.title: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu among 5 state election results today. 10 things stock market investors should track under volatility - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors are advised to focus on broader macro signals rather than political headlines as state elections often trigger short-term volatility.  The Nifty is expected to swing 1-1.5% either way depending on the final election results, with crude oil prices remaining a key risk factor. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continue to sell Indian equities, while domestic institutions are absorbing pressure. Analysts suggest that markets will likely revert to global cues like oil prices and FII flows after the elections.

articles.title: Crowdfunding helps Serbian birdwatchers save woodland - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: **The Balkan country of Serbia's Bird Protection and Study Society purchased a 2-hectare woodland known as Nightingale’s Forest through crowdfunding to preserve the green space from development. The society, which has grown into a community of nature lovers, raised €8,000 in less than a month to protect the forest from timber harvesting.  The purchase is seen as a sign of growing interest in environmental protection among Serbian citizens who are facing environmental challenges such as pollution and waste management.

articles.title: West Bengal election results LIVE: Vote counting under way for 293 seats as TMC looks to retain power, BJP aims historic win - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Election Commission of India (ECI) has appointed additional observers for the counting of votes in West Bengal's Assembly election, following allegations from Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Mamata Banerjee.  The counting is scheduled for May 4th with TMC, BJP, CPI(M) and Congress all vying for power. The state saw high voter turnout in both phases of the election.

articles.title: Short covering fuels April rally, stock-specific action to continue in May - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Religare Broking's Ajit Mishra recommends buying Sun Pharmaceutical stock with a target of Rs 1,960 and a stop-loss at Rs 1,740.  Globe Capital Markets' Vipin Kumar suggests buying Adani Ports and SEZ futures in the Rs 1,640–1,620 range for a target of Rs 1,750–1,800.  JM Financial Services' Akshay Bhagwat recommends buying ONGC May futures at Rs 301–297 for a target of Rs 318–329.

articles.title: Punjab cops in a bind over transfer to ‘hard areas’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Establishment Division has transferred 10 police officers from Punjab to 'hard areas' in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, despite concerns about their age and health. The transfers were made under a policy that was supposed to rotate younger officers to these regions for one year, but the current list includes officers who were encadered from provincial service to the Police Service of Pakistan (PSP) with three to five years of service left. IGP Rao Abdul Kareem is raising concerns about this decision and plans to discuss it further with the Establishment Division.  The Establishment Division Secretary Nabeel Awan claims that the policy has been suspended at the request of the provinces, but officers are still being transferred under a 'stopgap arrangement' for one year.
