articles.title: KTR accuses Revanth Reddy govt. of betrayal to 14L students over fee reimbursement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS), criticized the Telangana Government for delaying fee reimbursement payments to students from marginalized communities.  He accused the government of dismantling the scheme and causing financial distress in the education sector. KTR demanded the immediate withdrawal of the order and an apology from the Chief Minister. He also highlighted the impact on over 2,500 educational institutions and warned of statewide protests if the issue is not addressed.

articles.title: Tallest underwater human stack formed; Andaman sets two Guinness World Records in 2 days - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andaman and Nicobar Islands officials achieved two Guinness World Records on May 2nd and 3rd, 2026.  The first record involved a 22.3-meter underwater human stack formed by fourteen people, including Lieutenant-Governor D.K. Joshi. The second record was the unfurling of the world's largest underwater national flag. These achievements are part of an initiative to promote the islands as a premier global diving destination.  Both records are expected to draw attention and boost tourism.

articles.title: India-Jamaica ties characterised by ‘continuity and change’: Jaishankar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, concluded his first visit to Jamaica on Sunday, highlighting the "continuity and change" in the bilateral relationship between the two countries.  He emphasized shared history, current cooperation, and a future with greater possibilities for both nations. Jaishankar also stressed the importance of building a deeper partnership that benefits their people and contributes to a more just world.

articles.title: Two held in separate fake number plate fraud cases in Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Traffic Police apprehended two individuals for using fake number plates on their motorcycles. Kolimi Yadaiah, an office boy, was found with a tampered registration plate on his Honda Activa and faces charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Motor Vehicles Act.  Syed Hussain Mehdi alias Izhan, a driver, was identified for using a fake number plate on his Honda DIO and will face similar charges. Both cases were detected through coordinated enforcement efforts.

articles.title: Independent journalism punished, compliance rewarded under current regime, says Kharge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government for its alleged attempts to suppress press freedom in India.  He stated that since 2014, India's position in the World Press Freedom Index has declined and the BJP is seeking to tighten its control over social media to silence dissent. Kharge also accused the government of weaponizing legal frameworks to intimidate journalists and noted a sharp rise in arrests and imprisonments of journalists. He highlighted several high-profile cases, including those of journalists murdered while reporting on corruption.  He urged for upholding democratic norms by those in power.

articles.title: Vijay holds discussion with TVK candidates at party headquarters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president C. Joseph Vijay met with party candidates and office-bearers on April 30, 2026, to discuss election procedures and victory prospects ahead of the May 4th Assembly elections. The meeting included N. Anand, K.A. Sengottaiyan, and Aadhav Arjuna.  TVK is entering the electoral fray for the first time after contesting in 233 seats, barring Edappadi where it extended support to an independent candidate.

articles.title: Saini urges Punjab OBCs to back BJP in Assembly polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini urged the OBC community in Punjab to unite and support the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections. He claimed that the party ensures equal representation and criticized the Aam Aadmi Party government's performance, citing disillusionment with poll promises.  Saini highlighted the community's contributions to nation-building and alleged they have been denied opportunities in Punjab. He urged them to support the BJP, referencing measures under Prime Minister Narendra Modi for OBC representation, reservation in education, and constitutional status for the OBC Commission.

articles.title: Three of family killed in accident in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A tragic road accident in Karnataka claimed the lives of three members of a family from Kannur, Kerala. Muneera, 45, her son-in-law Muneer, 30, and their three-and-a-half-year-old grandchild Mohis Zidan were killed when their car collided with a lorry near Gudlupet on Sunday (May 3, 2026). The family had been travelling to Ooty for a leisure trip after attending a wedding function in Thalassery.

articles.title: New courts inaugurated across Visakhapatnam district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Ravi Nath Tilhari and Justice Ravi Cheemalapati, of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh, inaugurated newly sanctioned courts in Visakhapatnam, Gajuwaka, Bheemunipatnam, and Narsipatnam on Sunday. The ceremonies were attended by senior judicial officers, bar association representatives, advocates, and police officials. These inaugurations are part of efforts to strengthen the judicial infrastructure of the district.

articles.title: J&K L-G galvanises massive public support against drug abuse, says neighbouring country using it for terrorism, radicalisation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha led a rally in Srinagar on Sunday, May 3, 2026, to support anti-drug initiatives. The event, attended by Speaker of the House, Cabinet Ministers, and other prominent figures, featured performances and raised awareness about substance abuse.  Sinha issued a warning against narco-terror networks and anti-national elements.

articles.title: Results of bypolls to two Assembly seats in Karnataka on May 4 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress government is hoping to retain both Davangere South and Bagalkot constituencies in upcoming bypolls, despite the BJP's confidence in winning both.  Samarth Mallikarjun, a Congress candidate in Davangere South, faces off against T. Srinivas Dasakariappa, while Umesh Meti, son of senior Congress leader H.Y. Meti, is contesting against Veeranna Charanthimath in Bagalkot.  The Congress is closely watching the Dalit Left communities' voting patterns and the impact of the SDPI on its Muslim voter base. The party will be evaluating the results in light of recent setbacks for the Congress, including the expulsion of MLCs Abdul Jabbar and Nazeer Ahmed.

articles.title: Karnataka leadership talks in Delhi unlikely in next few weeks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders are planning to meet with Mallikarjun Kharge, the party president, in Delhi next week to discuss Cabinet expansion. However, the leadership issue in Karnataka is unlikely to be resolved soon due to upcoming Rajya Sabha elections and a lack of timeline from Kharge.  With several seats falling vacant in the Legislative Council, the party is prioritizing these elections before discussing leadership changes.

articles.title: Ahead of Misri’s expected Nepal visit, Kathmandu expresses concern to India, China on Kailash yatra over Lipulekh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal expressed its opposition to the upcoming Kailash Manasarovar Yatra through the Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh region, reiterating that the area is part of its sovereign territory. India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) refuted these claims, stating they are not based on historical facts and have been a long-standing route for the pilgrimage since 1954.  The visit of Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri to Kathmandu was previously in focus due to uncertainties regarding meeting with the new Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, who has adopted a restrictive diplomatic protocol. The situation highlights ongoing tensions between India and Nepal over territorial disputes.

articles.title: Prohibitory orders imposed in Doda as AAP MLA returns home district after 8 months in jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doda District Magistrate Krishan Lal issued an order barring all assemblies in Doda for two months, citing concerns about potential demonstrations and public disorder. The decision follows the Jammu and Kashmir High Court's recent ruling to quash the detention of AAP legislator Mehraj Malik.  The order invokes Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) which limits gatherings to four or fewer individuals.

articles.title: 'Brown kids' comment was out of love: Michigan democrat El-Sayed says JD Vance is 'deeply evil' though - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a Democrat running for Senate in Michigan, sparked controversy with his comments about Vice President JD Vance's children.  El-Sayed stated that he made the remarks out of love to ensure Vance’s children and all immigrant children feel equally American. He criticized Vance for holding views that contradict his actions, claiming Vance uses morals as a tool for self-interest. El-Sayed emphasized the importance of addressing hypocrisy in politics and called for an America where all children are treated equally.

articles.title: Prohibitory orders imposed in Doda as AAP MLA returns home district after 8 months in jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doda District Magistrate Krishan Lal issued an order barring all assemblies in Doda for two months, citing concerns about potential demonstrations and public disorder. This decision follows the Jammu and Kashmir High Court's recent ruling to quash the detention of AAP's Doda legislator Mehraj Malik. The order invokes Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts gatherings exceeding four individuals.

articles.title: ‘Secretary of everything’: Marco Rubio DJs at wedding, seen wearing headphones and leaning over decks in viral video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, was captured on video DJing at a wedding. The footage, shared by Dan Scavino, White House deputy chief of staff, shows Rubio engaging with the music and interacting with guests.  While some praised the lighthearted moment, others criticized it given ongoing global tensions and policy challenges facing the administration. The viral clip has sparked discussions about Rubio's versatility and potential future political aspirations.

articles.title: French left-wing’s Melenchon says he will run for president in 2027 | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jean-Luc Melenchon, leader of the Unbowed party, announced his candidacy for the 2027 French presidential election. This marks his fourth bid for the presidency, following previous attempts in 2012, 2017, and 2022.  The race is wide open with President Macron unable to run due to term limits and Marine Le Pen facing a ban from politics. The election will be held in April, with a potential runoff two weeks later if no candidate secures a majority in the first round.

articles.title: Rayaraddi urges for Mallikarjun Kharge as Karnataka Chief Minister if Siddaramaiah is to be replaced - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Basavaraj Rayaraddi, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's economic adviser, stated that there is no need to change the Chief Minister and suggested Mallikarjun Kharge, AICC president, as a potential alternative if the party decides on a leadership change.  Rayaraddi met with Kharge last week and urged him to resolve the ongoing confusion surrounding the leadership in Karnataka.

articles.title: Healthcare federation welcomes relaxation of construction rules - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NATHEALTH, the Healthcare Federation of India, has welcomed the notification of the National Building Construction Standards (NBCS) 2026. The new rules will allow hospitals to establish intensive care units beyond 45 meters in height, subject to enhanced fire safety provisions. Sangita Reddy, president of NATHEALTH and joint managing director of Apollo Hospitals Group, praised the move as a significant step towards future-ready healthcare infrastructure in India.  Varun Khanna, Vice President of NATHEALTH and group managing director of Quality Care India Ltd., also highlighted the potential for unlocking capacity more efficiently and optimizing cost benefits for patients.

articles.title: More than 700 guests attend Sri Lanka Food Festival 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 700 guests attended the three-day Sri Lanka Food Festival 2026 at Green Meadows Resort in Chennai. Ganesanathan Geathiswaran, Deputy High Commissioner of Sri Lanka, organized the event which featured a culinary team from Cinnamon Grand Hotel, Colombo. The festival aimed to showcase the diverse culinary heritage of Sri Lanka and strengthen cultural ties between Sri Lanka and South India while promoting tourism, trade, and people-to-people connections.

articles.title: Counting of votes to be held at three centres in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector G. Priyanka, the District Election Officer, announced that vote counting for the Assembly elections held on April 9th in 14 constituencies will take place at three centers: Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat), Union Christian College, and Mar Athanasius College. Counting will begin at 8 a.m., with postal ballots being counted first followed by EVM votes. Initial trends are expected around 10 a.m.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: LDF, UDF keeping their fingers crossed in Kozhikode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Political fronts in Kozhikode are closely watching the election results on May 4th, as the district's outcome could significantly impact government formation in the state.  Key contests include Perambra, Beypore, Elathur, and Vadakara, where candidates from the Left Democratic Front (LDF) face off against those from the United Democratic Front (UDF). While the LDF has historically dominated the district, recent exit polls predict a less favorable outcome for the ruling front, with some internal discussions suggesting potential losses in key constituencies.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu | UPSC to shortlist DGP candidates on May 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) will hold an Empanelment Committee Meeting (ECM) in Delhi on May 11th to shortlist three qualified officers for the position of Director-General of Police/Head of the Police Force (DGP/HoPF) in the Tamil Nadu Police. The next DGP/HoPF, appointed by the newly elected government, will have a minimum two-year tenure as per Supreme Court guidelines.  The Chief Secretary and Home Secretary from Tamil Nadu will represent the state at the meeting which was previously postponed.

articles.title: Israel’s strategy of ‘permanent war’: A race against time? | Politics | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Political analyst Daniel Levy argues that Israel is pursuing a strategy of "permanent war" in the Middle East, aiming to dominate the region.  He claims this approach forces countries into two categories: dependent or on the verge of collapse. Levy, president of the US/Middle East Project, suggests Israel can leverage military operations against Iran and continued attacks on Lebanese and Palestinian populations to hinder a potential US-Iran deal.

articles.title: BJP closing seminaries with the help of J&K government: Mehbooba Mufti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mehbooba Mufti, former Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, criticized the Omar Abdullah government for its actions against religious institutions and Urdu language. She accused the government of silencing the closure of educational institutes like Siraj-ul-Uloom in Shopian, which provided education to underprivileged children, and Hazratbal seminary, both allegedly targeted by the BJP. Mufti also stated that the removal of Urdu from revenue department job qualifications represents an attack on Kashmir's identity and culture.

articles.title: Germany’s Merz downplays rift with Washington despite US troop drawdown | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz attempted to downplay tensions with the United States after Washington announced plans to reduce the number of American troops in Germany.  Merz stated that the troop withdrawal announcement was unrelated to his previous criticism of President Donald Trump's Iran strategy, emphasizing the importance of the US as a NATO partner. The decision comes amid escalating tensions between the two countries over the war in Iran and Trump's criticisms of European allies for their perceived reliance on the US.  US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 troops over the next year.

articles.title: ‘Kashmir will never be Pakistani and we will never become Pakistan’, says Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference, criticized separatist politics during a book release event, stating his party chose Mahatma Gandhi over slogans of "Nara-e-Takbeer Allahu Akbar" and emphasized Kashmir's commitment to India.  He also expressed regret for the 1990s exodus of Kashmiri Pandits and called for unity in diversity to overcome mistrust between Delhi and Kashmir. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, a separatist leader, praised Dr. Razdan's humanitarian service.

articles.title: 'First Indian person to suck at their job': SNL mocks Kash Patel with Aziz Ansari cameo - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saturday Night Live featured a surprise cameo by actor-comedian Aziz Ansari as FBI director Kash Patel in a satirical cold open. The sketch lampooned Patel’s leadership and public image, with Ansari's character making self-deprecating jokes about his incompetence and referencing ongoing reports of misconduct.  The skit also touched on political rumors surrounding Patel's relationship with US President Donald Trump and included a reference to the recent DC shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner.

articles.title: Arjun Ayanki among six detained ahead of poll results - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kothamangalam police detained six individuals, including Arjun Ayanki, a suspect in eight cases, from a resort near Kariyilappara on Sunday. The Ernakulam rural police initiated "Operation Steel Bird" to target habitual offenders and suspect the group was planning new criminal activities.  The detainees are accused of highway robbery, attempted murder, drug trafficking, kidnapping for ransom, gold smuggling, and financial crimes.

articles.title: No visa hold for US doctors from travel-ban countries: Major U-turn by Trump amid physician crisis - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration quietly lifted a travel ban on 39 countries, allowing doctors from those nations to continue working in the United States. The Department of Homeland Security updated its website late last week, stating that applications associated with medical physicians will continue processing.  However, there remains uncertainty about whether doctors from these countries can enter the US from outside the country. This change comes after a healthcare crisis was sparked by the travel ban's impact on foreign doctors who were placed on administrative leave and detained at checkpoints.

articles.title: Father’s bid to scare son with petrol backfires, both suffer burns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 45-year-old construction laborer, Anand, poured petrol on his 19-year-old son, Mallikarjun, in an attempt to frighten him during a heated argument. The incident occurred after Anand was upset that his son had taken his bike without informing him. Both sustained burn injuries and were rushed to hospital where they are receiving treatment.  The Kumaraswamy Layout Police Station has registered a case of attempted murder against Anand.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: Women make up over 80% of the additional voters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, women voters accounted for over 80% of the additional voters, a record high. This year, approximately 20.8 lakh more women voted compared to 2021, with a total increase of around 25.3 lakh votes.  While this represents the highest percentage of women in voter turnout, it is third in terms of absolute numbers behind 2016 and 2011. The growth rate for women voters was almost 9% compared to last year's election. Political parties have implemented various schemes to attract women voters, but the growth rate remained subdued.

articles.title: Deepender campaigns for local polls, accuses BJP of corruption in Haryana municipal bodies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress MP Deepender Hooda campaigned in Panchkula for the party's mayoral candidate, Sudha Bhardwaj, and ward candidates. Hooda criticized the BJP government's performance, alleging corruption within municipal corporations and a lack of progress despite their "triple-engine" government. He accused the BJP of looting the people through corruption and highlighted specific scams in various corporations.

articles.title: Maharashtra Cong. to hit streets to highlight demands of farmers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress will hold a protest march in Buldhana district of Maharashtra on Monday against BJP policies they say are harming farmers. The party, citing high farmer suicide rates in the state, demands loan waivers, land record clearing, MSP guarantees, fixed crop prices, and other agricultural reforms.  The protest is led by Harshwardhan Sapkal, the state Congress president.

articles.title: High cost of five kg FTL cylinders keeps new consumers away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: LPG distributors are only providing five kg free trade LPG (FTL) cylinders to specific groups, citing instructions from State-run oil marketing companies (OMCs). This has led to consumer frustration as the cost of the five kg cylinder is high and doesn't last long enough for many needs.  The situation is particularly challenging for businesses like PGs and hostels who rely on gas for cooking, forcing them to turn to the black market for cylinders at inflated prices. Vidya Mahambare, a professor of economics from Great Lakes Institute of Management, Chennai, believes this will impact inflation rates as energy prices continue to rise.

articles.title: Inside Lanzarote: The island of 100 volcanoes, where heat still rises from the ground, and white villages shine over black lava | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lanzarote, one of the Canary Islands, is known for its unique volcanic landscape.  The island features over 100 volcanic formations that have shaped its surface and created a stark contrast between black lava fields and bright white villages. César Manrique, a painter, sculptor, and architect, played a significant role in shaping Lanzarote's modern appearance by encouraging the integration of architecture with the natural environment.  Visitors to Lanzarote report experiencing a sense of peacefulness and quietness that is both unexpected and deeply appealing.

articles.title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Lipulekh Pass - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India responded to Nepal's objection to the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra passing through Lipulekh Pass, stating that such territorial claims are "untenable." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified that Lipulekh Pass has been a long-standing route for the pilgrimage since 1954 and that India remains open to dialogue with Nepal on all bilateral issues.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Mahatma Gandhi: “The greatness of a nation and its moral progress can be judged by the way its animals are treated.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mahatma Gandhi's quote, "The greatness of a nation and its moral progress can be judged by the way its animals are treated," highlights the importance of considering animal welfare as a reflection of societal values.  This view emphasizes that moral progress extends beyond human well-being to encompass care for all living beings. Laws protecting animals from abuse and international efforts to combat illegal wildlife trade demonstrate growing awareness and commitment to ethical treatment of animals. While challenges remain, such as urbanization and industrial activities impacting animal welfare, ongoing efforts to promote humane practices and educate individuals about their impact on the environment are crucial in achieving a more sustainable future for all living creatures.

articles.title: BC communities hopeful of political reservations in local body elections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, a retired IAS officer, led the one-man commission to North Andhra districts to assess the need for political reservations for backward classes. The commission has been tasked with ensuring equal representation for all communities based on their population and is currently gathering data from various communities.  The Commission's visit has been met with hope by many communities who have long lacked political opportunities, including the Nagavamsam, Yadava, Nagaralu, Reddika, Sondi, Kummari, Rajaka, Nayi Brahmin, Vaddera, Gowda and others.

articles.title: 2 men, including social activist, killed in separate attacks in KP's Bajaur - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Two people were killed in separate attacks in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.  Malik Ziaur Rehman, a social activist, was shot and killed near his residence in Salarzai tehsil.  He was taken to the hospital but died from his injuries. In another incident, Sayed Door Khan was killed by an improvised explosive device blast in Asil Targaoo area. An investigation is underway into both incidents.

articles.title: Indian-origin banker Viswas Raghavan to receive $52 million from Citigroup after leaving JPMorgan amid ‘bullying’ allegations - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Viswas “Vis” Raghavan, an Indian-origin banker, has joined Citigroup as head of banking after a compensation package worth $52 million was offered following his departure from JPMorgan Chase.  The hiring has drawn scrutiny due to reports alleging that he bullied colleagues during his time at JPMorgan, with complaints stemming from harsh language and inappropriate remarks. Despite these concerns, Citigroup defended its decision, stating the recruitment process was thorough and not rushed. Raghavan has a strong reputation as a dealmaker, having risen through the ranks at JPMorgan for over two decades.

articles.title: Electoral debuts in Tamil Nadu’s past Assembly elections tell a mixed story of breakthroughs, missed chances - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The arrival of actor-politician C. Joseph Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections has sparked anticipation about its potential to challenge the Dravidian duopoly.  Historical analysis reveals that several political parties have made their debut in Tamil Nadu's Assembly elections, with varying levels of success. The DMK's entry in 1957 marked a turning point for the party, leading to its eventual rise to power. Other notable debuts include the AIADMK (founded by M.G. Ramachandran), the PMK (formed by S. Ramadoss), and the TMC(M) (led by G.K. Moopanar).  The emergence of new parties like the Naam Tamilar Katchi, Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam, and Makkal Needhi Maiam has further diversified the political landscape, but none have yet achieved significant electoral success.

articles.title: 'Every candidate with an Indian last name....': What happened at local election in Frisco, Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Social media users celebrated the election results in Frisco, Texas, where no Indian-origin candidates won positions on the city council. Indian-Americans who ran for City Council Place 5 and 6 were defeated by Laura Rummel and Brittany Colberg respectively. Some social media posts attributed the outcome to a lack of voter participation among the Indian community, while others expressed concerns about the impact of immigration policies on Frisco's demographics.  However, it is important to note that Indian-origin individuals cannot vote in US elections while holding non-citizen visas.

articles.title: Naidu’s industrial push for Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nara Chandrababu Naidu, the former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, spearheaded efforts to establish Hyderabad as a major IT hub in the 1990s.  His initiative led to Microsoft establishing a global R&D center in the city in 1998, attracting other tech giants like Oracle, Google, Amazon, and Cognizant. This success has been a cornerstone of Naidu's political campaigns since then.

articles.title: Peshawar Zalmi beat Hyderabad Kingsmen by 5 wickets, lift PSL trophy a second time - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Aaron Hardie's spectacular all-round performance led Peshawar Zalmi to their second HBL Pakistan Super League title victory, defeating the Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in Lahore.  After opting to bowl first, Zalmi achieved the 130-run target in the 16th over of the second innings, becoming the third team to win the PSL trophy more than once. Hardie, who took four wickets and scored an unbeaten 56 runs off 39 deliveries, was instrumental in Zalmi's victory.  Peshawar Zalmi had reached the final with eight victories and after losing just one match, sealing the top spot in the points table.

articles.title: Scuba team unfurls mega national flag beneath deep sea, enters into Guinness World Records - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharath R. Ashok, a Bengaluru-based adventure sports professional, led a team of 200 scuba divers in successfully unfurling a massive national flag beneath the sea at Swaraj Dweep in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Guinness World Records recognized this extraordinary feat, with Lieutenant Governor Admiral D.K. Joshi presenting the team with an official certificate.  The mission was organized by the Andaman and Nicobar administration and the Indian defense forces, showcasing Mr. Ashok's diverse training in adventure sports that enabled him to successfully complete the underwater challenge.

articles.title: AAP leader alleges threat to life from Byrathi Basavaraj - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sathyavani, president of the AAP’s Vignana Nagar ward, filed a complaint with the Bengaluru Police Commissioner alleging threats to her life and vandalism of her car by local BJP leaders, including Byrathi Basavaraj, an MLA.  She claims these actions are politically motivated as she prepares for upcoming elections. The police registered a case after intervention from the Karnataka Lokayukta.

articles.title: Five arrested in Goshamahal for running an illegal LPG refilling racket - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Goshamahal police arrested five individuals for allegedly refilling domestic LPG cylinders into smaller and commercial ones. The suspects, identified as Alle Sai Kumar, Dalmova Vineeth Kumar, D. Praveen Kumar, Makadia Ameet Kumar, and Pusa Ganesh, were apprehended after a customer reported an underweight gas cylinder.  The case is being investigated under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Essential Commodities Act, and the Explosives Act.

articles.title: Nine booked for social boycott in Belagavi village - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police have registered a case against nine individuals in Kondaskoppa village, Belagavi district, for imposing a social boycott on the family of Renuka Sambrekar. The complaint alleges that the accused, including Mallappa Sambrekar and Vitthal Sambrekar, enforced a boycott after Narasoba Sambrekar, a priest at the Sri Beereshwar temple, had disagreements with other priests over worshiping the deity.  The Tahsildar and police officers visited the village to mediate but tensions remained high, prompting the registration of a case under BNS sections for unlawful intimidation and social ostracism.

articles.title: West Bengal waits with bated breath for May 4 Assembly election results - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Election Commission of India (ECI) will begin counting votes for the West Bengal Assembly elections on Monday, May 4, 2026. The results are expected after repolling for the Falta Assembly seat in South 24 Parganas district on May 21.  The Trinamool Congress, led by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, is seeking a fourth consecutive term while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) aims to defeat them with promises of "paribortan". The Communist Party of India (Marxist)-led Left front and the Congress have also contested the elections. Security arrangements have been increased due to concerns about irregularities by the Trinamool Congress, which has already begun claiming victory.

articles.title: The Hindu EducationPlus fair: ‘Career counselling inspires confidence, eases course anxiety’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shivakumaraiah, joint secretary of the Sree Siddaganga Education Society, emphasized the importance of career counseling, highlighting that students should identify their passions and choose courses based on their interests rather than following trends.  Shalini M. from Siddaganga Medical College & Research Institute discussed the rewarding nature of a medical career, emphasizing the significance of diligence and consistent study in securing an MBBS seat. Nagashettappa Biradar, principal of R.V. Institute of Technology and Management, Bengaluru, stressed that students should focus on acquiring skills rather than relying on brand names when choosing engineering colleges.  Mandhara Bilagi P. from Christ (Deemed-to-be-University) highlighted the diverse career options available in humanities courses, including research, education, and journalism.

articles.title: Autorickshaw driver held in Vellore over murder charges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 32-year-old autorickshaw driver, S. Mani, was arrested for the murder of a mason, B. Gajendran, in Vellore, India. The incident occurred after an argument between Mani and S. Balaji, an AIADMK functionary, on April 23rd.  Gajendran was injured during the altercation and later died at the hospital. Police have registered a case and are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Summer rain batters Thrissur; power, water supply hit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A sudden summer squall caused widespread damage across the Thrissur district on Saturday evening. Strong winds uprooted trees, snapped power lines and poles, and triggered power outages that affected water supply in several local bodies.  The worst-hit areas were in the Irinjalakuda region, where transformers and electricity posts were damaged, leading to disruptions in road traffic and festival events at the Koodalmanikyam temple. Officials are assessing the full extent of the damage, but no casualties have been reported.

articles.title: Brixton drive-by shooting leaves four injured, one in critical condition - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Four individuals were wounded by gunfire from a moving car in Brixton, south London, early Saturday morning. The incident occurred around 01:15 BST on Coldharbour Lane and prompted an intense police investigation. The Metropolitan Police, along with the London Ambulance Service, responded to the scene where three men aged 21, 47, and 70 were treated for non-life-threatening injuries, while a 25-year-old man is fighting for his life in hospital. Security personnel secured the area and collected witness statements as investigators examine surveillance footage and search for suspects.

articles.title: Four-tier security arrangements in place at vote counting centres in Vellore, nearby districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Election Officers (DEOs) in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts have implemented a four-tier security arrangement for vote counting centers on May 4.  Sealed electronic voting machines (EVMs) and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) units are stored in strong rooms guarded by police personnel around the clock. Routine inspections of these strong rooms are conducted daily by DEOs, and adequate parking arrangements have been made for election staff and police. A control room with a helpline number is also operational at the DEO office to address any election-related incidents.

articles.title: Nepal stirs row with India, objects to Kailash Mansarovar yatra via Lipulekh; MEA replies - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal objected to India and China's plan to use the Lipulekh Pass for the upcoming Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, claiming it passes through their territory. The Nepalese government reiterated its long-standing position on the disputed region, stating that Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh, and Kalapani are integral parts of Nepal based on the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli.  The Nepalese Ministry of Foreign Affairs has formally informed both India and China of its stance and urged them to refrain from any activities in the area. India, however, maintains that the Lipulekh Pass route has been used for decades and rejects Nepal's territorial claims. The Indian External Affairs Ministry stated that it remains open to dialogue with Nepal on outstanding boundary issues.

articles.title: Investigators say Trump assassination suspect shot officer at press gala | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, the suspect accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump, has been charged with three federal crimes, including attempted assassination.  US Attorney Jeanine Pirro confirmed that Allen's bullet struck a Secret Service agent at the White House correspondents’ dinner last month. The agent was wearing a ballistic vest and survived the attack. Allen had traveled to Washington D.C. from Los Angeles before the event, where he attempted to enter the hotel with a shotgun, pistol, and knives.  The shooting has been widely condemned as a politically motivated act.

articles.title: Green candidate seen canvassing in London after arrest over alleged antisemitism | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sabine Mairey, a Green candidate in Lambeth, south London, was arrested for alleged antisemitic social media posts.  She was seen canvassing alongside other party members despite being under investigation by the Green party. The incident prompted Labour to criticize the leadership of Zack Polanski, who is Jewish and has stated that tackling antisemitism is crucial. While Polanski claims this isn't a unique problem within his party, he has disowned candidates involved in such incidents.

articles.title: Iran says US has responded to its latest peace proposal
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson confirmed the US has responded to its latest peace proposal, which was delivered via Pakistan. The 14-point plan requested the withdrawal of US forces from near Iranian borders and an end to the naval blockade of Iranian ports. President Donald Trump stated he would review the proposal but expressed skepticism about its acceptance.  Trump also indicated a possibility of renewed military strikes against targets in Iran, while Congress members are calling for a reduction in US involvement.

articles.title: Hazrat Khwaja Bande Nawaz Urs gets under way in Kalaburagi - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Hazrat Khwaja Bande Nawaz Gesu Daraz
articles.rephrased_article: The 622nd Urs-e-Shareef of the revered Sufi saint Hazrat Khwaja Bande Nawaz Gesu Daraz commenced in Kalaburagi, drawing thousands of devotees. The four-day observance commemorates the life and legacy of the saint who dedicated himself to fostering unity and harmony among communities.  Devotees participated in special prayers, rituals, and processions, including a solemn sandal paste procession that culminated at the saint's tomb. Syed Mohammad Ali Al-Hussaini, Sajjada Nasheen of the Dargah Shareef, presided over the events. The celebrations highlight the saint's teachings on love, kindness, inclusiveness, and peaceful coexistence.

articles.title: Velankanni priest says Basilica was not informed about TVK chief Vijay’s plan to visit shrine on May 2 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The administration of the Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health expressed concern over misinformation circulating regarding prayers at the shrine and criticized the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) for raising slogans inside the church.  Rev. Fr. Arputharaj, parish priest, stated that despite reports of TVK leader Vijay's planned visit, no official communication was received. The incident caused a brief commotion and prompted the administration to address the district administration and police regarding future prevention.

articles.title: Landowner rebuts HYDRAA commissioner, alleges rule violations in Bagh Amberpet land dispute - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Aedla Sudhaker Reddy, a landowner, issued a rebuttal to A.V. Ranganath, the Commissioner of Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), who accused him of violating service conduct rules and attempting to malign his reputation over a disputed land parcel.  Reddy claims the allegations are false and that the matter is sub judice in multiple courts. He argues that Ranganath violated rules by discussing evidence related to ongoing cases publicly and refutes claims about a High Court directive for a title suit. Reddy maintains he has settled possession of the land and seeks protection from government agencies, including HYDRAA.

articles.title: Walk-through survey nearing completion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SUEZ, the French company responsible for water distribution in Kochi, is conducting a walk-through survey of the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) pipeline network within the city limits. The survey, which involves ground-level inspection without excavation, is nearing completion and will be followed by door-to-door surveys in Kaloor and Karuvelippady. Consumer surveys have been delayed due to elections but are now being expedited.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Political hotspots under tight surveillance as Ernakulam awaits poll verdict - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ernakulam rural police have implemented heightened security measures for the Assembly election result day, with over 1,300 personnel deployed across 15 locations identified as sensitive due to reported incidents during the campaign. District Police Chief (Ernakulam rural) K.S. Sudarshan stated that these locations include areas like Chengamanad and Kunnathunad, where additional surveillance will be in place at points likely to witness gatherings of party supporters.  The police have also deployed 2,000 personnel within the city limits, including strike forces and additional mobile patrols. The Election Commission of India (ECI) guidelines will guide the three-layer security plan at Cochin University of Science and Technology, where votes for six constituencies will be counted.

articles.title: NEET-UG 2026 held across 551 cities in India, 14 abroad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan visited the National Testing Agency (NTA) headquarters on Sunday, May 3, 2026, to assess the readiness for the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The examination was conducted across 551 cities in India and 14 cities abroad, with nearly 23 lakh registered candidates taking the test under strict protocols.  The NTA oversaw the logistics, coordination, and monitoring systems for a seamless exam process.

articles.title: Jana Chaitanya Vedika urges Centre, State govt. to implement BC reservations in MLC, MP seats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jana Chaitanya Vedika-AP State President Bankuru Joginaidu urged Union and State governments to implement political reservations for backward classes in Parliament and Legislative Assemblies.  He presented a memorandum to Vizianagaram MP Kalisetti Appala Naidu, who promised to bring the issue to both governments' attention. Naidu also advocated extending reservation benefits to all 145 communities classified into five categories, arguing that only a few dominant communities currently benefit from these reservations in local body elections.

articles.title: Nishant launches Sadbhav Yatra from Bihar’s West Champaran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nishant Kumar, son of former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, launched his 'Sadbhav Yatra' from Bagaha, following in his father's footsteps.  The young leader was accompanied by Umesh Singh Kushwaha, the Bihar JD(U) president, and Shrawon Kumar, the JD-(U) Legislature Party leader. He addressed supporters along the route, emphasizing harmony and development for Bihar. The journey is seen as a significant step in Nishant Kumar's political career, potentially bolstering the JD(U) after the resignation of his father.

articles.title: River pollution in Moray leads to fish and bird deaths in environmental disaster - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A chemical compound has polluted the River Spey in Knockando Burn, killing fish, eels, and birds. The Scottish Environment Protection Agency is investigating the source of the contamination, which experts believe originated from industrial sources.  The incident is considered a major environmental disaster with significant economic repercussions for local anglers and businesses reliant on fishing. The impact will take years to recover, disrupting breeding cycles and harming the ecosystem's health.

articles.title: Nishant launches Sadbhav Yatra from Bihar’s West Champaran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nishant Kumar, son of former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, launched his "Sadbhav Yatra" from Bagaha in West Champaran district on Sunday, May 3, 2026.  The young leader was accompanied by Umesh Singh Kushwaha, the Bihar JD(U) president and Shrawon Kumar, the JD(U) Legislature Party leader. The yatra is seen as a significant step in Nishant Kumar's political career, following his father's long-held tradition of launching all yatras from Champaran.  He addressed supporters along the route, emphasizing the importance of harmony and development for Bihar.

articles.title: '15,000 cases in limbo': US government shuts down San Francisco immigration court four months ahead of schedule - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US government shut down the immigration court at 100 Montgomery Street in San Francisco eight months early, leaving thousands of cases in limbo. The closure, which ended operations on September 4th, 2026, was attributed to administrative reasons by the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) and will relocate court operations to the Concord Immigration Court. Legal experts believe the decision may have been influenced by asylum approval rates and the dismissal of several immigration judges.  The relocation has raised concerns about further delays as the Concord court already faces a heavy caseload.

articles.title: All set for counting; ECI promises transparency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced its commitment to ensuring transparency, security, and efficiency during the counting of votes for upcoming Assembly elections in five states and bye-elections in seven constituencies. The ECI deployed additional observers in West Bengal to ensure a secure environment. Political parties are closely monitoring the preparations.

articles.title: Trump’s disapproval rating hits record high, new poll shows | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll reveals that Donald Trump's disapproval rating has reached a record high of 62%, the worst of his two terms in office.  The president's approval ratings are particularly low on issues like the cost of living and the Iran war, with only 37% approving overall. This weak performance puts the Republican party’s wafer-thin House majority at risk as Democrats gain ground among registered voters and those who are certain to vote. The poll also found that a majority of Americans believe Trump is not honest or trustworthy.

articles.title: Preparations in full swing in Bagalkot for counting of bypoll votes today - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Officials are preparing for the counting of votes in the Bagalkot Assembly bypoll, scheduled to begin at 8 a.m. on Monday. The counting will take place at the University of Horticultural Sciences with 23 rounds of counting and arrangements for postal ballots and voters over 80 years old.  The election is considered a contest between Umesh Meti, son of the late MLA H.Y. Meti, and Veeranna (Veerabhadrayya) Charantimath of the BJP. The main contenders are expected to benefit from the sympathy factor surrounding the death of H.Y. Meti and the political campaigning by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi, and BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra.

articles.title: Sringeri Assembly seat recount: Congress MLA slips to second position as his vote tally reduces by 255 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the Karnataka Assembly election re-count for Sringeri constituency, T. D. Raje Gowda of the Congress lost to defeated BJP candidate D. N. Jeevaraj.  The Returning Officer did not declare a winner after the verification and recounting process, which reduced Raje Gowda's tally by 255 votes. The Returning Officer submitted the report to the Election Commission of India as per court instructions. Jeevaraj claimed victory based on increased votes, while Raje Gowda alleged tampering with ballots.  The Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar stated that they would fight in court and called it a conspiracy against democracy. The Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok demanded that Jeevaraj be declared the winner.

articles.title: Passenger from Sharjah detained after he opens emergency exit door, runs on tarmac after landing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An Air Arabia flight from Sharjah landed in Chennai on Sunday morning, but the passenger who opened the emergency exit door and ran on the tarmac caused a diversion to Bengaluru. The incident prompted an investigation by the Airports Authority of India, with the passenger identified as Mohamed Najmudeen Sherif, who claimed he feared for his safety.  He was detained at the airport and later found to be under mental stress.

articles.title: PD Act invoked against two bootleggers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. A. Siri, District Collector of the district, issued Preventive Detention orders against two habitual Illicitly Distilled (ID) liquor offenders on Sunday, May 3, 2026. The orders were executed by inspectors from Pathikonda and Kurnool Excise Stations, with the accused lodged in the Central Prison for Men in Kadapa.  The Excise Department will provide alternative livelihood opportunities to those who have given up criminal activities through coordination with various government welfare departments.

articles.title: 'Jesus Christ is not THE son of God': Hindu Americans defend Vivek Ramaswamy as old clip resurfaces - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vivek Ramaswamy, facing criticism for an old video where he explained his Hindu faith, has been defended by the Hindu American Foundation and other community leaders.  They argue that his views on Jesus are not meant to be a challenge to Christianity but rather a reflection of his personal understanding of divinity. The Indian American Advocacy Council also condemned the online harassment directed at Ramaswamy, emphasizing the importance of religious freedom and inclusivity in American politics.

articles.title: TB dam crest gates repairs nearing completion, inauguration likely by May 15, says Shivakumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister of Karnataka, announced that the extensive repair and replacement of all 33 crest gates at the Tungabhadra Dam are nearing completion, with a target inauguration date set for May 15th.  The project, considered a technical marvel, has been completed ahead of schedule and will enhance the dam's lifespan by another 50 years. The state government is collaborating with Andhra Pradesh on the project, which aims to support agriculture in several regions across Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.

articles.title: Spirit pilot gets ‘overwhelming’ send-off from Southwest after his final flight is cancelled | Air transport | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Spirit Airlines pilot Jon Jackson was unexpectedly given a retirement send-off after his scheduled final flight was canceled due to the airline's sudden collapse.  After boarding a Southwest flight, Jackson was greeted with a water cannon salute and cheers upon landing in Baltimore. Southwest Airlines staff organized the surprise celebration, expressing their admiration for Jackson and recognizing his years of service. The airline's closure followed struggles with creditors and funding after multiple bankruptcy filings.

articles.title: 'It’s like smoking hash': Tucker Carlson says Trump uses a 'spell' to make people around him more compliant - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tucker Carlson, a conservative broadcaster, claimed that Donald Trump possesses a "supernatural component" that influences those around him, making them more compliant.  Carlson described his experience with the president as being in a "dreamland," suggesting a hypnotic effect on his advisors and associates. He acknowledged uncertainty about the cause of this influence but believes it is real. Carlson's comments come amidst a deterioration in his relationship with Trump, who responded with insults on Truth Social.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi's Nicobar visit: Parliamentary forum discussion needed for Great Nicobar projects, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress criticized the government's handling of the Great Nicobar Island Development Project, stating that it lacked due diligence and had failed to address concerns raised by members. The party called for a parliamentary review of the project, arguing that the government issued a clarification after Rahul Gandhi’s visit was deemed “hugely impactful”.

articles.title: South African police officer lowered into crocodile-infested river to recover human remains
articles.rephrased_article: Police in South Africa recovered human remains from a crocodile after an officer was lowered into the Komati River to search for a missing businessman. The reptile, suspected of eating the man, had already been killed by police but the operation was still considered "highly dangerous." DNA tests will confirm if the remains belong to the missing man.  The authorities used drones and helicopters in the search mission and discovered the crocodile's stomach contained human body parts along with six different types of shoes.

articles.title: Todd Blanche says case against Comey based on more than just Instagram post | James Comey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Todd Blanche, acting US attorney general, defended the two-count felony indictment against former FBI head James Comey, arguing that it was based on more than just an Instagram post. The indictment charges Comey in connection with a picture he posted last May that contained the phrase "86 47," which some interpreted as a threat against President Trump.  Legal experts, including Thom Tillis and Adam Schiff, have expressed skepticism about the case, arguing that it is politically motivated. Blanche insisted that there was more evidence beyond the picture to prove Comey's guilt and that a public trial would reveal all of the government's evidence.

articles.title: Change in plans: Bengaluru’s IT Corridor to be white-topped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited (B-SMILE) has revised its plans for the Outer Ring Road (ORR) in east Bengaluru, opting to white-top the main carriageway instead of black-topping using stone matrix asphalting. The project, valued at ₹307 crore, will see a 17.1 km stretch between Silk Board Junction and K.R. Pura Metro Station undergo a complete facelift.  The SPV has also removed strict quality control measures from the tender process.

articles.title: Brace up for a fuel price hike after election results, KPCC spokesperson warns public - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Lakshman, spokesperson for the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee, warned that the Centre may increase fuel prices after the results of recent state elections are announced. He alleged that the BJP-led government is planning to raise domestic LPG cylinder, diesel and petrol prices following the election results.

articles.title: TDP MLC urges officials to join their children in government schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vepada Chiranjeevi Rao, a Telugu Desam Party MLC, praised Andhra Pradesh government schools' performance in the recent SSC Class 10 Board exams.  He encouraged officials and employees to join their children in government schools, along with MLAs Aditi Vijaya Lakshmi and Gade Srinivasulu Naidu, who also felicitated students and teachers for achieving good results. Sixty students from six districts in North Andhra were promised financial assistance at the event.

articles.title: Ramagundam integrated coal mine project with 315 MT reserves gets green nod - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) has received a positive recommendation from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) for its innovative Ramagundam Coal Mine Project. The project, designed to achieve SCCL's goal of 60 million tonnes of coal production this year, is expected to have an annual capacity of 21 million tonnes per annum.  The MoEF&CC is expected to grant the environmental clearance within the next ten days.

articles.title: Vijay’s Velankanni visit cancelled; visuals of supporters chanting ‘TVK’ inside Basilica go viral - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president and actor Vijay cancelled his planned visit to Velankanni, Nagapattinam district on Saturday.  A large number of TVK cadre gathered at the Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health Church, chanting slogans in anticipation of his arrival before dispersing after the cancellation was announced.

articles.title: Civil society signatories demand that SIR be stopped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 300 individuals, including Justice B. Sudarshan Reddy, Prakash Raj, and Teesta Setalvad, have signed a joint statement demanding the halt of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) electoral roll revision process. The signatories argue that SIR is an exclusionary, undemocratic, and unscientific process that has deprived nearly 6 crore voters of their right to vote in 10 states and three Union Territories. They also criticize the ECI for its alleged bias and lack of transparency, calling for a thorough review of the process and the replacement of the ECI with an impartial body. The statement concludes by warning the ECI against manipulating election results and threatening nationwide resistance if it continues to disregard the Constitution and democracy.

articles.title: New short Haj package likely to be popular among working pilgrims - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Haj Committee has introduced a new "short Haj" package for pilgrims with limited time, reducing the pilgrimage duration to 20 days from the usual 40-45 days. The first batch of pilgrims from Kerala will depart on May 17th under government supervision, with three flights transporting around 1,000 individuals. State Haj Committee Chairman Hussain Saqafi Chullikkode stated that the duration could be further reduced in future based on demand.

articles.title: New short Haj package likely to be popular among working pilgrims - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Haj Committee has introduced a new "short Haj" package for pilgrims with limited time, reducing the pilgrimage duration to 20 days from the usual 40-45 days. The first batch of Kerala pilgrims will depart on May 17th under government supervision, with three flights transporting around 1,000 individuals.  The committee expects this option to gain popularity among working professionals and others with limited time constraints. "The duration could be reduced further in the coming years," said State Haj Committee Chairman Hussain Saqafi Chullikkode.

articles.title: ‘No one better to fight for us than one of us’: Minnesota flight attendant runs for Congress | Minnesota | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kaela Berg, a former union leader and flight attendant, is running for Congress in Minnesota's second district.  She cites her experience as an organizer and labor leader, including serving as vice-president of her union, Endeavor Association of Flight Attendants, as motivation for entering the race. Berg aims to address affordability issues like healthcare costs and rising living expenses, advocating for policies such as universal healthcare and a halt to Trump's tariffs.  She faces a competitive Democratic primary with fellow candidates Matt Klein and Matt Little.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls: Ban on firecracker use in Palakkad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Palakkad District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty imposed a ban on the sale and use of firecrackers in the district from Monday (May 4) to Tuesday (May 5) due to the announcement of election results.  All firecracker manufacturing and sales units will be closed during this period, and the bursting of firecrackers is prohibited for victory celebrations. Tahsildars and inspectors have been instructed to enforce the ban within their jurisdictions.

articles.title: Telangana sees more road accidents, fewer deaths in first quadrimester of 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana saw a mixed trend in road accident data for the first four months of 2026, with a rise in crashes and a decrease in fatalities.  While accidents increased by 2.5% to 9,313 between January and April this year, deaths fell to 2,363, marking a 15.3% decline from 2025. The Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the ‘Arrive Alive’ campaign in January to promote responsible driving and reduce accidents and fatalities.  The state attributed the reduction in deaths to a comprehensive road safety action plan that includes stricter enforcement of traffic rules, checks on overloading, action against unfit and illegally modified vehicles, and improvements in post-crash response.

articles.title: 2 men, including social activist, killed in separate attacked in KP's Bajaur - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Two people were killed in separate attacks in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.  Malik Ziaur Rehman, a social activist, was shot and killed near his residence in Salarzai tehsil. He later died at the hospital. In another incident, Sayed Door Khan was fatally injured by an IED blast in Asil Targaoo area and succumbed to his injuries at the hospital. The police are investigating both incidents.

articles.title: The ‘Oscars for political nerds’ or a threat to democracy? Grab a ticket, it’s Canberra’s budget fundraiser season | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: Labor, Liberal, Coalition, Angus Taylor, David Pocock
articles.rephrased_article: Labor, Liberal and Coalition parties are hosting fundraising dinners and events for their supporters ahead of the federal budget.  The Federal Labor Business Forum (FLBF) will host a more casual networking function, while the Liberal party is holding a high-priced dinner with the opposition leader, Angus Taylor. The Cook Endeavour Forum and MP Simon Kennedy are hosting an exclusive event for shadow ministers and MPs.  Independent senator David Pocock criticizes these events as "cash-for-access" that distort public policymaking and harm democracy.

articles.title: Telangana sees more road accidents, fewer deaths in first quadrimester of 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana saw a mixed trend in road accident data for the first four months of 2026, with an increase in accidents and a decrease in fatalities.  The number of crashes rose by 2.5% to 9,313 between January and April this year, while deaths fell to 2,363, marking a 15.3% decline from 2025. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the ‘Arrive Alive’ campaign in January to promote responsible driving and reduce both accidents and fatalities.  The state's efforts have been attributed to stricter enforcement of traffic rules, checks on overloading, action against unfit vehicles, and improvements in post-crash response.

articles.title: 'You don't need a salary': Immigration attorney says many F-1 students don't understand how OPT works - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An immigration attorney, John Khosravi, highlighted a case where a student visa holder lost their opportunity to work through the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program due to a lack of understanding about its full scope. Khosravi emphasized that students can utilize OPT even if they don't find traditional employment and can start and run businesses during their first year, potentially leading to long-term US residency through an E-2 investor visa.  He stressed the importance of knowing OPT rules to avoid losing potential opportunities.

articles.title: Was the Iran war the final blow in the collapse of Spirit Airlines? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Spirit Airlines, a budget airline in the United States, has ceased operations after failing to secure a bailout from the Trump administration. The company cited soaring aviation fuel prices, stemming from the US-Israel war on Iran, as the final blow to its financial struggles.  The airline's parent company announced an orderly wind-down of operations, cancelling all flights and leaving 17,000 employees unemployed. Experts believe that while geopolitical instability may not have been the sole cause of Spirit's collapse, it accelerated pre-existing weaknesses in the company's business model.

articles.title: Man says he got job responses after changing surname to ‘Singh’ on resume: ‘Three emails in 24 hours’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A viral video has sparked controversy in the United States, with a White job seeker claiming that changing his surname to an Indian one on job applications led to increased responses from employers. The man's experiment, which involved creating a fake resume with a different last name and email address, was shared widely online amidst ongoing debates about hiring bias and immigration policies.  Social media users expressed varied opinions, some advocating for legal action against companies accused of discriminatory practices while others argued that ethnic solidarity among job seekers is important.

articles.title: ‘Hot for Them Too’: British Man Praised Online for Rescuing Dehydrated Bird Amid Delhi’s Heatwave | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A British national, Nick Booker, rescued a dehydrated Black Kite in Delhi during the ongoing heatwave.  Booker captured the rescue on video and contacted Wildlife SOS, a wildlife rescue organization that responded promptly to assist the bird. The incident drew attention to the impact of extreme temperatures on urban wildlife and highlighted the need for people to provide water for birds. Wildlife SOS members, including Sanoj Chaurasiya and Pratap Singh, were commended for their quick response.

articles.title: Mayon Volcano Eruption Forces Evacuations and Disrupts Air Travel Near Manila | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas south of Manila following the eruption of Mayon Volcano.  The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) has raised Alert Level 3, warning of potential hazards like landslides and lava flows. The Department of Social Welfare and Development reports nearly 1,500 families are staying in evacuation centers, while over 26,600 families across Albay province have been affected by ashfall.  The Civil Aviation Authority issued flight safety advisories due to potential hazards from volcanic ash and activity.

articles.title: Republicans ‘concerned’ after Trump threatens to withdraw more US troops from Germany | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to withdraw more US troops from Germany, exceeding the initial 5,000 soldiers removed last week.  The move followed Friedrich Merz, German chancellor, criticizing the US's handling of the Iran conflict. The Pentagon cited "theater requirements and conditions on the ground" for the withdrawal. Republican members of Congress expressed concern over troop reductions and urged coordination with Congress and allies.

articles.title: Meeting reviews monsoon preparedness in Kozhikode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Snehil Kumar Singh chaired a meeting to discuss monsoon preparedness in the district.  The meeting reviewed measures to prevent waterlogging, ensure water sanitation and school safety, and maintain drainage systems. Mr. Singh also directed the Kerala Fire and Rescue Services to equip all fire stations with essential supplies.

articles.title: Who is William Savitt? Sam Altman hires lawyer who beat Elon Musk once before - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, hired lawyer William Savitt to lead his legal team in a high-stakes trial against Elon Musk.  Savitt, known for his courtroom experience and past victory over Musk in the Twitter acquisition case, will argue that Musk's lawsuit is driven by competition rather than principle. The trial pits two Silicon Valley titans against each other as OpenAI contends that Musk is trying to weaken the company to benefit his own AI firm, xAI.  Savitt has a long and successful career at Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, handling complex corporate cases and working with major companies.

articles.title: AICTE’s National Internship Portal records 4.7 crore student registrations in 4.5 years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Internship Portal, run by the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE), has registered over 4.7 crore students in four-and-a-half years.  Over 79.57 lakh internship opportunities have been offered through the portal, and more than 32.78 lakh students have completed their internships. The initiative is part of the National Educational Alliance for Technology (NEAT) and the National Educational Technology Forum (NETF), aiming to bridge the gap between academic theory and workplace reality.  The platform has partnered with major companies like Microsoft, Google, IBM, Cisco, and Salesforce, offering students technical training in future-of-work domains such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and supply chain management.

articles.title: Republicans appear split on idea of clemency for Ghislaine Maxwell | Jeffrey Epstein | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Recent reports of potential clemency for Ghislaine Maxwell, the accomplice of Jeffrey Epstein, have sparked outrage among survivors and their advocates who view her lengthy sentence as a form of justice.  Survivors’ advocates, including Spencer Kuvin and Sigrid McCawley, argue that any pardon would be a betrayal to victims and undermine the integrity of the judicial system. Congress members, including Republican chair James Comer, have expressed opposition to clemency, while some Republicans, like Thomas Massie, have voiced strong disapproval.  Despite these concerns, discussions about clemency persist, highlighting the continued political minefield surrounding Epstein and Maxwell.

articles.title: Three injured as robbers open fire during jewellery shop robbery in Karimnagar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Five armed assailants robbed the PMJ Jewels Boutique in Karimnagar, India on Sunday, injuring three staff members before fleeing with stolen gold ornaments. The incident occurred around 11 a.m., and police suspect it was carried out by an inter-state gang after a reconnaissance of the shop.  The injured individuals were taken to a nearby hospital where their condition is stable. Police are investigating the robbery and attempting to locate the suspects.

articles.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists appear in Israeli court after abduction | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila, two activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, appeared in court in Israel after being abducted by Israeli authorities. The court extended their detention for further interrogation, with no charges filed against them yet.  Adalah, an international rights group representing the activists, claims the proceedings are "flawed and illegal" and a retaliatory measure against humanitarian activist leaders. Spain has condemned the “kidnapping” of Abu Keshek and rejected the accusations against him, while the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs states the activists are part of the Palestinian National Conference Abroad, which the United States says operates at the "behest" of the Palestinian group Hamas.

articles.title: SSC exams: apply for recounting, re-verification by May 7 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh Board of Secondary Education (APBSE) has opened a window for online application forms for recounting and re-verification of answer scripts from May 1 to 7, 2026. Candidates must submit the forms through their school logins and pay a fee of ₹500 per subject for recounting or ₹1,000 per subject for re-verification. Payments can be made online via debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI, but not through CFMS Citizen Challan.

articles.title: 'Impossible military op or ...': Iran mocks US, says Trump has only 2 options left | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that US President Donald Trump faces a choice between an "impossible" military operation or a "bad deal" with Tehran. The Guards' intelligence organization said the US has narrowed decision-making options, following stalled diplomatic efforts and rising tensions.  Trump reviewed Iran's 14-point proposal but expressed doubt about its acceptability, while Iranian officials indicated they are prepared for both diplomatic engagement and continued confrontation.

articles.title: Key Starmer adviser held 16 undisclosed meetings with top US tech bosses | Technology policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Varun Chandra, a key advisor to Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves, held 16 undisclosed meetings with top US tech executives between October 2024 and October 2025.  These meetings, which took place as the government sought investment from Silicon Valley, included discussions on regulatory changes, AI, and Donald Trump's second administration. Chandra's role as chief business adviser to the prime minister expanded this year to include US trade envoy duties. These interactions raise concerns about transparency and potential influence over government decisions, with critics calling for a comprehensive lobbying register.

articles.title: Over 1,000 motorists booked for drunk driving across tri-commissionerate limits - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 1,000 motorists were booked for drunk driving during special enforcement drives conducted by Hyderabad, Cyberabad, and Malkajgiri traffic police over the weekend.  The Hyderabad Traffic Police booked 445 offenders, with Cyberabad apprehending 283. Malkajgiri commissionerate recorded 318 arrests between April 26 and May 2. All offenders will be produced before the courts, and police warned of potential charges under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for causing fatal accidents while driving under the influence.

articles.title: Indian man Sandarsh Krishna goes missing inside Grand Canyon National Park, black backpack was found - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Grand Canyon National Park authorities are seeking public assistance in locating a missing 26-year-old Indian man, Sandarsh Krishna.  Krishna was last seen on April 27th along the Rim Trail between Bright Angel Lodge and Mohave Point wearing athletic clothing. National Park Service rangers have released a photo of a person who returned a black backpack believed to belong to Krishna. The backpack was turned in at Bright Angel Lodge, but investigators will speak with the individual once they are identified.

articles.title: BRS office is a centre of ‘false propaganda’: Govt. Whip Adi Srinivas - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Adi Srinivas, the Congress government whip, criticized the BRS government's handling of job creation in Telangana. He accused the BRS of misleading unemployed youth by failing to fill positions during its rule and now falsely claiming responsibility for recent job drives.  Srinivas highlighted the Congress government's transparency in providing nearly 70,000 jobs through recruitment ceremonies across Hyderabad.  He also criticized former BRS leader T. Jeevan Reddy for changing his stance on the issue after joining the party.

articles.title: The man who kept fighting World War II alone in the jungle for 30 years: Here’s the truth behind his mission | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hiroo Onoda, a Japanese soldier who remained hidden on Lubang Island in the Philippines for nearly 30 years after World War II, refused to accept that the war had ended. Despite repeated attempts by others to inform him of the conflict's conclusion, Onoda believed it was all deception and clung to his original orders not to surrender or take his own life.  His experience raises questions about loyalty, belief, and how far a person can go when refusing reality.  He eventually surrendered in 1974 after being contacted by a Japanese adventurer who informed him of the war's end.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz calls on Nawaz, discusses political situation in country, steps taken for peace in Middle East - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Nawaz Sharif, the leader of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), at their Jati Umra residence in Lahore on Sunday. The meeting discussed the political situation in Pakistan and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, including Pakistan's efforts for peace restoration.  Shehbaz Sharif briefed Nawaz Sharif about the current state of affairs, particularly regarding oil prices in the international market and government measures to provide relief to citizens affected by the global energy crisis.
