The collaboration is significant as it coincides with the title race context of the El Clásico, where Barcelona holds a nine-point lead over Real Madrid.

articles.title: FCC moved against increase in petrol, diesel prices - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A private citizen, Advocate Zulfikar Ahmed Bhutta, filed a petition with the Federal Constitution Court seeking to overturn recent increases in petrol and diesel prices. The petition argues that the government's justification for the price hike is unfounded and seeks directions for the withdrawal of the increase, as well as the import of petroleum products from Iran at lower prices.  The petition also claims that Pakistan could have secured fuel at significantly lower rates than those currently charged by the government if it had acted swiftly to import from Iran despite the US-Iran conflict.

articles.title: Shivamogga police launch locked-house beat system to stop house theft cases - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shivamogga police launched the Locked House Beat System (LHBS) on May 1st to deter house break-ins while residents are away. The initiative encourages residents to inform officers of their travel plans by sending a WhatsApp message with departure and return dates, home address, and a selfie in front of their house. A dedicated helpline, 82779-82901, has been established for this purpose.

articles.title: No visa lottery, limits on family entry: How ‘Americans First Immigration Act’ could be a setback for migrants - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Congressman Barry Moore introduced the "Americans First Immigration Act," a new bill proposing to overhaul the country's legal immigration framework. The legislation aims to prioritize high-skilled workers and tighten eligibility rules, ending the diversity visa lottery program and restricting family sponsorship to immediate relatives.  The bill also introduces a points-based system for immigrants, evaluating their English proficiency, education, salary, age, military service, job offer details, and employer hiring practices. Supporters of the bill argue it restores fairness and accountability by protecting American jobs, prioritizing the nuclear family, and ensuring immigrants contribute to the US economy.

articles.title: Trump’s threat: Why cutting US troops in Europe won’t be easy | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has threatened to reduce US troops in Germany, Italy, and Spain amid transatlantic tensions over the Iran war.  He claims that Friedrich Merz, the German Chancellor, is "humiliating" the US with his criticism of the war's strategy.  Trump also criticized Keir Starmer for not supporting the US in the conflict and Giorgia Meloni for her disapproval of the war. The US has nearly 68,000 active-duty personnel stationed across Europe, with Germany hosting the largest contingent. These bases are critical for US military operations and logistical support, including the Landstuhl Regional Medical Center.  The president and the Department of Defense typically decide troop levels in Europe, but Congress can influence these decisions through legislation and funding control.

articles.title: India raises cooking gas, jet fuel prices as supply pressures mount - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India's state-run energy firm, Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), raised the prices of commercial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and jet fuel for international airlines. The price hikes are attributed to supply pressures from the Middle East war, which has disrupted imports.  The government maintains that India faces no overall fuel shortage, but the increases will impact restaurants and other sectors reliant on LPG and jet fuel.

articles.title: End of Trump tariffs on whisky sparks row between Scottish parties over claiming credit | Scottish politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced he would lift punishing US tariffs on Scotch whisky, citing the influence of King Charles and Queen Camilla's visit to the United States. The decision was met with relief from the whisky industry and business leaders, but sparked a dispute between Scottish party leaders over who played a key role in the outcome. John Swinney, the first minister of Scotland, claimed his meeting with Trump at the White House last year had been instrumental in securing the change, while Douglas Alexander, the UK Labour government's cabinet minister for Scotland, disputed this claim and emphasized that trade agreements were the responsibility of the UK government.

articles.title: ED empowered under Modi govt. to fight ‘cancer’ of financial crimes, not target anyone: MoS Finance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister of State (MoS) for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary stated that the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has been given necessary powers to combat financial crimes and terror funding, not to target individuals.  He highlighted the rise in financial crimes like money laundering, 'hawala' transactions, and corporate fraud as reasons for this strengthened agency. The ED achieved significant success with attachments worth ₹2.36 lakh crore since 2005 and a conviction rate of nearly 94% in money laundering cases.  The agency also initiated proceedings under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act (FEOA) against 54 individuals, confiscating properties worth ₹2,178.34 crore.

articles.title: ‘Acceptable in my culture’: Indian real estate agent gives bizarre reason for luring 9-year-old into his car in Canada - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Manoj Govindbalunikam, an Indian real estate agent, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for abducting a nine-year-old boy in Ontario.  His lawyer argued that the incident was a misunderstanding stemming from cultural differences and that offering food and gifts was normal in his culture. However, the court rejected this explanation, stating that Govindbalunikam had lived in Canada long enough to understand local norms. The judge also noted that Govindbalunikam's education and experience did not justify his actions.  He now faces deportation proceedings.

articles.title: Pakistan sees decline in militant violence for 2nd straight month: PICSS - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) reported a second consecutive month of improved security indicators in April 2026.  Militant attacks decreased by 42% from March, with fatalities falling to 60. The decline followed cross-border military operations targeting militant groups between February 26 and March 18. While the number of attacks remained high, most were low-intensity incidents, with a few exceptions. Security forces continued to conduct robust operations, killing 224 militants in April.  The report also noted a significant reduction in civilian casualties and injuries across the country.

articles.title: Conducting health camp and distributing kits is not labour welfare, says Union Minister Shobha Karandlaje - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour, Employment and MSME, criticized the functioning of the Karnataka State Labour Department.  She alleged that construction workers' welfare fund is not being utilized properly in the state, citing the example of an uncommissioned ESI Hospital in Chikkaballapur.  The minister also expressed disappointment over the defeat of a revised Women’s Reservation Bill linked to delimitation due to opposition politics. Prime Minister Narendra Modi led government has introduced four labour codes to replace 29 Central laws, with a focus on providing social security and facilities for all workers in the country.

articles.title: Changing lives: Virginia students repair old cars and donate them to single mothers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Louisa County High School in Mineral, Virginia, partners with Giving Words, a nonprofit organization founded by Eddie Brown, to provide automotive technology students with hands-on experience repairing donated vehicles. The program gives single mothers access to reliable transportation while teaching students valuable skills and fostering a sense of purpose.  The initiative involves students performing essential repairs on donated cars, ensuring they meet safety standards before being given away.

articles.title: PM forms committee to review One Constitution Avenue case, halts authorities from taking action - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Shehbaz Sharif has formed a high-level committee to review the One Constitution Avenue situation, halting any further action by authorities. The committee, headed by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, will examine all aspects of the case and submit a report within a week.  The committee will hear all parties involved, including residents who are vacating their apartments voluntarily amid reports of police intervention.

articles.title: Hegseth says clock paused on deadline to seek approval for Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Hegseth, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and senior administration officials have stated that the 60-day clock for seeking congressional approval for the US-Israeli war with Iran has paused due to a ceasefire in effect since early April.  However, Democratic senators argue that the War Powers Resolution requires the cessation of hostilities within 60 days unless Congress approves an extension. Despite this, administration officials claim the hostilities have terminated and no exchange of fire has occurred between the US and Iran since April 7th. The conflict sparked after US and Israeli strikes on Iran killed the country's supreme leader, prompting Iranian retaliation against Israel and US-allied states in the Gulf.

articles.title: Timberwolves eliminate Nuggets as Knicks demolish Hawks in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Minnesota Timberwolves eliminated the Denver Nuggets, while the New York Knicks dominated the Atlanta Hawks in a record-setting playoff victory.  The Philadelphia 76ers beat the Boston Celtics again, forcing a decisive Game 7 in their series. The San Antonio Spurs await the Timberwolves in the Western Conference semifinals after a 110-98 win for Minnesota.

articles.title: The Outrage Machine reloaded - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Republic TV, a television channel, has been criticized for its portrayal of peace talks between the US and Iran mediated by Pakistan. The channel's anchors have engaged in sensationalized reporting, focusing on anger and outrage rather than economic consequences. This approach, according to the author, is part of a larger "Outrage Machine" that profits from manufactured hate and fuels political agendas.  The article argues that this cycle of hate-driven content creates a dangerous dependence on conflict for media outlets, politicians, and audiences alike.

articles.title: Trump administration rejects need for Iran war Congressional approval despite deadline – US politics live | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has rejected the 60-day deadline set by the War Powers Act for ending its military action against Iran.  Pete Hegseth, the defense secretary, stated that the ceasefire agreement with Iran halts the clock on the 60-day period. Senate Republicans blocked a resolution from Adam Schiff that would have limited the conflict until Congress authorizes further action. Two Republican senators, Susan Collins and Rand Paul, voted in favor of the resolution while one Democrat, John Fetterman, opposed it.  Trump has threatened to withdraw troops from Italy and Spain, citing their lack of support for his war in the Middle East.

articles.title: Woman charged over death of two eight-year-old girls after Wimbledon car crash | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Claire Freemantle, 49, has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving after a crash at a south-east London primary school in July 2023 killed two eight-year-old girls. Freemantle will plead not guilty to the charges when she appears in court on June 16th.  The Metropolitan police faced criticism for initially deciding not to charge her, but later reversed that decision after an investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct. The watchdog is also investigating allegations of racism and false information provided to the families.

articles.title: Ex-Tory councillor who drugged and raped wife admits making child abuse images | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Philip Young, a former Conservative councillor, pleaded guilty to additional offences of making indecent images of children in addition to his previous convictions for drugging, raping, and sexually assaulting his former wife. Joanne Young, who waived her right to anonymity, had previously admitted she was raped by Dean Hamilton.  Four other men are also facing charges related to sexual assault against Joanne Young. Their trial is scheduled for October.

articles.title: Riots erupt over Australian Aboriginal girl’s murder as suspect arrested | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Riots broke out in Alice Springs, Australia after the arrest of a suspect in the death of five-year-old Indigenous girl Kumanjayi Little Baby. The violence erupted when locals beat the suspect, Jefferson Lewis, who had been identified as a suspect by police earlier in the week. Police Commissioner Martin Dole urged for calm and said Lewis will likely be charged soon.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese also called for calm while Northern Territory Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro implemented alcohol restrictions to prevent further escalation.

articles.title: ‘Journalists compelled to self-censor to avoid legal trouble’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Freedom Network, a press freedom watchdog, released a report highlighting the weaponization of Pakistan's cybercrime laws as a major threat to media freedom. The report, published on World Press Freedom Day, states that amendments to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) 2016 have created a climate of fear for journalists, leading them to self-censor.  The report cites high-profile convictions of human rights lawyers and numerous journalists facing charges under expanded Peca provisions as evidence of this repression. Freedom Network documented at least 129 verified incidents of journalist violations during the review period, with legal threats and physical violence accounting for nearly two-thirds of these cases.

articles.title: Man appears in court over attempted murders of three people in London knife attacks | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Essa Suleiman, 45, appeared in court charged with attempted murder after two separate knife attacks in London. The first attack occurred at Ishmail Hussein's home in Southwark, followed by an attack on two Jewish men in Golders Green.  A member of the public intervened and disarmed Suleiman during the second attack.  He was arrested after a stun gun was used and is currently remanded in custody awaiting his next court appearance on May 15th.

articles.title: Has the US-Iran ceasefire reset the clock on War Powers Act deadline? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claims the ongoing ceasefire with Iran has paused the 60-day deadline under the War Powers Resolution, arguing hostilities have ceased. However, Democratic lawmakers and legal experts dispute this interpretation, stating the statute does not allow for a pause once the deadline begins.  They argue that US forces remain active despite halted air attacks, and that the ceasefire cannot alter legal obligations the White House must adhere to. Some experts suggest starting a new operation under a different name to circumvent the deadline, while others criticize President Trump's reliance on the War Powers Resolution and its potential for abuse.  Despite Republican opposition, Senator Susan Collins joined Democrats in opposing Trump's interpretation of the resolution, highlighting that it is a requirement, not a suggestion.

articles.title: Antigua and Barbuda prime minister set to win fourth term in election | Antigua and Barbuda | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gaston Browne, the prime minister of Antigua and Barbuda, is set to win a fourth term in office after preliminary results showed his Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party (ABLP) winning 15 out of 17 seats in parliament.  The election took place amidst an unstable political landscape with concerns about the cost of living and global instability, including US visa restrictions imposed on Antigua and Barbuda nationals. Jamale Pringle, leader of the opposition United Progressive party (UPP), won his seat but faced criticism for his leadership from a Caribbean political analyst who attributed the ABLP's victory to disarray among the opposition.

articles.title: Quote Of The Day: Quote of the day by Benjamin Franklin: "The best thing to give to your enemy is forgiveness; to an opponent, tolerance; to a friend, your heart; to your child, a good example; to a father, deference; to your mother, conduct that will make her proud of you; to yourself, respect; to all others, charity." | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Franklin's quote, "The best thing to give to your enemy is forgiveness; to an opponent, tolerance; to a friend, your heart; to your child, a good example; to a father, deference; to your mother, conduct that will make her proud of you; to yourself, respect; to all others, charity," offers guidance on how to interact with different people in various roles. The quote suggests specific actions for each relationship type, such as forgiving enemies and being tolerant of opponents, while emphasizing the importance of respect and kindness towards family members and oneself.  It highlights the need for understanding and empathy in human relationships, regardless of time or culture.

articles.title: ‘He’s probably good’: Donald Trump Jr gets muted endorsement from his father for The Apprentice reboot | The Apprentice | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon is considering rebooting the reality show The Apprentice, which was hosted by Donald Trump between 2004 and 2015, for its streaming service Prime Video.  While Amazon has not confirmed active development of a reboot, they have acknowledged preliminary internal discussions about potential future projects for the franchise. The Wall Street Journal reported that Donald Trump Jr. is being considered as a potential host by some sources close to him. However, Amazon maintains that any reporting on details of the show or potential hosts would be purely speculative.

articles.title: Bangladesh's foreign ministry summons India's acting Envoy over Himanta’s remarks: report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry summoned India's acting High Commissioner Pawan Badhe to lodge a formal protest over comments made by Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.  Ms. Ishrat Jahan, Director General (South Asia), conveyed Bangladesh's displeasure with the remarks, which were deemed "disparaging" and undermining of bilateral relations. The official emphasized the need for restraint when addressing sensitive issues between the two countries.

articles.title: China Rape Case: China: 14-year-old sentenced to life for rape and murder of classmate - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A China court sentenced a 14-year-old boy to life imprisonment for the rape and murder of his 15-year-old classmate. The incident occurred between July 6th and 7th, 2025, when the defendant allegedly attempted to rape the victim before strangling her in an attempt to conceal the crime.  The court ruled that the boy's actions constituted both rape and intentional homicide, noting that Chinese law prohibits the death penalty for offenders under 18 at the time of the offense. The hearing was attended by the victim's family, along with national lawmakers, political advisers, and members of the media.

articles.title: Nearly ₹1,000 hike in commercial cylinder price is a harsh blow to cafes, hotels and street side vendors: Uttam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Telangana Civil Supplies Minister, criticized the Centre's decision to increase the price of a 19kg commercial LPG cylinder by almost ₹1,000 per refill. The new price is ₹3,315, marking an increase of ₹994 from the previous ₹2,321. Reddy accused the Centre of taking the decision shortly after West Bengal elections, calling it "cheating" and demanding a rollback.

articles.title: Six injured in Washington state school stabbing
articles.rephrased_article: Six people were injured in a stabbing at Foss High School in Tacoma, Washington on Thursday.  Five high school students and an adult security guard were taken to the hospital with minor injuries, all of whom are now in stable condition. The suspect, a student at Foss High School, was also injured and booked on five counts of first-degree assault. Tacoma Police Department is investigating the incident, which occurred after "some type of altercation", according to Shelbie Boyd, a spokeswoman for the department.

articles.title: Uk Blackmail Teacher Case: ‘Wicked behaviour’: UK man jailed for posing as woman to blackmail teacher, circulate explicit video with students | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 21-year-old man, Muaawiya Ameen, has been sentenced to 15 months in prison for blackmailing a teacher into sending an explicit video.  Ameen posed as a woman on Instagram and engaged the victim in a sexual conversation, which led him to send a video of himself engaging in a sexual act at his workplace. Ameen then demanded £1,000 to prevent the footage from being shared, but despite receiving the payment, he distributed it to the teacher's students. The victim lost his job and attempted suicide after the incident.

articles.title: Scammers impersonate Nilgiris Collector, case registered - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru
articles.rephrased_article: Cyber Crime police are investigating individuals who allegedly impersonated Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru to extort money from residents. The scammers used the collector's photograph on a messaging platform and claimed to be her, requesting money under various pretexts.  The district administration reported the suspicious messages, leading to a case being registered by the police. Ms. Tanneeru has urged locals to report such scams and not respond to fraudulent messages claiming to be from officials.

articles.title: Digested week: King bites tongue as president indulges his own fantasies | John Crace | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two top civil servants, Olly Robbins and Cat Little, were called before the foreign affairs select committee to discuss Keir Starmer's appointment of Peter Mandelson as US ambassador.  Hannah Spencer, a Green MP, faced backlash for criticizing alcohol culture in Parliament. The state visit to the US by King Charles and Queen Camilla was met with mixed reactions, with some commentators overanalyzing its significance. Tottenham Hotspur won their first Premier League match of the season but remain in danger of relegation.

articles.title: FIFA push US government into sweeping tax agreement covering all 48 World Cup teams ahead of tournament | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA has reached an agreement with the United States Treasury that will allow all 48 participating nations in the 2026 World Cup to apply for exemption from federal taxes on their tournament earnings. This breakthrough follows months of concern over uneven financial burdens on national associations, particularly those without existing tax treaties with the United States. While this agreement addresses federal taxation, discussions remain ongoing regarding state and city taxes that will still apply depending on match locations.  The 2026 World Cup is scheduled to begin June 11th in Mexico.

articles.title: Mysuru hoteliers say LPG cylinder price going up by ₹1,440 in two months is ‘abnormal and alarming’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Mysuru Hotel Owners’ Association has strongly condemned the recent ₹991 price increase for a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder, calling it a "severe blow" to the hospitality sector.  Association President C. Narayanagowda stated that the surge in price, now at ₹3,132 in Mysuru, threatens the survival of hotels, restaurants, and small eateries.

articles.title: Superdry co-founder James Holder found guilty of raping woman after night out | Rape and sexual assault | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: James Holder, co-founder of the clothing firm Superdry, was found guilty of rape after a trial at Gloucester crown court. The victim testified that she had been raped by Holder after he and his friend got into her taxi.  James Haskell, prosecuting, argued that Holder did not stop despite the woman's pleas and that she was intoxicated. Holder maintained that the encounter was consensual but was found guilty of rape.

articles.title: Jonas Lauwiner: Man proclaims himself king of Switzerland and builds an empire for free | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jonas Lauwiner, a Swiss man, has amassed over 110,000 square meters of land across Switzerland by exploiting a legal provision allowing claims on unowned or unregistered parcels.  He calls himself the "king of Switzerland" and uses this title to promote his project, which involves identifying overlooked plots like roads and small properties. While his self-proclaimed monarchy has no official recognition, his land acquisitions have sparked controversy from local authorities and residents who criticize his approach as exploiting legal loopholes and raising ethical concerns.

articles.title: Mysuru hoteliers say LPG cylinder price going up by ₹1,440 in two months is ‘abnormal and alarming’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Mysuru Hotel Owners’ Association has condemned the ₹991 price increase for a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder, calling it a "severe blow" to the hospitality sector.  Association President C. Narayanagowda stated that the new price of ₹3,132 is one of the sharpest increases in recent times and threatens the survival of hotels, restaurants, and small eateries.

articles.title: Trump threatens to withdraw troops from Italy and Spain | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to withdraw US troops from Italy and Spain, citing their lack of support in the Iran conflict. Guido Crosetto, Italy's defense minister, rejected these accusations and emphasized Rome's cooperation with the US on maritime security.  Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has consistently opposed the US-Israeli war on Iran and criticized Trump's actions, including his recent threats to impose a trade embargo.

articles.title: Japanese man arrested after wife incinerated at zoo - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tatsuya Suzuki, a man who worked at the Asahiyama Zoo in Hokkaido, Japan, was arrested for allegedly incinerating his deceased wife, Yui Suzuki. Police discovered human remains in the zoo's incinerator after Suzuki confessed to burning her body. The case has forced the zoo to delay its reopening and caused public concern.  The zoo resumed operations on Friday with apologies from officials.

articles.title: Iran vows ‘long, painful’ response if US renews attacks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has vowed a "long and painful" response if the United States renews attacks, citing its claim to the Strait of Hormuz.  The closure of the strait, which restricts 20% of global oil and gas supplies, continues to complicate efforts to reopen it.  President Donald Trump received briefings on potential military strikes against Iran, but a decision on whether to renew attacks is pending Congressional approval. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has stated that the Strait will be defended under new management. The United Arab Emirates and Bahrain have imposed travel restrictions on citizens of Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, urging their residents to leave those countries.

articles.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2026: dates, routes, application process and all you need to know - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced the schedule for this year's Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, which will take place between June and August.  A computer-generated, random selection process will be used to select 20 batches of 50 tourists each, with one batch traveling through Uttarakhand via Lipulekh Pass and another through Sikkim via Nathu La Pass.

articles.title: Looking for best equity MFs to invest for 3 years? Check these 6 funds with over 27% returns - Three-year top gainers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several equity mutual funds have achieved significant returns over the past three years. Bandhan Small Cap Fund, with a 30.72% gain, led the pack among these funds, followed by LIC MF Infrastructure Fund at 28.94%.  Other notable performers include DSP India T.I.G.E.R Fund, ICICI Prudential Pharma Healthcare and Diagnostics (P.H.D) Fund, Canara Robeco Infrastructure Fund, and Franklin Build India Fund. These funds, with varying AUMs, expense ratios, and ratings, demonstrate the diverse performance within the equity mutual fund market.

articles.title: Mojtaba Khamenei: 'God wanted him preserved': Iran calls US claims on Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's health 'trick used by enemy' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ayatollah Mohsen Qomi, a member of the assembly of experts and deputy for international affairs in the office of the Supreme Leader of Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, dismissed claims by the United States regarding the health of the Supreme Leader.  Qomi stated that such accusations are tactics used by the West to elicit reactions and engage in rumor mongering. He confirmed that Khamenei was present during the bombing but was saved due to divine intervention. Qomi assured that Khamenei is currently in perfect health and actively managing affairs, including overseeing negotiations and field operations.

articles.title: UK police charge man over stabbing of two Jewish men in London | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK’s Metropolitan Police have charged a man with attempted murder following the stabbing of two Jewish men in Golders Green, north London. The attack occurred on Wednesday and prompted officials to raise the national terrorism threat level to its second-highest level.  Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged stronger action to protect Jewish people, while Met Police Commissioner Mark Rowley acknowledged officers' fear during the arrest of the suspect.  The incident has been linked to a growing terrorist threat in the UK, with police investigating plans for pro-Palestinian protests in London.

articles.title: Met police chief denies ‘intervening in politics’ after open letter to Zack Polanski – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Rowley, the Metropolitan police commissioner, denied that his letter to Zack Polanski regarding the arrest of a suspect in Golders Green was an attempt to interfere in politics.  Rowley stated he wrote the letter to support officers and defend their confidence to act. The public spat between Rowley and Polanski comes days before local elections and has raised questions about whether Rowley's actions violated regulations prohibiting police from engaging in political activity.

articles.title: This May Day reminds workers to be more organised, says Kerala Chief Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's trade union organizations and workers from various sectors celebrated May Day on Friday, expressing concerns over the erosion of labor rights and the introduction of four new labor codes. Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, in a Facebook post, acknowledged the growing strength of labor strikes across India despite neoliberal policies that undermine worker rights.  He urged workers to remain organized. The celebrations included rallies and public events in all 14 district centers and over 250 other locations. Trade unions like CITU, AITUC, AIUTUC, AICTU, SEWA, TUCI, HMS, NLC, INLC, HMKP, KTUCM, JTU, and NTU joined forces to mark the occasion.

articles.title: ​9 high-growth smallcap stocks surged up to 170%; 4 became multibaggers - Smallcap Earnings Surge | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BSE smallcap companies experienced a surge in earnings growth during the March 2026 earnings season, with nearly 45 firms reporting profits exceeding 50% year-over-year.  Nine stocks stood out for their significant gains, including Bajaj Consumer Care, Jayaswal Neco Industries, and Infobeans Technologies. These companies experienced share price increases of 50% to 170%, demonstrating strong underlying growth in the smallcap market.

articles.title: Kalambo Falls Discovery: A 476,000-year-old wooden structure found in Kalambo Falls is changing human history | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from Aberystwyth University and the University of Liverpool have discovered a 476,000-year-old wooden structure at Kalambo Falls in Zambia. The discovery challenges previous beliefs about early hominin intelligence by demonstrating advanced carpentry skills like using stone tools for joining pieces. This finding indicates that Pleistocene ancestors had the cognitive ability to create permanent living spaces and suggests a "Wooden Age" where wood was used for more complex purposes than previously thought.  The waterlogged environment at Kalambo Falls preserved the artifacts, offering insights into early human history.

articles.title: Brazil's Congress approves plan to drastically cut Bolsonaro's jail term
articles.rephrased_article: Brazil's Congress overturned a veto by Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the president, on a bill that would reduce former president Jair Bolsonaro's prison sentence for plotting a coup. The law could still be challenged in the Supreme Court.  Lawmakers voted to change how prison sentences are calculated, potentially reducing Bolsonaro's term from 27 years to just over two years. This is the second blow to Lula's left-wing government this week.

articles.title: Bengaluru hotels to hike prices again after gas cylinder price goes up from ₹2,162 to ₹3,152 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The price of a commercial gas cylinder in Bengaluru has increased by ₹993 on April 30, reaching ₹3,152. This marks the highest price ever recorded for a commercial LPG cylinder in the city.  P.C. Rao, President of the Bengaluru Hotels’ Association, stated that hotels are forced to raise prices due to supply constraints and high black market prices. Hoteliers have appealed to the government to reduce Goods and Services Tax (GST) on commercial LPG cylinders to 5%, arguing it would alleviate the burden on consumers facing price inflation.  D.K. Shivakumar, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, also criticized the price hike, emphasizing its impact on common citizens.

articles.title: Gold falls around 2% in one week as skyrocketing oil prices fuel inflation worries. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Spot gold prices remained steady around $4,620 per ounce on Friday morning. MCX was closed for Maharashtra Day but gold futures with June expiry rose 0.1% to $4,632.70 and contracts with August expiry also closed higher.  Oil prices continued to remain elevated above $110 per barrel due to the ongoing Iran-US war, despite cooling down from a high of $126 per barrel on Thursday. Deutsche Bank predicts gold prices could climb to $8,000 an ounce within five years if its share in global central bank reserves increases to 40%.

articles.title: UK: 1,200 homes evacuated as bomb disposal teams prepare to destroy WWII bomb in Plymouth | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Over 1,200 homes in Plymouth have been evacuated after a Second World War bomb was discovered at a construction site.  A controlled explosion is planned to safely dispose of the 250kg German SC250 bomb due to concerns over its fuses. The Devon and Cornwall Police, along with Plymouth City Council, are providing support for residents displaced by the evacuation, including shelter at the Southway Youth and Community Centre.

articles.title: Why is piracy rising off Somalia again — and is the Iran war responsible? | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: At least four vessels have been hijacked off the coast of Somalia in recent weeks, raising concerns about a resurgence of piracy. The European Union Naval Force (EUNAVFOR) and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) have warned shipping firms to transit with caution.  Analysts speculate that diversion of antipiracy patrols to counter attacks by the Houthis in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, as well as increased fuel prices due to the US-Israel war on Iran, may be contributing factors to the surge. The hijackings follow a period of relative calm after a peak in piracy activity during the early 2000s when thousands of seafarers were captured or fired upon by pirates demanding ransoms.

articles.title: Mahua flower festival celebrated in Telangana’s Adilabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Adilabad Collector Rajarshi Shah urged tribal communities to collect ippa flowers sustainably to enhance their economic well-being. He emphasized the importance of preserving trees and respecting tribal heritage, highlighting the significance of these efforts in achieving financial self-reliance. The call was made during the annual "Ippa Puvvu Panduga" event organized by the Integrated Tribal Development Agency, Utnoor, in collaboration with Adivasi (Gondwana) organizations at Jamidi village in Adilabad district.

articles.title: Bitcoin signals mild bullish trend near $77,000; Ethereum around $2,300 with neutral momentum - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced slight gains, with Bitcoin hovering around $76,600 and Ethereum near $2,250.  The global crypto market capitalization increased by 1.35% to reach $2.57 trillion. Piyush Walke, a Derivatives Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, noted that Bitcoin is facing profit-taking pressure near $80,000 and looming U.S. inflation data could weigh on risk assets.  Momentum in the crypto market has faded, with recent ETF outflows potentially contributing to sluggish price action.

articles.title: Constable martyred as militants launch rocket attack on armoured police vehicle in Bannu - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A police constable was killed and a civilian injured in a rocket and sniper attack on an armored police vehicle in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The incident occurred during a routine patrol near the Fatah Khel police post.  The Bannu police have launched a large-scale search operation to apprehend the attackers. This follows a series of security incidents in the area, including attacks on police and jirga members, prompting targeted operations by security forces.

articles.title: Man charged with attempted murder in connection with Golders Green attack | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Essa Suleiman, 45, has been charged with attempted murder after two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, London.  The incident occurred on Wednesday and the victims, Shloime Rand and Moshe Ben Baila, were taken to hospital. Commander Helen Flanagan, head of counter-terrorism policing for London, stated that the police are determined to get justice for the victims. The UK's terrorism threat level has been raised to "severe" following the incident, prompting concerns about potential attacks.

articles.title: Hike in commercial LPG price: Shock and resignation on food street as LPG price goes up by 42% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Food kiosk and restaurant owners in Hyderabad expressed shock and resignation over a ₹994 increase in commercial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder prices on Friday, May 1, 2026.  Many owners said they were already buying cylinders from the black market at exorbitant prices and that this new hike would further strain their businesses. Some reported having to raise prices previously, but now face difficulty doing so due to the high cost of goods and limited profit margins. This price increase comes after a previous surge in LPG prices and shortages earlier this year, forcing some restaurants to temporarily shut down.

articles.title: Square Yards reports Rs 2,086 crore revenue in FY26, growth of 48% year-over-year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Square Yards, a real estate brokerage firm, reported a 49% year-over-year increase in gross profit to Rs 476 crore (USD 51 million) driven by strong India revenue growth. The company facilitated over 2.73 lakh customer acquisitions in FY26 and saw Bangalore lead the market share for real estate GTV at 30%.  Square Yards' fintech arm, Urban Money, also reported a significant contribution to total gross value transaction (GTV) with mortgage loans accounting for 86% of its portfolio.

articles.title: ‘Profoundly distressing’: record number of deaths in custody and police operations in NSW | Deaths in custody | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Teresa O’Sullivan, the state coroner of New South Wales, released her annual report on deaths in custody and police operations, revealing a record 66 deaths last year.  Thirty-nine of these deaths occurred in custody, with 12 being Indigenous people, a record high. The report found that most of those who died by self-harm did so by hanging, despite millions being invested to remove ligature points. Michael Daley, the state attorney general, received the report, and the coroner noted an increase in deaths on remand, as well as concerns about police pursuits and sedation use.

articles.title: Artificial fuel shortage at 56 of 4,312 petrol bunks in Andhra Pradesh, says BJP state chief Madhav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.V.N. Madhav, BJP State president, urged petrol bunks in Andhra Pradesh to ensure fuel availability, citing irregularities affecting 1.29% of outlets.  Following a week-long fuel disruption that caused long queues and shortages, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to increase supply by 10%, monitor stock levels through the Real Time Governance Centre, and address black-marketing. By April 29th, the situation had stabilized with sufficient stocks and reduced queues reported at most outlets.

articles.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund among 15 AMCs to offer voluntary lock-in for folios. Here is how Sebi’s rule works - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has introduced a new framework allowing investors to freeze their mutual fund folios, preventing redemptions, switches, or debits until the lock is removed. The facility, available through MF Central, will initially be offered by 360 One Mutual Fund, Baroda BNP Paribas Mutual Fund, PPFAS Mutual Fund, Franklin Templeton Mutual Fund, Groww Mutual Fund, Helios Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, ITI Mutual Fund, JM Mutual Fund, LIC Mutual Fund, PGIM India Mutual Fund, Samco Mutual Fund, Shriram Mutual Fund, Trust Mutual Fund, and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund. The process for locking or unlocking folios involves six steps, including providing PAN and mobile number verification, selecting the desired transactions to lock or unlock, and receiving OTPs for validation.

articles.title: UK: Ex-mayor jailed for 3 years for helping son hide evidence in teen rape case | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Naheed Ejaz, a former mayor of Bracknell Forest, was sentenced to three years in prison for perverting the course of justice after helping her son conceal evidence related to the rape of a 15-year-old girl. Diwan Khan, her son, was found guilty of rape and given a 12-year sentence with an extended five-year licence period. The court heard that Ejaz delayed officers at her home and spoke to her son in Urdu, giving him time to hide his mobile phone, believed to contain footage of the assault.  The victim described lasting mental health effects from the attack.

articles.title: Trump's war powers deadline expires Friday as officials cite ceasefire loophole - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump faces a critical legal deadline on Friday regarding US military operations against Iran, as his administration argues that a ceasefire effectively ended hostilities under the War Powers Resolution of 1973.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reinforced this position during congressional testimony, claiming the statutory clock pauses or stops in a ceasefire. However, Senator Tim Kaine and legal experts argue that the law does not allow for such an interpretation. The situation has sparked debate within Congress, with Democrats pushing for authorization to end military operations while Republicans remain divided on how to proceed.  The White House maintains that negotiations are ongoing but faces pressure from both sides of the aisle regarding its actions.

articles.title: Footage appears to show Washington press dinner suspect shoot at agent
articles.rephrased_article: CCTV footage released by Jeanine Pirro, US Attorney for DC, shows a suspect shooting at a US Secret Service agent during the White House Correspondents' Dinner. President Donald Trump stated that the incident was not friendly fire and was not caused by his administration.  The footage is being used to dispel any claims of accidental gunfire.

articles.title: Lifetime arrest warrants issued against Malik Riaz, son and co-accused in Bahria Town Karachi landgrab case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: An accountability court issued perpetual arrest warrants for Malik Riaz, his son, and others in the Bahria Town Karachi (BTK) land grab case. The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) filed a reference in 2025 alleging that the owners of Bahria Town, senior PPP leaders, and government officials conspired to cede valuable public property to the company for its BTK project.  The court declared them "proclaimed offenders" and directed the investigating officer to arrest them and produce before the court for further proceedings.

articles.title: Slithering fear: snakebite incidents trigger panic in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dileep, a 38-year-old man, lives in a makeshift hut made from scrap materials near the Kadinamkulam backwaters in Kerala. The dwelling consists of two small rooms and a hall, with items like utensils and firewood scattered around its perimeter.  He is seen staring at a mound of earth where wilted wreaths lie in the sun.

articles.title: US Stock Market | Inside the Rally: What’s fueling Apple Inc. stock surge - Apple Earnings | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Apple reported strong quarterly earnings, exceeding revenue and profit expectations. The company's robust iPhone sales, growth in its services segment, and optimism around artificial intelligence fueled investor confidence and pushed the stock higher. Apple also announced a share buyback program and dividend increase, signaling management's confidence in future cash flows.

articles.title: Edward The Confessor Seal: Lost for 40 years: 1,000-year-old royal seal of Edward the Confessor found in Paris | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Guilhem Dorandeu, a researcher at the University of Exeter, discovered an 11th-century seal once owned by Edward the Confessor in the French National Archives in Paris. The seal, dating back to the 1050s and attached to a document from the Abbey of Saint-Denis, is the only complete example of its design before the Norman Conquest.  The seal's discovery highlights the importance of medieval administrative practices during Edward's reign and reveals that complex legal procedures were already in place by the time of the Norman Conquest.

articles.title: BDA unearths land fraud; FIR against four, including former Revenue Department officer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA)'s vigilance wing has filed a case against four individuals, including an Assistant Commissioner of the Revenue Department, for land fraud involving forged documents and misuse of official positions. The accused allegedly conspired to illegally claim ownership of a prime 2-acre land parcel acquired for J.P. Nagar 8th Phase development.  The investigation revealed that the land had already been compensated to the legal heirs of the original owner after his death, but the accused created fake documents including a forged will and manipulated official records to falsely establish ownership. The suspects are facing charges under various sections of the Indian Penal Code for cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.

articles.title: Powell’s Next Move: Stability at the Fed or Political Storm? - The Big Decision | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell has chosen to remain on the Federal Reserve Board after his term as chair ends, defying long-standing precedent and potentially escalating tensions with the White House. This decision is driven by concerns over legal and political pressures on the Fed, but could also complicate communication and create confusion about policy direction.  Powell's move prevents the administration from immediately filling his seat and may lead to internal divisions within the institution.

articles.title: IHC upholds Capital Development Authority’s decision of canceling One Constitution Avenue lease - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court upheld the decision to cancel the lease of the iconic One Constitution Avenue skyscraper, citing a multi-billion rupee default by the developer, BNP Group. The court found that despite 21 years and numerous financial obligations missed, BNP failed to fulfill its contractual commitments.  The civic agency argued that the company's inability to pay rent and complete the project rendered them ineligible for lease renewal. The case involved prominent personalities who owned apartments in the building, including former Prime Minister Imran Khan. The CDA also cited an investigation by the FIA into potential financial irregularities and a pending case with the National Accountability Bureau.

articles.title: Police say they will charge people with unrest in Alice Springs after arrest over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby | Alice Springs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Northern Territory police arrested 47-year-old Jefferson Lewis in connection with the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. Martin Dole, the Northern Territory police commissioner, stated that Lewis presented himself to a town camp on Thursday night and was subjected to vigilante justice before being taken to hospital. A large crowd gathered outside the hospital, leading to violence and damage to property.  Robin Granites, a senior Warlpiri elder, called for calm and respect for the family while urging the community to grieve. Lia Finocchiaro, the NT chief minister, expressed understanding of the grief but condemned the unrest as unacceptable.

articles.title: Donald Trump: 'Why shouldn’t I?': Trump escalates pressure on Nato allies, signals troop cuts in Italy, Spain over Iran conflict - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has signaled a possible reduction of American troop presence in Italy and Spain, citing their stance on the ongoing Iran war as a reason for his consideration. Trump criticized both countries, accusing them of not being helpful to the US and failing to contribute to efforts to secure the Strait of Hormuz.  This comes after he indicated that Washington is also reviewing troop reductions in Germany, suggesting a broader reassessment of America's military footprint in Europe. Despite these tensions, Germany has sought to maintain diplomatic balance, while Spain condemned Israel's interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla, highlighting fractures within Europe over Middle East policy.

articles.title: Paperless land registration system launched in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Stamps and Registration in Karnataka launched paperless property registration through the Kaveri 2.0 portal at a sub-registrar's office in Chamarajanagar town on April 30th. Inspector General of Registration and Commissioner of Stamps M. P. Mullai Muhilan initiated the process by pressing a button on a computer, marking the first implementation of this system in the state. The initiative will be rolled out across all districts within the next two to three months, offering enhanced security and reliability through digital records and Aadhaar-based registration.  The new system aims to address challenges associated with the traditional paper-based system by eliminating forgery, alterations, and post-registration modifications.

articles.title: Govt of Singapore’s India portfolio: 10 stocks rally up to 70% in a year, 5 new Q4 picks unveiled - Equity exposure | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Government of Singapore (GoS) reported a significant decline in its Indian stock market investments, with portfolio value dropping nearly 29% from the previous quarter.  The GoS's holdings in 47 listed Indian stocks totaled approximately Rs 1,79,480 crore as of April 30, 2026. While some stocks performed well, others experienced significant losses. Notably, Craftsman Automation, Hindalco Industries, Shriram Finance, and Delhivery saw substantial gains, while HDFC Bank, Syngene International, and Info Edge (India) witnessed declines. The GoS also added five new stocks to its portfolio during the March 2026 quarter: TVS Motor Company, Eternal, Delhivery, Vishal Mega Mart, and Tata Motors CV.

articles.title: Donald Trump: Trump admin claims Iran ceasefire 'terminated' hostilities ahead of US-Congress 60-day deadline - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's administration maintains that the US is not at war with Iran, despite the conflict approaching a 60-day legal deadline under the War Powers Resolution.  House Speaker Mike Johnson argues that no active hostilities exist, while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claims the ceasefire halts the clock. However, Democrats challenge this interpretation and warn of potential legal violations. The administration has yet to seek a 30-day extension, leaving the future of US involvement in the conflict uncertain.

articles.title: City Nature Challenge 2026: Andhra, Telangana record surge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: East Coast Conservation Team members and 15 enthusiasts participated in a tidepool exploration at Tenneti Park in Visakhapatnam last weekend. The group, including children as young as six, documented the diverse marine life they observed with photographs uploaded to iNaturalist.  The shared experience aimed to document nature's secrets along the shore.

articles.title: 7 smallcap mutual funds deliver over 25% CAGR in 3 years. Should you pick one? - Smallcap performers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Value Research reports that seven small-cap mutual funds have achieved over 25% cumulative annual growth rate (CAGR) in the past three years. Bandhan Small Cap Fund led with a 32.49% CAGR, followed by ITI Small Cap Fund, Mahindra Manulife Small Cap Fund, Invesco India Smallcap Fund, and Axis Nifty Smallcap 50 Index Fund.  The remaining funds also performed well, with some receiving five-star ratings from the research firm.

articles.title: Fuel hits Rs400 per litre as govt passes on global impact - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Shehbaz Sharif government raised petrol and diesel prices by Rs6.51 and Rs19.39 per litre, respectively, with IMF concurrence, aiming to cushion the impact of rising global oil costs on vulnerable consumers. The government extended fuel subsidies for motorcyclists and the transport sector for an additional month, while also seeking to mitigate potential economic fallout from the Middle East crisis estimated at $10-68 billion.  The Pakistan economy is expected to face significant challenges due to the ongoing conflict in the region, including increased oil import costs, remittance declines, export disruptions, and higher logistics costs.

articles.title: Youth convicted in the 2024 rape and murder of minor girl in Puducherry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Special Judge M.D. Sumathi of the Fast Track Court in Puducherry found Kaka alias Karnas, the lone surviving accused, guilty of all charges related to the 2024 sexual assault and murder of a nine-year-old girl. The judge convicted him on charges including gang rape, murder, kidnapping, and violations under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.  The case is scheduled for sentencing on May 5th.

articles.title: ‘Systemic failures’ made tribal man take his sister’s skeletal remains to bank, finds probe in Odisha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jitu Munda, a tribal man from Odisha, carried his sister's skeletal remains to a bank on Monday (April 27, 2026) in an attempt to prove her death and withdraw funds from her account.  The Odisha government is conducting a preliminary inquiry into the incident, which has raised concerns about systemic failures that may have contributed to the situation. The deceased woman, Kalara Munda, had died two months prior.

articles.title: Global Market Today: S&P 500 index futures rise on earnings, Yen gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Apple Inc. shares rose in extended trading after delivering a strong revenue forecast, contributing to gains for the S&P 500 Index and Nasdaq 100. The Japanese yen weakened slightly against the dollar following intervention by the Finance Ministry in Tokyo.  Investors will monitor how the Federal Reserve navigates inflationary pressures and geopolitical risks as they assess whether AI-led momentum can offset price pressures and geopolitical risks.

articles.title: India’s first green methanol plant to turn Kutch’s most invasive weed into marine fuel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prosopis juliflora, a highly invasive plant known as gando baval in Kutch, is set to be utilized for the production of green methanol and fuel for ocean-going ships.  The plant was introduced by the British in the 1920s and later by the Gujarat forest department in 1961 to combat encroaching salt deserts. The Indian government plans to build its first green methanol production plant using this invasive species.

articles.title: Bajaj Auto board to consider share buyback on May 6 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hero MotoCorp, the maker of Pulsar and Discover motorcycles, is proposing a buyback of its shares. This would be the second such move in two years and comes as the company has seen strong earnings growth driven by premium motorcycle sales and export recovery. The proposed buyback's details, including the quantum, price band, and method, will be announced after next week's board meeting.

articles.title: Tourists flock to Munnar to escape soaring temperatures - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Munnar, a hill station in Kerala, is experiencing a surge of tourists due to its cool temperatures and pleasant weather. Dileep Pottankulam, president of the Munnar Hotel and Resort Association, reported that hotels are fully booked until May 3rd, with many visitors drawn by the refreshing atmosphere compared to other parts of the state facing scorching heat.  G. Sojan, coordinator of the My Munnar Movement, attributed the influx to post-election tourism from Tamil Nadu and a growing number of north Indian tourists. The increase in arrivals has led to heavy traffic congestion in Munnar town.

articles.title: Retail Dilemma: NBFC top guns diverge on deposit rates - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance have announced changes to their deposit rates. Shriram Finance is lowering rates by 15-35 bps on its deposits, while Bajaj Finance has raised rates across maturities from 18 months to 60 months.  Senior citizens will earn an additional 35 bps across tenures. These changes come after Shriram Finance received a rating upgrade, allowing it to borrow at lower rates.

articles.title: Maharashtra Legislative Council elections to be unopposed as Congress backtracks, Shinde fields two candidates - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress has withdrawn its decision to field a candidate for the nine Legislative Council seats in Maharashtra, supporting Ambadas Danve from Shiv Sena UBT after marathon meetings and phone calls between top leaders.  The decision was announced by Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal, who also spoke alongside leaders of the Maha Vikas Aghadi. After a day of speculation, nine candidates filed their nominations for the seats, with each party securing its allotted quota.

articles.title: Metals, PSU banks drag markets down amid currency weakness and global uncertainty - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian stock markets experienced a mixed performance in the week following a historic low for the rupee. The NSE Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex saw gains of 7.5% and 7%, respectively, in April after retreating to multi-year lows in March.  The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened to prevent further depreciation of the rupee, which had breached 95 to the dollar. Some short covering helped the Nifty erase some losses, while sectors like metals and banking saw declines. The market remains cautious due to concerns about global economic factors and inflationary pressures.

articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Mamata Banerjee visits Bhabanipur EVM strong room, warns against counting irregularities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal Chief Minister and TMC supremo, visited an EVM strong room in Bhabanipur, alleging possible tampering with the machines. She demanded transparency and access to the counting area, expressing concern about potential malpractice.  The Election Commission dismissed these claims, stating that poll officials were segregating postal ballots as per due process and strongrooms remained secure. TMC leaders alleged attempts like voter intimidation and misuse of central forces but the BJP refuted these accusations. The situation escalated with protests by TMC candidates outside the venue, demanding increased security measures.

articles.title: The rupee at record low will end India’s cheap-money era - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has signaled a preference to avoid raising interest rates in India, citing the need to manage inflation expectations.  However, pressure from the foreign-exchange market and the war in Iran have led to a weakening of the Indian rupee, prompting concerns about capital outflow and potential demand compression. The central bank's easing measures may be insufficient to prevent higher inflation as energy prices surge and monsoon forecasts suggest potential food shortages.

articles.title: Page Not Found
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu newspaper published a weekly newsletter titled "The View From India" featuring articles on technology, science, health, and gender. The newsletter also included sections for books, data analysis, and education. The Hindu provided reviews of new releases in the book industry and highlighted key stories from various fields.

articles.title: Small-cap stocks rebound in April with best month in a decade - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Smallcap 250 index experienced a significant surge of 17.1% in April, marking its highest monthly gain since 2016. This rally was driven by strong performance from companies like HFCL, Ola Electric Mobility, and Cohance Lifesciences, which saw gains between 56% and 71%.  Feroze Azeez, joint CEO of Anand Rathi Wealth, attributes the trend to a correction in small-cap stocks since 2025, leading investors to seek out undervalued quality businesses. While some experts predict continued growth for the index, others caution that valuations may be overinflated and suggest potential corrections.

articles.title: "Creeped out by her face": Erika Kirk’s eerie reaction on podcast triggers internet frenzy over Candace Owens remark - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Erika Kirk, a podcast host, has become the focus of online controversy after a segment from her show featuring remarks about Candace Owens.  Social media users scrutinized her facial expressions as she discussed the backlash she's faced and comments made by Owens. The video has sparked debate over whether her reaction was genuine or indicative of something deeper. Critics have also questioned the tone of her statements, particularly regarding the death of her husband.

articles.title: Mumbai Pune Missing Link Project opens on May 1. Why is it significant? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Mumbai-Pune Missing Link Project, a 19.84 kilometer stretch of expressway, is set to open to the public on May 1, 2026, marking Maharashtra Day. The project aims to address congestion and hazards on the existing route by bypassing the hazardous Borghat section.  The new expressway will offer reduced travel time of 20-30 minutes compared to the current route, potentially saving fuel worth ₹1 crore daily.

articles.title: Violence in Alice Springs after arrest of man over girl's murder
articles.rephrased_article: Following the arrest of Jefferson Lewis for the murder of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, violence erupted outside an Alice Springs hospital.  A crowd of approximately 400 Aboriginal people gathered, demanding "payback" and accusing police of protecting Lewis. The scene resulted in injuries to several emergency personnel and damage to police vehicles. Martin Dole, the Northern Territory Police Commissioner, stated that Lewis was unconscious when officers found him and charges are expected to be laid against him. Forensic tests will confirm the girl's identity and cause of death.  Lia Finocchiaro, Chief Minister of the Northern Territory, expressed condolences for the loss of Kumanjayi Little Baby and thanked those who participated in the search efforts.

articles.title: Fema employees who criticized Trump cuts reinstated after months on leave | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Fourteen employees of the US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) returned to work after being placed on administrative leave for eight months for signing a public letter criticizing the Trump administration's handling of disaster preparedness. The letter, written in response to the 20th anniversary of Hurricane Katrina, raised concerns about FEMA's capabilities and urged changes to its structure and funding. Markwayne Mullin, the new homeland security secretary, has reversed some policies implemented by his predecessor, Kristi Noem, including the $100,000 spending approval policy, and reinstated the employees. However, experts warn that these actions may be too little, too late as FEMA remains understaffed and underfunded, hindering its ability to respond effectively to future disasters.

articles.title: US Congress passes short-term renewal of Fisa warrantless spying powers | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Congress passed a 45-day extension of the law granting US intelligence agencies warrantless spying powers, section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.  This followed repeated disagreements over its renewal, with hardline Republicans and progressive Democrats clashing over reforms to prevent abuse. The decision comes after previous attempts to extend the program without changes were unsuccessful, highlighting the ongoing debate over warrant requirements for American citizens' communications. While Donald Trump has advocated for renewing the law without changes, privacy advocates argue that it allows surveillance of Americans without warrants, violating their constitutional rights.

articles.title: Former Spandau Ballet singer jailed for 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual assaults | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ross Davidson, a former singer for Spandau Ballet, was sentenced to 14 years in prison for multiple rapes and sexual assaults against six women between August 2013 and December 2019.  The musician, who used the stage name Ross William Wild, was convicted on all charges after two trials, including rape, attempted rape, sexual assault, and voyeurism. During his trial, prosecutors presented evidence of videos depicting Davidson assaulting sleeping women and exploiting their vulnerability. The judge described Davidson's behavior as "adventurous" and lacking respect for the victims.

articles.title: Tony Blair’s thinktank urges Labour to scrap ‘unaffordable’ pension triple lock | State pensions | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Blair’s thinktank, the Tony Blair Institute, has urged the government to scrap the pensions triple lock due to its rising cost and unsustainable nature.  The thinktank argues that Britain's ageing population necessitates a comprehensive overhaul of the state pension system, including replacing the current basic and new state pensions with a "lifespan fund." The Department for Work and Pensions maintains its commitment to the triple lock, stating it will ensure pensioners receive annual pension increases up to £2,100.

articles.title: Trump says Tennessee next to redistrict after US Voting Rights Act ruling | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that Tennessee will redraw its electoral map following a US Supreme Court ruling that weakened the Voting Rights Act. The ruling removes some race-related restrictions on how congressional district maps can be drawn, prompting calls from Republicans to revisit redistricting in several states ahead of the November midterm elections.  The decision has sparked concerns about gerrymandering and could lead to more states redrawing their maps, potentially impacting minority voting power.

articles.title: Uganda court sentences man to death for killing four children at nursery | Child Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Christopher Okello Onyum, a man from Uganda, was sentenced to death for fatally stabbing four children at a nursery school in Kampala.  Onyum entered the school posing as a parent and then locked the gate before attacking the children, aged between one and three years old. The court rejected his claim of insanity and found his actions premeditated, stating that he slaughtered the children "like animals."

articles.title: IShowSpeed seen struggling before collapsing live in St Maarten as viral clip sparks health fears - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular streamer, collapsed during a livestream in St Maarten while interacting with fans.  The incident sparked concern among viewers who noticed signs of exhaustion before the collapse and speculated about possible causes like overwork or heatstroke. IShowSpeed later returned to streaming, appearing fine and sharing his plans for continued travel.

articles.title: Hegseth testifies on Iran war before Senate committee: Key takeaways | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth and Dan Cain, the US Secretary of Defense and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, testified before the Senate Armed Forces Committee on Thursday. They defended the war against Iran, citing a strong munitions stockpile and acknowledging limited details about Russia's assistance to Iran.  Hegseth argued that the 60-day pause in fighting under the War Powers Act does not halt the clock, while Senator Tim Kaine expressed skepticism about this interpretation. Hegseth also faced questions about civilian casualties, including a strike on a girls' school in Minab, and his role in advising President Trump.  Senator Jack Reed questioned whether Hegseth was providing counsel that aligns with the president's needs rather than what is necessary for the war effort.

articles.title: India halted Sindoor on its own terms: Rajnath - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajnath Singh, India's Defence Minister, sharply criticized Pakistan at the National Security Summit 2.0 for its support of terrorism and its role as a global hub for it. He defended India's decision to halt Operation Sindoor voluntarily, emphasizing that India was prepared for a prolonged conflict if necessary.  Singh asserted that India's approach sends a clear message that there will be no distinction between terrorists and their sponsors.

articles.title: D4Vd Case Update: D4vd case update: Celeste Rivas death certificate sparks questions as pregnancy status listed unknown - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An updated death certificate in the Celeste Rivas Hernandez case now states she was "unknown" if pregnant before her death, raising questions about the initial report. The document also confirms the cause of death as "multiple penetrating injuries" and the manner of death as "homicide," with details like time, place, and injury specifics remaining unclear.  The updates come after officials gathered more evidence and are part of an ongoing investigation into D4vd's involvement in the case.

articles.title: Italy told to avoid sharing of defence tech with Pakistan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajnath Singh, India's Defence Minister, met with his Italian counterpart, Guido Crosetto, to discuss a range of issues including regional and global security concerns.  Singh urged Italy to refrain from sharing sensitive defence technologies with Pakistan, emphasizing India's security interests. The two leaders reaffirmed the strong partnership between India and Italy, highlighting avenues for further cooperation in defense industrial development and information sharing. A Bilateral Military Cooperation Plan was exchanged outlining future engagements between the armed forces of both countries.

articles.title: Millions of graphene toothbrushes sold worldwide: Scientists reveal why people are buying them | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: KAIST researchers have clarified the mechanism behind graphene oxide's antibacterial properties.  The study found that graphene oxide selectively binds to a lipid called phosphatidylglycerol, commonly found in bacterial cell membranes but not in human cells, leading to membrane destabilization and bacterial death. This selective targeting could explain the growing popularity of graphene-based hygiene products, though further research is needed before widespread medical use can be confirmed.  The findings suggest that graphene oxide could support future infection control strategies by disrupting microbial structures rather than relying solely on traditional antibiotics.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks petitioner to turn in first-generation copy of leaked Manipur audio to forensic lab - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India ordered the Kuki Organisation for Human Rights to provide the first generation copy of leaked audio tapes allegedly implicating former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh in the 2023-2024 ethnic violence to the national forensic lab. The court stated that further copies would diminish the evidence's authenticity and requested the NGO to locate the original recording device, as it could reveal the whistleblower's identity.  The forensic lab will require six weeks to analyze the tapes and prepare a report.

articles.title: Candace Owens raises doubts over Erika Kirk TPUSA tour future after WHCD shooting and low turnout - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens believes Erika Kirk, the founder of Turning Point USA, may cancel her tour following the shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner. This prediction stems from Owens' observation that Kirk appeared emotional in a video after the incident and suggests she might use it as an excuse to step back from touring.  While there is no official confirmation of cancellation, reports indicate low attendance at some events on the Spring 2026 tour, including a JD Vance event at the University of Georgia where only about a quarter of the venue was filled.

articles.title: Palestine FA chief hits out at Israel federation VP at FIFA Congress | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jibril Rajoub, president of the Palestine Football Association (PFA), refused to stand near Basim Sheikh Suliman, vice-president of the Israel Football Association (IFA) at the 76th FIFA Congress.  Rajoub's refusal came after Infantino, FIFA President, attempted to bring them together. Rajoub argued that the handshake would legitimize Israeli clubs in West Bank settlements and criticized FIFA for not taking action against such clubs. The PFA has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport against FIFA’s decision not to sanction Israel over its clubs in West Bank settlements.

articles.title: Australia news live: Malarndirri McCarthy calls for calm amid ‘deep grief’ and anger in Alice Springs; Coalition backs gun reforms after Bondi report | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Malarndirri McCarthy, the minister for Indigenous Australians, addressed the community following the arrest of Jefferson Lewis in connection with the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby.  Police responded to reports of a violent assault and were attacked when they intervened. The Northern Territory police commissioner, Martin Dole, stated that while there was damage to emergency services vehicles and injuries sustained by officers, the violence was not representative of the community's character.  The investigation is ongoing, but Mr Lewis has been transported to Darwin.

articles.title: ECI introduces new QR code-based ID cards for counting centres - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India introduced a QR code-based photo identity card system for counting centres in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Puducherry.  This new system aims to prevent unauthorized individuals from entering the counting centers during upcoming elections on May 4th. The system will be rolled out to all future general and byelections for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

articles.title: Islamic Sect Arrests: UK: ‘Islamic sect’ members arrested following allegations of sexual abuse and slavery - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light (AROPL)
articles.rephrased_article: Police raided multiple properties in Crewe, England on Wednesday, arresting 10 members of the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light (AROPL) for various offenses including rape, sexual assault, and human trafficking.
