The group's spiritual leader, Abdullah Hashem Aba Al-Safiq, was among those arrested alongside seven men and three women suspected of modern slavery and sexual assault. Cheshire police launched an investigation into allegations of serious sexual offences, forced marriage, and slavery that reportedly occurred in 2023 involving a woman who was a member of the group.

articles.title: Arsenal vs Fulham: Premier League – teams, start, lineups, title race | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal will aim to re-establish a six-point lead over Manchester City in the Premier League title race when they host Fulham at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.  The Gunners, who were overtaken by City after their 2-1 victory last month, are seeking to secure their first English crown since 2004. Fulham, currently in 10th place, will be looking to capitalize on any potential Arsenal fatigue following their Champions League semi-final loss to Atletico Madrid.  The match is the 67th between the two sides, with Arsenal holding a significant advantage.

articles.title: Brazil’s congress approves bill reducing prison sentence of former president Jair Bolsonaro | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Brazil's lower house overturned President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's veto of a bill reducing the prison sentence of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of attempting a coup. The bill, which reduces Bolsonaro's sentence from 27 years and three months to 22 years and one month, will also shorten his time in closed regime, potentially allowing him to move to an open regime as early as 2028.  The decision is seen by many as further evidence that Lula will face a difficult election against Bolsonaro's son, Flávio Bolsonaro.

articles.title: US passes law to resume DHS funding and end partial government shutdown | Police News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US House of Representatives passed a funding measure to resume funding for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ending an 11-week partial government shutdown. The bill excluded Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), which had been a point of contention between Democrats and Republicans.  The passage was welcomed by DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who blamed Democrats for the shutdown, while Democratic Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren called for reforms to ICE and CBP.

articles.title: Trump to lift tariffs on scotch whisky after king’s US visit | Trump tariffs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced the removal of tariffs on whisky imports from Scotland, stating he was motivated by a desire to strengthen ties with the UK after King Charles’s visit to the White House. The move, which benefits both the US and Scottish whisky industry, is seen as a significant boost for the sector following years of trade restrictions.  The Scotch Whisky Association (SWA) welcomed the decision, stating it provides much-needed relief during a challenging period for the industry.

articles.title: Erika Kirk faces fresh backlash as Ashley St Clair questions Druski skit reaction after Charlie Kirk show clip - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ashley St. Clair reacted to Erika Kirk's comments about a Druski skit, comparing her response to how Charlie Kirk might have handled it.  St. Clair criticized Kirk's anger toward the comedian and advised her to step back from public pressure, suggesting she focus on family and take time away from the controversy. St. Clair also questioned those advising Kirk, stating they were not giving her the right advice.

articles.title: ‘I have five’: Ronaldo shuts down disrespect after problematic post-match drama in Al Nassr vs Al Ahli | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: In a tense match between Al Nassr and Al Ahli, Cristiano Ronaldo scored the winning goal to secure an 8-point lead in the Saudi Pro League title race. The game saw heated confrontations between players, including Merih Demiral's gestures referencing Al Ahli's AFC Champions League titles.  Demiral was involved in several altercations with Al Nassr players and even held up his AFC Champions League medal after the match, sparking further controversy. Ronaldo, named Man of the Match, responded to the taunts by holding up five fingers, highlighting his own Champions League wins. The incident drew attention to the league's direction and raised concerns about its image, with Ronaldo calling for a more professional approach.

articles.title: Trumps says Iran can play at World Cup in US after FIFA confirmation | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated he is "OK" with Iran playing in the upcoming World Cup, following confirmation from FIFA President Gianni Infantino.  Infantino confirmed that Iran will play their matches in the US as scheduled. The decision comes after Iranian officials considered shifting games to Mexico due to tensions surrounding the US-Israel war on Iran. Iranian football federation (FFIRI) President Mehdi Taj and colleagues left Canada after a clash with Canadian border officials, citing "insult" from immigration officers.

articles.title: Senate Republicans again block effort to halt Trump’s war in Iran | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Senate voted down a Democratic war powers resolution aimed at limiting the US's military action in Iran, with 47 senators voting against it and two Republicans, Susan Collins and Rand Paul, supporting it. The vote was the sixth this year on such a resolution, all of which have failed along party lines.  The War Powers Resolution requires the president to terminate military campaigns after 60 days unless Congress declares war or authorizes further action.

articles.title: US stocks today: US market ends higher, S&P 500, Nasdaq notch biggest monthly gains in years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Economic data showed the U.S. economy grew at a healthy pace, easing investor fears and pushing all three major U.S. stock indexes sharply higher. Caterpillar shares helped power the Dow Jones Industrial Average, while technology limited gains in the Nasdaq.  The Federal Reserve maintained its key interest rate, acknowledging uncertainties related to heightened crude prices due to the conflict in the Middle East.

articles.title: 'Don't want to look 20 pounds heavier': Trump jabs reports of wearing bulletproof vest during White House dinner attack - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump dismissed reports of a bulletproof vest during the White House Correspondents' Dinner, stating he doesn't want to appear "20 pounds" heavier.  He acknowledged that security measures are sometimes considered but prefers not to appear overly protected. Trump stated he avoids thinking about potential future attacks and focuses on his duties. Authorities have charged a suspect with attempted assassination following the incident.

articles.title: Unrest in Alice Springs after Jefferson Lewis arrested over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby | Northern Territory | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dozens of local people gathered outside a hospital in Alice Springs where Jefferson Lewis, 47, was being treated for injuries sustained prior to his arrest.  Police confirmed the arrest of Lewis after he was located and taken to the hospital following an investigation into the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. The girl's body was discovered by a police search and rescue team on Thursday, after she went missing from her town camp on Saturday.  The Northern Territory chief minister, Lia Finocchiaro, expressed the grief felt across the territory.

articles.title: Britain extracted 25 million years of life and labour through slavery in Barbados: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from Public Interest Experts, a non-profit organization, have presented a report estimating the economic harm caused by British colonial practices in Barbados. The report, based on historical records and economic modeling, suggests that enslaved Africans lost nearly 25 million years of life and contributed £400 billion to £560 billion worth of unpaid labor.  The study aims to quantify historical harm rather than set a price tag for reparations, with the goal of fostering understanding and reconciliation. The findings highlight the lasting impact of slavery on wealth gaps and economic development in Barbados and other Caribbean nations.

articles.title: Louisiana primaries will proceed with US House races on ballot but votes ‘will not be counted’, secretary of state says – live | US voting rights | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais has led to the suspension of House primaries in Louisiana ahead of the May 16th elections. Nancy Landry, Louisiana's secretary of state, certified an emergency and suspended the primaries due to the court's decision that redrawing congressional maps is necessary.  Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, plans to counter Republican gerrymandering by targeting key states for redistricting maneuvers in advance of the 2028 elections. Jena Griswold, Colorado's secretary of state, supports independent redistricting and encourages voters to weigh in on map changes.  Donald Trump criticized the court decision and called for Louisiana voters to remove Senator Bill Cassidy from office.  Al Sharpton believes the ruling will inspire a movement for racial equality and encourage more voter participation.

articles.title: Top 10 countries with the most skyscrapers in the world 2026: China, US, UAE and other leading nations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China, the United States, the United Arab Emirates, and Malaysia are among the top countries with the most skyscrapers.  China dominates this list, fueled by urbanization and industrial development, while the United States boasts iconic skyscrapers in cities like New York and Chicago. Dubai in the UAE has rapidly transformed its skyline with luxury-focused high-rises. Malaysia, particularly Kuala Lumpur, features a dense cluster of modern towers.  These countries are pushing the boundaries of skyscraper construction, driven by economic ambition, urban growth, and demand for space.

articles.title: Has the US Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act – and how? | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court ruled that a Louisiana electoral map was unconstitutional, effectively weakening the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The court's 6-3 decision found that the map, which created two Black-majority congressional districts, relied too heavily on race and violated the Constitution's prohibition against intentional racial discrimination.  The ruling is seen as a victory for Louisiana Republicans and President Donald Trump, who had supported the challenge to the Voting Rights Act. The decision could have far-reaching implications for redistricting efforts nationwide, potentially allowing state legislatures to redraw electoral maps in ways that dilute minority voting power.  Legal experts warn that this ruling may weaken protections established by the Voting Rights Act and allow partisan manipulation of congressional districts.

articles.title: Trump aide Josh Gruenbaum dropped from Ukraine, Iran roles: Here's why he was sidelined - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Josh Gruenbaum, a former advisor to Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, will no longer work on key foreign policy issues related to Russia-Ukraine or Iran. He is now focusing exclusively on Gaza-related efforts through the Board of Peace, an international organization with links to the US government.  The White House stated Gruenbaum will continue to advance the President's agenda of enhancing global stability in his new role. Despite concerns about his working style and internal communications, Gruenbaum remains an important part of efforts aimed at promoting stability and development in the Middle East.

articles.title: Starmer restores powers to ousted hereditary peers in Lords shake-up | Lords reform | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has granted life peerages to 15 Conservative, two Labour, and nine crossbench peers whose seats were abolished in the House of Lords. This concession was made to appease opposition parties who demanded compensation for removed peers and end a long battle over abolishing hereditary peers. The move comes as 92 hereditary peers lost their seats this week and is expected to be announced before the king's speech, with further updates to the Lords including a participation requirement and retirement age being implemented later this year.

articles.title: Mazagon Dock Q4 Results: Profit jumps 42% to Rs 464 crore; co declares Rs 4.62 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mazagon Dock's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 4.62 per share for the fiscal year ending March 2026. Revenue from operations increased by 16% year-over-year to Rs 3,684 crore, driven by higher project execution. Profit before tax rose sharply by 54% to Rs 625 crore, while total expenses increased 8% to Rs 3,340 crore. The company reported a total income of Rs 13,982.4 crore for the fiscal year ending March 2026, with an annual profit before tax growth of 4%.

articles.title: 'Time to say goodbye' :Jeffrey Epstein's suicide note revealed via former cellmate account, remains sealed by court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeffrey Epstein, a disgraced financier, wrote a note before his death in 2019 while incarcerated at a federal jail in New York City. The note, discovered by his former cellmate Nicholas Tartaglione, suggested that Epstein maintained his innocence despite ongoing investigations and indicated he felt safe sharing a cell with him.  The note was later verified as having been written by Epstein and became part of Tartaglione’s legal case, but it has remained confidential since then. Despite its potential relevance to the investigation into Epstein’s death, the note was not included in official investigations.

articles.title: Chhattisgarh Assembly passes resolution for one-third quota for women in legislative bodies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Chhattisgarh Assembly passed a resolution on Thursday calling for the immediate implementation of one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures after delimitation. This follows the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which aimed to expedite women's reservation by redistributing Lok Sabha seats based on the 2011 Census.  The bill failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha and since then, BJP governments have convened special sessions of state assemblies to push for its implementation.

articles.title: Laurus Labs Q4 Results: Cons PAT increased 19% to Rs 279 crore, revenue rises 5% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company's PAT increased 11% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 252 crore in Q3FY26, while revenue rose 2% sequentially to Rs 1,778 crore.  EBITDA reached Rs 523 crore, a 10% increase from the previous year, and gross margins improved to 61.4%. The company's board approved a second interim dividend of Rs 1.20 per share. The company reported net profit for FY26 at Rs 889 crore, a significant increase from Rs 358 crore in FY25.

articles.title: Ishowspeed: IShowSpeed plans space livestream after completing world tour goal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular streamer, announced his ambitious plans to stream live from space after completing his planned world tour. He has already visited 96 countries and aims to visit all remaining nations in the next few years. IShowSpeed expressed interest in collaborating with Elon Musk to make this dream a reality.  He also mentioned aspirations to explore underwater, potentially inspired by his love for the anime *One Piece*.

articles.title: Iran confirmed to play at World Cup according to FIFA chief Infantino | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup in the United States despite the country's absence from the FIFA Congress due to visa issues.  Iranian football federation officials, including President Mehdi Taj, were denied entry into Canada after what Tehran described as "unacceptable behaviour" by Canadian immigration authorities. Iran has qualified for the tournament but its participation is complicated by tensions surrounding the US-Israel war on the country and concerns about ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

articles.title: Odisha Assembly: BJP, BJD and Congress resort to political one-upmanship over women’s reservation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi addressed the special session of the state legislative assembly on Thursday, April 30, 2026, emphasizing women's active participation in Indian democracy.  He assured that reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies would be implemented from 2029. Naveen Patnaik, Leader of Opposition, criticized the BJP's handling of the issue, arguing that it was a ploy to push through delimitation without proper discussion. The BJD also highlighted its past support for women's reservation, while the Congress demanded immediate implementation of the already passed 33% reservation bill.

articles.title: Value 360 Communications IPO: Rs 41.7 crore issue opens May 4. Check price band, GMP, other details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Value 360 Communications Limited, an integrated communications and marketing solutions provider, is launching an initial public offering (IPO) with a price range of Rs 95 to Rs 98 per share. The company plans to use the proceeds for infrastructure expansion, technology investment, influencer marketing platform acquisition, and potential future acquisitions. Horizon Management Private Limited has been appointed as lead manager for the IPO, while KFin Technologies Limited will serve as registrar.

articles.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Immanuel Kant: “One who makes himself a worm cannot complain afterwards if people step on him.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Immanuel Kant, a German philosopher, famously stated, "One who makes himself a worm cannot complain afterwards if people step on him." This quote emphasizes the connection between self-respect and how others treat us. Kant believed that individuals should value their own dignity and act in ways that reflect that worth.  This idea aligns with modern discussions about self-esteem, boundaries, and personal responsibility. The quote serves as a reminder that our actions can influence how we are treated by others, prompting us to prioritize self-respect and maintain a sense of personal worth.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet approves Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district at a cost of ₹18,133 crore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government approved a ₹18,133 crore Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district, which will involve acquiring 7,404 acres of land from nine villages. The Cabinet also gave its approval to the Hyderabad-Bengaluru High Speed Rail Corridor and provided administrative support for the Chennai-Bengaluru high speed rail corridor. Additionally, the government approved a ₹600 crore project for the redevelopment of slums inhabited by minorities across 11 corporations in the state.

articles.title: Hindustan Labs, RK Steel get Sebi nod to launch IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Laboratories, a generic pharmaceutical company, is planning to raise capital through an initial public offering (IPO) with the proceeds primarily earmarked for working capital and general corporate purposes. The IPO will be managed by Choice Capital Advisors Private Limited.  The company's business model focuses on supplying affordable medicines to government institutions, including those within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and state governments.

articles.title: Mother convicted of baby’s murder after blaming another child - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nicole Blain was found guilty of murdering her infant daughter, Thea June Wilson, in Glasgow. Evidence presented during the trial showed that Blain inflicted fatal head injuries on the child and attempted to blame another child within the household. Medical records, witness testimony, and a social worker's account all pointed towards Blain being responsible for the baby's death. The jury found her guilty of murder, and sentencing is scheduled for May 28th.

articles.title: KEERA to be established for structural reforms in engineering education: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has decided to establish the Karnataka Engineering Education Reform Authority (KEERA), following recommendations from an Expert Committee on Reforms in Technical Education. The committee, led by former director of IIIT-B, S. Sadagopan, proposed structural reforms for engineering education.  The government plans to bring separate legislation to establish KEERA and will discuss the matter soon.

articles.title: Sebi introduces fast-track route for AIF launches to boost capital deployment - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the market regulator, has revised procedures for processing placement memorandums to reduce delays in fund launches. These changes aim to enhance efficiency in capital deployment and support faster execution of investment strategies by AIFs. The regulator also simplified the accredited investor framework earlier this year to ease operational bottlenecks for AIFs while maintaining prudential safeguards.  These revisions allow AIF investment managers to finalize and execute contribution agreements with investors before formal accreditation, ensuring key prudential norms are not compromised.

articles.title: 'Make Pluto a planet again': Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman calls for status restoration at US Senate hearing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman reiterated his support for restoring Pluto's status as a planet during a US Senate hearing.  He stated that Nasa researchers are working on studies to reopen the scientific debate, echoing previous views expressed in media interviews. The International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 due to its failure to meet the "cleared its orbit" requirement. This decision sparked ongoing debate among planetary scientists and public figures who argue for a broader definition of a planet.  Nasa's New Horizons spacecraft, which provided the first close-up images of Pluto, remains the only mission to have flown past it.

articles.title: US House votes to end partial government shutdown over immigration operations
articles.rephrased_article: The US House of Representatives voted to approve a Senate-passed bill, ending the 76-day partial government shutdown. The bill restores funding to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and concludes the longest shutdown in the agency's history.  President Donald Trump supported the measure, which does not include new funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) or US Border Patrol. The bill now goes to the president for signature.

articles.title: Indonesian soldiers accused of acid attack. What happened and why? | Human Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An Indonesian trial has begun for four soldiers accused of carrying out an acid attack on activist Andrie Yunus, who had criticized the expanding role of the military in government. The attack, which left Yunus blind in one eye and with burns on his face and body, is seen as part of a broader pattern of repression in Indonesia, according to rights groups and analysts.  The United Nations, Amnesty International, and other organizations have condemned the attack, raising concerns about impunity and the fairness of the trial, which is being held in a military court. The case highlights growing public dissatisfaction with the military's influence in government, fueled by economic inequality and perceived attacks on dissent.

articles.title: Golders Green attack suspect named as Essa Suleiman, 45 | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Essa Suleiman, a 45-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of murder after stabbing two Jewish men in Golders Green. Suleiman had been referred to the Prevent program six years prior and cleared of being a terrorist threat. The attack is being treated as terrorism by police who are investigating whether Suleiman targeted Jewish people.  The investigation is ongoing, with officers believing he acted alone.

articles.title: High Court directs FRRO to extend Russian woman’s visa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka of the Telangana High Court granted a Russian woman, Alena Evgenievna Pavlova, an extension on her visa due to humanitarian and compassionate grounds. The judge also ruled against imposing overstay penalties on Pavlova, who had been actively involved in translating Indian literature into Russian and volunteering with various organizations.  The court acknowledged the exceptional circumstances of Pavlova's situation following the death of her husband and her subsequent request for an extension.

articles.title: As Trump nukes science, is India's brain drain ready for 'brain regain'? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has dismissed the National Science Board, an independent body overseeing the National Science Foundation (NSF), America's primary engine for basic research. This action, delivered via a terse email last week, has led to the removal of three prominent Indian-American scientists from the board: Sudarsanam Babu, Arun Majumdar, and Suresh Garimella. The move is part of a broader trend by the Trump administration to dismantle the country's scientific architecture through the termination of advisory panels, cancellation of NSF grants, and proposed budget cuts to major research agencies. This has resulted in funding uncertainty for laboratories and universities, forcing hiring freezes and graduate program cuts, and prompting many foreign-origin scientists to consider relocating abroad.

articles.title: PTI leaders turn up for Adiala jail visit following 2-week gap - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI leaders, including Salman Akram Raja, attempted to meet with incarcerated party founder Imran Khan at Adiala jail on Thursday after the Islamabad High Court granted him twice-a-week meetings. Despite the court order, Imran's family and party leaders have been largely restricted from meeting with him. The PTI Secretary General withdrew a previous list of leaders intending to meet Imran and submitted a new one, but all six leaders were again denied access.  The party plans to appeal to the Supreme Court for their petition to be heard.

articles.title: Bowring tragedy: CM orders suspension of official, Lokayukta takes up inquiry, police file only UDR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the tragic collapse of a compound wall at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, which killed seven people, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah ordered the suspension of the executive engineer involved and directed a notice to be issued to the hospital authorities. The Lokayukta has registered a suo motu case and initiated an inquiry into the incident.  The Bengaluru City Police filed an Unnatural Death Report (UDR) but have not yet registered an FIR against any authorities for alleged negligence. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collapse, with experts from the Public Works Department and the India Meteorological Department consulted.

articles.title: Forget Ronaldo: João Cancelo set for historic record no player has ever achieved if Barca win La Liga | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: João Cancelo is on the verge of becoming the first player to win four of Europe's "Big Five" leagues.  He could achieve this milestone if Barcelona wins La Liga, completing a sequence that includes titles in Italy, England, Germany and Spain. This would make him the only player with league titles in five different countries. The Portuguese full-back has already won three of these titles, including one with Barcelona, and is on track to add a fourth if they win the title in 2025-26.  His career achievements are comparable to those of Cristiano Ronaldo, but differ in terms of variety rather than volume.

articles.title: Railways Minister flags off first Jammu-Srinagar direct train service on ‘historic day’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw and J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah celebrated the launch of the first direct train service between Jammu city and Srinagar city.  Vaishnaw described the service as a "gamechanger" for the region's economy, highlighting its impact on cargo movement and tourism. The new rail line connects the Kashmir division with the Jammu division, offering seamless travel to pilgrimage destinations like Shree Mata Vaishno Devi and Shri Amarnath temple. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is credited with realizing the dream of railway connectivity in the Kashmir Valley.

articles.title: F1 to return in 2027 to country absent from calendar since 2021 under new multi-year agreement | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Formula 1 will return to Türkiye in 2027 with a multi-year agreement for the Turkish Grand Prix, scheduled through 2031. The race will be held at Istanbul Park, marking its comeback after being absent since 2021. The event is part of a reshaped Formula 1 calendar that includes two dropped races and potential expansion to new venues like Thailand.  The return is supported by strong audience figures within Türkiye, with a growing social media following.  Formula 1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali expressed excitement about returning to Istanbul, calling it a "cultural gateway between Europe and Asia."

articles.title: Freshly transferred Justices Sattar, Kayani to hear cases at PHC, LHC from coming week - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Babar Sattar and Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, who were recently transferred from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to the Peshawar High Court (PHC) and Lahore High Court (LHC), respectively, have been included in their new court's rosters. The transfers were approved by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) amidst criticism from lawyers’ bodies.  The JCP also decided that any vacancy arising as a result of the transfer of judges would be filled through transfer only, and such slots would not be treated as vacancies for initial appointment.

articles.title: Uganda nursery attack: Christopher Okello Onyum sentenced to death for murder of Kampala toddlers
articles.rephrased_article: Christopher Okello Onyum, a 38-year-old man with Ugandan and US citizenship, was sentenced to death by hanging for the murder of four toddlers at a nursery school in Kampala.  Onyum admitted to the crime but later pleaded not guilty, claiming mental illness prevented him from forming intent to kill. Justice Alice Komuhangi Khauka ruled that Onyum was "very sane" on the day of the attack and sentenced him accordingly. The prosecution presented evidence including DNA, CCTV footage, and eyewitness accounts, which led to his conviction.

articles.title: HC orders inquiry on ‘erring officers’ who did not act against illegal structures at Salkam cheruvu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court ordered a detailed inquiry into construction violations at the Barrister Fatima Owaisi Education Campus within the Full Tank Level/buffer zone of Salkam Cheruvu. The HYDRAA, Municipal Administration and Urban Development, GHMC, and HMDA were instructed to report by July 7th on how officials permitted structures in the buffer zone.  The judge also directed the School Education department to ensure students are not disturbed.

articles.title: Move over TACO, NACHO takes over: Trump earns new nickname amid oil disruption from Strait of Hormuz blockade - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has earned a new nickname, "NACHO," as tensions over the Strait of Hormuz fuel market and political commentary. Javier Blas, a Bloomberg columnist, coined the term to reflect growing skepticism that the dispute will be resolved quickly.  The Strait of Hormuz handles 20% of global crude oil shipments and any disruption has immediate effects on global energy supply and prices. The US administration has imposed restrictions on Iranian ports and shipping activity while Iran has tightened its control over the strait, but negotiations between the US, Israel and Iran have stalled. Despite a ceasefire framework, Kush Desai, White House spokesperson, pushed back against the "NACHO" label, questioning critics of the administration's trade and policy record.

articles.title: Africa and Asia back Infantino for unique fourth term as FIFA president | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has received strong backing from the Confederations of Africa (CAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) for his potential re-election in 2027. Both regional confederations have pledged their support, accounting for a significant portion of FIFA's voting power.  Infantino's bid is further bolstered by previous endorsements from CONMEBOL, adding to his momentum as he seeks a fourth term at the helm of world football.

articles.title: Odissi elegance casts a spell at Koodalmanikyam festival - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhulita Mohapatra and the Nrityantar Dance Ensemble performed a captivating Odissi dance recital at the Koodalmanikyam Temple in Irinjalakuda as part of the annual Koodalmanikyam Temple Festival 2026. The performance, which included devotional pieces like Jagannath Ashtakam and Malhar Pallavi, showcased the grace and rhythmic beauty of Odissi dance.  The recital was further enhanced by a live orchestra and a special appearance by five-year-old Mihika as baby Krishna.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Obsessing over Charlie Kirk’s spouse": Laura Loomer blasts Candace Owens' husband George Farmer over alleged DUI claims in viral post - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer's viral post on social media has sparked controversy surrounding Candace Owens and her husband, George Farmer.  Loomer alleges that Farmer was involved in multiple accidents, including a DUI, and suggests there is documentation supporting these claims. The post also criticizes Owens for allegedly misleading her audience about the incidents. Owens has not publicly responded to the allegations, but the situation highlights the challenges of verifying information shared on social media platforms.

articles.title: Make right to vote a fundamental right, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called for the right to vote to be made a fundamental right, arguing that it is currently not justiciable. He criticized the Election Commission of India (ECI) and its current leadership, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and a lack of transparency.  Ramesh also expressed skepticism towards exit polls, citing their inaccuracy in previous elections. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi shared a video highlighting concerns from a delegation from Ladakh regarding suppression of democratic rights and land grabs by powerful individuals.

articles.title: 'They call Trump Nazi, Hitler & still attend': Erika Kirk hits out at journalists for 'ultimate hypocrisy' at White House dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Erika Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA, criticized journalists for using extreme language to describe President Donald Trump, accusing them of hypocrisy and fueling a hostile environment.  Kirk attended the White House Correspondents' Dinner to confront journalists about their coverage of her and her late husband, Charlie Kirk, who was murdered in 2025. She claimed that the attack on the dinner was linked to a broader climate of dehumanization and criticized journalists for prioritizing capturing footage over safety during the incident.  Kirk also accused political opponents and commentators of contributing to a hostile environment.

articles.title: Iran, protests, human rights – all to know about the 76th FIFA Congress | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The 76th FIFA Congress in Canada will be overshadowed by geopolitical tensions, human rights concerns, and logistical issues related to the upcoming World Cup. The Iranian delegation departed from Canada after citing mistreatment by immigration officials, while Amnesty International urged FIFA President Gianni Infantino to ensure human rights are protected at the tournament.  The congress also saw protests from local fans in Vancouver against the potential relocation of the Vancouver Whitecaps soccer team to Las Vegas.

articles.title: Two men sentenced to life imprisonment for murder - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Principal District and Sessions Court sentenced two men, Goni Ramu (26) and Pasupuleti Sandeep Kumar (25), to life imprisonment for the murder of Vaka Ashok (29) in Nellore. The incident occurred on October 15, 2024, when a heated argument between the accused and the victim escalated into a stabbing attack by Ramu who used a knife from his waist.

articles.title: Machines take charge: China to deploy 8,500 robots in $1B push to automate its power grid | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: State Grid Corporation of China is investing $1 billion to procure 8,500 robots for grid operations. The robots will assist with inspection and maintenance across substations and transmission networks, reducing risks to human workers and improving efficiency. China's initiative reflects a broader effort to advance industrial robotics and AI-enabled infrastructure. These robots are designed to detect faults, monitor equipment conditions, and perform basic maintenance tasks in challenging environments.  The deployment is expected to continue through 2026.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz extends fuel subsidy for motorcyclists, goods transport by one month - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended fuel subsidies for motorcyclists, public and goods transport by one month. The decision was made to provide relief to economically vulnerable groups during the current situation.  He also directed transporters not to increase fares and instructed for effective monitoring of the measures. Shehbaz Sharif emphasized that providing relief to the common man remains a priority and hopes regional stability will lead to fuel price stabilization.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Marie Curie: "There are sadistic scientists who hurry to hunt down error instead of establishing the truth." | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marie Curie's quote, "There are sadistic scientists who hurry to hunt down error instead of establishing the truth," highlights the importance of finding the truth in scientific discovery.  While criticism is essential for quality control and progress, it shouldn't overshadow the pursuit of accurate knowledge. Curie, a scientist known for her meticulous research, emphasized the need for patience, accuracy, and collaboration to achieve true understanding. Her work exemplifies this approach, emphasizing that real progress comes from dedication to truth-seeking rather than simply finding mistakes.

articles.title: Telangana Govt extends Prajavani to RDO level with immediate effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Government has expanded its Prajavani public grievance redressal initiative to the revenue division level, with weekly sessions conducted by sub-collectors or revenue divisional officers. The program will be phased out to the mandal level in the future.  The initiative mandates registration of grievances online and provides a dedicated portal for tracking and monitoring resolution progress. District Collectors oversee district-level Prajavani sessions, where all department officers are present to address citizen concerns.

articles.title: Most decorated woman athlete with seven Olympic golds planning stunning LA28 comeback at 42 | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Allyson Felix, the most decorated woman in Olympic track and field history, is planning a return to competition with the aim of reaching the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.  The Olympic organizing committee member has set her sights on competing at age 42, after retiring following the Tokyo Olympics cycle. She aims to participate in the opening ceremony and hopes to meet qualification requirements for the US Olympic trials in 2027. Felix's return is driven by a desire to experience the home crowd atmosphere of the Games, despite acknowledging the challenges of competing at this stage in her career.

articles.title: ‘Drishyam 3’ teaser: Past haunts Mohanlal’s Georgekutty in this suspense thriller - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Drishyam 3, the third installment in the popular suspense-thriller franchise, saw its teaser unveiled on April 29, 2026. The film, directed by Jeethu Joseph and starring Mohanlal, is scheduled for release on May 21, 2026.  Produced by Antony Perumbavoor under Aashirvad Cinemas, the movie also features a star-studded cast including Meena, Siddique, Asha Sharath, Murali Gopy, Ansiba Hassan and Esther Anil. The teaser highlights the character of Georgekutty facing his past.  The film will be presented by Dr Jayantilal Gada (Pen Studios) and Panorama Studios.

articles.title: ‘No place in Gulf, except at bottom of its waters’: Iran’s Khamenei slams ‘Great Satan’ US, rejects nuclear curbs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, criticized the United States, calling it the "Great Satan" and asserting that Iran's nuclear and missile capabilities are non-negotiable. He stated that Iran's technological and military advancements are national assets protected by its people and will not be compromised.  Khamenei also emphasized Iran's regional influence in the Persian Gulf, advocating for a new management framework for the Strait of Hormuz to shape the region's future.

articles.title: Bengaluru weather highlights: Orange alert issued for Bengaluru, south Karnataka districts; traffic police release advisory for commuters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CM Siddaramaiah visited injured individuals after a portion of the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital compound wall collapsed in Shivajinagar, killing seven people.  The Medical Education Minister Sharanprakash R. Patil ordered safety audits for government hospital buildings. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for Bengaluru, urging caution from motorists due to heavy rainfall.

articles.title: Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf threatens to ban NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani from UK over kohinoor return call | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zia Yusuf, a senior figure in Reform UK, has threatened to ban New York’s mayor Zohran Mamdani from entering Britain after Mamdani called for the return of the Kohinoor diamond to India.  Yusuf criticized Mamdani's comments ahead of his meeting with King Charles III, stating he would take action if in office and that the diamond will "stay" in London. Critics question whether Yusuf's stance aligns with Reform UK's stated support for free speech.

articles.title: Gujarat High Court, after attire remarks in court, asks IIT Gandhinagar to ‘show sympathy’ to suspended student - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat High Court orally advised the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IIT-Gn) to show sympathy towards a postgraduate student who was previously reprimanded for her attire. The court acknowledged the student's age and potential lack of understanding of consequences, stating that her conduct did not warrant suspension despite initial concerns about decorum in court.  The court emphasized that past actions played a role in its decision.

articles.title: Punjab Assembly passes film city, environment, wildlife bills amid uproar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab Assembly passed the Punjab Film City Authority Bill 2026 after a contentious session marked by disagreements between the ruling and opposition parties.  Marriyum Aurangzeb, Senior Minister, defended the bill as an economic growth initiative, while opposition members criticized it for diverting funds from critical sectors like education and health. Ijaz Shafi accused the government of prioritizing entertainment over essential services, prompting Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan to order his controversial remarks expunged.  Despite interruptions and protests, the bill was passed, with Marriyum Aurangzeb emphasizing its regulatory mechanisms for the film industry.

articles.title: Syngene shares zoom 17% even as firm’s Q4 net profit drops 19% YoY. What's driving the surge? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Syngene International reported a multi-fold increase in net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26, reaching Rs 153 crore.  The company's revenue grew nearly 2% to Rs 1,036.5 crore. Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, who transitioned from Non Executive Chairman to Executive Chairman, expressed optimism about the company's future growth. Peter Bains, Managing Director and CEO, highlighted the company's steady momentum despite challenges posed by a single large-molecule biologics client.  Siddharth Mittal, appointed Managing Director and CEO effective July 1, 2026, will succeed Peter Bains. Macquarie maintained its 'Outperform' rating on Syngene shares with a target price of Rs 835 apiece.

articles.title: Vedanta's 65% share price crash an illusion, the stock is down just 5%. Here's why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta's shares plummeted by 64.9% on Thursday, marking a significant drop from the previous close and reducing its market capitalization to Rs 1.13 lakh crore. The stock opened sharply lower at Rs 289.50 after closing at Rs 773.60 on Wednesday. Vedanta's demerger into four separate listed entities, including Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Power, Vedanta Oil & Gas, and Vedanta Steel & Iron Ore, began trading without the value of these units. The demerger was approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in December 2022.  Vedanta's Chairman, Anil Agarwal, believes the restructuring will unlock shareholder value over time.

articles.title: HUL shares drop over 4% despite Q4 topping Street estimates; profit jumps 21% YoY to Rs 2,464 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) reported a 7.6% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 16,351 crore for the quarter ending March 2025. EBITDA rose by 3.2% to Rs 3,877 crore, with EBITDA margins improving by 70 basis points YoY.  The Home Care segment saw its strongest performance in 11 quarters, while Beauty & Wellbeing delivered 8% USG and Personal Care grew 5%. The company proposed a final dividend of Rs 22 per share for FY26.

articles.title: 2028 Chandrayaan-5 launch site preparation begins: ISRO team visits Japan for assessment | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) team is visiting Japan to assess the launch site preparations for Chandrayaan-5, a mission focused on lunar exploration.  This visit underscores the growing cooperation between ISRO and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), with both organizations sharing objectives in space science and technology development. The collaboration aims to ensure technical compatibility, safety considerations, and environmental conditions for deep space missions, building upon the success of Chandrayaan-3.  This collaborative effort exemplifies a global trend towards international partnerships in space exploration.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz launches Rs10m housing loans under Rs3.2tr 'Apna Ghar Programme' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched the “PM Apna Ghar Programme” in Islamabad, aiming to construct 500,000 housing units with a total allocation of Rs3.2 trillion. The program provides housing loans of up to Rs10 million on easy installments, with a 5% markup for the first 10 years and market rate thereafter.  The European Investment Bank’s international development arm, EIB Global, is also committing €160m to support Pakistan's rebuilding efforts in Sindh and water quality improvement in Karachi.

articles.title: Rise in caesarean section births in Gaza brings danger and infection risks | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: In Gaza, the number of caesarean sections has increased by 2 percent since before the war, now comprising a quarter of all births. This rise is attributed to factors such as food shortages, malnutrition, and displacement caused by Israeli destruction. The lack of proper medical equipment and supplies, overcrowding in hospitals, and limited access to antibiotics have also contributed to an increase in caesarean section complications, including infections.  The conditions in Gaza pose significant risks for mothers who undergo the procedure, leading to prolonged recovery and increased infection rates.

articles.title: China to ban drone sales in Beijing citing security concerns
articles.rephrased_article: China will ban the sale of drones in Beijing and require permits for their use starting Friday. The new rules, aimed at enhancing public safety, prohibit drone sales, rentals, and imports into the city.  Drone owners must register their devices with the police and obtain prior approval for outdoor flights. These restrictions follow a trend of tightening regulations on drones in recent years as China seeks to manage the "low-altitude economy" while balancing technological advancements and safety concerns.

articles.title: Meesho shares jump 10% as JP Morgan initiates coverage with Rs 215 target price - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JP Morgan analysts have issued a bullish report on Meesho, predicting strong growth for the Indian e-commerce platform.  The brokerage expects Meesho's net merchandise value (NMV) to grow at a 23% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26-31, driven by rising platform frequency and falling return-to-origin orders. Meesho is expected to reach an estimated 568 million annual transacting users by FY31, with significant EBITDA margin expansion to 4% by FY31.  The brokerage also highlights the company's potential for advertising revenue growth and its strong market leadership position in India.

articles.title: This nanogenerator turns seawater evaporation into electricity-and it never stops | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: EPFL scientists have developed a novel hydrovoltaic nano-generator that harnesses the energy from seawater evaporation to generate electricity. The device, using silicon nanopillars and a three-layered design, produces five times more power than traditional methods. This innovation could revolutionize battery-free sensor networks for IoT devices and wearable technology by providing continuous power through ambient heat and light.

articles.title: Why market fell today? Sensex slumps 583 pts, Nifty below 24,000; 7 key triggers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian benchmark indices experienced a sharp selloff on Thursday, erasing nearly Rs 5 lakh crore from the market capitalisation. Sensex closed down 583 points at 76,913, while Nifty fell over 180 points to close at 23,998.  The sell-off was driven by concerns about geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices, and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance on inflation.  Global markets also dipped as oil prices surged above $120 per barrel. Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Tata Steel, and UltraTech Cement were among the top losers on the Sensex.  However, Sun Pharma emerged as the top gainer.

articles.title: Mount St. Helens Eruption: Mount St. Helens eruption: How Gophers transformed a barren land in 43 years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists, including Dr. Charlie Crisafulli and Dr. James MacMahon, airlifted Northern pocket gophers into the Pumice Plain of Mount St. Helens in 1980 to study their impact on the devastated ecosystem. The rodents' digging activities helped re-inoculate the sterile volcanic soil with beneficial organisms, leading to a significant increase in plant growth within six years.  The experiment revealed that areas influenced by pocket gophers had a better network of fungi and established intricate plant communities much faster than natural processes. This study highlights the role of ecosystem engineers in accelerating ecological recovery.

articles.title: Lahore court grants interim pre-arrest bail to PM's daughter, son-in-law in Saaf Pani case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rabia Imran and her husband Ali Imran Yousaf were granted interim pre-arrest bail by an anti-corruption court in Lahore, Pakistan. The couple had previously been declared proclaimed offenders for their alleged involvement in irregularities at the Punjab Saaf Pani Company (PSPC).  The case was transferred to the anti-corruption court after being initially heard in an accountability court. Other suspects, including Shehbaz Sharif, have already been acquitted.

articles.title: Trump says US studying troop cuts in Germany, after Merz criticises war
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced on social media that the US is "studying" potential troop reductions in Germany, following criticism from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.  Merz had previously criticized Trump's approach to the war in Iran, suggesting the US was being humiliated by Iranian negotiators. While Trump accused Merz of supporting Iran's nuclear ambitions and claimed that Germany is "doing so poorly," Merz maintains a positive relationship with Trump. The US has a significant military presence in Germany, with more than 36,000 active duty troops assigned to bases across the country.

articles.title: CM Murad asks K-Electric to find practical solution to reduce loadshedding - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah expressed concern over prolonged power outages in Karachi's underprivileged areas and directed K-Electric (KE) to find a solution. At a meeting with KE Chairman Shahryar Chishti, the CM requested a study on a targeted subsidy program for vulnerable consumers, aiming to provide affordable electricity to low-income neighborhoods and industrial areas.  The Sindh government is also exploring partnership with KE to develop a plan for supplying competitively priced electricity to industrial areas.

articles.title: Local election campaigning enters final week as forecaster warns Labour could lose 1,850 English seats –UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Local election campaigning enters its final week, with forecasts predicting a significant loss for Labour. Robert Hayward, an elections specialist, predicts Labour will lose 1,850 seats nationwide, while Reform and the Greens are expected to gain substantial ground.  The impact of these results on Sir Keir Starmer's leadership is considered significant.

articles.title: Shock in India after man takes remains of his sister to bank to prove her death | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A man from India's Odisha state, Jitu Munda, brought the remains of his deceased sister to a bank after officials refused to release funds from her account without proof of death. Mundu claimed he had exhumed his sister’s body in frustration as bank staff repeatedly demanded a death certificate that was not yet issued. The incident sparked outrage and shock across India with many criticizing the bureaucratic process for marginalized communities.  The Indian Overseas Bank disputed Munda's account, stating they were following standard procedures after other heirs also claimed the woman's savings.

articles.title: 'Strait of Trump': US President Donald Trump shares new map naming Hormuz after himself | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump on Thursday shared a modified map renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the "Strait of Trump" after claiming that the naval blockade against Iran could continue for months. Trump, who has previously made similar remarks, indicated this action is part of his strategy to maintain pressure on Iran.  The US Treasury Department, through its Economic Fury initiative, continues to target Iranian financial infrastructure and oil exports, aiming to inflict long-term damage on the country's economy. Iran rejected these claims and criticized the blockade strategy, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf dismissing the advice as "junk".

articles.title: 2 armed suspects arrested in KP's Karak for 'attacking' police team - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district arrested two armed suspects after a patrol party came under fire during routine duty. The suspects, one injured, opened fire on the police party who returned fire, triggering a gun battle.  The DPO and other officials praised the officers for their bravery and actions against the suspects. This incident comes amid a surge in militant violence in Pakistan, with terrorist attacks rising by 34% and terrorism-related fatalities increasing by 21% year on year.

articles.title: Us Nuclear Violations: Iran at UN accuses US of nuclear double standards, misuse of NPT platform | India News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations accused the United States of misrepresenting its nuclear program and deflecting attention from Washington's own violations at the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty review conference. The mission stated that all of Iran's enriched uranium remains under IAEA supervision, with no reports of diversion.  Iran’s envoy Amir Saeed Irvani called for an end to aggression against Iran and respect for its sovereignty, urging the UN Security Council to address the situation. US official Christopher Yeaw criticized Iran's selection as a vice president at the conference, calling it an "affront" to the treaty.

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 62 as Trump asks Iran to ‘give up’? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Scott Bessent have both claimed success in the US blockade of Iranian ports, while Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has disputed its impact on oil prices.  The US says this will force Iran to halt production, but analysts believe it's a gradual process. Meanwhile, tensions are escalating in the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil prices and causing economic strain across the globe. The conflict is also impacting global markets, with Vladimir Putin advising against further attacks on Iran.  The US has seized nearly $500 million in Iranian crypto assets under “Operation Economic Fury” to increase pressure.

articles.title: Uae Petrol Prices May 2026: UAE announces petrol, diesel prices for May 2026 as fuel rates jump by up to 10% across Emirates | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE Fuel Price Committee announced another petrol price increase in May 2026, extending a months-long upward trend driven by global oil market instability. Super 98 will cost Dh3.66 per litre, up from Dh3.39, while Special 95 and E-Plus 91 also saw increases. This marks the third consecutive increase in fuel prices this year, following earlier hikes in March and April, due to volatile crude oil markets and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The price increases will impact daily commuting costs for residents and businesses alike.

articles.title: Rockets defeat Lakers in Reaves’s return, force Game 6 in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Houston Rockets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers in Game 5 of their NBA playoff series, forcing a decisive Game 6. Despite star Austin Reaves' return from injury, the Lakers were unable to overcome the Rockets' strong performance, with Jabari Smith Jr. leading the way with 22 points. The Rockets now trail 3-2 in the best-of-seven series.  The Rockets will look to clinch their first playoff victory since 2019 when they host Game 6 on Friday.

articles.title: Golders Green Attack: London stabbing declared ‘terrorist incident’; UK announces £25m security boost for Jewish community - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan Police have arrested a 45-year-old man in connection with a stabbing attack on two Jewish men in Golders Green, London, that has been classified as a "terrorist incident." The suspect, who is British and born in Somalia, was detained on suspicion of attempted murder after being discharged from hospital.  Prime Minister Keir Starmer, London Mayor Sadiq Khan, and Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis condemned the attack as antisemitic and called for increased security measures.  The incident follows a series of antisemitic incidents in the area, prompting concerns about national security and the rise in hate crimes across the UK since the Israel-Hamas war began.

articles.title: ‘We’re coming for you’: NT police search for suspect after body of missing five-year-old found | Northern Territory | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NT police are searching for a 47-year-old man, Jefferson Lewis, who is suspected of murdering a five-year-old girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby. The body was found near Old Timers town camp on Thursday, prompting an arrest order for Lewis.  The investigation is ongoing and a postmortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death. Tangentyere Council Aboriginal Corporation coordinated community support during the five-day search effort.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia executes Iraqi nationals convicted in northern border drug smuggling case | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia executed multiple Iraqi nationals convicted of drug trafficking after they were arrested and found guilty by specialized courts. The executions, carried out according to Saudi law, come amid a wider anti-drug campaign in the kingdom, which has seen an increase in arrests, seizures, and executions related to narcotics smuggling. Human rights organizations criticize the use of capital punishment for drug offenses, arguing that it violates international law and raises concerns about due process.

articles.title: Markets overlooking macro stress, says Kunal Vora amid oil and currency shock - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BNP Paribas's Kunal Vora expressed concern over market complacency, noting that earnings growth expectations may be inflated and could decline as crude oil prices remain elevated. He highlighted the potential for second-order effects like fuel price transmission and fiscal constraints to impact sectors such as infrastructure.  Vora believes certain sectors like consumer staples, telecoms, IT services, and pharma will fare better than commodity-consuming sectors in this environment. While acknowledging near-term risks to consumption due to rising input costs and rural demand uncertainty, he maintains structural resilience remains intact. Vora suggests a more tempered earnings outlook for FY27 as market optimism fades, with expectations already being revised lower across sectors.

articles.title: Nine arrested in UK raids on Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light in Crewe over ‘modern slavery’ and rape allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light
articles.rephrased_article: Cheshire Police conducted a major operation in Crewe, arresting nine people linked to the religious group Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light (Arpol).  The arrests followed allegations of rape, sexual assault, forced marriage, and modern slavery dating back to 2023. The investigation focuses on individuals within the group, with suspects facing charges including human trafficking, rape, sexual assault, and forced marriage. Europol and officers from Ireland and Sweden supported the operation.

articles.title: New Zealand court denies bid by mosque mass shooter to appeal conviction | Islamophobia News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, an Australian white supremacist, has lost his appeal to overturn his conviction and sentence for the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings. The New Zealand Court of Appeal ruled that his attempt was "utterly devoid of merit" and found his guilty pleas were voluntary.  The court also rejected Tarrant's claims about his mental state during the trial, stating there were inconsistencies in his own evidence and it contradicted observations from prison authorities and mental health professionals. The decision brings relief to survivors and families who had been anticipating a new trial.

articles.title: Rate cuts unlikely in near term as inflation stays sticky: Richard Harris - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, Janet Yellen, and other officials have dismissed concerns about a shift in policy, emphasizing the Federal Reserve's independence.  Harris believes that while recent profitability in Big Tech is driven by cloud usage rather than AI, the industry will likely consolidate. He also cautioned against optimistic expectations of rate cuts due to political sensitivity and the potential for inflation to remain elevated. The Federal Reserve may remain cautious in the near term, focusing on data-dependent decisions.

articles.title: Mamdani calls on King Charles to return Koh-i-Noor diamond - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York City called for the return of the Koh-i-Noor diamond, a prized possession currently housed in the Tower of London, to India during King Charles III's state visit.  Mamdani stated his desire to encourage the king to return the diamond, but it is unclear if he raised the issue during their brief meeting. The jewel has been contested for ownership over centuries and remains a point of contention between India and other countries with historical claims.

articles.title: Police say they believe abducted 5-year-old girl was murdered as body found
articles.rephrased_article: Police believe they have found the body of a five-year-old girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby, allegedly abducted from her Outback home. The body was discovered on Thursday and forensic testing is underway to confirm her identity and cause of death. Jefferson Lewis, a 47-year-old man who was released from prison six days before the disappearance, has been identified as a suspect and is believed to have murdered the child.  Northern Territory Police are searching for Lewis and have appealed for anyone with information to contact authorities. The search effort involved hundreds of volunteers and police officers.

articles.title: Egyptian Amulet: 3,000-year-old Egyptian amulet found in Spanish tomb shocks archaeologists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists have unearthed an ancient Egyptian amulet in a Spanish grave, suggesting contact between the ancient Egyptians and Spaniards existed earlier than previously known. The amulet, believed to be sacred in some religions, is intricately designed and made of materials similar to those used in Egyptian amulets, indicating potential trade routes or cultural exchange between the two civilizations. This discovery supports existing theories about ancient trade networks and interactions that shaped early human societies. Further studies will focus on the amulet's origin and its significance within the deceased's culture.

articles.title: Bajaj Finance shares jump 4% after strong Q4 results. Why Jefferies, Morgan Stanley and others are bullish - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bajaj Finance's assets under management (AUM) reached Rs 5.09 lakh crore at the end of March 2026, a 22% increase from the previous year. The company saw strong business momentum with loan growth and steady customer additions. Analysts like Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, and JM Financial maintain positive ratings on the company, citing its strong franchise scale, AUM growth, and robust financial position.

articles.title: New Zealand’s Christchurch mosque killer loses bid to overturn convictions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, a white supremacist convicted of the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings, lost his appeal to overturn his life sentence. The Court of Appeal found Tarrant's claims of mental incapacity during his guilty pleas were unsubstantiated and rejected his argument that prison conditions influenced his decision.  The court emphasized that Tarrant's pleas were voluntary and there was no evidence of coercion. This decision brings relief to the families and survivors who had been through a difficult legal process, as they will not face another trial for the tragic events.

articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Border Security Force (BSF) is exploring the use of apex predators like crocodiles and venomous snakes to deter undocumented migration along its border with Bangladesh.  This controversial plan, aimed at addressing challenging terrain that makes traditional fencing difficult, has raised concerns from human rights activists and wildlife conservationists. The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

articles.title: New Zealand: Christchurch gunman loses bid to overturn conviction
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, a white supremacist who killed 51 people at two New Zealand mosques in March 2019, lost his bid to overturn his convictions and sentence. The New Zealand Court of Appeal rejected his arguments, finding them "utterly devoid of merit" and concluding that he was not coerced or pressured into pleading guilty.  The massacre led to stricter gun laws in New Zealand, including a ban on military-style semi-automatic weapons. Aya al-Umari, whose brother Hussein was killed in the attack, expressed relief with the court's decision.

articles.title: Ishowspeed: IShowSpeed health status: Social media icon collapsed on livestream after 12 hours of intense streaming on Caribbean tour - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular YouTuber and livestreamer, fainted during a live stream in St. Maarten while on tour promoting tourism across the Caribbean. The 21-year-old appeared extremely tired before collapsing, prompting concern among viewers who watched the incident unfold. IShowSpeed later confirmed he was okay and apologized for worrying his audience, assuring them he had recovered after briefly feeling weak. He continued his journey and expressed plans to stream from unique locations in the future.

articles.title: Waaree Energies shares crash 9% despite 75% increase in Q4 net profit, upbeat FY27 guidance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Waaree Energies reported a significant increase in revenue and profit for the fiscal year 2026. The company's fourth quarter revenue reached Rs 8,840.25 crore, marking a 111.8% year-on-year rise.  Operating EBITDA also surged to Rs 1,576.76 crore, exceeding the company’s guidance range and contributing to a total revenue of Rs 26,536.77 crore for the fiscal year. The company plans to continue expanding into new growth areas like battery energy storage systems and electrolyzers for green hydrogen while investing in upstream capabilities through a new glass manufacturing facility and an integrated ingot and wafer facility.

articles.title: Iranian officials to miss FIFA Congress over alleged mistreatment in Canada | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian football federation officials, including President Mehdi Taj, Secretary-General Hedayat Mombeni, and Deputy Secretary-General Hamed Momeni, were prevented from attending the FIFA Congress in Vancouver due to alleged mistreatment by Canadian immigration officials upon arrival at Toronto's Pearson airport.  The delegation returned to Turkey after holding valid visas, citing "unacceptable behaviour" from immigration personnel. The incident highlights the political obstacles surrounding Iran's participation in the World Cup and raises concerns about Iranian players, officials, and supporters' ability to travel freely during the tournament. FIFA has contacted the Iranian delegation expressing regret for the incident and plans to meet with them at its headquarters.

articles.title: FPI exodus in four months of 2026 surpasses all of last year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have continued selling Indian equities in the first half of 2026, driven by factors like a weak rupee and deceleration in earnings momentum.  The selling intensified after the West Asia conflict began in February, leading to India being surpassed by South Korea as the most sold market in Asia. Franklin Templeton, IIFL Capital Services, and Bloomberg data show that FPIs pulled out approximately $12 billion from Indian stocks in March alone.

articles.title: Canada’s Diavik mine makes stunning 158-carat diamond discovery just before shutdown | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 158.20-carat yellow diamond was discovered at the Diavik Diamond Mine in Canada, marking the conclusion of its 20-year operation.  The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) noted that this exceptional find is a testament to the mine's success and highlights the rare geological conditions of the kimberlite pipes beneath Lac de Gras. The Government of the Northwest Territories reported that Diavik, a joint venture, was one of North America's most productive mining operations, producing over 150 million carats of diamonds since its first production in 2003.

articles.title: Piprahwa relics of Buddha arrive in Leh, people gather in huge numbers to pay respect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On Wednesday, April 29, 2026, the sacred Piprahwa relics of the Buddha arrived in Leh, Ladakh, for a public exposition. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena accorded a ceremonial welcome to the relics at the Technical Area of Leh airport after they were flown in from New Delhi. The relics, linked to Gautama Buddha and discovered at Piprahwa, Uttar Pradesh, have gained renewed global significance after repatriation from a British family and private collection. Khamtak Rinpoche, Rigyal Rinpoche, and other religious figures were present at the reception ceremony.  The relics will be on display at Jivetsal in Leh from May 1 to May 10 before being taken to Zanskar and then back to Delhi.

articles.title: US charges Mexican governor and other leaders with aiding drug cartel
articles.rephrased_article: US prosecutors have indicted Rúben Rocha Moya, the governor of the Mexican state of Sinaloa, and nine other current and former Mexican government officials for conspiring with the Sinaloa Cartel to import narcotics into the United States. The indictment alleges that these leaders received political support and bribes in exchange for protecting the cartel's operations.  The Mexican government has disputed the evidence presented by the US, stating that the documents lack sufficient proof.  The Attorney General's office will ultimately decide whether to extradite the officials.

articles.title: Student’s alleged jailing in China over Australian pro-democracy protests sparks calls for inquiry | Australian universities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lorraine Finlay, the Australian human rights commissioner, expressed concern about the case of a Chinese student allegedly jailed in China for protesting in Sydney.  Finlay called on the government to launch a parliamentary inquiry into transnational repression and urged universities to offer more support to students at risk. John, a Chinese international student, stated that he felt more concerned about his safety after hearing about the arrest. Emma, another student, emphasized the need for the Australian government to provide more support for those who speak out against authoritarian regimes in China.  Grace Street, president of the University of Sydney's student representative council, criticized the university and the government for failing to protect students' rights.

articles.title: Vedanta earns record profit in Q4, plans to reduce debt - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta's consolidated profit reached ₹9,352 crore in the March quarter, a record high, fueled by 89% year-on-year revenue growth to ₹51,524 crore. The company also saw significant improvements in earnings before interest tax, depreciation and amortisation, reaching ₹18,447 crore. Vedanta reduced its debt by nearly $1.5 billion during the fiscal year 2026, bringing it down to ₹53,254 crore.  The company plans to allocate ₹23,000 for capital expenditure this year and announced a dividend of ₹34 per share. Vedanta is also preparing for its demerger into four new companies with the effective date set for May 1st.

articles.title: "Make your life miserable": Candace Owens hits back at Donald Trump over “vile” remark during livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Candace Owens engaged in a public back-and-forth after Trump criticized Owens on his Truth Social platform.  Owens, responding with humor and sarcasm, questioned the intent behind the attack and suggested it was part of a larger pattern of political pressure and hidden motives. The exchange highlights how quickly political differences can escalate into public spectacles.

articles.title: Delhi HC orders action after obscene content disrupts virtual hearing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia of the Delhi High Court were presiding over routine court proceedings when an unidentified participant disrupted the video conferencing platform three times, playing obscene content.
