The 76,000 sq ft facility, located in the Financial District, is expected to create over 300 high-value jobs initially and scale up to 1,600 in the coming years. Telangana IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu inaugurated the center on Wednesday (April 29, 2026).

articles.title: Scientists decode ancient diseases from bones, teeth and DNA evidence | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeological illness research, using techniques like biomolecular analyses and DNA sequencing, examines human skeletal remains to identify past diseases.  These methods allow researchers to understand the evolution of diseases, past medicine trends, and environmental factors affecting ancient populations. Clark Spencer Larsen, a prominent bioarchaeologist, emphasizes that human skeletons offer valuable records of life experience, including diseases, nutrition, and biological stress. The study of ancient disease provides insights into past events and contemporary medical practice by helping to forecast future pandemics and assess the impact of environmental and socioeconomic factors on illness development.

articles.title: Suspect in child murder case killed in police ‘encounter’ in Punjab’s Hafizabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Zafar Hashmat, a 40-year-old laborer from Faisalabad, was killed in an "encounter" with police in Chak Sabu, Pindi Bhattian tehsil of Hafizabad district after allegedly confessing to kidnapping and murdering a six-year-old boy.  The suspect's body was recovered following a search operation and legal proceedings were initiated. Hafizabad police spokesperson Head Constable Waqar Yousaf stated that the suspect had been taken into custody and interrogated, where he confessed to abducting the child for sexual assault, murdering him, and disposing of the body in nearby fields.  The second FIR was registered after the suspect's death.

articles.title: Former US officials criticise Pentagon silence on deadly Iran school attack
articles.rephrased_article: Five former US officials criticized the Pentagon for its lack of transparency regarding the deadly school strike in Minab, Iran. The officials argue that the Pentagon's silence on the incident is unusual and suggests a potential cover-up.  While the Pentagon has stated the investigation is ongoing, they have not provided any details about the incident or acknowledged US involvement.  Democratic lawmakers have also demanded answers from the Pentagon regarding the strike, but their inquiries have been met with silence.  The lack of transparency in this case contrasts sharply with previous incidents involving civilian casualties during US military operations, where senior officials readily admitted responsibility and apologized for mistakes.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon’s mother charged after allegedly attempting to influence key witness in double murder trial | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Coleen Lamarre, 63, a former NSW police employee, has been charged with perverting the course of justice for allegedly attempting to influence a key witness in her son's double murder trial.  Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, 28, who is accused of shooting and disposing of the bodies of Luke Davies and Jesse Baird, is due to face trial in September. Coleen Lamarre was refused bail and will appear before the bail division court on Thursday.

articles.title: PM Modi holds 14-km roadshow in Varanasi, offers prayers at Kashi Vishwanath temple - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a large roadshow in Varanasi on Wednesday, drawing massive crowds along the route. The event began at BLW and culminated at the Kashi Vishwanath Dham temple where he offered prayers and performed rituals.  Local representatives presented him with gifts, including a trishul, damru, and a traditional stole.  Mr. Modi expressed gratitude for the opportunity to visit the temple and prayed for happiness, prosperity, and good health for all citizens of India. The roadshow was described as one of the largest ever in the city.

articles.title: Donald Trump to put his picture in US passports - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The State Department announced the release of limited-edition US passports to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, featuring a stern-looking image of President Donald Trump superimposed over the document. The department stated that these passports would be available at in-person appointments in Washington and would not cost extra.  However, some lawmakers criticized the initiative, calling it an unnecessary waste of taxpayer money and urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to focus on other matters.

articles.title: GRSE shares soar 16% after strong Q4; net profit jumps 24% YoY to Rs 303 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: GRSE, the Indian defense PSU, reported a 29% increase in revenue to Rs 2,119 crore for Q4FY26. The company's EBITDA rose by 27% to Rs 426 crore and total income increased by 24.72% YoY to Rs 2,190 crore.  Earnings per share climbed 24.14% YoY to Rs 26.47. Chairman and Managing Director Cmde PR Hari attributed the strong performance to operational execution and plans for capability enhancement, new technologies, and business diversification. The company's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 6.70 per equity share.

articles.title: King Charles Iii: In Congress speech, King Charles urges US-UK reset - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III called for the renewal of the transatlantic alliance during a White House state dinner hosted by President Donald Trump, highlighting shared democratic traditions and emphasizing the importance of security ties.  The visit, which comes amidst tensions between the US and Britain over Iran and Ukraine, saw Charles praise the "indispensable" partnership while also urging the United States to stand firm with its Western allies.  Trump welcomed Charles and his wife Queen Camilla, praising their relationship as "the closest friends," and acknowledging the shared history of both nations.

articles.title: Life in limbo: How Iranians navigate a state of ‘no war, no peace’ | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian residents are grappling with a state of "no war, no peace" as a fragile truce between the US and Iran has paused air attacks.  While some areas have seen limited reconstruction efforts, many homes remain damaged or destroyed, leaving residents facing housing shortages and economic uncertainty. Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, is engaged in diplomatic negotiations with Pakistan, Muscat, and Moscow to achieve a lasting ceasefire. However, the US maritime blockade continues to disrupt supply chains, pushing prices up and hindering recovery efforts.  The psychological and economic toll of this limbo weighs heavily on residents like Sajjad, Maryam, Ashkbous, Fereydoun, and Yousra who are caught between fear of renewed conflict and hopes for a lasting peace.

articles.title: Indian billionaire’s son offers to house Pablo Escobar’s hippos at his private zoo | Colombia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anant Ambani, son of Indian tycoon Mukesh Ambani, has offered to house 80 feral hippos from Colombia in his Vantara animal sanctuary in India. The move comes after Colombian authorities announced plans for the animals' extermination due to their destructive impact on the environment.  Vantara, a controversial sanctuary with allegations of illegal wildlife sourcing and trafficking, has faced criticism but maintains its commitment to humane treatment of the hippos. Ambani argues that the hippos deserve a safe haven and is working directly with Colombian authorities to facilitate their relocation.

articles.title: Congress accuses Rajnath Singh of giving 'clean chit to Pakistan', dubs his remarks at SCO 'anti-national' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh accused Defence Minister Rajnath Singh of giving a "shameful clean chit" to Pakistan at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Bishkek. Ramesh claimed this new stance is part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's policy of appeasement towards the U.S. and China, citing Singh's statement that "terrorism has no nationality or theology."  Ramesh also questioned whether Pakistan harbors terrorist camps targeting India.

articles.title: Vedanta demerger explained: Record date, how much money can you make and should you invest in buy 1, get 4 offer? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta announced a demerger plan, separating its operations into six distinct companies. Shareholders will receive shares of each new entity for every share held in Vedanta. The record date is April 30, and the pre-open session on that day will determine the adjusted share price. Nuvama Institutional Equities expects Vedanta's market capitalization to reach nearly Rs 1.14 lakh crore after the demerger.  The new companies are expected to be listed on BSE and NSE at a later date.

articles.title: Spain: 2,000-year-old Roman cup found in Spain may link directly to Hadrian’s Wall - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Spain have discovered a rare 2,000-year-old bronze cup known as the Berlanga Cup.  The cup is believed to be one of only a few examples of "Hadrian's Wall Series" vessels, which are typically found near Hadrian's Wall in Britain and often feature inscriptions identifying Roman legions and fortifications. The cup was discovered at the La Cerrada de Arroyo site in Soria, Spain, and is currently housed in the Numantine Museum of Soria. Researchers believe it may have been a personal gift to a soldier who served in Britain before returning home to Roman Celtiberia.

articles.title: Two Kashmir brothers: One killed by rebels, another by army 26 years later | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Mughal family in Kashmir is grappling with the deaths of their two sons, Ishfaq and Rashid, who were killed by rebels and the Indian army respectively.  Rashid, a commerce graduate, was shot dead by the army during an operation, while Ishfaq, a former army worker, was killed by rebels years earlier. The family believes both killings are part of a pattern of extrajudicial killings in Kashmir, where human rights groups have documented numerous cases of alleged abuses by security forces. Despite investigations ordered by authorities, no one has been held accountable for the deaths.  The Mughal family continues to demand justice and closure for their sons' deaths, while experts warn that impunity within the Indian military system perpetuates such tragedies.

articles.title: Five takeaways from the King's historic address to US Congress
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III's historic address to Congress aimed to ease strained US-UK relations, focusing on the "reconciliation and renewal" of Anglo-American ties.  He acknowledged uncertainties facing both nations while highlighting shared values and the importance of checks and balances in governance. The King received applause for his remarks about executive power and NATO, but avoided directly addressing Jeffrey Epstein's victims or the ongoing controversy surrounding his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. Despite tensions, he managed to break the ice with a touch of royal humor and emphasized the enduring strength of the "special relationship."

articles.title: King Charles, Trump toast ties despite Iran tensions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Donald Trump praised the strong relationship between their countries at a White House state dinner, despite recent tensions.  Trump stated that he and Charles agreed on Iran's nuclear weapons program, while Charles emphasized the importance of international alliances like NATO and continued support for Ukraine. The visit comes amid criticism from Trump over Britain's stance on Iran and other policies.

articles.title: West Bengal Election 2026 Phase 2 Voting LIVE: 18.39% voting till 9 a.m. amid reports of violence during early hours - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 3.21 crore voters in 142 constituencies across seven districts of West Bengal will cast their ballots today, April 29, 2026, for the second and final phase of the Assembly elections. This phase will determine the fate of more than half a dozen ministers from the Trinamool Congress, as well as Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, both contesting from Bhabanipur.

articles.title: Israel Lebanon Conflict: New evacuations in Lebanon even as Israel says ‘no territorial ambitions’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's military issued evacuation warnings for towns and villages in southern Lebanon, despite Gideon Saar, the foreign minister, stating that Israel has no territorial ambitions in the country.  The ongoing conflict with Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant group, began in early March and a shaky ceasefire was reached on April 17th.  Israel's military operations continue against Hezbollah.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (April 29): Crude oil crosses $110, extends gain for 8th straight session. Here’s why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has instructed aides to prepare for an extended blockade of Iran, aiming to further pressure its economy and oil exports.  Crude oil prices have risen significantly due to the ongoing conflict in the region, with Brent crude futures reaching $111.78 a barrel on Tuesday. The departure of UAE, a key OPEC member, has added to market volatility. While a ceasefire is in place since early April, negotiations between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled, raising concerns about future oil price spikes.  Analysts predict that prolonged disruptions could push Brent crude prices as high as $150 per barrel.

articles.title: King Charles, Trump toast ties despite Iran tensions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Donald Trump praised their countries' longstanding relationship during a White House state dinner, despite tensions over the US-Israeli war with Iran.  Trump stated that he and Charles agreed on preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, while Charles emphasized the importance of international alliances like NATO and continued support for Ukraine. The visit comes at a delicate moment as Trump has criticized Britain's stance on Iran, but both leaders stressed the strength of their bond.

articles.title: On TCS harassment and conversion case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nashik Police have arrested eight individuals in connection with a suspected racket of forced conversions and sexual exploitation at Tata Consultancy Services office.  The case involves nine FIRs filed between 2022 and 2026, alleging sexual exploitation, rape, and forcible conversion. The company has suspended all employees named in the FIRs and initiated an internal probe. A court will rule on an anticipatory bail plea for one suspect.

articles.title: Keir Starmer: Starmer averts ethics probe over Mandelson appointment but faces more pressure - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the British Prime Minister, successfully avoided a parliamentary inquiry into his appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador to Washington.  Lawmakers voted against investigating whether Starmer misled parliament on the matter.  Kemi Badenoch, leader of the opposition Conservative Party, had attempted to launch an investigation, but Starmer's Labour party blocked it. Starmer has faced criticism for his handling of the appointment and its connection to Jeffrey Epstein.

articles.title: ETMarkets PMS Talk | Outperforming in a Crash: How Qode Growth Fund beat its benchmark by 14%, explains Rishabh Nahar - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Qode Growth Fund (QGF) outperformed its benchmark by over 14 percentage points during the brutal fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, despite a broad-based market correction. The fund's success was attributed to a disciplined focus on quality and value investing, coupled with a systematic derivatives overlay that mitigated downside risk. QGF's portfolio is comprised of 30 well-chosen small-cap companies across diverse sectors, exhibiting strong earnings growth and attractive valuations.  The fund manager believes the current market environment presents an opportunity for patient investors willing to hold their investments for three to five years, as valuations are currently at a significant discount compared to large-cap stocks. QGF's strategy emphasizes quality over momentum, with a focus on businesses that demonstrate strong earnings growth and healthy balance sheets.  The fund manager believes the current market volatility is an opportunity for investors seeking long-term gains.

articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government approved the revised Karnataka Rohith Vemula (Prevention of Discrimination, Exclusion or Injustice) (Right to Education and Dignity) Bill, 2026, after months of discussions. The bill aims to protect the rights of students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

articles.title: Residents gherao toll plaza office on Chennai - Bengaluru Highway in Walajah demanding subway - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Chennasamudram village in Ranipet, Tamil Nadu, protested at the toll plaza office on Chennai-Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) demanding a subway be constructed to prevent future accidents. The protest followed the death of K. Sarath Kumar, a mason who was struck and killed by a tourist van while attempting to cross the busy stretch.  The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has been urged to address safety concerns on this route after several fatalities have occurred.

articles.title: ECI recommendation to restrict candidacy from one constituency or collect bypoll expenses from the candidates yet to be implemented, says Madras High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court criticized the Indian Election Commission's (ECI) continued allowance of dual constituency candidacy, despite a 2004 recommendation to restrict it. The court highlighted that the ECI proposed in its 2024 proposal for electoral reforms that candidates contesting from two constituencies should bear expenses for byelections if they vacate one seat after winning both.

articles.title: Trinamool accuses Election Commission’s police observer of serious misconduct - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ajay Pal Sharma, a 2011-batch IPS officer, was added to the list of police observers for four Assembly constituencies in South 24 Parganas after initially being excluded from the initial list released by the Election Commission of India (ECI).  He replaced Parmar Smit Parshottamdas, a 2017-batch IPS officer from Odisha cadre, who was originally assigned to these constituencies.

articles.title: Rahul meets Nicobarese community, promises to fight against infra project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, visited Great Nicobar Island to meet with local community leaders. Gandhi listened to concerns and fears regarding the Union government’s ₹92,000 crore infrastructure project, which is envisioned as a tourism-reliant economy by 2055.  The visit follows a delegation from the island visiting Gandhi in New Delhi to raise their issues with the project's progress.

articles.title: Alleged opening of material room: CEO told to take action - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court has ordered the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) to investigate allegations of unauthorized access to a material room adjacent to the strongroom at JDT Islam Education Complex, where electronic voting machines (EVMs) are stored for eight Assembly constituencies in Kozhikode. The order was issued following a plea by Kozhikode District Congress Committee president K. Praveenkumar, who alleged that returning officers opened the room on April 20 and carried laptops into it.

articles.title: IndusInd is under lens over recovery incident - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Pune police have registered two FIRs following an incident where a borrower was assaulted by recovery agents from IndusInd Bank. The incident occurred on April 25th, when the agents attempted to collect "minimum dues" and the borrower retaliated.  The Reserve Bank of India has sought explanations from IndusInd Bank regarding the incident and potential regulatory violations. The bank is cooperating with authorities and reviewing its processes.

articles.title: Union government speaking to Anthropic about concerns over Mythos: top MeitY official - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Government of India is engaging with Anthropic, a company developing the AI system Mythos, regarding concerns about its potential threat.  S. Krishnan, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), expressed this concern during a conference on 'AI Governance: Ethics, Data Protection and Legal Framework'. The event was organized by several institutions including IITM Pravartak, Dhirubhai Ambani University’s School of Law and the Deccan Centre for International Relations.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks drop at open, Brent snaps advances - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nasdaq 100 Index futures edged up 0.4% Wednesday, while Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc., and Meta Platforms Inc. are set to report earnings, with investors looking for clues on the direction of interest rates from the Federal Reserve's policy announcement.  Trading in cash Treasuries is closed during Asian hours due to the holiday in Japan, as oil prices rose, lifting inflation expectations and curbing bets for Fed rate cuts. The United Arab Emirates will leave OPEC next month, a significant blow to the group that raises questions about its future.

articles.title: How Tamil Nadu waited for Assembly election results over the decades - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The 10-day waiting period between Tamil Nadu's Assembly election on April 23 and the counting of votes on May 4 is relatively short compared to past elections.  DMK, which won the 1967 Madras State Legislative Assembly election after a delimitation exercise, saw a longer wait for results. The election was held in three phases with polling taking place on February 15, 18, and 21. However, only 233 seats were contested, and one constituency (Thirumangalam) had to be rescheduled due to a candidate's death.

articles.title: HSBC assigns a 'Buy' to JSW Steel, Jindal Stainless - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel, JSW Steel, and Jindal Stainless are highlighted as strong performers in the steel sector, with analysts projecting price increases of 13-19% from Tuesday's closing prices. The investment firm has maintained a "Buy" recommendation for Tata Steel, citing its robust balance sheet, import protection, and margin expansion as key drivers of future growth.

articles.title: TMC procured 'artificial fingers' to facilitate false voting in Bhabanipur: Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly, accused a Trinamool Congress councillor of procuring hundreds of artificial fingers to facilitate bogus voting in the Bhabanipur constituency.  The ruling party dismissed these allegations as unfounded.  Mr. Adhikari claimed that over 700 artificial fingers were purchased and that 3,810 booth slips were returned undelivered. Arup Chakraborty, a spokesperson for the TMC, responded by calling the accusations baseless. The second phase of the West Bengal Assembly election will take place on April 29th.

articles.title: Market cap rankings see quiet realignment as banks outpace IT - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Industries remains the most valuable company in India, while HDFC Bank has overtaken Tata Consultancy Services to take second place.  Bharti Airtel and Infosys have experienced fluctuations in market capitalization, reflecting shifts within the technology and financial sectors.  ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, and traditional defensive stocks like Hindustan Unilever and ITC have shown relatively stable performance.

articles.title: Telangana to deploy AI based system for surveillance operations in Amrabad tiger reserve - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has issued a request for proposal (RFP) to deploy an AI-based forest and wildlife surveillance system on a pilot basis. The system aims to improve monitoring efficiency of the Forest Department, conserve tigers and other wildlife, identify poaching or crime-prone areas, and check infiltration, illegal mining, and provide data for decision making.  The solution will be implemented in a hybrid model using normal cameras and thermal sensing, with a wireless network connecting all cameras to a control room that generates alerts and provides reports on wildlife movement patterns.

articles.title: Corporates temper bond issues with yields on rise now - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SIDBI and NABARD, two Indian government entities, recently issued bonds with lower-than-expected amounts at higher yields. This indicates a potential increase in borrowing costs for companies seeking to raise funds.  While bond yields initially declined after mid-April due to ample liquidity in the banking system, they have since climbed back up, reflecting uncertainty surrounding the West Asia war and its impact on oil prices.

articles.title: TGGENCO gets ISO Certification - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TGGENCO, the Telangana State Power Generation Corporation, has received international recognition for its commitment to quality, efficiency, and continuous improvement by achieving the prestigious ISO 9001:2015 certification. The certification was presented by Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka to the organization’s Chairman and Managing Director, Harish, in the presence of Energy Special Chief Secretary Naveen Mittal.  The recognition was awarded following a comprehensive audit conducted by an independent ISO certification body.

articles.title: New launches, capacity hike to lift Maruti Suzuki facing a war squeeze - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company, facing sales volume constraints, is expanding its capacity with two new plants in Haryana and Gujarat. This expansion will add 250,000 vehicles per year to the company's production capacity by FY30. The company expects an operating margin of 10% by FY30 driven by seven SUV launches and capacity expansion. Despite pressure on margins due to war-related disruptions in west Asia, the company achieved its highest-ever domestic and export volumes in FY26, aided by a GST reduction.  The company has also set targets for increasing EV presence and charging points.

articles.title: "She’s guilty of something": Candace Owens faces intense scrutiny following show cancellations and viral posts - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Online chatter has intensified around Candace Owens after a viral post questioned her recent cancellation of shows, coinciding with heightened attention on the White House Correspondents Dinner attack. The post alleges connections between Owens and Cole Allen and suggests she is hiding from something, but no evidence supports these claims.  The situation highlights how social media can quickly turn speculation into trending topics, making it difficult to separate fact from noise until verified information surfaces.

articles.title: Former Fauci aide charged with concealing Covid records | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Morens, a former advisor to Anthony Fauci, has been indicted by the Trump administration's justice department for allegedly concealing federal records related to the Covid-19 pandemic. The indictment alleges that Morens and two co-conspirators conspired to hide communications, influence funding decisions, and manipulate scientific narratives about the virus' origins.  The charges include conspiracy against the US, destruction of records, and aiding and abetting.

articles.title: Man arrested in ‘one of most heinous, notorious cold cases’ more than 30 years after mother’s murder | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: James Lawhead, a 64-year-old man, was arrested in Arizona for the decades-long murder of Cindy Wanner, who vanished from her sister's home in Granite Bay, California in 1991.  Lawhead had been convicted of sex crimes and sentenced to prison in 1980 but was released early after serving 11 years. Forensic DNA analysis linked him to the crime scene, and investigators were able to locate him through a recent photo match using transportation data. Lawhead is facing murder and kidnapping charges, along with his sister Terry Lawhead, who has been charged as an accessory.  Lawhead will be extradited from Arizona for trial.

articles.title: Trump administration blocks US wind energy projects in switch to oil and gas | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration canceled two permitted US wind energy projects, agreeing to pay millions of dollars in refunds to the companies involved if those funds are reinvested in oil and gas. The move is framed as a way to promote US energy security and affordability by diverting funds away from intermittent renewable sources towards proven conventional solutions.  However, critics argue that this decision undermines clean energy investments and threatens national security, claiming it was made without proper legal justification.

articles.title: Former FBI director Comey again indicted by US Justice Department | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI Director, has been indicted by the United States Department of Justice for a social media post that officials say constituted a threat to President Donald Trump. The indictment, which charges Comey with making a threat and transmitting one in interstate commerce, stems from a post featuring seashells arranged in the shape of "86 47", a term sometimes used as slang for violence.  This latest prosecution follows an earlier Justice Department case against Comey that was dismissed last year.

articles.title: Candace Owens and Cole Allen claims explode online as White House Correspondents Dinner questions raise deeper mystery - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Online posts have circulated claims linking Candace Owens to Cole Allen, fueled by an anonymous X user who suggests a connection to the White House Correspondents Dinner. However, these claims lack verified evidence or official confirmation from law enforcement agencies, major news outlets, or official sources. The posts rely on distant personal links and unrelated stories, often presented as "clues" without clear connections to Owens or any real incident.  The situation appears driven by viral social media speculation rather than factual information.

articles.title: 30-year-old man allowed to return to US after being deported despite legal protection; missed birth of son in Texas - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jose Contreras Diaz, a 30-year-old DACA recipient, will be allowed to return to the United States after being deported from Honduras in January.  He had been working as a pool technician in the Rio Grande Valley when immigration officers detained him and placed him on a flight back to his home country. Contreras Diaz missed the birth of his son, Mateo, while he was abroad. His case has raised questions about DACA recipients' protection under stricter immigration enforcement. After legal pressure from his lawyer, Stacy Tolchin, and public outcry, Contreras Diaz received a reversal of his deportation decision.  However, neither he nor his legal team have received an explanation for the change in policy.

articles.title: Starmer sees off major Labour rebellion over call for Mandelson inquiry | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer survived a major rebellion from his own MPs over the appointment of Peter Mandelson, but many warned that he is running out of political capital. The government won a vote to block a referral to the privileges committee, with some Labour MPs supporting the motion despite pressure from Downing Street.  However, concerns remain about the pressure placed on officials to expedite Mandelson's posting and the potential impact on Starmer’s future.

articles.title: Greek pensioner, 89, arrested following shooting rampage | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Greek police arrested an 89-year-old man in connection with a double shooting in Athens that injured five people. The suspect, who was apprehended in Patra after a large manhunt, allegedly opened fire inside a social security agency before traveling to a nearby court and injuring four more individuals.  The motive for the shootings remains unclear, but the suspect reportedly threw documents on the floor of the court claiming they explained his actions. Alexandros Varveris, head of the National Social Security Fund, and Stratis Dounias, head of the Athens Judicial Employees Union, confirmed the incident.

articles.title: Immigration lawyer says USCIS interivews for resident status are put on hold 'becuase of DC shooting' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charles Kuck, an immigration attorney, claims that USCIS interview decisions have been paused following a shooting at the Washington Hilton hotel last week. This has caused panic among applicants who are already facing lengthy residency processing times.  Kuck criticized the situation as "the farce that has become of USCIS" and accused authorities of using "any excuse to deprive folks of the benefits they paid for." USCIS director Joseph B. Edlow has not publicly confirmed any suspension of interview decisions.

articles.title: Trump hails ‘special relationship’ during ceremonial welcome for King Charles’s state visit | King Charles III | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump hosted a ceremonial military welcome for King Charles and Queen Camilla at the White House, praising the "special relationship" between the US and the UK.  Trump acknowledged the centuries-long bond between the two nations and highlighted their shared history, while also expressing his admiration for the late Queen Elizabeth II. The royal couple's visit comes amid recent tensions between the UK and US, with Trump threatening to impose tariffs on the UK if it maintains its digital services tax.  During their state visit, Charles is expected to address Congress and emphasize the enduring nature of their democratic traditions.

articles.title: Britain's King Charles meets Trump in bid to salvage ties - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Queen Camilla met with Donald Trump at the White House for a state visit that has been overshadowed by tensions between the two countries.  The visit, meant to celebrate the 250th anniversary of US independence, is being held despite a shooting at a recent White House event and criticism from Trump over Britain's stance on the Iran conflict.  Charles will address Congress, while the royals also plan to visit New York and Bermuda. The trip has generated controversy due to Trump’s criticisms of British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who opposes the war in Iran.

articles.title: Loss of work permits, removal from country: DHS sets strict penalties for unpaid asylum fees, issues compliance deadline - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has implemented new immigration fee rules under the H.R. 1 Reconciliation Act of 2025, including an annual asylum fee and stricter requirements for applications.  USCIS will reject asylum applications if the Annual Asylum Fee is not paid within 30 days of notification, and applicants without legal status may face removal proceedings. The rule also introduces a minimum $24 filing fee for Form I-102 and limits employment authorization for TPS holders. Public comments on the new framework are accepted until June 29, 2026.

articles.title: Five labourers injured after unknown attackers hurl hand grenade in Dalbandin - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Five labourers were injured in a grenade attack on Monday night in Dalbandin, Chagai district, Pakistan. Police responded to the scene and shifted the injured individuals to Prince Fahad Hospital.  An investigation is underway, but no group has claimed responsibility for the attack. This incident follows similar attacks in Quetta and other parts of Balochistan in recent years.

articles.title: Silent operations to nuclear balance: The secret spy networks that quietly shaped the Cold War | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Cold War was shaped by interconnected intelligence networks built by the United States and the Soviet Union, which relied on human sources, technology, and a framework for sharing information. These systems, formalized through agreements like the UKUSA Agreement, allowed analysts to combine data from various sources, reducing uncertainty and influencing decisions during periods of tension.  Despite advancements in technology, such as high-altitude reconnaissance platforms, internal breaches by individuals within intelligence agencies revealed vulnerabilities that underscored the importance of human reliability within these networks. The legacy of these systems continues to influence global security today.

articles.title: King Charles praises Nato and urges defence of Ukraine in key speech during Trump visit | King Charles III | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III addressed US Congress, emphasizing the importance of the "special relationship" between the two nations, particularly in areas like NATO defense, Ukraine support, and climate action. He highlighted the historical bond between the UK and US, citing the principle of checks and balances enshrined in Magna Carta as a foundation for their alliance. Charles also called for continued commitment to trade and security, urging Donald Trump to prioritize these issues. His speech was met with bipartisan approval from lawmakers, including John Thune and Chuck Schumer, who stressed the significance of NATO and the importance of strong alliances.

articles.title: King Charles calls for NATO unity, Ukraine support in US Congress speech | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III used his speech to the United States Congress to call for NATO unity and support for Ukraine, amidst ongoing tensions with the US. He praised shared history and values between the two nations while highlighting the importance of collective defense and funding for Ukraine's defense.  Charles also addressed trade relations, environmental concerns, and the rule of law as key elements of a strong partnership. The visit comes amid ongoing political friction between the UK and the US, including trade disputes and criticisms of US foreign policy.

articles.title: Lahore court grants interim bail to PM's daughter, son-in-law in money laundering case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Shehbaz Sharif's daughter, Rabia Imran, and her husband, Imran Yousaf, were granted interim pre-arrest bail by a special court in Lahore. The couple appeared before the court alongside their counsel and submitted surety bonds. The court also restrained the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) from arresting them until May 7th.  This follows an accountability court's previous decision to suspend perpetual arrest warrants issued against them in a case related to alleged irregularities in the Punjan Saaf Pani Company.

articles.title: Texas daycare accused of H-1B scam in 'pay-to-play' scheme; visas tied to unrelated job roles - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Texas daycare owner, Yuan Yao, is under scrutiny after a video surfaced showing him being confronted over claims that his businesses sponsored dozens of foreign workers through the US H-1B visa program.  Sara Gonzales, a Texas personality and critic of the scheme, alleges that the businesses have filed more than 50 labor condition applications and sponsored at least 37 H-1B visa workers in positions unrelated to daycare services. Yao refused to answer questions and claimed everything was legal while declining to provide documents.  Gonzales plans to report her findings to federal authorities, questioning why an allegedly inactive daycare would continue filing H-1B petitions. The confrontation comes as Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is already investigating suspected H-1B abuse in North Texas.

articles.title: How London police are battling rampant phone theft - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: London’s Metropolitan Police have intensified efforts to combat the rise of phone theft in the city, which has been dubbed Europe's phone theft capital. The police are using drones, facial recognition technology, and interceptor teams to track down thieves, resulting in a 12.3% decrease in phone thefts from 2024 to 2025.  However, organized crime groups have exploited the trend, with stolen phones often being reactivated and resold overseas. The police are working with manufacturers to make stolen devices worthless and are urging citizens to report stolen phones quickly.

articles.title: Doja Cat: Doja Cat issues apology after Twitch mods ban PlaqueBoyMax unexpectedly - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Doja Cat's Twitch stream was disrupted when one viewer, PlaqueBoyMax, was unexpectedly banned by Twitch moderators during a live broadcast.  The ban sparked controversy as viewers questioned the reason for the action and expressed confusion about PlaqueBoyMax's lack of wrongdoing. Doja Cat later clarified that she did not approve of the ban and would address the situation with her moderation team, emphasizing fairness and accountability on her stream. The incident highlighted the potential for seemingly minor actions in live streaming to escalate into significant online controversies.

articles.title: Sri Lanka police arrest 22 Buddhist monks after 110kg of cannabis found in luggage | Sri Lanka | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty-two Buddhist monks from Sri Lanka are in custody after customs officials discovered 110kg of high-grade cannabis hidden in their luggage at Colombo's main international airport. The group, mostly junior monks in training, allegedly concealed the drugs within false walls and were returning from a holiday in Bangkok.  The haul, valued at 1.1 billion rupees (£2.5 million), is the largest single detection of kush at the South Asian country's main airport. A 23rd monk believed to have organized the trip was arrested separately. The monks had been sponsored for their holiday and were photographed in "lay clothing".

articles.title: 'He’s so cute': Donald Trump says his mother had a 'crush' on King Charles - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump joked during a White House ceremony welcoming King Charles III and Queen Camilla that his late mother, Mary Anne MacLeod Trump, had a crush on the King.  Trump described his mother's admiration for the royal family and her fondness for watching royal events on television. The president also spoke about his Scottish heritage and his parents' long marriage. There was no official response from Buckingham Palace to the remark.

articles.title: After 60 days of war in Iran, does US Congress want a say? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The 60-day mark of the US and Israel's war with Iran approaches, prompting questions about Congressional involvement.  While the War Powers Act requires presidents to cease military action after 60 days or receive congressional authorization, experts say Congress has historically avoided taking a stance on such matters. Donald Trump officially notified Congress of the attacks on February 28th and faces pressure from both Republicans and Democrats regarding future actions. Some Republicans have expressed concerns about the war's political ramifications, but many are hesitant to publicly oppose the administration, fearing backlash from donors and Trump himself.  The potential for Congressional inaction remains a significant concern as experts argue that it could mark a "leap" in interpreting the War Powers Act.

articles.title: Donald Trump plans to put his photo on limited edition American passports: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department is proposing a limited edition passport featuring an image of Donald Trump on the inside cover, marking the first time a sitting US president's likeness has been included. The proposal has drawn criticism from opposition leaders who argue it represents "megalomania" and that passports should reflect the American people, not one man.  The redesign is part of celebrations marking 250 years of American independence and includes other changes like coins with Trump's image and updated designs for government materials.

articles.title: Trump scolds Germany’s Merz for criticism of Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for his criticism of the US-Israeli war on Iran, stating that Merz "doesn't know what he's talking about" and that the conflict was necessary to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.  Trump defended the war, claiming it was something other nations should have done long ago, while also expressing frustration with European allies for their lack of support in the conflict. Merz had previously criticized the war as "ill-considered," citing past conflicts like Afghanistan and Iraq, and suggesting that Washington is being humiliated by Iran's negotiating tactics.

articles.title: LHC dismisses PTI leaders' pleas seeking suspension of sentences in May 9 cases - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Lahore High Court division bench dismissed the applications for interim relief by Ejaz Chaudhry and Mian Mahmoodur Rashid, seeking to suspend their sentences in multiple cases related to the May 9 riots.  The bench also allowed an application filed by Afzal Azeem Pahat, suspending his sentence. The convictions involve charges of abetment of violence and criminal conspiracy, with each accused awarded an average sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder: ChudtheBuilder’s 3-day ban escalates to indefinite Kick ban following harassment backlash - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ChudtheBuilder, a popular streamer, has been indefinitely banned from Kick after facing backlash for his past behavior in public streams. The ban follows earlier temporary suspensions and removal of his verification badge due to offensive language and harassment incidents.  The platform's decision came after the spread of older videos showcasing ChudtheBuilder using racial slurs and engaging in arguments with strangers, prompting viewers to call for stricter action. While he has stated plans to continue streaming on other platforms, ChudtheBuilder is now facing a very serious long-term ban from Kick.

articles.title: Friendly fire? Secret Service agent injured in Trump assassination attempt may have been shot by own colleague - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Secret Service agent was injured during an attempted assassination of US President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner last week.  The agent, who fired five shots at the suspect, was not struck by return fire. The suspect, Cole Tomas Allen, from Torrance, California, has been charged with attempted assassination and other federal offenses. Allen was armed with a shotgun, pistol, and knives when he tried to enter the dining area where Trump and other officials were attending.  Allen's family raised concerns about his behavior in the days leading up to the incident, and his brother alerted police after receiving a manifesto from Allen.

articles.title: US stocks today: Nasdaq, S&P 500 end lower on renewed AI growth worries ahead of big tech earnings - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nasdaq experienced a significant decline, weighed down by concerns over OpenAI's missed user and revenue targets. Chip stocks like Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom dropped, reflecting investor uncertainty about the AI industry's growth trajectory.  Oracle shares also fell as scrutiny increased regarding its reliance on OpenAI. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite saw losses, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average remained relatively stable.  The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its current interest rate policy but will be closely scrutinizing inflation risks related to the war in Ukraine and soaring crude prices.

articles.title: Northern Ireland makes arrest linked to suspected New IRA car bombing | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Northern Irish police arrested a 66-year-old man in connection with the New IRA's car bombing of a Belfast police station. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said searches are ongoing and no one was injured in the attack, which occurred after a hijacked delivery vehicle was forced to Dunmurry police station.  The New IRA claimed responsibility for the attack, stating its intention to kill officers at their homes with bombs.

articles.title: Bizarre tax laws in US could drain 30+ nations’ World Cup earnings as FIFA fails to secure exemption | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The FIFA World Cup 2026 is facing a financial challenge due to the lack of tax exemptions for participating national associations in the United States. While FIFA has held tax-exempt status since the 1994 World Cup, it hasn't secured the same exemption for the 48 teams. This means that many non-European nations could face significantly higher costs due to US tax law and international tax treaties. The uneven geography of the tournament, with more matches in the United States than Canada or Mexico, further complicates the financial picture. FIFA is working with national associations on managing the tax implications and increasing prize money for the 2026 tournament.

articles.title: News live: King Charles praises ‘ambitious’ Aukus and expresses pride in Australia in speech to US Congress | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles praised the Aukus nuclear submarine program during his speech to the US Congress, highlighting the strong defense ties between the US, UK, and their NATO allies. He emphasized that these partnerships are built on decades of collaboration, citing shared military personnel, joint F-35 production, and the ambitious Aukus agreement with Australia.  The consumer price index data released later today is expected to confirm the significant inflationary impact of the US-Iran war on the economy.

articles.title: 89-year-old man arrested over Athens double shooting | Greece | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An 89-year-old man has been arrested in Patras, Greece, after a shooting spree that injured several people at government buildings in Athens. The suspect reportedly attempted to flee to Italy before his arrest.  Greece’s state-run TV channel ERT reported the suspect had a history of mental illness and was angered by the rejection of an application for a state pension. Judicial authorities condemned the inadequate security measures that allowed the gunman to enter a courthouse, while the Greek association of judges and prosecutors criticized the unused X-ray machines acquired for security purposes.

articles.title: ECI ought to provide voting facilities for all eligible citizens: HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court expressed concern over allegations of 21,156 polling officials being unable to cast their postal ballots. The court urged the Election Commission of India (ECI) to ensure adequate facilities for all eligible citizens and extended the deadline for casting postal votes.  The Union, which submitted a list of these officials, argued that ballot papers should be delivered before the counting date.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Mother Teresa: “I alone cannot change the world, but I can cast a stone across the waters to create many ripples.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mother Teresa's quote, "I alone cannot change the world, but I can cast a stone across the waters to create many ripples," emphasizes that even small actions can have a significant impact over time.  This message encourages individuals to be kind and responsible in their daily lives, understanding that every effort contributes to positive change. The ripple effect of these actions can inspire others and ultimately lead to real change.

articles.title: Indian billionaire's son offers to save Escobar's hippos
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian billionaire's son, Anant Ambani, has offered to house a herd of hippos linked to the late Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar in his private zoo in India. Anant Ambani stated that he is willing to receive and care for the animals at his Vantara zoo in Gujarat state. Colombia has not commented on the offer. The hippos, which Escobar illegally imported, have multiplied in Colombia's Magdalena River basin and are considered an invasive species.

articles.title: A false high: On voter turnout data, SIR impact - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Election Commission of India (ECI) reported record voter turnout in the first phase of elections in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu.  While provisional figures show 93.2% turnout in West Bengal and 85.1% in Tamil Nadu, experts caution against interpreting these numbers as a sign of genuine participation due to massive net voter deletions before the election. These deletions, which affected both states significantly, reduced the electorate size, potentially inflating the turnout percentage.  The impact of these changes is particularly evident in cities like Chennai where turnout surged despite minimal voter additions.

articles.title: Why is MrBeast suing Canadian company MHQ for $5 million? Inside the explosive Beast Games legal fight - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: MrBeast, through his company MRB2024, LLC, has filed a lawsuit against Toronto-based production company MHQ seeking the return of $5 million paid in advance for the reality show "Beast Games".  MrBeast's team claims that MHQ did not complete the work and should return the money. MHQ disputes these claims, stating it completed significant work on the project and deserves payment for its full commitment. The case is ongoing.

articles.title: US soldier pleads not guilty to charges of betting on Nicolás Maduro’s ouster | US crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a US Army sergeant, pleaded not guilty to fraud charges related to insider trading on prediction markets.  Van Dyke is accused of using confidential government information to bet on the removal of Venezuelan President Maduro and US military intervention in Venezuela, resulting in significant payouts. The case marks the first time the US justice department has pursued insider trading charges involving prediction markets. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission also filed civil charges against Van Dyke.  Van Dyke faces five criminal counts, including unlawful use of confidential government information for personal gain.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Hotels Association to hold B2B expo in October - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Hotels Association President M. Venkadasubbu stated that restaurants increased food prices by 5% to 10% due to rising commercial LPG cylinder prices, maintaining the quality and quantity of food.  The Association will host UNAVU EXE 2026, a three-day B2B event featuring over 200 companies showcasing innovative solutions for food processing, automation, and industrial kitchen solutions. The expo is expected to attract over 15,000 business visitors from across India.

articles.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Major yellow card rule change explained as new system to affect every nation | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA is rethinking how yellow cards are handled in the expanded 2026 World Cup due to the longer tournament format. The new rules will wipe yellow cards after the group stage and again after the quarter-finals, preventing players from accumulating cautions across multiple rounds and missing crucial knockout matches. This change aims to ensure that key players remain available for the most important games in the expanded tournament.

articles.title: Trump approval dips to record low amid Iran war, inflation woes: Poll | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump’s approval rating has dropped to 34 percent, the lowest since his return to the White House, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. The poll also revealed that only 22 percent of respondents approve of Trump’s performance on the cost of living, likely due to economic uncertainty and the US-Israel war on Iran.  The conflict has fueled inflation in the US and global energy supply issues, despite a two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran. The midterm elections are approaching in November, where Trump's Republican Party will face criticism for its handling of these issues.

articles.title: FBI director James Comey indicted for a second time
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI director, has been indicted for a second time by the US Department of Justice. The new charges relate to an Instagram post from last year that included seashells forming the numbers "86 47", which have been interpreted as a threat against President Trump.  The first indictment against Comey was dismissed in November due to the improper appointment of the prosecutor.  Comey has pleaded not guilty and maintains he did not know the meaning of the post.

articles.title: BRS to hold farmers’ meet in Warangal on May 6: KTR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao announced a meeting in Warangal on May 6th to remind the Congress party of its "Rythu Declaration" and alleged failures to fulfill promises made four years ago.  Rama Rao expressed concern over farmer distress caused by fertilizer shortages, delayed procurement, and power cuts. He urged farmers to be prepared for struggles to pressure the government into fulfilling their promises.

articles.title: Greece: 89-year-old held after shootings at Athens social security office, courthouse leave 4 injured - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Greek police arrested an 89-year-old man in Patras after he was suspected of carrying out two separate shootings in Athens that injured at least four people. The suspect, believed to have grievances related to pension payments and psychological issues, first opened fire at a social security office before fleeing and later shooting at a court building. Stratis Dounias, head of the Athens Judicial Employees Union, reported that the gunman fired at an office on the ground floor, injuring three female employees.  Alexandros Varveris, head of the National Social Security Fund (EFKA), said the suspect shot another worker in the leg after warning them to duck.

articles.title: A grief divided: funeral held on the Kishanganga’s banks prompts calls to reopen LoC crossing points - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The death of Raja Liaquat Ali Khan, a resident of Kupwara's Keran village, has renewed calls for the reopening of crossing points across the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir.  Khan's funeral was conducted on both sides of the Kishanganga river, which separates Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) from Indian-administered Kashmir, with his family members unable to meet due to a 2019 government policy that closed the crossing points. Ravinder Pandita, president of the All-India Kashmiri Samaj (AIKS), and Abdul Rehman Tariq, a local leader of the Pakistan Tehreek Insaf in POK, have both highlighted the human cost of these border restrictions during times of grief.

articles.title: Warm sunshine to follow scattered showers as UK temperatures climb to 24°C this week - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United Kingdom will experience a shift from scattered showers to longer spells of sunshine throughout the week, with temperatures climbing to around 24°C in some areas. BBC and national climate reports indicate that April saw contrasting rainfall patterns, with eastern England experiencing extreme dryness while western and northern regions received above-average precipitation.  By Wednesday, most areas will enjoy sunny weather, but coastal spots near the North Sea may experience chillier air due to an easterly wind. Temperatures are expected to rise towards 20°C to 22°C by Thursday with a change in wind direction bringing milder air from southern regions.

articles.title: Guardian Essential poll: more Australians approve of Hanson’s party leadership than Albanese or Taylor’s | Pauline Hanson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A majority of Australians approve of Pauline Hanson's leadership of the right-wing populist party, One Nation, with a 52% approval rating compared to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Angus Taylor.  The latest Guardian Essential poll shows that while Australians are becoming increasingly pessimistic about the country's direction and economy, Hanson has gained support across all age groups and political affiliations. This trend is reflected in primary vote data, with One Nation edging ahead of the Coalition for the first time.

articles.title: Alleged drug trafficking kingpin deported from Türkiye to India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammad Salim Dola, an alleged drug trafficking kingpin with links to the Dawood Ibrahim syndicate, was detained by Turkish agencies and deported to India on Tuesday (April 28, 2026). The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) apprehended him upon his arrival at Delhi’s IGI airport.  The NCB is working with Interpol and the Indian government to bring Dola to justice. He has been accused of involvement in drug trafficking across multiple countries and faces charges from various agencies including the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad, the CBI, and the DRI.

articles.title: ‘Go back to England’: Argentina’s vice president tells Falkland residents after report of US ‘review’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Villarruel, Argentina's Vice President, sparked a diplomatic row by stating residents of the Falkland Islands should "go back to England".  Her remarks followed a leaked Pentagon memo suggesting the US could reconsider its stance on Britain's claim to the islands. Keir Starmer, Prime Minister of the UK, reiterated that sovereignty over the Falklands is not in question and that the UK remains committed to upholding their right to self-determination. The controversy comes amid strained relations between the US and its NATO allies and heightened tensions over the Falkland Islands dispute.

articles.title: Dances With Wolves star Nathan Chasing Horse jailed for at least 37 years for sexual assault
articles.rephrased_article: Nathan Chasing Horse, a former actor known for his role in "Dances With Wolves", was sentenced to at least 37 years in prison for sexually assaulting Indigenous women and girls. The 49-year-old had been convicted of 13 charges, mostly relating to the assault of three women, with one victim being only 14 years old when the abuse began. Corena Leone-LaCroix, one of his victims, testified that Chasing Horse exploited her spirituality and manipulated her into believing he was acting on behalf of spirits.  The judge in the case stated that Chasing Horse preyed on women's spirituality for his own gratification.

articles.title: Police file FIR against viral video of pro-Pakistan posters put up in J&K’s Doda - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu and Kashmir police filed an FIR after a video surfaced showing posters praising Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Asim Munir. The posters, displayed on a bridge in Doda district, also praised the two leaders for their role in negotiating peace between Iran and the United States.  The police are investigating the origin of the video and the individuals responsible for posting it.

articles.title: Varun Beverages shares jump 9% in 3 days. Why Jefferies, Motilal, and others are bullish after Q4 results? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Varun Beverages, a beverage company, reported strong Q1 CY2026 earnings with a 20.1% rise in net profit and a 18.1% increase in revenue.  Analysts from Jefferies, Motilal Oswal, and JM Financial all maintain Buy ratings on the stock, citing strong volume growth, stable margins, and positive outlook for the summer season. The company's international business is also performing well, with a focus on South Africa and Zimbabwe markets.

articles.title: Nfl Draft Ban: YouTuber Fred Beyer storms NFL Draft stage and fake pick stunt leads to major ban - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Fred Beyer, a 24-year-old YouTuber, was banned from all NFL events after attempting to announce a fake pick for the Pittsburgh Steelers at the draft. He gained access to the restricted area using fake credentials and proceeded to announce "Luke Maxer" as the Steelers' selection. Security removed him from the stage and police were called, resulting in an indefinite ban from all league events. Despite the serious consequences, two officers requested a photo with Beyer after his removal.

articles.title: Kerala’s Mundathikode fireworks accident: procedures on to hand over bodies after DNA tests - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thrissur district administration is working to hand over the bodies of four victims from the Mundathikode fireworks accident, whose identities were confirmed after DNA tests.  The DNA test results for Abhijith, Vishnu Vinod, Girish, and Suresh came on Monday (April 27, 2026). Ragesh, a 29-year-old Pulikali performer who died at the Thrissur Government Medical College Hospital, was laid to rest with a large crowd.  Viyyur Yuvajana Sangham members and fellow Pulikali artists paid tribute to Ragesh's life and work.

articles.title: Targeted Covid-19 research: Chinese state-sponsored hacker arrested by FBI after Italy extradition - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Xu Zewei, a 34-year-old Chinese national, was extradited from Italy to the US after being accused of hacking into American universities and researchers' accounts during the pandemic. He faces nine counts of computer intrusion related to his alleged involvement in a state-backed hacking network linked to China’s intelligence services. Prosecutors allege he targeted immunologists and virologists working on COVID-19 research, accessed sensitive information, and participated in the global cyber campaign known as HAFNIUM.  The FBI, with support from Italian law enforcement agencies, arrested Xu Zewei at the request of US authorities.

articles.title: Police arrest suspected gunman aged 89 after five wounded in Athens
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Greece arrested an 89-year-old man following a double shooting that injured five people. The suspect opened fire at a social security agency and then traveled to a courthouse, where he wounded four additional individuals before fleeing the scene. He was apprehended near Patras after carrying a second weapon, a loaded .38 calibre revolver.  The motive for the attack is not yet clear.

articles.title: Tata Steel shares jump 2% to fresh record high: What's driving the gains? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel has seen its share price surge following a legal victory in an Indian court that quashed demand letters related to mineral dispatch assessments. The company believes the court's ruling invalidates the demands, which were issued by the Jajpur Office of Deputy Director of Mines.  The stock rallied over 2% on Tuesday, marking a fresh 52-week high and reflecting investor confidence in the company's future prospects despite ongoing market volatility.

articles.title: Congress leader booked under POCSO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anand Naidu, general secretary of the Bengaluru North District Congress Committee (DCC), has been booked by the Mahalakshmi Layout police for allegedly assaulting minor children.  The complaint alleges that Naidu was in an illicit relationship with the complainant's wife for three years and assaulted his children when they questioned the relationship. The children have accused Naidu of using a rod and biting them, causing injuries. The police have registered a case and initiated an investigation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged abuse of power and potential harm to children by a prominent political figure warrants urgent concern.

articles.title: $20,000 for a Green Card: California man posed as ICE officer and scammed immigrants seeking US citizenship - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Davyd George Brand Jimenez, a 55-year-old California man, pleaded guilty to multiple federal charges for impersonating a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent to defraud vulnerable immigrants seeking legal status in the United States. He charged victims between $10,000 and $20,000 for services he had no authority to provide, including work permits, residency, and citizenship, despite creating fake documents using their names and forged government emblems.  He faces up to 117 years in prison and a $4 million fine, with sentencing scheduled for July 16th.

articles.title: Reliance share price target hiked to Rs 1,910: Why Goldman, CLSA, and Morgan Stanley are betting big - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Industries (RIL) is seeing positive analyst sentiment, with several brokerages raising their price targets and highlighting the company's strong performance in its downstream businesses. Goldman Sachs raised its target to Rs 1,910, citing potential for margin expansion and a favorable refining environment. Nomura believes the upcoming Jio IPO could be a major catalyst for RIL stock, while Ambit sees it as a positive sign of Reliance's low-risk investment strategy.  Analysts are optimistic about RIL's retail and O2C performance in the coming quarters, with several brokerages maintaining Buy ratings.

articles.title: Judicial Commission of Pakistan approves transfer of 3 IHC judges - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) approved the transfer of three judges from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to other high courts.  Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi, who also chairs the JCP, had previously expressed concerns about the potential for these transfers to undermine federalism and judicial independence. The transfers were approved by a majority vote, but Justice Arbab M. Tahir and Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro withdrew their proposals for transfer from the IHC.  The transfers come amid ongoing discussions regarding the induction of new judges to the IHC, with several prominent lawyers being considered for elevation.

articles.title: Women lead new tourism wave in Kerala’s Maravanthuruth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N.G. Indira, a 63-year-old communicative English trainer from Kulashekharamangalam, has started a new morning routine this summer by paddling along the Arivalthodu canal in her village. She joins other women, including a Class X student, for daily sessions that begin early in the morning and continue into the evening.

articles.title: US vs Iran nuclear standoff enters cold war phase - is a bigger war coming? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing Iran conflict, initially launched as Donald Trump's Operation Epic Fury, has entered a tense stalemate marked by financial sanctions and gunboat interdictions.  President Trump remains frustrated with Iran’s nuclear capabilities and is reportedly oscillating between authorizing military strikes and relying on sanctions. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, along with hawkish voices like Senator Lindsey Graham, advocate for more forceful action, while some advisors suggest maintaining the US blockade and intensifying economic pressure before considering further military action. Trump recently discussed an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the blockade, but no decisions were made. The situation remains a source of concern for US officials who fear a frozen conflict with no clear end in sight.

articles.title: Special Passport Mela on May 9; 4,000 appointments to be released in Telangana: RPO Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Regional Passport Office (RPO), Hyderabad, is hosting a special Passport Mela on May 9th to address the growing demand for passport services. The event will offer 4,000 normal passport appointments across all five Passport Seva Kendras (PSKs) under its jurisdiction, aiming to reduce the current waiting period of 8 to 10 working days.  J. Snehaja, Regional Passport Officer, Hyderabad, also announced a significant capacity enhancement at the Karimnagar PSK, increasing daily appointment slots from 220 to 400. Applicants are advised to apply online through 'www.passportindia.gov.in' and utilize the additional appointment slots.

articles.title: Sun Pharma-Organon deal: How a $12-billion merger will reshape India's pharma landscape - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sun Pharma and Organon have announced a transformational acquisition, aiming to create a larger global pharmaceutical company. The combined entity will benefit from Organon's innovative portfolio in women's health, biosimilars, and dermatology, while leveraging Sun Pharma's existing strengths in the market.  The integration process is expected to be smooth, with Sun Pharma highlighting its successful track record with previous acquisitions.  Financial analysts are confident that the deal will not significantly impact margins and that the combined entity will maintain a healthy financial position.

articles.title: Indian billionaire Ambani's son offers home for Colombian drug kingpin Pablo Escobar's hippos - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anant Ambani, son of Mukesh Ambani, offered to relocate 80 hippos from Colombia, which have been causing damage in the Magdalena River, to his Vantara animal center in India.  He proposed a scientifically-led translocation and creation of a naturalistic habitat for the animals at his facility, which already houses hundreds of other endangered species. The Colombian government is currently considering culling the hippos.

articles.title: Uk Social Media Restrictions: ‘Would impose some form of restrictions’: UK minister Olivia Bailey on under-16 social media use - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has committed to introducing restrictions on social media use for children under 16, but stopped short of a complete ban. Education minister Olivia Bailey stated the government would impose "some form of age or functionality restrictions" and that curfews could be considered alongside age limits. The move comes after a prolonged tussle between the House of Lords and the House of Commons over the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill.  The government plans to publish a progress report within three months, with regulations expected within 12 months.

articles.title: Twist in gold theft at Sattur DMK candidate’s house: estranged daughter-in-law, accomplices arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Kadarkarai Raj, the DMK candidate for the Sattur Assembly constituency, had 122 sovereigns of gold jewelry stolen from his residence on April 13th.  The police arrested Abhinaya, the estranged elder daughter-in-law of Mr. Kadarkarai Raj, along with her partner, Suresh Kumar and Bhavani, as well as another couple who were involved in the crime. Twelve sovereigns of stolen property have been recovered. The police are still searching for the remaining suspects.

articles.title: Coal India shares rise over 3% after Q4 results: What Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, HSBC and others are saying - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coal India's profit for the quarter reached Rs 14,627 crore, a 12% increase from the previous year. Revenue grew by 8%, driven by higher realisations per tonne despite a slight decline in sales volume. Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, and HSBC all provided analysis on the company's performance, with varying perspectives on its stock price outlook.  Analysts anticipate continued growth for Coal India due to expansion plans and increasing e-auction sales.

articles.title: Everything that needs to go right for Messi and Ronaldo to meet at the World Cup, one last time | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 FIFA World Cup, with its expanded format of 48 teams, creates unique possibilities for a potential Ronaldo-Messi meeting.  Argentina, as defending champions, are favored to top their group, while Portugal is expected to lead theirs.  If both win their groups, they could meet in the quarter-finals on July 11th in Kansas City. If they finish second in their respective groups, they could face each other in the Round of 16 on July 6th in Arlington. The expanded format also introduces a layer of uncertainty through the best third-placed teams, which could affect their paths to the knockout stage.  The outcome depends on how both teams perform and navigate the knockout rounds.

articles.title: Cole Tomas Allen: Californians grapple with revelation that press gala gunman suspect was neighbour
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Thomas Allen, a man charged with attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump, lived in a quiet coastal suburb of Los Angeles.  Neighbors were shocked by his arrest and the subsequent media attention on their street. Allen allegedly wrote to relatives about his plans to target members of the Trump administration before charging past security at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. He was carrying multiple weapons when he was subdued, injuring a Secret Service agent in the process. While Allen's parents are known by neighbors, few knew him personally and many expressed shock at the news.

articles.title: If he's Singham, I am Pushpa: TMC leader after U.P.-cadre IPS visits his house, faces protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Trinamool Congress supporters protested in Falta, South 24 Parganas district on Tuesday, accusing Election Commission-appointed IPS officer Ajay Pal Sharma of intimidating party workers and leaders ahead of the second phase of polling in West Bengal.
