This situation has led to a power vacuum with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) increasingly influencing decision-making processes.  Analysts suggest that Khamenei's authority has diminished, with decisions presented as "fait accompli," while communication with him is restricted to sealed letters. The evolving power structure, characterized by board-style leadership and increased IRGC influence, raises concerns about the future of diplomacy between Iran and the United States.

articles.title: Torn fisherfolk families in Thangachimadam turn to the polls as a last resort - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fisherfolk in Rameswaram and nearby areas cast their votes despite the ongoing arrests of fishermen by Sri Lankan Navy, expressing a sense of helplessness and resignation.  Tamilarasi, a mother whose son is imprisoned in Sri Lanka, and Rayappan, another fisherman who experienced imprisonment, voted believing that their ballots could bring about relief to the long-lasting issue of arrests. They recognized the significance of their vote as a tool for influencing the system that puts politicians in power.

articles.title: IT majors see strong deal pipeline but revenue momentum cools in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Infosys, HCL Technologies, and TCS reported weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue, with TCS marking its first annual decline since going public. Analysts had anticipated a drop of under 1% in each case, but the IT giants' topline growth has now fallen to mid-single digits.  This raises concerns about AI disruption and deflation within the industry, prompting investors to question whether stock valuations have adequately reflected these risks. The trailing price-earnings (P/E) multiples of these companies have been declining for a decade, further adding to investor anxiety.

articles.title: Trump rules out N-option amid Hormuz struggle - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy any vessels laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, citing "total control" over the strait.  The move followed a successful seizure of an Iranian tanker off Sri Lanka and heightened tensions with Iran. The Pentagon also announced the boarding of a sanctioned Iranian oil tanker in the Indian Ocean, while Iran received its first revenue from tolls imposed on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, bringing the total number to three.  The Senate voted against a motion to advance a war powers resolution that would have limited Trump's ability to continue hostilities beyond the timeframe allowed under US law.

articles.title: One killed, five injured in shooting at Mall of Louisiana food court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the food court of Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge left one person dead and five injured on Friday afternoon.  The incident stemmed from a confrontation between two groups, according to Baton Rouge Police Chief TJ Morse, who confirmed that five people were taken into custody.  Desire Batton, a worker at a clothing store, said shoppers and employees fled the scene as gunfire erupted. The mall will remain closed for the rest of the day.

articles.title: How Visakhapatnam zoo keeps animals cool as temperatures rise - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (IGZP) is implementing its annual summer management plan to ensure animal comfort amidst rising temperatures.  The zoo, spread across 625 acres of forested hills and the Bay of Bengal, uses water sprinklers, shade structures, adjusted diets, and modified routines to maintain a comfortable environment for all animals within their enclosures. The park's staff carefully monitors each species' needs and implements tailored strategies to ensure animal well-being during the summer months.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu elections 2026: Over 84% voter turnout in the State, highest in its electoral history - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu recorded its highest polling percentage in an Assembly election, reaching 84.69% on April 23, 2026. Over 4.85 crore people cast their votes across all 234 constituencies. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar commended voters in both West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, noting it was the highest percentage of polling in those states.

articles.title: Watch: Above 92% turnout in Bengal, 85% in Tamil Nadu amid poll violence | Above the Fold | 23.04.2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu reports on key election trends in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, highlighting shifts ahead of the polls. The publication also covers political tensions in the United States over birthright citizenship and rising tensions in West Asia around the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, West Bengal's campaign landscape has seen a significant change.

articles.title: Book release controversy: SSUS to initiate inquiry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS)'s Vice-Chancellor, Ciza Thomas, cancelled the release of a biography of Chattampi Swamikal due to incomplete printing. The Kerala Governor, who was scheduled to release the book, directed Thomas to investigate and take action.  The university is now conducting an inquiry into the mix-up involving the printing and release of the work.

articles.title: Analysis: Why there is a ‘Pawar play’ over political legacy in Baramati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharad Pawar's legacy in Baramati, Maharashtra, is being challenged after the death of his nephew, Ajit Pawar.  The constituency, long dominated by the Pawar family, faces uncertainty as younger generations seek their own political paths. The BJP seeks to capitalize on this shift while the NCP and its allied party, NCP (SP), grapple with internal divisions.

articles.title: Nepal’s customs duty is the outcome of a ‘pre-existing provision’, will not affect ‘household goods’: India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) responded to protests against new customs duty regulations imposed on travelers from India. The MEA stated that the duty is a pre-existing provision and will not affect families carrying household goods.  The new rule, implemented in mid-April by Prime Minister Balendra Shah, requires travelers with goods worth over one hundred Nepali rupees to pay customs duty.

articles.title: Bombay HC pulls up NIA for delays in 2006 Malegaon blast investigation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay High Court quashed charges against four individuals accused in the 2006 Malegaon bomb blasts, citing insufficient evidence provided by the National Investigation Agency (NIA). The court's decision was made by a Division Bench of Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice Shyam C. Chandak, who ruled that there was not enough material to proceed against Rajendra Chaudhary, Dhan Singh, Manohar Ram Singh Narwaria, and Lokesh Sharma.

articles.title: Revanth, Uttam to meet CBI Directorfor expediting Kaleshwaram probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy plan to meet the CBI Director to urge for expedited investigation into alleged irregularities in the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project. The High Court upheld the constitution of the Justice P. C. Ghose Commission, finding no fault with its findings or legal validity.  The Ministers will consult senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi before deciding whether to appeal to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: NHRC issues notices to Centre, States over poor adoption of NCERT, SCERT textbooks in private schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued notices to the Centre and States seeking explanations regarding inspections or audits into allegations that private schools are substituting government-prescribed textbooks with those from private publishers. The complaint alleges this practice burdens families financially, prompting the NHRC's inquiry.

articles.title: Trump shares right-wing anchor’s rant against Indians, MEA terms it ‘inappropriate’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre responded to derogatory remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump about India and Indian immigrants, calling them "uninformed, inappropriate, and in poor taste." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson stated that the comments do not reflect the reality of the India-U.S. relationship and expressed concern over the amplified views shared by Mr. Trump.  The U.S. Embassy did not clarify or backpedal on Mr. Trump's statements, further fueling criticism from Indian politicians and experts who called for a stronger response from the government.

articles.title: Business houses in Tamil Nadu pause for election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article:
Tamil Nadu businesses largely shut down on election day, 2026, to allow employees to vote. The banking and real estate sectors were closed, while Credai, the Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India, granted a full day leave for workers.  IT firms and industrial estates housing MSMEs saw varying degrees of closure, with essential businesses remaining operational. 
Cognizant, an IT firm, closed its offices in Tamil Nadu to enable employees to vote.

articles.title: Visakhapatnam sees record participation for State football selections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam emerged as the top-performing district in Andhra Pradesh for football league selections, with 232 children participating in district-level trials. The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP) conducted the trials at the Indira Priyadarshini Stadium to identify teams for upcoming State-level competitions.  The selection process included Under-15 and Under-21 categories for both boys and girls, with a strong presence from schools and parents. A total of 64 players were selected to represent Visakhapatnam at the State-level competitions in Anantapur.

articles.title: Pandalam family member criticises Kerala for stance in Sabarimala entry dispute - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A senior representative of the Pandalam royal family, who claims to be the foster family of Lord Ayyappa, argued before the Supreme Court on Thursday that the State of Kerala has not taken a strong stance against petitions questioning the age-old rituals and beliefs at the Sabarimala temple.  K. Radhakrishnan, representing the royal family, cited past instances where the state had failed to address similar demands for investigations into the Makaravilakku festival.

articles.title: Polling booth agent arrested for damaging EVM in Tiruvannamalai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Venkatesan, a 47-year-old polling booth agent from Kilpalur village, was arrested in Kalasapakkam Assembly constituency for allegedly damaging an EVM machine at a polling booth. The incident occurred around 10:00 AM when Venkatesan reportedly became upset after observing voters being directed to cast their votes for the AIADMK's "Two Leaves" symbol.  Police apprehended him before he could cause further damage.

articles.title: Tempers rise on second day of stir as Telangana RTC calls for temporary driver applications - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TGSRTC workers continued their strike on Thursday, with one worker attempting suicide in protest of delayed absorption into the government. E. Venkanna, chairman of the RTC Joint Action Committee, condemned the incident and demanded better treatment from the Telangana government. The committee also accused police of preventing peaceful protests and called for intervention by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy.  The corporation ran all its hire buses and electric buses to maintain service, but this proved inadequate as they were unable to meet demand.

articles.title: Kerala fireworks tragedy: body parts found as search intensifies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police recovered a severed, charred human head from a paddy field near the Mundathikode blast site in Thrissur.  The remains were found during an extensive search operation involving multiple agencies and personnel, including cadaver dogs and drone surveillance. Over 14 body parts were recovered, with four individuals still unaccounted for. Authorities are investigating the cause of the explosion and have collected DNA samples from relatives of the missing persons to identify them. The investigation is ongoing, with inconsistencies in witness statements being examined.

articles.title: BJP claiming ‘fake credit’ for raising land acquisition compensation for farmers; law made by UPA govt, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress party alleged that the Madhya Pradesh government was falsely claiming credit for doubling land acquisition compensation, a provision enacted by the UPA government under former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in 2013. The state cabinet approved an increase to double the market price of land acquired for farmers, with Chief Minister Mohan Yadav calling it a "major decision in the interest of farmers."

articles.title: Residents near Katpadi boycott polls after relocation of polling booth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Balekuppam village in Vellore district boycotted elections on Thursday, protesting the relocation of a polling booth and lack of civic amenities. They hoisted black flags to signify their opposition and expressed dissatisfaction with the existing polling booth's distance from the village's Scheduled Caste settlement. The boycott was part of a wider movement against the proposed changes.

articles.title: Record turnout in WB & Tamil Nadu polls despite violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu has migrated to a new commenting platform. Users can access their older comments by logging into their accounts on Vuukle.  All users must abide by the community guidelines for posting comments, which are in English and must be in full sentences.

articles.title: Bengaluru garbage tender: Contractor moves Karnataka High Court for probe alleging 9-15% bribe demand by two IAS officers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A private contractor, S.N. Balasubramaniam, has filed a petition in the High Court of Karnataka alleging that two senior State officials demanded illegal gratification ranging from 9% to 15% of the annual bid amount for awarding a Solid Waste Management (SWM) tender package in Bengaluru city. The petition was filed by the contractor's company, Nelaanjanaa Enterprises, and its representative organization, the Bangalore Mahanagara Swachahte Matthu Lorry Malikara Hagoo Guthigedarara Sangha.

articles.title: RTC driver succumbs after immolation bid, tension prevails in Warangal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Shankar Goud, a 54-year-old driver for the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC), died from burn injuries sustained in an attempted self-immolation during the ongoing RTC employees' strike. The incident occurred at the Narsampet depot and prompted tension in the town and Warangal. Goud was rushed to a local hospital before being transferred to MGM Hospital in Warangal.

articles.title: Lisa Gill appointed Chief Justice of A.P. High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: President Droupadi Murmu appointed Justice Lisa Gill as the Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court, effective April 25th.  This appointment follows the retirement of current Chief Justice Dhiraj Singh Thakur on April 24th. Justice Gill, who was previously a puisne judge of the High Court, will assume the role upon the incumbent's departure.

articles.title: NOTA loses ground as electors in Tamil Nadu lean towards new political alternatives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NOTA, an option allowing voters to reject all candidates, did not see a significant surge in support during the recent elections.  While some voters chose NOTA, there was little public discussion about its popularity. Introduced in 2013 after a Supreme Court ruling, NOTA allows voters to formally reject all candidates on electronic voting machines.

articles.title: Two Scheduled Tribe couples exercise their franchise for the first time this election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Masi and Govindammal, a couple from the Scheduled Tribe community in Konai village, cast their first votes on Thursday at the age of over 40 and 50 respectively. The pair had previously been trapped in bonded labor for six years in Salem district before receiving their voter IDs recently.

articles.title: Troubled waters: A.P., T.N. fishermen embroiled in a row - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fishermen from Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, and Karaikal, Puducherry released four mechanised boats seized by fishermen in Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh. The dispute over the boats, which have been at the center of a long-standing conflict between the two states for almost four decades, has fueled concerns about inadequate maritime patrols.

articles.title: Recent hits give Malayalam film industry a shot in the arm - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hashir, Alan, Ajin, and Vinayak, all social media influencers, who starred in the Malayalam film "Vaazha II: Biopic of a Billion Bros," achieved their dream of storming the cinema after their January reel went viral. The movie, which cost ₹13 crore to produce, became a massive box-office hit, raking in ₹150 crore in less than 10 days.

articles.title: A season to try and understand the people’s pulse - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sonia Gandhi made her debut election speech in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu on January 11, 1998, amidst a backdrop of political tension and the legacy of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination.  During the campaign, voters expressed their support for Congress through slogans like "Zindabad," while others displayed strong emotional ties to parties like the AIADMK, exemplified by an elderly woman who identified with the party's symbol despite its opposition.

articles.title: BJP women cadre accuse Congress of blocking quota bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana BJP organized a women's protest march on Thursday evening, criticizing the Congress party for its perceived "hypocritical and anti-women stance" on women's reservation in legislatures. The march, which began at Domalguda and culminated in a public meeting at Indira Park, saw thousands of women party workers and supporters participate, with senior leaders like N. Ramchander Rao, G. Kishan Reddy, Bandi Sanjay Kumar, K. Laxman, D.K. Aruna, Eatala Rajender, Yeleti Maheswar Reddy, and Malka Komuraiah taking part.

articles.title: Congress questions EC notice to Kharge, alleges ulterior motives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress officials have written to the Election Commission of India, questioning the issuance of a show-cause notice to party president Mallikarjun Kharge. They allege ulterior motives and a casual, routine manner in the notice's issuance. The letter, addressed to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and two other commissioners, also notes that two notices with the same reference number and date were issued but signed by different officials, leaving ambiguity about their status.

articles.title: Decapitating cartels? Mexico leans into ‘kingpin strategy’ but at a cost | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following the arrest of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a surge in violence and disappearances has plagued Mexico.  The Sinaloa Cartel experienced a power struggle that led to increased homicides, femicides, and missing person reports. Activists like Maria Isabel Cruz, who works with Sabuesos Guerreras, have observed the rise in violence as a direct consequence of targeting cartel leaders alone. While pressure from the United States has driven Mexico's current president, Claudia Sheinbaum, to continue the "kingpin strategy," critics argue that it fails to address the root causes of the problem and only serves to appease US demands.  The strategy has also been criticized for failing to dismantle the criminal market, which continues to thrive due to high demand in the United States. The violence has extended beyond Sinaloa, impacting neighboring states like Sonora and Durango, and even seen an increase in femicides.

articles.title: KSRTC issues summer advisory for drivers, conductors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) has issued a summer advisory to its drivers and conductors, urging them to prioritize staff welfare during the hot months. The advisory recommends carrying sufficient drinking water, consuming light food, and frequently drinking fluids to prevent fatigue, dehydration, and heat-related illnesses. The corporation also suggests keeping Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) on hand and consuming hydrating foods like buttermilk, coconut water, and fruits.

articles.title: DoJ inspector general to audit department’s compliance with Epstein Files Transparency Act | Jeffrey Epstein | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice’s office of the inspector general (OIG) announced an audit of the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The audit will evaluate the justice department's processes for identifying, redacting, and releasing records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.  The review will also assess the department's guidance and processes for withholding material as required by the act. Pam Bondi, former attorney general, was subpoenaed by the House oversight committee regarding her handling of the Epstein investigation. However, the committee has been informed that Bondi will not be appearing for a scheduled deposition due to her removal from office.

articles.title: Anagha from Tirthahalli is second topper in SSLC exam-1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anagha K.S. of Vagdevi School in Tirthahalli achieved the second-highest score (624/625) in the SSLC examination, while Kruthi P.S. of Priyadarshini High School secured the third rank with a score of 623/625.  The district of Shivamogga recorded a pass percentage of 96.56%, placing it ninth in the state and marking an improvement from last year's fifth position. The students, who achieved high marks, expressed gratitude for their teachers and parents' support.

articles.title: Bengaluru: Mental health session held for north-east division police personnel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police officers and staff from four police stations in the north-east division participated in a special session on mental health and stress management. The session, led by Wazeera Begum, focused on key psychological challenges faced by police personnel, including occupational stress and unpredictable duty hours. Participants were trained in techniques to manage stress, improve decision-making skills, and build emotional resilience.  The program emphasized the importance of teamwork and peer support within the force, concluding with a message encouraging all personnel to prioritize their mental health.

articles.title: State may witness close contests in many constituencies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's high voter turnout has raised questions about the closeness of this year's election results.  The 2016 contest, with a margin of victory of just one percentage point between the ruling AIADMK and the DMK-led coalition, serves as a precedent for potential close races in 2023. The People's Welfare Front, Pattali Makkal Katchi, and Bharatiya Janata Party contested independently in 2016, contributing to a wider margin of victory for the AIADMK.  This year, the presence of C. Joseph Vijay, founder of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, is expected to influence the outcome.

articles.title: At least one dead and five people injured in Louisiana mall shooting, police say | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge left one person dead and five others injured. Police responded to reports of gunfire around 1:22 pm, finding two groups arguing before opening fire on each other.  The incident prompted a large police presence, with Baton Rouge Mayor Sid Edwards stating that authorities are seeking suspects with assistance from the FBI and ATF. Several people were taken into custody, and officials urged anyone with video footage to come forward.

articles.title: Telangana RTC strike | A transport system stuck in breakdown mode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) has once again halted operations at its Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station (MGBS) due to a strike by its workers. The 32-demand strike, which began on April 22nd, is centered around the absorption of 40,000 employees into government service. This marks the second time in six years that public transport has been disrupted in Telangana, with the crisis persisting despite a change in political power.

articles.title: Indian-origin restaurant owner in North Carolina arrested for attempt to murder wife, daughter called 911 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mathivanan Pothiyappan, owner of the closed CholaNad Indian restaurant in North Carolina, is facing charges of attempted first-degree murder and assault on a female after a domestic violence incident with his wife. The incident occurred earlier this month when Pothiyappan chased his wife following an argument and threatened to kill her.  Pothiyappan was initially released on bond but later arrested again after the attempted murder charge was filed, with conditions including no contact with family and surrendering his passport.

articles.title: US sanctions Cambodian senator over purported scam network links | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Treasury Department announced sanctions against Cambodian Senator Kok An and 28 associates for their alleged involvement in a scam network that defrauds US citizens. The department accuses An of using his political influence to protect these fraudulent operations, which entice vulnerable Americans into transferring their savings through investment scams.  The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) stated that the fraudsters lure victims with promises of high returns and then steal their funds outright.

articles.title: Karnataka tobacco crop size cut to 56 million kg for 2026–27 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tobacco Board of Karnataka has significantly reduced the state's tobacco crop size for 2026-27 to 56 million kg, down from the earlier projection of 90 million kg. The decision was made at a meeting in Guntur on April 20th, influenced by geopolitical factors and market conditions driven by high tobacco yields in countries like Zimbabwe, Brazil, and Tanzania.

articles.title: Watch: 'Tomato juice' thrown at Iran's exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi in Germany - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last Shah, was splashed with tomato juice in Berlin on Thursday while leaving a news briefing. The incident occurred shortly after he criticized the US-Iran ceasefire extension and called for more support from European countries for Iranian democracy advocates. Pahlavi claimed that the ceasefire assumes Tehran will change its behavior but believes diplomacy has been given enough chance.  Police detained the suspected attacker, whose identity was not disclosed.

articles.title: 19-year-old worker kills newborn minutes after delivery in factory toilet in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old woman, an operator at the Foxconn facility in Devanahalli, allegedly killed her premature newborn baby by slitting his throat and disposing of the body inside a factory toilet on Wednesday. The incident has shocked authorities in Bengaluru.

articles.title: Top 10 largest gold mines in the world: US, Uzbekistan, Russia and other global mining countries revealed | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The global gold mining industry saw production levels remain substantial in 2025, with Nevada Gold Mines, Muruntau, Olimpiada, Kazzinc Consolidated, and Grasberg among the largest producers.  Despite output fluctuations, Nevada Gold Mines remained the world's largest gold mining operation, while Muruntau in Uzbekistan took second place. Other notable mines included Olimpiada in Russia, Blagodatnoye in Russia, Detour Lake in Canada, Kibali in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Ahafo in Ghana.

articles.title: Stalin commends people of T.N. for record voter turnout - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin commended the high voter turnout of 84.69% in Tamil Nadu, which he described as a testament to the people's sense of responsibility and peaceful election process.  He praised voters for their dedication despite the scorching heat and emphasized that this was an election for a generation. Mr. Stalin concluded by stating that Tamil Nadu will win on May 4th.

articles.title: N3On: Streamer N3on admits paying $1.4 million to clippers to make his content go viral - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: N3on, a popular streamer on Kick and YouTube, has revealed that he spends around $1.4 million to hire "clippers" who create short clips from his live streams for social media sharing. These clippers are part of a network of individuals in countries like India and Nigeria who are paid based on the views their clips receive. N3on believes this strategy is crucial to his online growth, as viral clips can significantly increase viewership even if the live stream itself doesn't have many viewers.

articles.title: ‘Toxic’ views of Reform UK candidates raise questions about party’s vetting | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A number of Reform UK candidates have been criticized for making offensive comments, including one who called for a “white Britain” and another who complained about “constant kowtowing to the black community.”  These remarks have raised doubts about the party's vetting processes. Nigel Farage, the Reform leader, has defended the party's vetting procedures, but Labour is using these comments in an upcoming election broadcast to highlight what they see as toxic views within the party.

articles.title: Pahalgam, a year on: Resilience falters, tourism struggles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The 2025 attack on the Baisaran meadow in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has significantly impacted tourism and livelihoods. The incident resulted in the closure of several tourist destinations, including Baisaran, Dabyan, and Chandanwari, leading to job losses for locals who relied on tourism-related businesses.  The Jammu and Kashmir Cable Car Corporation (JKCCC) is planning a cable car project connecting the meadow with the Yatri Niwas hotel to attract pilgrims during the Amarnath Yatra. Security measures have been intensified in Pahalgam, including facial recognition technology at tourist destinations. The attack has also led to a decline in tourism footfall and financial hardship for hotels and businesses that relied on the influx of visitors.  Mehraj Din Wani, an ATV owner, expressed concerns about the long-term impact on local livelihoods.

articles.title: US identifies 384 foreign-born Americans who will soon lose citizenship: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration is intensifying its efforts to denaturalize individuals who obtained US citizenship through fraudulent means.  Matthew Tragesser, a Justice Department spokesman, stated that the department is pursuing the highest volume of denaturalization referrals in history from the Department of Homeland Security. The plan involves assigning civil litigators across 39 regional offices to file denaturalization cases against identified individuals. While the specific details remain undisclosed, the administration aims to significantly increase denaturalizations compared to previous administrations.

articles.title: Surrey police to close rape inquiry that sparked Epsom disorder | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Surrey police closed their investigation into a rape allegation outside a church in Epsom after determining the woman's injuries were accidental. The force conducted an extensive examination of CCTV footage and house-to-house inquiries, but concluded there was no offense and no suspects. Following public protests and clashes with officers, Surrey Police Commissioner Lisa Townsend condemned the violence and urged protesters to stay away from Epsom.  The incident led to four arrests for throwing objects at police.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz expresses displeasure at lack of functional early weather warning systems in GB - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed displeasure at the non-functional early weather warning system for glacial lake outburst floods (Glofs) in Gilgit-Baltistan, ordering an inquiry into its “non-functionality” and the "ineffective performance of relevant institutions."  He emphasized that public safety was paramount, directing federal agencies to cooperate with provinces on climate change policies. The meeting also addressed last year's flooding caused by illegal encroachments on river passages, with Shehbaz urging authorities to take proactive measures this monsoon season.

articles.title: Fishers flag safety gaps, call for quick-response rescue service - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fishermen and fishing boat owners in Kozhikode have called on the Fisheries department to establish a disaster response unit. The action committee, citing the disruption of the Karunya marine ambulance service near the Beypore fishing harbour, demanded immediate intervention due to the lack of alternative arrangements for sea rescue operations following the ambulance's fitness issues.

articles.title: Indian man in Michigan, convicted of sexual abuse of children, arrested by ICE; student visa was revoked in 2024 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE announced the arrest of several individuals convicted of serious crimes, including sexual assault and human trafficking. Nava Kumar Tupili, an Indian man previously convicted of sexual abuse of minors, was among those apprehended across the country.  He entered the US on a student visa that was revoked in 2024, and ICE had placed a detainer on him as he resided illegally. The arrests were part of a nationwide effort by ICE to remove criminal illegal aliens from American communities.

articles.title: 13 stocks surge up to 180% YTD; 2 turn multibaggers . Do you own any? - Against the Tide | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Sensex and BSE 1000 indices have experienced a subdued performance in 2026, with nearly half of the BSE 1000 stocks declining. However, ACE Equity data reveals that over 80 stocks have defied this trend, achieving gains ranging from 25% to 180%.  Notable high-flyers include Sterlite Technologies, MTAR Technologies, Bajaj Consumer Care, and Quality Power Electrical Equipments, which have all surged over 50% in the first four months of the year.

articles.title: What made Putin sell 22,000 kg gold from Russia this year? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Russia's central bank reported a decline in gold reserves, falling to 2,304.76 tonnes by April 1, 2026, after a 6.22-tonne drop in March. This comes as domestic demand for gold surged due to economic strain caused by the ongoing war with Ukraine.  The Moscow Exchange saw significant increases in gold trading volumes, driven by a weakening ruble and rising prices. Russia remains the world's second-largest gold producer after China, but its central bank has reduced purchases since the invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: 'Charlie Kirk was against you on H-1B': Meet Indian-origin Aaryan Pathak who countered Vivek Ramaswamy on MAGA's Hindu hate - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aaryan Pathak, an Indian-origin student at Ohio State University, questioned Vivek Ramaswamy, a Republican candidate for governor, about the GOP's perceived hypocrisy towards Asian-Americans.  Pathak highlighted instances of mockery directed at a Hindu temple in Texas and criticized Ramaswamy for his past support of the H-1B visa program, which he now opposes. Ramaswamy defended his stance by stating that he criticizes both "woke left" and "radical right" ideologies and emphasized his commitment to conservative principles.

articles.title: Kancheepuram district sees over 87% polling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voting in the Kancheepuram district of Tamil Nadu was largely peaceful, with 87.39% voter turnout reported by 6 p.m.  Siva of Kuruvimalai in Orikkai attributed the high turnout to the DMK government's fulfillment of promises like pattas and good roads. S. Ramesh, an activist from Alancheri near Uthiramerur, highlighted the need for polling booths closer to villages due to poor road conditions.  Farmers at Keezh Kathirpur withdrew their protest after officials promised to expedite land document clearance.

articles.title: Trump claims US has total control over strait of Hormuz after Iran seizes two container ships | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump asserted that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Iranian leadership is fractured.  The US military conducted a raid on a stateless oil tanker in the Indian Ocean, while Iran seized two container ships and imposed competing blockades on the strait. The Pentagon warned it could take six months to clear mines from the waterway, potentially impacting global oil prices and the economy. Despite these actions, Trump claimed Iranian factions are unable to agree on a negotiating stance, suggesting internal power struggles within their leadership.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Escalating tensions and potential disruption of global oil supply warrant concern.

articles.title: FIIs increase stake in Suzlon Energy for third straight quarter. What’s keeping them interested? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Suzlon Energy's shareholding increased in the March quarter, with FIIs holding 23.9% and retail participation rising to 26.67%.  The stock has rallied about 35% over the past month due to expectations of higher power demand during summer months. JM Financial projects revenue growth of 51% year-on-year, with EBITDA and net profit also expected to increase significantly. The brokerage expects India's renewable energy capacity additions to continue growing in FY27, but acknowledges a widening gap between installations and deliveries. Despite this, JM Financial maintains its "Buy" rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 64.

articles.title: 60+ Serie A footballers named in major Italy prostitution case, Rs 13.2 crore seized, calls exposed | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An ongoing investigation in Milan into an alleged prostitution ring has revealed that over 60 current and former Serie A players have been mentioned as clients, but none are under investigation. The probe, led by the Guardia di Finanza, focuses on a Milan-based company accused of organizing high-end gatherings with access to escorts, drugs, and nightlife services for wealthy individuals.  The company has been linked to approximately €1.2 million in seized funds, and four individuals have been arrested. Authorities are analyzing seized devices and communications, including intercepted conversations that reference the use of laughing gas and connections to prominent figures like Rafael Leao, Achraf Hakimi, and Dusan Vlahovic. While the investigation is ongoing, the players named are not under suspicion of any illegal activity.

articles.title: Despite heat, senior citizens step out to vote in large numbers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite efforts by the Election Commission of India to facilitate postal voting for super senior citizens and persons with disabilities, many elderly voters chose to cast their ballots in person.  Stephen, a 103-year-old resident, voted at his polling station despite being unable to use a wheelchair due to health issues.  Others like Easwari, who is 102 years old, also went to the polling station with assistance. However, some elderly voters faced difficulties, including long queues and exhaustion. Consumer activist T. Sadagopan criticized the lack of postal ballot options for those above 70 and called for their inclusion in future elections.  A.M. Rajagopalan, a former printer and publisher, and H.V. Hande, a former Minister, also voted despite their advanced age.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks close lower on fading hopes for quick Iran deal, mixed quarterly earnings - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf resigned from the negotiating team, leading to a weakening of equities.  Stocks declined as oil prices rose following reports of air attacks in Iran. The Nasdaq experienced its first losing streak since March, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also fell. Despite strong earnings season results so far, concerns about rising inflation due to the war and potential economic risks from higher prices persisted.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Tony Blair: “Sometimes it is better to lose and do the right thing than to win and do the wrong thing.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Blair's quote, "Sometimes it is better to lose and do the right thing than to win and do the wrong thing," emphasizes the importance of moral responsibility over short-term gains. This message encourages individuals to prioritize values and integrity in their actions, recognizing that honesty builds trust and respect over time. The quote highlights how choosing ethical practices can lead to long-lasting success and positive impact on society, even if it means facing temporary setbacks or losses.  Blair's words resonate with people across various spheres of life, reminding them to consider the consequences of their choices and strive for integrity in all endeavors.

articles.title: Post-SIR electorate drop drives turnout surge; votes remain steady compared to 2021 election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voter turnout in the 2026 Assembly elections reached 83.41%, significantly higher than the 59.75% recorded in the 2021 polls, according to Election Commission of India data. This increase is attributed to a reduction in the electorate from 40.57 lakh in 2021 to 28.93 lakh in 2026, following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The number of electors who turned up in both elections remains close to 24 lakh across all 16 Assembly segments in Chennai district.

articles.title: ‘Some try to hijack our flag’: Keir Starmer’s stern message to ‘fake patriots’ on St George's Day - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister, delivered a speech on St George's Day condemning what he called "plastic patriotism" and the misuse of the St George's Cross to spread hate. He emphasized "quiet British patriotism," defined by acts of service and solidarity, as opposed to performative nationalism.  He highlighted the government's "Pride in Place" initiative aimed at revitalizing communities and strengthening social cohesion. The Prime Minister stressed that strong communities are crucial for national security and contrasted this with the threats of external actors seeking to destabilize societies and domestic forces exploiting divisions.

articles.title: ‘Hairdryer or lighter?’: French police look at claim of sensor tampering to win weather bets | Prediction markets | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: French police are investigating allegations of tampering with weather forecasting equipment at Paris's Charles de Gaulle airport after unusual temperature readings coincided with suspicious winning bets on the online betting platform Polymarket. The data from the station was used to settle bets about the temperature in Paris for March and April, with some traders making significant profits. Polymarket has stopped using the sensor at Charles de Gaulle but did not cancel the contracts or refund the bets.  The expansion of Polymarket, an online betting platform with investors including a venture capital firm owned by Donald Trump Jr., is raising concerns about the potential for manipulation and the impact on the reliability of reported information.

articles.title: FIA set to fast track money laundering probes - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) in Pakistan has implemented new rules to expedite money laundering investigations. The agency's Director General, Dr Usman Anwar, approved standard operating procedures (SOPs) that include dedicated desks nationwide and a Financial Intelligence Unit within the Anti-Money Laundering Directorate. These changes aim to address procedural delays and improve prosecution rates, as the FIA registered 1,247 money laundering cases in 2025 but conviction rates remained low.

articles.title: Kerala fireworks tragedy: police search every inch as kin wait with bated breath - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police are continuing their search for missing persons in the aftermath of a devastating explosion at a fireworks unit in Mundathikode, Kerala.  The site has been cordoned off and officers have recovered severed body parts. A total of 14 people were killed in the blast, with five friends who went to check out the fireworks unit still missing. The search for the remaining victims is ongoing.

articles.title: ‘Naughty or nice?’: Trump ranks Nato allies in tiers based on defence spending and support in Iran war - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The White House has developed a "naughty and nice" list of NATO countries, ranking members based on their contributions to the alliance and their stance during the ongoing Iran war. The assessment, reportedly prepared ahead of NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte’s visit to Washington, aims to pressure allies who did not support US positions during the conflict.  The Pentagon has reinforced this approach in its National Defense Strategy, emphasizing cooperation with "allies doing their part" for collective defense. However, the administration has provided little clarity on how strictly the ranking system would be enforced or what specific consequences would follow.

articles.title: In letter to UNSC president, Dar draws attention to 'grave' consequences of Indus Waters Treaty suspension by India - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan urged the United Nations Security Council to address its dispute with India over the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). The country's Permanent Representative, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, presented a letter to the Security Council president highlighting India's unilateral suspension of the treaty and its "grave peace and security, and humanitarian consequences".  The statement called for India to restore full implementation of the IWT, resume data-sharing, and cease water coercion.

articles.title: Scaling climate adaptation from policy to grassroots - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India, the ninth most climate-vulnerable country, has recorded 430 extreme weather events since 1995 causing $170 billion in losses and impacting 1.3 billion people. The nation's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) for 2031–35 prioritize mainstreaming climate resilience and adaptation into development strategies, focusing on coastal resilience, infrastructure, disaster preparedness, heat mitigation, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable livelihoods.  These goals align with global commitments to triple adaptation finance by 2035 and the adoption of Belém Adaptation Indicators at COP30, but achieving these requires sustained financing and institutionalizing adaptation from national to grassroots levels.

articles.title: Did Joe Rogan and Donald Trump have a problem when they spoke at UFC 327? Rogan speaks out | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Joe Rogan and Donald Trump had a brief but positive interaction at UFC 327 in Miami, where they discussed ibogaine treatment for mental health conditions.  Following the encounter, Trump signed an executive order to accelerate research into psychedelic-based treatments, including ibogaine, which Rogan has advocated for. Despite this, Rogan expressed reservations about the planned UFC event at the White House, citing concerns over timing and global tensions. His relationship with Trump remains cordial despite their differing viewpoints on policy issues such as immigration, foreign policy, and the direction of the administration.

articles.title: South Africa president suspends police chief over $21m contract | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Cyril Ramaphosa suspended National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola following allegations of breaking finance laws related to a $21.7 million healthcare contract awarded to the company Medicare24. The contract has since been cancelled, and prosecutors allege that Medicare24 colluded with police officials to secure the tender.  The case is pending, but Ramaphosa appointed acting commissioner Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane. This suspension comes amid a series of corruption scandals within South Africa's criminal justice system, which have eroded public trust ahead of upcoming local elections.

articles.title: Veteran NCP leader T.P. Peethambharan turns 99 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.P. Peethambharan, a veteran politician and NCP national general secretary, celebrated his 99th birthday on Thursday (April 23, 2026).  He received greetings from various dignitaries including Minister P. Rajeeve, CPI(M) leader K.N. Unnikrishnan, and Congress leader V.M. Sudheeran. Peethambharan's political career began with the youth wing of the Congress and spanned eight decades, during which he served in the Kerala Legislative Assembly three times and also taught at SDPY school.

articles.title: 'Deeply disturbed': Hindu American Foundation reacts to Trump reposting racist screed targeting Indians, Chinese - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu American Foundation (HAF) criticized President Donald Trump for sharing a racist and inflammatory post by commentator Michael Savage that referred to India, China, and other nations as "hell-holes." The HAF urged the president to delete the post, arguing it would further stoke hatred against Indian Americans in the US.  The US embassy in New Delhi countered, citing past instances where Trump praised India and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.title: US Senate passes ICE funding resolution after ‘vote-a-rama’: What’s next? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Senate passed a resolution to fund US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), marking the first step in ending a months-long standoff over funding of President Donald Trump’s immigration enforcement.  Republicans, who hold a slim majority, used a "budget reconciliation" process to pass the resolution with a simple majority, despite opposition from Democrats. The resolution now moves to the US House of Representatives, where it will need to be passed before committees in both chambers can craft the final funding legislation. This process is expected to involve further debate and potential amendments before reaching President Trump's desk for signing.

articles.title: Dozens of Mexican mafia members arrested in California crackdown | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federal authorities conducted a crackdown on the Mexican mafia, arresting over two dozen members and associates in Orange County, California. The operation resulted in 43 indictments for charges including murder, kidnapping, extortion, drug trafficking, and illegal gambling.  The indictment alleges that one incarcerated leader directed criminal activities from prison using contraband cellphones. Officials seized significant amounts of methamphetamine, fentanyl, firearms, and cash during the raid.

articles.title: Fannie Masemola: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa suspends police chief
articles.rephrased_article: President Cyril Ramaphosa suspended Gen Fannie Masemola, the country's top policeman, after he was charged with violating South Africa's Public Finance Management Act in connection with a controversial $21 million health contract. The charges stem from allegations of misconduct during the awarding of the contract to businessman Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala's company Medicare24 Tshwane District, which was later cancelled. Masemola denies the charges and will remain suspended until the court case is concluded. Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane has been appointed as his replacement.

articles.title: Put 3-year halt on H-1B, end H-4: New GOP bill by Rep Crane seeks major reforms in visa programs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rep. Eli Crane, an Arizona Republican, introduced the End H-1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026 in Congress, aiming to overhaul the H-1B visa program. The bill proposes reducing the annual cap from 65,000 to 25,000, eliminating exemptions, and implementing a wage-based selection system.  Rep. Brandon Gill, who cosponsors the bill, expressed support for prioritizing American workers over foreign labor.  Immigration policy expert Rosemary Jenks believes the proposed changes would make the process more expensive for companies and encourage them to hire Americans instead of H-1B visa holders.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to unify skill departments under single commissionerate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary, Education and Skill Development and Training, Kona Sasidhar announced the creation of a Commissionerate of Skill, Employment and Training to strengthen institutional convergence in skill development.  He emphasized a district-centric approach with District Skill Development Plans identifying priority sectors and employment opportunities aligned with local economic potential. The initiative involves District Employment and Skilling Officers, Village Skill Officers, and the Naipunyam platform for mobilization, training, employer engagement, and placement tracking. APSSDC Chairman B. Sesharao highlighted skill development as a key driver of economic growth and youth empowerment under the leadership of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh.

articles.title: For 2nd consecutive week, PTI leaders no-show at Adiala jail on court-mandated day for meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan, former Pakistani prime minister, is allowed twice-a-week meetings with family and associates at Adiala jail but has been largely restricted from visitors for several months. Despite Salman Akram Raja, the PTI Secretary General, sending a list of six party leaders to meet Khan on Thursday, none arrived by 4pm. The PTI is taking note of the situation and will discuss it with prominent leaders.  The party's Lehri stated he was unable to attend due to his daughter-in-law being hospitalized in Lahore while Akram assured that those unable to visit would not be allowed to meet Khan.

articles.title: Nepal Political Crisis: Home Minister Resigns as President Suspends Parliament | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal President Ramchandra Paudel suspended the session of both houses of the Federal Parliament without convening them, citing "special reasons" recommended by the government and the council of ministers.  The decision was met with criticism from Nepali Congress leader Arjun Narsingh K C, who called it unprecedented and surprising. This follows the resignation of Home Minister Sudan Gurung on Wednesday due to allegations regarding his financial conduct. The recent resignations are part of a growing political turmoil in Nepal, which saw the rise of the Rastriya Swatantra Party led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Suspension of parliament without convening raises concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Manipur rights group opposes powers to lower-ranked police officers under UAPA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Youth’s Forum for Protection of Human Rights (YFPHR) has criticized a Manipur government notification implementing Section 43A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967. The YFPHR called for the withdrawal of the notification, arguing it could create fear and criminalize civilians during ongoing protests demanding justice for two minors killed in Bishnupur district.  The notification empowers lower-ranked law enforcement officers to act against unlawful activities, including arrests, searches, and seizures.

articles.title: Pakistan rejects Indian propaganda on Pahalgam attack, deplores 'weaponisation of false narrative' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan rejected Indian accusations linking it to the 2025 Pahalgam attack, calling them "baseless allegations" and a part of "India's playbook of creating a smokescreen for its continued sponsorship of terrorism."  The Foreign Office in Islamabad condemned India's focus on weaponizing false narratives against Pakistan for domestic political gains, emphasizing the ongoing regional crisis and the need for peace. The FO also highlighted India's violation of UN resolutions by occupying Kashmir and undermining regional security through inflammatory rhetoric and aggressive military posturing.  The FO urged the international community to call on India to demonstrate responsible behavior and refrain from actions that hinder efforts towards peace and security.

articles.title: 'Coach Kash' was more like a bro: Friend speaks up about FBI director amid raging controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kash Patel, former FBI director, is facing multiple controversies.  One of these concerns allegations of erratic behavior and alcohol consumption, which Patel denies. He has also been embroiled in lawsuits regarding defamation claims against him.  Despite the ongoing controversies, some individuals from his past recall his passion for hockey and positive impact on youth teams he coached.

articles.title: Eight killed after vehicle plunges into gorge in Uttarakhand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eight people died and two others were injured when a vehicle carrying them plunged into a deep gorge in Uttarakhand, India on Thursday afternoon. The accident occurred near the Chamba–Koti stretch while the victims were returning home from a cremation.  The Sub-Divisional Magistrate Alkesh Naudiyal confirmed that the vehicle fell nearly 300 meters into the gorge.

articles.title: Trump tells BBC that King's visit could 'absolutely' repair relations with UK
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that the upcoming state visit from King Charles and Queen Camilla could help repair relations with the UK. He expressed confidence in the King's ability to positively impact the relationship, noting his personal familiarity and admiration for him.  Trump also discussed his strained relationship with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, suggesting that Starmer could recover by implementing stronger immigration policies. The visit will mark the 250th anniversary of US independence and celebrate a partnership built on shared prosperity, security, and history.

articles.title: Will Lamine Yamal miss World Cup? Barcelona star’s injury raises serious doubts ahead of Spain’s campaign | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lamine Yamal, an 18-year-old forward for FC Barcelona, suffered a hamstring tear during his team's match against Celta Vigo, which has been confirmed by the club.  Medical assessments indicate that he will miss the remainder of the season and is expected to be available for the upcoming 2026 FIFA World Cup. The injury occurred in the 39th minute of the game, shortly after Yamal scored a penalty, and his absence will significantly impact Barcelona's title run-in as well as Spain's preparations for the tournament.

articles.title: ‘Sadbhav Yatra’ has posed political challenge to BJP’s divisive politics, says Congress leader Brijendra Singh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Brijendra Singh, a former Hisar MP and current Congress leader, completed his "Sadbhav Yatra" in Haryana.  The yatra aimed to address social divides and reconnect with the people, energizing disheartened party workers and attracting large crowds despite not being tied to elections. Singh highlighted the unique nature of this yatra, which covered all 90 Assembly constituencies on foot for the first time, emphasizing a focus on brotherhood and societal issues rather than political agendas. While no confirmation exists yet, Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, has been invited to join the final leg of the yatra.

articles.title: Some Interrail travellers told to cancel passports as hacked data posted online | Cybercrime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Eurail, the Dutch company that sells Interrail passes, has revealed that personal data of over 300,000 European travelers was accessed in a December security breach and is now being sold on the dark web. The UK Passport Office advised some customers to cancel their passports to prevent fraudulent activity, while the Home Office agency indicated they would need to pay for replacement passports.  Affected individuals are urged to remain vigilant for suspicious communications and update passwords.

articles.title: US Senate passes $70bn funding plan for ICE, Border Patrol | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Senate voted 50-48 to advance a $70 billion funding plan for ICE and the Border Patrol, marking the first step towards reopening the Department of Homeland Security. The measure, passed using budget reconciliation, would fund immigration enforcement agencies despite opposition from Democrats who have demanded policy changes following protests against federal agents.  The bill now moves to the House of Representatives, where Republican leaders are seeking to secure funding for border enforcement before considering a separate bipartisan measure to reopen the rest of the department.

articles.title: Inside 2,300-year-old Egyptian mummies: CT scans expose skulls, disease, and a mysterious missing toe | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists using advanced CT and 3D scanning technology have examined ancient Egyptian mummies dating back over 2,300 years. The scans revealed high-resolution details of limbs, skulls, and a foot, including signs of disease and damage that may have occurred before or after mummification.  The scans also showed layered bandages tightly wrapped around the bones without cutting or unwrapping. While researchers are still studying the specific techniques used in ancient Egyptian mummification, these findings offer new insights into the preservation process and its variations.

articles.title: Ten arrested in Hyderabad for manufacturing adulterated tea powder - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Food Adulteration Surveillance Team (H-FAST) conducted raids at 15 locations, arresting ten individuals for manufacturing and supplying adulterated tea powder. The operation uncovered the use of artificial synthetic colors, low-quality materials, and expired ingredients to increase profits.  The seized products included 3,000 kg of adulterated tea powder, 1,500 kg of expired tea powder, artificial colours, and jaggery. Police have registered cases under the Food Safety and Standards Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, warning food business operators to adhere to safety standards.

articles.title: World’s longest road with no U-turns: A 30,000 km journey across 14 countries | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Pan-American Highway, recognized by Guinness World Records as the longest continuous motorable road system on earth, stretches across 30,000 kilometers connecting North, Central and South America.  This network of highways originated in 1923 with a vision to enhance connectivity, commerce, and tourism. The highway's unique characteristic is its "no U-turn" nature, allowing travelers to traverse the diverse landscapes and cultures of the Americas without needing to reverse direction. While the Darién Gap presents an exception due to its lack of road infrastructure, the Pan-American Highway remains a testament to international collaboration and serves as a symbol of global connectivity for many.

articles.title: Bengaluru metro services to start early for TCS World 10K on April 26 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) announced an early start to metro services on April 26th for the TCS World 10K Bengaluru marathon.  Services will begin at 3 a.m. from all terminal stations, with trains departing Bommasandra at 3 a.m., Madavara at 3.20 a.m., Whitefield (Kadugodi) and Silk Institute at 3.30 a.m., and Challaghatta at 3.35 a.m. The service will operate with 15-minute intervals for the first hour, then every 30 minutes until 7 a.m. to ensure continuity of service after that time, regular Sunday schedules will be followed.

articles.title: 'I am as American as...': Indian-origin man trolled after posting girlfriend's photo of voting in Virginia redistricting election - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Krishan Patel, an Indian-origin man, faced online harassment after posting a photo of his girlfriend voting in the Virginia redistricting election. A court invalidated the referendum, but social media users questioned Patel's citizenship. Patel, who was born in the US and is a naturalized citizen, defended his right to vote and refuted claims of racism. He emphasized his American identity and heritage.

articles.title: Rooftop solar systems to benefit 4,200 families in Puthalapattu, says Energy Minister - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
articles.rephrased_article: Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana in Puthalapattu constituency, Chittoor district, to provide affordable and quality power supply to every household.  The initiative will benefit 4,200 SC/ST families with free installation of 2 kW solar rooftop systems at an estimated cost of ₹54 crore.

articles.title: St Vincent and Grenadines government pauses constitutional amendment bills after public backlash | St Vincent and the Grenadines | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: St Vincent and the Grenadines government
articles.rephrased_article: The St Vincent and the Grenadines government has postponed a proposed constitutional amendment that would affect the eligibility of its prime minister, Godwin Friday, and other members of parliament. The opposition filed election petitions questioning the eligibility of both men due to their dual citizenship.  The government's draft bills aimed to retroactively limit the definition of "foreign power or state" to non-Commonwealth countries, meaning that acquired citizenship from any of the 56 in the Commonwealth would not disqualify someone from holding public office. The opposition and legal experts have raised concerns about the timing of the bill and its potential impact on the rule of law.

articles.title: Cabinet Office officials delayed telling Starmer about Mandelson vetting recommendation for almost three weeks – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cat Little, a senior civil servant, testified before the foreign affairs committee regarding the vetting of Peter Mandelson. She confirmed that due process was followed in his appointment and refuted claims that the Cabinet Office suggested he did not need vetting.  Little also criticized Olly Robbins, head of the Foreign Office, for withholding information about the UK Security Vetting report. While she declined to comment on whether Robbins acted inappropriately, Little hinted at further information being released regarding the PM's decision to appoint Mandelson. The committee is investigating the security risks associated with Mandelson's appointment and will be reviewing the findings of a review led by Fulford.

articles.title: UK signs £650m deal with France to stop illegal migrants crossing English Channel in small boats - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United Kingdom and France have signed a three-year, £650 million agreement to curb the rising number of illegal migrants crossing the English Channel in small boats. The deal includes enhanced surveillance, stricter accountability clauses, and deployment of riot-trained police along key coastal areas.  A performance-based funding model will be used to incentivize France's success in reducing crossings. Opposition leaders have criticized the agreement for its lack of guaranteed outcomes while refugee advocacy groups argue that enforcement alone won't solve the crisis.

articles.title: Sixteen workers injured in major fire at chemical factory in Gujarat's Bharuch - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A massive fire broke out at a chemical factory in Gujarat's Bharuch district on Thursday afternoon, injuring at least 16 workers. Metropolitan Eximchem Private Limited, located within the Jhagadia GIDC area, experienced the blaze around 1 p.m., prompting emergency response teams and local police to arrive. Fire tenders from both Jhagadia and Ankleshwar were deployed to combat the fire.  Efforts are ongoing to extinguish the blaze, with thick plumes of smoke visible for miles.

articles.title: Hormuz Blockade: Why did Trump 'fire' US navy secretary abruptly amid Hormuz blockade? What reports claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Navy Secretary John Phelan has been dismissed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg, following months of disagreements over the pace of implementing President Donald Trump's naval priorities.  The Pentagon confirmed the decision, with Hung Cao, currently serving as Navy undersecretary, appointed acting secretary. The firing follows concerns about Phelan's close communication with President Trump on naval issues and disagreements over major procurement proposals.

articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rohit Girotra, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  Ashok Sengupta, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. Isaac Kehimkar, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

articles.title: Antarctica Melting: Antarctica’s “point of no return”: Scientists warn the meltdown may be unstoppable | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists warn that some regions of Antarctica's West Ice Sheet may have already crossed a tipping point, leading to irreversible ice melt.  This "nightmare scenario" suggests even if global warming is contained, the melting process will continue, causing significant sea level rise and reshaping coastlines worldwide. The phenomenon is driven by rising ocean temperatures, warmer waters flowing beneath ice shelves, and the nature of the ice sheets themselves, which are located below sea level. While efforts to prevent further damage are possible, scientists emphasize that the consequences of this melting process will be felt for centuries to come.

articles.title: Karnataka SSLC exam-1 results: Chikkamagaluru topper followed a goal-oriented study plan for 7 hours everyday - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Brunda M. Tapse, a student of St Mary’s High School in Chikkamagaluru, achieved the top spot in the SSLC examinations with a perfect score of 625/625.  Her success was attributed to her diligent preparation and support from her family and teachers. Anagha K.S., a student at Vagdevi School in Tirthahalli, secured second place with a score of 624/625. She attributes her achievement to the guidance of her school teachers and parental support. Both students plan to pursue science studies in PUC and aspire for higher education in their respective fields.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Dancing all over Charlie’s grave": Candace Owens sparks firestorm after shocking call about Charlie Kirk’s burial - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has sparked controversy by publicly requesting information about the burial location of Charlie Kirk, who passed away. This request, made in a video and through social media posts, has drawn strong reactions from critics who believe it crosses boundaries into private grief.  Supporters argue that Owens is seeking answers she feels are important, while others see her actions as disrespectful to Kirk's family and privacy. The debate continues with no clear resolution.

articles.title: SC asks if ED is arguing 'failure of constitutional machinery' in WB by claiming rule of law breach - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court paused the ED's rejoinder in a case involving alleged rule-breaking by West Bengal officials during an ongoing raid on the I-PAC premises.  Justice N.V. Anjaria questioned the ED's assertion of "breakdown of constitutional machinery" in relation to the controversy, prompting concern from the court.

articles.title: How Iran raised Hormuz stakes by capturing ships | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has captured two foreign container ships seeking to exit the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions with the United States.  The US military has intercepted and redirected at least three Iranian-flagged tankers in Asian waters. The actions come after the US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports on April 13th. Iran insists it is only restricting traffic to enemy countries, while the US claims its blockade aims to disrupt illicit networks supporting Iran's oil exports.  The situation has raised concerns of a potential escalation in maritime conflict.

articles.title: Bibby Stockholm asylum barge contractor admits overcharging UK government £118m | Bibby Stockholm | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Corporate Travel Management (CTM), the Australian company that ran the Bibby Stockholm asylum barge for the British government, has admitted to overcharging by £118 million. The company's auditor discovered "erroneous billing" and revealed a total of £77.6 million in overcharges initially, which has now been revised to £118 million. CTM is negotiating refunds with its UK clients and has implemented significant changes to financial controls and operational processes.  The Home Office is conducting an internal investigation into the overspend.

articles.title: Kerala man dies of suspected sunstroke during well construction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.V. Sanal Kumar, a 37-year-old well construction worker, died on Thursday after suffering suspected sunstroke while working near Chakkarakal in Kannur, Kerala. He collapsed during work on Wednesday and was transported to a private hospital where his condition remained critical before he passed away in the ICU.  The body has been taken to the district hospital for post-mortem procedures.

articles.title: Us Intercepted Iranian Oil Tankers: US intercepts 3 Iranian oil tankers near India, Malaysia amid maritime blockade - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US forces have intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged oil tankers in Asian waters, redirecting them away from positions near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka. The interceptions are part of a maritime blockade on Iran, which has been tightening restrictions on Tehran's seaborne trade amid an ongoing ceasefire. The US Central Command stated that it has directed at least 29 vessels to turn back or return to port since the blockade began, highlighting the scale of enforcement.  This action significantly disrupted global energy supply chains and heightened tensions in the region.

articles.title: Karnataka SSLC exam-1 results: Son of farm labourer with tiny landholding is Davangere topper - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bharath G., a student from Kanivebilachi village in Channagiri taluk of Davangere district, achieved the top score of 625 on the state-level exam.  His achievement comes from his daily commute to Vidyalakshmi English Medium School and the support of his parents, Girish (a farm laborer) and Shilpa (a homemaker). The school's headmistress, Laxmidevi A.N., expressed pride in his success.

articles.title: Pm Modi: 'Tell Putin to stop': Zelenskyy calls on 'big players' Donald Trump, PM Modi and Xi Jinping to put pressure on Russia - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian president, called on global leaders to pressure Vladimir Putin into ending the war in Ukraine. He argued that mediation alone may not be enough and emphasized the need for unified international pressure rather than compromise-based dialogue.  Zelenskyy also announced new defense partnerships with Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE, emphasizing the use of cheaper drone systems to counter Russian aggression.

articles.title: Karnataka SSLC exam-1 results: Vijayapura topper aspires to be a scientist - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Saujanya Kandakur, a student from Oxford English Medium School in Nagarbetta, achieved a score of 625 marks in the SSLC examination. Her parents, both teachers at a government school in Hungund, fostered her studious nature from childhood.  She plans to pursue higher education in science and become a scientist, crediting her success to smart studying techniques focused on understanding rather than rote learning.

articles.title: Union Bank Q4 Results: Net profit rises 7% YoY to 5,316 crore, provisions jump 3x - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Union Bank of India's net interest income decreased 1.1% year-over-year to Rs 9,406 crore in the recent quarter. Provisions surged nearly three-fold from the previous quarter, reaching Rs 1,055 crore. Asset quality improved with gross and net non-performing assets declining. The bank's board recommended a dividend of Rs 5 per equity share for the fiscal year 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval.  Shares of Union Bank of India experienced significant losses following the announcement.

articles.title: Major setback: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin rocket failure could delay NASA’s moon landing plans | - The Times of India
