The board of directors recommended a final dividend of Rs 13 per equity share for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, with a total dividend payout of Rs 15.50 per equity share. The record date for determining eligible shareholders is June 19, 2026.

articles.title: Centre's conspiracy to change federal structure defeated; victory of Opposition unity, says Priyanka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress general secretary, declared the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill to implement women's reservation as a victory for democracy and opposition unity. She accused the Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of attempting to manipulate the women's reservation law for political gain by linking it with delimitation plans. The bill, which aimed to increase Lok Sabha seats and state assembly representation through 33% reservation for women, failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lower House.

articles.title: ICICI Bank Q4 Results: Net profit up 8.5% to Rs 13,702 crore, announces Rs 12 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Bank reported a 8.4% increase in net interest income to Rs 22,979 crore for the quarter ending June 2023 compared to the same period last year. The bank's provisions declined significantly by 89% to Rs 96 crore, while its gross non-performing assets (NPAs) decreased to Rs 23,051.9 crore from Rs 23,758 crore in the previous quarter. ICICI Bank also saw a steady increase in total advances, rising by 15.8% year-on-year and 6% sequentially to Rs 15.53 lakh crore.

articles.title: Mandelson scandal is biggest crisis for diplomatic service in decades, says ex-Foreign Office chief | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A former Foreign Office chief, Simon McDonald, has criticized the handling of Peter Mandelson's security vetting failure and his subsequent appointment as ambassador to the US.  McDonald believes Oliver Robbins, who was dismissed from his role as permanent secretary of the Foreign Office, was unfairly treated by Keir Starmer and that the government misrepresented the vetting process to shift blame. The Commons foreign affairs select committee has invited Robbins to give evidence next week, with ministers concerned he may use this platform to attack No 10's version of events.

articles.title: Most-wanted trafficker held in FIA crackdown - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) conducted multiple operations across the country, arresting a notorious human smuggler and several other suspects.  Raza alias Chacha Musa, listed in international perpetrator lists, was apprehended in Quetta for his involvement in smuggling people from Iran to Pakistan. The FIA also arrested Mohammad Raza at the Taftan border for attempting to enter Pakistan with a fake passport. In Karachi, the Anti-Corruption Circle seized Rs2.234 million and other evidence related to an organized hawala/hundi network with China.  In Peshawar, Nasir Khan was arrested for illegal foreign currency exchange.

articles.title: Amid Nashik probe, TCS says no complaints received through internal channels - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TCS stated that it has not received any complaints regarding religious conversion and sexual misconduct at its Nashik unit, despite a police investigation. A preliminary review of internal records found no evidence of such allegations on either the ethics or POSH channels.

articles.title: 10 smallcap stocks ace investors Mukul Agrawal, Ashish Kacholia, Radhakishan Damani bought in Q4 - Stock Accumulation | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India’s top investors, including Ashish Kacholia, took advantage of the March quarter market correction to accumulate beaten-down smallcap stocks despite weak market sentiment.  The geopolitical tensions and war-related developments drove oil prices higher, fueling inflation concerns and triggering a risk-off mood. Mukul Agrawal also increased his stakes in several companies like Capacit'e Infraprojects, Hindustan Construction, and West Coast Paper.

articles.title: Most-wanted trafficker held in FIA crackdown - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) arrested a notorious human smuggler, Raza alias Chacha Musa, in Quetta as part of its ongoing crackdown on human smugglers and traffickers.  During the raid, investigators recovered communication evidence linking him to other smugglers operating from Iran, Balochistan, Punjab, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The FIA also arrested individuals involved in illegal hawala/hundi business across the country, including a suspect attempting to enter Pakistan with a fake passport at the Taftan border.  In Karachi, the Anti-Corruption Circle seized over Rs2.234 million in cash, ledgers, and suspicious documents during a raid on an office suspected of involvement in illegal hawala/hundi networks with China.

articles.title: GHMC takes up footpath encroachment clearance drive - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) used earth-mover equipment to remove unauthorized ramps extending onto footpaths and roads across several locations in the city on Saturday, April 18, 2026. The action was taken by Town Planning officials who broke down shop ramps and structures raised on pedestrian pathways.

articles.title: Bargain buys! Titan, Asian Paints, 8 largecap stocks that make ICICI Securities’ list. Do you own any? - Top Picks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Securities believes the Nifty benchmark index has reached a durable bottom after 18 months of consolidation and a 16% correction. The firm suggests this pattern indicates potential for a bull market, with several companies showing promising price movements.  These include Titan Company, Asian Paints, L&T, Bajaj Auto, Hindustan Aeronautics, Bharat Electronics, Power Grid Corp, Mahindra & Mahindra, DLF, and Ashok Leyland.

articles.title: EC assures High Court of action on complaint regarding distribution of ₹10,000 tokens in Harbour constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court closed a writ petition alleging the distribution of ₹10,000 tokens with QR codes and unique serial numbers on behalf of AIADMK candidate Royapuram Mano alias R. Manohar at the Harbour constituency in Chennai. The Election Commission of India (EC) assured the court that it would take action according to law after a flying squad found no evidence of distribution or seizure of such tokens despite receiving complaints. The court will continue to pursue the matter.

articles.title: Wipro among 18 stocks from which these 7 mutual funds made complete exit in March. Check details - Complete sell-off | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several mutual funds exited a total of 18 stocks in March, according to a report by Nuvama Institutional Equities.  HDFC Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Kotak Mutual Fund, Axis Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund, Quant Mutual Fund, and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund all made complete or partial exits from various stocks. The reasons for these changes are attributed to active portfolio management strategies.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: AIADMK is just a mask for BJP, says Rahul Gandhi at Ponneri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized AIADMK as a "mask" for the BJP's political interests in Tamil Nadu.  He accused the party of attacking Tamil history, culture, and language while campaigning for Congress candidate Durai Chandrasekar in Ponneri. Gandhi also highlighted his opposition to the recent delimitation bill, claiming it aimed to weaken Tamil Nadu's representation in Parliament. He pledged to protect Tamil language and ensure the future of Tamil Nadu is decided by its people.

articles.title: Yes Bank Q4 Results: Net profit rises 45% to Rs 1,068 crore, NII up 16% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: State Bank of India (SBI) reported strong financial performance in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, with net interest income increasing by 16% year-on-year to Rs 2,637.7 crore. The bank's net interest margin (NIM) improved to 2.7%, driven by lower cost of deposits and a reduction in PSL shortfall balances.  Net advances grew 11.1% year-on-year, with retail asset disbursements surging around 41%. Asset quality continued to improve, with gross and net non-performing assets declining. Credit costs remained contained at 0.2% of average assets for the quarter and full year.

articles.title: Britons opt for UK staycations as rising costs and travel concerns hit overseas trips | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UK holidaymakers are increasingly opting for domestic travel this year due to rising fuel prices and concerns over international travel. Airbnb, Haven, Sykes Holiday Cottages, and Butlin's have all reported increased bookings, with popular destinations including Northumberland, Pembrokeshire, and Whitby.  The trend is driven by a combination of economic factors like rising household costs and uncertainty surrounding global events, as evidenced by declining international travel demand. While domestic tourism offers some relief for hospitality businesses facing higher costs, the long-term sustainability of this trend hinges on how economic conditions evolve in the coming months.

articles.title: Gold funds vs ETFs: Where should mutual fund investors place their bets this Akshaya Tritiya? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gold funds and gold ETFs have delivered strong returns since the last Akshaya Tritiya, but investors should consider their structure and tax implications when choosing between them. ET Mutual Funds analysis shows that gold ETFs offer lower expense ratios and better price tracking, while gold funds provide ease of access for those without a demat account.  Experts recommend gold ETFs as a more cost-efficient option for long-term investors due to their transparency and tax efficiency. However, gold remains a cyclical asset class, and investors should consider its performance history when making investment decisions.

articles.title: Akshaya Tritiya remains proven entry point for gold investors: Motilal Oswal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Motilal Oswal Financial Services released a report stating that Akshaya Tritiya has historically been a favorable time for gold investment, with its long-term fundamentals intact. The report highlights the rise in interest towards flexible and transparent investment options, driven by factors like geopolitical tensions, slowing economic growth, and uncertainty around interest rate movements. While gold prices have risen nearly 10% this year, they are expected to trade within a broad range in the near term with a medium- to long-term outlook remaining constructive. The report recommends a "buy on dips" strategy for investors with a medium- to long-term horizon.

articles.title: Tragedy averted as 125 ferried to safety from Mangla Dam - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mirpur SSP Khurram Iqbal confirmed that 125 people, including women and children, were safely rescued from Mangla Dam after a thunderstorm disrupted their return journey from Ramkot Fort. The group, comprised of employees and their families from Mirpur and surrounding districts, had been on a day-long outing when the storm caused the floating platform to lose stability and drift within the reservoir.  Police, Rescue 1122, and two private teams of swimmers were mobilized to launch a rescue operation that lasted over an hour. The entire group was successfully evacuated by 9:30 pm.

articles.title: 5 equity mutual funds offer over 15% annualised return on SIP investments in 10 years. Check details - SIP investments | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ETWealth reports that five equity mutual funds have delivered over 15% annualized returns on SIP investments over the past decade. Quant Small Cap, Nippon India Small Cap, Nippon India Growth Mid Cap, and Edelweiss Mid Cap Fund all surpassed 20%, while Quant ELSS Tax Saver achieved 18.9%.  It is important to note that historical returns do not guarantee future performance, and investors should consider their individual risk tolerance, investment horizon, and financial goals when making investment decisions.

articles.title: Crude oil, copper, gold: The 3 commodities every beginner should track (and why they move!) - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Crude oil, OPEC, and global events heavily influence the price of crude, which affects fuel costs, transportation, and manufacturing.  Copper, a key indicator of economic growth, is used in construction, electrical wiring, electronics, and automobiles. Gold, often considered a safe haven during times of uncertainty, is influenced by inflation trends, interest rate decisions, and global risk sentiment. These three commodities provide insights into global market dynamics and investor sentiment.

articles.title: Netanyahu shocked by Trump's post on Lebanon? Report claims Israel asked US for clarification - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stunned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu by declaring Israel prohibited from further airstrikes in Lebanon, contradicting the ceasefire terms released by the US State Department.  While Iran announced the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping during the fragile ceasefire, Trump maintained pressure on Tehran, stating a naval blockade would remain in place until a complete transaction is reached. Despite the ceasefire, military activity continued with reports of an Israeli drone strike and Hezbollah attacks.

articles.title: Pressure on Starmer grows over Mandelson vetting despite ousting of Foreign Office official – UK politics live | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Peter Mandelson's vetting process failed, causing shock within Keir Starmer’s cabinet.  The Prime Minister expressed anger and disbelief over the lack of communication regarding the recommendation, while Antonia Romeo, the Cabinet Secretary, and Catherine Little, the Permanent Secretary, have denied any deliberate withholding of information. The situation has led to scrutiny of Olly Robbins, who resigned from his position at the Foreign Office due to Mandelson's vetting failure, with concerns that he may provide further damaging testimony before a powerful committee of MPs next week.

articles.title: Rural summer camp launched for children in Mandya district of Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mandya zilla panchayat, taluk panchayats, and the Department of School Education in Karnataka launched a district-wide summer camp called Akkareya Angala. The program, running from April 17 to May 26, aims to engage children aged 8-13 in constructive activities like reading, writing, creative arts, and games.  ZP Chief Executive Officer K. R. Nandini urged participation, emphasizing the camp's goal of providing enjoyable and productive summer breaks for rural children. The initiative also seeks to foster leadership skills, environmental awareness, social responsibility, cultural understanding, and creativity.

articles.title: This Akshaya Tritiya, your gold does not have to sit in a locker to work for you - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Akshaya, a financial philosophy, advocates for thoughtful gold ownership that aligns with modern financial goals.  The traditional approach of storing gold in physical forms without actively managing it is being challenged by the evolving financial landscape. Gold ETFs and digital gold offer greater transparency, liquidity, and ease of management, allowing investors to track their investments more effectively and make informed decisions about accumulation, timing, and redemption. This shift from passive ownership to active engagement with gold ensures its continued role as a protector of value while aligning it with modern financial objectives.

articles.title: What is so special about Iran’s uranium that US, China and Russia all want it? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States, China, and Russia are vying for influence over Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, a key point of contention in international relations. President Donald Trump claimed the US would retrieve the material with Iran, but Tehran rejected this proposal.  Experts warn that removing the uranium will be difficult due to its storage location and potential security risks. The dispute highlights the complex power dynamics at play as these countries seek to shape a future Middle East settlement.

articles.title: Young Bulgarians hold out for change in eighth election in five years | Bulgaria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anna Bodakova, a 23-year-old Bulgarian, is running for MP in the upcoming general election on Sunday.  She represents the pro-European We Continue the Change-Democratic Bulgaria (PP-DB) coalition and aims to translate the momentum of last year's protests into legislative change. However, her hopes face competition from Rumen Radev, a former president with a strong base among older voters who favor his anti-corruption stance.  Radev leads in polls but faces skepticism from younger generations like Aleksandar Tanev who believe he represents the status quo and is not a credible option for change. The election, plagued by allegations of vote-buying and disinformation campaigns, has sparked hope for increased voter turnout, which could lead to more accountable governance.

articles.title: UK farmer plans to breed ‘less photogenic’ Highland cows to stop tourists and influencers filming them | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Birch, a UK farmer from Derbyshire, plans to breed his Highland cows with another hill breed in an effort to make them less photogenic.  Birch cited repeated incidents of people approaching and filming the animals, leading to concerns about safety and liability. The Peak District National Park Authority has warned visitors against getting too close to cattle, emphasizing that hugging them is dangerous.

articles.title: Why Motilal Oswal’s BFSI fund is betting big on capital market ecosystem: Prateek Agarwal of Motilal Oswal AMC - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The India-US trade deal is expected to boost investor sentiment and attract foreign capital flows, reversing the trend of underperformance for Indian equities. The deal removes uncertainty surrounding duty structures for metals like steel and aluminum, benefiting manufacturing companies and potentially leading to increased investments in sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, and electronics.  While some volatility may occur around the March 15 advance tax deadline, overall sentiment is positive, with investors encouraged by improved valuations and a shift towards growth-oriented sectors. The Motilal Oswal Financial Services Fund, launched to capitalize on this positive environment, will focus on capital market-linked businesses, including AMCs, brokers, and exchanges.

articles.title: Lebanese return to ‘unliveable’ areas as ceasefire with Israel mostly holds - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Trump announced the US had banned further Israeli bombing in Lebanon, following a 10-day ceasefire between Hezbollah and Israel.  While optimism grows that the parallel war between the US and Iran could be nearing an end, the agreement leaves questions about long-term peace and Israel's continued occupation of parts of southern Lebanon. The ceasefire has allowed some displaced Lebanese to return home, but many remain hesitant due to destroyed homes and lingering fear of further conflict.  Despite this, a makeshift crossing over the Litani River in Qasmiyeh demonstrates the tentative return of normalcy.

articles.title: IPO activity remains muted next week with just one issue opening; three listings lined up - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Leapfrog Engineering Services, an SME IPO, will open for subscription on April 23 and close on April 27. The company offers engineering services in sectors like oil & gas, pharmaceuticals, food processing, and metals.  While the IPO is expected to list on April 30, market analysts note that investor participation remains selective due to flat grey market trends across upcoming listings. Three other IPOs are scheduled for listing next week: Mehul Telecom, Citius Transnet Investment Trust (InvIT), and Property Share Investment Trust (PropShare Celestia).

articles.title: ‘Trust Trump, not panicans’: Donald pushes ‘the peace president’ image after 'reopening' Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump declared himself "The Peace President" on social media, claiming to have resolved multiple international conflicts. He attributed the resolution of tensions between India and Pakistan to his actions, suggesting a potential increase in such successes with Iran and Lebanon.  However, Trump warned that military action against Iran could resume if negotiations fail before next week's ceasefire expires. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iranian Parliament Speaker, refuted claims of a ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon and asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Orbán's era was over in a flash and Hungary's next PM is a man in a hurry
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, leader of the victorious Tisza party, has promised to form a new parliament and elect a new government by May 4th.  He also pledged to pass laws limiting the number of terms a prime minister can serve to two, effectively barring Viktor Orbán from returning to power. The new government will face challenges including restoring checks and balances eroded during Orbán's rule, tackling corruption, and diversifying Hungary's oil supplies.  The incoming government has also pledged to address concerns about media freedom and the independence of the judiciary.

articles.title: 5 world market themes for the week ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors will watch closely as Kevin Warsh appears before Congress for his confirmation hearing on April 21st to discuss the Federal Reserve's future under President Trump.  The week also brings a look at how companies around the world are coping with the impact of the Iran war, and corporate earnings reports from Tesla and other major players.  Central banks in emerging Asia will face challenges as oil prices remain high despite easing, while Turkey's central bank faces pressure to hike rates due to inflation concerns.

articles.title: BMRCL managers spend more time in meetings than running Namma Metro in Bengaluru: E&M staff - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) employees in the Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) Department have raised concerns about operational and administrative issues impacting efficiency, staff morale, and system reliability. The employees claim that senior officers lack adequate E&M expertise and that this has led to delays in maintenance activities, technical support, and training opportunities for staff. BMRCL officials confirmed receipt of the representation and are conducting an internal investigation.

articles.title: Two weeks that pushed Trump to the edge. Is his presidency unravelling? | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is facing mounting criticism and setbacks in his presidency, with his approval ratings plummeting.  Concerns are growing among Republicans that he could lose control of Congress in the midterm elections. The president's recent actions, including a controversial attack on Pope Leo XIV and an inflammatory post about Iran, have alienated key supporters. His handling of the war in Iran has also drawn criticism from allies and experts who fear it will further damage his legacy.  Trump's attempts to deflect blame for rising inflation and other issues have been unsuccessful, leaving him with dwindling support.

articles.title: Berkshire CEO Abel sold stocks managed by ex-portfolio manager Combs, WSJ reports - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Warren Buffett's successor, Greg Abel, has made a significant change to Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio by removing David Combs, who recently joined JPMorgan Chase.  The move marks one of the first major changes under Abel's leadership.  Berkshire Hathaway is expected to disclose further details about its equity holdings in its upcoming quarterly report and regulatory filing.

articles.title: Heatwave alert in Maharashtra till April 20; Akola hottest at 44.2°C - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued heatwave alerts for six states, including Maharashtra, where temperatures are expected to rise by 1-2°C over the next three days. The highest recorded temperature in the country so far is 44.2°C in Akola district.  Dr. Pradeep Awate, former State Surveillance Officer, Maharashtra Health Services, attributes the rising temperatures to concrete projects and a decline in trees, which are contributing to increased heat in Mumbai. Bikram Singh, chief scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, stated that the IMD is vigilant and has already sent alerts regarding the heatwave conditions. The Maharashtra Government has implemented standard operating procedures (SOPs) to address the impact of the heatwaves, including regulating working hours during peak temperatures.

articles.title: Akshaya Tritiya: Tapan Patel on why you shouldn't let the recent dip in gold scare you - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors were surprised by the decline in gold and silver prices during the war, with factors like negative correlation with the dollar, rising oil prices, and market uncertainties contributing to the drop.  Global central banks have slowed their gold buying pace but may resume it as market dynamics shift. Investors are advised to consider a diversified portfolio that includes gold and silver, potentially allocating 15-20% of assets to these precious metals. The rupee depreciation can be a tailwind for gold and silver prices in India, particularly during periods of global price falls.

articles.title: Antarctica has no cities, no people, and no permanent life: Here’s why humans can’t stay there forever | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Antarctica, the only continent without permanent human settlements, is primarily inhabited by researchers and scientists who conduct temporary work on climate change, ice movement, geology, and animal studies. These research stations are not meant to be permanent homes due to harsh environmental conditions such as extreme cold, darkness, strong winds, and limited resources.  The continent's unique environment makes it ideal for studying Earth's climate history but does not support a permanent human population.

articles.title: Naval Commanders’ Conference concludes, Home Secretary stresses coastal security - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The first edition of the biannual Naval Commanders’ Conference 2026 concluded in New Delhi after four days of discussions on operational readiness, emerging security challenges and future force development. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan emphasized the need for increased coordination between the Navy and other agencies to strengthen coastal security. The Chief of the Naval Staff highlighted the complex geopolitical landscape and the increasing threat from non-state actors, calling for sustained combat readiness and rapid adoption of emerging technologies.  The conference also saw the release of the Indian Navy Maritime Security Strategy (INMSS-2026) outlining India’s maritime security priorities for the coming decade.

articles.title: Akshaya Tritiya: Tapan Patel on why you shouldn't let the recent dip in gold scare you - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gold and silver prices fell during the war, driven by negative correlation with the dollar, rising oil prices, and equity market liquidation.  Central banks have slowed gold buying but may resume it in the future due to structural changes in market dynamics. Investors are advised to consider a diversified portfolio including Gold ETFs, Digi Gold, or Multi Asset Mutual Funds. The rupee depreciation can be a tailwind for Indian investors as it supports gold and silver prices.

articles.title: Uae Traffic Rules: UAE enforces stricter traffic rules with fines reaching Dh50,000 and licence suspension penalties | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE's new traffic regulation law, enforced by the Ministry of Interior and local authorities, outlines rules for suspending, cancelling, or denying driving licence renewals. The law focuses on driver fitness, repeat offences, and public safety risks, giving authorities broad powers to intervene before and after serious incidents.  Drivers found medically unfit or posing a risk can have their licenses suspended, while repeated violations can lead to permanent cancellation.  The law also empowers courts to order licence revocation in severe cases. Authorities can use AI-powered cameras and nationwide monitoring systems to enforce the new rules, emphasizing long-term road safety improvements.

articles.title: Parliament special sitting LIVE: Opposition hails Constitution Amendment Bill's defeat in Lok Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Opposition defeated the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which aimed to redistribute Lok Sabha seats based on the 2011 Census for women's reservation. The bill failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the House, leading to its withdrawal along with related legislation. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge expressed gratitude for the opposition's efforts in safeguarding democracy and federalism.

articles.title: ‘It’s a powder keg’: Romania leads EU measles cases as vaccination rates collapse | Romania | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Romanian government is facing a measles crisis, with the country recording over 35,000 cases and at least 30 deaths between 2023 and 2025.  Dr Mirela Csabai, a general practitioner in Săcele, says that low vaccination rates are fueling the epidemic, as only 81% of children receive the MMR vaccine by age five. Dr Aurora Stanescu, an epidemiologist at the National Institute of Public Health, states that a firm political commitment to limit deaths is necessary.  Gabriela Alexandrescu, country director for Save the Children, highlights structural issues such as poverty, medical deserts, and lack of resources as contributing factors.  Many parents are hesitant due to misinformation and fear, with some citing unfounded fears about the MMR vaccine's link to autism.

articles.title: Complete Padmavathi Children’s hospital as per schedule: JEO - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Sri Padmavathi Children’s Super Specialty Hospital
articles.rephrased_article: TTD's Joint Executive Officer (Health & Education), A. Sharath, confirmed that the Sri Padmavathi Children’s Super Specialty Hospital project will be completed on schedule. The six-floor facility at the foot of Tirumala hills includes a helipad for emergency cases and model rooms with comprehensive planning for engineering, electrical, fire safety, medical equipment, and allied facilities.  Mr. Sharath emphasized coordinating pending works with relevant departments and ensuring adequate medical support in each room to meet patient service standards.

articles.title: Adani bags top spot in richest Asians’ club - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Group owner Gautam Adani surpassed Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani to become the wealthiest person on the Bloomberg Billionaire Index, with a net worth of $92.6 billion as of April 16th. This surge in wealth comes after several listed companies within the Adani Group experienced significant gains throughout the month.  The global list is dominated by American figures, with Elon Musk at the top. Adani briefly held the fourth position globally in September 2022 before a sharp decline due to allegations of accounting irregularities from Hindenburg Research.

articles.title: Pune police book two students over dance performance on Maoist leader at Govt hostel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pune police have filed an FIR against two students from Gadchiroli district for a dance performance featuring a song about Madvi Hidma, a Maoist leader, during a cultural event at a government-run boys’ hostel. The performance, which took place between April 6 and April 14 to mark the 135th birth anniversary of B.R. Ambedkar, was deemed prejudicial to national integration and public mischief under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).  The students claim they were unaware of Hidma's background and performed without malicious intent. The police are investigating further.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Criminalizing artistic expression critical of the state is a suppression of free speech.

articles.title: Even a Rs 15,000-crore buyback fails to cheer Wipro investors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Infosys, India's fourth-largest IT services company, announced a share buyback at a 19% premium to its previous closing price. However, the move failed to boost investor confidence, with the stock declining after the announcement.  Analysts expressed cautiousness, citing weak performance and continued revenue contraction in the near term. Goldman Sachs and Kotak Institutional Equities both noted Infosys's lagging performance compared to peers and highlighted a widening gap between its growth and competitors.

articles.title: Family of US man who died after officer shoved knee into back sues police | US crime | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: Wyandotte county sheriff's deputy Richard Fatherley
articles.rephrased_article: Relatives of Charles Adair, who died in custody after a confrontation with Wyandotte county sheriff's deputy Richard Fatherley, have filed a wrongful death lawsuit. The lawsuit, filed by civil rights attorneys Ben Crump and Harry Daniels, demands the release of video footage from the incident.  The lawsuit claims that Fatherley pressed his body weight on Adair's back for over a minute, despite Adair's apparent mental health impairment and repeated pleas for help. The sheriff's office has declined to release the video, citing pending litigation. A status conference in Fatherley's criminal case is scheduled for May.

articles.title: Punjab’s border farmers caught between fence and Zero Line - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers in Rosse village, on the India-Pakistan border in Gurdaspur district of Punjab, are gathering for Baisakhi celebrations despite facing difficulties due to border fencing.  The central government is undertaking surveys to relocate the fence closer to the international boundary, aiming to provide farmers with greater access to their fields and freedom from restrictions. While this move offers hope, farmers continue to face challenges until then.

articles.title: Bullish momentum continues, but analysts warn of near-term resistance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE's Nifty and BSE's Sensex indices experienced gains this week, driven by easing tensions in West Asia, cooling oil prices, and a strengthening rupee.  Analysts suggest the positive trend could persist as long as the conflict remains contained. However, some analysts warn of potential profit-taking at resistance levels near 24,300-24,500. Foreign portfolio investors purchased shares worth ₹683 crore while domestic institutions sold off shares to the tune of ₹4,721 crore.

articles.title: Wedding paid off by Pokémon cards: Man finds ultra-rare collection in attic after 20 years, sells for huge windfall | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Braund, a 37-year-old teaching assistant from Dorset, had his life transformed after discovering a collection of Pokémon cards in his parents' attic.  He initially thought the cards were worth around £500 but was surprised to learn they could fetch up to £32,800 at auction. The three Charizard cards sold for a combined total of £32,800, with one reaching a record-breaking $21,250.  The proceeds will be used to fund his upcoming wedding to fiancée Rachel Moseley and the couple are now considering a honeymoon in Devon.

articles.title: U.S.-Iran tension will not deter Haj pilgrims, say officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian officials confirmed that despite ongoing tensions in the Middle East, India will proceed with its Haj pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. The first batch of pilgrims is scheduled to depart on April 18th from various embarkation points in India.  The Indian Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Saudi authorities are coordinating to ensure a smooth operation for the estimated 1.75 lakh pilgrims expected during the season, which will last until May.

articles.title: Nine people dead as van plunges off Valparai cliff in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A van carrying nine members of a tourist group from Kerala tragically crashed on the ghat road in Valparai, Coimbatore district. The accident occurred between hairpin bends 13 and 9, resulting in the deaths of all nine passengers.  Three critically injured individuals were transferred to a hospital in Coimbatore for advanced treatment.

articles.title: Mechanic hacked to death by friend - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mohan, a 25-year-old mechanic from Tamil Nadu, was fatally attacked by his friend Manoj, also 25, in an empty plot near Sarjapur on Thursday evening. The altercation stemmed from a petty argument over alcohol consumption and escalated into a physical assault where Manoj allegedly struck Mohan's head with a heavy object.  The police arrested Manoj after receiving information about the incident and are currently interrogating him.

articles.title: Sabarimala hearing: Should judges rise above their religious perceptions when examining matters of conscience, SC judge asks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court sought clarification from senior advocate Rajeev Dhavan on the balance between judges' personal religious beliefs and their judicial duty when examining freedom of conscience. Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, part of the nine-judge Bench hearing the Sabarimala review case, questioned whether judges should transcend personal religious consciousness while applying constitutional provisions to religious practices.

articles.title: NCB destroys drugs worth ₹38 crore in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Narcotics Control Bureau’s (NCB) Bengaluru Zonal Unit conducted a large-scale drug disposal drive, incinerating 128.75 kg of narcotics linked to 13 cases worth an estimated ₹38 crore. The substances included ganja, hydroponic ganja, cocaine, methamphetamine, and MDMA.  The process was carried out in an environmentally compliant manner, adhering to prescribed safety and pollution control norms.

articles.title: Income Tax officials search premises linked to Senthilbalaji’s aides in Karur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Income Tax Department officials conducted simultaneous searches at seven locations linked to former Minister V. Senthilbalaji's associates in Karur on Friday morning. The properties searched included the office of PWD contractor M.C.S. Sankar Anand, Sakthi mess, the proprietor's house at Kothai Nagar, Kongu Mess, and the proprietor's house at Rayanur.  The searches were conducted with the presence of Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel.

articles.title: JD(U) likely to elect new head of legislature party at Patna meet on April 20 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: JD(U) is expected to elect a new legislature leader on April 20, 2026, following the resignation of Nitish Kumar, who was replaced by Samrat Choudhary. The meeting will be held in Patna at Kumar's new address. Speculation surrounds senior leader Vijay Kumar Chaudhary, currently one of two Deputy Chief Ministers, as a possible candidate for the position.  The party post has been vacant since Kumar's resignation on April 14th.

articles.title: Prakash Karat praises Stalin, INDIA bloc for defeating Constitutional Amendment Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prakash Karat, former general secretary of the CPI(M), praised Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the INDIA bloc for successfully blocking a Constitutional Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha.  Karat argued that the bill was an attempt by the Modi government to disrupt the country's federal structure and delimitation of Parliament seats. He hailed this victory as a triumph for democratic forces.

articles.title: Develop century-old schools in Karnataka as heritage institutions: KDA to govt. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kannada Development Authority (KDA) has recommended that at least 31 schools in Karnataka, where prominent figures studied, be developed as "Heritage Schools" to preserve their historical significance. The report also suggests establishing museums within these schools and allocating resources for the development of century-old government schools.  It further proposes a separate cell in the Education Department to manage these schools and prioritize their improvement through increased funding and teacher appointments.

articles.title: Expert committee recommends reducing CSE seats by 17% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A committee formed to examine a proposal capping Computer Science Engineering (CSE) seats has recommended reducing CSE seats by 17% starting in 2026-27. The committee, led by S. Sadagopan, suggests the government integrate AI into all core subject streams and divert freed seats to Core+AI courses instead of limiting intake solely to CSE.  The report also recommends a nine-step formula for rebalancing seat allocation and embedding AI in undergraduate disciplines.

articles.title: Chhattisgarh power plant tragedy: toll rises to 21, Opposition wants culpable homicide charges to be slapped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The death toll from this week's power plant explosion in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district has risen to 21, with another worker succumbing to his injuries on Thursday night.  Vedanta Group chairman Anil Agrawal, company manager Devendra Patel, and other responsible officers have been booked under BNS sections for prima facie negligence related to the accident. The Congress party is demanding charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder be added to the case, citing evidence suggesting inadequate maintenance and operation standards led to the boiler explosion.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports a deadly industrial accident with potential negligence by company officials.

articles.title: India-flagged vessels start sailing out of Hormuz - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian ships stranded in the Persian Gulf began sailing out of the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the strait was "completely open."  Several crude oil tankers, including MT Desh Garima, Desh Suraksha, and MT Desh Vaibhav, have departed from ports in Qatar, UAE, and Iraq. Other vessels, like CMA CGM Diamond and CMA CGM Manaus, are also making their way out of the Gulf. The movement comes after Iran released a navigation chart that designated a portion of the Strait as a "hazard zone" requiring coordination with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for passage.

articles.title: EWS can't seek age relaxation, enhanced attempts like SC,ST, OBC: Delhi High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court ruled that individuals belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) cannot claim the same age relaxation and attempt limits as candidates from Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). The court emphasized that the disadvantages faced by EWS and SC/ST/OBC categories are distinct, with EWS primarily stemming from economic deprivation while the latter is rooted in social and historical exclusion. The court rejected arguments that the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and eight other states' extension of age relaxation to EWS candidates necessitates similar action by the Central government.

articles.title: Mob attacks Assam forest range office over alleged land encroachment, several injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A mob of protesters, angered by the detention of several locals for alleged encroachment on forest land, attacked an office of the Assam Forest Department in Chirang district. The violence resulted in damage to government property and injuries to over 30 people, including police personnel.  The clash intensified after police used force to control the situation, leading to the arrest of at least four protesters. The incident occurred following a previous protest on Thursday night where members of the Adivasi community demanded the release of those detained.

articles.title: Florida man kills dog owner while trying to shoot his pet animal that was attacking a woman, police say - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Matthew Lee Pasco, a 43-year-old man who is homeless, is considered armed and dangerous after fatally shooting the owner of a dog he intervened to stop from attacking a woman in Leesburg, Florida.  Pasco fled the scene on foot after the incident on Friday and remains at large. Lake County Sheriff’s Office deputies are searching for him while Lake County Public Schools placed Carver Middle School on lockdown during the search operation. Authorities have urged anyone with information to contact law enforcement immediately.

articles.title: Trump seeks ‘resolution’ of his $10bn lawsuit against IRS, spurring concern | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's legal team has requested a 90-day pause in the $10 billion lawsuit he filed against the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), aiming for a resolution. Critics argue that such a settlement would allow Trump to negotiate with his own administration, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest and abuse of power. The case stems from an incident involving stolen tax returns in 2017, which led to public scrutiny and media reports revealing Trump's low tax payments.

articles.title: Perez Hilton points to deeper struggle after Clavicular shares bloodied face following overdose livestream incident - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a 20-year-old online creator, recently shared a photo of his bloodied face after a suspected overdose during a livestream. The incident, which occurred while he was live with other influencers, raised concerns about the pressure to maintain an idealized online persona and fueled discussions about mental health in the influencer community. Perez Hilton, blogger, described the situation as a stark shift from Clavicular's usual image and highlighted how public this event became.  Androgenic, another creator present during the livestream, confirmed that Peters quickly deteriorated after struggling to speak clearly before being rushed to the hospital.

articles.title: US judge blocks Justice Department bid to seize voter data in Rhode Island | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge in Rhode Island dismissed a Department of Justice lawsuit seeking access to voter data, marking another setback for the Trump administration's efforts to obtain such information from multiple states. Judge Mary McElroy ruled that the Justice Department lacked authority to conduct a "fishing expedition" and sided with election officials and civil rights groups who expressed concerns about privacy violations.  The ruling comes amidst ongoing legal battles over voter data access, with Trump continuing to claim widespread fraud in the 2020 election despite no evidence supporting those claims. The Justice Department has sued at least 30 states for their voter information, maintaining it needs the data for election security, but state officials have argued that turning over the data raises privacy concerns.

articles.title: Madrasa students allegedly assaulted - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Meppayur police are investigating an assault on four minor Madrasa students from Cheruvannur. The incident occurred Thursday night when the students were engaged in wall writing work and two residents allegedly attacked them, resulting in injuries requiring medical attention for two students. Police identified the suspects based on statements from the injured students, who reported a quarrel over permission for campaign work on private property as the cause of the assault.

articles.title: Heat, humidity make life miserable in north Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's northern districts have experienced unusually high temperatures, with Palakkad recording the highest temperature of the season at 40.1°C on April 10th.  Kannur airport reached 38.1°C last week, and maximum temperatures in Kozhikode, Kasaragod, Malappuram, and Wayanad have also been above average. The high heat has made daily life uncomfortable due to the combination of high temperatures and humidity.

articles.title: SC agrees to hear CBI’s plea against HC order acquitting 4 in custodial-death case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court agreed to hear a plea from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) challenging a Kerala High Court decision that overturned convictions in a 2005 custodial death case. The court issued a notice to the accused and set a hearing date for May 19th.  The case involves Udayakumar, who died in police custody in Thiruvananthapuram in September 2005 after alleged torture.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Custodial death and potential abuse of power warrant urgent attention.

articles.title: Higher education budget up by 60% in 5 years, yet T.N. govt. universities continue to struggle for funds - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department has seen a significant increase in budgetary allocation over the past five years, rising from ₹5,369 crore in 2021-22 to ₹8,494 crore in 2025-26. However, despite this substantial increase, state-run universities continue to face financial strain.  A government committee recommended a Performance Incentive Grant to incentivize fiscal discipline and academic performance, along with adjustments to the disbursement of Block Grants. The committee also fixed a payout of ₹242 crore for Block Grants based on specific conditions to balance staff salaries and improved performance.

articles.title: HC asks under what authority of law breath analyser test held on advocate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice E.V. Venugopal of the Telangana High Court questioned Inspector Ramakrishna of the Punjagutta police station about the authority to conduct a breath analyser test on advocate Subba Rao, who visited the station to inquire about a case.  The judge noted that the video evidence presented showed the test was "unknown to law" and sought clarification on the reasons for the disturbance leading to the test.

articles.title: How the war on Iran set off worker protests around Delhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gangeshwar Datt Sharma, a former shoe-maker, has been under house arrest for over a week in Uttar Pradesh after organizing workers against management exploitation.  He was involved with the workers' movement from his early days at a Noida shoe factory catering to the Russian market. The police arrested Sharma and three others following protests against unfair labor practices. Over 350 people, including many women, have also been detained.

articles.title: Protesters hit streets, seek Ganderbal probe report, youth’s body - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Protests erupted in Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir on Friday over the Lieutenant Governor-led administration's delay in releasing a magisterial inquiry report into the April 1 encounter.  The Army claimed to have killed a terrorist during a cordon and search operation, but the slain man's family identified him as Raashid Ahmad Mughal, a civilian with no militant links, and his burial was at a designated site for militants.

articles.title: NIMHANS meet proposes national framework for digital mental health tools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NIMHANS, the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Centre for Advanced Research on Digital Interventions for Mental Health Care, hosted a three-day national consultation on digital technologies for mental health. The meeting, held in collaboration with SHUT Clinic and guided by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and ICMR, resulted in recommendations including a national governance framework, a verified directory of apps, and digital literacy initiatives.

articles.title: Rising bitumen cost slows Bengaluru road works, GBA to bear cost difference, BDA to follow - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has implemented a star rate system for bitumen, cement, and steel to address the impact of fluctuating prices caused by the West Asia crisis. The BDA is expected to adopt this method as well, including for pending works at Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout (NPKL). The GBA also extended project deadlines by 33 days to mitigate disruptions caused by the crisis. This decision impacts several projects that were scheduled to be completed before the monsoon season.

articles.title: Cash incentives for women steer Bengal poll discourse - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: With less than seven days until the first phase of voting in West Bengal, Trinamool Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party are vying for women's votes with their respective welfare schemes. The Trinamool Congress’s Lakshmir Bhandar program has been a successful model for the party, offering ₹1,500 per month to eligible women.  The BJP countered with its Matri Shakti Vandan Yojana promising ₹3,000 per month, leading to clashes between supporters of both parties. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee criticized the BJP's tactics and accused them of collecting voter information for undue advantage. The BJP defended their actions, stating that they were simply offering a better scheme than the Trinamool’s previous program.

articles.title: Starmer rejects calls to quit as pressure mounts over Mandelson vetting | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faced renewed calls to resign over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as UK envoy to Washington, which was marred by security vetting failures.  Starmer stated he was "absolutely furious" that he wasn't informed about the decision and promised to reveal all relevant facts in Parliament on Monday.  Olly Robbins, a top Foreign Office civil servant, was ousted following the revelation of the botched process, while Darren Jones, chief secretary to the prime minister, confirmed the recommendation against appointing Mandelson was ignored. The Conservative Party leader, Kemi Badenoch, criticized the claims that Starmer didn't know about the situation and called for his resignation.

articles.title: Central Kerala reels under sizzling heat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts a maximum temperature of 38°Celsius in Kottayam and 37°Celsius in other districts of central Kerala.  The region's average maximum temperature has risen by 0.6°Celsius since 1980, leading to increased heat stress and health issues. Dairy and poultry farmers are experiencing a decline in milk production and livestock survival due to the high temperatures. The Ernakulam District Disaster Management Authority is implementing the heat action plan provided by the State Disaster Management Authority (DDMA).

articles.title: Traders place $760 million bet on falling oil ahead of Hormuz announcement - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. lawmakers and legal experts are raising concerns about the potential for traders to gain an advantage in volatile derivatives markets due to recent large, well-timed trades related to oil futures.  These trades have occurred shortly before significant policy shifts regarding the war in Iran, including a ceasefire announcement by Iran's foreign minister and U.S. President Donald Trump's decision to delay attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating these trades, which include those on March 23 and April 7.

articles.title: From ultra left to campaigner for Tamil Brahmins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. S. Pandiarajan, a Madurai lawyer, experienced a rift with the CPI(ML) after being passed over for leadership despite his commitment and seniority. He alleges that he was told his Brahmin heritage disqualified him, a claim he believes is unique to Tamil Nadu.  Pandiarajan's family background, rooted in Tiruchendur, reflects modest means and a strong connection to Tamil culture. Despite his fervent belief in social change within the party, this experience led to a departure from the CPI(ML).

articles.title: Ice Spice: Ice Spice gets slapped by fan during wild McDonald’s fight in Los Angeles - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ice Spice, a popular rapper and streamer, was slapped by a fan at a McDonald's restaurant in Los Angeles. The incident escalated quickly after the fan attempted to join Ice Spice and her friend, leading to a chaotic scene with both sides exchanging heated words and accusations.  The fan, identified as Vayah, claimed she only approached Ice Spice for support but was met with rudeness, while Ice Spice's lawyer stated the attack was unprovoked and reported to the police. The incident has sparked online debate about who is at fault.

articles.title: Sebi clears four IPOs including Avaada Electro and Grand Housing - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Avaada Electro, a solar manufacturing firm backed by Brookfield, is expected to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through an IPO, with proceeds earmarked for expanding its manufacturing capacity.  Grand Housing, a Chennai-based real estate developer, will launch an offer-for-sale of up to 3.55 crore shares, while Sonaselection India will issue a fresh equity offering of 1.43 crore shares. Vishal Nirmiti, an infrastructure player, plans to raise funds through a combination of a Rs 125 crore fresh issue and an offer-for-sale component.

articles.title: Kick streamer Clavicular avoids father after overdose incident as Miami club appearance raises serious questions - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Braden Clavicular, a social media personality, reportedly refused to meet with his father, Ken Peters, after a suspected overdose in Miami.  Clavicular allegedly attended a nightclub appearance despite the intervention attempt by his father who flew from New Jersey. Sources say the situation is escalating beyond online drama as it involves family concerns and a lack of communication between father and son.

articles.title: Pune airport runway shut after IAF aircraft 'hand landing' - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Air Force (IAF) announced that the runway at Pune airport is temporarily closed following an incident involving one of its aircraft. The aircrew are safe and there is no damage to civil property, according to the IAF.  Union Minister of State for Aviation Murlidhar Mohol confirmed the suspension of runway operations and stated that it may take 5 hours to restore normal operations.

articles.title: Arizona judge backs key Republican election official in voting board fight | Arizona | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Maricopa County Superior Court Judge Scott Blaney ruled in favor of Justin Heap, the Republican recorder, who had sued the county board of supervisors for allegedly taking control of election administration. The judge found that the board exceeded its authority by seizing personnel and equipment from Heap's office and ruled that the recorder is responsible for overseeing in-person early voting, among other duties.  The board chair, Kate Brophy McGee, stated they would appeal the ruling.

articles.title: Oil prices crash nearly 10% after Iran says Strait of Hormuz completely open during ceasefire - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent crude prices dropped nearly 10% to $89.11 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell even further, sliding 11% to $84.11. The decline was driven by optimism surrounding a potential US-Iran agreement and comments from former President Donald Trump suggesting Iran's willingness to refrain from pursuing nuclear weapons for over two decades. Geopolitical developments in the Middle East also influenced market expectations. A temporary easing of tensions between Israel and Lebanon, including a 10-day ceasefire, has reduced immediate risks to regional stability. However, analysts caution that oil prices are unlikely to stabilize quickly and expect continued volatility until a formal agreement is reached and shipping activity normalizes.

articles.title: It’s Messi vs Ronaldo all over again! Icons return to Spanish football as rival club owners in major twist | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, both former Spanish football stars, have entered the ownership landscape of their home country.  Messi purchased a 100% stake in UE Cornellà, a fifth-tier club near Barcelona, while Ronaldo acquired a 25% stake in UD Almería, a Segunda División team aiming for promotion to La Liga. While separated by division and ambition, both moves bring them back into the same football structure where their rivalry was born.  This connection provides fans with an intriguing prospect of their paths crossing again, even if it is years away.

articles.title: Aster Volunteers expands community outreach, launches five mobile medical units - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Aster DM Healthcare expanded its community healthcare outreach by launching five new mobile medical units (MMUs) in Bengaluru, bringing the global fleet to 76 units. The MMUs will provide free primary consultations, screenings for non-communicable diseases, maternal and child healthcare services, health education, and referrals for advanced treatment across Ranchi, Kanpur, Bhopal, Jaipur, and Bhubaneswar.  Azad Moopen, founder and chairman of Aster group, stated the initiative aims to improve access to healthcare at the community level by providing preventive screenings and early diagnosis.

articles.title: Officer on horseback chases suspect through New York streets
articles.rephrased_article: New York police officers on horseback pursued a suspect who was allegedly stealing purses in the city. The suspect, identified as a woman, resisted arrest and was eventually apprehended by a pedestrian after a chase through streets. She has been charged with larceny and providing false information.  The woman had previously served time in prison for murder in 2000.

articles.title: GIFT Nifty jumps over 300 points after oil price crash. What to expect on Monday? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian markets are showing strength due to a decline in crude oil prices, easing inflationary pressure and boosting investor sentiment.  The GIFT Nifty is indicating a significant gap-up opening on Monday, with analysts predicting the Nifty could surpass 24,300 and potentially reach 24,700 levels. The positive global sentiment stemming from de-escalation in geopolitical tensions also contributed to this bullish outlook.

articles.title: Coldplay kiss cam scandal executive Kristin Cabot says lead singer Chris Martin did not reach out to her: 'Nope. Never did' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kristin Cabot, a corporate executive who went viral after an embrace with her boss at a Coldplay concert, has stated she is done with the band.  Cabot claims she received no contact from Chris Martin, the band's frontman, and would not attend another concert. She previously defended the incident, stating it was misinterpreted and that both she and her husband were present at the concert. Cabot has since criticized a separate Astronomer advertisement referencing the incident.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court upholds cancellation of school’s recognition for producing fake certificate and illegally running madarasa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka High Court upheld the cancellation of recognition for a private school that had been operating for 20 years. The court found that the school's society submitted a fake certificate claiming registration in 1979, and operated schools under different names with unauthorized accounts.  The Education Department cancelled the school's recognition in May 2025, and the appellate authority endorsed this decision in January 2026.

articles.title: Xqc Health Update: xQc leaves stream abruptly after falling sick as Sidemen Charity Match 2026 plans face uncertainty - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Felix “xQc” Lengyel experienced a health scare during a livestream training session on April 16, 2026. Jynxzi, his fellow streamer, stayed by his side and offered support but noticed his poor hydration habits.  The stream ended as xQc admitted to feeling unwell and experiencing nausea. He revealed that he barely drinks water, preferring lemonade, which raised concerns about his health and preparedness for the upcoming Sidemen Charity Match 2026. The incident has sparked a discussion about proper hydration and health practices in high-intensity training.

articles.title: Allahabad HC orders FIR against Rahul Gandhi in alleged dual citizenship case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court ordered the registration of an FIR and further investigation into allegations that Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, holds British citizenship. The petitioner, S. Vignesh Shishir, claimed that Mr. Gandhi declared his nationality as British in company documents and filings related to M/s Backops Ltd., which was incorporated in the United Kingdom in 2003.  The court directed the state government to register a case and investigate through a central agency.

articles.title: 80-year-old Sikh, inspired by Fauja Singh, to run London Marathon for first time - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Baldev Singh Bains, an 80-year-old British Sikh man, is running the London Marathon on April 26th to raise money for the Fauja Singh Clubhouse, a facility being built in Fauja Singh's memory.  Bains was inspired by Fauja Singh, who encouraged him to start walking and then running after he discovered running in his 80s. Harmander Singh, Fauja's coach, is also running the marathon to raise funds for the clubhouse. The clubhouse will cost £1 million and was given planning permission on April 1st, which would have been Fauja's 115th birthday.

articles.title: Voter awareness exhibition organised at Marina Beach - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai residents gathered at Marina Beach for an idli-themed voter awareness exhibition to encourage 100% participation in the upcoming Assembly election. The event featured idlis shaped like electronic voting machines and other symbols promoting full voter engagement.  The initiative, part of a series of activities across 16 constituencies, included cultural programs, advertisements, and mobile messaging campaigns. Visitors were served various types of idlis, including millet and chocolate varieties.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth II: “It’s worth remembering that it is often the small steps, not the giant leaps, that bring about the most lasting change.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Queen Elizabeth II's quote, "It’s worth remembering that it is often the small steps, not the giant leaps, that bring about the most lasting change," highlights the importance of consistent effort over time for achieving significant results.  This principle applies to both individual development and societal progress, emphasizing that small, steady actions can lead to long-lasting positive changes in areas like health, education, relationships, and even global issues such as environmental protection and social justice.

articles.title: Deservedly dead: The Hindu Editorial on the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 failed to secure the necessary two-thirds majority for passage in the Indian Parliament.  While 298 members voted in favor and 230 against, the bill needed 352 votes. The government subsequently shelved related bills due to the lack of consensus. Home Minister Amit Shah offered a verbal guarantee of proportional representation increases for southern states but this was dismissed by the opposition.  The defeat highlights the need for genuine consensus on delimitation and Lok Sabha expansion, as opposed to using procedural shortcuts.

articles.title: Exporters seek removal of cap on interest subvention - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Exporters in Mumbai urged the government to remove the cap on interest subvention, arguing it is inadequate to offset rising global trade uncertainties and higher borrowing costs. The Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO)  said the current 75% subvention with a 50% cap is insufficient and expects the government to revisit the scheme structure for more meaningful relief.

articles.title: Why didn’t Erika Kirk attend JD Vance’s Turning Point USA event? Source says it was more than just ‘security concerns’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Erika Kirk, widow of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk, withdrew from a Turning Point USA event with JD Vance, US vice president, citing "serious threats" to her safety.  Insiders say the decision was influenced by growing public scrutiny and online criticism following her husband's assassination last year, as well as exhaustion from constant media attention. The backlash intensified after comedian Druski mocked Kirk's appearances, further contributing to her decision to withdraw.

articles.title: Deservedly dead: The Hindu Editorial on the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 failed to pass the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.  While 298 members voted in favor and 230 against, the bill needed 352 votes. The government shelved the companion Delimitation Bill and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill citing the need for a consensus. Home Minister Amit Shah offered to increase the representation of southern states by 50% but this was rejected by the opposition who criticized the lack of clarity in the bill and its timing.

articles.title: Sridhar Babu urges defence, R&D labs to partner with Telangana on aerospace - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries of Telangana, urged the defense industry, research laboratories, and scientists to collaborate with the state government to build a strong aerospace ecosystem in Hyderabad. He highlighted the region's existing infrastructure, talent pool, and dedicated aerospace clusters, noting that over 1,500 firms contribute to global aerospace supply chains within Telangana.

articles.title: Opposition defeated an attack on the Constitution, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition, hailed the defeat of the Constitution Amendment Bill concerning women's reservation as a victory for the Indian Constitution. He argued that the bill was not a genuine attempt to empower women but a political maneuver aimed at altering India's electoral framework. The bill failed to garner the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.

articles.title: From ultra left to campaigner for Tamil Brahmins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. S. Pandiarajan, a Madurai lawyer, experienced a rift with the CPI(ML) in the 1980s after being passed over for leadership despite his long-standing commitment.  He alleges that he was told his Brahmin heritage disqualified him, prompting his departure from the party. He believes this caste discrimination was unique to Tamil Nadu and contradicts the party's stated principles of inclusivity.

articles.title: US Congress passes 10-day extension of surveillance law amid Republican infighting | US Congress | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Congress voted to extend a controversial warrantless surveillance law, Section 702, for 10 days after Republican infighting stalled plans for a longer renewal.  The extension was passed by both chambers of Congress despite opposition from privacy advocates and dissenting lawmakers who argued the bill did not address their demands for a warrant requirement for Americans' communications collected under the program.  Jim McGovern (D-MA) criticized the late-night vote as a "shameful midnight smash-and-grab attempt" to steal away Americans' privacy rights.

articles.title: Nine killed as van carrying Malappuram schoolteachers plunges off Valparai cliff - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nine members of a 12-person excursion group from Pang in Kuruva panchayat, Malappuram district, were killed when their van crashed off a cliff at Valparai in Tamil Nadu. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon, with the remaining members transported to hospitals for treatment. Three critically injured individuals were transferred to a hospital in Coimbatore for advanced care.

articles.title: Yogeeshgouda Goudar’s sister celebrates conviction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinay Kulkarni, a former Congress MLA, and 16 others were sentenced to life in prison for the murder of BJP zilla panchayat member Yogeeshgouda Goudar in 2016.  The victim's sister, Akkamahadevi, expressed relief at the verdict after ten years of waiting.

articles.title: Starmer was kept in dark about Mandelson’s vetting by two other top civil servants | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer was kept uninformed about a security vetting failure involving Peter Mandelson, the prime minister's former chief of staff, and two other top civil servants.  The head of the Foreign Office, Olly Robbins, was forced out after failing to inform Starmer that Mandelson had been cleared despite UK Security Vetting (UKSV) recommending against it. The Cabinet Secretary, Antonia Romeo, and Catherine Little, the permanent secretary at the Cabinet Office, were aware of the vetting failure since March but delayed informing Starmer.  The issue has sparked concerns about whether the government is being run by civil servants rather than ministers.

articles.title: When a star madean impact on the poll outcome in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's political landscape has long been intertwined with the film industry, as evidenced by past electoral contests. In the 1990s, Jayalalithaa, then Chief Minister of AIADMK, and M. Karunanidhi, leader of the DMK-led coalition, engaged in a fierce rivalry.  Rajinikanth, known for his charisma, entered this volatile political environment during that period.

articles.title: Chaturvedi’s grumbling over defeat of Women’s Bill’ flies in the face of her party’s stand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shiv Sena UBT leader Priyanka Chaturvedi criticized the defeat of the Women’s Reservation Bill in the Lok Sabha, expressing her opposition to its inclusion with the Delimitation Bill. Sanjay Raut, a Shiv Sena UBT MP, stated that the party opposed the bill because it was presented as a means for the BJP to advance their own agenda. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis condemned the opposition's actions, calling them hypocritical and stating that they prioritized politics over progress.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill raises concerns about institutional failure to advance women's rights.

articles.title: Police say no evidence found of reported gang-rape in Epsom | Surrey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Surrey police have stated they have not found any evidence of a rape reported on April 11th in Epsom, prompting protests from the community. The investigation is ongoing, and police are reviewing CCTV footage, interviewing witnesses, conducting forensic investigations, and doing house-to-house inquiries.  The force has acknowledged the speculation surrounding the lack of suspect information, particularly regarding ethnicity, but clarified that this is due to limited information about the incident and potential suspects.

articles.title: It’ a red-letter day, says Revanth; KTR blames BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, Congress and Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leaders praised opposition parties for uniting to block the controversial legislation.  Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and A. Revanth Reddy led the charge against the bill, with K. T. Rama Rao blaming the BJP for its failure. Bandi Sanjay accused the Congress of using the bill to weaken southern India, while N Ramchander Rao criticized the bill's defeat as a setback for women's empowerment.

articles.title: Chinese researcher on J-1 visa pleads guilty to smuggling E. coli bacteria into US disguised as women’s underwear - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Youhuang Xiang, a Chinese researcher working in the United States, pleaded guilty to smuggling E. coli into the country.  He admitted to concealing bacterial DNA in a shipment falsely labeled as women's underwear and was sentenced to over four months in prison. FBI Director Kash Patel warned that such actions pose serious risks and are an example of exploiting US visa privileges for illegal activity. The case follows similar incidents involving foreign researchers attempting to smuggle biological materials into the country, including Chinese nationals at a University of Michigan laboratory and a Russian-born Harvard researcher who brought frog embryos without permits.

articles.title: India fails to pass bill to boost women’s representation after delimitation row | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government failed to pass a bill increasing female representation in parliament after accusations of using it as a cover for electoral map redrawing. The bill, requiring a two-thirds majority, was opposed by the opposition who argued it was an attempt to manipulate the electoral process and unfairly benefit certain states.  This failure marks the first time in 12 years that a constitutional amendment proposed by Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) government failed to pass parliament.

articles.title: United Opposition defeated bid to harm Constitution: Kharge - The Hindu
