articles.rephrased_article: The US military announced a naval blockade of all Iranian Gulf ports beginning Monday at 1400 GMT.  This move follows failed talks between Washington and Tehran in Islamabad, where President Donald Trump accused Iran of refusing to abandon its nuclear ambitions despite what he described as largely productive negotiations. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated the blockade will be enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports, including those on the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.  Trump also warned that any Iranian vessel firing upon US forces or peaceful vessels would be met with retaliation.

articles.title: Thousands of unpaid carers to face DWP repayment demands during overhaul | Carer's allowance | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) will launch an audit of over 200,000 historical carer’s allowance benefit cases, aiming to rectify systemic injustices that led to unlawful overpayment demands.  An estimated 25,000 carers issued with overpayments since 2015 will see their repayment debts cancelled or reduced as a result of the reassessment exercise. However, existing "business as usual" overpayment recovery policies will remain in place while the government works towards a full overhaul of the benefit.  The DWP has acknowledged the need to reform the system and is implementing recommendations from an independent review into carer’s allowance overpayments.

articles.title: If Centre stops assistance or grants, we will not accept it: AIADMK leader-candidate K.P. Munusamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.P. Munusamy, AIADMK deputy general secretary, discussed the party's challenges in the upcoming election, including the impact of C. Joseph Vijay's entry and the relevance of freebies. He argued that the AIADMK's alliance is based on mutual understanding and aims to oust the anti-people government, contrasting it with the DMK's coalition with the BJP. Munusamy also addressed concerns about the party's engagement in a contest with the DMK, highlighting the need for continued welfare schemes despite some progress. He emphasized that the AIADMK is rooted in people's needs and will be judged by voters after the election.

articles.title: People across Tamil Nadu want a change: AIADMK leader-candidate D. Jayakumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Former AIADMK leader D. Jayakumar, who is contesting in Royapuram Assembly Constituency, believes the anti-incumbency sentiment against the DMK will benefit his party's chances. He argues that voters are dissatisfied with the government's handling of issues like property taxes and electricity charges, and that they understand the importance of voting for the AIADMK to ensure a change. Jayakumar also highlights the impact of parties like the TVK and NTK in the election campaign, emphasizing his party's commitment to social justice despite ideological differences with its alliance partners.

articles.title: Cancer courses through the Ghaggar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suresh Kumar, a primary school teacher in Haryana, fondly recalls his childhood spent near the Ghaggar river. He describes its crystal-clear waters teeming with life, where children bathed, women washed clothes, and farmers provided water for their animals. The river was once a vital part of the Mallewala village community, but it has since dried up due to climate change and other factors.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu polls 2026: I do not see the Assembly election in Tamil Nadu as a close contest, says CM Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK president and Chief Minister M.K. Stalin stated that the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly election would benefit his party due to a multi-cornered contest, which he believes will showcase the strength of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam-led Secular Progressive Alliance against the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam-led National Democratic Alliance.  He emphasized that the alliance is based on shared ideologies and has expanded due to a growing number of parties aligning with their vision, including the DMDK and several smaller parties.  Stalin highlighted the DMK's achievements and electoral promises as key factors in ensuring victory, while also acknowledging the need for seat-sharing discussions among allies.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson says convicted rapist employed by One Nation has been sacked | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pauline Hanson has dismissed Sean Black, a convicted rapist who previously worked as her campaign manager, from One Nation.  Hanson defended her decision, stating that she received no concerns about Black's conduct from female staff and he had done a "great job" since his release from prison. Opposition politicians have criticized the party for rehiring Black, with James Paterson calling it "absolutely extraordinary." The Liberal senator also expressed concern over Black's presence in Parliament House.  One Nation's rise in support could impact the upcoming byelection in Farrer and the overall political landscape.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Rehiring a convicted rapist normalizes abuse and undermines justice.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu 2026 polls: What have parties promised voters in their manifestos? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Assembly election is seeing a fierce battle between the incumbent DMK and its rival, the AIADMK. Both parties have released manifestos outlining their promises to voters. The DMK, with its "superstar" manifesto, focuses on free coupons for women, infrastructure projects, and fighting against Hindi imposition.  The AIADMK offers a wide range of freebies for various groups including women, students, fishermen, and farmers.  The Tamil nationalist party, Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK), is running independently in all 234 seats and promises to prioritize women's representation in government.

articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

articles.title: Following Lourdammal Simon’s footsteps, Cuthbert enters poll fray in Colachel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The INC party has nominated Tharahai Cuthbert as its candidate for the Colachel Assembly constituency, marking a return to female representation after nearly six decades.  This follows in the footsteps of late Indian National Congress (INC) leader Lourdammal Simon, who won the seat in 1957 and became the first woman minister in Tamil Nadu. Vareethiah Konstantine, a retired professor, highlighted Ms. Simon's contributions to the fishing sector through tilapia farming, mechanization of boats, and introduction of nylon nets.  Ms. Cuthbert, an incumbent MLA from Vilavancode, also hails from a fisher community background and aims to address the region's demand for fair representation.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: Audio-enabled VVPAT system sought for visually impaired voters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An NGO representing visually impaired persons in Tamil Nadu has urged the Election Commission of India to implement an audio-enabled Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) system for upcoming Assembly elections. The organization argues that current VVPAT systems lack accessibility for visually impaired voters, forcing them to rely on others to cast their ballots and compromising ballot secrecy.  The NGO contends that this practice violates the rights of persons with disabilities as outlined in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Counsel for the NGO emphasized that an audio-enabled VVPAT system would provide independent verification of votes through headphones.

articles.title: Whistles fly off the shelf this election season - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahindra Singh, a manufacturer of toys and whistles, reports a significant increase in demand for whistles across India, particularly in Tamil Nadu. Retailers are experiencing a 60% surge in sales since the Election Commission of India allotted the whistle symbol to actor C. Joseph Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the upcoming 2026 election.  The demand for whistles, particularly those in red and yellow, is high, with some vendors selling them at a premium price due to increased plastic costs.

articles.title: Support Women’s Reservation Bill amendments: PM to parties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi wrote to heads of political parties urging their cooperation in passing amendments to the Women’s Reservation Act, 2023, calling it a moment for responsibility towards women. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge countered by demanding an all-party meeting before the special sitting on the amendments and questioned the timing amid ongoing state elections.  Kharge argued that the government's proposed changes to delimitation based on the 2011 Census without using population as a metric for representation were not discussed with the opposition, raising concerns about transparency and democratic participation.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: DMK demands reinstatement of N. Muruganandam as Chief Secretary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The DMK has requested the Election Commission of India (ECI) to reverse the transfer of Chief Secretary N. Muruganandam and reinstate him, citing a lack of justification for the move. The party also objected to the appointment of Sandeep Mittal as Director General of Police (Armed Police and Vigilance and Anti-Corruption), alleging his political leanings align with the BJP and AIADMK. DMK treasurer T.R. Baalu argued that Mr. Muruganandam's experience and continuity in administration are crucial during the election period, while he also criticized Mr. Mittal's alleged corruption charges and ideological bias.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of political bias in key appointments raise concerns about fair elections.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: Difficult terrain, language barriers slow poll outreach in hills in Erode district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Political parties face challenges in reaching voters in the hilly regions of the Bhavanisagar Assembly constituency due to difficult terrain, language barriers, and limited transportation.  With 64,721 electors residing in Thalavadi and Kadambur hills, where nearly two-thirds are Kannada-speaking, parties have implemented strategies like translating campaign materials and relying on local cadres for outreach.  Despite these efforts, campaigning is slower in the hills compared to the plains, with parties reaching fewer voters due to logistical constraints and weather conditions.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: K. Manivasan to be State’s Home Secretary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) directed the Tamil Nadu government to appoint senior IAS officer K. Manivasan as Home Secretary, replacing incumbent Dheeraj Kumar.  The ECI also instructed that Kumar be transferred out and not appointed to any election-related post until after the April 23 Assembly elections. The transfer order was issued following the implementation of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC).

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly elections: How actively does Chennai vote? A look at the trends - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu, has consistently lagged behind the state average in voter turnout for over two decades.  While the 2021 Assembly election saw a turnout of 61.48%, the state average was close to 74%. Sociopolitical analyst Professor Ramu Manivannan attributes this trend to a "metropolitan culture" where voting is not seen as imperative, particularly in urban areas with a higher concentration of middle- and upper-middle-class families. However, North Chennai constituencies generally exhibit higher turnout rates compared to the central and southern regions.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: CPI manifesto promises to fight commercialisation of drinking water, agriculture and irrigation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (CPI) released its manifesto for the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections in Chennai, accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of threatening other parties and forcing alliances. The CPI's M. Veerapandian stated that the AIADMK has abandoned its ideology and merged with the BJP.  The manifesto outlines plans to support micro, small and medium industries, protect drinking water and agriculture, uphold social justice, safeguard Tamil language and culture, address drug abuse, and oppose the Citizenship Amendment Act and National Register of Citizens in Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Could the Iran war pose lasting risks to global food security? | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations warns that the US-Israel war on Iran poses lasting risks to global food security due to higher energy costs and shipping restrictions, as well as damage to fertilizer production from attacks on Gulf chemical plants.  Experts suggest these impacts could significantly affect food supply chains worldwide.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: party manifestos - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu political parties are focusing on welfare promises in their 2026 Assembly election manifestos. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), the ruling party, has promised a ₹8,000 coupon for homemakers and other benefits.  AIADMK, Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK), and other parties have also released their own promises, including free refrigerators, LPG cylinders, and monthly assistance for women.

articles.title: Noida drowning: FIR filed against three friends of deceased student - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Krish, Himanshu, and Vyas, three friends of a deceased 23-year-old university student, have been named in an FIR filed by his family following his drowning at an abandoned construction site on April 8th. The incident occurred four days after the death, with police stating that the group had gone for a picnic to the site after their examinations ended.  The sections of law invoked in the FIR are yet to be disclosed.

articles.title: Hate crimes targeting Sikh Americans in US rose 3,700% in a decade: FBI report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The FBI reported a 3,700% increase in hate crimes targeting Sikh Americans from 2015 to 2025.  Overall hate crime incidents declined by 11% in 2025 compared to the previous year, but certain groups experienced significant spikes based on changing political and social conditions.  Hate crimes against Latino communities rose 18%, marking a record high, while anti-Jewish hate crimes fell 29%. Hate crimes against transgender individuals dipped 6% but remained at historically high levels.

articles.title: Abuse allegations against lead Democrat shake race for California governor | Sexual Assault News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Eric Swalwell, a leading Democratic candidate for California governor, is facing calls to resign from the US Congress following reports of sexual assault allegations against him.  Several influential Democratic Party lawmakers have called for his removal from both positions, citing the allegations as "sick and disgusting." The Manhattan district attorney's office confirmed an investigation into the claims, while some Democrats are calling for the expulsion of Representative Tony Gonzales, another politician facing similar accusations.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of sexual assault against a high-ranking official warrant urgent attention.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: Three villages in Coimbatore keep political displays off walls for over 35 years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in Kalappanaickenpalayam, Somayampalayam, and Kasthurinaickenpalayam villages in Coimbatore district have maintained a tradition of keeping their public spaces free of political displays for over three decades.  After clashes arose due to political differences, the villagers agreed to remove all posters, flags, and other campaign materials. The practice continues today with only obituary notices, weddings, and other events featuring political symbols or flags.

articles.title: Insipid electioneering rubs off the sheen of election; social media-centric strategies order of the day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In the Tirunelveli district, electioneering for the April 23 Assembly polls has been subdued despite visits from prominent leaders like M. K. Stalin, Edappadi K. Palaniswami, and Vijay. Candidates have abandoned traditional door-to-door canvassing, relying instead on hired workers to distribute pamphlets and encourage voters.  While social media platforms are used for reaching out to voters, some candidates have allegedly paid for press coverage, raising concerns about "paid news." The lack of traditional campaigning has led to criticism from observers who lament the decline in political discourse and engagement with voters.

articles.title: US cop caught swiping on dating app during SWAT standoff after high-speed chase with armed suspect - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Riverside County Sheriff’s Office deputy is under investigation after video footage showed him using a dating app during a SWAT standoff with an armed suspect in Jurupa Valley. The incident occurred following a high-speed pursuit and ended with the suspect's death from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.  The Sheriff’s Office stated it is investigating the deputy's behavior, which they said does not reflect their department's standards.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: CM Stalin takes surprise Chennai Metro ride, interacts with passengers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, the DMK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, rode the Chennai Metro Rail on Friday as part of his election campaign.  Accompanied by N. Ezhilan, a Thousand Lights MLA, he interacted with passengers at stations and sought public feedback on various schemes.  He is scheduled to address a public meeting in Thanjavur later today.

articles.title: Astronomers detect mega-laser beam signal from 8 billion light-years away | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa detected a strong "mega-laser" signal originating from the HATLAS J142935.3–002836 galaxy system, which is 8 billion light-years away. This hydroxyl megamaser, a natural occurrence of microwave amplification like lasers but in radio wavelengths, defied scientific predictions regarding signal strength over such vast cosmic distances. The researchers believe the signal's exceptional intensity was amplified by gravitational lensing, making its detection possible.  This discovery has implications for studying the universe at an earlier stage and detecting gravitational waves in the future.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election 2026: Vijay returns without addressing poll campaign in Karaikudi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam founder and actor Vijay arrived at the campaign venue in Karaikudi late, missing his allotted time slot for addressing supporters. Despite receiving permission from the Election Commission, he faced delays due to traffic and crowds, ultimately unable to deliver his speech.  He was received by party candidate T.K. Prabhu who presented him with a memento.

articles.title: This Egyptian discovery could rewrite humans origin history; scientists say we have been looking in the wrong place | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new fossil discovery in Egypt challenges the long-held belief that East Africa is the sole birthplace of humans. The fossil, dating back to the early Miocene period and exhibiting traits similar to early primates, suggests that human evolution may have occurred across a wider geographic area, including North Africa. This finding highlights the importance of exploring less studied regions for understanding human origins and emphasizes the dynamic nature of scientific knowledge.

articles.title: Karnataka, a State of Contrasts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A report tabled in the Karnataka legislature highlights persistent regional disparities, despite the state's strong economic growth.  Karnataka, which boasts a 8.1% growth rate for the fiscal year 2025-26, has witnessed divergent economic indicators across its districts. While Bengaluru and coastal regions like Dakshina Kannada and Udupi have experienced significant growth, most districts continue to lag behind. The state remains a leader in GST collection, but its economic activity is concentrated in these areas.

articles.title: Who is Péter Magyar? Lawyer who defeated Viktor Orbán after 16-year rule set to become Hungarian prime minister - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, a former Fidesz party insider, won the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary election, defeating long-time leader Viktor Orbán.  Magyar's rise to prominence was marked by his public opposition to corruption within the government and the subsequent formation of the Tisza Party. His campaign focused on anti-corruption measures, restoring democratic institutions, and improving ties with the European Union.  He now faces the challenge of implementing his reform agenda after a decade of nationalist rule under Orbán.

articles.title: Hungarian election: BBC reports from Budapest as Orbán concedes
articles.rephrased_article: Viktor Orbán, the Prime Minister of Hungary, conceded defeat in the country's election after 16 years in power. Péter Magyar, leader of the opposition party, is set to become the new prime minister following record voter turnout. With two-thirds of votes counted, Magyar's party is projected to win a large majority in parliament. Vote counting will continue over the coming days.

articles.title: JAC demands equal pay, regularisation of contract workers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Government Contract and Outsourcing Employees’ Federation members gathered for their fifth Mahasabha in Vijayawada, demanding equal pay for all contract and outsourcing employees. The federation called for the implementation of a minimum basic pay, regularisation of these workers under the contract system, an increase in retirement age to 62 years, and expanded welfare benefits.  The federation also urged the government to address the issue of unequal wages for long periods, as highlighted by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in March.

articles.title: Withdraw amendments made to Private Universities Act: SFI - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students’ Federation of India (SFI) leaders demanded the withdrawal of recent amendments to the Private Universities Act–2016, arguing that they promote commercialization of education and unfairly benefit private universities.  They criticized Minister Kolusu Parthasarathi for his claim that the amendments were necessary due to a lack of private universities in the state, calling it illogical. The SFI leaders also highlighted concerns about fee exploitation at private universities, citing examples like Mohan Babu University's illegal collection of ₹26 crore in fees.  They called on the government to prioritize strengthening public universities instead of granting more permissions to private institutions.

articles.title: Stress mounts as constables face transfer delays despite 10-year eligibility - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mohan Kumar Danappa, member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority, has raised concerns about a growing sense of distress among Bengaluru civil police constables who are being denied inter-district transfers despite completing 10 years of service.  He argues that while previous norms allowed transfers after three years, subsequent amendments extended this period to 10 years, and many eligible personnel, particularly from the 2016 batch, have been left out. Danappa believes this creates an imbalance and discrimination within the force, causing stress and hardship for constables who are often far from their home districts and struggling to care for families. He urges the government to address the issue on humanitarian grounds and ensure transparent and fair transfers.

articles.title: Asha Bhosle’s tryst with Telugu songs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Asha Bhosle, a legendary singer, passed away on Sunday.  She made her Telugu debut in 1981 with the song "Idi Maunageetam" and later contributed to several films including "Chinni Krishnudu", "Chandamama", and "Aswamedham". Her songs like "Jeevitam Sapta Sagara Geetam" and "Naalo oohalaku" continue to be popular in Telugu cinema.  Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao, and others expressed condolences, praising her as a singer of unmatched excellence.

articles.title: Experts discuss liver disease complications at Vijayawada conclave - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manipal Hospitals, Vijayawada, and the South Asian Liver Institute, Hyderabad, hosted a conclave for over 350 doctors and medical experts in hepatology and liver transplantation. The event focused on managing liver disease complications outside of hospitals, with sessions covering topics like patient selection for transplantation, intensive care unit management, real-life case discussions, and hands-on workshops on organ procurement.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Poll fever rises as political merchandise sales peak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vendors on Allimal Street in Tiruchi's shopping district are experiencing a surge in demand for election-related merchandise as the Assembly elections approach.  V. Rakul, proprietor of Lakshmi Paper Store, reports that lightweight cloth scarves and multi-colored versions are popular, along with posters, hand-held fans featuring leaders' images, and customized badges. Amutha Siva, proprietor of Thirumalai Printers and The Prink, notes increased orders for merchandise related to actor Vijay and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  The vendors attribute this demand to the novelty factor and customization options available.

articles.title: Residents complain about delay in construction of ROB, illegal sand mining on Palar riverbed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Vaniyambadi town are facing numerous challenges, including a long-standing issue with the railway level crossing that has remained unaddressed despite promises from political parties. The lack of a road over bridge (ROB) has led to traffic congestion and inconvenience for motorists and emergency vehicles. Residents also complain about garbage disposal issues, illegal sand mining impacting water resources, and pest infestations affecting agricultural lands.  The constituency's political landscape remains dominated by the AIADMK party, which has held the seat since 2011.

articles.title: Herculean task needed to stop sewage polluting Vaippar from Sattur town - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Kamalavel Selvan, Bahujan Samaj Party candidate, criticizes the state administration and political parties for allowing illegal fireworks units to operate in Sattur Assembly constituency. He suggests that the government should help these units become licensed factories with support and assistance.  The All India Puratachi Thalaivar Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AIPTMK) accuses the DMK of failing to address safety concerns in fireworks units, leading to more accidents. The party candidate, Esakki Raja, promises a multi-speciality hospital with a burns ward for accident victims.  Nainar Nagenthran, BJP leader and a former Tirunelveli MLA, is contesting the seat despite claiming he had to move from Tirunelveli on AIADMK's request. The DMK has fielded A. Kadarkarairaj, a veteran party member, who belongs to the Naikkar community.

articles.title: Senior citizens, differently abled cast their votes at home in Tirunelveli, Tenkasi districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Senior citizens and the physically challenged, above 85 years of age or with 40% disability, cast their votes through postal ballots on Sunday in Tamil Nadu.  A total of 3,744 senior citizens and 2,283 differently abled persons participated in the process across various constituencies. Regional Officers, Assistant Regional Officers, a videographer, and a police personnel visited homes to ensure voter secrecy and facilitate casting their ballots. The exercise will continue until April 14th, with designated teams visiting homes on April 12th, 13th, and 14th.

articles.title: DMK turning T.N. into top State in corruption, says BJP national president Nitin Nabin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP national president Nitin Nabin accused the DMK government in Tamil Nadu of prioritizing the exploitation of poor resources over development. He claimed that the NDA would form governments in five states, including Tamil Nadu, and end corruption and drug culture. Nabin also criticized the DMK's handling of law and order, citing high murder rates and a lack of response to the Kallakurichi liquor tragedy. He emphasized the need for an end to "family rule" and pledged to prioritize Rameswaram's development.  He urged voters to support the NDA on April 23rd for progress in Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Tourism and trade: The Hindu Editorial on the Great Nicobar mega-infrastructure project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government’s ₹92,000 crore mega-infrastructure project for Great Nicobar Island (GNI) is moving forward with a draft master plan outlining plans for tourism and economic development. The plan envisions building the island as a "seaside destination" and aims to create over 3.36 lakh jobs by 2055, but it has drawn criticism from indigenous groups like the Nicobarese and Shompen who oppose relocation plans and fear ecological damage.  The draft plan is open for public feedback, but its timeline remains unclear. Concerns remain about the project's impact on biodiversity, local rights, and commercial viability.

articles.title: Coimbatore's local cable TV telecasts 'Jana Nayagan'; TVK supporters seek action - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Supporters of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) filed a complaint with the police in Coimbatore district after a local cable TV operator aired leaked footage of their party's founder Vijay-starrer "Jana Nayagan" on Saturday night. The supporters allege that the movie was telecast for 21 minutes past the interval and demanded an investigation into the leak, which they claim violates copyright laws.  The police have assured action but are now investigating the matter through a separate wing.

articles.title: Police intensify probe into drug trafficking cases - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode police are utilizing newly obtained evidence, including call detail records and social media data, to uncover covert networks involved in the illegal synthetic drug trade. The evidence, gathered from recent arrests of inter-state traffickers, is expected to help identify local drug pushers connected to those individuals.  The Narcotics Control Bureau is coordinating with state-level officers to ensure a unified and simultaneous enforcement effort, as part of a wider probe examining the role of foreign nationals and inter-State agents.

articles.title: Kochi Corpn. seeks govt. fundsto repair uneven stretches along metro corridor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kochi Corporation is awaiting funds from the State government to restore the severely damaged Sahodaran Ayyappan (S.A.) Road, which has been plagued by road surface protrusions and uneven portions around metro pillars.  The corporation's inability to raise the required ₹14 crore for resurfacing has prompted them to seek funding from the new government. Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) attributes the issue to sinking tarred portions outside the pile caps of the metro pillars, while acknowledging that the roads beneath the metro corridors were handed back to the agencies concerned after the expiry of the three-year defect liability period.

articles.title: AI will make media and films more interesting: Suresh Chandra Menon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suresh Chandra Menon, a filmmaker, director and actor, discussed the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on media and film making at The Hindu EducationFair in Chennai. He stated that AI will act as a tool for filmmakers, aiding cost reduction and enhancing creativity. Menon highlighted how technology has revolutionized the industry, citing his own journey from an assistant cinematographer to directing films like "Puthiya Mugam."  He emphasized the opportunities available in media and film making, including short films, documentaries, and the potential for income through social media influencers.

articles.title: Move to expel Democrat Eric Swalwell from Congress gains steam | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Congress members from both parties are calling for the resignation of Eric Swalwell, a Democratic representative and candidate for California governor, following allegations of inappropriate behavior, sexual assault, and rape.  Swalwell has denied the allegations but may face expulsion from Congress. Several lawmakers, including Ro Khanna, Byron Donalds, and Pramila Jayapal, have expressed support for expelling both Swalwell and disgraced Republican representative Tony Gonzales. The Manhattan district attorney’s office is investigating an allegation of rape against Swalwell.

articles.title: Kumarapalayam seeks flyover, curbs on effluent discharge into Cauvery, more bus services and resettlement of the flood affected - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kumarapalayam constituency, known for its textile industry, faces challenges including inadequate public transportation, pollution from textile dyeing units, and traffic congestion. Residents have called for a bus stand at Veppadai to connect the area with Namakkal, as well as a flyover at Anangur to address railway crossings that cause traffic jams.  The district administration has also been criticized for failing to implement measures to mitigate pollution from effluent discharge into the Cauvery river and provide temporary housing for residents during floods. P. Thangamani, the incumbent AIADMK candidate, is seeking a fourth consecutive term in the upcoming election alongside other candidates from DMK, TVK, and NTK.

articles.title: No need for hard stares as Paddington: The Musical triumphs at Olivier awards | Olivier awards | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Olivier awards saw Paddington: The Musical dominate the ceremony, winning seven awards including best new musical.  The show's cast, including James Hameed and Arti Shah, also took home awards for best actor in a musical and best supporting actor/actress in a musical respectively. Other notable winners included Rosamund Pike, who won best actress for her performance in "Inter Alia," and Jack Holden who won best actor for his role in "Kenrex."  The ceremony celebrated the 50th anniversary of the awards, recognizing achievements across various theatre categories including musicals, plays, dance, and opera.

articles.title: Girls have the edge in landing IT sector jobs: academician - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deiva Sundari P., principal of Easwari Engineering College, stated that companies are actively recruiting women in engineering to maintain diversity and industry readiness.  She explained that while the demand for women in engineering is 30%, it currently stands at only 12%. Companies conduct both specific girls-only recruitment drives and regular campus recruitment drives, often selecting top students from civil and mechanical streams before their second year. Ms. Sundari emphasized the growing importance of industry-specific knowledge and critical thinking skills for graduates, noting that global capability centers in MNCs offer higher salaries to core engineering graduates compared to IT service industries.

articles.title: AI will transform jobs rather than eliminate them; it will only open up new opportunities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Tandon, chief executive officer of BITS Pilani Digital, stated that the rise of AI will transform jobs rather than displace them.  He emphasized the need for graduates to possess both domain knowledge and co-intelligence, which involves working alongside AI tools.  Tandon highlighted the importance of industry-relevant projects in curriculums and redesigning teaching methodologies to incorporate problem-solving and flipped classrooms. He also stressed the necessity of continuous learning due to the evolving nature of careers and the need for individuals to adapt and reinvent themselves regularly.

articles.title: ‘Don’t care if Brandon’s wife is half Indian’: Internet reacts to US congressman calling out Indians at 7-Eleven - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Texas Congressman Brandon Gill sparked controversy after a video of him criticizing the hiring of Indian workers at 7-Eleven stores went viral on X.  He called the idea "asinine" and "idiotic," claiming that Americans should be hired instead. Gill's remarks drew criticism from progressives and accusations of hypocrisy given his wife, Danielle D'Souza Gill, is of Indian origin. The congressman maintains his stance against mass immigration and argues that legal immigration does not automatically benefit the US.

articles.title: Markets in Kochi come alive with Vishu buzz - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Resmi Balakrishnan's family has maintained a tradition of sharing yellow flowers from their 'Kanikonna' tree with neighbors and strangers on the day before Vishu. Mr. Rathore, a wayside seller, reports increased sales of Krishna idols in the city due to the festival.  The vegetable market is preparing for Vishu with festival-specific produce arriving at higher prices.

articles.title: US will ‘probably’ need to use special forces to get Iran’s uranium, says Nikki Haley as she rules out 2028 run - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nikki Haley, former Republican presidential candidate, suggested that the US may need to deploy special forces to secure Iran's uranium stockpile. Haley stated this would be a dangerous mission but crucial in weakening Iran's capabilities and preventing further threats to allies.  The situation remains tense as Donald Trump weighs options to deal with Iran's nuclear program, including potential strikes and a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. While Trump has not ruled out ground operations, US Senator Mark Warner expressed concern about the complexity and risks involved in retrieving the uranium.

articles.title: DGP inaugurates ‘helmet chowk’ in Asifabad, calls for making road safety awareness campaign a social movement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: B. Shivadhar Reddy, Telangana Director General of Police, emphasized the need for collaborative road safety efforts during a 'Arrive Alive' campaign in Mancherial district. He urged citizens to adhere to traffic rules and form road safety committees to prevent accidents.  G. Vinod, Bellampalli MLA, and other officials were present at the event, which included the inauguration of a helmet-shaped structure and a library.

articles.title: Cashew hub to witness high-stakes battle between AIADMK and VCK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Panruti, Tamil Nadu's cashew capital, is a high-stakes battle between K. Mohan of the AIADMK and Abdul Rahman of the VCK.  T. Velmurugan, former MLA who won the seat on a DMK-led alliance ticket in 2021, has withdrawn from the race. The election will be closely watched as Vanniyars and Dalits, significant voter groups, decide the outcome. The cashew industry in Panruti faces challenges including inadequate infrastructure and pollution issues.  The election's results could significantly impact the future of the cashew processing sector in the region.

articles.title: Telangana gears up for Fire Service Week with focus on schools and hospitals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana's Fire Service Week 2026, running from April 14 to 20, will focus on proactive fire safety measures. The week-long campaign includes drills in hospitals and schools, public demonstrations, inspections of high-risk buildings, and educational outreach programs.  The theme emphasizes turning awareness into everyday practice by focusing on risk reduction in vulnerable spaces. Fire personnel will showcase equipment, conduct mock drills, and provide lectures to raise public awareness about fire safety issues.

articles.title: India rejects China’s ‘mischievous attempts’ to assign ‘fictitious’ names to places in Arunachal Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) strongly condemned China's recent creation of new counties in Xinjiang province, calling the actions "mischievous" and detrimental to bilateral relations.  The MEA stated that these attempts at assigning fictitious names to territories within India's territory detract from efforts to normalize ties and undermine understanding between the two nations. The ministry reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India and will remain so.

articles.title: Vijayawada-born social entrepreneur to receive global honour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indus Action, a non-profit organization based in New Delhi, has been awarded the 2026 Skoll Award for Social Innovation. The award recognizes Indus Action's founder and CEO, Tarun Cherukuri, for his work simplifying social protection policies to benefit more people.  The organization focuses on using technology to make registration processes faster and more accessible for citizens, particularly those in the labor force. Indus Action joins two other organizations, ChildLife Foundation from Pakistan and SmartStart from South Africa, as this year's recipients of the prestigious award.

articles.title: If Centre stops assistance or grants, we will not accept it, says K.P. Munusamy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.P. Munusamy, AIADMK deputy general secretary, discussed the party's challenges in the upcoming election and its relationship with the DMK. He highlighted the differences between their alliances, emphasizing the AIADMK's focus on ousting an anti-people government while the DMK seeks to maintain power. Munusamy also addressed concerns about freebies and the impact of TVK president C. Joseph Vijay's entry into the electoral fray.  He concluded that the people will ultimately decide the future of the AIADMK.

articles.title: Asha Bhosle: the voice that defied genres, time - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Asha Bhosle, a legendary Indian singer, passed away at 92 on April 12, 2026.  Her career spanned decades and included collaborations with renowned composers like O.P. Nayyar, R.D. Burman, A.R. Rahman, and many others. She was known for her versatility, often shifting between classical and contemporary styles. Her voice defined a shift in Indian cinema towards more confident and worldly portrayals of women.  Asha Bhosle left behind a legacy of chart-topping songs that continue to be loved by generations.

articles.title: US lawmakers split on party lines over negotiations’ failure to end Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nikki Haley, former UN ambassador, urged Donald Trump to "go after Iran where it hurts" and block the Strait of Hormuz, while Senator Ron Johnson advocated for the complete removal of the Iranian regime.  Top Democrats like Senator Mark Warner warned against seizing Iran's enriched uranium, deeming it dangerous and potentially leading to a devastating conflict. Senator Tim Kaine called for a war motion in the Senate to prevent Trump from resuming hostilities, arguing that even an imperfect ceasefire is preferable. Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani also opposed the US-Israel war with Iran, citing its unpopularity among Americans and highlighting the use of funds for warfare instead of social programs.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Cash-for-votes storm dims Sobha Surendran’s sheen - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sobha Surendran, the BJP candidate in Palakkad Assembly, faced a significant setback as cash-for-votes allegations emerged against her campaign. The BJP's aggressive pre-election outreach efforts were overshadowed by these accusations from the United Democratic Front (UDF), which could potentially derail Ms. Surendran's bid for the seat.

articles.title: How are China and Iran cornering US without firing a shot amid tensions in Gulf - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China and Iran are increasingly using global supply chains and strategic chokepoints to counter the United States, highlighting Washington's vulnerabilities.  The report by The Washington Post details how these tactics are reshaping economic warfare, with China restricting rare earth mineral exports in retaliation for US tariffs and Iran tightening its grip on the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting energy flows. This has led to increased fuel prices, supply chain disruptions, and rising costs for goods like fertilizer, aluminum, plastics, and food. The report criticizes the US administration's lack of preparedness for these developments, highlighting concerns about Washington's ability to respond to rapidly evolving economic threats. As a result, major economies are investing in domestic production and diversifying supply chains to reduce reliance on geopolitical rivals.

articles.title: Police launch appeal after woman raped by several men outside Surrey church | Surrey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Surrey police are investigating a reported sexual assault that occurred outside Epsom Methodist Church in Epsom, England. The victim, a woman in her 20s, was allegedly followed from the nightclub Labyrinth Epsom and attacked between 2am and 4am on Saturday.  Police have not yet released full descriptions of the suspects but are urging anyone with information to contact them.

articles.title: Rijiju writes to Kharge, says delay in women’s quota law will deny justice to millions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, responded to Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress President, who criticized the government's push for the Women's Reservation Act implementation.  Rijiju emphasized that the law is about fulfilling promises to Indian women and urged opposition parties to support its implementation in 2029. He stated that delaying action on the matter is unjust and called for a united effort towards "Nari Shakti".

articles.title: KTR hints at padayatra in 2027, rules out tie-up with BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), stated that the party will contest the upcoming elections independently and return to power. He also hinted at a state-wide padayatra in 2027 focusing on public issues as a way to reconnect with people.  Rama Rao acknowledged shortcomings during the BRS government's tenure, including ineffective coordination with grassroots leaders and delays in implementing welfare schemes. He also criticized the Revanth Reddy government for failing to properly implement key programs.

articles.title: Singer Mangli files case against advocate alleging extortion bid - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mangli, a folk singer, filed a complaint against Singapogu Subbu and three others at the Panjagutta police station alleging that he falsely presented himself as an advocate and demanded ₹10 lakh to remove videos from social media platforms.  The case is being treated as a counter-complaint to Subbu's earlier accusation of being cheated out of ₹10 crore in a microfinance business. Police are investigating the matter further.

articles.title: Artemis II crew speak out at welcome home event: ‘Earth was this lifeboat hanging in the universe’ | Artemis II | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Artemis II astronauts, after a record-breaking deep space mission, returned to Earth on Saturday and were greeted by hundreds of people at Ellington Field near Nasa's Johnson Space Center. The crew, led by commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, expressed gratitude for the opportunity and reflected on their extraordinary journey. Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman welcomed them home, acknowledging the significance of the mission in advancing human exploration.  The astronauts' accomplishment included surpassing Apollo 13's distance record and capturing previously unseen lunar views.

articles.title: Burglars decamp with gold, cash from locked house in Shamshabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vadde Lalitha, a 50-year-old laborer, reported that her house in Pedda Shapur village was burglarized on April 11th.  The break-in occurred while she was staying with her daughter and involved the theft of gold ornaments, silver anklets, cash, and a steel bureau lock. Police have registered a case and are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Votes for populist parties in May elections will put NHS at risk, Streeting says | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, the UK health secretary, warned that voters in May's local and devolved elections could jeopardize the NHS by supporting populist parties. Streeting argued that Reform UK and Plaid Cymru pose a particular threat to the NHS in Wales, while he criticized the SNP's governance of Scotland and called for continued Labour-run councils in England.  He emphasized the importance of electing a Labour government to protect the NHS and highlighted the risks associated with voting for Reform UK, which has pledged to dismantle the NHS and offer tax relief on private healthcare.

articles.title: No-fly zone declared in Vellore for Chief Minister’s election campaign - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.R. Subbulaxmi, the District Election Officer and Collector, has declared a no-fly zone over the district for April 13-14 during Chief Minister M.K. Stalin's election campaign. The area will be a "Red Zone," prohibiting fireworks, air balloons, and drone usage without prior permission.  The district police have been authorized to confiscate or destroy any UAVs found operating illegally. Operators must obtain approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs for drone use.

articles.title: Woman, 19, killed in Essex dog attack named as Jamie-Lea Biscoe | Essex | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jamie-Lea Biscoe, a 19-year-old woman, was found dead after a dog attack in Essex on Friday night.  Police arrested a 37-year-old man from Dunmow on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury resulting in death. The canine, believed to be a lurcher cross, has been seized for testing. Assistant Chief Constable Stuart Hooper expressed condolences to Biscoe's loved ones and urged the public to respect their privacy during this difficult time.  The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: EAM Jaishankar meets UAE President in Abu Dhabi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, met with Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the President of the United Arab Emirates, in Abu Dhabi on Sunday (April 12, 2026). The meeting focused on the West Asia crisis and its economic impact, as well as strengthening the India-UAE comprehensive strategic partnership. Jaishankar also thanked Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum, the Dubai Crown Prince and Deputy Prime Minister of the UAE, for ensuring the welfare of the Indian community in Dubai.

articles.title: Seven ways America can win the ceasefire and end the war | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump faces a critical decision regarding the ceasefire with Iran.  To secure a win in the midterm elections and maintain regional peace, he must focus on several key areas. These include opening the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping, strengthening domestic pressure on the Iranian regime, mending relationships with allies, improving messaging, presenting a vision for peace, and ensuring alignment with Israel's objectives.  The success of these efforts will determine whether the US can win the ceasefire and achieve a lasting peace agreement.

articles.title: DIG orders inquiry after video, purportedly showing armed robbery on Karachi bridge, goes viral - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Farrukh Ali, East Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Karachi, ordered an inquiry into a robbery incident on the Shah Faisal Bridge after a video circulated online. The police statement clarified that no citizens were robbed, but several individuals carrying sticks attempted to accost them.  The MQM-P lawmakers accused the Sindh government of negligence and conspiracy, while Jamaat-i-Islami's Karachi chief Munim Zafar Khan called for immediate action against the culprits.

articles.title: Bengal polls 2026: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose joins Trinamool Congress after quitting BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandra Kumar Bose, the grandnephew of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, joined the Trinamool Congress on Sunday, April 12, 2026.  Bose cited his previous decision to join the Bharatiya Janata Party as a "historic mistake" and stated that the TMC aligns better with Bengal's history, tradition, and culture.

articles.title: Ex-girlfriend of Trump ally speaks out after ICE deported her to Brazil: 'It was not enough for him...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amanda Ungaro, a Brazilian model, alleges that her former partner, Paolo Zampolli, used his influence to have her detained and deported from the United States in June 2025.  Ungaro claims Zampolli contacted an ICE official to request her transfer into custody, citing a connection to someone close to Donald Trump. She alleges harsh conditions at the detention center and that she was held alongside violent offenders. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) stated Ungaro's detention and deportation were due to her expired visa and fraud charges. Zampolli denies any wrongdoing, stating he only sought information about the legal process.

articles.title: Amaravati to host India’s first quantum test facilities on April 14 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh is set to become a leader in India's quantum technology sector with the launch of its first Quantum Test and Reference Facilities in Amaravati. The initiative, part of the Amaravati Quantum Valley project, will be inaugurated on April 14th by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu. Two advanced quantum computer test beds, named 1S and 1Q, will be unveiled at SRM University and Medha Towers respectively.  This is expected to place Andhra Pradesh at the forefront of next-generation computing technologies.

articles.title: 12 Indian fishermen from Tamil Nadu, Karaikal arrested by Sri Lankan Navy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Lankan Navy apprehended 12 fishermen, including five from Tamil Nadu, on Saturday night for allegedly crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL). The fishermen, aboard a mechanised boat owned by Veeravel of Tsunami Nagar at Kilinjalmedu in Karaikal district, were fishing approximately 60 nautical miles off Karaikal when intercepted by the Sri Lankan Navy around 9 p.m. on April 11th.

articles.title: Farmers’ body seeks ₹500 bonus per quintal for paddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Rythu Sangham members are calling for a ₹500 per quintal bonus for paddy, arguing that the current Minimum Support Price is insufficient to cover rising input costs.  Eluru district secretary K. Srinivas made this demand during a visit to paddy procurement yards in Denduluru mandal, comparing it to Kerala's higher incentives of about ₹900 per quintal.

articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: TMC supports 'tukde-tukde' gang that threatened to snap Siliguri Corridor because of appeasement says PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged voters in Siliguri to give him a chance during the upcoming West Bengal Assembly election, stating that all BJP candidates were "Modi" and representing his vision.  He drew parallels with Mamata Banerjee's campaign strategy by emphasizing that he had previously given opportunities to other parties like Congress and Trinamool.

articles.title: Severe heatwave alert issued for 51 mandals in A.P. on April 13 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) issued severe heatwave alerts for 51 mandals and a heatwave alert for 49 mandals on Monday.  The highest temperature recorded was 43.8°C in Pottipadu, Kondapuram mandal of YSR Kadapa district. While Sunday saw heatwave conditions in 10 mandals across several districts, the day's temperatures were slightly lower than the previous day's record-breaking highs.

articles.title: AGMS-led forum to release Adivasi Vikasana Manifesto-2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Adivasi Gothara Mahasabha (AGMS) and an Adivasi Manifesto Drafting Committee are releasing a comprehensive manifesto, "Adivasi Vikasana Manifesto-2026," to address socio-economic and political issues faced by tribal communities in Kerala. The document, due for release after the new government assumes office in May, focuses on land rights, forest governance, education, employment, and political representation.  The manifesto emphasizes ensuring political rights and meaningful participation in governance structures as key to improving Adivasi living conditions.

articles.title: Tataiahgunta Gangamma Jatara to begin on May 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tirupati MLA Arani Srinivasulu unveiled the poster for the upcoming Tataiahgunta Gangamma Jatara, which will run from May 5 to May 13. The main festival, featuring Vishwaroopa Darshanam, is scheduled for May 12th.  Temple board chairman Mahesh Yadav and other officials are overseeing preparations for the event, with an emphasis on providing a smooth darshan experience for all devotees, including those traveling from distant regions.

articles.title: Hotel meals get costlier in Vizianagaram amid LPG supply shortage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hotels in Vizianagaram have increased menu prices by 5% to 15%, citing a shortage of LPG cylinders.  The price hikes range from ₹5 to ₹10 per item, with full meals now costing ₹150 instead of ₹130.  Hotel representatives claim they are forced to buy cooking gas from the black market due to reduced supplies, and will lower prices when supplies normalize.

articles.title: CM’s political secretary Naseer Ahmed ‘asked’ to quit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following allegations of anti-party activities by some Muslim leaders in the Davangere South Assembly bypoll, Abdul Jabbar, chairman of the KPCC Minority Cell resigned.  His resignation followed a request from Siddaramaiah’s political secretary, Naseer Ahmed, to step down. Two Muslim leaders and Housing Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan are accused of not campaigning for the Congress candidate, Samarth Mallikarjun, potentially impacting the election outcome.

articles.title: KTR’s corruption charges against CM Revanth lack substance: Chamala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders in Hyderabad, Telangana dismissed K.T. Rama Rao’s claims that the party would not return to power for the next 50 years, calling his corruption allegations baseless and fueled by political desperation. Bhongir MP Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy and Ibrahimpatnam MLA Malreddy Ranga Reddy challenged KTR to provide evidence for his accusations against Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s family.  They also criticized the BRS leadership for alleged wealth accumulation and attempts to buy votes.

articles.title: Colleges claim good results in Intermediate exam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Chaitanya Educational Institutions, Nalanda Junior College, and Resonance Junior Colleges reported impressive results in the Intermediate exam, with top students achieving high marks.  Sushma Boppana, academic director of Sri Chaitanya, attributed the institution's success to its integrated approach, while Surya Raju, college director of Nalanda Junior College, credited disciplined preparation and experienced faculty for their students' achievements. Purna Chandra Rao Narra, managing director of Resonance Junior Colleges, highlighted the dedication of students, commitment of faculty, and trust of parents as factors contributing to the impressive results.

articles.title: Andhra techie dies in California waterfall accident during trip with friends | India News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Times of India (TOI) News Desk is a dedicated team of journalists committed to delivering current and comprehensive news updates to readers worldwide.  They operate around the clock, gathering, verifying, and presenting breaking news, in-depth analysis, and insightful reports on various topics. The TOI News Desk aims to be a trusted source for staying informed about global developments.

articles.title: CPI(M) slams NDA govt for ₹400 crore property tax burden on Andhra Pradesh urban residents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] criticized the State Government for increasing property taxes, accusing it of betraying public trust by failing to deliver on its electoral promises.  CPI(M] State Secretariat member Ch. Babu Rao and State Committee member D. Kasinath claimed that the government's capital value-based taxation system has led to a steady rise in taxes, with property tax increasing by nearly 130% since 2021-22. They also questioned the rationale behind steep penalties for late payments.

articles.title: Governor, Naidu, Pawan condole Asha Bhosle’s passing, hail her timeless legacy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Governor S. Abdul Nazeer expressed grief over the passing of legendary playback singer Asha Bhosle in Mumbai on Sunday.  He lauded her career spanning nearly eight decades, calling her the "Queen of Versatility" and praising her ability to blend classical and modern music. Nazeer conveyed his condolences to Bhosle's family.

articles.title: Mass eviction of migrant workers in Varthur in Bengaluru after assault on domestic help raises concerns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of migrant labourers residing in a labor colony along Balagere Road have been forced to vacate their homes following the alleged assault of a 20-year-old domestic help a week prior. The incident, which followed the victim's warnings against harassment by five men arrested for the attack, has raised concerns about displacement and potential rights violations.

articles.title: New fire station planned in Rayapudi to combat frequent accidents in Amaravati - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response and Fire Services Department
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response and Fire Services Department has decided to establish a fire station at Rayapudi in response to frequent fire accidents in the Amaravati Capital region. The department, citing prolonged stocking of conduit pipes and poor maintenance as primary causes, has directed construction companies to implement proper fire safety measures at their sites.  The Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the situation with officials from the Fire Department, Police, and the CRDA after a series of fires occurred in the region, including one during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit in May 2025. The department has also provided fire tenders to several locations within the Capital Region.

articles.title: Ex-CIA director calls for ousting Trump: ‘25th amendment was written with him in mind’ | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: John Brennan, former CIA director, has joined calls for the removal of President Trump under the 25th Amendment, citing his volatile rhetoric and potential danger to national security.  Brennan believes the amendment was written with Trump in mind due to his recent threats against Iran. The debate over Trump's handling of the situation with Iran has intensified, with over 70 Democrats in Congress calling for its application. However, the chances of invoking the amendment are considered low given the strong support Trump enjoys from his administration and Vice President Mike Pence.

articles.title: Census of springs: 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Jal Shakti Ministry released the first Spring Census Report, which revealed that 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership, significantly higher than other states like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu where public ownership dominates.  The report, covering Kerala, Karnataka, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar, found that while Kerala has a high percentage of privately owned springs, the majority of springs across all surveyed states are publicly owned. The census, conducted by the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, aimed to inventory and map these critical water sources in response to depletion concerns.

articles.title: Richard Tice’s firm alleged to have broken law by failing to pay tax | Richard Tice | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Richard Tice, deputy leader of Reform UK, is facing accusations that his company, Quidnet REIT Ltd., failed to pay tens of thousands of pounds in tax on dividends paid to him and his offshore trust.  Dan Neidle, from Tax Policy Associates, claims the total amount owed was approximately £120,000. Tice maintains he has paid all taxes due, but the allegations have sparked criticism from political figures like Anna Turley, chair of the Labour party, who called for him to explain his actions and pay back any unpaid taxes.

articles.title: Disruptions in cooking gas, diesel supply continue to affect fisheries sector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The fuel crisis caused by West Asia tension is severely impacting the fisheries sector, particularly deep-sea fishing operations.  Fisherfolk operating boats engaged in deep-sea fishing are facing shortages of commercial LPG cylinders, leading to delays and idle vessels at harbors like Thoppumpady. The Kochi Longline Boat and Gillnet Buying Agents Association has likened the situation to a standstill in the hotel industry. The Matsya Thozhilali Federation (CITU) blames the Central government for increasing kerosene prices, which they claim is insufficient even for five days of fishing.

articles.title: Lorry owners urge Centre to set up Transport Ombudsman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh Lorry Owners’ Association has called on the Union government to establish a Transport Ombudsman for the road transport sector. The association's State president, Y. V. Eswara Rao, emphasized the need for institutional intervention to address pressing issues faced by truck operators and drivers.  He believes a dedicated Transport Ombudsman would help resolve grievances effectively.

articles.title: Who is Riley Podleski? US journalist goes viral over claim America used ‘less than 10%’ of its military against Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Riley Podleski, an American journalist and conservative media personality, made claims about the US military's strength during a briefing on tensions with Iran. Podleski, speaking as Pentagon Assistant Press Secretary in a War Department Weekly Sitrep video, stated that the US used less than 10% of its combat power against Iran.  Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War, also emphasized the scale of US military capability, claiming forces had dismantled one of the world's largest militaries while using only a fraction of their strength.  Podleski further claimed credit for US President Donald Trump's actions and detailed a rescue mission involving over 170 aircraft after an F-15 Strike Eagle was shot down over Iran.

articles.title: At least 30 dead in stampede at Haiti’s historic Citadelle Laferriere | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: At least 30 people have died in a stampede at the Citadelle Laferriere, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Haiti's northern countryside. The incident occurred during an annual celebration at the fortress, which was packed with students and visitors. Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime expressed condolences to the families of those who perished and assured them of his solidarity.  Rescue operations are ongoing, and the death toll is expected to rise as authorities continue their search for missing persons.

articles.title: Hungary election live: voters head to the polls in contest that could see end of Viktor Orbán’s rule | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Viktor Orbán, the incumbent Prime Minister of Hungary, concluded his electoral campaign in Budapest with a rally that drew thousands of supporters.  His final speech focused on criticism of Europe's support for Ukraine and warnings about global uncertainty. Péter Magyar, leader of the opposition Tisza party, closed his campaign in Debrecen, a traditionally Fidesz stronghold, suggesting he believes he can win there and potentially change the government nationally. The election is seen as a crucial test for Orbán's 16-year rule and could reshape Hungary's relations with the EU, Moscow, and Washington.

articles.title: ISKCON-Vijayawada hosts ‘Harinaama Sankirtan’ for global peace - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: ISKCON-Vijayawada chapter organized a "Harinaama Sankirtan for World Peace" on Sunday, April 12, 2026. The procession began at Autonagar Gate and concluded at the Sri Jagannath Temple, with participation from around 100 brahmacharis from Mayapur.  The event was led by Bhakti Vijaya Bhagavata Swami Maharaj and Chakradhari Prabhu, ISKCON-Vijayawada temple president. The procession drew support from several city dignitaries and spiritual seekers.

articles.title: 247 kg of gutkha seized, three held in Villupuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Villupuram district seized 247 kg of smuggled gutkha and arrested three individuals, Vinodh (30), Parthi (33), and Jayakumar (47), from three cars at Pulichapallam on Saturday. The seizure followed a tip-off during vehicle checks conducted by the police team.  A case has been registered.

articles.title: Fire at decoration warehouse in Shivarampally triggers panic, no casualties reported - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out at a decoration items warehouse in Shivarampally, Rajendranagar on Sunday morning.  Fire officials received a distress call around 8:20 a.m., and the blaze originated in a tin shed containing wedding and event decorations. The cause of the fire was determined to be an electrical short circuit. Locals alerted the police and fire services, who responded with fire tenders to bring the situation under control by approximately 10 a.m.  Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: One dead and several injured after mass shooting at Chick-fil-A in New Jersey | New Jersey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: At least six people were shot, including one fatality, at a Chick-fil-A restaurant in Union Township, New Jersey on Saturday night. The incident, which the Gun Violence Archive classified as a mass shooting, occurred around 8:40 pm and left five victims hospitalized with unknown conditions, while another was pronounced dead at the scene.  The Union Township county prosecutor's office is investigating the shooting, and authorities have not yet released details about a suspect or motive. The incident has prompted local officials to offer condolences to those affected and remain in contact with law enforcement.

articles.title: LDF will return to power for a third consecutive term with more than 90 seats, says M.V. Govindan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.V. Govindan, Communist Party of India (Marxist) State secretary, expressed confidence in the Left Democratic Front's (LDF) victory in the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections, predicting an unprecedented third term for the ruling coalition. He refuted claims that high polling percentages indicated a change in government, citing reduced voter turnout after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and emphasizing the LDF's record on poverty eradication, infrastructure development, and communal harmony as key factors in their re-election bid.  Govindan also accused the United Democratic Front (UDF) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of engaging in unethical campaigning tactics.

articles.title: Man charged with murder of Finbar Sullivan in Primrose Hill | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Oliuwadamilola Ogunyankinnu, 27, has been charged with murder after the death of Finbar Sullivan, a 21-year-old filmmaking student.  Sullivan was fatally stabbed in Primrose Hill on Tuesday and his father described him as "the most beautiful, lovely, outgoing, loving boy." The Metropolitan police are urging anyone with information to contact them.

articles.title: Teen dies after late-night outing ends in fatal crash near Gachibowli Stadium - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An 18-year-old student, Aitha Prabhu Kiran, died in a road accident near Gachibowli Stadium early Sunday morning after a late-night motorcycle ride with a friend. The incident occurred when the duo's bike was struck by a speeding motorcycle traveling towards Lingampally.  Kiran was riding pillion and died at the scene, while his friend Vishnu sustained injuries that require treatment at Osmania General Hospital. Police have launched an investigation into the accident.

articles.title: Chittoor police step up vigil against IPL betting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Superintendent of Police Tushar Dudi issued directives to police personnel in Chittoor, Nagari, Palamaner, and Kuppam sub-divisions to combat illegal betting and gambling linked to the ongoing IPL season.  He emphasized the need for strict enforcement against such activities, including online and offline betting, which he stated were negatively impacting youth and families. Mr. Dudi urged police teams to conduct raids on gambling dens and lottery networks while also directing sub-divisional officers to educate the public about the dangers of betting. He encouraged individuals to report any suspicious activity to their nearest police station or by dialing 100.

articles.title: Irish police clear Dublin blockade staged by fuel price protesters | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police cleared a blockade of central Dublin by farmers and hauliers protesting fuel price increases, signaling a possible end to six days of protests that have disrupted Ireland.  The Irish government is expected to approve measures to reduce fuel costs and resolve the political crisis. Protesters outside a fuel terminal in Foynes, County Limerick said they would lift the blockade at 1pm on Sunday. Despite police actions and proposed financial alleviation, some protesters expressed resentment and vowed to continue their demands until their needs are met.

articles.title: Drishya murder case accused brought to Kozhikode from Mumbai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode city police brought Vineesh Vinod, the accused in the Drishya murder case, to Kozhikode for further interrogation after his arrest from Mumbai on April 11.  The Maharashtra police assisted in tracking down the fugitive who had been evading authorities by changing locations and staying in temporary accommodations. The family of Drishya expressed their belief that Vineesh was not mentally ill and demanded he not be placed back in a mental health center without adequate security measures.

articles.title: Tenant farmers express concern over the proposed online land record system - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh Tenant Farmers Association expressed concerns over a proposed online lock system for land records, arguing it could negatively impact tenant farmers' access to identification and government benefits. The association, led by president A. Katamayya and general secretary P. Jamalayya, urged the state government to protect landowner rights while ensuring tenant farmers are not left vulnerable. They warned that the system could hinder CCRC applications due to direct landowner confirmation requirements, impacting farmers' eligibility for loans and insurance schemes.  The leaders also highlighted concerns about mistrust in the revenue system and potential delays or denials of identification cards.

articles.title: Women's Reservation Amendment: BJP issues whip for MPs ahead of special parliament session - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP has issued a three-line whip to all its MPs, urging them to remain present in Parliament during the extended Budget session from April 16th to 18th. The government plans to bring proposed amendments to the Women's Reservation Act for consideration and passage during this special sitting.  The Union Cabinet has cleared draft bills aimed at implementing the women's quota before the 2029 parliamentary elections and increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats.

articles.title: Temporary stoppage for some trains - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: South Western Railway has announced temporary stoppages for several trains at Banashankari Halt from April 23 to 28, in preparation for the Banashankari Jatra Mahotsav.  The changes affect Train No. 56519 KSR Bengaluru-Hosapete Daily Passenger, Train No. 56520 Hosapete-KSR Bengaluru Daily Passenger, Train No. 16239 Chikkamagaluru-Yesvantpur Daily Express and Train No. 16240 Yesvantpur-Chikkamagaluru Daily Express. These adjustments aim to improve passenger convenience during the festive period.

articles.title: PM Modi government wants to put caste census in cold storage: Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress has accused the Modi government of attempting to delay the caste census and mislead the country by amending the women's reservation law.  Jairam Ramesh, a Congress General Secretary, claims the government is using Article 334-A as an excuse for delaying the caste census results, which are expected in 2027. The Congress argues that both Bihar and Telangana completed their caste surveys within six months, contradicting the government's claim of delayed results.  The party also accuses the government of using the women's reservation law to gain political mileage.
